While the pull-down slides (`g_dropdown_menu_state` 1 or 2, or its `timer_idex` slide timer running) the wheel does nothing there, in brightness and volume mode alike (`edit_key`), so a tick during the swipe or the slide moves neither: only the open, rested panel takes it. Stock's slide timer (`0x4a1f4c`, 10 ms, 80 px a step, added by the dialog's pointer-up handler at state 1 or 2) sets `timer_idex` back to -1 and the state to 3 once the dialog is down, and ends a push up in `dialog_quit`, whose quit handler sets the state to 0, so an open panel at rest reads 3 and -1. Its swipe up to close may start on that slider, which then moved the brightness before stock took the swipe. `ringnav_dispatch` keeps the slider's pointer-down back (Quick Settings' only, under `statusbar_dialog`; Settings' Brightness page is stock's): the slider gets it, at the touch's start, only once a move goes `SLIDE_PX` (10 px) more sideways than up or down, or with a tap's release. A touch that first moves `SLIDE_PX` up or down, or any while stock slides the pull-down or it follows a swipe (`g_dropdown_menu_state` 1 or 2), never reaches the slider, and a press it already has is aborted (`EVT_POINTER_ABORT`). A withheld event returns 0 rather than `STOP`, which would also end its parents' handling, so the window manager's pointer-down still records the touch's start (`g_pressdown_y`) that stock's swipe measures from. A drag that set the brightness before the pull-down moved keeps it. Under OLED neither applies: the wheel walks the page's rows, Center on Brightness gives it the slider, and a held Play/Pause is stock's ([ipod](ipod.md#quick-settings)). Stock's swipe down (`on_wm_tsmove_fun`) sets `g_dropdown_menu_state` 1 and opens the dialog off screen; only the touch's release reaching the dialog starts its slide (its pointer-up handler adds the `timer_idex` timer, which ends at 3, open). The dialog is modal: its init leaves `to_modal` on, so `navigator_to` runs `dialog_modal` inside that pointer move, and the nested loop drains the input queue before its first timers and idles. Above the screen the dialog catches a touch only once opened (`window_manager_find_target`, stage 3, set by `EVT_WINDOW_OPEN` in the window manager's open idle `0x69beb0`). So a release already queued goes to the page under it: a flick quicker than the dialog loads, or any swipe queued behind a blocked loop, as during a track start. That left the dialog on top and invisible at 1, with the page under it sent to the background by that same idle, so Now Playing's 250 ms timer (cleared by its background handler `0x53dfbc`) stopped and the time, bar, title and art froze while the music played, until a key closed the dialog or a touch showed it ([#189](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/issues/189)). `quick_stuck` treats it at 1 or 2 with no touch down and no `timer_idex` timer as stuck, and `quick_poll`, in every `ringnav_sleep` right after `stale_heal`, then hands the dialog a pointer-up through `ringnav_dispatch`: the release it missed, late, so stock's handler (`0x4a1e6c`) slides it the way the swipe asked (`g_slide_direction`). That handler ignores the event's place and, at states 1 and 2 with `timer_idex` -1, always adds its slide timer (`0x4a1f4c`), which always ends, so one pass does it. A stale press holds it for at most `STALE_TOUCH_MS`, as `stale_heal`'s release (the input queue paragraph under [Hooks](#hooks)) reaches the same handler; a finger resting that long on a half-pulled panel also lets it slide. That a flick can beat the dialog's load is inferred from the code's order; the load time is not measured. **Set date and time** (`manualtime_page`: year, month, day, hour, minute) and the **sleep timer** (`sleepshutdown_page`: hour, minute) edit one `text_selector` at a time, framed in two white pixels by the border hook: the wheel steps its selected index (`SELECTOR_INDEX`, set through stock `text_selector_set_selected_index`) within `text_selector_count_options`, Center moves to the next field, switching the date page's `slide_view` to the time page after the day, then to OK (`btn_enter`), drawn while it is next as a selected row (an off-white `MINIMAL_FILL` card, `SEL_RADIUS` corners, its label dark at `EDIT_OK_PX`) rather than framed, which the next Center clicks; a turn on OK goes back to the last field (Previous) or the first (Next). A swipe between the date and time pages moves the field to that page's first. The side keys (Next, Previous) move between the fields and OK the same way, stopping at the ends, ahead of stock's track skip (`field_key`). A side key also drops a Center still waiting for its double (`stop_timer(&st.edit_press)`, the editor's own press; `cancel_center` stops only a list row's), so only the key acts: the Center would step once more after it, or press OK from the last field. Under a set with no toolbar (OLED's) with the Sleep Timer switched off, the press it drops is the switch's flip. A Center pressed again inside the dropped one's `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS` does nothing: `center_press` arms no single that soon after a press. On the date and time page OK sets the clock (stock's `set_systime`, which stays on the page) and then goes back to the Time page (`time_ok`, `navigator_back`), after a tap (`ringnav_dispatch`) or Center's click (`edit_single`); the sleep timer's OK stays stock's. Center waits `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS` (`center_press`) and clears `KEY_LOCKOUT` as a list's click does, and a double press is stock's screen toggle. The field lives in the page's `_edit_field` property, so it dies with the page.

<a id="inline-sliders"></a>On OLED, Settings no longer opens four of these pages: Playback's Max Volume, Balance, Crossfade's length and Default Volume's level and Display's Brightness are inline slider rows (`patch/inline_slider.c`, [design](oled-design.md#inline-sliders)), whose values are set with stock's own setters, each as its page sets a step: Max Volume writes `g_maxvolume` and `PLAYSET MAXVOLUME`, pulling `g_volume` down with `device_set_volume(v, 1)` and `PLAYSET VOLUME` as stock's minus (`0x4bb360`) does; Balance calls `config_balance` (-10 left to 10, the DAC's ioctl and `PLAYSET BALANCE`; stock's caller clamps, so ours does) and reads `mclGetBalance`; Brightness calls `config_lightness` (0 to 100: `g_lightness`, the backlight and `SYSSET LIGHTNESS`; the backlight page's slider has no `min` or `max`); Default Volume's level writes `g_bootvolume` and `PLAYSET BOOTVOLUME` and its switch flips `g_bootvol_flag` and writes `PLAYSET BOOTVOLFLAG`, as `0x4b73b8` and `0x4b7334` do; Crossfade's goes through `xfade_set` (`Q2POD XFADE`, `XFADESEC`). Stock's Balance and Brightness rows stay in their lists, hidden, as their pages' code finds them by place. A row's click grabs it; while grabbed `inline_slider_key`, beside `lr_edit_key` in `ringnav`'s key filter, takes the wheel (`wheel_level`, a click per step whose press `ringnav_keydown` silenced) and Center or Return, the row's `list_item` grows on a timer of its own as a captioned row's does (`is_step`, its progress an `anim_t`, `MO_SPATIAL`), the list laid out again each step (driven from the selection's paint, it stalled part way on the emulator, as those paints stop coming); and `inline_slider_sel`, beside `caption_sel` in `paint_selection`, sets it down when the selection moves off it. The emulator has no DAC, so stock's `mclSetBalance` (`0x5c0a08`, which stores the value only with the DAC open) leaves Balance at Center there. ponytail: a drag on a grabbed track does not set it; a tap sets it down.

Pickers flagged `CHOICE` in `patch/contexts.inc` (Play mode, Filter, Language, Sort and the like) open on the row holding stock's `select` check image instead of the remembered position, so the bar starts on the current setting. Stock's radio images (`select`, `unselect`) are emptied (`ringnav_image_add`), and the border hook draws a checked row's mark itself, the theme's check (`paint_radio`). The Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and Tidal rows' white delete mark (`navbar_delete`) is drawn again there as `list_delete`, a build-added copy that loads in `list_into`'s gray; `navbar_delete` itself stays white, as the playlist page's Delete wants it.

USB mode's exit asks whether to scan for music in a `confirminfo_dialog` before it clears `g_usblink_status`, both when the cable comes out and when the mode page's Stop is pressed with the computer still plugged in (`g_usbdet_value` 1); while `g_usblink_status` is 2 that prompt alone counts as usable, so its buttons take the wheel and Center either way, the first selected as it opens and the wheel stopping at either end (`test_the_usb_scan_prompt_opens_on_its_first_button_and_the_wheel_moves_it_cable_in_or_out`). The Shut Down prompt (`on_wm_keylong_fun`, a Center hold) sets `g_power_longkey`, which `on_wm_keyup_fun` clears at that hold's release and `ringnav` leaves Center to stock while set. Stock's confirm handler since V1.34 (`0x499b9c`, V1.32's `0x49890c` took Return only) stops every Center and wheel release itself, so the release never reaches `on_wm_keyup_fun`: `ringnav` clears `g_power_longkey`, `g_ingore_bootkey_flag` and `BOOT_KEY_GUARD` itself on a Center release over a `confirminfo_dialog`, or every later Center in the prompt was dropped as that release (#303; found from the decompile, the hold itself is not in a host test).

## Queue menu

Holding Play/Pause (key 171) fires the stock long press once per press, after 700 ms (`KEY_HOLD_MS`, as Return's hold does; every other key keeps stock's 1000 ms, 500 for key 232, unused on the Q2): `HOLD_KEYS` turns the key-down's `timer_add` into `ringnav_hold_timer`, with the key in `$a3`, and the timer's `input_device_status_find_key_long_press_info` into `ringnav_hold_info`, so both the timer and its threshold give those two keys `KEY_HOLD_MS`: `input_device_status` (`wm+0x98`, via `window_manager_get_input_device_status` at `0x681ce4`) dispatches `0x111` to the window manager, where stock `on_wm_keylong_fun` has no action for 171. `ringnav_keylong` takes it only with the navigation gates, AirPlay off (`airplayGetFlag() != 2`), no batch-select mode (`g_navbar_status`) and the row a center press would open, on a `CTX_LOCAL`/`CTX_FOLDER` page, an artist's page (`artistinfo_page`, whose tabs fill the showlist) included. There the row's class is `g_local_classinfo_save+0`, which its tabs' `load_localartist_list` sets (`0xff07` songs, `0xff01` albums); `g_class_type` keeps the class the page opened or was last returned to with. The page's row count must equal `deque_size(*p_deque_showlist)`: these lists bind row _i_ to showlist record _i_ (Local Songs `table_row_of` → `deque_at` at `0x4aac14`), and a grid or extra clickable row fails the check. Everything else tail-calls the stock body. Centre or a finger held on a song's row opens the same menu ([Centre hold menu](#centre-hold-menu)).

The release still reaches `playpause_quick_click` (`on_wm_keyup_fun` `0x4f3308`), which has no long-press check. The hold stores the key record's u64 press time (record `+8`; 16 records of `0x18` from `+0x30`); the key-up hook swallows a Play/Pause release carrying that time and clears the latch on every Play/Pause release. AWTK drops the release when it aborts pressed keys on a window change (`input_device_status_abort_all_pressed_keys`, on the window manager's `0x12e`, which a window's open event, `0x129`, and every window's destroy send, so Hold Return: Home, which opens nothing, ends the press too); a later press has a new time, so a stale latch cannot eat it.

<a id="held-keys"></a>**A held key across a window change.** The Q2's buttons repeat their key-down while held (a repeat follows within 258 ms), and since V1.34 stock's `input_device_status` takes a key-down for a record it has aborted as a new press (`0x6b35f8`: `should_abort` set, it clears the record and times it again), where V1.32's kept the record and dropped the key until its release. So from V1.34 a hold that opened a window came back to life in that window with the button's next repeat: a key-down there, the release delivered with a new press time, and a second long press once that time had run the hold (the timer skips aborted records and, Center's apart, those it has already emitted). Play/Pause's release then failed the latch's compare and played or paused under the hold's menu, wherever the hold opens one; Return's went back from the Now Playing its hold had opened ([Hold Return](#hold-return)) (#303). A Return still held about 2 s on would have gone back by its second hold: read from the timer, not reported. `KEY_ABORTED` (`tools/build.py`) takes the branch past the clearing always, which is V1.32's code: an aborted record stays until its release, and its repeats and release are dropped; Center's release (and key 236's) is delivered even then, on both versions, which the Shut Down? prompt's fix relies on. Read from both versions' handlers and run on stock's own code in `test/patch.py` (`held_key`: the press, the hold, the abort, a repeat, the wait, the release); that the buttons repeat on V1.34's kernel as on V1.32's is taken from the two reports, not measured. The limits are V1.32's, as in 1.7.6: a button held past its first repeat while some other window opens or closes (a toast, the volume dialog's 3 s close) loses that press, and a release lost after an abort leaves the record, so the key's next press is dropped whole, clearing it.

The target is the showlist index plus hashes of the record strings (`+8` name, `+0xc` path, `+0x10`, `+0x14` album, `+0x18` artist) and of the browsing state (`g_folder_path`, `g_class_type`, `g_local_classinfo_save`, `g_artist_type`); the dialog open and the action both re-check it. A type-8 record is one song. In `g_class_type` `0xf003` a row is an album: `getMusicByAlbum(id == -1 ? NULL : album)`, as `load_album_detaillist` → `load_localclass_list(0xff10)` does. In `0xff01` (an artist's albums) it is `getMusicByAlbumAndAlbumSonger` when `g_artist_type == 1`, otherwise `getMusicByAlbumAndSonger`, with `(album, classinfo[0xa] ? NULL : artist, id == -2)` (`0xff11`). A composer's (`0xff02`) or genre's (`0xff03`) albums use `getMusicByAlbumAndComposer`/`getMusicByAlbumAndGenre` with `+0x20` composer or `+0x1c` genre and `classinfo[0xb]`/`[0xc]`. An artist row (`0xf004`) is `getMusicBySonger(+0x18)`, or `getMusicByAlbumArtist` when `g_artist_type == 1`; a composer (`0xf005`) `getMusicByComposer(+0x20)`, a genre (`0xf006`) `getMusicByGenre(+0x1c)`; an id of -1 (Unknown) passes NULL. These are the expansions `batch_add_file` (`0x4ff344`) runs for each class. A folder row (type 4) calls `toolsLoadDirectory(g_folder_path + "/" + name)` like `folder_enter`, then the same for each type-4 subfolder in that listing's order (`folder_tracks`: names starting with a dot skipped, 8 levels deep at most). A path that doesn't fit its 1024 bytes adds nothing, for the row as for a subfolder: cut, it would be another folder's. ponytail: one directory load per folder on the UI thread, so a large tree blocks for a while; a database path-prefix query would be quicker but misses unscanned files. Queries fill `tools_pdeq_directory`; its type-8 records join in order and the staging deque is restored.

A hold on Home's Cover Flow row (`home_cf_hold`: the selected row is, or holds, `img_cover_flow`), opens Display's Cover Flow page (`display_open(DISPLAY_COVERFLOW)`) over Home; the release is latched as any taken hold's.

Coverflow album holds resolve the live `SLIDE_INDEX` against the current sorted album deque, without opening its tracks. Sort, Refresh, preparation, empty screens and pending screen changes are excluded. Both the deferred open and action revalidate the selected record. Play Next, Add to Queue and Shuffle use `coverflow_album_tracks`, shared with opening an album, so disc/track/path/CUE ordering and staging restoration are identical. Go to Artist is available when the album has an artist; playlist actions remain omitted.

A playlist row (Library → Playlists; its Add to Playlist picker, `PLAYLIST_ADD_MODE` set, keeps stock's hold) is the header at the index its `img_more<n>` dots name in `*p_deque_playlist`, checked against that deque's size and the header's hash. Its songs are `getMusicByPlayList(cd_num)`, the query the playlist opens with, less spoken tracks and anything not a song, as its opened list (`0xff20`, `music_records`) shows them. The rows are Play Next, Add to Queue and Shuffle (an empty queue loads them as class `0xf001`, a song list, as Shuffle's `play_folder` does), then More…, which opens `localmusic/playlistsmore_page` with that index, as the dots do.

The menu is the stock `dialog/sortselect_dialog`: its init is synchronous and clears `to_modal`, so `navigator_to` returns with it on top, and it is already a navigation context. The payload replaces its five sort rows with the row's own, titles it with the item (a song by its title tag, the player's parsed title while it plays an untagged folder record, else its file name less the extension), and swaps its key-up (`0x4a0b54`) and back arrow (`0x4a0810`) handlers, both of which set `g_sort_changeflag`, which makes Local Songs reload and scroll to the top on return. The open is deferred out of the long-press dispatch and the action out of the row click; successful queue, favorite and rating actions are silent; failures use a stock `dialog/msginfo_dialog` toast (`{1, 2000, text}`). The menu has no `anim_hint` in any theme, so it opens in one frame and a pick's close leaves the page on top at once (stock's close keeps an animated window on top until its animation ends, `0x69d368`, and the rows read the page under it). A 300 ms dialog fade here, as on the confirms and Add to Playlist, shows black before the menu: the dialog's background is clear, and by our reading the animator's snapshot of it has those pixels black; that was not traced in stock's code. Stock's own dialog assets carry no `anim_hint` and its code sets none, so no theme's dialog animates.

The rows are stock actions. Every row has Play Next and Add to Queue. A song (and a Coverflow track) adds or removes a favorite, labelled from `checkFavExist`, as Now Playing's heart (`manage_myfav`): Add selects the row alone in the batch record (`batch_init_selectrecord(rows)`, `batch_set_selectitem(index)`, as `player_addplayList` does) and runs batch-select's Add to My Fav, `batch_add_file(class, 0xf00a, list, *p_vector_select_record, 0)`, which reads a folder file's tags first; Coverflow passes its own deque as class `0xf001`. Remove is `deleteMusicFromFav`, and on My Fav (`0xf00a`) it sets `g_delete_flag` so the list reloads, as the heart does. Either then clears the song's 1-4 hearts and sends its line to a ratings app, as the heart does (`qm_rated`, [Server library: Ratings](#server-library)). Albums, artists, composers, genres, folders and playlists get Shuffle instead: their songs, the play mode saved as shuffle, from a random song, as Shuffle Songs. Everything but Coverflow and a playlist gets Add to Playlist: the row selected the same way, then `localmusic/playlist_page` with context `1 << 16 | class`, the page's add mode, whose pick runs `batch_add_file(class, 0xf00b, showlist, ...)` for the playlist and shows its own toast. A song gets Go to Album and a song or a row of all albums Go to Artist, when the record has one: Now Playing More's Album info (`0x5397cc`: `classinfo` `+0` = `0xff10`, `+9` = 0, `+0xd` album, `+0x10d` artist, then `playerjumpinfo_page`) and Artist info (`localmusic/artistinfo_page` with `{class, record}`). Both pages reload from `g_local_classinfo_save`, and so do the pages underneath when they come back, so the payload copies it before and writes it back on the opened page's `EVT_WINDOW_CLOSE`. Go to Album is left out on an album's own list (`0xff1x`) and either is left out while its page is already open (`navigator_window_is_exist`): both keep single-instance state, which stock's More means to close first. Its Artist info (`0x5398fc`) asks `navigator_window_is_exist` for `artistinfo_page` and `albuminfo_page`, then closed `localmusic/artistinfo_page` and `localmusic/albuminfo_page`, the asset paths it opens them by: `navigator_close` finds a window by its own name (`widget_child`, a `strcmp`), which has no folder, so on stock neither closes and, for a song played from an artist's page, a second artist page opens over the first. The page's record is one global (`0x58` bytes, its strings `malloc`ed by the init, which only `memset`s what was there) that its `EVT_WINDOW_CLOSE` handler (`0x4aec54`, `toolsFreeStSongInfo`) frees without clearing, so the older page's close freed the newer page's strings and the newer's freed them again. With Artist View on Cover Flow that came at once: the new page's covers close the old covers and the artist page under them (`scoped_open`), then Return closes the new artist page (`keyup`), a double free: glibc 2.28's tcache takes the chunk twice without a check and hands it to two owners, which by our reading is #303's crash on that Return (no crash log came with it). `MORE_ARTIST_CLOSE` in `tools/build.py` gives each close the name its check asked for (two `addiu` immediates), so both pages close before the new one's init, as the handler was written to do, and Return from the artist comes back to Now Playing with the Artists list under it. ponytail: only More opens an artist page over another (the Go to rows are left out, as above); a new way to open one must close the old page first, or `localmusic_artistinfo_page_init` wants the guard. With a `coverflow_page` open (the song was played from Coverflow) or Display → Coverflow → Artist View set to Cover Flow, Go to Album opens the album's tracks in Coverflow instead (`coverflow_goto_album`, see [Artist Albums in Coverflow](#artist-view-and-go-to-album-in-coverflow)), falling back to `playerjumpinfo_page` when the album has no tracks; it is left out while that Coverflow already shows this album (`coverflow_shows_album`). Now Playing keeps its stock heart and More page; Videos have no menu.

A song whose path is on the card (`/mnt/mmc/`) gets **Go to Folder** after Go to Artist, also on Now Playing, when `song_folder` accepts its parent: it fits `g_folder_path` (1024 bytes with its terminator), has no empty, `.` or `..` name (stock's `folder_enter` never builds one) and is still a directory (`__xstat`, checked again at the pick: "Folder not found"). The pick stores the path and its layer (the card 2, each folder below one more, as `folder_enter` counts) and opens `folder_page`, whose synchronous init, `ringnav_folder`, opens it through the [Folder Root](#folder-root) block, the card present; the pending folder is cleared either way. Stock `folder_back` then climbs to the card and out, as from Folder Root. The path is copied, never formatted. The page opens at the folder's top, not on the song. ponytail: the row is left out while a `folder_page` is open (stock keeps one), so Now Playing after a folder play has none; Return reaches that page, which shows the previous folder once the play has moved on.

The queue is `*mcl_pdeqplaylist` (`0xa3a888`) with static state at `0xa4ff88` (shuffle pool, a deque of unplayed indices), `0xa50068` (shuffle previous index), `0xa5006c`/`0xa50070` (gapless preloaded index/flag), `0xa50078` (queue class), `0xa5007c` (position), `0xa50080` (mode) and `0xa5008c` (player socket). Only a local queue (class 1 or `0xfxxx`) grows. An empty queue is loaded by `mclLoadPlayList(tracks, 0, class)`, which does not start playback. Otherwise Add appends with `_deque_push_back`, and Play Next appends too, then turns the new rows into place at position+1 by swapping rows' bytes (`REC_SIZE`, three reversals). `deque_at` points into the deque's own storage and stock's `stSongInfo` copy (`0x5c65ac`) gives every string its own buffer, so a row moves whole and only the new rows are copies. Rebuilding the deque (`deque_clear` + `deque_assign`, as stock loads it) held a library-wide queue twice, as `staged` once did ([Play counts](#play-counts), "`staged`'s memory"). Crossfade's fade key holds the rows' paths as well as their addresses for this reason: after the move, the next row's address holds the Play Next song. `playback_queue_insert` (`patch/playback.c`) owns every queue index fix-up for both: the pool entries, the last pick and the previous index (`back_to`) at or after the insert shift, the new indices join the pool, and then advanced play's seen, history and pending list follow (`playback_insert`, a no-op when it is off). Gapless preloads only pos+1 (modes 0 and 3), so a set preload flag is closed exactly when the tracks land there, with the `mclSetPlayMode` sequence (`{mcl-closegapless\null}` to the socket, flag -1); advanced play then closes any preload as its own (flag 0, index -1). In shuffle the checked call at `0x5c0870` in `mclNextSong` (`bal 0x5ba7d0`, delay slot `a0 = 1`) becomes `jal ringnav_shuffle`: it runs the stock pick, then makes the first Play Next track the position once, if the queue still holds it there. Repeat-one repeats the current track by design.

Now Playing holds capture the queue pointer, length, index, song identity (including CUE offsets) and an ordered queue hash. Deferred opening and actions revalidate this target. View Queue, Now Playing's queue button and its swipe up open the payload's Up Next (`patch/upnext.c` `up_next`, `np_queue` in `patch/navigation.c`, [design](oled-design.md#up-next)) in every play mode, in the [menu sheet](#inset-modal): a sortselect dialog from `modal_sheet`, renamed `upnext_page` so its context and `own_order` stay a page's; stock's `playerqueue_page` (its rows in list order, the playing one marked ▶ by `stock_row_style` and Inter's drawn `play_mark` glyph, `tools/build.py`) is no longer opened from them. Up Next lists, after the playing song, Playing Next (`playback_next_rows`: the pending list) and then the rest of `playback_upcoming` in play order: under advanced play the successor walk of its order, outside it (`plain_upcoming`) the rows after the playing one, and under Repeat All the rows before it and itself again; Repeat One has none. At most `UN_ROWS` (500) rows, under ringnav's `MAX_ENTRIES` (512) stops, taken again once a second when the song playing, the queue's size or loads, the mode or Playing Next change (`un_sig`). Its heading reads "From" and what the pick that loaded the queue came from (`un_source_take`, called from `ringnav_load`): an album's class (`0xff1x`) its album, else the bar's title of the page in front. A row plays through stock's `player_start_queue` (`0x520df0`, which `mclSetPlayPos`es and starts the player) and closes the page. A card app's playlist session adds its songs not yet queued after the queue's rows, as [pending rows](#pending-rows) (`addon_pending`, `UN_PEND_ROW` in `un.idx`), and Centre on one moves to it (`addon_pending_play`). **Playing Next.** Play Next's list is queue indices in play order, at most 64 (`PEND_LIMIT`); Play Next past that drops the list's last entry, Play Last (the hold menu's, `qm_apply` with 2, in place of stock's Add to Queue) adds nothing more to it. Under advanced play Play Next's tracks go to pos+1 and the list's front, Play Last's to the queue's end and the list's end. Outside it, under List or Repeat All, the list is the run of rows right after the playing one (`plain_follow`): Play Next's go to pos+1 and start it, Play Last's to its end (pos+1+its length); a track played from it leaves it, and anything else (Previous, a pick elsewhere, a stock edit, another mode) ends it, its songs playing where they stand. ponytail: the plain snapshot keeps no run, so a restart forgets which songs were queued. Up Next's bump (a tap on a queued row's arrow, or a Play/Pause hold on it: `ringnav_keylong`'s `un_hold`) and its lift (Center held, the wheel, Center) move an entry within the list (`playback_next_move`): under advanced play only the list's order changes, so the queue, its indices, the order and every album or folder group stay as they were; outside it the row moves among the run's rows (`swap_rows`), and stock's shuffle pool, last pick, preload and `back_to` follow (`stock_remap`). Clear (`playback_next_clear`) takes the list's songs out of the queue: the rows kept close up in order, the others go last and are popped (`deque_pop_back`, which frees their strings), stock's indices and the position follow, and advanced play follows the queue by identity (`follow_queue`). The gapless preload is closed when the next track changes. Nothing toasts. A Play/Pause hold on a row of the rest of the queue does nothing. Playing one takes its order entry to the cursor, as a Shuffle Songs pick does (`commit`'s `play_now`). ponytail: a row from the next pass (Repeat All) still plays in that pass too. Its hook (`ringnav_start_queue`, `patch/playback.c`) commits the pick in advanced play first, so Previous returns to it. Under Shuffle Songs it goes through Play Next's path, moving it right after the cursor, so the order carries on after it: the pick does not play again later in the pass, and the tracks it jumped stay up next. An ordered queue (or Shuffle Albums, Folders, a category) moves the cursor to it, so the tracks after it follow. A pick inside a pending Play Next takes only its entry off the list; the rest stay pending. Stock's own View Queue delete under advanced play is followed on the UI thread (`follow_queue`: each UI pass, a View Queue row, and Next, Previous or a preload when they run there): `rebuild` keeps each entry's identity (`rec_id`: a library row's id, disc, track and CUE start, any other row's path's end and CUE start, hashed to the 15 bits `mark` holds; [Shuffle order](#shuffle-order)), so the entries left keep their seen marks, history and Play Next places, shifted down as `playback_insert` shifts them up, and the order is drawn again over them as an insert's is, Shuffle Songs' keeping its sequence (`pass_keep`). The playing entry deleted, stock's position names the one after it, which joins the history, so Previous goes back to the track before the deleted one; with none after it (the last row), Previous goes there too and Next ends the queue. A size change that isn't a deletion takes a new order as a new load gets, Play Next and the history dropped. Off the UI thread (headset keys, a natural change) a resized queue takes stock's way for that one Next or Previous, and the next UI pass follows. ponytail: only a size change is seen (a delete always makes one); a same-size swap would need the identities compared every pass. Stock Shuffle draws each next track at random at the change (`mclNextSong`'s pick from the pool, `0x5ba7d0`), so it has no order to list, show the car or look ahead to. On a local queue it is never left to do so: Shuffle Songs and a collection's Shuffle save stock's Shuffle mode, then hand the loaded queue to advanced Shuffle Songs with Repeat All (`playback_shuffle`), and a stock Shuffle chosen elsewhere (Now Playing's shuffle button, the car's SetMode) or a queue loaded under it is handed over the same way on the next UI pass (`shuffle_own`, from `playback_poll`; View Queue's `playback_listable` too, should that pass not have come), while the song playing is still the only one stock's shuffle has played. The order is then the one thing Up Next lists, Next, Previous, a song's end, the gapless preload (`ringnav_preload`, which opens the real next song, so a Shuffle change is no longer a cold start) and Crossfade's next (`playback_next`) all read, so what is listed is what plays by construction, not by two orders kept in step. A queue it cannot take (over `QUEUE_LIMIT`, out of memory) keeps stock's shuffle and is not tried again until it changes or a mode is chosen (`own_tried`); a DLNA or online queue (`0xf1`, `0xf2`) keeps stock's. The order is fixed until Shuffle goes off or a new queue loads: a song put in keeps it (`pass_take`, `pass_keep`): Play Next lands right below the playing song, at the head of Playing Next; Play Last (the hold menu's Add to Queue) at the end of Playing Next, so after every Play Next and before the rest of the order; an app's song (a playlist session's download) at the end of this pass, and somewhere in the next; a song taken out (Clear, a stock delete) leaves the rest as it was. Shuffle off (any other mode, `ringnav_mode`) ends it: the queue plays on in its own order from the song playing, and Up Next is the queue's order again. Shuffle on again draws a new order, the song playing first, nothing played above it. At the order's end Repeat All (stock's Shuffle never ends) plays the next pass, a new shuffle drawn when a listing or this pass's end first reaches it (`cycle`, `next_pass`; a grouped mode's when this one began), so what is listed after this pass is what then plays; a new pass rather than the same order again, as stock's shuffle draws afresh once every song has played. Under a shuffle Up Next lists the songs already played above the playing song's header, oldest at the top (`playback_played`: the history before the playing song, at most `UN_PAST`, 100, of its `HISTORY_LIMIT`, 4096, kept on the heap), so the row right above it is the one Previous plays and the row right below is the one Next plays; it opens with the header at the list's top (`un_open_at`, the rows' end padded so a short rest of the queue can't hold it lower), and again each time a new song plays, and a played row pressed plays that song again (`un_past_click`, a pick as any). Stock Shuffle played this way counts as Now Playing's mode, not the hold menu's extended play (`playback_active`), so the car's and the phone's shuffle and repeat are Now Playing's pair and set them. A Play Next stock's Shuffle was holding (`qm_forced`) is moved to the front of the pending list when View Queue hands a stock Shuffle over. On Now Playing's hold menu a last row, More…, sends Now Playing's own `img_more` a click (stock's handler opens `playermore_page`), only while that page is open (`np_more`). Playlist add mode 2 uses the playing queue; its existing row click handlers are guarded again before the stock callback, with the captured row selected. Browsing state is independent.

## Centre hold menu

Centre held `CENTRE_MENU_MS` (500 ms) on a song's row, or a finger held as long on it, opens that song's [queue menu](#queue-menu), the one a Play/Pause hold opens (`patch/centre_menu.c`, `qm_centre_hold` and `qm_touch_hold` in `patch/nav/hold_menu.c`). The time is half of stock's Centre hold, `STOCK_CENTRE_HOLD_MS` (1000 ms): `input_device_status_handle_event`'s key-down adds every key's long-press timer with `li $a2, 0x3e8` at `0x6b3654` (500 for key 232 alone), and from it `on_wm_keylong_fun` opens Shut Down? ([Center button](#center-button)). The rows are the songs the hold menu already resolves, with its own checks and its own menu: `qm_hold` with `songs` set (the showlist's type-8 records on a `CTX_LOCAL` or `CTX_FOLDER` page: Songs, an album's or an artist's songs, a genre's, a composer's, My Fav, Folders' audio files; Cover Flow's tracks, Most Played and the Ratings lists through `page_tracks`), a payload playlist page's song (`playlist_page_song_hold`, with its Remove row), a song result of Search or of a list page's own search (`search_strip_song_hold`: the result's record at its place in the library's songs, `ss.songs`, or in the page's showlist; Play/Pause's hold opens it there too) and Up Next's queued song (`un_menu_hold`: the song at the row's queue index through `qm_song_hold`, its menu a song's: Play Next, Play Last, Add to Playlist, Favorite, Go to Album, Go to Artist, Go to Folder, then **Remove from Queue**, below). A card app's own page (`addon_page`, a `CTX_DYNAMIC` window that `qm_hold` turns down) asks its app instead (`addon_row_hold`, before `qm_hold` in the chain): a row whose hold op is `hold` gets the menu the app answers it with ([Card apps: a row's own menu](#card-apps)), q2-subsonic's song rows on an album's page, Top Songs and All Songs; its other rows, and the lit pair of an artist's or album's page, keep stock's Centre hold. Up Next gives every song row the menu (`un_menu_hold`): the queue's coming songs, Playing Next's (Centre's menu at `CENTRE_MENU_MS` comes before the row's `UN_HOLD_MS` lift and cancels it; its Move starts the lift, below, and a Centre hold that times no menu, a double press's second, lifts it itself), a shuffle's played songs above the playing one (each with Remove from Queue, `playback_queue_remove` at its queue index), and a pending row, a card app's song not yet queued and with no file yet (most of a Subsonic stream: the app keeps a few songs in the player's queue and the rest itself), whose menu is `qm_far_hold`'s: Play, which runs the row's own press (`addon_pending_play`), then Sync Offline and Go to where they apply, from a record of its own (`addon_pending_one`), as the rows are taken again every second; no Play Next, Play Last, playlist or Favorite rows, which would name a file not there yet. Now Playing, album, artist, genre, folder and playlist rows, Search's artist and album results and every other page get no menu from it. **No Shut Down? from a row:** a hold whose 500 ms finds a row under the selection with no menu (`qm_row_under`: the selected row of the list surface the wheel moves on, as `ringnav_select` left its `SEL` and `COUNT`, or a Search result; never Now Playing) arms `cm_guard_due` for `CM_GUARD_MS` (900 ms), which, when nothing took the press meanwhile (stock's hold still pending, the window it began on still in front: Up Next's lift, Edit Library's and Edit Home's, the tuner's and Control Center's holds at 550 ms each take it first), removes stock's hold timer and takes the release, so the press does nothing: a prompt over a row reads as a misfire. The prompt stays a Centre hold where no row is under the selection: Now Playing (whose release past `NP_HOLD_MS` turns the screen off), a page with no list, Search's letter strip. A server's songs listed in the Library are showlist records and get the Library's menu.

**Remove from Queue.** Up Next's menu ends with it (`qm_song_hold`'s red last row, `un_remove`), on any queued song, never the playing one, which has no row there. `qm_run` checks the record is still the row's first, as for every row; then `playback_queue_remove` (`patch/playback.c`), built as Clear's `playback_next_clear`: the rows after it close up by their bytes (`swap_rows`, no row copied) and the last is popped, the deque freeing its strings; `stock_remap` moves stock's indices (the shuffle pool, the last pick, the preload's, `back_to`), the plain Playing Next run loses the row by the same map, and under advanced play `follow_queue` maps its order, history and Playing Next by the rows' identities. The playing song plays on untouched at its new place (`MCL_POS` mapped), stock's preload closes when the row after the playing one left (or the first, which a Repeat All wrap preloads), and Crossfade's next song is named again: its key holds the next row's path pointer, which now names the song after (`xfade_poll`, `next_publish`). The snapshot is saved at once (`playback_save`), so a restart resumes the shorter queue. Up Next takes its rows again with the selection on the row that took the removed one's place; a refused removal toasts "Queue unchanged".

**Centre.** `cm_keydown` (from `ringnav_keydown`) times a press, never its repeats, when the screen is usable and no first press's open is pending (`st.center_timer`: this is a double press's second, which stays the screen off and Wake's). When it fires, the same press (`st.centre_at`, chord_gate's) must still be down with stock's hold still pending (`st.centre_hold`): a release, a [rim chord](#center-button) (an edge button within `CHORD_MS`, which ends stock's hold) or another payload hold that took it first leaves it. Taken, it removes stock's timer, as Edit Library's and Up Next's holds do, so this press never reaches Shut Down?, however long it is held: the menu is up from 500 ms, and a prompt over it at 1000 ms would be the misfire the half time is there to prevent. Shut Down? is a fresh Centre hold where no row is under the selection (above). The menu's window aborts the press (`KEY_ABORTED` drops its repeats); Centre's release is still delivered ([held keys](#held-keys)), and `cm_key_release`, in `ringnav`'s key filter before the row editors, takes it, so it neither opens the row nor picks the menu's first row; a release that never came is forgotten at the next press. Up Next's Playing Next rows get Centre's menu before their lift (`un_keydown`, `UN_HOLD_MS`), which it cancels; the menu's **Move** (`qm_held_move`, `QA_MOVE`, last before the destructive gap and Remove from Queue, its symbol `q2coda/grip`, the lifted rows' three bars) starts the same lift (`un_move`: the row found again by its queue index, selected, and `un_lift`), the card the wheel carries, Centre dropping it and Return putting it back (`un_key`). Stock's own queue page, which Now Playing's More opens from its Queue row (`playermore_row_on_click`), is asked of the navigator (`ringnav_nav_to`) and opened as Up Next instead (`upnext_instead`), so the queue has one page: stock's rows went to its table's list order, stale once the queue changed under it, and had no menu. Edit Library's and Edit Home's hold (`LR_HOLD_MS`), the radio tuner's and Control Center's are on pages with no song row, where the menu's timer finds nothing and leaves them theirs. A game's keys stop before `ringnav_keydown`; a dark screen, and Buttons Lock with it, is not usable.

**A finger.** Search's results are painted on one sheet, not rows: `search_strip_touch_hold` finds the result under the finger by the list's pitch, as a tap does, and lets the sheet's own press go (`ss.pressed`), so the abort and the lift open nothing. Elsewhere, `cm_touch`, from `ringnav_input`'s raw pointer events (the panel's portrait axes: the UI's x is the raw y, its y 319 less the raw x), times a touch from its landing; a move past `CM_SLOP` (8 px), a lift or an abort ends it, so a drag or a scroll never opens it. When it fires with the finger still down, `qm_touch_hold` selects the row under it (`widget_to_local` against each loaded row's box, `ringnav_select`) and asks the hold menu as Centre does, but with no key record (`QM_BY_TOUCH`) and past `qm_hold`'s gate on a pressed pointer; a row that is no song gets its selection back. Taken, the touch is aborted through the window (`EVT_POINTER_ABORT`), so the row's press and the list's drag let go and the lift clicks nothing. On Up Next a finger gets the menu on every song row, a played and a pending one included. ponytail: the raw axes are read from `status_touch`'s use of them and checked on the emulator, not on a Q2.

## Slide menu step

Home is an ordinary list ([ipod.md](ipod.md#home)) that bumps and wraps like a ring list. A `slide_menu` the payload steps (Cover Flow's covers; `carousel_page` also names Home's page, whose stock carousel is hidden) uses `HOME_SLIDE_MS` (200 ms) for isolated ticks and `HOME_FAST_SLIDE_MS` (120 ms) when consecutive same-direction ticks arrive at most `HOME_FAST_WINDOW_MS` (200 ms) apart. There is no extra input gate; stock filtering and audible ticks stay stock-controlled. Each accepted tick retargets one animator from its live offset, extending the intended destination by one item. Reversal discards that destination and heads toward the adjacent item in the new direction at normal speed. Stock completion handles wrapping and selection; center confirmation follows the intended final item. Touch, native clicks, center presses, leaving the page and unavailable navigation reset speed tracking; wheel input cancels pending center confirmation. Allocation failure settles on the requested item without retaining an animator.

### Home's layouts and stock's carousel

Display's Home has two layouts, Split and Full (`IPOD/HOME` 0 and 1; `tools/theme.py` `SETTINGS` counts two values): any other stored value reads as Split (`config_value`) and is never written back, as the row's next save is 0 or 1. Both keep the Settings row on Home's list always (`library_edit.c`: Settings is `LR_LOCKED`, never hidden), so Display, and the Home row on it, can always be reached from Home. Stock's carousel of cards and its arrows stay in `home_page.bin`, hidden and insensitive (`tools/ipod.py` `ipod_home`), since `home_page_init`'s visitor binds the arrows and the cards by name; nothing shows or steps them, and V1.36's Album Wall card is left out, as its page does not ship. Its cards' art (`menu_*`) has no exception in the image hook, so it would take the Theme like any image. `IPOD/SHORTCUT` is not a setting and is never read.

## Coverflow

Coverflow (`patch/coverflow.c`) follows Rockbox PictureFlow: albums and tracks come from the stock library queries, never from tags, and the payload owns only a thumbnail cache. Audit (V1.32, 2026-09-28; the addresses are V1.36's, carried by `tools/rebase.py`); every entry point is exported, and the builder pins the executable through the stock ZIP's SHA-256:

| Stock entry                                       | Address                 | Size      | Prologue                                                |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `home_page_init` (hook)                           | `0x534b6c`              | 1028      | `50001c3c3c309c2721e09903`                              |
| `getAllAlbum`                                     | `0x507a20`              | 800       | `53001c3c109e9c2721e09903`                              |
| `getMusicByAlbum`                                 | `0x50a348`              | 480       | `52001c3ce8749c2721e09903`                              |
| `toolsThumbSpecCover`                             | `0x5d71a8`              | 264       | `46001c3c70279c2721e09903`                              |
| `toolsGetAlbumCover`                              | `0x5d709c`              | 268       | `46001c3c7c289c2721e09903`                              |
| `window_create`                                   | `0x67d824`              | 72        | `3c001c3c4cca9c2721e09903`                              |

| `image_base_set_image`                            | `0x656d04`              | 228       | `3e001c3c2c359c2721e09903`                              |
| `widget_load_image` / `widget_unload_image`       | `0x66f75c` / `0x66fdf4` | 196 / 124 | `3d001c3cd4aa9c2721e09903` / `3d001c3c3ca49c2721e09903` |
| `bitmap_create_ex` / `bitmap_destroy`             | `0x642f34` / `0x642ae4` | 248 / 256 | `3f001c3cfc729c2721e09903` / `3f001c3c4c779c2721e09903` |
| `bitmap_lock_buffer_for_read` / `_for_write`      | `0x643570` / `0x6435e8` | 120 / 120 | `3f001c3cc06c9c2721e09903` / `3f001c3c486c9c2721e09903` |

Data: `tools_pdeq_directory` (`0xa3a8a0`, 4), `parse_cover_mutex` (`0xa4bc28`, 24) and `g_playcover_mutex` (`0xa4db88`, 24) are size-checked `CONTEXT_DATA`; the scan thread handle `0xa3b0c8` and done flag `0xa3b0c4` have no symbol (`offsets.inc`).

**Albums.** `load_localclass_list(0xf003)` (`0x51357c`) is `getAllAlbum()` followed by `deque_assign(*p_deque_showlist, *tools_pdeq_directory)`, so the payload calls `getAllAlbum` itself through `staged`, into a deque of its own: no private state, and a Local Music page underneath keeps its showlist. `getAllAlbum` runs `select id,album,songer,fileurl from songtable group by album COLLATE NOCASE` on `/mnt/data/database.db` through `toolsQueryDbTable` (`0x5dad14`: the lazily opened shared handle at `0xa50114`, `deque_clear`, `sqlite3_exec`, then `algo_sort_if` with the stock comparator). Its row callback (`0x506e94`) skips empty albums and fills `+0` id, `+0x10/+0x14` album, `+0x18/+0x20` artist and `+0xc` the group's `fileurl`, which is the first-track path the art build uses. When any album exists it then appends an "Unknown Album" row (id -1, no path). It returns the query count: -1 without a database, 0 when empty. That grouping is by name alone (stock's Albums list shares it), so Coverflow then runs `ALBUM_SQL`, the same columns plus `albumsonger`, grouped by album, then album artist, or for songs without one the folder (`rtrim(fileurl, replace(fileurl, '/', ''))`), through `split_row`: `album_row` on the first four columns, then the album artist into `+0x24` (`REC_ALBUM_ARTIST`), which the `stSongInfo` copy (`0x5c65ac`) duplicates. An album's path, which its art comes from, is the song `ALBUM_TRACK` picks: the lowest disc, then track, then path, each number padded to four digits, a missing one taken as 0 and one outside 0-9999 (a date as the track, or -1) as its bound, so the prefixes stay four digits and the path whole. A bare `fileurl` was whichever row SQLite read last, so an album whose songs carry different covers showed a random one. Covers already made from another song stay until **Refresh Coverflow** (`coverflow_refresh_art`), which empties Coverflow's cache and stock's `.sldp` (Library's album covers, made once per name, which otherwise only a settings reset, `init_usersetting`, clears) and drops AWTK's cached bitmaps, as the cover thread writes the same names again. Each stock row is replaced in place by its name's rows (`split`), one per `album_cmp` album, so same-named albums by different artists are separate covers with separate art keys; `album_cmp` tells albums apart the same way everywhere else (tracks, Sort ranks, play counts, playback's album groups). Its folder fallback takes a trailing disc folder (`CD1`, `Disc 2`, `Disk_03`: cd/disc/disk, an optional space, `_` or `-`, digits) as its parent, so an untagged multi-disc album is one; the SQL keeps disc folders apart and `split` merges them. Shuffle Folders (`folder_cmp`) keeps each folder apart. The stock Albums list gets the same split (`ringnav_localclass`), and a row's album page (`load_album_detaillist`, hooked to keep the row) and resume (`memeory_startplayer`'s 0xff10 rebuild) keep only that album's songs from `getMusicByAlbum`. Its art cache, `/mnt/mmc/.sldp/<md5 of the name>0.jpg`, adds the album artist, else the album folder, to a name that adjacent rows share (`art_key`): the row renderer (`0x4a52bc`), the page's `albumcoverinfo_init` cover tasks the art thread hashes, and the album page's big cover (`0x4a910c`). An artist's albums tab (`load_localartist_list(1)`, hooked) groups by name too, and has one row of a name another artist shares, so adjacency can't tell: `ringnav_artist_list` splits a copy of the tab as Albums is and gives each row its album's `art_key`, the same-named album in its folder, else with the row's artist as album artist. Its renderer (`0x4adb4c`, the row in `$s2`) and three `albumcoverinfo_init` calls (Album tab entry `0x4aeb70`, page return `0x4b07f0`, which V1.32 had twice, init `0x4b12ac`) use those keys, and the album page's big cover follows its cover task as before. Local art completion (`0x4f84c0`) passes the worker's copied key (`sp + 0x1688`) to `ringnav_cover_done`; the folder-cover path, which branched to the call itself (`0x4f94fc`), now enters one word earlier so it passes the key too: under `aclist_mutex`, it sets the small/big ready flag only if that row still has the key. A job finishing after navigation rebuilt the list therefore cannot mark a different album ready and make later requests skip its missing cover. When `rename_covers` changes a row's key, it clears both ready flags under the same lock, including a completion arriving between stock initialization and renaming. The grids' scroll start (`0x14e`: `0x4ace30` an artist's albums, `0x4a3910` Library Albums) set the worker's shared `albumcover_taskstate` to 2, which it sleeps through, and their scroll end resumed it (`local_albumcover_task`) only when the first row in view changed; a wheel tick within the same rows, or the return to a scrolled grid (its `scroll_view_set_offset` sends `0x14e` alone), left every grid without art until reboot. Library Songs (`music_table_client`, scroll start `0x4a9c00`) did the same, so returning to a scrolled Songs list showed every row's placeholder until the wheel moved. All three stores are `nop` (`COVER_PAUSE`): the worker keeps going, and each scroll end replaces its queue as before. An artist's albums scroll end (`0x4b0adc`) took its first row as `yoffset / 256 * 3`, though its rows are 160 px as Library Albums divides; it divides by 160 (`ARTIST_COVER_ROW`), so the nine covers it requests, and the renderer (`0x4adae0`) draws, are the ones in view. Coverflow keeps this order and shows the Unknown row with the placeholder, only when its card's query, `getMusicByAlbum(NULL)`, finds a song (`drop_unknown`, as [Unknown rows](#unknown-rows)): before V8.6 it showed even with every song tagged.

The copy outlives the page, because the query is the slow part of an open: `toolsQueryDbTable` sorts with a stock comparator (`0x5cd188`) that runs `utf8_to_pinyin` on both names, four `snprintf`s and several `memset`s per comparison. Only `scanAllMusicFile`, `scanSpecFolder` and `deleteMusicFromMusicDb` write `songtable` (every other `toolsInsert/Delete/UpdateDbTable` caller writes the favorites, playlist and play-record tables); their hooks step a generation before and after stock runs, and an open queries again only when the generation moved since the list was taken, or on Refresh. A list taken while a writer runs is never kept, and an empty or refused result is not kept at all. **Opening.** A cold open (none kept, or the generation moved) runs that query with Home still up, in three steps (`query_step`): `getAllAlbum`, then `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`'s grouping, then `split` and `music_albums` on its rows, then the Sort's ranking (`sort_albums`, `OPEN_SORT`) when the order is not kept; the page opens after the last, as a warm open in its kept order does at once. An open that keeps the albums but has a new order to make (a Sort changed in Settings, or Year order or Artists for Year's and Artist's) runs that ranking step alone, the same way. An open whose albums' art is not known (`art_clean`, see Build) then looks for it (`OPEN_ART`) as a last step the same way; one that keeps the albums, their order and their art opens at once. Before 2026-11-19 the ranking ran in `load` on the UI thread once the page was up: Recently Added's on 6,000 albums held the emulator 377 of the 441 ms `load` took, a cold open's spinner stopping for 564 ms before the covers and a warm open's frozen 490 ms with no spinner (a Q2 several times longer, user 2026-11-18). Each step runs on a thread of its own (`open_start`, as `name_order.c` sorts). For the open's first `OPEN_SPIN_MS / 2` (75 ms) the UI thread waits for the steps, looking every `STEP_POLL_MS` (2 ms), so a warm open or a small library's opens as it is pressed; past that it goes back to the main loop and a timer (`open_step`, every `STEP_TICK_MS`, 16 ms) collects each step as it ends and starts the next, the selected row's chevron the spinner meanwhile (`coverflow_spinner`, drawn by `paint_chevrons` through `spinner_icon` on a `CHEV_ICON` theme, OLED; its eight frames are `tools/art.py`'s `spinner`, turned by `list_marks.c`'s spinner timer). Home stays live (`coverflow_wait_input`, first in `ringnav_input`): the wheel's ticks move its rows; Return's press goes nowhere and its release gives the open up; any other key or a touch gives it up and then goes on to Home, so a press into another page works at once; another window over Home gives it up at the next look. Giving up (`open_end`) stops the running step first (`open_stop`): it sets the step's cancel and joins its thread. A step stops within a few ms: every connection `stock_db_open` opens (stock's shared one, which `getAllAlbum` and `toolsQueryDbTable` use) has `coverflow_query_stop` as its SQLite progress handler, every 1,000 VM steps (`QUERY_STOP_OPS`), which ends the statement on the step's thread once cancelled and nothing else's, and `art_find` looks at the cancel between albums. demo imports no `sqlite3_progress_handler`; `tools/peq.py` reaches it from `sqlite3_exec`'s GOT entry by the rebuilt libsqlite3's offset between the two (`SQLITE_PROGRESS_DELTA`, -648,348 in 3.54.1, checked at each build), as `localtime_r` is reached from `tzset`'s, and does nothing while that entry is still demo's lazy stub (`stock_db_open` runs its own `sqlite3_exec` first). A step given up leaves nothing: the query's rows (`cq`) go, a Sort cut short is dropped (`open_work`), and the next open starts again. A library query of the payload's own on the UI thread while a step runs (`staged_into`) gives the open up the same way first (`open_yield`), so nothing on the UI thread meets the step's use of stock's staging pointer (`tools_pdeq_directory`) or its connection. Measured on the emulator (slot 1, 9,300 songs in 930 albums, cold): `getAllAlbum` 104 ms and the grouping 89 ms, which held the UI thread whole before 2026-11-19, the press-to-page 245 ms. Since, on 80,000 songs in 8,000 albums: the press holds the UI thread 75 to 77 ms, the page opens 1,047 to 1,085 ms after it with the wheel turning Home meanwhile, Return gives the open up in 5 ms, and Centre in 151 ms (a step in its sort, below). Half of 150 ms is the cue because what follows `getAllAlbum` costs at least half as much again: in the emulator (QEMU, 2,018 albums of 20,106 songs) `getAllAlbum` took 110–380 ms and the rest of the query 290–690 ms, and on a Q2 with 6,175 albums `getAllAlbum` was 524 ms of an 878 ms open ([server-library](server-library.md)). The emulator's 18-album card opens cold in under 100 ms and never shows it. ponytail: a step's own sorting and splitting (stock's name sort inside `getAllAlbum`, `music_of`, the Sort's ranking sort) runs to its end once begun, so a give-up can wait for it, a few hundred ms on a large library; a stock library call on the UI thread outside the payload's paths would not wait for a step (none from Home is known). Cover Flow's own open groups the library once, not twice: `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`'s rows split `getAllAlbum`'s names as `ALBUM_SQL`'s would, since a name's `ALBUM_SQL` rows are its music rows and more (the `WHERE` drops songs, never a group's key), and `music_albums` drops the more; a name with no music keeps its stock row, which `music_albums` drops as it would that name's `ALBUM_SQL` rows. `split_by` leaves the grouping's Unknown rows (`REC_ID` -1, `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`'s untagged songs) out of the names, so an album tagged "Unknown Album" is split as before. That cut the emulator's cold open (press to the covers' first frame) at 2,018 albums from 1,230–1,340 ms to 860–1,080 ms, the two builds alternated across reboots (784–907 ms to 470–560 ms on a quieter host), and with a signed-in server's 834 more albums from 1,250–1,290 ms to 970–1,090 ms; a warm open, 40–140 ms, is unchanged. The Albums list (`coverflow_split`) and the rated albums still split with `ALBUM_SQL`.

**Folder tag refresh.** Scan specified folders keeps stock's recursive scan and cancellation, but its `toolsCheckItemExist` call (`0x5dc4d8`) goes through `ringnav_scan_refresh`: existing `songtable` rows re-read tags and update in place, matching filename, full path and CUE start/end. IDs, creation time and song count stay intact; a file the library doesn't have yet is stock's to add, at any count. CUE entries use the freshly parsed CUE metadata; ordinary files use `toolsGetMusicInfo`, including the FLAC album-artist fallback, after checking TagLib can read them. Tag validation and refresh disable TagLib audio-property reads, so rescanning existing tags does not probe the audio duration. The title’s stock pinyin initial is refreshed too. SQL text is bounded and quotes apostrophes; an unreadable tag leaves the existing row intact. The existing scan writer hooks invalidate cached album groups. New songs keep stock's insert path. Update Local Music drops `songtable` (`scanAllMusicFile`'s second argument is `toolsInitDatabase`'s drop flag) and dates every song again from `toolsGetFileCreateTime` (`0x5d0954`): `st_ctime` on FAT32, the directory entry's creation time, but the file's `st_atime` when `getDiskMemoryInfoAndSetFormat`'s format byte says exFAT or NTFS, where stat has no creation time and a fresh copy's access time stood in for it. The update's own tag reads move it (relatime, once a day), so each full update dated the whole library to its last update or play, and `getAllRecentAddRecord`'s `order by time_create desc limit 100` (Library → Recently Added; Coverflow's Recently Added sort reads the same column) filled with those songs, the album added that day lost among them (#170, #188). `ringnav_file_created` hooks the function: `statx` with `STATX_BTIME` (`ringnav_statx`, the o32 syscall; demo imports none) reports the creation stamp the exFAT directory entry keeps, which reads never move (stock's 5.10.21 kernel has the mainline driver, which fills it), so every full update dates the library the same way; the first one on this version replaces the dates 1.6.1–1.6.3 kept and repairs those lost before them. Windows and Linux stamp a copy with the time of copying; a Mac keeps the file's own creation date. A file whose filesystem reports no stamp, or a failed call, takes stock's date (the stock kernel mounts no NTFS, so only exFAT takes the access-time path). 1.6.1's keyed `ringnav_added` copy of `time_create` across the drop is gone; one left by an update interrupted on 1.6.1–1.6.3 stays in the database, unused. The query hook keeps that `ORDER BY` outside its `songtable` subquery.

**Scan Folders' rows.** Stock's row click (`0x53f9b4`) ticks the row for a tap left of x 81 and opens the folder for one past it. The list holds folders only, so `specfolder_enter` refuses a folder with none inside, and stock answered "Folder not found" (`msg_notfolder`, #254), which left no way to reach an album's folder without knowing the column is there. `ringnav_specfolder_click` (`patch/scan_folders.c`) asks stock's `toolsLoadDirectory` and `toolsCheckTypeDeque` first, the same check, so a tap on such a folder moves to x 0 and stock ticks it; Center's click already arrives at x 0. Limits: a folder that does open is listed twice on the tap, and a folder holding only folders stock hides (`.Trashes`, `System Volume Information` and the like) ticks rather than failing. Stock's `unselect` ring is emptied (`ringnav_image_add`), so the tick column shows nothing on a row until it is ticked.

**Indexes.** Stock's `songtable` has only its primary key, so `getMusicByAlbum` (`album like '%s'`: an album's page, Go to Album, an artist's All albums card, and twice for each album of Era's Play All), `toolsCheckItemExist` and `toolsDeleteDbTable` (`filename='%s' and fileurl='%s' and time=%d and time_end=%d`: the folder scan's check and `ringnav_scan_refresh`'s update for each file, and each song a delete removes) and `getAllRecentAddRecord` (`order by time_create desc limit 100`) each read the whole table. Both scans' hooks end (`library_scan`) with `create index if not exists` of `songtable_album` (`album collate nocase`), `songtable_filename` and `songtable_time_create` (`time_create desc`), through `toolsUpdateDbTable` on the scan thread and stock's shared handle: after stock's writes, as Update Local Music drops the table and its indexes with it (so a full scan inserts into a bare table and builds each index once), and before `wait_scan` sets the done flag, so the library reads as scanning meanwhile. `like` takes a `NOCASE` index on a text column (stock's `VARCHAR`) while `case_sensitive_like` is off, which nothing sets. The query hook's `MUSIC_WHERE` subquery is flattened into the query, so the scoped queries use it too; a pattern that starts with `%` or `_` still reads the table. With stock's libsqlite3 3.19.3 under QEMU (instructions on a cold connection, the row callback's fill included), an album's songs take 1.2 M instead of 257 M at 65,000 songs (9 tracks), and 1.4 M instead of 1.56 G at 400,000 (16), so Era's Play All on the 65,000-song library's largest decade (760 albums, 1,520 queries) is about 1.8 G of queries rather than 0.39 T; a file's check, delete or refresh 0.6 M instead of 50 M, and 0.6–0.7 M instead of 306 M; Recently Added 4.2 M instead of 780 M at 65,000 and 4.77 G at 400,000. The build costs 1.04 G at 65,000 songs and 7.30 G at 400,000, adds 5.4 MB and 33.6 MB to `database.db` (21.4 MB to 26.8 MB, 106 MB to 140 MB) and sorts through up to 2.6 MB and 15.9 MB of temporary file in `/tmp` (RAM) an index; a folder scan's new song then costs 40 k (65,000) to 64 k (400,000) more to insert. A library no scan has run on since has none and reads as before: a build anywhere else would hold the database's write lock for seconds while stock's library pages query it. A connection still reading when the build writes (a count started before the scan) fails the create with `SQLITE_BUSY` once the 500 ms the shared connection waits (`stock_db_open`) run out, and the indexes wait for the next scan. A full scan (`drops`, Update Local Music) adds three more first, when `/mnt/data` has `DATA_ROOM_MB` (8 MB) free (`card_room`): `songtable_group` on `ALBUM_GROUP`'s three terms as their text (`album collate nocase`, `ifnull(albumsonger,'') collate nocase` and the folder `case`; SQLite matches an index's expression to the query's), which Albums' grouping (`ALBUM_SQL` and the other `ALBUM_GROUP` queries) walks in group order with no temporary B-tree, `songtable_album_exact` on `album` and `songtable_artist` on `ifnull(nullif(albumsonger,''),songer)`, which the [Unknown rows](#unknown-rows) checks (`album=""`, the album-artist one) search instead of scanning the table. In the emulator at 20,103 songs (instrumented build, three opens each, back to back): the grouping 240-347 ms to 171-273 ms, each Unknown check 37-67 ms to 0-2 ms, Artists' and Songs' queries unchanged; 786,432, 487,424 and 413,696 bytes of `database.db` (1.69 MB; 4.87 MB without them), each built in 0.14-0.54 s by q2-coda's SQLite under QEMU. They go before the other three because SQLite takes the most recently created of two indexes that serve a query equally: made after `songtable_album`, `songtable_group` took `getAllAlbum` and stock's other `group by album COLLATE NOCASE` queries and picked another song as each group's bare-column row (its `id`, `songer`, `fileurl`); made before, all 17 of stock's grouping queries give the rows they gave without it, on 3.54.1 and on stock's 3.19.3, checked over a library with albums and artists in two cases. A folder scan adds none, so they come with the next Update Local Music. Stock's 3.19.3 misplans the payload's own `group by ifnull(nullif(albumsonger,''),songer) COLLATE NOCASE` over the binary `songtable_artist` and splits artists that differ in case (402 groups for 202); q2-coda runs SQLite 3.54.1 ([third-party](third-party.md)), which groups them right, and stock never runs that query. ponytail: a full scan whose drop failed keeps `songtable_album` older than `songtable_group`, so the album groupings take the wider index until the next full scan.

They change other plans, for the same rows. An index keeps equal keys in rowid order, as stock's sort did, so with `desc` songs of one second (a CUE image's tracks, files copied together) keep their order newest first (Recently Added, `getAllMusic(3)`: Time added (descending), and the payload's unsorted reads). Oldest first (`getAllMusic(4)`, Time added (ascending)) would walk the index backwards and reverse them, so `library_query` adds `, id` to its `order by`; an ascending index would reverse the newest-first lists instead, and Recently Added would keep the other end of an album its `limit 100` cuts. `count(*)` counts `songtable_time_create` (5.2 MB at 400,000 songs) instead of the table (99 MB): 1.9 M instead of 22.6 M, so the count Update Local Music's message takes before the scan holds its lock for less of the scan's start. `getAllMusic(3)` walks `songtable_time_create`: 1.51 G instead of 2.02 G at 65,000 songs, and no sort spilled to `/tmp` (15 MB). `getAllMusic(4)` walks it too and sorts only each second's songs. The album groupings walk `songtable_album`, a row lookup each in album order: `getAllAlbum` 386 M instead of 889 M at 65,000 (2.32 G instead of 6.26 G at 400,000) with no 10 MB spill, `ALBUM_SQL`, Era's and Home's album count 5–14% fewer, their three-term `group by` still sorted through `/tmp`, an artist's albums tab 13% more (328 M instead of 289 M), and the other `like … group by album` queries (album artist, composer and genre tabs, album search) walk it the same way. Each reads its pages out of order, over twice a scan's (227 MB rather than 99 MB at 400,000). ponytail: those reads are unmeasured on a Q2; `not indexed` puts a grouping back on the table if they prove slow.

**Empty or scanning.** Only the modal Update Local Music dialog (`dialog_updatemusic_dialog_init`) starts the scan: `tk_thread` `wait_scan` → `scanAllMusicFile` (`toolsInitDatabase`, `toolsLoadAllFile`, commit), storing the handle at `0xa3b0c8` and clearing `0xa3b0c4`, which `wait_scan` sets when it ends. The same init sets the byte at `0xa3b0c0` (`SCAN_WHOLE`): 1 for the whole library's scan, 0 for a folder's, as we read stock's code; no device run has checked it. Its Back button stops the scan and quits the dialog before the thread ends. Coverflow shows an empty page while a scan runs (handle set, flag clear) or when `getAllAlbum` returns ≤ 0, as PictureFlow's `check_database()` does: under OLED the empty state (`feedback.c` `empty_state`, its tiles, words and row on a view the page's painter reads, `empty_state_paint`) by cause (`patch/cf_empty.c`): music on the card but none in the library (a walk of the card, dot-folders left out, at most 6 deep and 4,000 entries, stopping at the first song file) is "No Albums Yet" with Scan Music Now (stock's `dialog/updatemusic_dialog`); else a catalogue app signed in (`catalogue_signed`: its card folder holds its `credentials` file, which is looked for and never opened, since the app's status file is in `/tmp` and gone at boot, and signing out deletes it) is "No Albums", "Streaming albums can show here", with no button (its albums join once its catalogue is in); else "No Albums", "Copy music to the SD card". The page's timer (`empty_poll`) loads the covers again once `library_gen` moves (a scan, an import). Other themes keep stock's words, "Update Local Music first". Stock's own limit on a scan went with V1.36: until V1.34 `toolsLoadAllFile` (`0x5dc330`) stopped, as Back does, once the song count (`toolsGetMusicNum`) reached 20,000; now it scans until `/mnt/data` is full, which its insert (`tools_insert_song_to_db`, `0x5da07c`) finds with `toolsGetFreeSpace` after each 100 songs' commit and reports by setting the stop flag to 2 (`toolsStopUpdateMusic`'s byte, `0xa50528`, which Back sets to 1; the scanner looks at it before each folder entry and stops above 0), and the scan dialog then says `msg_no_storage`. Q2 Muse's own limit, 65,000 songs while stock's was 20,000, went with it: nothing counts the scan's songs now. The queue's `QUEUE_LIMIT` is 65,536, and a larger queue (a larger library's Songs, a folder's, a playlist's) gets no advanced play: `rebuild` refuses it before it takes its tables ([Shuffle order](#shuffle-order): 4 B a song for Shuffle Songs, 8 B and a working 12 B for a grouped mode). Play Next or Add to Queue past it (`playback_insert`), or a stock edit that grows the queue past it (`follow_queue`), still takes a 2 B a song `mark` first.

**Update during a count.** `toolsInitDatabase` drops `songtable` and creates it again on the connection every `tools*` function shares (`0xa50114`), which since playlist art waits up to 500 ms for a reader (`stock_db_open`, [Songs' hashes](#playlist-art)): a count outlasts that. A count reading `songtable` on its own connection, the dialog's `msg_count` or Home's `count_worker`, holds a read lock on the database until it ends, and a count reads every page of the table. So the drop could not commit: it failed with `SQLITE_BUSY` (stock ignores the result, `0x5d9d9c`), the create then failed as the table existed, `toolsInitDatabase` closed the handle and returned -1, and `scanAllMusicFile` skipped the update: the old library stayed and nothing said so. `coverflow_scan_all` now waits on the scan's thread, before the marker walk and stock's body, while either count runs (`library_counting`: `home.counting` or `st.msg_counting` 1), looking every 100 ms. Each flag is set on the UI thread before its worker starts: `msg_open` sets the dialog's as the dialog loads, before stock's init starts the scan's thread, and `home_counts` starts no count while a scan runs (`library_scanning`). The wait is outside SQLite and holds nothing, so no statement on the shared connection waits with it. The UI thread waits on it only when the dialog opens again over a running scan: stock's init stops the old thread and joins it, and the stop ends the wait within 100 ms. It can't deadlock: the counts' connections are their own, and a count takes no lock the scan's thread holds. Back ends the wait (`toolsStopUpdateMusic`'s flag, `toolsGetUserStop`) and skips stock's body, returning its 1, as `wait_scan` skips a scan stopped before it starts (`0x4a24a4`): the drop would otherwise commit in a count's last 100 ms and `toolsClearDbCount` erase the Back, leaving a scan running behind a closed dialog, or fail and close the shared handle with a count still running. A folder scan never drops the table (`wait_specfolder_scan` passes a 0 drop flag) and does not wait. `test/patch.py` runs stock's `scanAllMusicFile` and `toolsInitDatabase` on a real SQLite file while the dialog's count holds a read lock on it. ponytail: the dialog stays on its first line for as long as a count runs: Home's album count runs about 14 billion instructions on a 400,000-song library.

Coverflow's main, artist and rated views keep only albums with a track outside `/mnt/mmc/Audiobooks/` and without an `.m4b` extension, case aside (`music_albums`, `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`). Filtering precedes the SQL grouping so a mixed album uses a music track for its artwork. The stock library lists keep their audiobook entries.

**Tracks.** A cover opens `getMusicByAlbum(id == -1 ? NULL : album)`, which is what a stock Albums row opens (`load_localclass_list(0xff10)` with `g_local_classinfo_save+0xd`, `+9` flagging Unknown); it returns stock-ordered songs (`algo_sort_if`). The Albums list has no -2 row; that one only occurs in an artist's albums (queue menu). The result comes through `staged` the same way, keeping only the cover's own album (`album_cmp`: the query matches the name alone). Coverflow then re-orders the copy into album order, disc then track then path then CUE start, so an untagged album keeps its file-name order. Its row callback (`0x506428`, `select *` from `songtable`) fills `+0x08` the file name, `+0x10` the tag's title, `+0x3c` `track` and `+0x40` `cd_num` (`REC_NAME`, `REC_TITLE`, `REC_TRACK`, `REC_DISC`). Each row shows the title tag when present, otherwise the file name less its file's extension; a CUE track's name, which does not end in it, stays whole. Folder play gets the re-ordered deque, so playback follows the list.

**Play class.** `0xff10` would resume the wrong album: memory-play re-runs `getMusicByAlbum` from `g_memory_info+0x611` (`memeory_startplayer` `0x5211f4`), which only `player_load_songlist` (`0x51e31c`) fills, from the live `g_local_classinfo_save`. Coverflow therefore plays the cover's songs as `0xff10` through `play_folder`, after `album_memory` has written the cover's album (or the Unknown flag, `+0x60d`) into `g_memory_info`, so that rebuild finds the cover's own album, and `playing_page` gets `{tracks, index, 0xff10, 2}`. `mclLoadPlayList` copies the deque synchronously. A restart resumes the saved queue whole from `ringnav_queue`; stock's rebuild (`stock_memory`, then `album_only`) runs only when no snapshot exists, in practice a queue of more than 999 songs (`SAVE_LIMIT`). The Unknown Album card's rebuild keeps every untagged song the card lists, whatever its folder (spoken and scoped-out ones left out, and the playing song kept). ponytail: the rebuilt queue is stock's order (name), not the card's file-name order, so Next and Previous after such a restart follow stock's; sort with `album_before` in `album_only` if that shows.

**Art.** Every stock caller holds a lock around the art calls, and none nests the two: `parse_albumcovertask_thd` (`toolsGetAlbumCover` `0x4f8638`/`0x4f9728`/`0x4f97f0`, `toolsThumbSpecCover` `0x4f9080`/`0x4f99f0`) and the UI-thread online thumbnails (`0x536248`/`0x536260`) hold `parse_cover_mutex`; `player_parsecover_thd` holds `g_playcover_mutex` around `toolsGetAlbumCover` (`0x51dc90`) and `parse_cover_mutex` alone around its Tidal/Baidu downloads. `toolsGetAlbumCover` writes and removes the shared `/tmp/.tmp_picture`, so both stock threads can already race on it; Coverflow takes both locks, parse then play. `taglib_album_picture` (`libtag_c` `0x12508`) dispatches by extension to the C++ `get*_file_albumpic` helpers, none of which touches `libtag_c`'s unlocked string list (`taglib_tag_free_strings`), which the UI thread's `toolsGetMusicInfo` uses. That list is what failed the first design; embedded art is only as concurrent as stock's own player thread already is. `toolsThumbSpecCover(src, dst, w, h)` decodes JPEG (≤ 6 MB; libjpeg scales by the longest side, 1/1 to 1023 px, 1/2 to 2048, 1/4 to 4096, 1/8 beyond, `0x5cb198`, so a baseline 3000×3000 cover is cheap, while a progressive one still holds its full coefficient planes, about 27 MB at 4:2:0, in demo) or PNG (≤ 1 MB and at most 1024 px on either side, `slti 0x401` at `0x5c9358`, but only after `png_read_png` at `0x5c9308` has expanded the whole image in demo, about 64 MB at 4000×4000 RGBA), by their magic bytes (`toolsGetPictureInfo`), and encodes, or `cp`s a source already small enough, straight to `dst` with no extension check, so `<key>.jpg.tmp` is safe. Both return 1 on success. Stock's own cover cache (`/mnt/mmc/.sldp/<md5>{0,1}.jpg`) and folder-image finder (`toolsGetExternCover`, `0x5d7640`) are not used: the first fills lazily as the album grid scrolls, and the spec fixes cover.jpg → folder.jpg → embedded. Coverflow tries embedded art, then `cover`/`folder` `.jpg`, `.png`, `.webp` (none from a folder so deep that the image's path would not fit 1024 bytes: the cut name is a prefix, another file's at best), then ffmpeg on the embedded art (last: a process for every album without art). Whatever stock refuses (WebP, a PNG over 1 MB or 1024 px, a JPEG over 6 MB) goes to stock `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` (`ff_thumb`: fork and exec, its first picture or embedded `attached_pic` fitted into the box, written as a baseline 4:2:0 JPEG). `ff_thumb` has ffmpeg write `<dst>.ff` and renames it onto `dst` only on exit 0 with a non-empty file; otherwise it removes `<dst>.ff` and leaves `dst` alone, as stock's grid cache takes any file at its path for art. ffmpeg creates its output before decoding, so a picture it can't decode leaves an empty file even on exit 0, and a killed run a partial one. `-xerror` ends the run at a picture's first decode error instead of demuxing the rest of the audio file, and `waitpid` is retried on `EINTR` so the child is always reaped. That covers the embedded picture in `build_art` and every `thumb` caller with a readable source (playlists' art, Tidal, Spotify).
