It writes no shared file and takes no lock. `thumb` reads the source's header first (`big_picture`: a PNG's IHDR, or a JPEG's frame header within its first 64 segments, a fill byte before a marker counting as one) and gives a PNG over 1024 px either way, a progressive JPEG (SOF2) over 1024 px, or a JPEG whose frame header it didn't find (it may be either, [GHSA-w54x-mvfw-c7v3](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/security/advisories/GHSA-w54x-mvfw-c7v3)), to `ff_thumb` alone: stock would hold the whole picture in demo, which the OOM killer then takes ([#216](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/issues/216)). A baseline JPEG, a smaller picture and another type it can't size stay with stock, and so do the arithmetic and hierarchical progressive frames (SOF6, 10, 14), which ffmpeg 4.2 can't decode. ponytail: a progressive cover cut short, which libjpeg shows with a warning, fails ffmpeg's `-xerror` and has no art now; fall back to stock when ffmpeg exits by itself if such covers turn up. Embedded art gets no such check, as its picture reaches a file only inside `toolsGetAlbumCover` (`/tmp/.tmp_picture`, between `taglib_album_picture` and the decoder's `jalr` at `0x5d7140`), so a large embedded PNG or progressive JPEG still decodes in demo. **16-bit PNGs.** Stock's PNG reader (`png_load_file`, `0x5c91bc`) called `png_read_png` with `PNG_TRANSFORM_EXPAND` alone, so a 16-bit PNG's six-byte pixels were read as two three-byte ones: the cover came out twice as wide with its colours in vertical stripes (the emulator, 2026-11-22: the pool card's RGB48 covers in red and blue stripes on Cover Flow's side covers, column-to-column second differences up to 38 levels on a flat green cover). The build adds `PNG_TRANSFORM_STRIP_16` to that call (`PNG_STRIP16` in `tools/build.py`, the word `addiu $a2, $zero, 0x10` at `0x5c92fc` made `0x11`), so libpng 1.2.59 hands the reader 8 bits a channel, the stride its rows assume: every cover stock decodes (an embedded one through `toolsGetAlbumCover`, a folder image through `toolsGetExternCover`, the thumbnailer) reads right, in demo, with no ffmpeg run. An 8-bit PNG is unchanged (the strip is a no-op on it). Neither do stock's own callers of a folder image: Now Playing's `toolsGetExternCover`, tried before Coverflow's fallback, and the album grid's `parse_albumcovertask_thd`, so a big `cover.png` still decodes in demo when its album plays or its grid row shows; trampolining `toolsThumbSpecCover` itself would cover both. Stock's decoder also refuses palette and grayscale PNGs (its PNG reader, `0x5c91bc`, takes only color types 2 and 6). Now Playing gets the same fallback: `player_parsecover_thd` tries `toolsGetAlbumCover` (embedded) and then `toolsGetExternCover` (folder images) under `g_playcover_mutex`, and that second call (`PLAYER_COVER`, `0x51dccc`) becomes `jal coverflow_player_cover`. That runs stock's call first, then `ff_thumb` on the same `cover`/`folder` names and then on the embedded picture. It never calls `thumb`, whose `parse_cover_mutex` would nest under the player's lock in the opposite order from `build_art`'s. Folder images cost a process only when one exists. The embedded probe costs one for every track without art, so it is skipped when `g_play_id3_info` holds the track's path (`player_get_id3info` parses it before the cover thread runs) and Coverflow's cache file for those parsed tags, keyed as Home's art is, is an empty marker. ponytail: the marker records one track's result, so another disc's tracks, or tracks of a same-named album, whose only art is embedded WebP or a large PNG show none on Now Playing; tracks on albums Coverflow hasn't built, or by another artist than the album's key (compilations), still pay a probe per play. Albums already marked empty need **Refresh Coverflow** (Display → Coverflow). ponytail: one process per refused cover; a resident decoder if first builds drag. Library Albums grids and Folder view get the Ogg case: `parse_albumcovertask_thd`'s three `toolsGetAlbumCover` calls (`GRID_COVER`, `0x4f863c`/`0x4f9738`/`0x4f97f4`: an album's cover, a folder's first track with art, a track row) become `jal coverflow_album_cover` (the first), `jal coverflow_folder_cover` (the second) and `jal coverflow_grid_cover`, each stock's call and then, for an `.opus` or `.ogg` track only (stock's libtag reads no Ogg picture), `ff_thumb`. All three run on stock's one cover thread (`platform_init` starts it) under `parse_cover_mutex`, which the UI thread also takes for Library's online thumbnails (`localmusic_page_init`, `0x536248`/`0x536260`) and Spotify's art (`thumb`), so the lock is dropped for the ffmpeg run and taken again before returning. That is safe: each call's source and destination are the thread's stack paths (`.sldp/<md5>{0,1}.jpg`, `.downpic/fd_<md5>.jpg`), which no other lock holder writes (the UI thread's are `.downpic/s_<md5>.jpg`), and what stock does after it (`toolsGetExternCover` on the album call) runs with the lock held again. The album call's stock fallback is `toolsGetExternCover`, which scans the folder for any `.jpg`, `.png` or `.jpeg`, `folder`/`cover` names first; `coverflow_album_cover` calls it before ffmpeg, so an Ogg album whose art is a folder image costs no process, and its Ogg art is ordered as Coverflow's. The folder-row call already runs it first, and the track-row call has no folder fallback, so neither does. Stock caches only a hit (`.sldp`, `.downpic`), so a track ffmpeg found no picture in is remembered in memory (an FNV hash of its path; not when the track itself is gone, the fork was refused or ffmpeg was killed) and its rows ask no further process. ponytail: 1024 misses remembered until reboot, the oldest overwritten; a picture added to such a track since shows after a reboot. Stock's folder row reads the folder in directory order, the order its files were copied to the card, and keeps the art of the first audio file that has any (folder images, then that file's own), cached as `.downpic/fd_<md5>.jpg`, which stock deletes at every Return in Folder view. So an album copied out of order showed a later song's cover. `coverflow_folder_cover` lists the folder itself and tries its first song by name, as Folder view lists it, before the song stock passed: regular files with the extension of stock's song, no dot files (a Mac's `._` copies). The folder, its first song and whether that song had art are kept for stock's next call; a hit ends stock's walk and clears them, so the next walk lists the folder again. ponytail: names compared by `strcasecmp`, not the list's own comparator; a folder with no art at all stays kept until another folder is shown.

**Build.** A cold open looks for each album's cache file (`art_state`: the art cache's name, and a server album's app cover's) and copies each uncached album's track path (`strdup`) and FNV key (artist, album) into a job array: on the open's step thread (`OPEN_ART`, `art_find`) with Home's spinner when the open goes through `open_step`, or in `load_albums` for a page that loads its albums otherwise (the Sort card, a scan's end, a scoped page). The look asks the card for no file an album: it reads the art cache's folder and each app's covers folder once (`names_of`: one `opendir`/`readdir` pass, the names kept as sorted 32-bit hashes on the heap, 4 bytes a name, 46 KB for the owner's 6,200 cached albums and 5,240 covers, at most `NAMES_MAX` names a folder), and reads a folder again only when its modification time (seconds and nanoseconds) moves, or, for the art cache, after a build or Refresh Cover Flow wrote to it (`names_stale`). On the owner's Q2 (exFAT, 2026-11-24) each `access` of a file in a 5,000-name folder took about 12 ms, so a look that asked twice an album held a first open of 6,173 albums behind Home's spinner for about 74 s (`the cover lookup, 417 of 6173 albums looked at` at 5 s, and no covers a minute on); `test/coverflow.py` `slow_card` puts those costs on its fake clock (12 ms a lookup, 20 us a name a folder read returns) and the covers of 6,000 albums show 240 ms after the press, where a look an album took 72 s. A folder that can't be read or kept leaves the look to the card's answer, a file at a time. A look that finds every album's art there, or a build that ends, marks those albums (`cf.stock`, its `library_gen` and size) known (`art_cleaned`), and an open of them after that is warm: the covers at once with no file asked for per album on the UI thread (on 6,000 albums those `access` calls took the emulator 20-28 ms), the first album found where it was last (`centre_of`), and a thread (`verify`) looking over every album's art behind the covers; an album it finds without art makes the next open cold again, which builds it behind its covers. Meanwhile it shows the placeholder, as any album whose file is missing does. Every change to the albums list joins that thread first (`verify_join`). The covers show at once (`art_build`), each album without art on the placeholder, and one pthread renders the art behind them, 160×160 to `/mnt/mmc/.coverflow/<key>.jpg.tmp`, renamed into place. It takes the album nearest the covers' position first (`next_job`: the jobs are in album order, so that is the first not made after the position or the last before it, round the ring), and follows the wheel, whose position `art_poll` passes it every `ART_POLL_MS` (250 ms); at the same look a cover on the placeholder whose album has been made since decodes again at the next frame (`art_shown`, the flat fallback's images set again), and once every job is made the thread is joined and, for the library's albums, their art known (`art_cleaned`). A close, a load of the albums again (the Sort card) or the card going at Standby (`coverflow_art_stop`, `card_release.c`) stops it after the album in hand; what it made stays, and the next open builds the rest, nearest its position first. The open's own wait (Home's spinner) is the albums' query and the look for missing art; on the owner's library shape the emulator shows the covers 1.1 to 2.1 s after the press on a first open and within 0.1 s on a reopen, the whole build taking 20 to 26 s behind them (see [Cover Flow log](#cover-flow-log)). Missing art leaves an empty `<key>.jpg` marker; a track that is gone, or an ffmpeg run that never reached its own exit (a refused fork, a kill), leaves nothing, so the next open retries it. Before each album the thread writes the album's key and its track's path to `/mnt/mmc/.coverflow/building`, synced in place (a sync per album; not through a rename, whose directory write a reset could lose; a torn note reads short), and removes it after the last. One still there at the next open names an album whose build never ended: demo died on it, or hung on it until the watchdog restarted the Q2, and as nothing marked it every open would try it again and end the same way (two testers' "Preparing artwork… 0/2" restarts, 2026-11-09). `art_strike` gives that album the empty marker, unless its cover is there (a death between the rename and the next note), so it shows the placeholder until **Refresh Cover Flow**, and appends the track to the card's `q2-crash.log` under `== cover flow skipped`: the boot hook's `== last art` names it only when demo itself died ([boot.md](boot.md)), and the tester's log was the watchdog's "demo did not end" with no stall record, demo alive and the Q2 frozen, which fits a swapless kernel thrashing on a large embedded picture decoded in demo (the unguarded path above). One strike per restart, so a card with several such albums restarts once for each. A clean end mid-build (`coverflow_clean_end`, from `ringnav_clean_end`) removes the note and sets the cancel flag, so the thread stops after the album it is on, with no note for the next, which the kill that follows would otherwise have left for `art_strike`: a power-off is no album's fault. ponytail: the battery running out mid-build strikes an innocent album, which Refresh Cover Flow puts back. A 3000×3000 cover costs ffmpeg tens of MB (a PNG frame 27-36 MB, a progressive JPEG's coefficients up to 54 MB) on a device with no swap, and the kernel's OOM killer takes the process with the most memory, which was demo, so the Q2 froze and the watchdog rebooted it mid-build ([#169](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/issues/169); only a dead demo reboots, see [boot.md](boot.md), a hung one never does). every child demo forks (`child_oom_first` in `patch/peq.h`: `ff_run`'s and the boot logo's ffmpeg, Audiobooks' chapter read, Tidal's tagger, q2video) writes 1000 to its `/proc/self/oom_score_adj` between fork and exec, so the kernel takes the child first; the album is then retried at the next open rather than marked artless, and Now Playing's `marked_empty` skip does not apply to it. Demo's own baseline matters too: `staged` keeps the staging deque's contents across a query by copying them out and back (`deque_init_copy`, `deque_assign`), so after Library → Songs on a 65,000-song library every `staged` call briefly holds two copies of that list (a `stSongInfo` is 0x58 bytes plus its strings), the likeliest link to Songs' deferred crash; a move would need the stock deque's layout. There is no build below `MIN_FREE_MB` (16) free on the card (`statfs`, o32 `f_bsize` word 1, `f_bavail` word 7). The jobs made, the cancel flag and the position are volatile `.scratch` ints, and each job's own made flag is the worker's alone. A close and window destroy join the thread, a wait bounded by one album. A folder holding tracks of two albums gives neither its `cover`/`folder` image, which may be the other's: `folders_shared` finds those folders in one pass before the jobs, sorting the albums by folder (FNV hash, then the folder itself and the album key), replacing a check of every album against every other on the UI thread, albums squared: the likely cause (inferred from a tester's watchdog restarts, not reproduced) of a big library's first open stalling until the watchdog restarted the Q2. A cold open, one that queries the albums or finds albums with no art, also writes its phases (`start`, `staged`, `split`, `music_albums`, `drop_unknown`, `sorted`, every 1000th job and `done`, each with the milliseconds since it began) to `/mnt/data/q2-cf-trace`, synced, a few lines per open (a warm one writes nothing), and removes it when `load` ends, so after a forced restart `S90play` puts the phase it reached in `q2-crash.log` ([Watchdog](#watchdog)). Before each album the thread's `crash_note` names its track in `/tmp/q2-art-file` and, every 50th album, appends the count, demo's VmRSS and the track to `/tmp/q2-art.log`, for the crash log ([boot.md](boot.md)). **System settings → Display → Coverflow → Refresh Coverflow** (`coverflow_refresh_art`) first stops [playlist art](#playlist-art)'s build (a Playlists page can be open under Settings), then unlinks the cache directory and steps `library_gen`, so the next open queries the albums again and rebuilds their art.

**Page.** The Home card clones `btn_localmusic` at index 2 in the carousel, reusing its images, and is the third row of Home's list; `home_page_init`'s `widget_foreach` visitor (`0x534750`) binds `img_*` clicks and translates `label_*` by name and ignores unknown names. The Local Music card's label is renamed `label_library`, so it skips it too and its literal "Library" shows in every language. Since stock V1.34 the visitor knows `img_coverflow` and `label_coverflow`: its own Album Wall card's, which `ipod_home` deletes; the Cover Flow card's are `img_cover_flow` and `label_cover_flow`, so stock neither binds the card to its Album Wall nor names it so. The hook runs the stock init through `stock_home_trampoline` (`0x534b78`), then binds `widget_lookup(win, "img_cover_flow", 1)`, whatever stock returned. In iPod it also sets up Home's art ([ipod.md](ipod.md#home)). The card opens a runtime `window_create(NULL, 0, 0, 0, 0)` named `coverflow_page`; `window_base_create` opens it through `window_manager_open_window`, and the window-manager key handlers that `home_page_init` registers route it like any page (`CTX_DYNAMIC`, exempt from the rootfs window-name check). Covers are a factory `slide_menu` of `image_create` children, each item `h` square (`0x605ed0`); with depth (below) the children stay empty and the payload draws the covers. In the flat fallback they are stock images (`image_set_draw_type` 4, as stock cover rows). `slide_menu` dispatches `EVT_VALUE_CHANGED` (`0xe`, after `0xd` will-change, `0x60609c`) with the new index already at `+0x78`, which updates the captions (the album over its artist; with Artists set to Album Artist, `artist_type` 1, the album artist tag when it has one, `cover_artist`, so a compilation reads "Various Artists" or its compiler, and the Artist sort and its letter jump use the same name, sorting again when Artists changes); a caption whose text changes has its marquee stopped and its `xoffset` set to 0 (`caption_text`), so a long name starts at its start after the house hold (`MARQUEE_HOLD_MS`, `ringnav_hscroll_start`), where setting `xoffset` alone was undone by the running scroll's next step and the next album's long name went on from the last one's place (user, 2026-11-18); in the flat fallback only covers within ±3 then load their file, the stock way: `widget_load_image` → `image_base_set_image` → `widget_unload_image`. A failed load (the empty marker) shows `default_album_flow`. Clicks only schedule screen changes on a 0 ms timer, so no screen change destroys the widget whose click is running. Tracks hide the covers rather than destroy them, so Return restores the album.

Coverflow’s Album and Artist sorts, on ticks (a finger on the screen, the page sliding in or no depth frame; otherwise the thumb's letters apply, [Letters](#coverflow-thumb)), once a spin passes `CF_FIRST_MS` (700 ms, longer than the lists' `LIST_FIRST_MS`), jump to the first album of the next or previous populated initial group; with Fast Navigation on Year jumps the same way by year, the next or previous year that has albums, the undated last (`group`, below). The active sort key skips leading articles; numeric, punctuation, separator and missing-name initials share `#`, while other Unicode initials are retained. The same carousel animator is retargeted; utility cards and wrap edges remain individual stops. On ticks the big letter expires after 400 ms (`LETTER_MS`); with Fast Navigation on the thumb's letters hold it until the lift. Recently Added, Most Played and Random keep single-album stepping.

## Tag text

Stock reads a song's tags with its own `libtag_c` (`toolsGetMusicInfo`, `0x5d8b98`, for the library scan and the player): for each of six fields (title, artist, album, genre, composer, album artist) it asks for the field twice, `taglib_tag_<field>(tag, 0)` (TagLib's `String::to8Bit(false)`: one byte per character, Latin-1) and `(tag, 1)` (UTF-8), and whether TagLib found every character below U+0100 (`taglib_tag_islatin1`, `String::isLatin1`). `toolsFixId3ErrorCode` (`0x5d8950`) then took a field for GBK whenever it was "Latin-1" that way: it converted the Latin-1 bytes from GBK to UTF-8 (`toolsIconvConvert(s, "utf-8", "gbk")`, with an `iconv_open("gbk", "utf-8")` round trip as its check) and kept the result, so any Western title with an accented letter came out Chinese: "Lo que la música me enseñó" pairs `ú` and `s` (0xFA 0x73), `ñ` and `ó` (0xF1 0xF3) into GBK characters. That covers FLAC and Vorbis comments (always UTF-8) and UTF-8 ID3v2 frames as much as Latin-1 ID3 frames: the test is on the decoded text, not the tag's encoding. `TAG_TEXT` in `tools/build.py` turns that round trip's `strcmp` (`0x5d8ad4`) into `jal ringnav_gbk_tag`, which also asks that the Latin-1 bytes read as GBK (`gbk_text`): not UTF-8, and every byte from 0x80 one of a pair, lead 0x81–0xFE then trail 0x80–0xFE, with no pair between two ASCII letters. Western text puts an accented letter next to an ASCII one ("mú-s" is 0xFA 0x73) or a pair inside a word ("Can-çã-o", "Beyonc-é’-s"), so it fails and keeps TagLib's UTF-8 copy; a GBK-tagged MP3 (Chinese rips' Latin-1 frames holding GBK bytes) is all pairs and still converts. Limits: a GBK character with an ASCII-range trail byte (0x40–0x7E, the rarer GBK/3 and GBK/4 ones) or a single one inside a Latin word ("a周b"), makes its field read as Latin-1, and Western text whose accented letters only come in pairs at a word's edge ("ñó" alone) reads as GBK. Stock's conversion writes back over a CUE field unbounded, and GBK grows by half as UTF-8, so a CUE field over 340 bytes is read as Windows-1252 instead. The library keeps what the scan stored: **Library → Update Local Music** reads the tags again.

TagLib 2.0.1 joins multiple genre values with `" / "`. Stock copied the result unchecked into the 128-byte style field at `info + 0x200`, immediately before the title at `+0x280`, so a joined genre of 128 bytes or more replaced the title in the library and player (`toolsFixId3ErrorCode`'s `snprintf` stops the value at 255 bytes, so nothing goes past the title). `GENRE_COPY` changes that one copy to `ringnav_genre_copy`, which keeps the whole entries that fit 127 bytes, or as many whole characters of an oversized first entry as fit. Tag files are unchanged. Limits: only `" / "` is an entry boundary, so a single value joined with `;` or `//` over 127 bytes is cut at 127 (at a whole character), and an empty first entry followed by an oversized one stores an empty genre. The library keeps what the scan stored. Update Local Music drops `songtable` and inserts every row through `toolsGetMusicInfo`, and Scan specified folders refreshes existing rows (**Folder tag refresh**), so either repairs the title. Favorites, playlists and play records keep their own copy of a row, which neither touches: a bad title saved there stays until the song is added again.

Every scrolling text is a stock `hscroll_label`, and its holds and pace are set where every one of them passes. Stock's start (`hscroll_label_start`, `0x5fb4ac`, which a label's focus, its paint on a new text, its lull and the payload all call, PC-relative or through the GOT) waits the label's `delay` before its first step; nothing sets one but a page's XML, so most labels moved at once. A looping label then ends a pass by adding its `lull` timer (2000 ms from `set_hscroll_label_attribute`, 3000 by default), whose callback (`0x5fb658`) restarts it: the start's step put the text back at its start, so the lull held the end and the start never held. Its pace is `speed` in pixels per ms (`set_hscroll_label_attribute` sets 0.05 since V1.36 and 0.1 before, some pages 0.2, Now Playing's title and artist 0.05), or, with no speed, the whole overflow in its `duration`. The `hscroll_label_start` hook (`ringnav_hscroll_start`, `HOOKS` in `tools/build.py`) sets every label's `delay` to `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS` (1500) and caps its speed at `HSCROLL_PACE` (0.05, Now Playing's; a label with none takes it too) before stock's start runs. `HSCROLL_LULL` turns the end-of-pass `widget_add_timer` into `jal ringnav_hscroll_lull`, which adds its own timer, `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS` whatever the label's lull, through `hscroll_lull_end`: it sets `xoffset` to 0, then runs stock's callback, so the end holds `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS`, the text goes back to its start, and the start holds the same before the next pass. A looping `yoyo` label scrolls back instead: its lull is 0, since the delay holds whichever end it is at. A label that doesn't loop (`set_hscroll_label_attribute` leaves `loop` off, so most stock rows that scroll by themselves scroll once as their page opens) ended its pass at once, its timer removed, and stock painted its start with the ellipsis the moment it reached its end, or a `yoyo` one stayed on its end: `HSCROLL_ONCE` sends that pass to the lull too, whose end clears the label's timer id and stops it on its start, as stock's own lull callback clears it, so the timer ends by its `RET_REMOVE`. Since V1.36 `set_hscroll_label_attribute` (`0x4f1ed8`), which that release calls for most rows' labels, also gives a label a `loop_interval_distance` of its own width, AWTK's seamless loop: the label's range grows by that distance, so the text runs off the label and comes in again behind the gap, with no end to hold. `hscroll_label`'s range (`0x5fb1e4`), timer and paint honour it only from 0 up, and the default is -1, so `HSCROLL_GAP` drops the one call that sets it (`widget_set_prop_int`, `0x4f1f4c`) and every label keeps the pass described here. The same function sets `only_parent_focus` in Menu Mode alone, which `WHEEL_MODE` never lets stock be in. V1.36's Albums rows (`localmusic_album_on_prepare_row`) call it where V1.34's set a focus flag outright, the list row's artist line (`only_focus`) and each grid cell's title (`only_parent_focus`), so those four labels would have scrolled once by themselves as the page painted; their calls go through `ringnav_album_label` (`ALBUM_LABELS`), which sets `only_parent_focus` after stock's call. A row of Baidu Netdisk's download list lost its `only_focus` the same way and is left as stock has it: Q2 Muse takes that page's row off Streaming. While a label holds its start it is running, so stock paints it without its ellipsis. An `only_focus` label stock won't restart (unfocused) rests on its start rather than its end, and one started while unfocused holds its start before its first tick stops it, as stock's does. Stock counts a pass's time in its 16 ms ticks, so on the UI loop's idle passes (25 ms) every label runs about a third slower, as it always has.

**The ellipsis.** A label at rest with `ellipses` set ends a long text in stock's `"..."` (`canvas_draw_text_bidi_in_rect`, `0x64cc00`, which `widget_draw_text_in_rect` hands its text): it keeps the characters that fit, each measured alone, while the dots, those kept and the next are under the box's width. On its own a cut just after a word keeps the space, so a title reads `Wicked Garden (2017 ...`, a gap before the dots. `HSCROLL_ELLIPSIS` turns `hscroll_label_on_paint_self`'s one call that asks for the ellipsis (`0x5fc074`) into `jal ringnav_ellipsis_text` (`patch/navigation.c`), which runs stock's count itself and, when the kept characters end in spaces, hands stock a box one pixel wider than the dots and the characters up to the last that isn't a space: those still fit, and the space after them (wider than a pixel) doesn't, so the dots follow the word. A cut inside a word, a text that fits and a scrolling label (the other call, no ellipsis) are stock's as they were.

**Marquee fades** (OLED's `list.marquee.fade`). The text itself fades, onto whatever stands behind it, so no color is guessed: the selection's blue, a destructive answer's red, the page, a cover. When an `hscroll_label`'s text (`HSCROLL_TEXT_W`, 0x94) is wider than its column, the label's box inside its style's `margin_left` and `margin_right` (2 px unless the style says otherwise, as a folder row's does past its icon), `ringnav_paint_bg` calls `marquee_fade_under` (`patch/list_marks.c`) as the label's background paints, before stock draws its text: it copies the `MARQUEE_FADE_PX` (12) columns at each end that needs one out of the canvas's buffer (the lcd_mem's `LCD_OFFLINE_FB`, BGRA8888: what is behind the text), the right end while the offset (`HSCROLL_XOFFSET`, 0x90) is short of the overflow, the left while it is past 0, so a text at rest on its start is crisp. After stock has drawn the text, `ringnav_paint` calls `marquee_fade`, which blends each column back toward the copy by how near the end it stands: behind + (painted - behind) x i / 12, the end column exactly what was behind, which is the text's own coverage times a ramp over the real background, as an offscreen alpha mask would give. Only rows inside the frame's clip are touched (outside it the buffer holds an older frame), and a canvas whose buffer is not 32-bit (none on the Q2's screen) shows the text clipped, unfaded. A stopped label with `ellipses` (`HSCROLL_ELLIPSES`, 0x7c) set keeps stock's ellipsis untouched, so only a scrolling text pays: two copies of at most 12 x 24 pixels and a blend of them a frame. The status row's title is `only_focus` and never focused, so it never scrolls and a long one ends in its ellipsis. The text stays in its own box, which stock clips it to: OLED's boxes end on the right column, a row's before its chevron or value and Now Playing's on `np_grid`'s, so nothing runs under the glass.

**Now Playing's marquee** (OLED: `list.marquee.fade`). The title, artist and album move on one clock (`patch/np_marquee.c`), the way Spotify's do, not each on its own label timer. Every line that overflows its column holds at rest `NPM_HOLD_MS` (2750), then all slide left together until each line's end meets its column's end, hold there `NPM_END_MS` (`MARQUEE_HOLD_MS`, 1500) and go back to rest together: the longest line's overflow at `NPM_PX_S` (35 px a second), linear, and the others stretched to the same time. A line slides only what overflows, never past its end: V1.36's `hscroll_label` paint (`0x5fbd08`) draws a second copy of the text only when `stop_at_begin` (`+0x98`) is set (`0x5fc1a0`), and then at the range plus the gap, not behind the text, so a pass that slid the text its whole width plus a 40 px gap, expecting a copy, left the column empty: measured in the emulator, the title was blank for 1,416 ms of each 9.5 s cycle (frame capture of the title's box). Its ellipsis is cleared, and while it rests on its start or slides, its right end fades (`list_marks.c` `fade_ends`), its left once it has moved. `npm_tick` sets each `xoffset` from the clock, a frame each time the longest line moves a pixel (the timer rounded up to that pixel), and nothing runs while the lines rest, fit, or the page is dark or covered. Stock's own timer never runs for these lines: `ringnav_hscroll_start` hands an owned line's start to `np_marq_reset`, and the page's opening calls it too, which stops the title's timer that stock's page init started before the payload bound the lines. Left running, that timer moved the title through the hold and between the clock's frames (seen in the emulator: offsets 3, 42, 5, 0, 45 within 120 ms), which was the snap back. While a pass runs, `ringnav_sleep`'s idle sleep ends by the next frame (`np_marq_wait`). The bar does the same between the player's seconds: stock sets the slider's value once a second, and `paint_scrubber` runs the fill on from it by the time since it changed (at most a second, so it never goes back), with a one-shot repaint for each pixel (`bar_glide`, at least `GLIDE_MIN_MS` apart) and `np_glide_wait` in the idle sleep. Measured in the emulator: the title moves one pixel a frame about every 28.6 ms with no backward step, and the bar one pixel about every 760 ms on a four-minute track. The emulator's shim sleeps 16 ms in every `FBIO_WAITFORVSYNC`, so each paint there takes about 18 ms; a frame due during another paint (the times' each second) arrives that much late, and paints of 80 to 300 ms every second or two on a loaded host skip a few pixels at once.

The info page's Genre line (`genre_fill`) is a private `hscroll_label` at stock's label's place, in the style `s_scrlabel_white16c`, for every value: stock's plain 225-pixel centered label clips a long value at both ends, and stock rewrites it every 250 ms, which would reset an animation on it, so it stays hidden as the value source. The private label's text is set only when the value changes; a value that fits is centered and never moves. A wider one scrolls on `genre_step`, the album marquee's chained timer and pace (`np_marquee`: `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS`, then `MARQUEE_PX` every `MARQUEE_MS` to the end, `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS` there, back to the start), looping while Now Playing is the top window, lit, on its third slide (`view_info`, value 2). Otherwise the chain ends where it is, costing no timer and no repaint, and the next fill restarts it. AWTK's own scroller stays off (`only_focus`, with no focus); `hscroll_label_set_xoffset` moves the text. Stock measures `text_w` when it paints, so the first fill of a new label sees 0 and a later one starts the hold. A new page's `ringnav_playing` ends the last page's chain, since `np_gone` ignores a page already replaced. ponytail: `np_animating` doesn't count this chain, so after 2 s without input the loop's idle passes stretch a step past `MARQUEE_MS` and the line runs a little slower than the album's; counting it would hold the loop at its fast pace for as long as the line moves.

CUE sheets went through the same `toolsIconvConvert(field, "utf-8", "gbk")` in their parser (the unnamed function after `toolsFreeStSongInfo`, seven fields, `CUE_TEXT`): each call is `jal ringnav_cue_text`, which keeps UTF-8 (lead and continuation bytes, nothing overlong, no surrogate), passes GBK (`gbk_text`, as for tags) to stock's conversion, and reads anything else as Windows-1252, the code page Western rippers write, re-encoded in place and cut at a whole character to 511 bytes (the fields' buffers hold at least 512, and their lines 500).

`test/patch.py` runs the patched `toolsFixId3ErrorCode` on accented Latin-1 fields and on a Chinese one, and `ringnav_cue_text` on UTF-8, Windows-1252, overlong and surrogate input.

## English

Q2 Muse runs in English with nothing Chinese left in stock's interface:

- **Strings:** `en_US.bin`'s About row `system_prove` reads Certification (stock: 技术证明), with the other `LABELS`.
- **UI assets:** stock's `.bin` layouts carry Chinese `text` in about 40 of them, designers' placeholders that stock's code mostly replaces, but some shows in every language: Search's tabs (单曲, 歌手, 专辑, 风格), Now Playing's info labels, Folder's and Streaming's titles, Quick Settings' rows, the factory test pages. The build finds every asset with Chinese text (`CJK`) and `english_ui` gives each such `text` in English (`ENGLISH`, with per-asset choices in `ENGLISH_IN`), checking the round trip and that nothing Chinese is left. Layouts the build already rewrote (`patch_asset`) are given English after that.
- **Keyboard:** stock's T9 keyboard, the one page with Chinese keys, is not in the image ([The keyboard](#the-keyboard)).
- **Streaming:** stock's Baidu Netdisk row (a Chinese cloud drive, signed in to from Baidu's app) is removed (`ringnav_stream` destroys the row whose image is `list_baidu`). That row is the only way into Baidu's pages (`baidu/netdisklogin_page`, `netdiskfolder_page`, `netdiskdownload_page`), and stock sends the sign-in's access token to `pan.baidu.com` over plain HTTP, so the boot (`BOOT_HOOK`, `tools/build.py`) also deletes a sign-in stock saved before, `/mnt/data/baidu_token.conf`; only stock's Baidu code reads it.
- **Tags:** [Tag text](#tag-text).

The Language row is hidden (`ringnav_systemset` hides stock's row 0, its page left whole): stock's other twelve string tables (`strings/*.bin`) are untouched, so they lack the relabelled keys and Q2 Muse's own pages stay English in all of them. A unit already set to another language keeps it until Reset. ponytail: no language is forced at boot; show the row again when translations ship.

## Sorting

Every name-sorted library list (artists, album artists, composers, genres, albums and songs: the `group by … COLLATE NOCASE` queries and `sort_first_alphabet`) is sorted in C, not SQL: `toolsQueryDbTable(…, 1)` and `toolsQueryDbTableAndSort` mode 0 pass `algo_sort_if` one of two comparators, `0x5cd188` or, with the flag at `0xa5011d` clear, the pinyin one `0x5cc870`. The `ORDER BY` queries sort by time, sample rate or id, and folders sort by file name in `toolsLoadDirectory`'s own comparators. Both name comparators `snprintf` the row's `+0x10` name into a local buffer and `bal toolsTrimLeft` on it, falling back to the file name when it is empty. Those four calls (`SORT_TRIMS`) become `jal ringnav_sort_key`, which trims and then drops a leading "The ", "A " or "An " (any case) when a name follows, as Apple does; the record is untouched. "Them", "Anthrax" and a bare "The" keep their place, and equal keys ("The Cure", "Cure") stay as stock's `algo_sort_if` leaves them. Coverflow follows this order. Stock has no A–Z jump index; on a `CTX_LOCAL` page iPod's fast-scroll letter skips the same article, and OLED's [A-Z index](#a-z-index) files rows past it too.

## Name order

A name sort costs the most on a large library's open: `algo_sort_if` with stock's comparator makes about 1.5 n log2 n comparisons, each copying both names into buffers, trimming them (`ringnav_sort_key`) and comparing them character by character. In the emulator, on a synthetic library of 20,103 songs, Library > Songs took 3.2-3.6 s from Center's release to the first paint, 2.4-2.7 s of it the sort (865,614 name copies), and it took that on every open: `load_localclass_list` loads the list again each time. With 10,000 server songs beside them (a server signed in) the sort was 1.9-2.0 s of 2.5 s. `patch/name_order.c` sorts those loads itself and keeps the order. `library_query`, on the UI thread (`ui_thread`, `playback_poll`'s), runs a sorted load (`toolsQueryDbTable` with its sort argument, or `toolsQueryDbTableAndSort` in any mode) as `toolsQueryDbTable` with sort 0: the same `sqlite3_exec` and row callback into the same staging deque, no sort. `name_order` then sorts the deque as stock would have, with the same call: `algo_sort_if(deque_begin, deque_end, comparator)` (`cstl_sort`; libcstl's imports, `cstl_iter` the 28-byte iterator they pass by value), the comparator the one stock picks for that sort and `NAME_SORT_FLAG` (`0xa5011d`): `NAME_CMP` or `NAME_CMP_PINYIN` for the name sort, `FILE_NAME_CMP` or `FILE_NAME_CMP_PINYIN` for mode 1, `PATH_CMP` for mode 2. `tools/build.py` reads each from the `lw`/`addiu` pair that loads it in stock (`NAME_COMPARATORS`, checked against demo's GOT at build time) and writes them into `stock.h`. The same records in the same order through the same comparator come out in the same order, equal names included: the order hash of Songs, Albums and Artists (an FNV-1a over the shown ids) was the same on stock's sort and on this one, `d94a25cf`, `8a3d8075` and `b55baf3d` at 20,103 songs, a third of the titles repeated. A list of 512 records or more (`NO_MIN`; below it the sort is a few milliseconds) is sorted on a thread of its own (`spin_sort`; in place when none starts) while the UI thread waits under the [loading wait](#loading-wait)'s framebuffer overlay (`load_block`), captioned "Sorting songs…", "Sorting albums…" or "Sorting artists…" by the list (`sort_caption`, from `name_order_list`'s class), from 300 ms of the sort on. What it covers is put back once the sort is done, before anything else paints: no frame is drawn while the UI thread waits, as none was while stock's sort ran on it. In the emulator the first Songs open at 20,103 songs showed a spinner from about 1.0 s after Center's release to 2.3 s, and the screen under it came back pixel for pixel. Stock's comparators and `ringnav_sort_key` touch only their own buffers, and the UI thread runs nothing else meanwhile. The sorted list is then kept: each record's id in the sorted order, under a key of the query's final text (after every rewrite: the album-artist one, the music filter, the server union, the Library's scope), its sort (`toolsQueryDbTable`'s argument, or `0x100` and `toolsQueryDbTableAndSort`'s mode) and `NAME_SORT_FLAG`, with the count and a hash of the records as they came, in order (`list_hash`: each id and type, and what the comparator reads, the title and file name, or the path for mode 2; FNV-1a 64). Four slots: a new order takes its key's slot, else the slot of the same Library list (below), else the least recently used. The next load of that key whose records hash the same, in RAM or after a reboot, maps each record's id to its kept place and moves the records there whole (`rec_permute`, song_sort.c's cycle walk, their strings with them) instead of sorting. A changed record, a record more or fewer, or the same records in another order (which could settle equal names otherwise) sort again, as does an id not kept or an id twice. Each slot is also a file on the card, `/mnt/mmc/.q2pod/order0` to `order3` (`keep`, written whole through `blob_io`: a temporary file, synced, renamed over): a 32-byte head (`no_head`: a magic, `Q2POD_VERSION`'s hash, as the comparators run `ringnav_sort_key`, the key, the count, the records' hash and a hash of the ids, and the Library list it is) and the ids. The first sorted load of 512 or more after a boot reads the four heads; a slot's ids are read when a load matches its head, whole or not at all: a short or long file, another magic or version, or ids that do not hash to the head's are dropped, and the load sorts. A Songs open that sorts and keeps writes 80,444 bytes at 20,103 songs, Albums' 8,076. A kept Songs open took 300-330 ms from the load's start to the first paint (from 1.4-1.6 s at the same machine load; 550-610 ms from 2.5 s with the server's songs), Albums' `getAllAlbum` 55-70 ms from 125-135 ms. The first Songs open after a boot, with the order on the card, took 534 ms from the load's start to the first paint (414 ms its query, the card's file read included), against 1,855-2,930 ms sorting on the same build and emulator; Albums' `getAllAlbum` 76 ms against 173-189 ms. A load whose records differ from the kept ones (a scan, a server import or a deletion that changed them) sorts once. ponytail: the card's heads are read once a boot, so a card inserted after the first sorted load is not read until the next boot; the file is written on the UI thread after the sort, 80 KB at 20,000 songs on the card's write speed.

**Sorted ahead.** A load whose records changed sorts at its open, and on a library that is mostly a server's rows that is every first open after a server change: the app's walk writes the catalogue in the server's order, so a song added renumbers every server row after it (`CAT_ID_BASE` plus its place in the file), and Songs, Albums and Artists all hash differently. In the emulator on the owner's catalogue (9,212 songs, 6,179 albums, 2,888 artists, nearly all server rows), such an open sorted for 0.5-1.1 s (Songs), 0.5-1.0 s (Albums) and 0.24-0.41 s (Artists) with the spinner over the Library page, the Q2 about three times that. So the Library's lists are sorted before they are opened. Each slot's head names the list it is (`no_head.cls`: `NO_SONGS`, `NO_ALBUMS` or `NO_ARTISTS`, which `ringnav_localclass` sets through `name_order_list` around its load; 0 for any other load), in RAM and in its file, so a list's new order takes its own slot. `name_order_poll` (every UI loop pass, from `ringnav_sleep`) marks Songs, Albums and Artists due at its first pass with the screen lit after a boot (a dark pass with nothing changed touches no file) and each time `library_gen` moves (a scan's end, a catalogue's load at boot, import or match), opened before or not: the owner's first Songs open after an update (2026-11-24) sorted at its open for 1.8 s, as its kept order was another firmware's and Songs had not been opened in that boot. It loads one a pass once the card is mounted (`card_mounted`), no scan runs (`library_scanning`), no Cover Flow open's step runs (`coverflow_opening`: `staged_into` would give that open up) and the screen is dark or `WARM_IDLE_MS` (3 s) have passed since the last input. `library_warm` (`patch/nav/library_pages.c`) runs the list's query as its open does (`getAllMusic` with the Sort flag, `getAllAlbum`, or `getAllArtist` or `GetAllAlbumArtist` by the artist setting, the server's songs beside the card's) into a deque of its own on the UI thread, step `library warm` for the [UI pass watchdog](#ui-pass-watchdog), with `name_order` told it is that load: it hashes the records and, when no slot holds them, notes their key, hash and count and returns unsorted. Rows stock adds after its sort (the Unknown row) are taken off again, and the records, when they still hash as noted, are sorted on a thread of their own (`warm_sorter`) with stock's call and comparator while the UI runs on. The next pass that finds the sort done keeps it as an open's sort is kept, in the slot of the same list, so the other three slots stay, frees the records and logs `I ui list 1 sorted ahead: 9224 rows in 662 ms`. An open that finds no kept order while that sort runs waits for it under the spinner and looks again, rather than sorting a second time. The order is the one a sort at the open gives: the same query text, the same records in the same order, the same `algo_sort_if` and comparator. In the emulator, with 12 songs added in the middle of the owner's catalogue, the FNV-1a of the shown ids after the sort ahead was the one a sort at the open gave, on this build and on the build before it, for Songs, Albums and Artists. Its cost: the list's query on the UI thread at a quiet moment (a pass of 157-432 ms in the emulator, step `library warm`, as other jobs loaded the machine) and, while its sort runs, a second copy of that one list's records, about 320 bytes a song (2.96 MB at 9,212 songs; fewer for Albums and Artists), freed when the sort is kept; the state is 72 bytes of `.scratch`, the code 2,304 bytes of the payload. ponytail: a list sorted ahead still runs its query and the album split at its open (in the emulator a kept Songs open's pass took 140-350 ms, Albums' 290-650 ms, Artists' 60-230 ms); keeping the records themselves would save that for about 3 MB held all the time.

## Unknown rows

`load_localclass_list` (`0x51357c`) runs the class's query into `tools_pdeq_directory`, `deque_assign`s it to `*p_deque_showlist`, clears the staging deque and returns `deque_size(*p_deque_showlist)`, which its callers take as the row count (Playlists, `0xf00b`, and Baidu's `0xff26` fill their own deque and return its size). For `0xf003`–`0xf006` the query is `getAllAlbum`, `getAllArtist` (`GetAllAlbumArtist` when `g_artist_type == 1`), `getAllComposer` or `getAllGenre`, and each appends an Unknown row (id -1) whenever the list has any rows (`getAllArtist` `0x508034`: type 4, the "Unknown Artist" string), even when every song carries the tag. `ringnav_localclass` runs stock, and when that class's last row has id -1 it runs the query the row's press would run (`class_query`, shared with the [Queue menu](#queue-menu): `getMusicBySonger(NULL)` and its kin, `where songer=""`). With no song it `deque_pop_back`s the row and returns one less. Whether a song exists is all it asks, so `ringnav_localclass` sets `library_first` around that call and `library_query` ends the scoped query with `limit 1`: stock puts one record in the staging deque, not every song without the tag, and SQLite stops at that song. Once a full scan has added `songtable_album_exact` and `songtable_artist` ([Coverflow](#coverflow), Indexes), the album and album-artist checks are an index search; ponytail: the composer and genre checks still scan `songtable` up to the first such song, and all of it when every song has the tag. The Queue menu's query on the same row (`qm_query`) still takes every song. The staging deque is cleared again, as stock leaves it. Coverflow builds its own album list and drops an empty Unknown card the same way (`drop_unknown`), but its query has no limit. A list with no rows at all (no card, an empty library): `empty_class`, from a 0 ms timer so the page that loads it is up, closes that page (`album_page` or `localclass_page` on top with `g_class_type` the list's class) once the window manager has marked it opened (its `stage` property `WINDOW_STAGE_OPENED`, set after the open animation; the close path reads the same at `0x69d218`) with `window_manager_close_window_force`, polling every `EMPTY_POLL_MS` until then or until it stops being on top, then opens the empty state's page (`empty_class`, `feedback.c` `empty_open`: `empty_page`, titled Albums, Artists, Composers or Genres, "No Albums" and so on, or "No SD Card" with no card in). Stock opened the black page, and an empty Albums grid's Return then did nothing until a restart, though Hold Return: Home's `back_to_home` left it; where its `window_close` went was not found, so no Return reaches that page now. A page that is no longer on top, or is another, keeps the toast alone.

## Shuffle

`localmusic_page_init` (`0x535334`) destroys `scroll_view_localmusic`'s children and builds 11 rows (`0x535508`), each button named by its index; the shared row click (`0x53510c`) `atoi`s that name into a switch. Stock's rows, by index (`get_localmusic_showinfo`, `0x50bf30`), are Update Local Music, All Songs, Album, Artist, Genre, Hi-Res, My Fav, Frequent, Recent, Recently Added and Playlist. The hook runs stock through `stock_localmusic_trampoline`, appends its own rows in the same widgets and styles (`list_row`, also Display settings'; `library_into` adds stock's `list_into` chevron), then tags every row with its letter and `widget_restack`s them into the saved order ([Library order](#library-order)), by default the menu review's (2026-11-15): Shuffle (hidden), All Songs, Playlist, Artist, Album, Search, Genre, Years (see [Era](#era)), Ratings (My Fav hidden after it, see [Ratings](#ratings)); Recently Added, Recent, Most Played, Frequent (hidden: Most Played lists the same from every listen), Hi-Res (hidden), Long Songs (hidden); the media rows; Games; Upload Scrobbles (hidden); Update Local Music last. A hidden row is built and kept in its place, as My Fav is, so a later build that shows it again finds it there; nothing on the Q2 shows it. A page that doesn't hold exactly 11 rows is left as stock built it. The added buttons have no name, so stock's click never sees them. The Shuffle row carries the `local_shuffle` icon, a build-added copy of stock's 52 px `playset_playmode`, which iPod pre-sizes to 40 px for Settings, and opens `shuffle_page`, a runtime page (`page_list` and `page_row_detail`, as Most Played's). Its Shuffle Songs row runs `getAllMusic(3)` (`0x5079cc`, no title sort) through `staged`, scoped to music as the Library's Artists and Albums are (`MUSIC_WHERE`, see [Podcasts and Audiobooks](#podcasts-and-audiobooks)), saves shuffle with `config_playmode(2, 1)` (`0x4fe718`, as the play-mode setting does), clears advanced play (`playback_clear`, so stock Shuffle's keep-the-groups rule below doesn't rebuild group shuffle), and folder-plays the copy from `rand_below(n)` as Coverflow does with `toolsRandnum` (`0x5cc71c`). Shuffle Songs is one-shot: `playback_unshuffle` takes the stock mode it replaces (or the one an earlier Shuffle Songs still holds), and when the next other queue loads, `ringnav_load` applies it with `config_playmode` before stock does, ending the advanced shuffle; a mode choice in between (`ringnav_mode`) is kept instead, and a reboot mid-shuffle keeps Shuffle, as the mode is held in RAM only. Its Shuffle Albums and Shuffle Folders rows run `playback_groups(all, 0|1)`. Picks leave the page open for another, and a note under the rows says albums and folders take a moment to shuffle. A resume after reboot therefore reloads the last track's folder, not the library. An empty library shows "Update Local Music first". **Most Played** uses `local_frequentplay`, the icon of stock's Frequent; see [Play counts](#play-counts). **Upload Scrobbles** shows with an account set up; see [Scrobbling](#scrobbling). **Podcasts**, **Audiobooks** and **Videos** show with their folders; see [Podcasts and Audiobooks](#podcasts-and-audiobooks) and [Videos](#videos).

## Library order

The Library's rows go in the order the user last left in Edit Library (`patch/library_edit.c`; the theme's side is [oled-design](oled-design.md#edit-library)). `lr_default` is the one table of the default order: each row's letter (Shuffle `h`, Artists `a` and so on, its comment lists them; `S` Search and `G` Games are gone since 2026-11-19, so an order holding them loads without them, and Update Local Music `u` is never listed, `lr_retire`), in the order the rows take with nothing saved. `ringnav_localmusic` (`patch/home.c`) builds every row, stock's and the payload's, tags each with its letter (`lr_put`, the `_lr_code` property) and restacks them in the saved order (`lr_apply`); Home's Library list, built by the same function, follows. The order is `/mnt/data/ringnav-library-order`: the letters in order, each led by `+` or `-` once the user has shown or hidden that row (below), NUL-ended in 64 bytes, written whole through `blob_io` (a `.tmp` beside it, `fsync`ed, renamed over it), so a power cut leaves the old order or the new one, never half of either; a missing or short file reads as nothing saved. `lr_resolve` reads it against `lr_default`: a letter it doesn't know, or one it has already seen, is dropped, and every row it doesn't name, one a later firmware adds, goes in at its default place, straight after the nearest row before it in `lr_default` that the saved order has (first if none), so new rows in a run keep their default order and the user's order is kept. A change to the default order is a change to `lr_default` alone; a new row takes a new letter, never one used before. Saving (`lr_save`) reads the shown rows' letters in the view's order and puts them in the places those rows held in the saved order (`lr_merge`): a row the editor doesn't list (My Fav and Frequent, always; Search or a media row when absent) is neither shown nor moved, and keeps its place.

**Which rows show.** Each row's visibility is Auto, Shown or Hidden. Auto, no mark in the file, leaves it to the row's own rule, its `_lr_auto` property: shown (`lr_put`'s default), hidden until the user shows it (`lr_auto_hide`: Shuffle, Hi-Res, Long Songs and Upload Scrobbles, the menu review's), or never listed (`lr_retire`: My Fav and Frequent, which Ratings and Most Played replace). Shown (`+`) and Hidden (`-`) are the user's and stick whatever the rule says (`lr_shows`); Home's Settings is locked shown, a mark or none. `lr_resolve_in` reads the marks into one byte a row by its place in the default order, a mark before a letter it doesn't know going with that letter; a firmware from before the marks reads them as unknown letters and drops them, so its order is kept. `lr_apply` shows each tagged row as its mark and rule say. In the editor every row with a rule shows, a hidden one's text in Text Tertiary (`lr_edit_dim`, from `ringnav_style_color`), and Play/Pause's release (`lr_edit_key`; not a release that ends a hold, `play_hold_released`, and the hold itself does nothing there, `ringnav_keylong`) or a tap in the first `LR_VIS_ZONE` (52) columns (`lr_edit_click`, with the press's x from `lr_edit_touch`, which starts no hold there) flips the selected row from how it shows now to the other, the user's from then on (`lr_toggle`), and saves. Leaving the editor (`lr_leave`, `lr_show`) hides the hidden rows again and keeps the selection on its row, or the next one shown if it went. Each row's words move right of its circle while the editor is open (`lr_edit_labels`: to x 52 on screen, their right end kept, and back after).

**Home.** Home's main list (`tools/ipod.py` `HOME_ROWS`) has its own order and visibility, `/mnt/data/ringnav-home-order` against `lr_home` (`pltgfcqS`: Now Playing, Library, Radio, Games, Folders, Cover Flow, Search, Settings; until 2026-11-19 `s`, Streaming, stood where `g` does: an older order loads without it and its marks, and Games, then on 2026-11-20 Radio (`t`), goes in after the row before it by the rule above), its rows tagged by their names when Home is made (`lr_home_tag`, from `coverflow_home`). `coverflow_home_layout` calls `lr_home_apply` where it used to place Now Playing alone: the rows in the saved order, each shown as its mark and rule say, Now Playing only while something is loaded (its Shown cannot show it with nothing to play), and the hidden rows restacked last, as the list's layout keeps a hidden row's slot. Folders' rule (`home_folders`, `patch/home.c`) is the empty Folders page's test: stock's listing of the card's root (`toolsLoadDirectory` of `/mnt/mmc`, which leaves out what stock hides) holds a row. It is read again only when `/tmp/mmc_add` or the root's `st_dev` and `st_mtime` change, never during a library scan (which fills the same deque), and `coverflow_home_np` (each bar paint) asks only while Home is on top, laying Home out again when the answer changes; the card and its root are looked at again when they may have changed, or at once when a library scan has rewritten the library (`library_gen`), not on every paint. <a id="card-watch"></a>What may have changed comes from `patch/card_watch.c`: a thread, started on the first look, waits in `poll()` on an inotify descriptor watching the card's root for entries made, removed or moved (`CW_MASK`, folders only), and on `/proc/mounts`, which the kernel marks with `POLLPRI` whenever anything is mounted or unmounted (the card put in, taken out, lent to USB storage and back; the file is opened again after each mark). Each time it sets the watch again, so a new mount is watched, and only then counts a change (`card_watch_gen`). A new card or a new root folder shows on the next paint; with nothing changing the thread sleeps and nothing is looked at. Without inotify, `/proc/mounts` or the thread the generation is 0 and the caches look again every `CARD_RECHECK_MS` (5 s), as `logo_poll`'s mount edge does. Each row that comes or goes calls `home_keep` with its place among the shown rows, which keeps the selected row selected (`COUNT` moved with it, so the list's load doesn't start the selection over) and the rows in view, as Now Playing's coming and going always did. Edit Home is Edit Library on that list: `lr_view_of` takes Home's main list from `coverflow_home_edit_view` (Home on top, its main list shown), the status row reads Edit Home (`bar_title_sync`), `paint_chevrons` leaves the list's chevrons to the grips (`lr_edit_list`), and while it is open `ipod_home` answers Full for Split, so the list spans the screen under the hint and the art is hidden; Settings' circle is locked. Its lift's abort goes to the row's last child, Home's tap image (the Library's button is its only one).

**Edit Library**: on `localmusic_page`, Center's press (`ringnav_keydown` calls `lr_edit_keydown`) starts a `LR_HOLD_MS` (550 ms) timer; released sooner, the press is a row's click as before. When it goes off, Edit Library starts (or, in it, saves and ends), stock's own Center hold timer (`st.centre_hold`, Shut Down? at 1000 ms) is removed, and the release is taken (`lr_edit_key`, in `ringnav` before stock's key-up), with stock's wheel lockout (`KEY_LOCKOUT`) cleared so the wheel moves at once. In it the status row reads Edit Library (`bar_title_of` with `lr_edit_title`, refreshed with `title_gone` and `bar_title_sync`), `paint_into` draws no chevron on a Library row (`lr_edit_row`), and `lr_edit_paint` draws the rest (`list_marks.c` `grip_mark`, `check_circle`, `lift_card_paint`), clipped in screen coordinates within the paint's own clip (`clip_within`). From the rows' view's paint, before the list's fades go over it (`row_paint.c` `list_fade`, `home.c` `home_fades`), each row's grip where its chevron was and its check circle at its left, in the view's whole box, so a scrolled list's top row and the rows past its end fade with their marks; from the page's border paint, after everything, the hint's band (the ground from `LR_FOOT`), the hint, and the lifted row's card over all of it. The card is the selection bar's box (`LR_CARD_X`, 16 px in each side), `LR_LIFT` (108%) of the row's height about its middle, and its circle, grip and words (Inter Medium at the row's 20 px, from the label's own `LR_LABEL_PAD` margin) are drawn where the row's own stand, so a lift changes the row's look and moves nothing (the user, 2026-11-16, from the device: the card had grown 8% to x 2 to 372, its marks and words moving out with it). While the editor is open its list ends `LR_ROOM` (a row, 32 px) higher than the set's list end, so the hint sits under the rows with the room a list has above the screen's foot: `lr_edit_room` takes it off `navigation.c` `sel_height` (where a selected row stops), `list_fade`'s end and `home_rest` (Home's rows at rest: six in Edit Home, which then scrolls), and `lr_edit_foot` moves the fades' ground from y 316 to `LR_FOOT` (284), the band's top, as far below the raised end as 316 is below 282. Center lifts the selected row (`SEL`, its place among the shown rows) and puts it down again, saving; a tick of the wheel while one is lifted moves it a place (`lr_move`: restacked before the row it passes, which `widget_layout` lays out; it stops at either end) and selects it, clicking as a row change does when the press was silenced; Return while one is lifted restacks it at the child index it had when lifted, which puts it back exactly, as only it moved; Return otherwise saves and ends. A held Return's release (its latch set) is stock's: it leaves for Home, and the page's close ends Edit Library. The rows a moved row passes slide over `LR_SLIDE_MS` (150 ms, cubic out, a frame every `LR_STEP_MS`): `lr_place` notes where each row shows, restacks and lays out, then puts each back where it showed and moves its `W_Y` towards its new place each frame; the moved row itself goes at once.

**Touch.** `ringnav_touch` hands a press on the Library page under OLED to `lr_edit_touch` after stock's. On a row it starts the same timer, which a move past `LR_SLOP` (8 px) or a lift stops (the page's move-before, up-before and abort, bound once a page, `lr_event`); when it goes off, Edit Library starts if it hasn't and the finger takes the row (`lr_grab`). In Edit Library a press in the last `LR_GRIP_ZONE` (64) columns, on the grips, takes its row at once. Taking a row at a hold's end dispatches `EVT_POINTER_ABORT` through the page so the rows let go of the press, as the A-Z index does, and ends the pull to search the press began (`pull_cancel`); a press on a grip is taken before stock hands the press to the rows (`ringnav_touch` runs first), so the lift sends the abort to that row's button alone (`stock_dispatch_trampoline`): an abort through the page also reaches the scroll view, which then glides back to the offset it was pressed at, undoing the drag's edge scroll (seen in the emulator: its animator set straight after the abort, the list back at its top); from then the page's moves and lift stop at `lr_event` (`STOP`), and `ringnav_touch` passes moves straight to stock while `lr_edit_dragging`. `widget_to_local` on the view gives its content's coordinates, its scroll counted. The row's top follows the finger, kept within the list's box on the screen (never over the status row or the hint) and within the rows, and it takes the place its middle is over; within `LR_EDGE` (16) px of the list's top or bottom (the view's top to the set's list end) the list scrolls `LR_SCROLL_PX` (8) every `LR_SCROLL_MS` (40) while the finger stays. The lift slides the row into its place and saves. A tap in Edit Library selects its row and opens nothing (`lr_edit_click`, in `ringnav_dispatch`'s click observer).

## Coverflow depth

The shelf and caption values below are the theme's `cfs` (see Themes). Coverflow draws its covers in software, after Rockbox PictureFlow's renderer: the selected cover faces the viewer at its native 160 pixels, its neighbours are turned inward, pushed back and dimmed, and each has a reflection. Where the side covers stand is the iPod preset of the Cover Flow Parameter Lab in [#329](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/issues/329) (spghetti), in OLED: the lab's selected cover is 1000 units wide and the Q2's 160 px, so its numbers times 0.16, with the selected cover's pull forward (`front`) taken off the camera's distance and added to the side covers' depth, since the Q2's selected cover is the plane at its native size. `eye` (1650 - 50) × 0.16 = 256, `tilt` 90, `x1` 800 × 0.16 = 128, `xs` 220 × 0.16 = 35, `z1` (430 + 50) × 0.16 = 77, `zs` 0, and `horizon` 64: the lab's vanishing point is 34 px under the middle of its 250 px cover, 63.6% down it. Until 1.8.1 the side covers turned 60 degrees (`eye` 300, `x1` 112, `xs` 48, `z1` 90, `zs` 20, `horizon` 50). `patch/coverflow.c` owns the drawing; the stock `slide_menu` stays the navigation and animation controller, so the wheel (one retargeted animator, 200 ms or 120 ms fast, reversal), wrapping, center, the saved album and track positions all work as before. Touch is the payload's own (below): the `slide_menu` stays insensitive, so stock's drag and throw never run. Tunables are `coverflow.shelf` in OLED's `theme.xml` (the shelf's geometry and the thumb) and `CF_*` in `patch/offsets.inc`; adjust them together.

**Layout.** With depth the `slide_menu` spans the frame, 375 × `view_h` (`CF_VIEW_W`; `coverflow.shelf.view_h`, 220 by default as `CF_VIEW_H`, `CF_TOP` + 160 + `CF_REFLECT` and a row; OLED's `coverflow.shelf.reflect_top` is 0, so each reflection is the page's own color and none shows, and its caption, at `text_y` 173, has the artist's box `artist_y` 27 px under the album's, baselines 24 px apart and the artist's on y 277 on screen, so its tails (p, y, g, q) end on the lists' end, y 282) at the top of the page, so every animator step invalidates all of it. Its items stay `h` square (`view_h`), and `slide_menu_set_spacer` (a store at `+0x84` and an invalidate) sets the spacer to `CF_STRIDE - view_h`, so the stride that stock scroll, completion and ringnav's wheel steps use (item width plus spacer) is `CF_STRIDE` (110 px). The children are `image` widgets with no image, so stock paints nothing under the frame, and there are only `CF_POOL` (8) of them, whatever the library: `SLIDE_INDEX` is the album's index of `cf.count` (the albums and cards, `slide_count`), and child `j` stands for the album nearest the centre that is `j` modulo the pool (`slide_child_index`), which is what Centre's click on the centre child (`pick_child`) and navigation's row ids (`lists.c` `load`) read. Stock reads the children only through `slide_menu_fix_index` (`0x606184`, the index modulo the children), and its `slide_menu_set_value` (`0x6080b8`) stores the index as given; only its scroll end, `slide_menu_on_scroll_done` (`0x6064e4`), wraps the index by the children, so a glide on Cover Flow's covers ends in `home_done` (`nav/home_carousel.c`) with the same commit, `index - round(offset / stride)`, round the albums. One child per album cost a 6,000-album open 22-25 ms to make them and 25-40 ms more to its first paint (stock's layout passes every child, and navigation read up to `MAX_ENTRIES`, 512, of them each tick). The flat fallback (no memory for the frame) keeps one child per album, each drawn by stock; ponytail: a pool there would rebind the images round the visual centre mid-glide. The album and artist captions sit under the covers at `CF_TEXT_Y`, over the reflections' faint tail, and follow the center cover: when the album `coverflow_paint` drew in the middle changes, a zero-delay timer (`retitle`, never text set inside the paint) names it, once per change; `EVT_VALUE_CHANGED`, when a move commits, writes them again.

**Position.** `ringnav_paint`, the border hook, calls `coverflow_paint` for every widget after stock has painted it; only Coverflow's `slide_menu` on the covers screen draws. The visual position is the index less the live offset over the stride (stock completion commits `index - offset / stride`): center album `c` and `frac`, 16.16, in `[-1/2, 1/2)`. Every cover's rotation, place, depth, brightness and reflection come from that one continuous value, so an incoming side cover unfolds into the center as the outgoing one turns away.

**Projection.** All integer (the stock build is `-mfp64`, and integer arithmetic is also cheaper here). A cover `t` albums from the position gets a rotation that grows linearly to `tilt` at one album (a 17-entry sine table to `CF_ANGLE`, 60 degrees, and a second to 90 for any other tilt, OLED's among them), a center `x` that reaches `x1` then steps `xs` per album, a depth that reaches `z1` then `zs` per album, and a brightness of 256 at the center, `CF_BRIGHT1` (75%) one out, `CF_BRIGHT2` (50%) two out, and 0 three out unless `third`, so covers fade in and out at the edge of reach. A theme can turn its covers another way: `coverflow.shelf.tilt` other than 60 reads a second table, 0 to 90 degrees, stepped by the same interpolation. `horizon` puts the shared horizon that percentage down the cover (50 by default), and `third` (`CF_THIRD`, on in OLED) keeps every cover from the second out at `bright2`. Still (nothing moving: no thumb on the covers, no glide or step animating, no finger on them; `coverflow_paint` passes it, `cf_still`), the shelf draws the seven it always has, the same bytes. Moving, it draws all of the ring (`shelf_draws`), so the cover coming in at either edge is whole from its first pixel, its reflection too. A move's frame on a whole album is a moving one, and the frame is drawn again when the covers stop; a tap hits only the covers the frame on the screen draws (`coverflow_hit`, `fx_still`). The fold lands on the still shelf: its covers past the third out fade to nothing on the fold's ease, as they always have. With no thumb the ring is seven, and the third cover out is gone by half a step past it, so the ring's reach ends it without a pop (with `third` 0 it vanished as the covers came to rest). `swing` changes only the path between center and first slot. At 0 `x` is quadratic up to one album, so the two covers turning mid-step keep clear of each other on a 60 degree shelf; at 2, OLED's, it goes straight out as the cover turns, as the lab's does. 1 is for a near edge that would otherwise balloon on a short eye (not OLED's): depth follows the sine of the turn, less `lift` px at most mid-way, and the near edge's screen x is two parabolas meeting flat at 45% of the way, 3 px past its rest place (`cf_rest16`, with the sine at one album `cf_s1`, cached by `cf_restyle`), with `xc` derived from it, so the cover swings on its outer edge with no corner in the path. Every other reader (`unproject`, `coverflow_hit`, the reflection) reads the pose, and at whole albums the pose is the one without it. Left covers mirror right ones about the center line (between columns 186 and 187). For each screen column the renderer inverts the perspective (eye `eye` px away) to the cover column under it and the cover's projected height there, then steps down the texture column, top and bottom rows weighted by coverage. Only those two rows can step off the art, so only they clamp the texture row; at full brightness (the center cover) a texel goes in unshaded. At rest the selected cover is its texture pixel for pixel. Below each cover its reflection is the column mirrored, `CF_REFLECT` rows at native size scaled by perspective, from `CF_REFLECT_TOP` of its brightness down to nothing: no blur or glow. By default it is 46 rows from 90/256 (35%); OLED's `reflect_top` 0 starts it at none, so no reflection shows.

**Compositing.** The frame is drawn nearest cover first: each pixel's alpha byte holds the coverage so far and every layer fills only what is left, which composites as drawing back to front would, and per column a span of rows known to be opaque is skipped outright, so hidden parts of side covers cost nothing. A last pass makes every pixel opaque over black. The hit test walks the same order, nearest first, over cover bodies only.

**Frame and textures.** One `bitmap_create_ex(375, view_h, 1500, 3)` (`coverflow.shelf.view_h`, 220 by default; BGRA8888, the screen's format; `bitmap_t` is 0x48 bytes, flags `u16 @0xc`, format `u16 @0xe`, buffer `@0x14`) is created with the covers and marked `BITMAP_FLAG_OPAQUE` (bit 0, as `bitmap_init_from_rgba` sets it for opaque images); `bitmap_lock_buffer_for_write`/`bitmap_unlock_buffer` bracket each render and `canvas_draw_image(canvas, bitmap, src, dst)` (`0x6487c4`, `dst` relative to the canvas origin, which is the `slide_menu`'s) draws it 1:1. Stock's `lcd_mem_draw_image` (`0x6a6884`) copies an image whose format is the lcd's, opaque, unscaled, under a global alpha of at least 250, with `image_copy` (`0x688f18`: a `memcpy` a row; the lcd is turned without fast portrait, so not `image_rotate_ex`), and blends any other with `image_blend`, about 39 instructions a pixel against 3 (`opaque_frame`). The renderer works in the textures' order (RGBA8888, red low) and its last pass, which makes every pixel opaque, swaps R and B; the alpha stays `0xff`, as stock's later blends and Night Shift read it from the screen. It is re-rendered only when the position or a texture changes; a repaint in place only draws. Textures come from the existing JPEG cache: `widget_load_image`, `bitmap_lock_buffer_for_read` and `bitmap_unlock_buffer` read the decoded image (the stock loader, `stb_load_image` called with RGBA8888 for both formats at `0x69467c`, never premultiplies), fitted whole and centered (a non-square cover between black bars), sampled to 160 × 160 over black into the payload's own buffer, and the load is dropped at once with `widget_unload_image`, as stock cover rows do; the image manager's copy is only read. `fx_base()` slots hold the covers nearest the position, seven (`CF_RING`, within three albums) or 15 under a thumb theme (`CF_WIDE`, **Textures.** below); as movement crosses an album the one leaving is dropped and the one entering is decoded. A small library repeats round the ring as the `slide_menu` wraps, each album decoded once. Missing art and a card (an artist's All albums, the rated albums' Sort) use `default_album_flow`, a 160px copy of Home's disc resized with Lanczos at build time and decoded 1:1. Both are decoded once and left in the manager's cache as theme images. iPod clips each cover column to rounded corners at the Now Playing radius ratio (12/166), including the mirrored bottom in its reflection; the insets are computed once, with no alpha processing in the pixel loop. The frame and the textures (`fx_base()`'s and the placeholder: 16 under a thumb theme, every built-in's, about 1.6 MB) are allocated together when the covers are built; if either fails, Coverflow keeps the flat stock covers exactly as before. Closing the page destroys the frame and frees the textures.

**iPod artwork.** Home's 290px disc is the master placeholder for album rows, Now Playing, the full-screen art and AirPlay, pre-sized at build time to each stock asset's dimensions, keeping the disc's transparent corners so a selected row's bar shows through them (Now Playing's to the 166px art it fills; the full-screen `default_bigcover` to its `BC_ART` square, the centered art clear of the glass). The artist-person icon keeps its stock image. Library thumbnails (`file:///mnt/mmc/.sldp/`) get rounded alpha at radius min(width, height) × 12/166 in `ringnav_image_add`, before the image manager caches them. The hook clears the cached opacity flag and keeps straight RGB, so stock can blend the corners over wallpaper or selection panels. Alpha is clamped to arc coverage, making reuse idempotent. Stock's temporary playing covers (`coverpic.jpg`, `externpic.jpg`, `album_tidal.jpg` in `/tmp`) are not: Now Playing, Spotify and the full-screen art round them after scaling, in `paint_cover`; Home's Split art is cropped past its corners.

<a id="coverflow-touch"></a>**Touch.** The covers' view takes `EVT_POINTER_DOWN`, and the page (`open_page`) the move, the release and `EVT_POINTER_ABORT`, so a release off the covers still ends the touch (`touch`); the payload moves `SLIDE_OFFSET` itself and finishes through `carousel_glide` (`patch/navigation.c`), the wheel's one retargeted animator split out of `home_step`, with the run's easing set on the animator (`ANIM_EASING`, `+0x38`: `widget_animator_init` stores `easing_get(type)` there, so a reused animator would keep its first). Every finish commits through stock's completion as a wheel step does. On an album's tracks the view is hidden and made insensitive: stock's hit test (`widget_find_target_default`, `0x67d21c`) checks only the enable and sensitive bits (`+0x24` mask 9), not visibility, so a hidden covers' view over the list would take its taps and swipes.

- **Drag.** A move past `CF_SLOP` (8 px) more sideways than up or down is the covers'; one more up or down leaves the touch to stock (the Quick Settings pull-down). From there the offset follows the finger, one album per `CF_DRAG_PX` (90 px, about the center cover's own travel on screen), starting where it passed the slop so nothing jumps. An artist's albums give past an end as iOS's rubber band, `x · 0.55 / (1 + x · 0.55 / D)` with `D` two fifths of a stride, so the center never passes half a cover, where `visual` would wrap to the other end. A touch catching the band (or a wheel bounce) starts from its inverse (`unbound`), so the shelf doesn't jump.
- **Release.** The finger's speed is taken over its last 100 ms of moves, by each event's post time (`EVENT_TIME`; moves queued behind a frame are dispatched together) (0 if it rested `CF_STILL_MS`, 60 ms, before lifting; at most `CF_VMAX`, 6000 px/s, so a burst of queued moves can't throw the shelf). The covers glide to the whole cover that speed reaches in `CF_PROJECT_MS` (400 ms), and a flick of at least `CF_FLICK` (250 px/s) never settles back against its direction. The glide is `cubic_out` (`EASE_CUBIC_OUT`, AWTK's `easing_type_t` 5) for `3 d / v` whenever the goal lies ahead of the finger's motion, so it starts at the finger's speed and decelerates, between `CF_SETTLE_MS` (280 ms, also a still release or one that settles back) and `CF_GLIDE_MAX` (1.4 s); an artist's ends clamp it.
- **Tap.** A touch that never passed the slop hit-tests the drawn frame (`coverflow_hit`): the frontmost cover body under the finger, nearest first as drawn, rounded corners (`cf_inset`, where the arc crosses each texel column's middle) and reflections left out, and no cover under a quarter bright. The center cover at rest opens, as Center's click; a side cover glides to the center with the wheel's easing in `CF_TAP_MS` (320 ms). The flat fallback opens its center cover only.
- **Catch.** A touch while the covers move pauses the animator where they are. Lifting without a drag settles on the nearest cover and opens nothing; a drag carries on from there. A down while a touch is still open (a release the input queue dropped), or any key with the window manager no longer pressed (`coverflow_lost_touch`, in `ringnav`), ends the old one first, so Center opens the cover the shelf settles on; a touch ending after Center changed the screen still settles the covers on a whole one, and covers built anew drop it.

ponytail: no MIPS run of the gesture: `test/coverflow.py` drives the C on the host (`-m32`), and `test/patch.py` checks the MIPS renderer byte for byte. The drag scale, reach and glide lengths are `CF_*` in `patch/offsets.inc`, set by eye.
