**Checks.** `test/coverflow.py` builds the renderer on the host and checks the selected cover pixel for pixel, that nothing is drawn outside the frame, mirror symmetry at rest and mid-turn, brightness one and two out, the reflection's rows and fade, that a small step changes little (including where the center album changes hands), the texture window's loads and releases, the center click, touch (the hit test against every drawn pixel at eight positions, taps, drags, flicks, a flick dispatched in one batch, a resting release, a vertical move, a catch and a dropped release), going by letters (`thumb_letters_held`: letters held through a slow turn, a still thumb and a turn back; `letters_entry` and `enter_frames`: the entry, with no cover turning and no hole opening; `held_row`: the held row's geometry, the formed row's, with no cover turning; `entry_handover`: no art change and no stop across the first letter; `fold_flow` and `fold_frames`: the fold's landing, its frames and paint order; `lift_handoff`: the lift's hand-off at `fold_near`; `fold_clearance`: every two covers kept clear), the arch (`arch`: its poses in every built-in theme, none nearer the eye than the side covers, and the follower forming it only at speed, with Fast Navigation off), one- and two-album libraries, missing art, Refresh, return from tracks and the allocation-failure fallback; `--captures DIR` writes the renderer's frames at rest and a quarter, half and three-quarter turn as PNGs. `test/patch.py` runs the MIPS payload's renderer against the host build byte for byte, and the page's paint, center click and fallback, and prints the payload's instructions per frame (about 3.5 million for a frame mid-turn under the mocks): a relative measure, not a frame time.

## Coverflow step

Cover Flow's two steps may name `easing="follow"` (`EASE_FOLLOW`, one past AWTK's 24 names), and `tools/theme.py` refuses it on any other kind: `easing_get` has no such id and a window's `anim_hint` no such name. Under it the row's `ms` is a time constant, 81 ms, and the run's length comes from the distance. Other themes, the carousel and touch's release and tap keep their easings.

**The curve.** A critically damped follow of the goal: a tick only moves the goal, so the speed carries on through it, and nothing overshoots. Over `s` time constants a run `d` px long leaves `(d + (d - v tau) s) e^-s` to go, `v` being the speed it started with. The share is `1 - (1 + a s) e^-s`, with `a = 1 - v tau / d`, floored at 0 for a goal right ahead of a cover too fast to stop for it. `coverflow_follow_aim` takes the speed from the last run at `ANIM_ELAPSED`, only when the animator's easing is still the follow (a touch's glide gives a start from rest), and returns the run's ms, until within half a px of the goal.

**The animator stays.** `carousel_glide` sets `ANIM_EASING` to `coverflow_follow` after `scroll_create`, which gets `linear`, so `ANIM_X_TO`, `EVT_ANIM_END` and `home_done` work as for any step. `widget_animator_time_elapse` (`0x679684`) calls the easing with `$25` set, `k` in `$f12` clamped to 1, and passes `$f0` to the update (`+0x3c`, `0x6954e0`), which writes `from + (to - from) p` truncated to whole px. That's AWTK's `float_t` as a plain single in this `-mfp64` build, so the easing is a float C function. It returns exactly 1 at `k` 1, so the truncated offset's last move is one whole px at most.

**The pose.** `coverflow.shelf.eye_turn` (0 in every built-in theme since the shelf became #329's) draws the eye back mid-turn by `eye_turn (1 - t^4)` px, in `pose()`, kept per cover in `pose_t.eye` for `project()`, `unproject()` and so `coverflow_hit`. Depth moves with it, which holds the near edge's place and height and lengthens the far edge. At `t` 0 and 1 no pixel moves, so rest poses are the same bytes.

**Frame gaps (`--dev`).** Each painted frame of a run goes to a ring in RAM, and at the first paint after the run to `/tmp/q2-cf-gaps.log`, if `/tmp/q2-cf-gaps.on` exists (off by default). `python3 tools/q2remote.py sh 'touch /tmp/q2-cf-gaps.on'`, turn the wheel, then `sh 'cat /tmp/q2-cf-gaps.log'`. Each run is a `== run` line, then a row a frame, all in ms: `gap`, since the frame before (a run's first row counts from the last run); `decode`, spent in `fx_ring` loading textures; `render`, spent in `coverflow_render`; then `offset`, the px when it was painted. The last row is the frame after commit. The crossing is where `offset` passes half a stride: a `decode` near that row's `gap`, with `gap` well over its neighbours, says the decode stalls the step. A big `gap` on the last row alone points at the commit.

## Coverflow thumb

OLED's covers are held by the thumb: `coverflow.shelf.thumb` is 1 and every number below is an attribute of that element, so retuning on the wheel needs no C change. The carousel isn't the covers' page, so `coverflow_wheel_poll` never takes the wheel there and it stays on ticks and the animator, as it does on the covers' page whenever the thumb isn't shown (a finger on the screen, the page sliding). A theme with `thumb` 0 is on ticks throughout, letters after `CF_FIRST_MS`.

**The wheel.** `thumb_poll` (`ringnav_sleep`, before `lyric_poll`) calls `coverflow_wheel_poll`. The wheel is raw only with the covers' page on top, not animating, `usable()` and no finger on the screen, and that's decided afresh each pass, so no way off the page can leave `wheel_raw` set. It's `WHEEL_THUMB` (2), not the `WHEEL_RAW` (1) of the lyrics and Vortex, for one reason below; each of the two pollers gives the wheel back only if the value is still its own, so neither clobbers the other's in the pass the wheel changes hands. A still thumb sends no frames, for seconds, so a gap in frames is never a lift: the thumb is `wheel_held`. `contact_ms` debounces it each way: a shorter contact is ignored with its travel, and a shorter lift changes nothing. A press only anchors (`wheel_sample`). Shake of `dead` units moves nothing. If a lift is lost (a known case: a thumb on the ring and a screen tap), `hold_ms` covers it.

**The goal.** The covers move as the lists do ([Wheel acceleration](#wheel-acceleration)). `th_turn` scales the travel into ticks by Wheel Sensitivity (`ticks_turn` a turn at 50%, `wheel_pct()`), counted exactly in `th.tick_acc` (units times `ticks_turn` times the percentage, 10,000 a tick), and each whole tick moves the goal as many albums as `wheel_accel` answers for it: one for a slow or new turn, 2 once a run of ticks no more than `WA_RUN_MS` (140 ms) apart has gone on `WA_FIRST_MS` (300), one more each `WA_RAMP_MS` (200), at most `WA_MAX_ROWS` (8) a tick; a slower tick inside the run keeps its step, a pause past `WA_RUN_MS` or a turn back starts at one again. The covers follow the goal through every album between (the position, below). Part of a tick carries over, rests included, so a slow crawl of a unit a pass still moves an album each tick's worth. Cover Flow never jumps by letter: `wheel_accel` is given a length of 0, under `WA_LETTER_ROWS`. Turning back drops the goal to within `back` of the position. Home's carousel and the covers on ticks (no thumb: a finger on the screen, the page sliding) take the same steps (`home_step`, `input.c`'s own `wheel_accel_t`), a bounded row stopping on its end.

**No letters.** Neither the thumb nor the ticks go by letters, and no letter shows over the covers (the user, 2026-11-19: momentum through every cover). ponytail: what drew and fed letters stays compiled with nothing to drive it: the entry, the held row and the fold (`coverflow_letters.c`), the letters' windows in `fx_window`, the half copies and their loader (below), Year's groups (`lettered`, `coverflow_jump`, `coverflow_letter_next`), the letter over the covers (`coverflow_letter`) and their theme attributes (`jump_*`, `big_jump_*`, `enter_albums`, `slide_ms`, `fold_near`, `ticks_album`, `top_speed`); removing them, and deciding what is left of Fast Navigation, is a cleanup of its own.

**The arch.** With Fast Navigation off the covers at speed bend in to the middle, as the lab's do (`th_arch`, `arch_pose`). `th.arch` goes from 0 to 1 as the covers' own speed goes from `arch_at` to `arch_full` albums a second (8 to 16), times how far past one album the goal is ahead of them, up to two: a step of one album never forms it, and it is gone as the covers land. It follows that by `arch_in` ms rising (100) and `arch_out` falling (62). Formed, every cover within `arch_span` (5 albums) of the middle is at the side covers' depth, the middle one too, so none swings towards the eye, and is turned `tilt` × smoothstep of its share of the span instead of standing at `tilt` from the first out; partly formed, depth and turn are that far between the shelf's and the arch's. Each cover's place across and its brightness stay the shelf's, the covers are drawn nearest the middle first as at rest, and at `th.arch` 0 the pose is `pose()`'s to the byte. There is no facing point ahead of the covers (`lead` stays 0), so the texture window stays round the middle and none of the row below is drawn. The covers follow the wheel's goal by one time constant throughout, `arch_tau` (56 ms: the lab's spring, stiffness 18 a second), in place of `track`, `snap` and `spin`. ponytail: so a slow step settles in about 0.6 s instead of 0.3 s, and touch, which waits for the follower to stop (`th.on`), is ignored that long after a wheel step; `arch_tau` only while the covers move or arch would undo that. The lab's thresholds are 15 and 30 covers a second, which its key repeat reaches; the wheel tops out at `top_speed` 20, where the goal is 2 `arch_tau` `top_speed` = 2.2 albums ahead, so 8 and 16 form the arch between 9 and 18 albums a second: none at a turn a second, nine tenths of it at two. `arch_span` 0 leaves a theme the row at speed. With Fast Navigation on there is no arch: its entry and held row come in from the row at speed, with the follower that row was tuned on.

**The position** follows the goal, critically damped and exact over the real elapsed ms of the pass, so a slow frame costs no accuracy and speed stays continuous. With no arch its time constant is `max(base, min(tau, rest))`: `base` is `track` blending to `spin` with that smoothstep (`snap` with no thumb), `rest` is `snap` to `spin` by `smoothstep(left / far_left)`. Only the thumb raises it, which removes a snap: lag raising it would add lag, and the row would jump out at one speed. A detent of `detent (1 - smoothstep)` draws the target towards albums, thumb down only.

**Settling.** A lift, the hold's timeout, or no tick for `stop_ms` with more than `stop_left` left sends the goal to the caption's album, so a stop from speed lands on what's named, with speed only falling. Otherwise a slow cover stays part-way while it's held. `th_commit` ends it through `carousel_glide`'s immediate move, so `EVT_VALUE_CHANGED` and `changed()` run as for any step. The position and goal are albums from `SLIDE_INDEX`, so once the position is `TH_REBASE` (64) albums out, `th_rebase` moves `SLIDE_INDEX` by the whole albums (`slide_menu_set_value`) and takes them off the position, goal and click count: nothing moves, and a float keeps the 1e-4 its settling needs however long a spin goes (past about 1024 albums it didn't, and the covers settled a step short and stayed held). The pass names the album in the caption and keeps it as the one to reopen on whenever the caption changes, so `closed()`, which can come while the page is being destroyed, only lets go.

**The row** (Fast Navigation on, or a theme with no arch). `lead` is `l smoothstep((|l| - lead_from) / (lead_full - lead_from))`, `l = goal - pos`, through a `lead_ms` follow. `draw_row` measures each cover's `t` from `pos + lead`, on that side, and slides everything `lead row_shift` px. `b` is `smoothstep` from `row_from` to `row_full`: `row_shrink`% smaller, no receding past `row_flat` from the focus (`row_out` px an album instead), and `e = b smoothstep(t / row_edge)` narrows a cover by `row_width e` (40: a side cover of #329's shelf is 64 px across two albums out, where the 60 degree shelf's was 101, so 60 left gaps between the held row's covers) and flattens its keystone by `row_key e`. At lead 0 none of this runs and `coverflow_render` takes its own path, byte for byte. A cover's columns take the art through `cf_texel`, as `draw_cover`'s do, so the two paths meet with no jump: the near half `r` times as wide as the far half, `r` going from 1 (even) at `coverflow.shelf.art_persp` 0 to the plane's own near over far height at 100. At 100 it is `unproject`'s own texels to the byte.

**Textures.** The row shows about 11 covers, so a thumb theme keeps `CF_WIDE`, 15, around the facing cover (`fx_reach`, `fx_base`): 1.6 MB with the placeholder. The window (`entry_window`, through `row_window`, for `coverflow_paint` and `draw_row` alike; with Fast Navigation off the row at speed keeps 1.7.6's, round the facing cover) starts from the farthest cover behind the facing point that shows (`CF_SHOW_PAST`), so the covers the row draws are the ones loaded, a cover joins or leaves the window only where it adds nothing to the frame, and every cover any of which shows is drawn whole (`edge_drawn`). A decode takes 6 to 9 ms on the UI thread, so while the thumb holds the covers `fx_window` loads nearest the center first: with Fast Navigation off `FX_DECODES` (two) a frame, as 1.7.6; in it, within a frame's budget: `FX_BUDGET_MS` (8), `FX_ENTER_MS` (2) in the entry, `FX_LETTERS_MS` (1) going by letters, or `FX_SLACK_MS` (10) in a frame `FX_LATE_MS` (30) or more after the last. A frame's first load always starts, and each after only if the last load of its kind (`fx.half_ms`, `fx.full_ms`) would still end within the budget; a copy asked for and missing is a full decode, costed and timed as one. At rest the seven the shelf shows load at once, but in the covers' first frames (`fx_fresh`, until none is left to load): there the center alone loads at once and the rest within the budget, so an open's first frame comes the six side covers' decodes sooner (about 40 ms on the emulator, several times that on a Q2), the side covers filling in over the next frames. A cover not yet loaded shows the placeholder, and `fx.todo` has the thumb's pass ask for frames until none is left.

**Half copies** (none are made now: they served letters, and no idle pass writes them). Every cover the held row shows is turned and narrow, so half the art draws it as well. Each album gets `<key>.jpg.half` beside its cache file: 80 × 80 texels, each the rounded mean of four, raw (25.6 KB, about 26 MB for 1000 albums; each file takes at least a cluster of the card, so on exFAT's 128 KB clusters 128 KB, about 128 MB for 1000), read with one `fread` into the last quarter of a texture slot and spread two by two (`half_load`, `half_spread`). Only the idle passes at rest make them, only with Fast Navigation on, never a frame: `coverflow_wheel_poll` (the covers shown, no touch, nothing gliding or loading) calls `coverflow_halves`, which makes one a pass, decoded into 100 KB of heap freed once it is written, no sooner than `HALF_GAP_MS` (100) after the last, since a decode is 6 to 9 ms of the UI thread, written to `.half.tmp` and renamed, none with the card's free space under the larger of `HALF_KEEP_MB` (512 MB) and `HALF_KEEP_PCT` (5%) of its size (`card_room`; the art build and the rest keep `card_space`'s `MIN_FREE_MB`), so they stop short of filling the card and stay until Refresh Cover Flow, and once every album has one returns before asking the card for space. A copy cut short reads as none, and the cover's own art decodes instead. Refresh Coverflow empties `.coverflow`, the copies with it. Going by letters the pool grows to `FX_POOL` (64) slots (`fx.more`), and `fx_window` wants, in order: the window of the letter gone to, where the row will stop; the window on the screen; up to `CF_WIDE` albums ahead towards that letter; and the next and previous letters' windows, so a step finds its letter loaded. Covers load from their half copies in the entry, letters and the fold, then full art over the screen's copies where it shows face on: at rest, and in the held row once it is there, but not during the fold, whose covers sharpen after it lands, the landing cover first (`half_art`). At any landing, `fx_unletter` drops the covers kept away from the landing album, so its window, wherever it was loaded, takes the shelf's slots (a touch or Center mid-letters, not only the fold: `loader_test`), moves those in `fx.more`'s slots to the shelf's free ones and frees it.

**The loader.** A half copy's read is about 4 ms of card, so the copies are read on a thread of their own (`loader`), on the Q2's second core, started at the first copy asked for. Each frame `ld_ask` asks for the copies of the covers `fx_window` wants and lacks, in its order, up to `LD_SLOTS` (32) at once, each into its own 25.6 KB of `fx.stage`; a request no longer wanted is taken back, and one the frame has not reached gives up its place to a nearer one. The loader reads the one asked for first (`ld_step`). A request goes `LD_FREE` to `LD_WANT` (the UI thread), `LD_READ` and `LD_READY` (the loader) and back (the UI thread) by atomics, so neither thread waits on the other; the loader sleeps on a semaphore when nothing is asked. The UI thread spreads a copy that is there into its texture within the budget (`ld_take`), decodes the art of a cover with no copy whole. Its first call (`thread_lower(1)`) puts it at nice 19 and its reads in the idle I/O class, else best effort's lowest level. At any landing, painted or not (a window over the covers, the screen going dark), `fx_unletter` (from `coverflow_wheel_land`, or the next frame) asks it for nothing more (`ld_ask(0, 0)`), so it parks after the read in hand and the UI thread never waits on it; the next letters use the same thread. Only closing the page stops it (`ld_quit`), joined after the read in hand, and frees the stage, so the stage's 0.8 MB stays while the page is open once letters have run (a known limit: joining at a landing with no request `LD_READ` would give it back). `fx.more`'s 5 MB calloc is an mmap that the kernel's overcommit grants whatever is free, so it never fails on the Q2 and its pages, filled as covers load, would end in the OOM killer: it isn't tried with `MemAvailable` (`mem_available_kb`, shared with `mp4_fits`) under its size plus `MP4_SPARE_KB` (16 MB), and refused that way or by a failed calloc, it isn't asked again until letters end (`fx.no_more`), the letters loading the screen's window alone. Full art stays on the UI thread: `cf_decode` goes through AWTK's image manager, which is not thread safe. If the thread or its stage can't be had, the copies are read on the UI thread (`loader_test`; `test/patch.py` runs its body as MIPS).

**What ticks gave.** Each is rebuilt, and `test/patch.py` holds a case for it:

- `KEY_LOCKOUT`: its first `LOCKOUT_KEEP` tenths drop travel, as `ringnav` keeps it for ticks.
- `tick_gate`: no frame in `WHEEL_FRESH_MS` drops travel read after a stall.
- Two Returns: `wheel_sample` counts `WHEEL_THUMB`'s travel into `wh_since` a tick's worth at a time, so the second Return stops it, and the poll honours `wheel_mute`. The lyrics and Vortex stay out of it, as before.
- `chord_gate` works as it did: it is on key events, and dark isn't `usable()`, so the wheel is ticks.
- `hold_wheel`: a turn begun during the page's slide is ticks, raw being off. They play in as a step, and the next travel takes that animator over, goal kept (`th_grab`). A tick still queued as the wheel goes raw is dropped.
- The wheel's momentum: the lists' (`wheel_accel`), rows only, on ticks and on the thumb alike; never a letter.
- The end bounce: an artist's albums clamp the goal, and the first push past an end in a contact kicks the covers out `1 / CF_BOUNCE` of a stride.
- The click: once an album of the goal (`buzzeer_switch`). A turn also resets the screen's timeout and the idle clock.

Wheel Sensitivity scales the travel (`wheel_pct`), as it does other lists' ticks. Center lands at once on the album named, then opens it. A touch during a spin settles first: its press does nothing, and the covers run down to the album named (`coverflow_hit` only ever runs at rest).

The `--dev` frame gaps ([above](#coverflow-step)) go on working: `th.on` is a run, and its frames go to the log at the first paint after it.

## Cover Flow browsing position

`coverflow_position.c` draws an optional position bar, off by default. Display → Cover Flow's **Position Bar** persists `Q2POD/CFPOSITION`. The track matches the central cover's 160 px width, and its center is halfway between the last caption's bottom and the page's bottom. The 2 px track and 9×4 px gray thumb share a centerline. Virtual Sort/All Albums cards hold at the last album; wrapping to the first album returns the thumb to the left, at the half cover where `visual()` wraps. A bounded list's bounce or rubber band past its first album holds the thumb at the left. Zero or one album hides it.

The painter reads the wheel thumb's follower (`th`) while it holds the covers, otherwise the slide's live offset (touch and stock's step), so wheel and touch movement update it before settling. It stays opaque during movement, holds for 800 ms and fades over 300 ms. A temporary 33 ms UI timer invalidates only the 160×8 px footer strip; queuing that damage outside painting avoids the toolkit consuming it in paint cleanup. The timer stops after clearing, when disabled, or at page teardown. There is no worker, image cache, scan, or music-file access.

`test/coverflow_position.py` executes the production painter against a native canvas boundary; it also models shelf-only invalidation and paint cleanup. `test/patch.py` checks the real MIPS painter's placement in both halves, plus the persisted setting.

## Position memory

Position memory is a bounded 64-entry table keyed by the audited top-window context in `patch/contexts.inc` and a content fingerprint. Selecting a row updates its entry and moves it to the front; a full table evicts the least recently selected entry. Restoration alone does not promote an entry.

Local folders use the full bounded `g_folder_path`; local music lists use the stock browsing class, saved query and artist/album modes (`g_class_type`, `g_local_classinfo_save`, `g_artist_type`, `album_modetype`). Root Albums, Artists, Composers and Genres lists ignore the saved detail query: opening an artist overwrites it without changing the parent collection. `playlist_page` keys on none of these: opening a playlist writes the browsing state, so `context_now` scopes it by the page's add mode alone (`PL_MODE` + 1), and back from a playlist keeps its row while the Add to Playlist picker keeps its own. These are the inputs used by the stock folder and local-list loaders, not playback metadata. The builder verifies each object's size against the stock ELF. A changed fingerprint resets selection even if a surviving surface has the same row count, then restores the matching recent position and reveals it, or keeps the stock viewport if none is remembered. Fixed settings menus can restore by window name alone, but for Display's sub-pages (Appearance, Cover Flow, Controls: `display_page` opened again by `ringnav_display`, which marks each with its `DISPLAY_SUB`), whose scope is that mark + 1, so each opens on its own first row rather than on the row Display was left at; multi-pane and other dynamic pages without an audited content identity keep their live widget selection but do not restore across recreation.

Under a theme with `list.reopen.top` (OLED's), Return's release forgets the entry of the list being left (`forget_left`, before stock leaves the page, so `context_now` still names it): choosing that list again opens it at the top, as an iPod's menus and stock's own pages do (stock keeps no row of its own but Folder's, whose `folder_enter` pushes the parent's position and `folder_back` pops it), while the page Return lands on keeps its row. Home's own lists (Library, Streaming and Settings sliding in over its menu) are hidden rather than closed and Home keys no position memory, so Return there (`coverflow_home_back`) drops the row its view keeps and scrolls it back to its top (`forget_rows`). A theme that turns it off restores every list.

Memory lasts until power-off, with no filesystem writes. The table occupies 1,280 bytes. Ordinary paints do not search it; repeated selections in the current scope match its first entry and shift nothing. Lookup and promotion are bounded by `POS_MEM` (64).

Non-virtual lists also remember hashes of the selected row's first two text values, read through the stock `widget_get_text` UTF-32 accessor. A matching second text outranks proximity; equal matches choose the occurrence nearest the remembered index. Rows without text fall back to the index within the same content scope. The stock rows expose no stable item id. Both scroll views and virtual music tables protect an interrupted recall glide from silently replacing the remembered selection with a currently visible row. A real tap cancels the glide and selects its target; a wheel step advances from the remembered logical row. Pointer-down and synchronous click delivery load rows without recall, so native touch sees the widget it pressed and a rebuilt list cannot move or rebind that row first. Synchronous table rebinds discard the old row-pool snapshot before resolving the selected entry.

## Touch mode

A session-wide touch-mode flag suppresses only custom drawing, independently of logical selection and gesture state. Touch-down and native clicks (including clicks without touch-down) set it and invalidate the visible window. A press at the left edge that [Swipe back](#swipe-back) takes as a candidate is not yet a touch on the rows: `ringnav_touch` puts the flag back as it was and leaves it while the swipe holds the touch (`swipe_back_holds`), so the selected row's bar rides with the page and is still lit after a spring back; a candidate dropped as the page's (dragged up, down or left, or let go where it came down) sets it then (`touch_hide`). Before 2026-11-21 the edge press hid the bar for the whole swipe. A touch on the keyboard (a `keyboard` top window) or the lock window (`g_lockscreen_pageflag`) leaves it as it was: it touches no row, so the list shown after it (a playlist just named, the page under the lock) keeps its bar. It persists through settling and page changes. Accepted wheel input, including a turn at a boundary, center selection or an accepted Return release restores drawing, so the page Return goes back to shows its row; iPod's Home list ignores the flag and always draws its bar; synchronous center-generated clicks bypass the native-click observer.

Once a drag on Home settles, its bar, shown under touch, must stand on a row the wheel could leave it on: `reconcile` (`nav/lists.c`) keeps the selected row only while it stands whole in the rows the list rests on (`sel_height`: the main list's seven, from y 40 in Split), and otherwise moves the selection to the whole row nearest the list's middle, as it does on any list for a row out of sight. A drag that stops between rows, or ends with the first row under the status row or the last in the fade past the rest, so never leaves the bar under the clock or in the fade. That repair runs in a paint, often one clipped to Split's panning art, which draws neither the moved bar nor the band, so `paint_selection` marks it and the next frame repaints the page and the status row whole (`nav/row_paint.c` `list_reach_due`), or the old bar would stay drawn on the row under the clock until something else repainted there. The band's own paint of the scrolled rows (`list_reach_paint`), which moves the view up under the status row for the length of that paint, draws the selection as it stands and never settles it: judged by the moved view, a row the wheel left whole in the rest could look cut and lose the selection. Elsewhere touch hides the bar, and the wheel reveals the row before it shows again, so a row partly in sight keeps the selection.

A drag is no tap on a row. AWTK clicks a button on a lift inside it however far the finger moved there, and a list's scroll view takes only drags up or down, so a sideways drag across a Settings row clicked it (a 110 px drag changed Gain, one across Default Volume switched it on). `ringnav_dispatch` follows each touch (`touch_track`: its press, and whether it went more than `TAP_PX`, 10 px, from it either way before its lift) and drops the click that lift makes on a row inside a scroll view (`drag_click`). A tap's few pixels of jitter still click, as does Centre after a drag (a key event ends the lift's claim on the next click), and a button in no list (a dialog's, the keyboard's) keeps stock's click. Swipe back aborts its press before the lift, sliders and the scrubber move on their drags rather than a click, and the Up Next sheet's drag-down is its own handler's, so none of them is changed. `test/fw/test_nav_hold.py` covers the drags, the taps and Centre after a drag.

## Drawing

The canvas hook intersects the existing clip with the viewport and restores the clip, the LCD fill color and the LCD stroke color; this firmware's `canvas_save/restore` do not save those properties. The outline is one translucent fill (`0x402b2b2b`, a per-color alpha) plus two concentric one-pixel `canvas_stroke_rounded_rect` calls, a dark separator at radius 9 and the 70%-opaque white line at radius 8, with `bg_r = NULL`. The separator is the stock dark surface at `0xb32b2b2b`, so it disappears on the dark theme and only shows over bright artwork. It never calls `canvas_set_global_alpha`, so the shared alpha is untouched. A rounded call that reports failure (either stroke) or a row too small for the corner radius, keeps the square separator-plus-white outline instead.

iPod draws a selection bar instead of the outline. `widget_paint` (`0x6727fc`) calls `widget_on_paint_background`, then the widget's own paint, its children and `widget_on_paint_border`, so the background hook paints the bar behind the rows. The border hook then draws nothing, and the selection is loaded and settled once per frame, in the background hook. The bar spans the full surface width at the selected row's height and position, leaning with the wheel's tug (`patch/tilt.c`); an entry narrower than half the surface, a grid tile, gets the bar in its own rectangle. `paint_selection` draws it ([Themes](#themes)): on a list row the accent's flat bar (`gradient()` in the scheme's tones), `list.selection.inset` in from each side, its ends rounded by `list.selection.radius` at most (OLED's 16 and 8), under the rows' own ink, which stays white on it (`sel_accent`, resolved from paint ancestry by `ringnav_style_color`, without mutating recycled widget styles); a grid tile gets a square card in the accent's tone, `TILE_INSET` inside it, and the theme insets a grid tile's cover, so the card frames it. The bar uses the same clip, color restore and touch-mode rules as the outline. Rows only show it where they are transparent: after the iPod style edits, list rows, table rows, grid tiles (`s_btn_listblack`) and the settings rows (`s_btn_listitem`) are.

The iPod border hook draws the chevrons. Windows flagged `DRILL` in `patch/contexts.inc` get the stock `list_into` image on every row, over the bar as well: `widget_load_image` (`0x66f75c`, served from the image manager's cache) once per paint, then `canvas_draw_icon` (`0x64c20c`: canvas, bitmap, center x, center y, relative to the canvas origin like the fills) per row, placed as stock rows place their `img_into`: left edge `CHEVRON_W` (58) from the row's right edge, inside the same viewport clip, which hides rows outside it. A playlist button spans the same 20 to 355 pixels as a category or album button, so the glyphs cover the same screen columns (317 to 327); Local Music's own images sit 5 pixels further right at a fixed x. On a drill window the row layouter lays out as if that image were the last child, so the title and a playlist's "more" button end before it. The widget's own window, found through its parents, decides, so a window painted during a transition keeps its own rows. Rows narrower than half the surface (tiles) get none, and none are drawn while `g_navbar_status` is set, as stock hides its own chevrons in multi-select. The Add to Playlist picker (`playlist_page` with its add mode, `PL_MODE`) gets none either: its rows add in place and close, so they open nothing (`drill`), and its status row reads Add to Playlist (`pl_rows`).

The iPod border hook also draws the fast-scroll letter over the list. A step of more than one row (so the list has more than `SHORT_LIST_MAX` rows and the run has reached `LIST_FIRST_MS`) restarts a one-shot `LETTER_MS` (400 ms) timer. While it runs and the spin run is still past `LIST_FIRST_MS`, the surface draws the selected row's first non-space character, past an article on a library page ([Sorting](#sorting)). `paint_letter` draws none on a list OLED's [A-Z index](#a-z-index) shows on (`az_on`), which lights the letter itself. The letter is opt-in, by the list's page: the wheel handler arms it only when `name_sorted` (`patch/az_index.c`, the same rule as the A-Z index's) names the top window's list a name-sorted Library list, and every other list, however long, never arms it (Wi-Fi's networks, which come by signal, showed a letter until 2026-11-16; Bluetooth's devices, Settings, Up Next, View Queue, Chapters, Most Played, Era's albums, Internet Radio, card apps, Spotify and Tidal, the downloads, search results). The name-sorted lists: `localclass_page` and `album_page` (the Library's class lists), `artistinfo_page`, `folder_page` (a folder sorts by its file name), `coverflow_page` (its covers: `paint_letter` draws none over an open album's tracks, `coverflow_tracks` of the widget's own window, which `in_order` puts in disc and track order), Edit Playlist's Add Songs picker (`playlistedit_page` while `ple_listing` is 0, the whole library A to Z), and Library's song list, `allmusic_page`, while its class and Sort put it in name order. The wheel handler tests the top window's name where it arms the letter, not at paint, where the top may already be the page a Return brings back. An album's songs in the Library are not among them: stock shows them only in `albuminfo_page` (its init, `0x4a9a48`, is `load_album_detaillist`'s one caller: classes `0xff10`, `0xff11`, `0xff12` and `0xff14`) and `playerjumpinfo_page` (Album info and Go to Album, `0xff10`), and `getMusicByAlbum` and its kin sort them by disc, then track (comparator `0x5063f0`). `allmusic_page` shows lists of both kinds, so there the class decides, and its list is in an order of its own while it shows Recent, Frequent or Recently Added (`0xf007` to `0xf009`: `ORDER BY id DESC`, `getAllOftenRecord`'s own sort `0x506414` and `ORDER BY time_create desc limit 100`, each without the name sort), a playlist's songs under its Sort's Time added (`0xff13`, passed by a playlist row's click at `0x4b4bdc`, under a Sort of Time added, `g_playlistsort_flag` not 0: `getMusicByPlayList` `0x50b6c8` then lists them through `sort_playlist_addtime`, to which `library_query` adds `order by id`, the playlist's own order; sorted by name, 0, the list is A to Z and keeps the letter), Songs under Sort's Time added (`g_sort_flag` 3 or 4, or `song_sort.c`'s own orders), or an artist's Songs tab or a genre's songs from Genres (`0xff07` and `0xff09`: `getMusicBySonger`, `getMusicByAlbumArtist` and `getMusicByGenre` have no `ORDER BY` and ask for no sort, so the rows come as the database holds them). Songs A to Z, Hi-Res and My Fav are in name order (`getAllHr` and `getAllFav` ask `toolsQueryDbTable` for the name sort whatever their SQL's order). The class is the page's own, which its init stores (`0x4acd3c`) and its return handler puts back when another page changed it (`0x4ab728`); a class would not do on other pages, since `g_class_type` keeps its last value on pages that do not set it. That handler returns early while a song delete started on the page still runs (`g_delsong_state`, `0x4ab6c0`), so a class left by a page opened meanwhile can outlast the return; no other page stores a class tested here, so that can only leave the letter on. Edit Playlist, `playlistedit_page`, while it shows the playlist's songs (`ple_listing`: `ple.mode` 0, listed by `sort_playlist_addtime` whatever the playlist's Sort) is in the order they were added. The text is the row's first non-empty `widget_get_text`, taken from the same `row_id` walk as the position-memory hashes, and a virtual table finds its logical row in the recycled pool; an offscreen or textless row draws nothing. The box is `LETTER_BOX` (80) square, `canvas_fill_rounded_rect` at radius `LETTER_RADIUS` (12) in the stock dark surface at `LETTER_ALPHA` (85%), or a square fill without a vgcanvas. The glyph is `LETTER_PX` (60) in the system default font (`canvas_set_font` `0x6473dc` with a null name), white (`canvas_set_text_color` `0x64730c`), centered by `canvas_draw_text_in_rect` (`0x64ca94`) with the canvas alignment fields (`+0x34` horizontal, `+0x30` vertical) set to center and middle. The clip, fill and text colors and alignment are restored afterwards; the font is not, since stock sets it before drawing its own text. The expiry repaints the live surface, which then draws nothing.

## A-Z index

OLED's A-Z index ([oled-design](oled-design.md#a-z-index)) is `patch/az_index.c`. It indexes a `table_client` over `p_deque_showlist` with more than `AZ_MIN_ROWS` (50) rows whose count is the deque's: `allmusic_page` while `name_sorted` says its list is in name order (not Recent, Frequent, Recently Added, Time added, nor an artist's or a genre's songs, see [Drawing](#drawing)), and `localclass_page` or `album_page` for classes `CLASS_ALBUMS` to `0xf006`, whose rows name the album, artist, composer and genre at `REC_ALBUM`, `REC_ARTIST`, `+0x20` and `+0x1c`, as `class_query` reads them. A song row's name is `track_name`'s (the title, else the file name), which is what the name comparators sort on. `az_initial` gives a name's letter as the sort sees it: through `ringnav_sort_key` (trimmed, its article dropped), A to Z in either case, anything else `#` (0), as `catalogue.c`'s `initial` files a title; a class list's Unknown row (`REC_ID` -1, last) has none.

**Touch.** `ringnav_touch` hands a press to `az_touch` after stock's, before it marks the touch on the list. A press in the last `AZ_EDGE_PX` (28) columns of an indexed list takes the touch the way a claimed pull does ([Pull-to-search](#pull-to-search)): `EVT_POINTER_ABORT` dispatched through the page lets go of the rows it pressed, and `az_event`, bound once per page to its move-before, up-before, abort, close and destroy, swallows the moves and the lift (`STOP`), so the list neither scrolls nor takes a tap; `ringnav_touch` passes moves straight to stock while `az_held`; a press while it holds (a lift it never saw) ends the hold, and the strip fades as after a lift. The press is on the edge by its place in the list's view: `widget_to_local` gives it in the content, the scroll added, so `az_touch` takes the table's offset (`TABLE_TOP`) off again; a scrolled list once took a press low on the strip for one below the list. On the press `az_touch` walks the deque once and keeps each letter's first row (`az.first`); the finger's screen row picks a letter evenly over `AZ_TOP` to `AZ_BOTTOM` (80 to 240), all 27 whether or not the column is folded (`az_letter_at`), and `az_target` takes that letter's first row, else the next letter's that has rows, else the last before it. `ringnav_jump` (`patch/navigation.c`, where `load`, `select` and `wheel_offset` live) selects it and sets the table's offset to put it at the top, as far as `max_top` allows, with `touch_mode` cleared so the bar shows.

**Wheel.** The list tick calls `az_wheel` after `select` and `reveal`. With the strip hidden it costs one test of `wheel_speed` (degrees a second, [Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)); at `AZ_SPIN_DPS` (300) or more the strip comes up on the list with the selected row's letter lit and the bubble beside it. 300 is where Rockbox's acceleration, `(speed / 270)^4` rounded, first gives 2 (`vol_accel`'s step 2): the averaged speed needs about a turn to get there, so a fast spin shows the strip after half a turn or so, and a slow turn never does. A slower tick while it shows keeps the lit letter in step and drops the bubble, without putting the fade off.

**Showing and fading.** `az.list` is the table it shows on and `az.page` its window, compared and never followed. It shows until `UI_SHOW_MS` (1000 ms, `patch/ui_kit.h`'s show-then-fade, `ui_fade_alpha`) after the lift or the last fast tick, fading over the last `UI_FADE_MS` (200), as the scroll indicator does: `az_due` repaints the strip's columns of the top window every `UI_FADE_STEP_MS` (40) through the fade, then the whole window once it is gone, when the rows move back. `az_paint` draws it from the window's border paint (`ringnav_paint`), after everything in it, since Songs' table starts at y 90 under its Shuffle row, above `AZ_TOP`'s 80; it places itself by the canvas's own origin (`CANVAS_X`, `CANVAS_Y`). The column is `az_column`'s: 27 letters do not fit `AZ_SLOTS` (14) slots of `AZ_SLOT` (11) px, so it keeps seven, evenly from `#` to Z, with a U+2022 dot between each two, each in its share of the 160 px. While `az_on` a list, `az_right` moves its right column `AZ_RIGHT_IN` (4) px in (`song_row`'s lengths and right-hand artist, `paint_chevrons`' theme chevron) and `az_bar_in` takes `AZ_BAR_IN` (8) px off the selection bar's right end (`paint_selection`); `paint_letter` and `wheel_sb_alpha` draw nothing on it. The bubble is drawn, not `search_strip.c`'s key-pop art, which points down from a 30 px head.

## Accent

iPod's accent ([ipod.md](ipod.md#display-settings); OLED's own Blue) replaces Shanling red wherever it is drawn:
the theme's style colors, inline `style:*` colors (a mutable style answers through the same
vtable), decoded images, and the payload's own selection bar and progress fill, which read
the active scheme's tones (`tones()`, [Themes](#themes)). `accent_map` (`patch/theme_engine.c`) is
a pure function on one `color_t` (bytes r, g, b, a). Stock uses `#FF1448`, `#7F0A24`, the
pressed tint `#3D1920` and `#FF144840`, all stock red blended with a neutral: each channel is
`t * red + k`. Least squares against red with
the mean removed gives `t` (in 1/4096), then `k`. A color within `RED_TOLERANCE` (8) of that
blend, with `t` between 1/16 and 17/16 and `k` not below the tolerance, becomes `t * tone + k`
for one of the preset's tones (`ACCENTS`): the red tone for text colors (a property name ending
`text_color`, `tk_str_end_with`) and image pixels, the light tone for every other color property
and gradient stop; alpha is kept, and anything else, grays and other hues included,
is returned as it was. Anti-aliased edges onto black, white or a transparent background are such
blends, so they follow. No preset's colors are red blends, so mapping twice changes nothing.

- `style_get_color(color_t *ret, style, name, default)` returns its color through the hidden
  first argument. The hook runs stock through a trampoline and maps `*ret`, comparing the
  property name only when the color maps. Stock first asks `style_get_gradient` for every color
  (`bal` at `0x65d558`; `style_data_get_gradient` turns a plain color into a one-stop gradient),
  so the gradient hook leaves the call that returns to `0x65d560` unmapped, and the color hook
  alone picks the tone. The builder pins that `bal`.
- `style_get_gradient(style, name, gradient_t *out)` (`0x65d4ac`) is a 12-instruction leaf with
  no GOT setup: null checks on the style and its vtable, then a tail call to the vtable's
  `get_gradient` (+0x18). The builder pins its first three words (`0x10800009, 0, 0x8c820000`)
  and replaces the first two with the jump; the payload repeats the checks, calls `get_gradient`
  through `$t9`, and maps the stops only when it filled the caller's `out`: `gradient_t` is 0x4c
  bytes (`gradient_init`), with the stop count at +8 and up to 8 `{color, offset}` stops from
  +0xc (`gradient_add_stop`, `gradient_get_first_color`). Widget backgrounds come this way.
- `image_manager_add(manager, name, bitmap_t *)` copies a freshly decoded bitmap into the cache.
  The hook maps its pixels first, only for plain theme image names (no `/` or `:`, so covers by
  path, `file://` or online URL are never touched), and only when the format
  is one of the 32-bit ones: `bitmap_t` has w at 0, h at 4, the format as a u16 at 0xe
  (1 RGBA, 2 ABGR, 3 BGRA, 4 ARGB in memory order, 4 bytes each by `bitmap_get_bpp_of_format`),
  its row stride from `bitmap_get_line_length`, and the pixels from
  `bitmap_lock_buffer_for_write`/`bitmap_unlock_buffer`. Premultiplied pixels are red blended
  with black, so they map the same way.

The confirm pop-up's discs (`confirm_ok`, `confirm_cancel` and their pressed images, names
starting `CONFIRM_IMAGE`) go through the same mapping with `CONFIRM_SURFACE` (`#2B2B2B`) as the
tone under every preset, Crimson included ([ipod.md](ipod.md#pop-ups)). The quick settings'
control discs (names starting `DROPDOWN_IMAGE`, `drop_`, except the brightness suns, `DROPDOWN_SUN`)
take the preset's red tone; when that tone is brighter than `GLYPH_LIGHT_MAX` (Graphite's silver),
an image that holds red also maps its neutral glyph pixels to `CONFIRM_SURFACE`, so the white glyph
turns dark ([quick settings](ipod.md#quick-settings)). Gray discs hold no red and are unchanged.
Any other image that holds red and an opaque pure-white pixel (a switch's knob, a disc's glyph; `#7F7F7F`
on a pressed disc) takes
the light tone instead of the red one, as do button backgrounds (names starting `BUTTON_IMAGE`,
`btn_`), whose white label is a widget's text; an image with red alone (a tick, the time page's
colon) keeps the red tone. Only Graphite's two tones differ, so only it scans for white.
The settings rows' category icons (`settings_icons` in `patch/ipod.json`, which the builder
writes to `SETTINGS_ICON_NAMES` in `stock.h`) are never mapped: several use stock red as their
category color (Network, DLNA, Wi-Fi, Backlight), like the purple and orange ones.
`red_map` is the mapping with an explicit tone;
`accent_map` is it with the preset's tone.

Changing the accent saves it, sets the progress fill, calls `image_manager_unload_all(image_manager())`
(`0x658594`) and `widget_invalidate_force` on the window manager. Widgets ask for their style
colors, gradients and images on every paint, so the next frame decodes the images again through
the hook and shows every recoloured part; nothing needs a restart.

## Rounded corners

Every rounded thing the payload paints itself is anti-aliased from one table: `corner_cover(r)` (`patch/corner_cover.c`) gives a radius `r` corner's coverage, `r` rows of `r` pixels from the outermost, each the share of 16 x 16 sample points inside the circle, out of 255. It works a radius out the first time it is drawn (16 integer square roots a row of pixels) and keeps it on the heap, a pointer a radius up to 160 in the scratch page, so any radius costs one fill per boot and a table lookup after. `tools/art.py` `corner_cover` is the same table in Python, which `test/fw/test_corners.py` holds the C to at every radius to 40 and beyond. The readers:

- `round_row` and `round_ring` (`patch/nav/row_paint.c`): a box a row at a time, each corner pixel the colour at its coverage. The scroll bar, the sheet, artist discs and boxes, About's tiles and `fill_box` where AWTK will not round (no vgcanvas, or a radius of 2, which stock declines under 3).
- `gradient`: the selection's pill, its bands' ends at their corner pixels' coverage.
- `corner_mask`: what lies outside a box's corners painted in the colour behind at the share the arc leaves, which rounds a square cover already drawn: Now Playing's art (`paint_cover`), About's, Control Center's, Up Next's and the artist pages' covers (`ar_corners`). `modal_corners` blends the screen towards the sheet's material by the same share.
- `round_corners` (`patch/nav/theme_titles_paint.c`): a decoded list thumbnail's alpha clamped to its coverage.
- Cover Flow's `column` (`patch/coverflow.c`): in a corner's texel columns, each end row the corner covers in part takes that texel's coverage too, so the arc is smooth where it runs steep (across the columns) as well as where it runs flat; the reflection mirrors it. The covers are drawn a column at a time, so this costs only the corners' end rows.

AWTK's own rounded rects (`canvas_fill_rounded_rect`, `canvas_stroke_rounded_rect`, through vgcanvas) are anti-aliased already and are left to it at a radius of 3 or more.

## Themes

OLED is the one built-in theme: `themes[]` (`patch/theme_engine.c`, from the generated `themes.inc`; the
types are in `patch/theme.h`) holds its one row, `THEME_N` is 1, and `theme()` reads the settings first
(`accent()`) and returns `&themes[0]`; `scheme()` returns its scheme for the stored accent in the half
Light Mode picks. Code asks the theme for a field, never which theme it is. The stored `THEME` is always
3, OLED's number when there were four themes: `theme_boot` (`patch/navigation.c`) gives a unit an older
build left on another (0, 1, 2, or no key) OLED's preset once, through `theme_preset`, and writes 3
([ipod.md](ipod.md#theme)).

- `theme_t` holds the surface flags (monochrome icons, `art_final`, the theme's own art left final,
  Now Playing opacities), the fonts per role, the Home and settings geometry, the Now Playing bar
  heights, the selection bar's radius and inset, the scrollbar, the accent's slot and config key
  (`accent_slot`/`accent_key`: OLED's `OLED_ACCENT`, an own key in `st.own[]`; `ACCENT` for a theme
  that names none), its schemes, its options, the Cover Flow style and its art prefix (`art`, `"oled_"`).
- `scheme_t`: one per `ACCENTS` row and theme's own accent, indexed by the stored value; its tones are that row, or
  the own scheme's `tones` when it states them (`<id>_tones[]`), read through `tones()` or `tones_of(v)`. The roles
  `chevron` (a mono theme's icon gray) and `muted` (second lines) are `0xRRGGBB`, 0 meaning unused; `sel_text`
  is the text on the selection, `paper` and `ink` the half's ends, and `label` an own scheme's name ("Blue").
- `option_t`: the Appearance rows, in order. At the first read, a stored value outside
  `values` becomes `def`. `theme_preset` writes each option's `preset` unless the stored value is
  its `keep` (Light's Auto), and only values that change. The accent row cycles within `values`.

The table is generated. Each built-in theme is `assets/themes/<id>/theme.xml`. The format is a strict
XML subset: elements with double-quoted attributes, self-closing tags and comments, only whitespace
between tags, the entities `&amp; &lt; &gt; &quot;`, UTF-8, at most 32 KB. `tools/theme.py` fills
each theme in this order: the schema defaults, its `extends` base (a theme may extend another
in `assets/themes/`; OLED extends none), its own elements, then
`ROLE_MACROS`, which takes the numbers a theme leaves to `patch/offsets.inc` (OLED's: Home's Full
label end, the chevron gray, Cover Flow's `CF_*` and the motion), so a theme file never names a macro. Any unknown name or
value stops the build. The tool writes `themes.h` (the enums and macros, which navigation.h includes) and `themes.inc`
(the tables, which theme_engine.c includes after the accent tables, where the hand-written table
stood) into the build directory, and `THEME_N` into `stock.h`, because `setting_counts[]` uses it. `edit_paint`'s OK is an off-white card (`MINIMAL_FILL`). A theme's `art` attribute (its own id by default) names the theme whose generated images (`tools/art.py`, `<art_id>_*`) it draws, and the payload loads them by that prefix (`theme_art`, `patch/list_marks.c`): OLED's are `oled_*`. `art.theme_images` packages each name once, stopping the build if two themes would draw one name.

**Faces.** A theme names a face for each font role (`theme_t.font[ROLE_*]`: the list row's title, its second line and a two-line row's title, the bar's title, Now Playing's title, Home's rows, the small info text) by a key of `FACES` in `tools/build.py`, the one list of them: `regular` (stock's `default.ttf`, uncut), and `inter` and `inter-medium` (Inter 4.1 Regular and Medium, OLED's). Each entry gives the face's name on the device (`fonts/<name>.ttf`, and AWTK's `font_name`), its original in `assets/fonts`, the name its subset takes, its license files (`FONT_NOTICES`, shipped beside the fonts), and the face a text falls back to when this one lacks a character, with that fallback's size as a percentage of its own (the two faces' cap heights' ratio: 98 for Inter's to stock's), and for Inter the suffix of its tabular figures' glyph names (`.tf`). `subset_font` cuts each face but stock's to its Latin, Greek, Cyrillic and punctuation, with a play mark at U+25B6, and points 0-9 and the colon (`TABULAR`) at a face's tabular figures, so a clock or a song's time keeps its width as it counts; `stock.h` then holds `FONT_<NAME>` (its index, in `FACES`' order), `FONT_NAMES`, `FONT_FALLBACK`, `FONT_FALLBACK_PCT` and the faces' cmap runs (`FONT_RANGES`, a face's from `FONT_RANGE_AT[i]` to `[i + 1]`, and `<NAME>_RANGES` each). `tools/theme.py`'s `FONTS` is the same keys. navigation.c's `face_has` looks a text's characters up in those runs (stock's has none listed, and every character), and `theme_font` (a label, in its role's face) and `theme_face` (canvas text, in the list title's face) walk the fallbacks from the theme's face until one has them all, scaling the px at each step.

**Cover Flow.** `theme_t.cf` (`cf_style_t`: `coverflow.shelf` top, x1, xs, z1, zs, eye, bright1,
bright2, reflect, `reflect_top`, stride, radius, tilt, horizon, third, swing, lift, `view_h`, the thumb's and the arch's; `coverflow.caption` `name_px`, `artist_px`, `text_y`) is
copied to coverflow.c's `cfs` by `cf_restyle` at every page open, so the stride is in place before
`slide_menu_set_spacer`; a radius change refills `cf_inset`, and a render before any page restyles
once. OLED takes the top, brightness, reflection, stride and frame height from offsets.inc's `CF_*` and the radius from `NP_ART_RADIUS` (`ROLE_MACROS`); where the side covers stand (x1, xs, z1, zs, eye, tilt, horizon, swing), `reflect_top`, the captions, the thumb and the arch are its `theme.xml`'s. An arch (`arch_span`) needs `arch_in`, `arch_out` and `arch_tau`, a span of an album at least, and `arch_full` past `arch_at`.
tools/theme.py checks each range, top + 160 + reflect ≤ `view_h` ≤ the client height, eye + z1 > 80 sin(tilt) (a first side cover's near edge in front of the eye), with swing 1 also eye - max(0, 80 - z1 / sin(tilt)) - lift / 4 > 0 (and all through a step), bright2 ≤ bright1, and
the caption's lower box, `text_y` + the greater of `CF_NAME_H` and `artist_y` + `CF_ARTIST_H`, ≤ the client height. A caption may overlap a taller frame: its labels draw
over it. `CF_EDGE`, `CF_VIEW_W`, `CF_CX` and `ART_SIZE` stay fixed. The frame's paper is the scheme's, as is a
placeholder's corners', so a theme's own white paper meets the page with no band.

**Bar and client height.** The grid's bar height is in `geom_vals` (`themes.inc`, the `V_*`
columns), 58 for OLED's. `client_h()` (theme_engine.c) is `320` less that bar, the window's height under
the bar. Cover Flow's views, Home's art panel, its pan frame, render loop and clip read it, and the
battery slot (`bar_sync`) takes the same bar. The page fallbacks
(`widget_get_prop_int(page, "h", 290)`) stay sized for 290, and `DRIFT_TEXELS` for a pane the screen's height (a `split_art_up` as tall as the bar). On the
build side `Geometry` and `with_geometry(g)` (`tools/ipod.py`) drive `ipod_home`, `status_bar`,
`playing_page` and `patch_asset`.

**Geometry set.** The build bakes one set, the theme's (`tools/theme.py built_geometry`): `patch_code` writes its
values into stock's row immediates (`ipod.json`), and `ui_pages` (`tools/ipod.py`) builds every page under it, each
written over stock's own. `themes.inc` holds the same values for the payload: `geom_words` (the immediates' words,
`G_*`, which `geom()` reads) and `geom_vals` (the values that are not immediates, `V_*`, which `geom_val()` reads).
The Library and Edit Playlist rows the payload builds follow the set: `list_row_core`
reads the Library constructor's body and icon x words, and Edit Playlist's row
takes the set's `pitch` and `body` (`geom()`).

**Geometry fields.** OLED is the one theme and its grid the one the build bakes: its theme.xml states it in one `<geometry bar="58" …/>`, each omitted field stock's own (`STOCK_GRID`, the `Geometry` defaults: stock's page measurements) or, for a theme that extends another, that theme's; `tools/theme.py` checks each field's range (`GEOM_RANGES`) and that the themes share one grid (`built_geometry`). The build writes it into stock's row immediates (`patch_code`) and pages (`ui_pages`), and the payload reads the values that are not immediates from `geom_vals`; nothing is patched at boot, and no other grid is built.

- Values that follow the grid but are not immediates (the bar, the settings rows, the battery body, the text inset) are `geom_vals[V_*]`, and `client_h()` is `320 - geom_val(V_BAR)`.
- `list_end`: list boxes take the whole window, so rows draw down to the glass (OLED's end their rows at `list_end` instead, the strip below black), while the selection's scroll limit (`sel_height`, `max_top`) stops at `list_end` so a selected row never lands where the glass hides its text. A last row selected leaves the glass's strip below it empty. A list ends after the last row whose text clears the glass at `text_x` (`fit_bottom`).
- `action_row`: Songs' action bar as a plain row. Stock rebuilds that view's children on each refresh (0x4a9e78: the label, Play All's image, Sort's image only on some pages), so the assets shape only the boxes around it and `action_row()` shapes its children as it paints, once per rebuild. They stay stock's widgets with stock's handlers.
- `home_lib`: Home's Library row, in Split (OLED's grid has `home_lib` 0), slides in a list of the Library's rows (`list_view_homelib`, filled by the same `library_rows` the page uses, `home_library`) instead of opening the page; each row opens its stock page and Return comes back to the list. The bar's title names the open list (`coverflow_home_title`). Full keeps stock's page. Its Streaming row does the same (`list_view_homestream`, `home_streaming`, `stream_rows`): stock's `stream_page_init` takes the list for its window, finds no `view_navbar` there and rebuilds the rows in the view of that name, its timer stopped by `STREAM_BG` and its handlers dropped, and the rows take Home's height (`home_fill`). Full's page still follows it through `stream_row`. `svc_toggle` looks in every window, as Home's list comes first and is empty under Full.
- Songs' rows have their own immediates (`song_pitch`, `song_body`, `song_title24_y`, `song_meta_y`) and page kind `song`. With no text art (the grid's `text_art` 0), a row taller than the pitch whose leading image has no width is two lines (`two_lines`): art and playing gif hide, the second line stays, and the artist is what stock's bind (0x4ab208) writes, "Unknown Artist" when untagged. A playlist's songs are the same page and list; album tracks and an artist's songs are other constructors, title only.

**A theme's own options.** A theme declares them in theme.xml (OLED's `<option key="SONGARTIST" label="Song Artist" default="Inline" preset="Inline">` over its `<value label="..."/>` rows). The payload draws, cycles and stores them generically (`SETTING_OWN`, `theme_keys[]`, `st.own[]`) and reads their keys after the thirteen in declaration order. Each is a plain choice the payload reads as `st.own[OWN_<KEY>]` through `theme_own` (0 while the theme does not offer it), saved at once. `tools/theme.py` accepts only the plain keys in `PLAIN_KEYS`, the ones the payload reads: OLED's `SONGARTIST`, `SONGLENGTH` and `NPTIME` (`theme_engine.c` `song_artist`, `song_length`, `np_time_total`). An own option takes `preset` and `keep` as a payload setting does (into its `option_t` line), so `theme_preset()` writes it with the rest. Undeclared settings take the theme's value, and their stored keys are untouched.

**OLED.** `assets/themes/oled/theme.xml`, built to [oled-design.md](oled-design.md). It extends no other theme and is built on its own `oled` set: a status row overlaid on a full-bleed page (`status_y` 23, its ends `STATUS_ROW_INSET` 62 px in from the sides: `tools/ipod.py` `status_row`) with no band, then content resting from y 58: 32 px rows (52 for art lists and Search), the text at `text_x` 24 and the right column at `right_x` 28, and `list_end` 224, so a list's box (`patch_asset`, `fit_rows`, the settings lists' too, and the payload's own `page_list` pages through `fit_view` and `list_fit_end`) holds the whole rows that end by y 282 on screen and the strip below stays black. The status row's `label_title` and `label_clock` start in one box at `text_x`, in the bar's face at `bar_px`; `bar_title` (np_bar.c) keeps the clock beside a title, and `clock_place` (navigation.c, each bar paint) moves it, its box sized to its text as measured in the bar's face, so the label's own alignment plays no part: on a full-width row, titled or not, the text is centered on x 187.5 and the title's box ends `CLOCK_CLEAR` (12) short of the widest clock, "00:00" as measured once, centred, so its ellipsis stops there; on Home in Split (`coverflow_home_split`) the clock is over the list at the row's left, its text starting `STATUS_ROW_INSET` (62) in, as the battery's nub ends that far from the right edge, the slots keeping the row's right ([Status row slots](#status-row-slots)), and where the art runs up under the row it takes Text Primary in each state its style names, as it had over the art; the color written last is kept and compared, so an unchanged clock never asks for another repaint. `bar_title_sync` gives Home's own list and Now Playing an empty title there (`coverflow_home_sub`), and names the Library (`localmusic_page`) and the whole Songs list (`allmusic_page` under class `0xf001`) by those words where stock's hidden toolbar says "Local Songs" for both; `allmusic_page`'s other lists keep stock's title (an album's, a playlist's). On a set with a right column the settings rows' trailing images end on it (`set_edge`, `list_toggle`'s switch), a feature's "Title: value" row (Crossfade, Resume Songs, Night Shift, Wheel Sensitivity, Folder Root and the Library & Folders rows, `row_value_text`) shows as a key/value row, and `value_fit` ends the value 21 px short of the column on a row that opens a page, so it stands beside the chevron, and splits the row between title and value as a [label/value row](oled-design.md#labelvalue-rows) does (`kv_row`). `list.art.radius` (OLED's 4) is a row cover's corner radius on screen at the set's art size, scaled to the thumbnail's own size when `round_corners` rounds it; 0 keeps `NP_ART_RADIUS`'s share. The right group is the battery; the play state, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and EQ are off-screen, and the payload paints the row's other glyphs left of the battery ([Status row slots](#status-row-slots)). Its own scheme (`oled-blue`, five equal tones) is the only one `OLED_ACCENT` offers, its faces are `inter` and `inter-medium` at 1.21 times the design's sizes (AWTK sizes a face by its line), and `settings.values.ink` gives its key/value rows their gray, final in each half (`list_value`, through `text_ink`, which the selection's `sel_text` still overrides), the value's right end on the right column. `settings.values.switch` (`theme_t.set_switch`) keeps an on/off row a switch where `set_text` would write On or Off: `list_toggle` makes its `switch_on`/`switch_off` image as on any theme, the image hook empties stock's switch art (and Gain's `gain_high`/`gain_low`, the Wi-Fi page's `wifi_sig1`..`4`), and `paint_into` draws `switch_mark` (`patch/list_marks.c`, vgcanvas: 40x24, the knob 20 px sliding over 200 ms when a switch at the same place flips (`sw_knob`, `SWITCH_SLOTS` places remembered), the on-bar pair white track and accent knob, or a 1.5 px white ring) on the image's right end, Gain's High or Low as a value (`paint_gain`), a disabled row's `list_intodown` as `chevron_muted` in Text Tertiary with its label's stock #777777 mapped to the scheme's `muted` (`ringnav_style_color`), and a picker's mark as the theme's 12 px `check_a`/`check_w` (`paint_radio`); settings rows' text starts at `text_x` less hscroll_label's 2 px (`set_text_x`). Under it stock's four slider windows take one form (`patch/slider_page.c`: `slider_page_open` from `slider_open` as the window loads, `slider_page_paint` after its children: the toolbar's title and switch as a selected row, the value from stock's label, which stays laid out but clear so its writes still repaint, the track, knob and range ends, `xfade_ends` for crossfade.c's pages), EQ's Simple tab draws rows and vertical sliders (`eq_rows_paint`, `eq_tabs_paint`, peq_ui.c's `e3_paint` and `e3_touch` on `EQ_*` rows), and the Wi-Fi page is restyled after each `wifimenu_rows_build` (`patch/wifi_rows.c`: stock's Scanning row, whose tap scans, reads Search Again with its spinner hidden; `wifi_rows_pre` and `wifi_rows_post` from `ipod_list_layout`, `wifi_mark` from `paint_into`, the scan records' flags from `wifi_showlist` for the lock, `wifi_searchtime` for Searching...). About is a key/value table (`patch/settings_pages.c` `about_rows`, from `ipod_list_layout`: each row split by `kv_row`; its rows take the selection, so the wheel walks them and a value cut off at its column scrolls on the selected row, as `marq_moved` takes a row's first cut-off label; stock's row click, `systemset_about_row_on_click` `0x4c12f8` and its serial-number QR code, gives way to `about_click`, which does nothing; keys in Text Primary and values in the value gray, white on the selection), Reset Settings' three rows lose stock's `list_into` (hidden and insensitive, as they open the card at once) and each takes its caption once (`reset_rows`, from `ipod_list_layout`; what each reset takes is stock's `init_usersetting` and `init_database`, called from reset_page's row click (unnamed, after `systemset_powermanager_page_init`), and the cards say it, `feedback.c` `asks[]`), Lock Screen's pictures sit three a row on the text and right columns without stock's blue default-picture corner (`lock_grid`, from `lockscreen_rows`), and EQ's Advanced list shows whole rows down to the set's `list_end` (`eq_list_end`), its box running on to the window's foot so the rows past it fade there (`list_fit_end`, navigation.c `list_fade`). The rest are drawn by `patch/list_marks.c`: stock's `list_into` is emptied and the theme's own caret drawn on every drill row's and every `list_into` row's right column (`chevron_icon`: `paint_chevrons`, `paint_into`), white on the selection; a theme with `list.scrollbar.w` (OLED's 4) draws the track (`list.scrollbar.track`) and thumb only while the wheel turns (`wheel_sb_arm` from the wheel's tick, `wheel_sb_alpha` in `paint_scrollbar`, a fade over the last 200 ms of a second, repainted every 40 ms by `sb_due`, and nothing while the [A-Z index](#a-z-index) shows on the list); `list.divider.ink` draws a 1 px divider under each row taller than the pitch, from its text column (`list.art.text_x` under a theme with art rows) to the right column, on neither edge of the selected row (`paint_separators`); the lists keep no reading margin (`reveal`), so they scroll a whole row at a time, and where a row of another pitch (Power's 12 px gap before Restart) would leave the view's end inside a row, cut at the top, the view stops on the next row's top instead, its content grown to allow it (`fit_top`); the battery is the iOS-proportioned one (`battery_slim`, vgcanvas), and the play state is `status_row.c`'s level bars. A theme's own images are named by its art prefix (`theme_t.art`, `"oled_"`, `theme_art`), which `art_final` reads in the image hook: OLED's are final in each half, drawn per half by `tools/art.py` from Phosphor's SVGs (`phosphor`, filled by the nonzero rule). A one-line song row shows what its list calls for (`patch/song_rows.c`): `paint_songs`, from the list's background hook after `paint_selection` and so before the rows paint, hands each row to `song_row`, which picks the list by its window (`song_list`: `allmusic_page`, Songs and the lists stock opens there such as a genre's, mixed; `artistinfo_page` an artist's, `albuminfo_page` an album; any other list keeps stock's row), fits the title's box to its measured ink (`song_fit`) and draws the rest in the meta face in the scheme's `muted` (Light Mode's flip turns it for paper), its `sel_text` on the selection. The artist is the text stock bound to the row's hidden second line; an album's track number (`REC_TRACK`) and a length (`duration_text`, so only once a durations pass has measured the song) come from the row's `p_deque_showlist` record, taken only when its `REC_TITLE` is the row's title, at the row's index or the one before. Song Artist (`SONGARTIST`: Inline, Selected Row, Right, Off) and Song Length (`SONGLENGTH`: Albums, All Lists, Off) are the theme's own plain options (`song_artist`, `song_length`); a length takes the right column, so a Right or Selected Row artist stands inline beside it. A grayed row's offline mark ([Server library](#server-library)) takes the right column's place: `ringnav_paint_bg` runs `grey_rows` before `paint_songs`, which passes `song_row` the mark's left (`offline_x` less half `CAT_MARK_W`) for a row `catalogue_row_greyed` names, and the length, a right-hand artist and the title's room then end `SONG_COL_GAP` short of it; `song_row` clears the title's `_catw` so `catalogue_fit` never gives back a width the row no longer has. Track Time (`NPTIME`: Remaining, Total) is a third: Now Playing's right-hand time (`np_sync`, `np_time_total`), switched by a tap on it (`np_time_tap`, `np_time_toggle`, which saves it under `theme_keys`' key). A box changed while its list paints repaints once (`widget_move_resize`); a relayout gives the title its full box back and the next paint fits it again. Folder view (`folder_page`, `SONGS_FOLDER`) reads as an album under it (`folder_row`): the set's `folder_pitch` and `folder_body` (OLED's 32; 0 takes `art_pitch` and `art_body`, the `folder_*` immediates in `patch/ipod.json`) make its rows one line, so the compact layouter hides their artwork. Once per listing (the folder path's hash, the showlist's size and first record) `folder_tracks` asks the library for the songs under the folder by `fileurl` (one `era_sql` query, the path's quotes doubled) and keeps each of the folder's own files' tag title and track by the record's `REC_PATH`; a file it doesn't know is named from `REC_NAME` without its extension, a leading track number (which becomes its number) and the longest "Artist - " every such name shares. A song's row then shows that title (written into stock's label once, as stock binds the file name), its number and its length (`duration_text`); a folder's, or any file's that isn't a song, the theme's `folder_d`, `folder_l` or `folder_w` glyph (`tools/art.py` `FOLDER_INKS`) with the name at x 52, stock's chevron left as it is. `list.shuffle.row` turns Songs' action bar (`view_navbar_allplay` on Songs' page, an album's and a playlist's songs: the pages `songs_action_row` sizes) into a Shuffle row the wheel reaches: `action_row` writes "Shuffle" into stock's label 28 px after the text column and centers Sort's bars in a 44 px pill inside the bar inset, and `shuffle_paint` (the bar's background hook) draws the theme's `shuffle_a` glyph (Phosphor's regular `shuffle`, 20 px, the accent's top tone) on the text column with the label in the accent, or, with the selection on it, the accent's bar and the white `shuffle_w`, the label white (`ringnav_style_color` gives the lit label the selection's text color, as a selected row's, so Light Mode's flip leaves it white). `shuffle_key`, ahead of the list's own wheel and Center in `ringnav`, puts the selection on the row (`st.shuffle_on`, `SHUFFLE_STOP`) on a tick up from the first song, and on Sort's bars (`SORT_STOP`) on another when the list has them (OLED hides the bars, and the stop with them: Sort is its hold menu's Sorting row, see [Inset modal](#inset-modal)); a tick down comes back, and the list's bar is hidden meanwhile (`paint_selection`). Center on Shuffle, and a tap on the row, which `ringnav_dispatch` takes before stock's Play All handler, run `shuffle_page`: the page's `p_deque_showlist`, when it holds the surface's rows one for one, through `shuffle_play` (Shuffle Songs: a random first song, the rest in a shuffled order Up Next lists, Now Playing opened); Center on Sort clicks the bars, so stock's sort picker opens. Any row's selection (`select`) and the action view's destroy (`shuffle_gone`) take the selection off the row; another page on top keeps it (`title_gone` and `shuffle_key` leave it), so Return from the Now Playing that Shuffle opened lands on Shuffle, the row that was left. ponytail: Sort stays on the row until the options menu has it (SPEC-next 2). Under it Streaming's rows are one line at the set's `stream_row` 32, and `stream_marks` (`patch/home.c`, from `ringnav_stream`, so Home's Streaming list too) hides each row's logo on its disc (`list_tidal`, `stream_spotify`, `stream_app`, `stream_radio`, `stream_airplay`, `stream_config`) and tags the row; `stream_mark_paint`, which `ringnav_paint` calls only for the rows of the two lists it tagged (`stream_mark_views`), draws the theme's 20 px mark for it centered on x 34 (`oled_stream_*_d`, `_l`, `_w` from `tools/art.py`: Phosphor's `spotify-logo`, `app-window`, `radio`, `airplay` and `sliders-horizontal`, TIDAL's four diamonds drawn there, and q2-coda's own `assets/icons/q2coda/subsonic.svg`) in Text Secondary, white on the selection (the row or, on a settings row, its button), and keeps the row's words at x 52, moving them where the settings layout (`set_row`) or Home's (`library_look`) put them. The settings layout hides every leading image on these rows (`set_child`: OLED's `stream_row` and `set_row` are both 32 and `set_icon` is 0), so a card app's row is marked too: `ringnav_stream` tags each with its app's index (`_stream_app`), and an app whose id `stream_apps` names (`subsonic`) takes that mark, with or without icon files; any other app's own icon (`addon_is_icon`) is hidden and drawn by `stream_own_icon` scaled into the mark's 20 px box, as the image hook leaves it (`icons.addon_mono` grays it); an app without one shows `stream_app`, so `app-window`. `patch/feedback.c` gives OLED its feedback forms: `feedback_toast_paint` (from the background hook, `ringnav_paint_bg`) takes `msginfo_dialog`, clears the dialog's background and fits its first line onto a `#1c1c1e` pill (y 236 to 268, the text's measured width and 16 px each side) in Inter at 16 px, so the page shows round it; `paint_selection` draws the page's held row under the toast as under a sliding page, and `bar_title_sync` treats the window under it (`feedback_under`, the window manager's last window before it) as the top, so the page keeps its title and Shuffle row. `toast` lasts 1.5 s under it. `confirm_prompt` hands `confirminfo_dialog` to `feedback_confirm_dress` on its first paint, which draws it as the confirmation card ([oled-design](oled-design.md#confirmation-card)): the prompt's lines are hidden and its text, through a table of stock's English prompts (`asks`, each with its title, verb and any body), becomes the card's title; the dialog's background is cleared so the page shows, with the status row painted under the card's scrim (`feedback_confirm_bar`, `confirm_paint`); `img_cancel` and `img_enter` become the card's answers, 8 px in from its sides (`confirm_surface` keeps their width in `paint_selection`), their words cleared and painted over the selection by `confirm_rows_paint` (the second the verb: `asks`, the prompt's first word when it is a verb, or `confirm_over`'s; red, after a 12 px gap, when it loses something). Delete Song's `msg_delcheckbutton` is the card's switch row above them: its words painted, a click handler that makes it a wheel stop (the check turns itself on any click, Center's too), and `switch_mark` by its value. `feedback_switch_bar` puts the selection's bar on Sleep Timer's switch row while its fields are hidden (the switch off), the row's words white through `st.sel_accent`. `ringnav_stream_row` opens `feedback_offline`'s page (`empty_open`'s `empty_page`, titled Streaming: the empty state, "Not Connected", **Turn on Wi-Fi**, which opens `systemset/wifi_page`) for Tidal's row with no link under OLED, in place of stock's toast. Playlists' action rows take the playlists' pitch (`pl_pitch`), and `pl_rows` sets the list's `item_height` to it, as the Add to Playlist picker lays its rows out by that. The page's list is built at the set's `playlist_pitch` (52, `page_detail`'s height: `tools/ipod.py` `page_rows`), so `fit_rows` ends its box on a whole playlist row and the list takes no `item_height` from the bin, which the 32 px `default_item_height` of a list beside the settings rows would add (`navigation.c` `settings_list`). The App Store's lone Check for Updates line is centered in its row. `qm_run` toasts what Play Next, Add to Queue and the favorite rows did. The empty state (`empty_state`, [oled-design](oled-design.md#empty-and-offline)) is one view over the page, named `_empty_state` and insensitive so the rows beside it keep their taps, holding the glyph, title, hint, button label and stack top in its props for `empty_state_paint` (from `ringnav_paint_bg`), and at most one button, a one-row list named `_empty_row` the capsule's height with blank words and no fill, whose capsule `empty_state_paint` draws (`ui_cta_paint`) and whose selection bar `paint_selection` leaves out (`empty_button`); Songs' Scan Music Now is stock's `btn_upmusic` made the same band, its capsule drawn by `feedback_scan_bar`; it is made once per page and written again on each call, and a call with no state hides it. `empty_list` is `page_list` with no rows, its caption hidden for the status row, and the empty state in the body (Most Played, Long Songs, Ratings' lists, Era, Downloads, Chapters, Internet Radio's station lists, Cover Flow); `empty_open` is a page of its own holding only that; `empty_paint` paints the stack for Search's sheet; and from the bar's paint an `allmusic_page` whose `p_deque_showlist` is empty (`feedback_songs`, by `g_class_type`, the Shuffle row hidden) and an empty `folder_page` (`feedback_folder`) show theirs. Playlists' sits under its rows (`image_wait`, stock's spinner, sized to nothing), and Car Remote's under its switch.
