The older note is two labels (`feedback_empty`, `feedback_note`) centered between the end of the page's rows and y 282: `page_empty` uses it in place of its first line (Internet Radio's Loading and Battery History), and so do Spotify's message, the App Store's Check for Updates row and a card app's empty page. `feedback_shuffled`, from `shuffle_play` and `shuffle_groups`, opens a window of its own over the Now Playing they open: the theme's `confirm_shuffle` art (Phosphor's bold shuffle at 56 px in the accent, `tools/art.py`), what was shuffled and the song count, closed by a 1.2 s timer or the first key. `paint_separators` draws `list.divider.ink` under a page_list's two-line rows too, and `page_fit` cuts a page_list's box to the whole rows ending by `list_end` (Era, Most Played, Long Songs, Ratings' lists), as `fit_rows` does stock's.

**A theme's own accent.** `<colorScheme name="oled-blue" base="cobalt" label="Blue" tones="#2160d8 #2160d8 #2160d8 #2160d8 #2160d8"/>` (OLED's) adds a scheme after the `ACCENTS` rows that only this theme has: it starts from its `base` row's roles, and `tones`, five colors in an `ACCENTS` row's order (selection top, bottom, light tone, red tone, highlight), replace that row's tones, so its selection, progress fill and mapped reds are exact without a shared row every theme would offer. Without `tones` it takes its base's. The tones are one row for both halves: Light Mode keeps a colored scheme's, and gives a neutral one its red tone (`tone_of`). `tones` on an `ACCENTS` row is refused. `<colorSchemes accents="oled-blue"/>` offers it alone. A theme holds at most 10 schemes, the nine rows and its own, so a theme has room for one scheme of its own. Ten is the format's own bound (`tools/theme.py`), not a reader's: `config_value` reads up to three digits and stock's `write_int_config` writes any; past 32 the accents mask (`option_t.values`) could not hold a scheme.

**The selection bar's shape.** On a list row the bar is `list.selection.inset` in from each side of the row (default `SEL_INSET`, 6; OLED's 16) and its ends round by `list.selection.radius` at most (default `SEL_MAX_RADIUS`, 160, more than half any row, which is the pill; OLED's 8): the radius drawn is the lesser of it and `pill_radius`'s, so a cover's corner still shrinks it, and 0 is square ends, still inset. A grid tile's card is square.

**The progress bar's track.** `playing.scrubber.track` (default `TRACK_COLOR`, `#1c1c1c`) is the plain bar's track: `np_theme` writes it into the slider's `bg_color` in each state, and writes `TRACK_COLOR` back after a theme with another, so a theme on the asset's color writes nothing. The volume over Now Playing and Spotify's bar draw it too. It is one value for both halves, which Light Mode treats as it treats `TRACK_COLOR`. OLED's is `#333333`.

**Rows.** `list.row.tall_font`/`tall_px` (`ROLE_TALL`) are a two-line row's title, and `list.divider.ink` the 1 px divider under each two-line row (`paint_separators`), final in each half. A final value a half leaves out is the other half's, flipped (`half()`).

**The bar's title.** On OLED's status row the bar's `label_title` names the top window by `bar_title_sync`'s rule, Home by the list it shows (`coverflow_home_title`: "Q2 Muse" on its own list, else "Library", "Streaming" or "Settings"); a page with no title leaves it empty and the clock centered. It is written during a paint, where an invalidate is lost, so `title_due` forces it on to the panel just after. The clock stays beside the title (`clock_place`; [ipod.md](ipod.md#status-bar-and-clock)). The title and clock are laid out at the set's `bar_px` (`tools/ipod.py` `status_row`) and drawn at `bar.title.font_size`, so `tools/theme.py` rejects a `bar.title.font_size` other than the `bar_px` of each of the theme's sets that has one.

**Stock details the slider pages lean on.** `playset_bootvol_page_init` makes `img_bootswitch` in `view_navbar` after the load, so `slider_paint` finds it at its first paint. Stock's slider fills its knob in `border_color` and draws none when it is clear (`0x62e290`).

**Message screens.** `msg_open` (`patch/scan_page.c`) takes Update Local Music's `updatemusic_dialog` as the loader hands it over (USB mode's page stays stock's); stock's `img_animation`, `label_msg` and `label_scanfolder` stay by name, hidden, and `btn_no` keeps its binding, laid unseen (no fill, no words) over the painted button. `oled_scan` adds a label for the folder's name, which scrolls as the house marquee; `msg_paint` paints the status row the dialog covers first (`widget_paint` of the system bar, as `cc_paint` does; `bar_title_sync` lets the dialog title it, "Update Library", through `msg_title`), then the rest as the empty states' stack ([oled-design](oled-design.md#update-library)): the figure, the title, the line and the shared button (`ui_button`), in screen rows. While the scan runs (`SCAN_DONE` 0), the figure is Software Update's spinner (a frame each 80 ms poll) and the title the count, "1,284 songs found", until it can be measured: stock gives no total, so `msg_sync` reads the first number in `label_msg` against the songs a detached worker counts as the dialog opens (`msg_count`, `library_count`, its own connection), and on a whole-library scan (`SCAN_WHOLE` 1, by our reading of stock's code) with the count at most that total the figure is a ring with the percent, held at 99%, and the title "312 of 704 songs". The line is the last name in the hidden `label_scanfolder` after a folder glyph (the card's root as it is). Stock's ending, read from its own code (`updatemusic_dialog_refresh`, `updatemusic_dialog_on_timer`): once `wait_scan` sets `SCAN_DONE`, each 200 ms tick writes `scan_updatefinish` with the count, or `msg_no_storage` when the stop flag (`toolsGetUserStop`) is 2 (`/mnt/data` full), and the third tick pauses the animation, sleeps 2 s on the UI thread and quits the dialog. So the page's ending (`scan_state`) is the check circle with "Library Updated" and the songs ("738 songs, 34 new" when a whole scan grew the library past the count before it), "Scan Stopped" after Stop (flag 1: stock's Stop only stops the scan while the counter is under 3, and the same ending follows), or the memory chip with "Not Enough Space" (flag 2), each with Done in the accent; it holds until stock closes the dialog. Stock has no card-removed state: with the card pulled mid-scan (emulator: its music moved away and `/tmp/mmc_add` removed, 2026-11-16) it ends as a finish with the songs it had read, which become the library (3,800 songs fell to 3,000), and toasts its own "SD Card Removed". A finish with `/tmp/mmc_add` gone (stock's mount marks the card with it) is therefore drawn as the card glyph, "SD Card Removed" and "Put it back and scan again", not as Library Updated. `msg_sync` also runs in the paint hook, so it writes the folder's label only when it differs, and marks any change (`msg_dirty`) for the next poll to repaint the whole stack: stock's own repaint of its hidden label's box can read the ending first, which left Stop under the check in the emulator. Center presses the button there (`ringnav`, a click on `btn_no`), as a tap does; Return stops the scan as stock's does.

**USB Storage's eject.** `ringnav_ui_load` adds `usb_poll` to USB Storage's `usbmode_page` (`g_usbmode` not 1) as a 500 ms widget timer, so it goes with the page. Stock's `storage_config.sh` exports the card as LUN 0 of the configfs gadget `storage_demo`. The computer's eject is a SCSI START STOP UNIT with LoEj set and Start clear. Linux 5.10's `f_mass_storage` answers it in `do_start_stop` with `fsg_lun_close`, unless the host holds PREVENT ALLOW MEDIUM REMOVAL ([f_mass_storage.c](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v5.10/source/drivers/usb/gadget/function/f_mass_storage.c#L1298)). After that, `functions/mass_storage.msg/lun.0/file` reads empty (`fsg_show_file`, [storage_common.c](https://elixir.bootlin.com/linux/v5.10/source/drivers/usb/gadget/function/storage_common.c#L330)). Once that file has read a path, an empty read is the eject. A missing file (no gadget yet, or one torn down) is none. Stock's timer (0x542d44, every 500 ms) rewrites `scrlabel_info` "USB Connected" through `usbmode_showface`, so `usb_poll` hides it and puts an `s_scrlabel_white24c` label in its place. The LUN stays closed until stock rebuilds the gadget, so the poll ends there and the page never goes back to Connected. Stock's teardown (`storage_config.sh stop`, from `usbmode_exit` at the page's window close, on the UI thread) unbinds the UDC, which closes nothing, then removes `lun.0`, which closes the LUN and its file together, so no tick reads it empty there. Limit: only a host that sends LoEj counts (macOS Finder, Linux `eject` and udisks, Windows Explorer's Eject). Windows' Safely Remove Hardware may only stop the device, which leaves the page on Connected. The vendor kernel (5.10.21 X2000) builds `f_mass_storage` in, and its xImage carries mainline's eject and close-backing-file messages; its only visible change there is the `pc_check` parameter (stock's PC-link status).

**USB DAC on a host that never reads the card.** Stock's `check_usb_status` (`0x4f3744`, once a second from the idle loop `on_wm_idle_status`) starts a gadget as soon as a cable is in (`g_usbdet_value` 1, `g_usblink_status` 1): under Audio and DAC (`g_usbmode` 1) the UAC2 one (`uac_device_config.sh start`), otherwise the card's (`storage_config.sh start`). It waits there until `toolsGetpclinkStatus` (`0x5d1ebc`) returns 1 (`g_usblink_status` 2), and only then does `on_wm_timer_dialog` open `usbmode_page`. For the Q2 (device type 23, the word `platform_init` hands `initToolsModule`) the link is a UDC state (`/sys/class/udc/13500000.otg/state`) of `configured`, in both USB modes. A charger has no host, so the UDC never reads `configured` there. Up to stock V1.32 the gate was `/sys/module/usb_f_mass_storage/parameters/pc_check`, which the vendor kernel sets when the host sends the drive a SCSI command, and the storage gadget came up first in both modes: a Nintendo Switch 2 configures the gadget and never sends it a SCSI command, so stock stayed a drive nobody read (#290). Q2 Muse hooked `check_usb_status` for that until its base moved to V1.34 (`patch/usb_dac.c`, gone), which does the same itself.

**Motion.** A theme's `<view name="motion">` holds one `<element>` per kind, `ms` and `easing` (`linear`, `cubic_out` and the rest of AWTK's names, and `follow` on Cover Flow's two steps: see [its step](#coverflow-step)) on each, and defaults to 0 ms; OLED's come from `ROLE_MACROS` (`MOTION_ROLES`: `PAGE_SLIDE_MS` and the rest, `patch/offsets.inc`). A window kind (`page`, `playing`, `coverflow`) also takes `anim` (`htranslate` unless `fade` or another AWTK animation) and becomes the window's `anim_hint`, e.g. `htranslate(duration=300,easing=sin_inout)`, as it loads or opens (`motion_load`, `motion_open`); a kind with no ms writes nothing and leaves the asset's own hint. `page` is a stock page that slides, `playing` Now Playing's close (its open stays immediate), and `coverflow` its page. No kind hints a page that has no slide of its own, nor any dialog: a dialog's background is clear, and an animated window is two snapshots, so a fade over a clear one shows black first (see [Queue menu](#queue-menu)). Every dialog, popup and the hold menu opens and closes in one frame. A widget kind (`inplace`, `swap`, `step`, `step_fast`, `coverflow_step`, `coverflow_step_fast`) glides a widget's own property with an animator: a level inside a page, Home's lists to and from Settings, a slide menu's wheel step, slow and fast (`step_fast` within `HOME_FAST_WINDOW_MS` of the last), and Cover Flow's, the same. `recall ms` is how long a remembered row's glide takes (0 jumps). Every reader takes these rows through `motion_row` (`patch/ui_kit.c`), which under Reduce Motion (`IPOD REDUCEMOTION`, `motion_reduced`) answers `fade(duration=150)` for a window kind (Page's too, whose slide is its windows' asset hint `SLIDE`, so `motion_load` writes the fade over it on each window it loads), ms 0 for `inplace` and `swap`, and the steps as they are; the recall goes through `motion_ms`. A window already loaded keeps the hint it took, so the change shows from the next window opened. The rest of the payload's animations, each with its own `*_MS`, take their duration from `motion_ms(ms, kind)`, their curve from `motion_ease` (AWTK's `easing_type_t` numbers) and, where they have no loop pass of their own, their frames from one shared timer (`anim_start`, `motion_frames`: a 16 ms `timer_add` that repaints the top window and removes itself 16 ms after the last run ends); overlays (a toast, the confirmation card) run through `ovm_t`. A toast's exit outlives its dialog: `toast_gone` (its `EVT_DESTROY`) starts the exit and `feedback_toast_leave`, from `ringnav_paint`, paints the pill over the page under it until the exit ends. The confirmation card and a toast fade through their dialog's `widget_set_opacity`, which the shared timer sets on each frame (`ovm_bind`, `ovm_opacity`; 255 at once for an enter under Reduce Motion), from `confirm` on for the card and from the toast's first paint, at stock's 255, for a toast; `ovm_bind` forgets the dialog on its `EVT_DESTROY`. Never from the dialog's own paint: stock's `widget_paint` (demo 0x672848) returns before any paint hook while a widget's opacity byte (+0x34) is under 9 (`OVM_PAINT_MIN`), so a dialog at 0 whose paint was to raise it was never painted again: the card showed only the status row's dim, and a toast nothing. The card's answer waits the exit's 120 ms. The marquee, the volume and slider eases, the progress fill, the scroll indicator's and A-Z index's fades and the spinners are feedback, kept under Reduce Motion, and keep their own timers.

**Slider pages.** `slider_open` takes stock's Backlight, Max Volume, Balance and Boot Volume windows as they load, before their init, into the slider page's own form (`patch/slider_page.c`, [oled-design](oled-design.md#progress-and-sliders)), with stock's widgets kept by name.

**Dialogs.** Every question is the confirmation card over the page that asked (`confirm`, stock's confirm pop-up dressed as it by `feedback_confirm_dress`: the dialog's background cleared so the page shows, the card painted under its cells, the cells' words painted over the selection by `confirm_rows_paint`; ours on stock's `sortselect_dialog`, as the menu sheet's pickers; [Confirmation card](oled-design.md#confirmation-card)), the toast a pill over the page, and an empty page the empty state, the note under a page's rows its own form (`patch/feedback.c`, `feedback_confirm_dress`, `feedback_toast_paint`, `empty_state`, `feedback_empty`; [oled-design](oled-design.md#dialogs-and-toasts), [Empty and offline](oled-design.md#empty-and-offline)).

<a id="inset-modal"></a>**Menu sheet.** OLED draws its menus as [oled-design.md](oled-design.md#menus)'s frosted page sheet (`patch/menu_modal.c`). Now Playing's More is a stock window, which its asset makes a dialog (`modal_page`: root type `dialog`, the screen's box, no slide), so the window manager keeps painting Now Playing under it; its init (`ringnav_playermore`) sets `to_modal` 0, as sortselect's init does, so `navigator_to` returns rather than running `dialog_modal`'s loop. `modal_frame` hides the title bar, clears the dialog's background, puts the list at y 50 (58 with no header) down to the screen's foot and stacks the rows 32 px high and the screen's width (`modal_row_w`); the header's space is an empty label 72 px high named `_mm_head` at the head of the rows, so it scrolls away with them, and a gap is an empty label 12 px high; neither is a row (`collect` takes only clickable widgets). The header (`modal_head`: name, line under it, cover) is set by the caller before the frame: `qm_open`, `modal_more` (the playing song, `queue_now`), `ringnav_playlistsmore` and `playlist_page_hold`; a picker over a sheet copies that sheet's. A cover is the player's own for the playing song (`now_cover`), else the server library's (`catalogue_cover`) or Cover Flow's cached one (`art_path` by `album_key`), as an album page finds it. The list's content is padded by what lies past the list end (y 282 to 320) and `list_pad` reads that pad (`_list_pad`, `_list_padded`), so `scroll_end` stops the wheel's and a drag's last row on y 282; `sel_height` gives a sheet's rows the height to the list end (`modal_sel_height`) and `fit_top` leaves them unsnapped, since they pass under the sheet's top fade. The list's `item_height` and `default_item_height` go to 0, so the stock layouter stacks each child at its own height and `settings_list` never reads the list as settings rows. `modal_paint`, from `ringnav_paint_bg` on the dialog, draws the page receding and the sheet straight into the screen's 375 x 320 BGRA buffer, as `engine.c`'s `eng_paint` does, within the canvas's clip: on the first paint whose clip is the whole screen, while nothing slides, `sheet_build` reads the page under it there (every window under the dialog has just painted) and makes, once, the 80 rows the receding page can show in (bilinear at 94% about the center, then dimmed) and the material for the sheet's rows (the receding page averaged onto a 94 x 80 grid, three box passes of radius 5 each way, scaled back bilinearly, its color raised 1.6 times from its luma, 28% kept under 6% white or, in Light Mode, under 75% white, with no grain; the grid holds each cell's sum, 16 times its mean, and every step keeps those 16ths, rounding, down to the one write in whole levels, dithered by a 4 x 4 Bayer matrix (`sh_dither`): darkened to 28%, a smooth page spans as few as 8 levels across the sheet, and whole levels drew it as bands often over 100 px wide and about 1.5 levels dark, from truncating at each step), about 540 KB on the heap until the last open sheet closes, when what it drew straight into the buffer is cleared to black and the whole screen is painted again (`modal_gone`, `sheet_repaint`): a page that paints nothing under the status row, Edit Home's, would keep it; the sheet's 40 px top corners are antialiased from a table of their insets. Until then, and on a window's snapshot, it draws the page dimmed in place and a flat `#1C1C1E` sheet. `paint_modal_rows`, on the rows' surface after the selection, draws each row's symbol (`menu_<stem>_<d|l|w>`, `tools/art.py` `MENU_ICONS`), value (ending in an ellipsis short of its label) and direction caret from the props `modal_row` left on it; a destructive row (`modal_red`: `QA_DELETE`, Delete Song, Delete Playlist, a `trash` action of `modal_actions`) sets its label red, white while lit, and `paint_selection` fills its bar `#FF3B30`. `modal_after`, from `ringnav_paint` on the rows' surface once they are painted, draws the header at the rows' scroll and fades the rows into the material by `foot_alpha` from y 266 and, once scrolled, for 14 px under the list's top, the lit row never, all within the rows' box. The scroll indicator is a list's. `paint_selection` keeps a row bar the rows' own width and lights the row of the page under a sheet, which names what the menu acts on, and `bar_title_sync` titles the bar from the page under one (`feedback_under`) and leaves Songs' action row in place, so after a dialog over the sheet that wrote its own title (Delete Playlist's confirm, `feedback_confirm`) closes, the bar names the page again. The menu's row is lit from the pass after it opens (`modal_lit`): a tap that opened it would otherwise hide the selection. Return closes the dialog itself (`modal_back`, in place of stock's `on_common_keyup`, which goes back a page and would close the page under it). The sheet moves through ui_kit.h's `ovm_t` ([Overlay motion](oled-design.md#overlay-motion); `sheet_run`, the one place its timing and easing are given): `modal_frame` registering the first open sheet sets it waiting (`sheet_wait`: progress 0, the rows 280 px low), and its first whole paint, once the material is made, keeps the page alone (`sheet_start`, a 375 x 320 copy, 480 KB until the last sheet closes) starts the rise (260 ms `cubic_out`, `ovm_enter`) and a 16 ms timer (`sheet_tick`) that reads its level (`ovm_level`), moves the rows (`sheet_shift`: the list, or a dialog of rows alone's rows) and paints the screen again; `sheet_frame` draws each frame from the kept page, scaled from 100% to 94% about the center and dimmed by the progress, under the material faded in by it from the sheet's lowered top with its corners, and `modal_after` lowers the header with the rows. Return (`modal_back`, `pick_back`, the hold menu's `qm_back`, Up Next's `un_back`) goes through `modal_close`, as does a finger on Up Next (`modal_touch_close` binds `sheet_touch` on its window for the pointer's down, move-before, up-before and abort, all before the window's children): a tap whose down and lift are both above `SH_TOP`, or a drag down from a down on the strip above the rows or on rows whose `SCROLL_Y` is 0. The drag is claimed in the move-before that first finds it `TAP_PX` down and more down than across, before the rows see that move: left to them, stock's scroll_view takes it as a scroll from that move on and aborts the press through the window (`EVT_POINTER_ABORT` with each move, seen on the emulator with real touch input on 2026-11-18), which is how a pull that came down a few px under the grab bar, on the rows, left the sheet up on the device. Claiming, `sheet_touch` aborts the window's pressed widgets itself (`mt.aborting` lets its own abort pass) and returns `STOP` for the moves and the lift; a drag up or sideways first stays the rows'. Claimed with the sheet standing (`MO_UP`, the material and the kept page there, motion not reduced), the sheet follows the finger (`MO_DRAG`: `sheet_drag` sets `mo.off` to the drag and `mo.e` to the level the rise has at that drop, `drag_level`, and moves the rows with `sheet_shift`), so `sheet_frame` draws the page behind coming forward as it drops. A lift 48 px (`SH_DRAG_PX`) or more below the down closes it, however far across: a thumb holding the Q2 swipes down on a slant, and at 30 to 35 degrees off the vertical the half-as-far-across rule this lift once had sent the sheet back up, which is how a swipe down still left Up Next open on the device (2026-11-21; reproduced on the emulator with the panel's own event stream); short of that (or another's abort, a swipe back's) it rises back from where it is (`drag_back`: `ovm_enter` with its `from` set to the drag's level). `sheet_touch_close` runs the close from the next pass, once (`_mm_closing`), while the window is still a sheet (`modal_win`): with the material and the kept page it falls (180 ms quadratic ease-in, `ovm_exit`, from where a rise or the finger left it), `modal_closing` makes `ringnav_keyup` take every key meanwhile, and `sheet_tick` closes the window at its end; with neither, or for a picker over another sheet, it closes at once. A pick closes at once. Under Reduce Motion `sheet_frame` draws the sheet in place and cross-fades the strip above the rows from the kept page, and `modal_after` the rows' box, linear, over `ovm_t`'s 150 ms in and 120 ms out. Up Next (`upnext.c`) is a sheet with `_mm_own` set, so `modal_frame` keeps each row's own height (46 px songs, 24 px Playing Next, 26 px "From"); its header is the playing song (`modal_head` and `modal_head_bars`, which draws `un_bars` after the name), taken again when the rows are (a frame with a new header replaces the old), and a row's cover and Clear's pill round onto the material (`modal_corners`). In More, stock's rows keep their buttons and handlers: the symbol comes from each row's kind (`PLAYMORE_ROWS` by the button's name), AirPlay's and Get Album Lyrics' from their images; stock's Download Cover & Lyrics reads Get Cover & Lyrics; Delete Song moves last behind a gap (its confirm is stock's); A-B Repeat's stock switch image hides and `modal_row_paint` draws the theme's switch on the right column from that image's state (`switch_on`, `switch_off`: `switch_mark` in `patch/list_marks.c`, 40x24 with a 20 px knob, as settings rows' are drawn); Multiple Speed's four buttons hide, insensitive too (stock's hit test skips only an insensitive widget, so a hidden one still took a tap on the row and set its speed; a pick dispatches its click to the button all the same), and its row reads "Speed" with the speed as its value, opening `modal_pick`, a sortselect dialog of the four (the Shuffle and Repeat pickers' too), under which More's rows, sheet and header hide (the dialog stays shown: a hidden window hands the keys to the page under it); a pick sends stock's own speed button for it a click, so stock's debounce, `PLAYSPEED` and the folder speed (`ringnav_speed`) are unchanged. In the hold menu, a setting's value is its choice without the label's word (`qm_value_name`), and Group by flips in place on Center (`qm_run`, which leaves the sheet open and writes the setting rows' values again, `qm_values`). ponytail: the material is made once, so a page that changes under an open sheet (Now Playing's time) shows as it was; making it again on each whole paint would follow it.

The hold menu (`qm_open`) is the same panel: every row takes its symbol by action, and Shuffle, Repeat and Group by are settings, their values on the right column; the set writes Favorites in US English. On Songs (class `0xf001`) the menu has no Sorting row: Songs' order is Settings > Playback > Library > Sorting's Songs picker (`library_settings.c`), and the Shuffle row's Sort bars hide (`action_row`), and the row's wheel stop with them (`shuffle_key`). `patch/song_sort.c` keeps the order: Recently Added is stock's `g_sort_flag` 3 or 4 (newest or oldest first), which `getAllMusic`'s query takes; with the flag 0 (title order) `[IPOD] SONGSORT` and `SONGDOWN` name Title, Artist or Album and the direction, and `songs_load` reorders the loaded list (`song_order`: a stable merge sort of indices by artist, or by album then disc and track, an untagged name last either way, then the records moved into place a cycle at a time, whole, as Play Next moves rows). A pick writes all three keys at once and sets `g_sort_changeflag` (`song_sort_commit`), which Songs reads as it comes back to the top, as after stock's picker. `name_sorted` (`patch/az_index.c`) keeps the fast-scroll letter for titles A to Z alone. Other themes keep stock's picker and order.

A playlist's More (`ringnav_playlistsmore`) is a dialog over Playlists the same way, its rows the list_items in the dialog itself, placed in the panel by `modal_frame` with no list: Rename, Edit Playlist, then Delete Playlist after a gap, which asks first (stock's confirm).

**A page's switch.** The pages have no toolbars (`tools/ipod.py` `patch_asset`), so stock's toolbar switch moves to a row reading On or Off: `ringnav_sleeptimer` on Sleep Timer.

**Final text.** `text_ink` stores a label's final color as what Light Mode's style hook turns into it, so the stored value depends on the half. `light_apply`'s `text_inks` walks the windows at Auto's turn and writes each again.

**Home's pane.** It follows the highlighted row (`coverflow_home_row()`, from `paint_selection` and the wheel): Now Playing's row shows the playing cover and every other row the library's slideshow (`art_source`, [ipod.md](ipod.md#home)).

**Light and dark.** Every scheme has a dark and a light half (`theme_t.schemes`, `theme_t.light`). Light Mode (Off, On, Auto) picks one through `scheme()`, and a scheme's `mode` can keep it to one. theme.xml states a half's drawn-as-stated colors as `light.<key>`/`dark.<key>` (unprefixed: the dark half, stock's terms), and a half it leaves out is the flip of the other's grays. A theme that states no final value has one array serve both of its halves.

**Other keys.** `tools/theme.py` also reads `list.art.*` (x, text_x, text_end, placeholder, radius) and `list.scrollbar.*` (`paint_scrollbar`'s track and thumb while the wheel turns, from a list's border paint, with stock's bar drawn clear; `sb_w` 0 keeps stock's).

### Playlists without a toolbar

With no toolbars `tools/ipod.py` hides `view_navbar` and takes its room for the list, whose `default_item_height` is the Songs pitch with no `item_height`: `children_layouter_list_view` (`0x5fcd44`) then gives each row its own height, so 52 px playlists stack with 32 px action rows. `ringnav_playlist`, after every stock rebuild (`0x4b5444`), dresses the rows (`pl_dress`): the tile row at index 0 hides and each playlist row's art (stock's 52 px image, [Playlist art](#playlist-art)) shows only where the set has row art (`geom(G_ART)`, OLED's; not in the picker), at the page rows' art place (x 22) with the text from x 80 and 60 px narrower, as an album row's, else hides; the parts take `pl_fit`'s places on the page rows' boxes, under a full-width button so the chevron and band are the list's. Stock's count label is re-worded from its own number, so no second query runs. Rows it can't have are added: Select All, New Playlist… and Select Playlists… restacked to indexes 1 to 3, above the playlists (the two modes never show Select All with the other two), then Import Playlists, Export, Delete and Done; the Add to Playlist picker, which has no tile row, gets New Playlist… alone, at index 0. They are shown by `pl_rows` for the mode, each list item tagged with its action (`PL_ACT`), which `pl_rows` reads in one walk, so no row is found by its place. Select All reads Deselect All while `g_allselect_flag` (`0xa4ca30`) is set: stock's Select All (`0x4b46a4`) toggles on it, and a row's mark sets it to whether every row is marked (`0x4b4950`), so a hand-marked full list clears on the next tap. No stock function is replaced. Each row's click runs next pass (the latest click in a pass wins; the action is the timer's ctx) and finds its target by the handler bound to it, in the hidden toolbar or the hidden tile row (`pl_stock`), and dispatches a click there, so `g_navbar_status`, the marks in `p_vector_select_record`, every dialog and the reload stay stock's; `0x4b44d4` and `0x4b45ec` rebuild only the toolbar, so `pl_rows` runs after them, and after each mark on a second click handler. A row is its action whatever scrolled: nothing keys on an index. The separators (`PAGE_TALL`) go on every shown row, playlist or action, but the list's last, in one walk from the end. With nothing remembered (a first open, or a count changed), `reconcile`'s fresh-page row, the first visible, moves past an action row to the first playlist (`pl_first`), as stock's and the iPod's lists hold playlists alone; an empty list stays on New Playlist…. Just after New Playlist made one, it lands on that one instead, as an iPod's list lands on what was added: `ringnav_playlist_create` keeps the new name (`pl_made`) and `pl_first` finds the playlist row whose `p_deque_playlist` record has it, then forgets it. A remembered row comes back by its text (position memory), so the playlists' shift by two rows lands on the same playlist. Between modes `pl_rows` maps the selection: into select mode on the first playlist, out of it a playlist keeps its own, Select All goes to the first playlist and an action row to Select Playlists…. Export reads `g_navbar_status` after its confirm returns, which `dialog_modal` (`0x65271c`) does before an idle closes the dialog (`0x6521dc`), so a marked Export stays marked; that close is what ends select mode (`0x4b58d4`, `EVT_WINDOW_TO_FOREGROUND`), as stock's. Return in select mode runs Done: `0x4f2394`, which would close the page and leave the flag set, is rebound to `pl_keyup`, which falls through to it when no Done target exists; a page destroyed in the mode (held Return to Home, `PL_MARKING` set) clears the flag, and only then. Stock's hit from x 286 opens More outside select mode (`0x4b48a8` branches on `g_navbar_status`, `0x4b4988`), so every row's click goes through `pl_pick` first: a picker's rows pick with a fresh click at x 0, and in the list a tap left of the dots' column (from x 333), the chevron's column (from x 317, `CHEVRON_W` from the edge) with it, opens the playlist the same way. The dots sit at the right edge, centered on the picker's tick (x 346), as the other trailing marks and values do, since only the selected row has a chevron; on that row the chevron shows in their place, and a tap opens the playlist out to the edge (its More is the hold's). The picker draws no chevron, since a pick adds and closes. Stock's relayout of a playlist row keeps `pl_fit`'s places: `compact_row_layout` hands a `PL_ROW` item's button to `pl_fit`. The dots and marks are `paint_radio`'s; stock's `img_more` keeps its name for the hold menu, its image emptied as a ring. The bar reads the toolbar's first label, which stock writes with the last list opened (`g_navbar_name`); `pl_rows` writes what the mode is.

**Playlists' add mode and memory.** `PLAYLIST_ADD_MODE` is one global that only a mode 2 pick clears, and the page reads it as it comes back to the front, so a page below a picker rebuilt in the picker's form. `ringnav_playlist` keeps each window's own in a prop and writes it back before each rebuild. Opening a playlist writes `g_local_classinfo_save` (`0x4b4be8`), which `context_now`'s scope hashed, so the page lost its row on the way back; its scope is the add mode alone, so the picker keeps its own row.

## Page transitions (iPod)

Stock V1.36 carries AWTK's window animators and uses one: `saverscreen_page.bin` has `close_anim_hint` `slide_left(duration=200,easing=cubic_out)`, the only hint in the stock assets (the lock window, which the build leaves out: [Screen off and wake](#screen-off-and-wake)). The window manager builds the animator named by a window's `anim_hint` (`window_animator_htranslate_create`, `0x696fb8`, for `htranslate`) when it opens or closes. `navigator_to_with_context` (`0x4f6e74`) opens a page above the rest and `navigator_back` (`0x4f6ffc`) is `window_manager_back`, so the page below stays alive and Return reverses the slide.

iPod sets the hint in its assets ([ipod.md](ipod.md#transitions)). `htranslate` animates two snapshots. `window_animator_prepare` (`0x696498`) paints both pages into offline canvases, through the payload's paint hooks, before `window_manager_is_animating` (`0x6810a4`) becomes true and while the sliding page is the top window; a hinted page is not painted before that, so its snapshot is its first paint. Each frame then blits the snapshots (the page under drifting and darkening: [Page parallax](#page-parallax)) and paints only the status bar. The payload follows the snapshots in four places (`slides()`, `patch/navigation.c`). A surface whose own window is under a sliding top window draws the row it holds and nothing else: loading, recall and settling read the top page's state. A sliding page reveals its remembered row at once instead of by the glide, so it does not arrive mid-glide. Home's art is checked when Home itself is painted, not only when it is the top window. After a touch, a Return by button ends [touch mode](#touch-mode) on a 0 ms timer instead of at once: the closing page's snapshot, painted inside stock's handling of the release, keeps its row hidden, while the page behind shows its own.

## Status bar (iPod)

The background hook also handles top-level widgets, whose parent is the window manager. The status bar widget, which `system_bar_init` stores in the `system_bar` global (`0xa4e8a0`, a size-checked `CONTEXT_DATA` entry), gets one `canvas_fill_rect` in black, `BAR_COLOR` (`#000000`), without a highlight, with the LCD fill color restored.

`label_clock` in the bar shows the device's local time, read once a minute rather than on paint: `clock_show` calls `time` and `localtime_r` (stock libc, with a caller-owned time buffer) for the hour and minute (`struct tm` `+8`, `+4`), applies Auto Light Mode's hour, and arms a timer due at the next minute (`60 - tm_sec` seconds; a minute after a failed read). The label follows stock's 24-hour setting (`g_time24h_flag`): `%02d:%02d` (`18:14`), or, on a bar with its own title (OLED's status row), `%d:%02d` so it clears the title, or `%d:%02d %s`, a 12-hour clock without seconds or a leading zero (`12:05 AM`, `6:14 PM`), through `tk_snprintf`, then `widget_set_text_utf8`. A failed `time` (`-1`) or `localtime_r` (null), or an out-of-range field, shows `--:--`. The minute and the 24-hour setting are kept as a key, so the label is looked up and written only when what it shows changes. Besides the timer, `clock_show` runs at once for a new time zone (`ringnav_timezone`), a time set by hand, and a wake, and the pass after the bar first paints or paints with a new 24-hour setting rearms it at 0 ms; a network time sync while lit shows at the next minute. Nothing else reads the time, so stock threads' `localtime` (one shared static buffer) has nothing to race. Every page and dialog shows it. There is no volume flash: stock `on_wm_keyup_fun` opens `dialog/volume_dialog` on every volume turn (`0x4f333c`).

The same paints run `bar_sync`. `systembar_showface` (`0x5417d0`) sets `img_bt`'s image every tick: a codec badge (`bar_sbc`, `bar_aac`, `bar_aptx`, `bar_aptxhd`, `bar_ldac`, by `bt_showcoding`) while Bluetooth is linked, otherwise `bar_bt` or `bar_btcon`. It also sets `img_battery`'s image (`bar_charge`, `bar_lowcharge` under 15%, else `bar_battery`), `label_battery`'s `%d%%` text and `progress_battery`'s value, and never the battery widgets' visibility. A badge that differs from the last one arms a `CODEC_MS` UI timer, whose steps set `widget_set_opacity` (`0x66d494`, the widget's `+0x34` byte, which `widget_paint` applies as the canvas global alpha) down and back up, switching the image to `bar_btcon` halfway. After that the bar's background paint, which runs before its children, puts `bar_btcon` back over each badge stock sets again, so no badge frame is drawn. A hidden `img_bt` or a non-badge image other than `bar_btcon` ends the flash. `bar_sync` then hides `img_battery` and `label_battery` and shows `view_battery` with `widget_set_visible`, which returns early for an unchanged state and otherwise marks the parent for relayout (`widget_set_need_relayout_children`). The slot is sized to its ink: a percentage is its digit count times the `'0'` advance plus the `'%'` advance, both measured with `canvas_measure_text` on the first battery paint (`BATT_PCT_W` until then). `view_battery` is painted in the background hook from the level (`label_battery`'s text, since stock sets `progress_battery` to 0 while charging) and the charge state (`img_battery`'s image), and is invalidated when those or its displayed mode change. Stock's battery writes land on the hidden `label_battery` and `img_battery`, so they repaint nothing, and the bar paints each second only while something on it changes (a codec badge stock sets again): `ringnav_showface`, after stock's tick and while lit, reads the same level and charge state and, when they differ from what the slot shows, keeps them and invalidates the bar, so the next frame shows them and `bar_sync` has nothing more to repaint. A change while dark waits for the wake's paint. `BATTERY=3` uses a compact 28×15 solid rounded battery (radius 3; stock squares any radius under 3) with dark 13 px digits inside, omitting the percent sign; its body follows the charge-state color. Resizing the slot immediately relayouts its parent row.

## Level bars

The playing song's level bars (the status row's play state, Home's first row in `home_np.c`, Up Next's header through `un_bars`) are one motion in `ui_kit.c` ([oled-design](oled-design.md#level-bars)). `lvl_h16` gives bar `i`'s height at a time `t`, between a user's `lo` and `hi` px in sixteenths: a Catmull-Rom spline through `lvl_keys`, the status row's ten approved frames (0 to 1000 a bar), one every `LVL_STEP_MS` (125 ms), so a 1.25 s loop that passes each frame without stopping; the sums are in thousandths, so nothing needs 64-bit arithmetic on the MIPS. Each user keeps an `lvl_clock_t`: `lvl_run` starts it from the time it held and stops it where it is, so a pause holds the bars and a resume goes on from that height, never a jump; zero is stopped at the loop's start. `lvl_fill` draws a bar of whole pixels with its part-covered top row at that part of the ink's alpha, so a canvas without subpixel boxes still shows a height between pixels (the status row draws its round-ended bars with vgcanvas at the float height instead). Frames come from `motion_loop`: one shared `MO_LOOP_MS` (33 ms) timer calls each user's frame function while it returns 1 (`sr_bars_frame`, `hn_frame`, `un_bars_frame`), and each invalidates only its bars' box (the status row's 10 px play box on the bar, Home's 13 x 13 glyph box on `img_playing`, Up Next's 12 x 13 box where `un_bars` last painted, on the sheet's window); the timer ends with the last loop and never repaints the top window, as `motion_frames` does. A user's frame function says 0 once its bars stop (paused, out of sight, the screen dark, Reduce Motion: `MO_DECOR`), and its own sync starts the loop again (`status_row_sync`, `home_np_sync`, `un_poll` and `un_bars`). ponytail: the cost is measured only in the emulator (qemu-user on a laptop, 2026-11-17, a frame about 47 ms there, so about 20 a second): `demo`'s CPU with the bars moving less with them still was 8.5 points of a core on a titled page, 10.2 on Home and 6.9 on Up Next, where the 8-a-second steps had cost 2.7, 7.3 and 8.6 (Up Next's then repainted the whole header). A Q2 with Bluetooth audio playing, measured over q2remote, would say whether `MO_LOOP_MS` should go to 40 or 50 ms.

## Status row slots

OLED's status row (`patch/status_row.c`, [oled-design](oled-design.md#status-row)) lays its glyphs out right to left from the battery as slots (`status_slot_t`: a width function, 0 while hidden, the gap before the shown slot to its right, a painter): the battery (`SLOT_BATTERY`, stock's `view_battery`, which the bar's right group still places and `paint_battery` paints), the play state (`SLOT_PLAY`, 10 px), Wi-Fi (`SLOT_WIFI`, `SR_WIFI_W` 16 px), a card app's sync (`SLOT_SYNC`: the turning arrows' `SR_SPIN_W` 12 px, their upright ink, while it checks, and the download ring's `SR_RING` 16 px), Bluetooth (`SLOT_HEADSET`: the rune's 14 px while a device connects or one is connected with no level, a car's glyph at `SR_CAR_W` 19 px, or a headset's `headphones` glyph, 2 px and a 15x8 battery and its nub, 33 px) Buttons Lock's padlock (`SLOT_LOCK`, 13 px) and a card app's server out of reach (`SLOT_OFFLINE`, `SR_OFFLINE` 14 px: `cloud-slash-bold` in Warning, `tools/art.py`'s `status_offline`, shown while `addon_offline`, [Card app reach](#card-app-reach)), each `SR_GAP` (6) left of the one on its right. A hidden slot takes no room. On a full-width row `clock_place` centres the clock and ends the title's box `CLOCK_CLEAR` (12) short of the widest clock ("00:00") centred, and gives the slots a room from `CLOCK_BESIDE` (7) past that clock's text to the battery (`status_strip_room`, `strip_left`); slots that run past its left edge (`sr.over` px) are a strip that `layout` moves right by what the marquee has not slid yet (`sr.off`), so at rest its leftmost glyph is at the room's edge and `status_slots_left` answers that edge. The marquee rides ui_kit.c's shared loop (`sr_strip_frame` through `motion_loop`, started by `status_row_sync`, from rest whenever `sr.over` changes): `strip_off` holds `SR_MARQ_HOLD_MS` (2.75 s) at rest, slides at `SR_MARQ_PX_S` (35 px/s), holds `MARQUEE_HOLD_MS` at the end and starts again, and a frame invalidates the strip's box alone when the offset moved. `status_slots_paint` clips the canvas to that box (the vgcanvas takes the canvas's clip in `canvas_get_vgcanvas`) and fades each cut end (`strip_ends`) over `SR_MARQ_FADE` (6) px with list_marks.c's `text_fade_under_n`; `status_slot_at` takes no tap on a slot whose centre is scrolled out of it. On Home's Split there is no room (`status_strip_room(0)`): the slots run left from the battery over the art, and `clock_place` puts the clock at the row's left, its text `STATUS_ROW_INSET` in. `status_slots_paint`, from `ringnav_paint_bg` after the bar's own background (and Split's art rows, an artist's cap, About's header), paints every shown slot but the battery in final colors (`ui_ink_raw`), so Home in Split inks them over the art (`home_ink`, one ink for the row, [Home](ipod.md#home)). Every glyph is `SR_INK` (11) px tall on the clock's digits' rows, 17 to 27 on OLED's `status_y` 23: a glyph box `SR_GLYPH` (14) tall goes on `cy - 7` with its ink from `tools/art.py`'s `STATUS_TOP` (1), and the slim battery's 12 px body rises `BATT_BODY_RISE` (1) to rows 16 to 27 (`batt_top`). The glyphs are `tools/art.py`'s: Wi-Fi's fan drawn from geometry (`wifi_fan`, `status_wifi`), `wifi-x`, the Bluetooth rune, `headphones` and `car-profile` sized by their ink's height (`status_fit`, `STATUS_FIT`), the padlock as before. Sizes and gaps are `mock_status_icons.py`'s (the user's, 2026-11-16).

The play state is drawn with vgcanvas from `play_bars`' boxes, in Text Primary playing or paused: playing, three 2 px bars with round ends 4 px apart, their feet `SR_BAR_DROP` (5) below the row's center (the digits' baseline), their heights from ui_kit.c's level-bar motion (`lvl_h16`, 3 to 11 px, at `sr.clock`'s time: [Level bars](#level-bars)); paused, the pause, two `SR_PAUSE_W` (3) px bars 11 tall with 0.9 px corners at 0.5 and 6.5 px into the same 10 px box; stopped, none (`bar_status`, any player). Between playing and paused the two cross-dissolve over `SR_XFADE_MS` (250 ms, cubic ease-out) in that box: `status_row_sync` starts `sr.xfade` (`play_xfade_sync`) when the state changes with the slot shown at the sync before (a slot that appears shows its state at once), `play_paint` draws the bars at their stopped frame at the opacity left and the pause over them at the rest, the bars' loop moves no frame while it runs (`bars_moving`), and the frames come from ui_kit.c's shared timer, which calls `sr_xfade_frame` (`motion_hook`: the timer repaints only the top window, and the bar is a window of its own) to invalidate the play box alone, once more after the end. The run is `MO_SPATIAL`, so Reduce Motion makes it a cut. Wi-Fi reads stock's own status-bar widget, `img_wifi`, kept off-screen and current by `systembar_showface`: `bar_wifi1` to `bar_wifi4` light the fan's dot, then its two bands (3 and 4 all three), the rest in `#3A3A3C`; off, Smart Wi-Fi's radio off, not connected or `bar_wifi0`, the slot hides. Connected with no internet is `wifi-x-bold`, read as stock's network monitor's word (`networkGetConnectStatus`, `0x5c2bdc`, a load of the state its thread sets) at 0 while the bars say connected. ponytail: that is a link with an address, not the internet; nothing on the Q2 probes past the access point (stock has no such check), so a captive portal or a dead uplink shows the full glyph. A DNS lookup or an HTTP check from a worker thread would lift it. The Bluetooth slot reads stock's link list: its last item at status 3 is a device connected (as stock's rows read it), and a link thread running (`bt_connectstatus` 1) with an item listed is one connecting (the rune in Text Tertiary, `status_btdim`); connected, a car by its Class (`bt_headset_class`, `bt_kind`) shows `car-profile`, a headset with a level (`bt_headset_battery()`, 0-100, -1 for none, read from BlueZ's `org.bluez.Battery1` by `patch/bt_battery.c`, [Headset battery](#headset-battery)) `headphones` and `battery_slim`'s 15x8 battery at that level (red under 20% as the status battery's), any other the rune in Text Primary. While a guest plays (`guest_active`, [Guest Play screens](#guest-play-screens)) the slot is the guest's phone in the accent (`status_guest`), and with `out` a Bluetooth device the relay mark and that device's glyph. Stock's own status-bar Bluetooth glyph and its codec badge stay off-screen. A --dev build reads `/mnt/data/q2-status.fake` (`status_fake`, at most every 500 ms) for the emulator, which has no radio or charger: `wifi=N`, `charge=1` and `charge=2` stand in for the Wi-Fi level, a charging cable and a cable holding the battery full (`battery_now`), and `volume=N` for a headset's volume change ([Volume pill](#volume-pill)), so those can be shown and shot there; a release build has none of it.

The bars ride ui_kit.c's shared loop (`sr_bars_frame` through `motion_loop`) while `bars_moving`: lit, playing, the slot shown, no dissolve running and motion allowed; `status_row_sync` starts it, and each frame invalidates only the play box. The sync arrows ride the same loop (`sr_spin_frame`, 30 frames a second) while the screen is lit and a sync checks, Reduce Motion or not, as they report what the app does: `status_row_sync` adds it, from `bar_state_sync` (each bar paint and stock's 1 s showface), and the first frame that finds none drops it. Their frame is the clock's place in the half turn (`SR_TURN_MS`, 1 s, over `SR_SPIN`, 30 frames: the glyph repeats every half turn), so a late timer never slows the turn, and a frame that moved invalidates only their art's box of the bar (14 px, a px either side of their 12 px slot). The loop holds `MO_LOOPS` (6) at once: the status row's bars, strip and arrows, the volume pill, and Home's and Up Next's bars, which can overlap for a frame as one page gives way to the other. Either repaints only those columns, inked over Split's art there with the cut edges kept (`INK_CUT_*`). `status_row_sync` also keeps a signature of what the slots show (which ones, the play state, Wi-Fi's level or its crossed glyph, the sync's kind and its ring to a fiftieth, the Bluetooth slot's kind and the headset's level, the lock) and returns 1 when it changes, so the whole bar repaints once after the frame and the clock moves. A tap (`status_touch`) finds its slot with `status_slot_at`: a 44 x 40 px target round each shown slot's center (the battery's body's, or its percentage's on Percent), the nearer center where two meet. The battery's toasts its state ([Charging](#charging)); the bars' opens Now Playing (`playback_np_open`, from a 0 ms timer, after the input's dispatch), as stock's `img_state` did before it went off-screen.

## Volume pill

A volume change made off Now Playing shows in the status row, in the clock's place (`patch/vol_pill.c`, [oled-design](oled-design.md#status-row)). The paths that change the volume with nothing of the Q2's own on screen are two: a Bluetooth headset's (its own keys or its AVRCP absolute volume, read by `bt_volume_poll`, [Headset controls and volume](#headset-controls-and-volume)) and the Car Remote's `volume N` command (`coda_rc_shim.c`). Both go through `vol_show` (`patch/volume.c`). The Q2 has no volume keys of its own and reads no wired inline remote (the wheel, Center and four side buttons; a headset's AVRCP keys reach `headset_command`, none of them a volume key), and the rest set the volume on a page that shows it (the wheel on Now Playing, Control Center's slider, Playback's Volume page, Max Volume's slider, AirPlay's speaker level on its own player page). `vol_show` keeps the volume dialog in front, Control Center and Playback's Volume page as they were; on a volume page (`vol_page`: `playing_page`, `airplay_page`, `radionp_page` and Spotify's Now Playing, the page in use past toasts) it opens stock's `dialog/volume_dialog` on Now Playing's band; on any other page it calls `vol_pill_show`, which needs no dialog and takes no keys, so it shows over a confirmation card too, and the wheel keeps its page. Not dark, over a video or where stock's `on_wm_keyup_fun` opens nothing (the lock window, test mode, the first-boot guide, powering off).

The pill is drawn by the status row itself: `status_slots_paint` (`status_row.c`) calls `vol_pill_paint` after the slots, in the bar's background paint (`ringnav_paint_bg`), so it is wherever the bar is painted. Its box (`vp_box`) is `VP_W` (199) wide, centred on x 187.5, narrower and still centred down to `VP_MIN_W` (141) as the slots reach left (`status_slots_left` less `VP_CLEAR`), then `VP_MIN_W` ending at that edge; 30 px tall on `V_STATUS_Y`. The clock (`label_clock`) and the title (`st.bar_title`) are stock's labels, children of the bar painted after its background, so the pill does not paint over them: `vp_labels` sets their opacity to 255 less the pill's alpha. The level is `g_volume` of 100 in every case: with Link Volume on, `bt_volume_poll` has already read the headset's 0 to 127 back onto the Q2's scale (`bt_vol_q2`, within the volume limit), so the pill's number is the one Now Playing and Control Center show. 0 is the mute: `status_mute` and no fill.

**Timing.** Each change stamps `vp.at` and the pill at full; one timer, `vp_due`, `VP_HOLD_MS` (2 s) after the first, re-arms itself for what is left while changes keep coming, then starts the fade: `vp_frame` on ui_kit.c's shared loop (`motion_loop`, every `MO_LOOP_MS`), the pill's alpha `VP_FADE_MS` (250 ms) along `EASE_CUBIC_OUT` to 0 and the labels' opacity back to 255, then dropped. Under Reduce Motion `vp_due` ends it at once. A change during the fade brings it back to full and drops the loop.

**What repaints.** A change while the pill shows invalidates the pill's box on the bar and nothing else (`vp_dirty(0)`); its first change, and each fade frame, the band from the screen's left to the leftmost slot in the pill's rows (`vp_dirty(1)`), where the labels' opacity changes. Neither repaints the page under it, which `motion_frames` would every frame (the lesson of [Control Center volume drag](#control-center-volume-drag)). A pill up when a volume page or Control Center comes in front, or a video starts, ends in its next paint (`vp_hidden`), the labels back before they paint in that frame.

**On the emulator**, which has no headset, a --dev build's `/mnt/data/q2-status.fake` takes `volume=N` (`vol_pill_fake`, from `status_row_sync`): each new N moves the volume there as a headset's change would. `test/fw/test_vol_pill.py` covers the pill shown off Now Playing, its updates and the box each repaints, the hold and fade, Reduce Motion, Now Playing and Control Center, the mute, a linked headset's level on the Q2's scale and the Car Remote.

## Now Playing (iPod)

`playing_page_init` (`0x53e334`, standard PIC prologue, resumed at `0x53e340`) registers the page's handlers, runs the page update (`0x53cf08`) once and starts a 250 ms widget timer (`playing_timer_start`, `0x53d928`) that runs it again. The update finds each widget with a recursive `widget_lookup`, skips any it does not find, and gets the times from `player_playtime_and_length` (`0x51ee10`): elapsed and total seconds from `mclGetPlayTime` (`0x5be768`), less a CUE track's start, elapsed clamped to the total, both 0 while stopped. It sets `slider_play` to value = elapsed, max = total, and formats both labels with `toolsTimeItoa` (`0x5cef40`): `%02d:%02d`, or `%02d:%02d:%02d` from an hour. `label_playlen` is its only reference to that name.

The hook runs the stock init, then caches `label_ipod_album`, `label_ipod_remain` and the slider, and syncs them. It also caches `img_cover`, whose border paint (after the image) rounds its corners in the page's black with `corner_mask`, each corner pixel at the share of it the arc leaves uncovered ([Rounded corners](#rounded-corners)). Painting the top window or the status bar syncs them again. The page shows no queue position; `MCL_POS` and the queue's length still go into the album's key, so a new song of the same album restarts its marquee. The album is that record's `REC_ALBUM` (the record comes from `queue_now`, which Home's art shares), or, once `player_get_id3info` (`0x51f3a4`) has parsed that record's file, the album it parsed: `g_play_id3_info` (`0xa5520c`, `0xa9c` bytes) holds the parsed path at `+0`, album at `+0x404`, artist at `+0x504` and title at `+0x684` (`now_tag`). For a CUE track (`mclGetCueFlag`: the playing record has a CUE start or end) stock copies the record's tags instead of reading the file: stock's sheet parser (`0x5d2f4c`) gives each track the sheet's `TITLE` as album and the last `PERFORMER` seen (the track's, else the sheet's) as artist. Its copy of the parsed path (`ID3_PATH`, `0x51f5d0`), which every fresh parse reaches before Now Playing's title and artist lines are written, becomes `jal ringnav_id3_path`: an empty album or artist there is taken from the file's own tags (`toolsGetMusicInfo`), so a sheet without `TITLE` or `PERFORMER` (common for audiobooks) shows the book and author instead of Unknown Artist. Album artist is filled the same way. ponytail: only the playing track's tags; Library lists and the database keep the sheet's empty fields (Library's Artists and Albums leave audiobooks out anyway), so Home's and Now Playing's art key (artist, album) can miss Coverflow's cache, keyed on the database's values; fill at scan time if that matters. When a folder play (class 1) reaches its last track with the folder-jump setting on (Folder Skip, the byte `0xa5002b`), `mclNextSong` calls `on_player_autochange` (`0x51eca8`), whose `toolsLoadNextDir` and `player_refresh_playqueue(1)` replace the queue with the next folder's untagged file records, and only the parsed tags name the next album. Every stock folder jump tests class 1, so Coverflow plays its albums as stock's album class `0xff10` and Most Played and Shuffle Songs as `0xf001`. `album_memory` also writes the album into `g_memory_info` (`+0x60d` Unknown flag, `+0x611` name), as `player_load_songlist` does for stock lists, so stock resume rebuilds that album with `getMusicByAlbum`. Home's art keys its Coverflow cache lookup the same way. The remaining time is the slider's max less its value, in stock's format with a leading minus, so it matches the elapsed label and follows a touch drag. Each label is written only when its source changes (position, queue length, album string pointer, or those seconds); `EVT_DESTROY` drops the cache. Stock's total label stays hidden.

**One page.** Stock's navigator opens a `playing_page` over whatever is in front, so a song played from a page Now Playing opened (its artist or album tap, the ⋯ page's Look up, then Shuffle or a song there) would leave the first page under it: covered, its 250 ms timer stopped, still showing the song it last showed, and the page Return comes back to before Home. Once stock's init has built the new page, `ringnav_playing` force-closes every other `playing_page` in the window manager (`np_only`, `patch/nav/now_playing.c`) and leaves the pages between, so Return goes to the artist page and then Home. A start refused for want of an output opens no page (`ringnav_nav_to`, [no output](#no-playback-without-an-output)), so it closes nothing. `play_folder` (`patch/coverflow.c`) also closes a Now Playing in front before it opens one, so that open slides from the page under it.

The V8.6 folder-rollover regression in `test/patch.py` executes stock `player_mainscheduling` → `mclAutoChange` → `mclNextSong` → `on_player_autochange` → `toolsLoadNextDir` → `player_refresh_playqueue` → `mclLoadPlayList`, then stock tag parsing, cover-worker completion and the Now Playing timer (`0x53d810`). Filesystem enumeration, tag decoding, image decoding and the audio decoder are mocked at their boundaries; the harness does not supply the resulting player metadata globals. Equal-sized and one-track sibling folders, reused positions, missing tags/art, consecutive transitions, and delayed scheduler/cover completion pass in Stock and iPod. iPod's paint hooks also verify album text and Home art before and after completion. This does not reproduce a V8.6 regression, so no additional metadata firmware change is made.

**Info page**. The page update fills the info page through `0x53bc78` (its one call, a `bal` at `0x53d308`, after the player status checks): `label_album`, `label_genre`, `label_encode`, `label_year`, `label_bits`, `label_kbps` and `label_sample` as `%s:%s` or `%s:%d…` (`Album:Kid A`, `Bit Depth:16bit`, `Sample Rate:44.1kHz`; `%s:%s` is also wpa_supplicant's literal, so stays), `label_size` as `%s:%.2fMB`, and `label_location` as the bare folder with `/mnt/mmc/` as `SD:/` (it looks up `player_location` and never uses it), a missing value as the first `player_unknown`, which en_US has twice ("Unknown Artist", then "Unknown"). The build makes that call `jal ringnav_np_info` (`NP_INFO_CALL`), which runs it, then rewrites each line: `: ` after the label, a space before `MB`, `kbps` and `kHz` and a hyphen before `bit` after a digit, "Unknown Artist" as "Unknown", and the folder after `player_location`'s label (`getFormatString`), only where the text changes. Its labels **Genre** and **Year** are `LABELS` renames of `genre` (which the search page's tab shares) and `player_era`. The page is not in the swipe: `tools/ipod.py` `np_info_out` takes `view_info` out of the `slide_view` (so the dots count the art and lyrics pages) and makes it the window's first child, hidden, its box the slide's place in the window and its own layout dropped; stock's lookups are by name and deep, so its fill finds the labels there. ⋯'s **About** row (`more_rows` in `patch/onlinematch.c`, `list_row` with stock's `system_about` icon, under OLED's menu sheet the Phosphor `info` symbol) runs `np_about_open` (`patch/np_about.c`): a payload window (`page_open`, `npabout_page`) titled About (`page_title`), into which it moves `view_info` (`widget_remove_child`, `widget_add_child`, stock's own, in `FUNCTIONS`) and shows it, then fills it at once. A payload window has Now Playing's box, so the details stand where they stood on the swipe, or under the page's title where the theme shows it as a first row and the details start above its foot. While it is open `ringnav_np_info` fills the page instead of Now Playing's window, the Genre marquee (`genre_fill`, `genre_over`) runs while About is the top window, Smart Awake holds the screen on it and Enlarged Album Art's countdown stays full. Return (`ab_key`) puts `view_info` back in Now Playing's window, hidden, while both are whole, then goes back a page (`page_keyup`), to ⋯ as its other rows' pages do; a close by any other way puts it back from the destroy event, or, if Now Playing went first (`np_gone` calls `np_about_np_gone`), leaves it to go with the page. No setting or saved state names a Now Playing page: stock opens the page on the art each time, so nothing points at the old third page.

`playing_page`'s labels are the source of About's info grid (`np_info_values`, from `np_grid`): each label gets a hidden `<name>_value` `hscroll_label`, and the view stays hidden. There `ringnav_np_info` renames stock's English "File Size", "Encoding" and "Bitrate" to the grid's "Size", "Format" and "Bit Rate" (another language's names stay stock's) and ends with `np_about_fill` (`patch/np_about.c`). While About is open that reads the values back from the page: the header's title, artist, length (the slider's `max`) and cover (Now Playing's `img_cover` image, drawn scaled with `canvas_draw_image`, its corners rounded into the page's black); the quality line, Lossless or Hi-Res Lossless by codec, bit depth (over 16) and sample rate (over 48 kHz), DSD by codec with its multiple of 44.1 kHz from the bit rate (stock's sample rate for a DSF reads half the DSD rate: a DSD64 file's reads 1411.2 kHz, measured in the emulator), the codec and bit rate for anything else; and the cells, a value empty, `Unknown`, the language's `player_unknown` or 0 left out. Location comes from the playing path, not stock's `SD:/...` folder: a file in a card app's hidden folder is the server's, `Streaming` when it lies straight in the app's `stream/` (q2-subsonic's uncached stream, removed after the list) and `Downloaded` otherwise, as is a file under `Subsonic/` (the app's sync folder); any other card file reads `SD Card` and its folder. The grid is painted, not laid out: one view over the window, `np_about_paint` from `ringnav_paint` with `ui_kit.c`'s `ui_text`, repainted when a hash of what it shows changes. The view covers the page's full-bleed window, so its header stands from y 46, under the status row's overlay; scrolled, the paint clips the grid at the row's foot, as a list's rows end there. `np_about_key`, before `ringnav`'s allowlist (as Spotify's page takes its keys), takes every wheel tick on the page: one scrolls the grid `AB_ROW` (44) px, as far as its last row ending on the list's end (`list_fit_end`, y 282), and none reaches stock's volume. A vertical drag scrolls it too (`ab_touch`, on the grid's view for the press and on the page for the move, lift and abort, as `peq_ui.c`'s `e3_touch`): the scroll follows the finger pixel for pixel from where it went down, clamped by the same `ab_scroll` as the wheel to 0 and the last row's end, and stops at the lift with no momentum, so a flick cannot carry it past either end.

`set_repeatpoint`'s marker placement (`0x53b9d8`) puts the 3x10 A-B markers at x = 50 + t \* 290 / length, y 250. iPod keeps y and patches x and width to `NP_BAR`; a bar laid out elsewhere (OLED's grid) takes them along at the same share of its width (`ringnav_ab_x`) and its centre line (`ringnav_ab_move`, in place of the two `widget_move` calls `AB_MOVE_CALLS`, which set the y). The slider's 44px target is centered on the same bar (window y 255), with the page dots moved 6px up, outside the target. The dots' `slide_indicator` gets its own anchor (`anchor_x` `187px`, `anchor_y` `0px`, the point stock's took: the slide_view's center, above the indicator's middle, so the dots on its top edge). With none, stock centers them on its `indicated_target` as `widget_to_screen` places it, and that subtracts the widget's own `xoffset` property, which `slide_view` sets to the drag during a swipe. The indicator lays its dots out again only after its own layout (any relayout of the window), but then from wherever the slide_view was dragged, so the dots slid with the page until the next layout. Native `slide_with_bar` accepts a press anywhere in that rectangle and grabs the pointer, so a drag stays on the slider outside its bounds. Its dragger is skipped when the `icon` style lookup is empty and `border_color` is transparent (`slider_on_paint_self`, `0x62e080`). The asset clears `border_color` in every state. The icon needs more than leaving it out: the slider's style name (`s_ipod_progress`) has no theme entry, and stock then reads what the inline style lacks from its `default` slider style (the style's state change, `0x6b48cc`: the name's state, the name's `normal`, then `default`'s), whose `icon` is the knob, `rounded_n`, `rounded_o` when focused or over and `rounded_p` when pressed. With an icon stock draws the knob, sizes the dragger to it and fills and seeks half a knob short of each end. `slider_knobless` therefore sets `icon` to a value that's no string in all five states, which reads as none, on every slider `plain_slider` makes: this one, Quick Settings' brightness slider (both with their fill, `slider_fill`) and the four settings slider pages' at their load (`slider_open`). No thumb shows and the fill ends exactly at the value. An empty `icon` in the asset reads as none too, as on stock's own brightness bar, but stock then looks the image up at every paint. `np_fill` sets the fill in every state a press passes through, so a touch keeps the accent.

**Volume.** Outside a scrub the wheel stays on the volume, and stock opens `dialog/volume_dialog`, a full-screen transparent dialog holding `slider_vol` and `label_vol`. Its `highlight="default(alpha=200)"` made the window manager draw everything under it as a dimmed snapshot taken at open, so iPod's `volume_dialog.bin` drops that property (`volume_dialog` in `tools/ipod.py`) and nothing dims. When the paint hook paints that dialog, `vol_paint` draws the volume in the dialog's own paint. With Now Playing directly under it (the window manager's second-to-last child) it covers the band from `slider_play` to `label_playtime` in black, then draws the track (the theme's `playing.scrubber.track`, `TRACK_COLOR` by default, the slider's `bar_size`) and a white fill to `value / max`, both pills like the capsule, and "Volume N" centered in the times' row at `NP_TIMES_PX`; under a status row's set (OLED's) the bar is inset `VOL_SPK_INSET` (24) at each end, its fill white, with the theme's 16 px speakers (`vol_lo_*` and `vol_hi_*`, Phosphor's `speaker-simple-none` and `speaker-simple-high` fill in Text Secondary, `tools/art.py`) centered `VOL_SPK_X` (8) in from each end of the progress bar on its center line, and no text. A paint whose clip misses the number (a repaint of the bar's rows alone) sets `vol_drawn` to -1 too, so `vol_poll` repaints the dialog whole and the number follows the bar within `VOL_POLL_MS`. Without the poll timer, or with the dots already hidden, they are left alone and no number is drawn. ponytail: the paper over the elapsed time's box also covers the art reflection's last rows there (a few percent at most), a faint notch while the volume shows; hiding the two labels under the dialog instead needs a restore when it closes. Over any other window, Quick Settings included, it draws a rounded `VOL_PANEL_*` panel in the fast-scroll letter's style (`FILL_RGB` at `LETTER_ALPHA`, `LETTER_RADIUS`) exactly over Quick Settings' brightness row (the build checks it), its rounded corners clear of the glass corners, with the bar as a pill on a `VOL_PANEL_TRACK` gray track (a non-zero fill at least a round dot) and just the number at its right, at `VOL_PANEL_PX`. `slider_vol` and `label_vol` are hidden in the iPod asset before the first paint, so transition snapshots cannot expose the stock full-screen controls; `slider_vol` is moved onto the area drawn, so stock's partial repaints land on it. Those alone stopped after a tick or two, so while the dialog is up a `VOL_POLL_MS` (16 ms) timer compares `slider_vol`'s value with the one last drawn and repaints the whole dialog when it changed, or while the bar eases after a wheel tick ([Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)); it removes itself once the dialog is no longer on top.

**Dark volume.** With the screen off the wheel does nothing ([Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)): `wheel_lock_gate` drops its ticks before anything sees them. Behind it, a tick no page takes that reached `on_wm_keyup_fun` dark would be dropped by its hook, as would a tick over a volume dialog left open past the screen-off, which `vol_keyup` sends on there. Stock's opened the dialog on a dark tick (that tick changes nothing, as lit), and the ticks after it were the dialog's own (`volume_dialog_on_keyup`, `0x4a3688`: a step, the save, its 3 s count restarted, `RET_STOP`). Since V1.34 stock's handler returns 0 at once while `g_backlight_status` is clear, so each later tick went on to `on_wm_keyup_fun` again, and `navigator_to("dialog/volume_dialog")` finds an open window only by that path (`widget_child`, a `strcmp` with the window's name, `volume_dialog`), never matching: every dark tick loaded one more dialog over the last and none changed the volume. A dialog's close timer stops when it leaves the top (`0x12a`) and starts again when it is back (`0x12b`), so once lit the stack came down one dialog every 3 s, each drawn the same; Return or a tap off the bar closed only the top one, and a drag on the bar ended with the dialog under it showing the value it opened with (#303). `VOL_DARK` (`tools/build.py`) removes the branch at `0x4a36b4`, so the dialog's other keys are its own dark as V1.32's were; its wheel ticks dark go on to `vol_wm_keyup`, which opens nothing. A stack could still come from a lit pass: a dialog `navigator_to` has just loaded is the window in front at once, but the window manager's key target (`W_KEY_TARGET`, where `widget_on_keyup` sends a release) only from its open event (`window_base_on_event` focuses it on `0x128`/`0x129`), which the open's idle dispatches, or the end of its animation. A tick dispatched before that goes to the page under it and on to `on_wm_keyup_fun`, which loads another dialog; the loop dispatches every queued event before its idles, so a stalled pass took several ticks and opened a dialog for each, only the last stepped. `ringnav` takes such a tick itself, after stock's lock filter: with the screen lit and the volume dialog in front and not the key target it steps the volume (`vol_step`, the dialog's own clamps and save), sets `slider_vol` and stops the key, so one dialog is all a turn opens. The dialog's 3 s count is not restarted by these ticks; its own, a pass later, restart it.

**OLED's grid.** The grid's `np_art` (150, with `np_bar_y` 228) has `playing_page` move the iPod layout's boxes onto it (`np_grid` in `tools/ipod.py`); every name the payload looks up keeps its widget. `img_cover` sits at the text column on the window's top (y 58 on screen), its corners `playing.art.radius` px (6, `paint_cover`); the title, artist and album boxes start 18 px right of it on line tops 64, 96 and 120, each 2 px wider than its column at both sides for `hscroll_label`'s margins, so the text ends on the right column; `img_fav` and `img_more` sit at the right end of an 18 px line whose baseline is the art's foot (`NP_GRID_ROW_PX`, `NP_GRID_ROW_ASCENT`) on the art's page, More's center `NP_GRID_MORE_INSET` (7) px left of the right column, so its dots end on it. Their images are the theme's (`np_glyphs` in `patch/np_bar.c`, under `playing.modes.icons`; `tools/art.py` `np_fav`, `np_unfav_*`, `np_more_*`, `np_moredown_*`, 20 px): stock's update and click, and `rate_fav_click`, keep setting the heart to `play_fav` or `play_unfav`, so each paint of the window (`ringnav_paint_bg`, before the buttons paint) turns either into the theme's name, the empty heart in the half's ink, and More's five `bg_image` states into the half's dots once per half (`ringnav_playing` binds both through `np_glyphs_bind`). An app's heart (`tidal_fav_add`, `tidal_fav_rm`) stays stock's. `slider_play` runs 6 px high from the text column to the right column with its top at y 228 and a 22 px target, the times 22 px under it in Inter. `img_playmode` stays at opacity 0, centered on y 276, as the target for the theme's shuffle and repeat, which `np_modes` (`patch/np_bar.c`, `playing.modes.icons`) draws 44 px apart about its center, each in Accent Blue when lit, else Text Secondary (`tools/art.py` `mode_*`; repeat-once has its own glyph). They are two controls over stock's one mode: `ringnav_dispatch` hands a click on the target to `np_mode_click` before stock's handler, which stepped Order, Repeat One, Shuffle, Repeat All; the left half toggles shuffle and the right steps repeat Off, All, One (`np_mode_step`). The outer buttons reach past the target, touch only (the user's, 2026-11-18): `np_tap`, the window's pointer handler, hands a tap's down and lift to `np_corner_tap`, and `row_corner` gives shuffle the window from its left edge, and Up Next to its right edge, from the target's top to the window's foot, across to `np_mode_click`'s midpoint with the neighbour (radio, repeat), so a corner's tap presses that button (`row_press`, the same square on the glyph) and never Radio. `MCL_MODE` can't say everything two controls can: stock has no shuffle under Repeat One, and its Shuffle (2) never ends, drawing again once every track has played. So Repeat One plays as 1 whatever shuffle says, shuffle with repeat Off or All both play as 2, and the payload keeps the rest (`np_shuf_one`: shuffle under Repeat One; `np_rep_off`: Off chosen under shuffle, All otherwise, as that is how stock's Shuffle plays), saved as `[IPOD] NPSHUFONE` and `NPREPOFF` when either moves and read back on first use (`np_modes_read`), so a restart draws the pair as it was. Shuffle with repeat Off therefore keeps playing after the last track. A change that leaves `MCL_MODE` as it is sends nothing; one that moves it goes through `config_playmode`, as the play mode setting saves it, and so through `ringnav_mode`'s rules: stock Shuffle keeps Shuffle Albums or Folders, any other mode ends advanced play. The page dots sit at y 302; the slide (the lyrics) ends 5 px above the bar. `np_sync` sets the artist and album in `playing.artist.font`'s face as their text allows (`face_font`, `theme_font`'s rule for a named face).

**Quick Settings and prompts.** Stock's pull-down (`on_wm_tsmove_fun`, `0x4f2a4c`) opens `dialog/statusbar_dialog` for a touch that began above y 31 (`g_pressdown_y`, written by `on_wm_tsdown_fun`) and moved 20 px down. It stays out of its own Add and Delete prompts by their flags, but tests `g_poweroff_state` only for 2, and the Shut Down? prompt (`on_wm_keylong_fun`, a modal `dialog/confirminfo_dialog`) is state 1, so Quick Settings opened over it. Return there is stock's (`usable` is false with the state set and another window in front), and it took the windows away under the prompt's modal loop: Shut Down? stayed or came back with buttons that did nothing and `g_poweroff_state` still 1, so only Now Playing worked until a restart (#303). `ringnav_input` passes a pointer-down to stock and then, with a `confirminfo_dialog` in front, moves a `g_pressdown_y` above `QS_PULL_Y` down to it, so no touch on a prompt, the Shut Down? one or one of ours, can pull Quick Settings down. Inferred from the handlers, not reproduced: the emulator mocks the window manager.

A theme with `motion.inplace` moves a level inside a page, with no window animating (`page_push`, `coverflow.c`): after `page_list` rebuilds it, the list_view starts a window's width to the side and animates its `x` to rest. `addon.c` keeps the depth's change in `pg.moved` through its Loading level, so the push falls on the first rows or error; a refresh finds it 0. A folder level moves stock's `tableview_folder` when `ringnav_folder_click` or `ringnav_folder_back` sees `g_folder_layer` change and stay above 0. A level still sliding goes to its rest first.

## Boot resume (iPod)

Stock `home_page_init` resumes when Memory Playback (`g_memory_play`) or car mode (`g_carmode`) is set. `memeory_startplayer` (`0x5211f4`) reads the saved state, rebuilds the queue into a new deque, sets the saved position with `mclSetStartSeekTime` when `g_memory_play` is 2 or in car mode, and returns the track index; it neither plays nor opens a page. Home then calls `navigator_to_with_context("playing_page", ctx)` (the `jalr` at `0x534cf8`) with `ctx` `{queue, index, class, mode}`, mode 2 in car mode and 3 otherwise. `playing_page_init` passes `ctx` to `player_start` unless the class is `0xff`; `player_start` loads the queue, starts the player and pauses it (`mclSetPause`) unless the mode is 2.

iPod makes that `jalr` a checked `jal ringnav_boot`; the delay slot still stores the mode. In car mode `ringnav_boot` makes the stock call unchanged, unless Headphones Required (under Settings order) refuses the start, which then is the paused one. Otherwise it makes the page's `player_start` call without the page, so the queue and track come back paused and Home stays; the saved time is restored in Location mode, while Track starts at the beginning. Home destroys its deque afterwards, as before, since `mclLoadPlayList` copies it. The page's two resets before `player_start` (key-seek mode and a countdown) are page state, set again when it opens. `hciplayer` touches `/tmp/notfile` or `/tmp/notsupport` for a missing or unsupported track; the window manager's `on_wm_timer_dialog` (`0x4f4d18`) turns them into a `msginfo_dialog` toast on any page, and `playing_page_init` only deletes stale ones, so a bad restored track still shows its toast on Home.
