In-Vehicle Mode (`SYSSET CARMODE`, `g_carmode`) also ties the Q2 to the car's power, in stock code the payload leaves alone. `on_wm_idle_status` calls `check_cardmode` (`0x4f3c24`) on every pass. In car mode, with no cable (`g_charge_state` 0: `get_battery_capacity` keeps it as `usb_detect` reads the cable, and 0 while `g_last_otgid` is 1, so Charge Limit, which only switches charging, leaves it alone), it sets `g_carmode_state` from 0 to 1; with the cable, from anything above 0 back to 0. `on_wm_timer_dialog` takes 1 to 2, wakes the screen (`awake_screen`), opens `dialog/autoshutdown_dialog` ("Shutdown") and sets 3. The dialog's one-second timer (`0x498f04`) closes it once the cable is back; otherwise it counts down from 10 and at 0 closes it and opens `poweroff_page`, so the Q2 shuts down 10 s after the power goes. Car mode also skips the idle Auto-standby and Auto-shutdown (`check_to_poweroption`, `0x4f3d70` and `0x4f3e40`) and the USB Connected prompt on plugging in (`check_usb_status`). Nothing in demo powers the Q2 on with the cable. Settings → Power's row says both in its caption (`pod_caption`, `patch/settings_pages.c`).

The English stock labels are Memory Playback: Off / Track / Location and
System: In-Vehicle Mode. Home's Now Playing action (`on_home_playing_onclick`
at `0x5343f0`) calls `on_backplay_click` (`0x4f1e84`), which opens the player with
class `0xff`; this skips `player_start` and preserves the paused state. Play/Pause
resumes audio.

## Memory Playback and a streamed queue

A queue of server songs plays from the songs' downloads (a card app's `.play` queue file, [server-library.md](server-library.md#download-ahead-and-the-streaming-state)), and the firmware's queue holds only the ones already on the card: the song playing and those Download Ahead fetched. The rest are Up Next's pending rows (`addon_pending`), read from the app's queue file. The snapshot holds the firmware's queue alone, so a restart used to bring back those one or two songs and nothing fetched the others.

**What is saved.** Each snapshot write (`playback_save`) also writes `.q2pod/ringnav-queue-stream` (`save_tail`, a card blob beside the snapshot): its magic, a checksum of the rest, the snapshot's checksum, a count, then the paths of the songs Up Next lists as pending (`addon_pending_paths`), each with its NUL, at most `SAVE_LIMIT` with the queue. No pending songs: the file is dropped. A tail whose snapshot checksum is not the snapshot's is ignored, so the snapshot's format is unchanged and an older build reads it as before. ponytail: an app's rewrite of its queue file that changes no queued song (a radio's more songs) is not saved until the next snapshot write.

**The ask.** After `ringnav_memory` restores what is on the card, `ask_resume` hands `addon_resume_ask` every saved song's path (the snapshot's, in queue order, then the tail's), which were restored, the index of the song the restore made current, its seconds (`s.resume_elapsed`, 0 for Track) and whether it plays (car mode) or waits paused. The app whose folder holds a saved song (`/mnt/mmc/.<id>/`) is asked when its q2app says `resume=1` and a song after the current one was not restored; otherwise nothing changes. Once the app's socket is there (`resume_poll` in `addon_poll` starts it with `addon_wake`, as a `.catplay` does, and an app takes a request already there at its start as answered) the request is written whole to `/tmp/q2-<id>.resume`:

```text
<seq> <index> <seconds> paused|playing
<card path>
```

one path a line, every saved song in order, index counting them from 0 (a streamed file's name carries its server id, `stream_path.h`). The app answers `resumeack=<seq> <code>` in its state file (0 resumed, 1 not its songs, 2 it can't: signed out, the song restored unknown to the server, or the server not answering), then a `.play` named by that seq whose queue file starts with the song restored.

**Kept paused.** That `.play`'s first entry, the same song as the one restored (`catalogue_same_song`), is passed over as a radio's seed is (`resume_keeps` beside `song_radio_keeps` in `m3u_songs`): `playback_queue_rest` keeps it at its place and replaces the songs after it with the app's, so nothing loads and the paused song stays paused at its seconds. ponytail: the restored songs before the current one leave the queue then, as a radio's do. While that song waits paused, `.playing` is not written (`sm.hold`), so the app reports no play for it; Play, or another song, writes it. Download Ahead's `.ahead` is written as for any session, so the app fetches the songs after it at once.

**Meanwhile and otherwise.** Until the answer, Up Next's pending rows are the saved songs after the current one that were not restored, named from the catalogue as any pending row (`card_record_tags`), so it lists every saved song. The app not listening within `RESUME_START_MS` (30 s), no queue within `RESUME_WAIT_MS` (30 s) of the request, a code other than 0, or another queue played first: the rows go, the queue is the songs on the card as before, and the unified log has a `W resume` line saying why. A late `.play` of that seq is never played (`rs.dead`), nor one whose first song is not the one restored. `test/fw/test_stream_resume.py` checks these.

## Scrub (iPod)

**Stock audit.** `playing_page` is not a navigation context, so a center release (218, the power key) passed through to `on_wm_keyup_fun`, whose `screen_action` (`0x501f64`) turns the screen off, and a wheel release to the same handler, which changes the volume and opens `dialog/volume_dialog`. The page's own key-up handler (`0x53da5c`) knew only Return and keys 222/223 until V1.36, which gave it the center release too: a second one within 350 ms turns the screen off at once (`power_keyup_detect`, 250 ms until then), a single one does 350 ms later (`power_keyup_pending_custom`), and either stops there. `ringnav` takes the center release on this page before that handler runs, and what it passes on is for `on_wm_keyup_fun`: a release under stock's power-key rules (`g_power_longkey`, `g_ingore_bootkey_flag`, the guard after Standby), whose flags only that function clears, and one during a window animation. So the handler's test for Center never matches (`NP_CENTRE` in `tools/build.py`), and it passes Center on as V1.34's did. Those drive stock's key seek: a long press sets `0xa4e880` (`0x53b4d0`), key-down (`0x53e000`) calls `playing_timer_clear` (`0x53dee0`), sets the mode byte `0xa4e881` to 1, steps `slider_play` 5 seconds within `[0, max]` and writes `label_playtime`, and key-up calls `player_seek_time` (`0x51f234`) with the slider value, then `playing_timer_start` (`0x53d928`). A touch drag takes the slider's handlers from the page's `widget_foreach` visitor (`0x53c5dc`): value-changing (`0xf`, `0x53e1fc`) writes the label and, in mode 0, clears the timer and sets mode 2; value-changed (`0xe`, `0x53dea8`) seeks the same way only in mode 2 (`0x53dbf8`). `player_seek_time` takes track seconds: it adds the current record's CUE start (`+0x48`), pauses DLNA, calls `mclSetSeek` (`0x5bd89c`), then polls `player_playtime` every 10 ms, up to 2 s, until it reaches the target. `player_seek_start` (`0x51f090`) is DLNA's and not used. `slider_set_value` emits will-change (`0xd`) and changed (`0xe`), never changing, so a set value in mode 0 neither seeks nor writes the label.

**Scrub.** On the top `playing_page`, with no window animation or pressed pointer, the key-up hook takes the center button and runs an iPod classic's Center cycle (`np_centre`, no `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS` wait): at rest a release starts the scrub; while scrubbing it ends the scrub (`scrub_end`, which seeks) and puts a focus ring on the first stop of shuffle, repeat and the heart (`st.np_stage`, `NP_STAGE_*`; `np_stop_ok`: shuffle and repeat need the theme's pair and no radio, the heart that `np_heart` finds it showing on the art page). A wheel tick moves the ring to the next or previous stop and stays at the ends (`np_stop_next`); it never changes a control. Center works the ringed one: shuffle or repeat steps as a tap on it does (`np_mode_step`) and the ring stays; the heart is clicked as a tap does (`stock_dispatch_trampoline` on `np_heart`), its like on or off, the ring staying. `np_modes` draws a 2 px Text Primary outline round the ringed control (`glyph_framed`; the heart's, `heart_ring`, the same box drawn as two `round_ring`s with no fill, so the heart shows through: the glyph's ink, its alpha's bounds as `glyph_ink` reads the loaded bitmap, joined with the on dot while it shows, 6 px clear to the stroke; a tap's fading `#2C2C2E` square is the same box 8 px clear, `press_share`, [oled-design](oled-design.md#now-playing)); `NP_STAGE_MS` (`SCRUB_MS`) without a key, Return, a touch or another top window end the stage (`np_cancel`). A theme without `playing.modes.icons` has no ring, and the scrub's press ends the cycle. A release `NP_HOLD_MS` (400 ms) or more after its press (`ringnav_keydown` stamps `center_down_at` with the press's time, `chord_gate`'s `centre_at`, which the key's repeats keep: a held Center's key-down repeats every 50 ms, so a stamp at each would make every hold a press), outside a scrub, is a short hold: it replays the release to `on_wm_keyup_fun`, which turns the screen off; stock's long press (Shut Down) never reaches the page. So is a double press, as on every other page: the first press scrubs at once, and a release within `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS` (250 ms) of the one that started that scrub, the wheel not turned between (`np_dc`, disarmed by any tick), ends it unseeked (`np_cancel`) and replays the release in place of ending it and ringing Shuffle; before, the double went into the ring. Apple's iPod classic guide (160 GB, "Press the Center button to cycle through these additional items") lists scrubber bar, Genius slider, shuffle slider, song rating and lyrics; the Q2 has no Genius, and its lyrics are a page of the swipe. Outside a scrub, with `dialog/volume_dialog` on top and Now Playing directly under it (`vol_band`, where `vol_paint` draws its band), the keys are the page's: a center release takes the same path rather than reaching stock, which turned the screen off at the first. `scrub_start` closes that dialog with `window_close`, as stock's own tap beside the bar does (`on_volume_tsup_fun`; its close timer is a widget timer, gone with the dialog), so the wheel's ticks reach the scrub and the band no longer covers the bar. The close sends Now Playing `EVT_WINDOW_TO_FOREGROUND`, whose stock handler (`0x53d9f0`) refreshes the page, setting the bar to the player's second, and restarts its timer, so `scrub_start` reads the target and clears the timer after closing. After a paused scrub that refresh drops the bar's held target, as any window closing over the page does, the dialog's own timeout included. Wake is unchanged: a press that wakes the screen never reaches the page, and one within `WAKE_MS` after it is dropped (`wake_gate`), so with the cycle a press soon after waking starts a scrub rather than turning the screen off. Starting (`scrub_start`) calls `playing_timer_clear`, reads the slider value as the target and sets the slider's fill (`fg_color` in the normal, pressed, over and focused states) to white; under a status row's set (OLED's, `V_STATUS_Y`) the fill keeps the accent and `paint_scrubber` draws a `NP_KNOB` (14 px) white knob on its end instead. While scrubbing, a wheel release moves the target by `SCRUB_STEP` (5) seconds times the 100 ms ramp's step (`ramp` keyed on the slider with `WHEEL_RAMP_MS`, so 5 to 40 seconds; the lists' gentler curve does not apply: every tick moves the target), clamped to `[0, max]`. It sets the slider value, writes `label_playtime` in stock's format and syncs the remaining label, marks the target moved if the step changed it (a tick against an end does not), rearms the `SCRUB_MS` (3 s) end and swallows the release. A playing track follows the moved target (`seek_scrub`, `patch/seek.c`): the first move sends `mclSetSeek(target + the record's CUE start)` at once, as the [scan](#scan)'s jumps do, and later ones at most every `SCRUB_SEEK_MS` (200 ms) since the last, a one-shot timer sending the latest target when the wait is over, so a spin of ticks 40 ms apart sends about one seek in five and the music is heard at the target as the wheel turns. Ending, if the target moved, the track plays and the player followed it, `seek_scrub_end` sends the target only if the last seek didn't (a seek to where the player already is would take it back to the target after it played on); otherwise (paused, below, or a target no tick moved, as a [chapter](#podcasts-and-audiobooks) row's) the end commits once through `seek_position`, as before. A playing track's scrub never calls `player_seek_time`, whose wait for the player's second would hold the UI thread on every move. It then restores the accent's light-tone fill. Paused (`mclGetPlayStatus` 3), `player_seek_time` would resume the track (`config_outputchannel`, then `mclSetResume`) to reach the target, so the scrub sends the seek alone, `mclSetSeek(target + the record's CUE start)`, as `player_seek_time` adds it: hciplayer's `mcl-seek` handler (`0x42c614`) mutes the DAC and flags the seek, and its seek (`0x42b070`) leaves the DAC muted while paused, so the track stays paused and plays from the target at Play. Unlike `player_seek_time`, it does not pause DLNA first, so a paused seek is not reported to a DLNA controller. After a seek, `playing_timer_start` waits for `settle_poll` (every `SETTLE_MS`, 250 ms): paused, the player's second stands still until Play, and the page's timer would put the bar back on the old second. The bar keeps the target until `player_playtime_and_length` is within a second of it, the track changes, the player stops, or `SETTLE_PLAY_MS` (2 s) of playing pass without it; a new scrub, the lyrics' wheel or an exit drops the wait (an exit that ends a scrub keeps the one its seek starts). A paused seek is remembered with the player's second when it was sent: reopening Now Playing on the same track, still paused and at that second, puts the bar back on the target and waits again, so a new scrub starts from it; playing or another track forgets it. Without a seek the timer restarts at once. It ends on a center press, the timeout, Return (swallowed on the page), a touch (before the slider sees it, so a drag seeks the stock way), another top window, or the page's `EVT_DESTROY`, which drops the target. After the playing track changed (queue position and path, recorded at the start) the target is dropped: the next tick ends the scrub without moving it, and any other end does not seek. The live seeks are measured in the emulator (`Test/08 position 44k16.flac`): ticks a second apart were heard at once, 5 s on each; a spin of ten ticks sent three seeks about 200 ms apart and played on from the last, with no seek at the end. On a Q2 each seek's DAC mute ([Wired start](#wired-start)) is a short gap per jump, not measured. The mode byte stays 0 throughout. Outside scrub the wheel stays on the volume.

**Lyrics.** The page's 250 ms timer also keeps the lyrics in view: when `mclGetLyricSize()` is positive it finds the current line among `scroll_lrc`'s children (`0x53d4dc`), sums the rows' heights up to three lines before it (stock creates a row 20 px tall, or 25 px a line when its text is wider than 225 px and wraps, `0x53b838`), and calls `scroll_view_scroll_to(scroll_lrc, 0, y, 10)` whenever the view's y offset (`+0x84`, `SCROLL_Y`) differs, so a moved offset lasts one tick. That y is a row top, but `scroll_view_scroll_to` (`0x603008`) clamps it to the end, content height (`+0x7c`, `VIEW_CONTENT_H`) less the view's 178 px, which is no whole number of rows, so near the end the top row was cut through. The call (`jalr` at `0x53d6e4`, `LYRIC_FOLLOW`) becomes `jal ringnav_lyric_follow`: `lyric_pad` first grows the content to the first row top at or past that end plus the view's height, so the end is a row top and under a row of blank space shows below the last line. A content no taller than the view is left as is. The page's refresh (`0x53cf08`) rebuilds the rows (`0x53b67c`, which ends with `scroll_view_set_offset(scroll_lrc, 0, 0)`) whenever `g_forcerefresh_flag` is set: Play/Pause (`playpause_quick_click`), the player's state changes and the page's return to the front (`EVT_WINDOW_TO_FOREGROUND`, `0x12b`) all set it, so the lyrics jumped to the top until the next follow scrolled back. Its one call (`bal` at `0x53d10c`, `LYRIC_ROWS`) becomes `jal ringnav_lyric_rows`, which puts back the offset the view had; the follow moves it if the line changed. Limit: the rebuilt content is its natural height until the next follow pads it, so near the end the relayout's clamp can cut the top row for up to 250 ms, as above. Limits: scroll_view's relayout (`0x604638`) recomputes the height from the children and clamps the offset, which cuts the row again until the next follow, at most 250 ms on. `ringnav_playing` keeps `slide_view` and `scroll_lrc`.

**Lyrics wheel.** Every UI loop pass, `lyric_poll` (iPod, from `ringnav_sleep`) checks for the lyrics page in front: `slide_view`'s value is 1, `playing_page` is the top window, `usable()`, no window animation or pressed pointer, `scroll_lrc` has children and `mclGetLyricSize()` is positive. While it is, `wheel_raw` is set, as for [Vortex](#games), so the wheel posts no ticks and each pass takes the raw travel from `wheel_travel` (200 units a turn). Setting or clearing it zeroes the travel, so nothing from before carries over, and the wheel is back on ticks and the volume within a pass of leaving. The travel moves a target, in sixteenths of a pixel so that slow turns keep their fractions: `LYRIC_ROW_PX` (20, stock's row; a one-row line, `lyrics_row_h`'s 51 px, on the [lyrics page](#word-timed-lyrics)) per tick's worth of travel at the Wheel Sensitivity (`WHEEL_TICK_UNITS` x 50 / `wheel_pct()` units), clockwise down, within `[0, content height - view height]` after `lyric_pad`. A turn moves the lyrics as far as its ticks did, but a pixel at a time instead of a row. Each pass then glides the offset towards the target (`lyric_step`, `scroll_view_set_offset`): a `dt / (dt + LYRIC_EASE_MS)` share of the way left (50 ms, `dt` capped at it), at least a pixel, so the motion eases in whatever the loop's pace. Starting a glide stops any stock scroll animator on the view, a drag's fling among them. While a finger stays on the wheel the lyrics stay where its travel put them; once it lifts (`wheel_held`, which `wheel_sample` sets at a finger's first sample and clears at its lift, raw or not) after travel moved them, the glide's target becomes the row top nearest it (`lyric_snap`), so no row is left cut at the top; the end is a row top already (`lyric_pad`). No key event reaches stock, so the travel itself sets `ringnav_input`'s idle stamp and calls `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 1)`, which keeps the loop at full pace and the screen on; `np_animating` keeps the pace while a glide moves. A tick that reaches the page before a pass has taken the wheel raw goes to `np_lyrics`, ahead of scrub, which glides to the next or previous row's top from the glide's target, so quick ticks add up.

**Lyrics hold.** Moving the lyrics, by wheel travel, a tick, or a finger that dragged `scroll_lrc` (a press that came down on the lyrics page, with `playing_page` on top, and the offset different at its release; stock's scroll animator stops at the press, so only the finger moves them, and a swipe that brings the page in holds nothing), ends any scrub (`scrub_end`, committing a moved target) and holds them (`lyric_hold`, keeping the playing track's `np_track`). Stock's timer keeps running, so the bar, the times and the highlighted line go on, but `ringnav_lyric_follow` returns without scrolling while the lyrics are held on that track, and while a pointer is pressed. A swipe to the art or info page and back keeps the hold; the page's destruction (`np_gone`, leaving Now Playing) ends it, and so does another Now Playing replacing the page before it goes (`ringnav_playing`, as `np_gone` leaves a replaced page alone), as does full screen. On the [lyrics page](#word-timed-lyrics) with timed lines (`lyrics_timed`: any line with a stamp) the hold also ends after `LYRIC_RESUME_MS` (5000 ms) at rest: `lyric_hold` stamps `lyric_held_at`, and every pass `lyric_poll` stamps it again while the thumb rests on the wheel with the page taking its travel (`wheel_held`) or a finger that came down on the page stays down (`lyric_touch` 1); once that long has passed since, on the page or off it, the hold drops and the follow takes the lyrics back to the playing line (gliding on the page, jumping off it). Untimed lyrics, which the follow keeps at their top, and stock's rows (`lyrics_on` 0, out of memory for the table) keep the hold as before. Another song (`np_track`: queue place and file, checked every pass while the page exists, on top or not) drops it too and puts the lyrics at the top at once, with no glide, stopping stock's animator (`lyric_top`). So does `ringnav_lyric_rows` when it rebuilds the rows for another song than the last rows' (`lyric_rows_song`): it leaves stock's offset 0 instead of putting back the old one, whatever moved the view since the song changed. Stock's `scroll_view_scroll_to` animates for 300 ms whatever its duration, ignores a new target while an animation whose goal is the top or the end runs, and an animation started with the screen off can still be moving when it comes back on: a follow sent with the last song's rows could otherwise carry the new song's lyrics back to the old place, or move them under a swipe onto the page. Off the page, not held, the follow is stock's `scroll_view_scroll_to`, so the lyrics are on the current line when you swipe back; on the page it glides there instead (`lyric_glide`). Another window on top, the screen off or a touch leave the hold alone. Any other page, or no lyrics, leaves the wheel on the volume. Before 1.4.6 the wheel jumped a row a tick and stopped stock's timer, bar and highlight included, until `SCRUB_MS` after the last tick or a touch, when the page jumped back to the current line. Limits: a drag on the screen stops anywhere, so it can leave the top row cut, and one that ends where it began holds nothing; a song repeated on its own (Repeat One) is the same song, so lyrics held on it stay held.

<a id="lyrics-search"></a>**Lyrics search.** Now Playing's ⋯ lyrics match (`onlinematching_page`) runs stock's `online_lyricthd` on its own thread: `online_setkeyword_info` has filled `keyinfo` (`0xa545f4`: file name, title at +0x200, album at +0x400, artist at +0x500) from the playing track's tags; the thread copies it (`online_getkeyword_info`, under its lock) and searches `title/artist` with `kugou_obtainlyric` (`0x51b3f4`: `mobilecdn.kugou.com` search, then `krc.php`), then `com163_obtainlyric` (NetEase `api/search/pc` and `song/media`, which now want a phone-bound account and return no lyric). Each writes the reply to `/tmp/oslyric_<thread>`, which the page shows. Accepting it (`0x535f24`) turns the file name into `<name>.lrc` (`modifystringtolrcsuffix`, `0x51caa8`: its last `.` on made `.lrc`) and, with a card (`/tmp/mmc_add`), `snprintf`s `cp -rf /tmp/oslyric_N "/mnt/mmc/.downpic/<name>.lrc"` (format `0x7867f0`) for `system()`, then reloads the lyrics (`mclLoadExLyric`); it never saved beside the song. That call (`jalr` at `0x536488`, `LYRIC_SAVE_CALL`; the format's `addiu` before it is pinned) becomes `jal ringnav_lyric_save`: for the queue's local song (the playing one first) whose file name stock turns into that `<name>.lrc`, not a CUE track's, it copies the file to `<path without extension>.lrc` beside the song through `.part`, removes `.downpic/<name>.lrc`, which the loader would show first, and leaves the command `:`, so `system()` does nothing and the reload finds the new file; otherwise (another song, a CUE track, a card that can't be written there) it copies the file to stock's `.downpic/<name>.lrc` itself, through `.part` too, and still leaves `:`: stock's command put the name, a file name or a card app's title, inside double quotes for `/bin/sh` as root, where `$(...)` and backticks still run ([GHSA-qp92-mq7c-6r64](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/security/advisories/GHSA-qp92-mq7c-6r64)). A name with a `/` (no file name has one, but a card app's title may, and `../` would leave `.downpic`) or whose `.downpic` path would not fit 0x208 bytes saves nothing. Limits: a song whose file name another song shares is saved beside the first of them in the queue; stock's "no lyrics" choice still removes only `.downpic`'s copy, and that command, `rm -rf "/mnt/mmc/.downpic/<name>"` for the same `system()`, is taken the same way: its `snprintf` (`0x53650c`, `LYRIC_DROP_CALL`) jumps to `ringnav_lyric_drop`, which unlinks the copy and leaves `:`. Kugou counts as found whenever the transfer completes, so NetEase ran only offline. The entry of `kugou_obtainlyric` jumps to `ringnav_lyric_search` (`patch/onlinematch.c`): it copies `keyinfo` the same way, asks `https://lrclib.net/api/search?track_name=&artist_name=` (percent-encoded, `lrclib_url`) through libcurl with the bundled CA file, parses the reply with demo's cJSON and writes the first result's `syncedLyrics`, less its opening credit lines (`lrc_body`: each line before the first sung one whose text holds `:`, as NetEase's `作词 : X` or `Mix Engineer : Y`, with any blank line among them; a tag line such as `[offset:...]` ends the search and stays, and a result with no sung line is skipped), UTF-8 with a BOM as Kugou's, to the same file; without one it writes nothing, and the page finds no lyrics. When the search finds no synced lyrics and taking the accents off the title or artist changes them (`lrc_fold`: each Latin letter of U+00C0-U+017F and U+1E00-U+1EFF, Vietnamese's among them, and `ơ`/`ư` as its plain letter, strokes and ligatures too, `ł` l, `ø` o, `đ` d, `æ` ae, `ß` ss, `þ` th, combining marks dropped), it searches those once more: LRCLIB's search already matches `é` to `e` but not `ł` or `ø`, and holds some songs only under the plain names ("Hataałii" finds none of its "Hataalii" entries). A reply that isn't a results array (LRCLIB's 503 `ServerOverloaded`, below) is asked again 2 s later, 3 requests in all, as Get Album Lyrics does (`LRC_BUSY`). LRCLIB is the only source: the hook never resumes Kugou's search, whose first result was often another song's (a song LRCLIB lacks got unrelated Chinese lyrics), and returns nonzero so that `online_lyricthd` skips NetEase too, whose `api/search/pc` now answers code -462 (bind a phone) and finds no song. Limits: no duration check, so a live or remastered version's timing may come back; plain-only results are skipped, since stock's loader drops lines without a stamp; the reply is capped at 512 KB (`LRCLIB_MAX`); a sung opening line with `:` in it is cut as a credit, while credits written `作词：X` (no spaces), after a tag line or after the first sung line stay.

<a id="cover-search"></a>**Cover search.** The same page's cover match runs `online_searchcover` (`0x51cbf0`): it clears stock's cover list (`p_deque_onlinecover` `0xa4db5c`, under `ponline_mutex`), adds `scover_default` (the track's current cover) and, when `/mnt/mmc/.downpic/<file name>.jpg` exists, that path, then starts `online_coverthd` (`0x51c624`). The thread copies `keyinfo`, builds the keyword `title&artist` (`artist&album` without a title), URL-encodes it and calls `kugou_obtaincover` (`0x51bf74`), `com163_obtaincover` (`0x51c46c`) and, while the list holds under 12, `baidu_obtaincover` (`0x51bbdc`), then sets `onlinematch_cover_threadflag` (`0x9b3281`). Each source adds image URLs with `online_addcoverlist` (`0x51b7a8`: up to 0x200 bytes, a duplicate string is dropped); Kugou's parser (`0x51bd20`) takes only a `.jpg` URL, only while the list holds under 12, and only if a HEAD (`getDownloadFileLength`) reports under 1 MB or fails. Once the flag is set the page makes one 110 px `onlinecover_%d` image per entry, three to a row, and queues them all (`online_coverlist_init`, `batchadd_onlinecover_task`): stock's cover thread downloads each URL with `curl_http_request` (redirects followed, at most 3, 5 s in all, verified as [Stock HTTPS](#stock-https) describes) to `/tmp/online/ori%d.jpg` and sizes it to 330 px `thumb%d.jpg` (`toolsTidalSpecCover`). Picking another than the first sizes that thumbnail into `.downpic/<file name>.jpg` and `.downpic/s_<md5>.jpg` (`toolsThumbSpecCover`, under `parse_cover_mutex`, `0x536248`); picking the first removes both. Now Playing's cover thread (`player_parsecover_thd`) shows `.downpic/<file name>.jpg` before the song's own art when it exists, by `snprintf`ing `cp -f "<it>" '/tmp/externpic.jpg'` (format `0x782974`) for `system()`: the file name sat inside double quotes for `/bin/sh` as root, so a `$` or a backtick in it was expanded, and a file name with a `$` never showed its pick. That call (`jalr` at `0x51db14`, `COVER_PICK_CALL`; the format's `addiu` in its delay slot is pinned) becomes `jal ringnav_cover_copy`, which copies the file through `.part` and leaves `:`. Stock's other `cp -f` commands, in `parse_albumcovertask_thd`, name only MD5s. The entry of `kugou_obtaincover` jumps to `ringnav_cover_search` (`patch/onlinematch.c`), which adds its own candidates in place of Kugou's search, and the entries of `com163_obtaincover` and `baidu_obtaincover` jump to `ringnav_cover_none`, which returns at once: the song's title and artist reach none of Kugou, NetEase (`music.163.com`) and Baidu (`image.baidu.com`), each asked by stock over plain HTTP. `online_coverthd` is the only caller of the three, and the three the only users of their host strings. With the album (else the title) and artist from `keyinfo` it asks MusicBrainz `ws/2/release/?query=release:"ALBUM" AND artist:"ARTIST"&fmt=json&limit=10` (Lucene-escaped and percent-encoded, `mb_url`; no artist clause without one) and, for each new `release-group` `id`, at most 4, sends a HEAD to the Cover Art Archive's `release-group/<id>/front-500` (5 s each): a redirect (307 today) names the group's front as a 500 px JPEG thumbnail on archive.org (`REDIRECT_URL`), which is added; a 404, no art, adds nothing. Then iTunes Search `search?entity=album&limit=5&term=ARTIST ALBUM` (`itunes_url`): each `artworkUrl100` with its last `100x100` made `600x600` (`itunes_art`), a JPEG. Ours stop once the list holds 10 (`COVER_FILL`); when they find nothing the page offers only the covers it started with. Requests use libcurl with the bundled CA file (DigiCert Global Root G2 signs MusicBrainz and iTunes, ISRG the Cover Art Archive), `Q2POD_UA` (`Q2Muse/<version> (repository URL)`, as MusicBrainz asks), 10 s to connect and 20 s in all (the HEADs 5 s), replies capped at 256 KB (`COVER_MAX`), on stock's cover thread; the images themselves are fetched by stock's cover thread (`curl_http_request`, [Stock HTTPS](#stock-https)). One MusicBrainz request per search keeps under its 1 request a second. Limits: a failed MusicBrainz request skips iTunes too, as a likely sign of no internet, so with Wi-Fi up but none the page waits one 10 s connect timeout more than stock; MusicBrainz answers a busy server with an error, which adds none of its covers; archive.org can take more than stock's 5 s download, which leaves that tile on the default art; the same cover from two services shows twice; only release groups' chosen fronts are offered, not each release's.

<a id="album-lyrics"></a>**Album lyrics.** Now Playing's ⋯ page (`playermore_page_init`, `0x539f60`, hooked by `ringnav_playermore` in `patch/onlinematch.c`) builds 8 rows, each button named by its position; its row click (`0x539dbc`) `atoi`s the name into a table of kinds (`PLAYMORE_ROWS`, `0x786a70`: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 0, 1), so Download Cover & Lyrics, kind 4 in `get_playmore_showinfo`, is third. For a playing song on the card with an album tag (not an online queue, `MCL_TYPE` `0xf1`/`0xf2`), the hook adds **Get Album Lyrics** under it in `list_row`'s widgets, with stock's `player_onlinesearch` icon and its rows' 24 px, 253 px label; the button has no name, so stock's click never sees it. A press needs Wi-Fi (`get_wifisignal`), then copies the album's tracks off stock's records (`coverflow_album_tracks`, as Go to Album: the album's songs in disc and track order; a CUE track is left out, as it shares its file's `.lrc`) and starts one worker thread (`album_lyrics`), which outlives the page. A 500 ms timer shows "Downloading N of M" on the row while the page is open, keeps standby and auto power-off waiting (`reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 0)`), then joins the worker and toasts the summary (`album_note`). A press while it runs cancels it ("Cancelling…"); USB storage (`ringnav_usbmode`) cancels and joins it first, quietly. Each track is on its own: a file gone from the card since the library's scan is passed over; one with a `.lrc` or `.LRC` beside it is left as it is; any other is searched exactly as the single search above searches LRCLIB (`lrclib`, shared: the record's title and artist, the first result with synced lyrics, less its opening credits), its lyrics written to `<name>.lrc.part` and renamed to `<name>.lrc` once whole, and then stock's `.downpic` copy for it (`lrc_name` of its file name), which would hide it, removed; a song LRCLIB lacks keeps that copy. LRCLIB answers some uncached searches with a 503 `ServerOverloaded` object (`Retry-After: 1`) instead of a results array, and the same search a moment later with results; the single search and the job both ask again 2 s later (`LJ_RETRY_US`), up to 3 requests a track (`LRC_BUSY`, `LJ_BUSY_TRIES`). Once LRCLIB has answered in the job, a failed request is retried once, 2 s later; two tracks in a row unanswered or still busy end it ("Can't reach LRCLIB", or "LRCLIB stopped answering" after some answered), as does a card that can't be written. A cancel stops a transfer at curl's next progress call (`XFERINFOFUNCTION`). However it ends, no `.part` stays and the lyrics saved before stay. Limits: one album at a time; a song without a title tag counts as not found; LRCLIB down while the internet is up reads as offline; as the single search, a live or remastered version's timing may come back.

**Lyrics from tags.** Stock's `mclLoadExLyric` (`0x5bd384`) clears the list and, unless the queue is online (`MCL_TYPE` `0xf1`/`0xf2`), loads the playing record's `<path without extension>.lrc` or `.LRC`; before them, for source types 3, 6, 12, 13, 15, 21 and 23 (the word at `0xa40000 - 0x413c`, mask `0x3a0b048`), `.downpic/<name>.lrc` (`/mnt/mmc/`, or `/tmp/` without a card), and for play type `0xf0` `/tmp/hifi/`, so a stale `.downpic` copy hides the `.lrc` beside the song (`0x5bbdc8`). It keeps only lines whose `[` is followed by a digit. A file without a byte-order mark that it does not take for UTF-8 it converts from GB18030 first (`iconv` to `/tmp/templyric`). Its test, `mclIsUtf8WithoutBOM` (`0x5bbc4c`, also the lyrics match page's), read only the 6 bytes from the first non-ASCII one and knew no 4-byte character, so a UTF-8 `.lrc` with an emoji, or with a character starting 4 or 5 bytes after that first one (`é` and three letters, then `’`; Korean's one-syllable words), was converted and loaded garbled or cut short. Its entry jumps to `ringnav_lrc_utf8` (`patch/lyrics.c`), which reads the first `LYRIC_TAG_MAX` bytes and checks them with `utf8_text`, the tag check in `patch/xiph.c`; a file that fails it still goes through stock's GB18030 conversion. Limit: a multi-byte character cut by that 64 KB read fails it. `ringnav_lyric` runs it first; when `mclGetLyricSize()` is still 0 for a local song (`REC_TYPE` 8, an absolute path), it opens the file with `taglib_file_new` and reads `LYRICS`, else `UNSYNCEDLYRICS`, with libtag_c's `taglib_property_get`, which demo does not import: its address is the one that call bound in demo's GOT (`TAGLIB_NEW_GOT`) minus `TAGLIB_FILE_NEW`, plus the pinned library's offset, and an entry still holding demo's stub reads nothing. Each line (CR, LF or CRLF), without the spaces at its ends, goes into stock's `stLyricInfo` list (`MCL_LYRICS`, under `MCL_LYRIC_LOCK`) at time `0x7fffffff`, which no track reaches: the page's timer then keeps the first line current and the view at the top, the wheel scrolls it as above, and the line `0x4da628` shows in `label_title` stays the default (both read from the disassembly, `0x53d550` and `0x4da700`). No temporary file is written. Limits: unsynced text only, so an ID3 `SYLT` frame is not read and `[mm:ss]` stamps inside a tag show as text; lines starting past the first 64 KB (`LYRIC_TAG_MAX`) are dropped; the file's tags are parsed once more on every track start without a `.lrc`, on the thread that starts it.

<a id="server-lyrics"></a>**Lyrics from a card app's server.** A song a card app put on the card (streamed, cached or synced) whose own lyrics are none, no `.lrc` beside it and no `LYRICS` or `UNSYNCEDLYRICS` tag, is asked of its app while the lyrics page shows it. At the end of every load `ringnav_lyric` notes the playing record when the load found nothing and the record is a local queue's song on the card (`playing_file`: not a `0xf1`/`0xf2` queue, `REC_TYPE` 8, an absolute path), as its path's FNV-1a (`la_key`, one word, so the loader's thread writes it whole), else 0. Every UI pass `lyric_poll` (`patch/nav/now_playing.c`) calls `lyrics_ask_poll` with whether the lyrics page is in front and lit; then, when the noted song is still the playing one, `mclGetLyricSize()` is still 0 and the path is not the one asked last (never the same song twice in a row, an answer of none or no answer included), `addon_lyrics_ask` (`patch/addon.c`) finds the app: the one whose folder (`/mnt/mmc/.<id>/`, its streamed and cached songs) or `q2app` `downloads=` folder (`/mnt/mmc/<downloads>/`, its synced songs) holds the path, when its `q2app` says `lyrics=1`; apps not listed since boot are scanned once (`addon_scan`, `lq.scanned`) so a song of none of them costs no scan after the first. It starts the app if needed (`addon_wake`) and writes `/tmp/q2-<id>.lrcask`, one line, `<seq> <path>`, once the app's socket is there, as the radio's `.radio` (the app takes a request there at its start as answered); until then each poll passes the path again (`addon_lyrics_answer`), so no path is kept in the scratch state, and a song changed meanwhile ends the wait. The app answers in its state file, `lyricsack=<seq> <code>`: 0 the `.lrc` is beside the song, 1 not its song, 2 its server has none, 3 no answer. `lyrics_ask_poll` reads it every `LYRIC_ASK_POLL_MS` (250 ms), for `LYRIC_ASK_WAIT_MS` (30 s) at most, and reads nothing while no request waits. Meanwhile the page shows what it shows for a song with no lyrics. On 0, with the song still playing and still without lyrics, it runs the load again on the UI thread (`ringnav_lyric`, as stock's lyrics match does after its accept, `0x535f24`) and sets `g_forcerefresh_flag`, so the page's next refresh rebuilds `scroll_lrc`'s rows from the new list (`ringnav_lyric_rows`, [Word-timed lyrics](#word-timed-lyrics)). Any other answer leaves the page as it is. Once the `.lrc` is there, stock's loader finds it at every later play and nothing is asked. q2-subsonic answers from the server's `getLyricsBySongId` or `getLyrics` and writes `[mm:ss.xx]` lines when they are timed, plain lines when not. A plain `.lrc` is read as text: stock's loader keeps only lines that start with a stamp, so when it kept none of a `.lrc` it opened, `ringnav_lyric` parses the copy it kept (`lrc_parse`) and puts its lines in stock's list a line each at `0x7fffffff`, as an unsynced tag's, without lines that are an LRC tag alone (`[ar:...]`, `lrc_idtag`); a `.lrc` of nothing but such tags gives way to the song's own tags. ponytail: a song is asked about once while it plays: an answer that comes after `LYRIC_ASK_WAIT_MS`, or a server back after none came, shows at the song's next play after another song's; two paths with one FNV-1a would count as one song. Checks in `test/fw` (`test_addon.py`, `test_lyrics.py`): the request and answer, a synced song in a `downloads=` folder, an app without `lyrics=1`, the page asking once and loading again on the answer, a plain `.lrc` and one of tags alone.

<a id="now-playing-links"></a>**Links.** `np_taps.c` makes the art page's artist (`scrlabel_artist`), album (`label_ipod_album`) and art (`img_cover`) links. `ringnav_playing` registers `np_tap` on the window for the pointer's down, move-before, up-before and abort: the window sees every touch whatever child takes it (the slide_view, its page, a label, or OLED's lyrics column), as `np_time_tap` does for the right-hand time, so the boxes are hit-tested from the window (`np_hit`), in whichever theme's layout the page has. A box counts only while the slide_view rests on its first page (`value` 0) and the lyrics are not full screen. A down on a box lights it; a move more than `TAP_PX` (10, AWTK's drag threshold) from where it came down unlights it, so a swipe never goes anywhere, and an up within `TAP_PX` on the same box starts `npt_go` on the next pass, outside the touch's dispatch. The handler returns 0 throughout, so the slide_view still swipes and the bar, heart and More keep their touches. `npt_go` calls `np_goto` in navigation.c, which runs the hold menu's own `qm_goto` for the playing record (`queue_now`), an album as `QM_LOOKUP_ALBUM`: `playerjumpinfo_page` as ⋯'s Look up Album opens it, never Cover Flow's tracks, which the menu's Go to Album opens under Artist View or an open Cover Flow (an artist still opens as Go to Artist and Look up Artist do, in Cover Flow under Artist View), under the menu's gates: Now Playing on top and usable, no menu up, a Library or folder queue (`MCL_TYPE` 1 or a `0xf000` class), not AirPlay, a card app's song only where its app has a page (`addon_goes`), and `qm_goes`, which the menu's Go to Album and Go to Artist rows share: a tag to go by and the single-instance page not already open (nor Cover Flow showing that album alone). A box that fails the gates is not lit and its tap does nothing. Lit, the label's text is the accent's text tone, or white (Light Mode's ink) when that tone is gray, as Graphite's is next to the line's own gray (`np_tap_ink`; `ringnav_style_color` asks `np_tap_lit`), and the art gets a 15% black fill (`np_tap_dim`, from `paint_cover`, before the rounded corners). Stock binds `img_cover`'s click to Enlarged Art (`0x53cb38`: `navigator_to("bigcover_page")` while the player is not stopped); `ringnav_dispatch` stops that click, so the art's tap is only the link, and a hold opens the full-screen art instead: a down on the art, lit while the album goes somewhere or the full-screen art may open (Now Playing in front and usable, `mclGetPlayStatus` not 1, stopped), starts `npt_hold` `ART_HOLD_MS` (500) later; a move past `TAP_PX`, a lift or an abort stops it. When it runs with the art still lit it unlights it, sets `npt.held` so the touch's lift is no tap, and calls `navigator_to("bigcover_page")`, whatever `g_bigcovermode` (Enlarged Album Art) says. `np_tap` also takes the swipe up to Up Next (`np_queue` on the next pass): a lift `SWIPE_UP_PX` (48) or more above its down, less than half as far across, with the slide_view at rest on the art page, from a down inside the slide_view's box (`np_hit`, above the bar). A down on the times or the state row never counts (the user's, 2026-11-18): a tap on Radio that rolls up 48 px as it lifts would otherwise open the queue, and its lift, off the row, gives Radio no click.

## Word-timed lyrics

iPod's lyrics page (`patch/lyrics.c`; [ipod.md](ipod.md#now-playing)): large lines, the playing one centered and lit word by word.

**Times.** Stock's `.lrc` parser (`0x5bbdc8`, inside `mclLoadExLyric`) keeps each line's whole seconds (`toolsTimeConvert`, `0x5cedbc`) and the text after its last `]`, A2 word stamps and all. Its `jalr fopen` of the file it parses (`0x5bc30c`, `LYRIC_OPEN`; after the encoding probe and any conversion, so the file is UTF-8) becomes `jal ringnav_lrc_open`, which opens it as stock asked and keeps a copy of its first `LYRIC_TAG_MAX` bytes. After stock's load `ringnav_lyric` parses that copy as it parses a LYRICS tag (`lrc_parse`): leading `[mm:ss.xx]` stamps to the millisecond (`.x`, `.xx`, `.xxx` or `:xx`), and A2 `<mm:ss.xx>` word stamps cut from the text, kept for a line with one stamp as each word's millisecond and byte offset; a UTF-8 byte-order mark is skipped. Every line loses the spaces at its ends (ASCII's space, tab, vertical tab and form feed, no-break, ideographic and zero-width spaces, a byte-order mark; `lrc_trim`, its word stamps' offsets moved with the text), and a blank one goes: an empty line between verses, a line of spaces, a stamp alone (stock's `" "`, an instrumental break) and the empty line CR CR LF line ends leave between every two. So both lyrics pages keep an even spacing between lines; lyrics that are all blank leave stock's result. Synced lines replace stock's list (`deque_clear`, then each line at its whole seconds, under `MCL_LYRIC_LOCK`), so the list never holds word stamps and is in millisecond order; unsynced ones leave it. Every load then sends its synced lines, or none, to the page (`lyrics_publish`): their UTF-32 text, starts and word stamps, and an FNV-1a sum of each line's whole seconds and characters as stock's rows will hold them.

**Rows.** The page's refresh still rebuilds `scroll_lrc`'s labels (`0x53b67c`, `LYRIC_ROWS`), and so does `playing_page_init` (`0x53e524`, before `ringnav_playing` knows the page), so `ringnav_playing` takes the rows its init built too (`lyric_init`). `lyrics_rows` takes the sent table when its sum matches the labels' (`lrc_time` and text), keeps the last one when that matches, and otherwise builds one from the labels (whole seconds, no word stamps), so the page never shows another song's. It lays every line out with `widget_get_canvas`'s canvas in the playing line's face at `LYRIC_OLED_PX` (27, the design's 22): rows of `375 - 2 * LYRIC_OLED_X`, breaking before a space or beside a CJK character, else mid-word, up to `LYRIC_ROWS` (4, which still fit the view) of them, the rest cut. Each label's text is then emptied and it becomes the view's width and its line's rows high, 30 px apart (`LY_PITCH`), plus `LYRIC_GAP` (`LYRIC_SLOT` less a pitch at `LYRIC_PX`'s 34, 21 px, so a line of one row is 51 px, `lyrics_row_h`). `lyric_init` gives `scroll_lrc` the list layout `list_view(x=0,y=LYRIC_SLOT,s=0)` (`tools/ipod.py` gives `view_lrc` and `scroll_lrc` the full 375 px), which stacks the rows after a blank slot. A line's follow target centers its row in the view (`lyric_centre`); `lyric_pad` makes the content the last row's plus the view's height, so the last line can reach the middle. `ringnav_paint` draws each row's line (`lyrics_paint`, the row found among the children), its rows centered in it, `LYRIC_OLED_X` (24) from the left, in Inter (`ly_face`: Medium for the playing line, which also measures every wrap, Regular for the rest), every row in view at full alpha. The playing line is drawn `LYRIC_LIT` with the clip ending at its lit width and Text Secondary (`LYRIC_OLED_REST`) with the clip starting there; other lines Text Secondary; after the rows, the view's own border paint (`lyrics_fade`, from `ringnav_paint`) lays `LYRIC_FADE_PX` (32) one-row fills of the page's ground (`ui_ink`, so white in Light Mode) at the top and foot of what shows of the view, found by intersecting its ancestors' boxes (the window under the status row, the slide above the progress bar), each from clear inside to opaque at the edge, as `marquee_fade` does a label's columns. They paint in the canvas's clip, so a scroll's repaint fades each line where it now is. Cost: 64 calls and at most 2 x 32 x 375 = 24,000 blended pixels in stock's `fill_bgra8888_rect` a full repaint, less in a dirty rect, and nothing per pixel in the payload. With no memory for the table the rows stay stock's, and the [lyrics wheel](#scrub-ipod) moves them as before, a row a tick.

**Follow.** Stock's follow (`ringnav_lyric_follow`) does nothing on the page. Every UI pass with the page in front and lit, else every `LYRIC_FOLLOW_MS` (250 ms, stock's timer's pace), `lyric_follow` finds the playing line, the first of those starting when the last started line did (lines sharing a stamp light together), and targets the offset that centers its row (line 0's before the first starts): glided to on the page, set at once off it, never while held or while a pointer is down. After a tap's seek to a line (`np_lyric_line`, under Full screen) `lyric_seek_ms` gives the follow that line's start instead of the clock's position until the player gets there: until the position is at or past the line's start (and under `LYRIC_SEEK_MS`, 2000 ms, past its whole second), or `LYRIC_SEEK_MS` of playing pass without it (paused, the wait restarts every pass, as the bar's `settle_poll` waits for Play); another song drops it (`lyric_top`). So the view goes straight to the tapped line instead of back to the one playing before the seek landed. Limit: a tapped line that started less than `LYRIC_SEEK_MS` before the position counts as reached at once, and the old line shows until the player gets there. Wheel travel moves a one-row line's height (`lyrics_row_h`, 51 px) per tick's worth instead of `LYRIC_ROW_PX`, so a tick lands on the next row's top, where the snap on letting go keeps it. `lyrics_now` reads the clock on those passes, so its bounds narrow on each second's change; off them (another page, another window on top, the screen off) the follow goes by the whole second (`lyrics_sec`, as stock's), which lets the bounds go, so the clock starts again, wide, when the page is back in front. While `playing_page` is on top and lit, the playing line's rows repaint when its lit width changes, at most every `LYRIC_PAINT_MS` (66 ms, about 15 a second; a word-timed line's width moves nearly every pass, and the idle loop passes every 25 ms), and the last line's when another line starts. Limit: the lit sweep moves in steps of up to `LYRIC_PAINT_MS` of the song, a few pixels at a fast word; the value is a guess.

**Full screen.** Stock's page binds nothing to its lyrics, so `ringnav_playing` binds nothing to its lyrics, so on either layout `ringnav_playing` binds `view_lyric`'s `EVT_POINTER_DOWN` (before children), `EVT_POINTER_UP_BEFORE` and `EVT_POINTER_ABORT` (`np_lyric_touch`). A release within `TAP_PX` (10, AWTK's drag threshold) of its press either way, so no swipe or drag of the lines, with lyrics on (`lyrics_on`) or already full screen, toggles `np_full`: the page's column (`tools/ipod.py` `playing_page`: full width, under the 40 px top row, down to just past the dots; the title is on the art page) takes the whole window: y 0 and the window's height, its dots `NP_FULL_FOOT` (20 px) above the foot, and `view_lrc`, whose `self_layout` fixes it at the slide's `lift` and 178 px, from the top to 20 px above them (`widget_set_self_layout_params`, the old place written back off); the width stays 375, so nothing rewraps. The hold drops, so the follow glides to the playing line. Off, the column goes back to its index, place and `slide_view` height from before (`np_was`). Return ends it as a tap does, and stays on the page (`STOP`). A tap on a line seeks instead when it can (`np_lyric_line`): the lift's point in `scroll_lrc`'s content (`widget_to_local`, its scroll counted) inside the view, on a row whose line has a time and does not start with the playing line (`lyrics_row_ms`, -1 otherwise), with the player playing or paused (`mclGetPlayStatus` 2 or 3); then the track goes to that line's whole second as a chapter row's pick does (`chapter_pick`): the scrub's fields set to it, `scrub_end`, which seeks a playing track (`player_seek_time`) or a paused one on Play (`seek_position`, `mclSetSeek` and `held_sec`), the bar and elapsed time on the target until `settle_poll` sees the player there, and a pending resume (`rs_pending`, `rs_go_key`) dropped. The hold drops and `lyric_seek` starts (Follow). A tap on the playing line, off every row, on untimed lyrics or with the player stopped toggles full screen as before. The sources that seek are every one Now Playing shows: it shows only the Library's player (`now_source.c`), a card file or a stream q2player reads (a card app's `0xf1` queue, a URL queue), so the tap seeks where the bar's scrub does; AirPlay's sender is that player too, the speaker following behind (`airplay_lyrics`). Spotify, Radio, Internet Radio and videos have no lyrics page; a Library held for them (`now_hold`) is stopped, so it takes no seek. Handlers return 0, as the heart's do: the `slide_view` behind takes a swipe and `scroll_lrc` a drag of the lines as stock does, and either's abort ends full screen, so the pages slide in their column; a touch taken that way is no tap at its lift (`np_tap_x` `1 << 20`). `lyric_poll` ends it off the lyrics page, while a window over the page leaves it as it is; the page's destruction drops it; a page without `slide_view` has no column, so `np_full` does nothing and full screen never starts. Limits: a tap brings back lyrics the wheel or a finger held; any window over the page, a toast or the volume included, ends it; the covered widgets still repaint under the column (the bar every second, a long title's scroll), redrawing the lyrics beneath them.

**Clock.** `player_playtime_and_length` reports whole seconds, which stock's status thread (`mclSyncPlayerStatus`, `0x5bb874`) asks hciplayer for every 200 ms (`{media-info\get-music-info}`, its fourth field). `lyrics_now` keeps the offset from `time_now_ms` to the position as an interval: the first second seen, or one after a jump (a seek, another song), puts it anywhere in that second plus a poll (`LYRIC_POLL_MS`, 250); the next second's arrival while playing puts the position at most a poll past that second, and the two intersect, or restart from that change when they disagree. Paused (`mclGetPlayStatus()` not 2) it holds; on Play it goes on from where it stopped until the next second replaces that guess. It never runs more than a poll past its reported second.

**Lit width.** A line without word stamps is lit whole from its start (`ly_lit`). One with them is lit through them, from stamp to stamp, each at its character's distance along the line's rows laid end to end; before the first, from the line's start; past the last, at `LYRIC_UNIT_MS` a letter (90 ms; three for a CJK character; `LYRIC_MIN_MS`, 800, at least), done by the next line's start. Limits: the clock knows the position to about a poll, 0.1 s either way, and doesn't allow for the output's latency (Bluetooth's); a line longer than four rows is cut.

## Pull-to-search

Pull-to-search starts from the existing touch hook only on a real pointer-down (`0x100`; the stock window manager registers `on_wm_tsdown_before_fun` for that type), while the separate move-before callback (`0x102`) tail-calls the same entry point. It applies to Local Songs (`localmusic_page`), the same list where a set with `home_lib` shows it on Home's window (`scroll_view_localmusic` on `home_page`, in Split), and Internet Radio (`radio_page`): Folder view has no working stock search, so it is excluded. It checks the screen coordinates, list bounds and initial scroll offset, then uses page-owned move/up-before-children callbacks (`0x102` / `0x104`). A downward drag of at least `PULL_CLAIM_PX` (8), greater than its horizontal travel, claims the pointer. The native abort event (`0x107`) clears pressed descendants; a widget-owned suppression flag also rejects late row clicks until the next touch. A floating, non-interactive label overlays the page without changing the list or its indices. Release at `PULL_SEARCH_PX` (48) invokes the stock Local Songs search callback `0x5350d4`, which opens `dialog/search_dialog` without replacing the browsing page; on Internet Radio it calls `radio_search` (radio.c) instead. The stock search dialogs quit on Return even while their edit's keyboard is open, which destroys the edit under the keyboard and freezes demo; `search_key` (navigation.c's `ringnav`) reads the editing target from the input method (`IM_WIDGET`, `+0x04`, pinned against stock's `input_method_request`), since the keyboard is a separate top window and its focus chain does not contain the search edit. It closes the keyboard on the first Return (`widget_set_focused(search_edit, 0)` plus `input_method_request`, since the searchbox dialogs' edit does not close on blur), and the next Return runs stock's quit with the keyboard already shut. Moving back below the threshold cancels activation. Page/surface destruction, backgrounding, close and input interruption clear the gesture. The stock quick-settings start region (`y < 31`) is excluded. The Library has a **Search** row (`ringnav_localmusic`); under `list.entry.ipod` (OLED's) the row and the pull call `library_search_open` (`patch/search_strip.c`) instead, which opens `searchstrip_page`, an iPod classic's letter strip with no keyboard: one sheet the payload paints (`search_strip_paint`), its keys taken in `ringnav` before stock's (`search_strip_key`), the songs from `staged_music(all_songs)` searched for songs by title, artist or album as the playlist editor's Add Songs search is, then artists, then albums (one row per name, case aside). The tab picks the list (`ss_filter`): All takes `SS_GROUP` (32) of each group, so a string most titles hold still reaches the artists in 32 wheel ticks (the strip's list moves a row a tick, with no ramp), its artists and albums deduplicated against those before them in song order; Songs, Artists and Albums take their group whole, the artists and albums sorted by name (`qsort`) and deduplicated in one pass, since checking each of a big library's thousand artists against the rest per keystroke would not keep up. Any song matching means some group does, an artist's or album's song holding the text too, so a submit goes to the results (or, on an empty tab, the tabs) only then. The tabs are `segments_paint` (`slider_page.c`), the segmented control EQ's Simple and Advanced draw, given a 30 px track in the first row under the query. The text is ASCII, a byte a character, and `ss.cur` is the cursor: `ss_type` inserts at it and `ss_erase` takes the character before it, Previous and Next move it (`ss_move`), and `ss_typed` draws the query's run of characters that keeps the cursor on its line. A selection runs from the byte `ss.mark - 1` (0: none) to the cursor, either way round (`ss_sel`), so a drag only ever moves `ss.cur` and the loupe stays on the moving end. `ss_grab` counts taps in `ss.taps` (each pressed within `SS_MULTI_MS`, 350 ms, of the last one's release and `SS_MULTI_DX`, 20 px, of it): the second selects `ss_word`'s word, the third the whole text, the fourth is a tap again; a press within `SS_HANDLE_DX` (12 px) of either end takes that handle, `mark` and `cur` swapping when it is the anchor's. `ss_reach` moves what `ss.drag` says the finger holds: the cursor, a double tap's word (`word_a` to `word_b`, kept while the end on the finger's side follows it) or a handle (never onto the other end). `ss_cut_sel` takes the selection out before `ss_type` inserts and as a held Previous's first erase (a space it leaves doubled or first going too, unless a box's), `ss_move` collapses it to its start or end, and `ss_field` and `ss_loupe_paint` draw the highlight (`accent_tone(2)` at `SS_SEL_ALPHA`, 40 %) under the text and the handles over it. It adds 16 bytes to `ss`. The strip is one loop of stops, `ss.stop`: 0 the set switcher, then the set's characters and a space (`ss_run`), then the return key (`ss_stops`); `ss_sets` holds the four sets, every printable ASCII character between them, and `ss.off` is the run's first cell shown, moved by `ss_follow` only to keep the highlight a cell in from either edge of the ten. `ss_turn` steps the stop round the loop; a wheel tick under `SS_GESTURE_MS` (250 ms) after the one before (`ss.turn_at`) belongs to the same turn, and a turn that reached the return key (`ss.halted`) goes no further, so crossing from it to the switcher takes a new turn. The run's letters fade where more of the set lies past an edge by their own alpha (`ss_run_letter`): a character in the 22 px band is drawn a 2 px slice at a time under `canvas_set_clip_rect`, each slice in its own alpha, rather than a gradient of the pill's colour laid over it. Return's press starts `ss_hold_tick` (`search_strip_down`); let go before `SS_HOLD_MS` (600 ms) and `search_strip_key` shuts the strip (`ss_shut`: the wheel to the text, `SS_ON_FIELD`, the erase and pop timers and any grab let go; the strip is not painted while `ss.focus` is set, and the results' foot, `ss_foot`, is then `client_h()`, so they fill the page), or, the strip already shut, leaves (`ss_leave`), else the tick closes the page (`ss_leave`) and arms `RETURN_RELEASE_LATCH` itself, as stock's long press does, so stock's key-up filter swallows the release; stock's own long press comes at `KEY_HOLD_MS` (700 ms), after the close, and `search_strip_hold` takes it for the page that closed (`ss_hold_closed`, within 400 ms) so the page under it does not open Now Playing. A held Return reaching `compact_now_playing` with no press seen closes the page at once. Previous's press arms `ss_erase_due` 450 ms ahead; each erase arms the next, 500 ms, then 15 % sooner each time down to 110 ms, and the release, its erases made, moves no cursor. `search_strip_owns` keeps a hold of Previous or Next there from scanning the song (`seek.c` `seek_allowed`) and from stock's long press (`ringnav_keylong`). Play/Pause on the strip submits (`ss_submit`): a box's OK, a name's save, Search's results. A drag along the strip runs on `EVT_POINTER_MOVE_BEFORE`, moving the highlight a stop per 19 px as one turn (`ss_slide`), each step popping as a wheel tick; a tap types the cell under it, cycles the set on the switcher, or submits on the return key. Each result row is grayed as other lists' are ([server library](server-library.md#grayed-rows)): `catalogue_unavailable` for a song, `catalogue_artist_unavailable` and `catalogue_album_unavailable` (`group_unavailable`) for an artist or album, the text in `#666666` (the bar's white at 70 % on the selection) and `catalogue_mark_paint` at the right column, the text ending 12 px short of the mark. The key pop is `tools/art.py`'s images for a theme with the key (`pop_images`): the bubble (`oled_search_pop`, one SVG path, nonzero fill, in the accent's top tone) and a strip of a cell per character of the sets in their order (`oled_search_pop_letters`, 24 px Inter Medium, `POP_CHARS`; `ss_pop_cell` finds the cell), each glyph's ink centered on its cell from the face's outlines without snapping; the key under the bubble keeps its character drawn as the strip's letters are, in white at 60 %. The return key's marks are six more (`oled_search_return_<kind>_w` and `_a` for `search`, `go` and `save`, `return_mark` from `RETURN_MARKS`: the user's mock-up's 24-unit glyphs, a magnifier, an arrow right and a check, round stroked and scaled into a 20 px box). Which one shows is `ss_ret_kind`: the kind the caller gave (`STRIP_*` in `peq.h`: an edit's `_strip_return` int prop for `search_strip_box`, `search_strip_return` before `search_strip_text`, or set by Search, Add Songs, Rename and New Playlist themselves), else the magnifier when the text is on the query line (a stock search box, TIDAL's) and the arrow anywhere else. `search_strip_paint` draws the bubble's cells at whole pixels with `canvas_draw_image` over the lit cell, in place of its key; `ss_pop_step` times it on each wheel step and drag step (`SS_POP_MS`, `SS_POP_FAST_MS`) and `ss_pop_due` invalidates only the bubble's box. An artist opens `localmusic/artistinfo_page` with `{0xf001, record}` as Now Playing's Artist info does, an album `coverflow_goto_album` as Era's albums do, and a song plays with `play_folder` as a song list (`0xf001`) of the songs found ([ipod.md](ipod.md#search)). Every other text box types on the strip too, on the keyboard window its input method opens ([The keyboard](#the-keyboard)). A password shows as dots (`ss.secret`, `ss_secret_box`), and no stock edit says it holds one: every box's `input_type` reads back 0, its page's `password` included. A network's own password box (`kbwifipass_dialog`) is the edit named `edit_passwd`; Add Network's two rows both open `editwifi_dialog` (its edit named `edit`, `tr_tips` unset), whose init keeps the context its opener passed, 1 for the password row and 0 for the name, in an unnamed word at `0xa3b070` (`EDITWIFI_PASSWORD`, stored at `0x49a698` and read to pick the hint at `0x49a6b4`). A payload box marks itself: a card app's field titled as a password or showing the app's asterisks (`addon.c` `field_secret`) sets `_secret` on its edit, and the Guest Play hotspot's password calls `search_strip_secret` before `search_strip_text`. The character just typed shows for `SS_PEEK_MS` (1 s), a timer (`ss_peek_due`) repainting the dots when it ends, and moving the cursor ends it at once.

`patch/ipod.json` records the added private prologue and native event ABI instructions alongside the compact sites and assets. The builder checks them against the pinned stock executable and checks the byte sizes of all referenced global flags/values.

## Search bar

<a id="search-bar"></a>A music list page's own search (`patch/search_bar.c`, `search_strip_scoped` in `patch/search_strip.c`; [oled-design](oled-design.md#search-bar)). **The bar.** navigation's wheel (`input.c`), where a list's first row meets a turn up and would lean against the end, asks `search_bar_up` first: on a page `sb_page` names (the Library's music lists, stock's and the payload's), under `list.entry.ipod`, it moves the surface's parent (the list or table view) down `SB_BAND` (40) px with `widget_move`, notes its rest place and the band's top in the page's coordinates, and sets `st.touch_mode`, so the rows' selection hides as after a touch. `ringnav_paint` paints the band (`search_bar_paint`: the ground, then `search_pill_paint`'s outlined pill, the words "Search " and the status row's title). `search_bar_key`, in `ringnav` before a list's own keys, takes the lit bar's: a turn down (`search_bar_off`: the list back, the selection shown), a turn up (nothing), Centre (the search). One page's bar at a time; its `EVT_DESTROY` (bound once a page, `_sb_bound`) forgets it.

**The search.** `search_strip_scoped` opens `searchstrip_page` over the page with its rows in `sc.rec`, as they are (`sc_take`): a `table_client` over `p_deque_showlist` gives its records, `SC_NAMES` with the class's name field on `localclass_page` and `album_page` (Albums, Artists, Composers, Genres: the A-Z index's fields), else `SC_SONGS`, a song's title, artist or album matched as Search's songs are; any other surface gives its rows, `SC_ROWS`, matched by their first label's words (`sc_words`). `ss_filter` takes `ss_scope_filter` instead: the rows holding the text, in the page's order, kind `SS_SONG` or `SS_NAME`. The query line is the bar (`search_pill_paint`, lit while the strip or the wheel is on the text); `ss_alone` gives it Add Songs' behaviour with no tabs: Return shuts the strip (`ss_shut`, the text and results kept), a turn down goes to the results, the go key to the first result or with none the text (`ss_submit`), and Return on the text leaves (`ss_leave`) to the page, its bar still lit. Centre on a result (`ss_scope_go`) closes the strip's page and keeps the row's place; `ss_scope_due`, a 16 ms timer, waits for the page on top and settled, then puts the bar out of sight, selects the row (`ringnav_jump` on a table, `ringnav_select` else) and sends Centre's press and release through `ringnav_input`, so the row does what it does on the page. ponytail: `sc.rec` is the page's rows at the open; a page that rebuilds its rows under the search (none of these do while it is on top) would leave its results pointing at the old ones.

## The keyboard

Stock's on-screen keyboard is gone (the user's, 2026-11-18): the letter strip ([oled-design](oled-design.md#text-entry)) is the only way the wheel or a finger types. AWTK opens a keyboard window in one place, the default input method's request (`input_method_default`'s show, inlined in the request at `0x69f650`, `KB_REQUEST`), which picks the keyboard's name from the edit (its `keyboard` property, else by input type: `kb_ascii_t9`, `kb_float`, `kb_uint`, `kb_ufloat`, `kb_hex`, `kb_phone`) and calls `window_open` with it at `0x69fb5c`, then, should that fail, with `kb_default_t9` at `0x69fbd0`. Both `bal window_open` words become `jal kb_host_open` (`KB_OPEN_SITES`, `patch/keyboard.c`), which makes a bare keyboard window with `window_base_create(NULL, g_keyboard_vtable, 0, V_BAR, 375, 320 - V_BAR)` (`g_keyboard_vtable` is in `CONTEXT_DATA`), names it as stock's would be, and hands it and the input method's edit to `search_strip_box` before it returns, so the strip is on it in its first frame. It is a keyboard, so the input method keeps the edit focused under it, and its close still ends the strip (`kb_gone`, `ss_closed`). The request's `widget_set_prop_str(keyboard, "open_anim_hint", "popup")` at `0x69fef4` becomes `jal kb_open_hint`, which sets nothing (`KB_OPEN_HINT`), so the window does not slide up from the screen's foot. `kb_host_bg` paints its ground black (a bare keyboard has no style), in `ringnav_paint_bg`, and `ringnav_paint` leaves stock's border paint out for it (`kb_host_border`): with no style of its own, stock drew the theme's default border round it, a light outline round the strip's page from the status row's foot down, on every text box. A box on a stock dialog of its own, a network's password (`kbwifipass_dialog`) or Add Network's (`editwifi_dialog`), sits in a row at the status row's height with stock's back arrow (`img_return`) beside it, on a black dialog of the whole screen; the window manager paints dialogs after the status row, so that band covered the bar and its title (stock's "Please enter password" box stood where the title belongs). While the strip types, the keyboard window covers the dialog below the bar, so `search_strip_box` hides the dialog's children that start above `V_BAR` and clears its ground (`ss_band_clear`, as the confirmation card clears stock's), and the status row shows through. Under the bar then lies what the dialog's highlighter (`highlight`, `default(alpha=100)`) dims, Add Network's own dialog's title row among it (on the emulator), so the bar lays a black ground of its own meanwhile (`search_strip_bar_ground`, in `ringnav_paint_bg`); the highlighter dims the bar too, so `ss_bar_over` paints it again over the dialog, after its children (`search_strip_overlay`). `ss_closed` puts the dialog back, black as stock made it, if it is still up (an OK that leaves it open; `ss_band_back`).

Before this, the strip took stock's T9 keyboard window from the loop pass after its first paint, and the window's 0.5 s slide-in ran first: on Add Network's password the T9 keys slid up under the dialog's own box, lifted to the status row, for 25 frames before the strip replaced them (recorded on a pooled emulator, 2026-11-18). Now the dialog is followed by the strip in the next frame.

**What the build checks.** `stock_window_opens` walks stock demo's text for every call to `window_open` and `window_open_and_close` (a `bal`, a `b` tail call, or a `jalr $25` of the GOT slot holding either, the name argument followed back through the GOT loads and `addiu` that build `$4`; `_gp` is `.got` plus `0x7ff0`), and for every instruction that forms the address of a keyboard's name (`KB_NAMES`). `check_keyboard_opens` stops the build unless the calls inside `KB_REQUEST` are exactly `KB_OPEN_SITES`, every other call is one `WINDOW_OPENS` names (ten in V1.36: the navigator's page opener, a widget's open action, the file chooser, the combo box's popup, the text editor's context menu, `window_open_and_close` and the `window_open` stub, none passing a keyboard's name), and the only code naming a keyboard is `KB_NAME_READS` (the Wi-Fi and rename dialogs' own widget lookups and Tidal's quality picker closing one by name). So a new caller that could open stock's keyboard fails the build. `test/unit/test_build.py` proves each refusal; `test/build.py --build` runs the check on the stock image and reads the three patched words.

**What the image drops** (`KB_ASSETS`, removed with the stock EQ pages and `OBSOLETE`): `ui/kb_default_t9.bin` (15,591 bytes), `styles/keyboard.bin` (3,736) and the ten `images/xx/keyboard_{del,enter,upper,lower,space}{,_down}.png` (5,693), 25,020 bytes in all; nothing else names them (the `keyboard_password`, `keyboard_netname` and `keyboard_keyword` in the strings files are text ids, and `peq_ui.c`'s `kb_default_t9` is only a name the input method hands `kb_host_open`). `english_ui` no longer rewrites the T9 page. On the `--dev` build of this branch the root filesystem is 8,192 bytes smaller compressed (51,568,640 to 51,560,448), and the payload's code 1,408 bytes smaller, its wheel walk over stock's keys (`kb_wheel_key`, `kb_wheel_bg`) gone (322,296 bytes free of 1,572,864; scratch state 12,868 free).

## Page parallax

`patch/page_parallax.c` ([oled-design](oled-design.md#motion)). Every sliding window's hint is stock's `htranslate` (`tools/ipod.py` `SLIDE`, the theme's `motion.page`), whose animator (`window_animator_htranslate_create`, `0x696fb8`) snapshots both windows at the start and draws them each frame from its vtable at `0x93b234` (`.data.rel.ro`; `window_animator_t`: duration `+0`, `prev_win` `+0x14`, `prev_img` `+0x1c`, `curr_img` `+0x64`, `open` `+0xac`, `percent` `+0xb4`, eased, `canvas` `+0xb8`, `time_percent` `+0xbc`, 1 at the end). Stock's `draw_prev_window` (`0x696d90`) draws the page under `w * percent` left (the whole way with the new page) and paints any window between the two shifted with it; `draw_curr_window` (`0x696c40`) the new page `w * (1 - percent)` right; `update_percent` (`0x696bd0`) eases `time_percent` (reversed for a close). `tools/build.py` `HTRANSLATE_SLOTS` points the update, draw_prev and draw_curr slots at `parallax_update`, `parallax_prev` and `parallax_curr`, each of which runs stock's own (`PRIVATE_FUNCTIONS` `htranslate_*`) with its change: `parallax_update` runs a close's `time_percent` `PAGE_SLIDE_MS / PAGE_POP_MS` as fast before stock eases it, so a pop ends after 200 ms where a push takes 220 (the animator's end is that time's, read after); `parallax_prev` calls stock's with `percent` scaled to `PX_UNDER_PCT` (30%), then darkens what the new page does not yet cover, black at `PX_DIM_ALPHA` (64 of 255) times `percent`, in both halves as iOS dims. The status row is the system bar's own window, painted over the slide in place, so it stays put; its title is the new page's at once (a `ponytail:` in the file: cross-fading it would draw both pages' titles into the bar). Stock paints the bar first in each frame (`window_animator_begin_frame`, `0x6968f8`), before `window_animator_update` (`0x6961f8`) runs `update_percent`, `draw_prev_window` and `draw_curr_window`; every page is the whole screen ([oled-design: Full-bleed](oled-design.md#full-bleed)), so the snapshots cover that paint, and `parallax_curr` paints the bar again after stock's draw of the new page, with the page under and this frame's `percent` readable through `parallax_slide` for that paint alone. The bar lays no ground of its own: every page is full-bleed, so each page's own ground runs under it. Home in Split under the slide keeps its band, the art's and the raised list's rows under the status row, in its own snapshot, drifted and darkened with it; the title (`bar_title_fades`, `theme_titles_paint.c`) shows only over the sliding page, faded to its share, in place, clear of the status row's glyphs. The glyphs keep the bar's ink over the art while it slides (`ponytail:` the still bar inks them by contrast with the art under them from the screen's buffer, `home_ink_bar`; the slide's paint leaves them as they are, so in Light Mode the clock is dark on the art until Home settles). Under Reduce Motion the hint is `fade` (`motion_row`), whose animator is untouched. The page slide is `PAGE_SLIDE_MS` 220 (the theme's `motion.page.ms` and `motion.swap.ms`).

## Swipe back

`patch/swipe_back.c`, after iOS's edge swipe ([oled-design](oled-design.md#gestures)). **Claim.** `ringnav_touch` hands every pointer-down that stock, the A-Z index and Edit Library left alone to `swipe_back_down`; one within `SB_EDGE_PX` (24) of the left edge is a candidate when the top window is a normal `window` (not a dialog or Control Center) or the letter strip's (a text box's keyboard window, `search_strip_open`), no window animates, `usable()` holds, Return would leave something and the press is not on full-screen lyrics (Return stays on the page there). What Return leaves, the layer that moves: on Home, the list one of its rows opened (`coverflow_home_sublist`, what `coverflow_home_back` closes); elsewhere the top window, if a normal window lies under it in the window manager's stack (Home's own list has none, and takes no swipe). The window gets `sb_event` for destroy, close, abort, move-before and up-before, bound once (`_sb_bound`), as `pull_event` is. Stock forwards each move-before to the press's hook too, so only a real press resets the state. The touch is claimed once it has moved `SB_CLAIM_PX` (10, AWTK's drag threshold) right and more right than up or down; a drag that goes `SB_CLAIM_PX` up or down first, or left, ends the candidate and stays the page's, so a list scrolls from the edge as before. The claim aborts the window's pressed widgets (`EVT_POINTER_ABORT`, dispatched recursively, as pull-to-search and the A-Z index do), so a row, a slider or Now Playing's `slide_view` lets go, and every later move and the lift return `STOP`. A sideways drag that starts mid-screen is never a candidate: Now Playing's pages, Cover Flow, the letter strip and the sliders keep it.

**The letter strip.** Claimed over a page whose strip is open (`search_strip_open` 2), the swipe shuts the strip instead (`search_strip_close`, as Return there does, [oled-design](oled-design.md#text-entry)): `sb.shut` is set, nothing moves, no bitmap is taken, and the rest of the touch is swallowed; the next swipe takes the page.

**Follow.** Each move puts the layer at the finger's distance from the press (`widget_move`, which moves without laying the children out again; `widget_move_resize` lays a list out, and Home's lists lost their fades and scroll to it). The window manager paints from the topmost normal window up, so the page under a window is not painted until Return has closed the window over it: at the claim `under_snap` paints it once into an offline canvas (`canvas_offline_create`, `widget_paint`, as stock's animator snapshots a window) and keeps it as a bitmap, and `swipe_back_paint`, first in `ringnav_paint_bg` for the swiped window, draws the strip left of it from that bitmap (the window's canvas reaches left of its own box), `parallax_under_x` short of its place and darkened to `parallax_dim` (page_parallax.c's, the push's own drift and dim at the share of the page still in), still and undimmed under Reduce Motion. Each move invalidates the whole window manager, as the strip moves with the page.
