- `done`, `fly`: packets a second the controller says it delivered (Number Of Completed Packets, event 0x13, read off the same raw socket, whose filter takes it with Command Complete), and packets in its buffers now: `acl_tx` less the completions since the socket opened, from the least difference seen (`bt_fly_step`: the count at the opening is not known, and the buffers empty whenever the link keeps up). `fly` over `done` is how long a packet waits in the controller: the radio retransmitting, the headset not acknowledging, shows as `done` falling and `fly` at the buffer count (`bufs`) before `wq` grows. The events come about one for each few packets, so about a hundred reads a second on aptX HD.
- `wtx`, `wrx`: wlan0's kB/s each way (`/sys/class/net/wlan0/statistics`). The RTL8733BS is one module for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth ([hardware](hardware.md)): Wi-Fi traffic takes airtime from Bluetooth through the module's coexistence arbitration.
- `cpu`, `ba`, `own`: all cores' busy percent (`/proc/stat`), bluealsa's and q2guard's own CPU in percent of one core (`/proc/PID/stat`, written `ba=9.0`; as a second holds 100 clock ticks it moves in steps of 1.0, and logs written before 2026-11-18 have the tenths, `ba=90`, which `tools/q2bt.py` reads as the same), so a stall from the Q2 not feeding the encoder (the UI, a scan) is told apart from the radio's, and the monitor's own cost is in the log.
- `er`, `ew`: bluealsa's encoder thread, found by the name bluealsa gives it (`ba-a2dp-sbc`, `ba-a2dp-aptx-hd`, ...: `bt_encoder_thread`), in ms a second: on a CPU and waiting for one, from `/proc/PID/task/TID/schedstat` (`bt_schedstat`; with no schedstat in the kernel, `er` from its ticks and `ew` "-"). An encoder on a CPU for most of the second could not keep up; one waiting for a CPU was kept from one; one mostly asleep was waiting, for PCM when the socket had room (`wq` 0) or for room when it had none. The thread ends at a codec change and another, named for the new codec, starts: that is noted at once (`ENCODER`), and bluealsa is asked for the codec then.
- The codec: `dbus-send ... GetPCMs` in the background at the START, when the encoder thread changes and every minute (`BT_PCMS_MS`), its A2DP source PCM's Codec, Sampling and Delay (`bt_pcms`), noted when it changes, as `bt_battery.c`'s loop already asks every 30 s for the rate.
- `bp`: SBC's bitpool on the frame bluealsa encoded last, the third of its `BT_SBC_POOL` bytes (**SBC bitpool** below), "-" on another codec or a bluealsa without them.
- `pl`, `pr`, `pd`, `pw`, `dk`, `gw` and the `PLAY` note: **the player's side**, for the encoder fed short with the radio idle (**The encoder fed short** below). `pl` is the player's CPU (the process named `hciplayer`, which is q2player at stock's path) in percent of one core, as `ba`; `pr`, `pd` and `pw` its kB/s from `/proc/PID/io`: read (`rchar`: its files, cached or not, and its sockets), read from storage (`read_bytes`) and written (`wchar`: mostly its PCM into bluealsa's FIFO, 172 kB/s for 44.1 kHz 16-bit stereo); `dk` the microSD's (`mmcblk4`) busy ms in the second, its `io_ticks` in `/proc/diskstats`; `gw` 1 while grow.c waits for a song still arriving (its `/tmp/q2player.wait`), 0 not. `PLAY` notes each card file the player holds that it did not at the last line (`/proc/PID/fd`, the logs under `.q2muse` left out), so a song's start and its preload, opened under 6 s from the end of the one before ([player](player.md#what-demo-sends-and-when)), are in the log. Reads only; "-" where the player is not running, or the kernel keeps no task I/O accounting.

**EDR.** On 2026-11-18 the RTL8733BS (UART H5) and a Bowers & Wilkins Px7 S3, both able to use EDR 2 Mbps, were found on multi-slot basic-rate packets: aptX HD's packets of about 778 bytes took 16 slots each, so the link carried at most about 96 a second, 96% of the airtime, with nothing left for a retransmission. The kernel's default packet-type mask (0xcc18) does not forbid EDR, and `hcitool cpt MAC DM1,DM3,DM5,DH1,DH3,DH5` changed nothing; `hcitool cpt EC:66:D1:CF:59:3F DM1,DH1` at 06:15:05Z (Change Connection Packet Type, OGF 1 OCF 0x000F, mask DM1|DH1 = 0x0018 with the EDR "shall not use" bits 0x3306 clear) moved it onto EDR: it then sustained 96 packets a second with 1 or 2 in flight, which DH1-only basic rate cannot carry, and a walk had 6 seconds with a dip in 152, against 19 in 120 before. So the monitor sends that command itself (`bt_edr_step`, the same bytes), once to each ACL handle of the A2DP sink while a stream runs: on the first line once the sink is known, and again on the new handle after a codec change's reconnect. The sink is the device bluealsa streams to, its address read from the path of the `a2dpsrc` PCM in the same `GetPCMs` answer as the codec (`bt_pcms_sink`) and matched in `HCIGETCONNLIST` to a classic ACL link (`bt_acl_handle_of`), so a phone (the Car Remote, or one streaming to the Q2, an `a2dpsnk` PCM) and every LE link are never sent it. On the first stream after boot that is a second or two in, when `GetPCMs` has answered. The raw socket's filter also takes Command Status (0x0F) and Connection Packet Type Changed (0x1D), and `bt_edr_event` notes the outcome in the q2-bt log, `LINK ptype=0x0018 status=0x00 h=2`, or `ptype=-` with the controller's status when it refuses; the first outcome, and any unlike the last, also goes to the unified log (source `bt`, a warning unless it is 0x0018 accepted). A handle is never sent it twice, accepted or refused, so a controller that refuses or a link that does worse is not asked again each second; the record is cleared at a stream's STOP, as a headset that reconnected in a pause may come back on the same handle number, so a refusing controller is asked at most once a stream. There is no setting: it is always on. The saturated line (**Reading it**) says which rate a walk got. ponytail: a codec change's reconnect gets it at the next line, so its first second or so is on whatever the controller chose.

**Packet size.** EDR at 2 Mbps is the best the Q2's link gets: the RTL8733BS reports EDR 2 Mbps with 3- and 5-slot packets, and its configuration clears 3 Mbps (the chip study's `0x8d=fa`, `0x8f=bf`), so the largest ACL packet is a 2-DH5, 679 bytes of payload in 5 slots. Acquire gives bluealsa a write MTU of 1021 (the controller's ACL MTU, `1021:5`), and every encoder packs its packets to that, so each media packet went out as a 2-DH5 and a 2-DH3. Android caps the media MTU at 663 in exactly this case (`MAX_2MBPS_AVDTP_MTU`, `avdt_api.h:100`: 679 less L2CAP's 4 and AVDTP's 12). The build does the same where bluealsa stores the MTU: `transport_acquire_bt_a2dp`'s call to `g_dbus_message_get_unix_fd_list` (0x40abf8), whose delay slot stores the write MTU at transport + 0x48, goes through `mtu_clamp` (`tools/bt_silence.S`, a site in `BT_SILENCE_SITES`), which cuts it to `BT_MTU_MAX`, 675 (679 less L2CAP's 4-byte header; Android's 663 plus RTP's 12), for every codec but LDAC. Shanling's bluealsa sets the socket's send buffer to a fixed 3648 bytes, not from the MTU, so `wq` and the step-down's thresholds see the same queue as before. **The link budget** (each baseband packet plus the headset's 1-slot answer, of 1,600 slots a second): aptX HD at 48 kHz (576 kbps) was 168 frames, 1020 bytes, 71 packets a second, each a 2-DH5 and a 2-DH3, 10 slots: 714 slots, 45% of the air; at 675 it is 110 frames, 672 bytes, 109 a second in one 2-DH5 each, 6 slots: 655, 41%. The 778-byte packets the chip study measured at 96 a second were 960 slots, 60%, against 41%. aptX: 255 frames (1020 bytes, no RTP header) become 168 (672). SBC at bitpool 51 and 48 kHz: 8 frames (933 bytes, 47 a second, 29%) become 5 (588, 75 a second, 28%). The air saved is small; what matters is that a packet is one baseband packet, so one lost on a crowded band costs one 5-slot retransmission, not a pair of which either can fail, and the controller holds more, smaller packets in its 5 ACL buffers. AAC (fdk-aac VBR with a 240 kbps peak, [Bluetooth AAC](#bluetooth-aac): about 551 bytes a frame at 48 kHz on average and at most 638, measured offline; 401 and 586 at the 220 kbps peak and mode 4 before it) fits one packet; a frame over 663 bytes would be split across two packets as RFC 3016 allows, the mark bit on the last, which stock bluealsa already does above its MTU. **LDAC keeps 1021**: libldacBT's `ldacBT_init_handle_encode` refuses an MTU under 679 (0x1a4c) and builds every packet to 661 bytes whatever the MTU (handle + 0x24), which with RTP's 12 and the 1-byte media header is 674, one 2-DH5 already. `test/bluealsa.py` runs stock's and the patched acquire under Unicorn (1021 kept by stock, 675 patched, LDAC 1021, a smaller MTU kept), then each encoder thread on the shipped encoders (SBC built in, aptX and aptX HD libopenaptx; fdk-aac scripted): aptX HD 1020 bytes on stock and 672 (110 frames) patched, aptX 672 (168), SBC at bitpool 29 9 frames (652 bytes, 14 on stock), every packet as full as its MTU allows; AAC frames of 900, 400, 663 and 664 bytes go out as 675+249, 412, 675 and 675+13, marked on each frame's last, the 900 whole; and libldacBT's init on 675, 678, 679 and 1021. Not measured on a Q2 yet. The check is the q2-bt log: `START`'s `mtu=` is the controller's ACL MTU and stays 1021; the bytes a packet are `kbps` x 125 / `acl` (each media packet is one HCI ACL packet either way, as both fit 1021), about 1030 on aptX HD before and about 680 after (both with H5's framing); and on the next walk the stall seconds and `wq` backlog against the 2026-11-18 walks.

**Step-down.** Under Auto a headset without LDAC gets aptX HD where it has it (the Px7), and the first walk heard that break up where SBC did not. So while a stream runs on aptX HD or aptX, `bt_step` (`q2bt_core.c`) watches each line for the codec not fitting what the radio delivers: the controller holding every ACL buffer (`fly` at START's `bufs`) with something waiting in the A2DP socket, and what it delivered (`kbps` by `done` of `acl` packets) under `BT_STEP_SHORT` (90%) of the codec's rate on the link (`bt_codec_kbps`: aptX HD 614 and aptX 412 kbit/s at 48 kHz as the log shows them, SBC by its frame at the encoder's own bitpool, all scaled by the sampling rate). A backlog with the rate whole is not a shortfall: the encoder or a late player can cause one, and on the home walk it was 224 s of 746 with the rate short in 11. `BT_STEP_STALL` (2) short seconds in a row step it straight to SBC, from aptX HD or aptX alike: where the commute's aptX HD fell short aptX did too (**The commute replayed** below), so a stop there costs a second gap and saves nothing, and on SBC the bitpool adapts with no gap (**SBC bitpool** below). It steps back to the codec the stream was on before any step (a headset that chose aptX goes back to aptX) only after `BT_STEP_CLEAN` (60) clean seconds in a row, each not short, the AFH map at `BT_STEP_AFH` (60 of 79 channels) or more and SBC's bitpool at its own, and no sooner than its wait since the last switch: `BT_STEP_UP_MS` (3 minutes), doubled each time a step up is undone within `BT_STEP_UNDONE_MS` (5 minutes), to `BT_STEP_UP_MAX_MS` (24 minutes), so a band that has not cleared is not walked back into every few minutes. A quiet second (under `BT_STEP_QUIET`, 50 kbit/s, handed with no buffer held: between songs, a switch's own gap) counts neither way. The `BT_STEP_SETTLE_MS` (10 s) after each switch count neither way: they are the reconfigure's gap (**The switch and the player** below). LDAC, AAC and a codec not yet known are left alone, and the place it started and the wait are kept through a pause (a stream resumed on SBC still climbs back to aptX HD) and forgotten for another headset (the sink's address from `GetPCMs`). It runs only under Auto (`[SYSSET] BTCODING=2`, Quality's Auto) with `[Q2POD] BTSTEPDOWN` 1, Quality's Adapt to Signal switch (`patch/bt_ui.c`, off until turned on: [Bluetooth page](#bluetooth-page)), which q2guard reads from `/mnt/data/config.ini` itself at each START and with each `GetPCMs` answer (`bt_step_allowed`), so a change takes effect within the minute. The switch turned off while stepped down puts back the codec it started on, once; another Quality choice is left to stock, which selects its own codec, and nothing is put back over it. A switch is bluealsa's `org.bluealsa.PCM1.SelectCodec` on the A2DP source PCM (its object path from `GetPCMs`, `bt_pcms_path`, which passes only letters, digits, `_` and `/`), the codec named as bluealsa names it (`aptX-HD`, `aptX`, `SBC`). `dbus-send` cannot send it, as its second argument is an empty `a{sv}` and `dbus-send` puts no variant in a container, so `q2bt-codec` (`patch/q2bt_codec.c`, against the rootfs's libdbus, as `coda-rc` and `q2-guest`) sends it, run from `sh` in the background as `GetPCMs` is, so q2guard links no libdbus and never waits on bluealsa. Each switch is noted, `STEP aptX-HD -> SBC`, in the q2-bt log and the unified log (source `bt`), and the codec is asked for 3 s on and again when `q2bt-codec` ends; one that fails notes `STEP failed` with bluealsa's error in both (a warning), and no other switch is tried in that stream. The force-EDR command follows the new handle by itself (**EDR** above). **The switch and the player.** bluealsa is bluez-alsa 4.0.0 (`v4.0.0` in its strings), and its `SelectCodec` reconfigures rather than reconnects: `ba_transport_select_codec_a2dp` (`0x40c02c`) asks BlueZ to set the new codec on the headset's endpoint (`bluez_a2dp_set_configuration`, `0x412290`), BlueZ clears the old transport, which ends its encoder thread and closes the PCM's FIFO, and sets up a new one, which bluealsa leaves idle with no encoder (`ba_transport_set_a2dp_state`, `0x40cee8`: a pending transport is acquired only for an A2DP sink; a source's waits for a client to open its PCM). The ALSA plugin, 4.0.0's too, sees its FIFO's write fail and answers the player's next write with `-ENODEV`. The first commute with the step-down (2026-11-18, the Px7, `test/fixtures/q2bt-commute-20261118.log`, `STEP aptX-HD -> aptX` at 14:32:16Z) shows exactly that: `CODEC aptX` two seconds on, the same `h=5`, no `ENCODER` note, `er` "-" (no encoder thread) and nothing sent for five seconds while the radio was well (`rssi` -6 to -14, `wq` 0, `err` 0, `fly` 1), and q2player, which ended a song on any write error, never opened the new PCM; the link dropped six seconds after the switch, with nothing on it. So q2player opens bluealsa's PCM again when a write answers `-ENODEV` on Bluetooth (`bt_reopen`, `player/output.c`: up to 50 looks 100 ms apart while the new PCM is not there yet, the rate and the resampler taken again) and writes on into it, which opens the new transport and starts its encoder; a headset gone for good leaves no PCM and the song fails after the wait, as before (`test/player/run.py`'s `test_alsa_sw_params`, against `alsa_test.c`'s libasound). What the link drop was is open (**The switch and the link** below): the log's other drop, 14:31:35Z, the encoder gone first and the link three seconds later with the signal strong, has the shape of a Quality pick's reconnect, not of a fault. ponytail: the switch's gap on the Q2 and the Px7 is not measured, nor whether the reopen holds the link up: on the next `STEP` a `CODEC` note followed within about three seconds by an `ENCODER` note for the new codec (`ba-a2dp-sbc`) and `kbps` back at the codec's rate is the fix working; a `CODEC` with no `ENCODER` and `er` "-" is the player still not reopening, `adb.exe -s Q2CODA shell 'grep -A8 STEP /mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-bt.0'`. The commute of 2026-11-18 had one, aptX HD to aptX at 14:32:16Z, 13 s after a reconnect: `CODEC aptX` came 2 s on, but no `ENCODER ba-a2dp-aptx` note, nothing was sent for the next 5 s, and then the link dropped (14:32:22Z) and the stream stopped; whether the switch or the walk ended it is not known. ponytail: the plan below asked for a switch at a track change where it can; q2guard does not see tracks, so it switches when the link falls behind.

**The switch and the link.** A codec change can be made two ways, and only one of them is meant to drop the headset. **Stock's pick.** Quality's click (`btquality_item_on_click`, `0x4c54f4`) on a new choice with a headset linked opens stock's confirmation (`msg_btreconnect`), stops the player (`player_save_stop`), clears its link state, calls `switchBtPriority` and then `bluetoothLink(2)`, whose thread (`0x4fc798`) is `btDisconnect`, a wait of up to 10 s for the link to go, and `connectBtDevice`: `switchBtPriority`'s `btctl_set_codec_priority` only orders the endpoints bluetoothd offers when a link is set up (`a2dp_find_eps`), so stock reconnects to make it count. The commute's log has it three times, each with the encoder gone, two silent seconds and a new ACL handle (`LINK h=2` at 14:25:11Z, `h=3` at 14:25:19Z, `h=4` at 14:27:51Z), and a fourth at 14:31:35Z whose reconnect failed twice (`LINK h=0` at 14:31:38Z and 14:31:50Z, a link still being paged) and took 28 s: the stream before it was SBC by choice and the one after stepped down, which only Auto does, so Quality was changed there. **bluealsa's switch.** `SelectCodec` (the **Step-down**'s) asks BlueZ's `MediaEndpoint1.SetConfiguration` on the headset's endpoint for the other codec; bluetoothd's `a2dp_reconfig` closes the AVDTP stream (`avdtp_close`) and, from `close_cfm`, sets the other endpoint up and opens it (`a2dp_reconfigure`; upstream BlueZ waits 500 ms between the two). The ACL link, the AVDTP signalling channel and the pairing are not touched. AVDTP's own Reconfigure changes one endpoint's parameters and cannot move a stream to another codec's endpoint, and bluetoothd never sends it for this, so close and open is the least there is. The new stream then waits in AVDTP's open state until bluealsa acquires the transport, which for a source it does only when a client opens the PCM: the player's reopen (`bt_reopen`, above) is what starts it. **What is built.** A Quality pick that changes the codec on a live link is bluealsa's switch, not stock's reconnect (`bt_quality_linked`, `patch/bt_ui.c`, called in place of the click's read of `bt_linkstatus`, `BT_QUALITY` in `tools/build.py`; [Bluetooth page](#bluetooth-page)), so both ways now leave the ACL link alone. q2guard notes who ends a link: its raw socket also takes Disconnection Complete (0x05) and `bt_down_event` writes `LINK down h=5 reason=0x13 headset` to the q2-bt log and the unified log for the link it follows (`bt.down_h`, read before a changed handle is let go), the reason as the controller gave it: 0x13 to 0x15 the headset's own, 0x16 this host's (bluetoothd, the kernel once no L2CAP channel is left, or stock's reconnect), 0x08 and 0x22 the radio's timeouts. ponytail: the one switch a Q2 has made (14:32:16Z) lost its link 6 s later with the player dead and no reason logged, so what a switch does to the Px7's link with the player reopening is not known. After the next `STEP` or pick, `tools/q2bt.py` or `grep -E 'STEP|CODEC|ENCODER|LINK' q2-bt.0` shows it: the same `h=` on the lines after the switch and no `LINK down` is the link kept; a `LINK down` names the side to look at (`headset`: its own idle or reconfigure handling, and the gap before `ENCODER` is what to shorten; `q2`: bluetoothd or demo, and the unified log's lines at that second say which).

**SBC bitpool.** On 2026-11-18 a commute on SBC (the Px7, `test/fixtures/q2bt-commute-20261118.log`, 14:30:35Z to 14:31:37Z on handle 4) broke up with the signal strong (RSSI -8 to -38) but the 2.4 GHz band crowded (a train, a street): the AFH map fell from 31 of 79 channels to 20 at 14:30:40Z and was 20 to 27 in all but three seconds until 14:31:21Z (74 from 14:31:22Z, the link clean again), and in 26 of 63 seconds the socket held more than 4 kB with all 6 ACL buffers taken; in 18 seconds the controller delivered only 8 to 30 packets a second (42 to 158 kbps) against the 54 a second (266 kbps) the stream needed. That was SBC at bitpool 33, stock's medium quality at 48 kHz, so even SBC did not fit what the radio had left, and nothing lower than SBC exists to step to. So on SBC the bitpool steps down instead. **How bluealsa sets it.** Stock bluealsa (bluez-alsa 4.0.0) sets it once, when the encoder thread starts (0x406268): `sbc_a2dp_get_bitpool` (0x412c30) picks it by `g_sbc_quality` (Shanling's `SetSBCQuality`, through `libbtctl`) from tables at 0x42ce50 (48 kHz joint stereo 29, 33 and 51 for low, medium and high; 44.1 kHz 29, 35 and 53), clamped to the configuration's minimum and maximum, into the thread's own `sbc_t` on its stack. `g_sbc_quality` is read only there, so a change waits for the next transport start. `SelectCodec("SBC", {"Configuration": ...})` with a lower maximum bitpool would work in stock (its "Invalid configuration blob" and "Bitpool out of range" checks are there), but it is an AVDTP reconfigure: the transport is torn down and opened again, the gap the **Step-down** pays at each switch, and on the commute's one switch the sound never came back (the player did not open the new transport's PCM, which it now does: **The switch and the player** in **Step-down**). libsbc itself needs neither: its `sbc_encode` (0x424954) compares the `sbc_t`'s bitpool with its frame's at each call and, when they differ, works out the new frame length and uses it (0x4249c4). **What is built.** The thread's one `sbc_encode` call (0x406580, `jal` to its stub 0x4038e0) goes to `sbc_bp` (`tools/bt_silence.S`, in `BT_SILENCE_SITES`): it keeps the bitpool the thread started with in the `sbc_t`'s padding byte (11, after `endian`, which `sbc_init_a2dp` cleared), sets the bitpool to the lesser of that and the byte at `BT_SBC_POOL` (0x450600, `tools/build.py`, in the payload's read-write segment; 0 or 1 meaning its own), publishes its own and the one used in the two bytes after, and jumps on to `sbc_encode`: about a dozen instructions a frame (375 frames a second at 48 kHz). Never above its own, as bluealsa sized its buffers for that one's frames. `test/bluealsa.py` runs the shipped libsbc under Unicorn through the patched call: frames of 79 bytes at 33, 71 at 29, 51 at 19, back at 33 for 0, still 33 when 45 is asked; stock's stay at 33. q2guard writes the byte through `/proc/PID/mem` of bluealsa (`pool_write`, read back to check), and reads the three each line (`pool_read`, `bp=`). **The gap.** None from the change itself: the next frame is encoded at the new bitpool, its header carries it, and the headset's decoder reads each frame's bitpool from its header, so nothing is renegotiated. Not measured on a Q2 (the emulator has no radio and this was not tried on the user's device); argued from the code above and the Unicorn run. ponytail: packets keep their frame count, as bluealsa sizes its PCM buffer for the starting frame length's count (bluez-alsa 4.0.0's encoder loop), so a lower bitpool makes each packet shorter, not fewer: at 19 a packet of seven frames is about 370 bytes against 566 at 33, a third less on the air; the commute's worst seconds (42 to 80 kbps delivered) would not have fitted even the floor. **The policy** (`bt_sbc_step`, `q2bt_core.c`). The trigger is more than `BT_STEP_WQ` (4 kB) waiting with every ACL buffer held, two seconds in a row; each steps a rung down, 45, 35, 29, 23 and the floor `BT_SBC_FLOOR` (19), never at or above the thread's own (from 33: 29, 23, 19), and `BT_SBC_SETTLE_MS` (2 s) after each change count neither way while the queue drains at the new rate. Up a rung after `BT_SBC_CLEAN` (30) clean seconds and `BT_SBC_UP_MS` (a minute) since the last change, to the thread's own last; a rung up that is undone within its wait doubles the wait (to `BT_SBC_UP_MAX_MS`, 8 minutes), so a link that carries 29 and not 33 settles at 29. Replayed on the commute (`test_the_commute_replayed_steps_sbc_down_to_the_floor`): 33 to 29 at 14:30:40Z, to 23 at 14:30:44Z, to 19 at 14:30:50Z, ten seconds into the trouble. While the bitpool is lowered the codec stays on SBC (`bt_step` counts no clean second): the bitpool climbs back first. It runs under Auto, SBC HQ or SBC (`[SYSSET] BTCODING` 2, 6 or 7: `bt_sbc_allowed`) with the same switch, `[Q2POD] BTSTEPDOWN`, at 1; with the switch off nothing lowers SBC's bitpool, SBC chosen by hand included, as that is quality the user did not ask to give up; on another codec, the switch off or another choice the byte is put back to 0, once, so the next SBC stream starts at its own. Each START starts afresh and puts the byte back to what the policy holds (0), so a q2guard started again or a byte left from another stream is corrected on the first line. Each change is noted, `STEP SBC bitpool 33 -> 29`, in the q2-bt log and the unified log (source `bt`); a write that does not take notes `STEP failed SBC bitpool N: /proc/PID/mem` (a warning) and no other is tried in that stream. ponytail: the bluealsa q2guard reads is the first named `bluealsa` (`find_bluealsa`); with the guest receiver's second daemon running ([Bluetooth receiver](#bluetooth-receiver)) it may be that one, whose byte no SBC encoder reads, and `bp` stays "-".

**Not counted in bluealsa.** Stock bluealsa (bluez-alsa 4.0.0, its `v4.0.0` string, with Shanling's `libbtctl`) writes A2DP packets to a blocking socket and waits (`poll` for `POLLOUT`) when it is full; it never drops one, so the socket's queue is where a stall shows, and the PCM FIFO behind it backs up into hciplayer. A counter of those waits would say what `wq` says, at the cost of more hand-assembled MIPS on the audio path ([Bluetooth AAC](#bluetooth-aac)'s patches), so none was added. The PCM side is not counted either: the FIFO from hciplayer could be measured only by opening it (`/proc/PID/fd/N`), which makes the sampler a reader of the pipe and so changes what hciplayer sees when bluealsa closes its end, and hciplayer's blocking in `write` is not told apart from its other waits in anything `/proc` gives; `er` and `ew` with `wq` say which side waited.

**Cost.** Each line is one ioctl, four HCI commands and their answers, and about a dozen small `/proc` and `/sys` reads, and the player's `stat` and `io`, its open files (about fifteen `readlink`s) and `/proc/diskstats`; the parsing and the line take about 0.7 µs on the build machine (a C loop over `q2bt_core.c`, 2026-11-17), and nothing is read while no stream runs except the one ioctl every 5 s. q2guard runs at `nice -5`, so this is a short burst each second, mostly asleep in `poll`. `own` measures it on the Q2: `tools/q2bt.py`'s summary prints its mean (q2guard's whole process, the heat log's 5 s work and the die temperature's window included) for each codec. With no Bluetooth socket (the emulator) `bt_sleep` tries again a minute later and otherwise sleeps as before. ponytail: `own` has the kernel's 10 ms tick resolution, so a single line reads 0 or 1.0%; only a stream's mean is meaningful. A flush already running when a stream starts or stops takes its note at the next minute's flush, not at once.

**Reading it.** `tools/q2bt.py q2-bt.3 q2-bt.2 q2-bt.1 q2-bt.0` (or `-` from `adb exec-out`) cuts each stream into one segment per codec (at an `ENCODER` note, or at a `CODEC` note naming another codec, which can come up to a minute late: then the seconds since the last gap in sending go to the new codec) and prints each with its median rate, every stall with the 10 s before it and which signals moved over them, and a per-codec summary (seconds streamed, link, encoder and source stall seconds, seconds with the socket's queue backed up, median and lowest RSSI, bluealsa's and q2guard's CPU in percent of one core); `--all` prints every second. A second is behind when the controller was handed under 80% of its segment's median: a **link** stall when something waited in the socket (`wq` > 0, the radio's), an **encoder** stall when nothing did and the encoder thread was on a CPU 800 ms of the second or waited 100 ms for one, a **source** stall when nothing did and the encoder slept (the player's PCM late). Each segment logged with `done` and `fly` also gets a **saturated** line: in the seconds the controller held all its ACL buffers (`fly` at `bufs`) the radio was the limit, so the median `done` then is the link's capacity, set against the most basic rate (DH5, DH3, DH1, each with the headset's return slot, in 1,600 slots a second) and EDR 2 Mbps (2-DH5, 2-DH3, 2-DH1) carry for packets of the segment's size (`capacity`, `slots`): at most 10% over basic rate's ceiling says basic rate, past halfway to EDR's says EDR, between them undecided, and under 5 such seconds too few. For aptX HD's packets of about 790 bytes that is 100 a second on basic rate (96 needed: 96% of the airtime) and 160 on EDR (60%); the Q2 has no 3 Mbps. HCI says nothing of the packet type a link uses (the two radios agree it between them), and the host does not forbid EDR (`hciconfig ptype` lists the EDR types only when they may not be used), so this is how a walk tells which one the Q2 and the headset settled on. The reconnect at a codec change (the idle gap and up to 3 slow seconds either side) is a switch, and nothing sent with nothing waiting is idle (a pause), as is a slow second beside one: neither is a stall.

**Capturing an A/B walk** (on a Q2 with this build, from WSL with Windows' `adb.exe -s Q2CODA`, [adb](adb.md)):

1. Check the counters before walking, music playing to the headset: `adb.exe -s Q2CODA shell 'hciconfig hci0 | grep bytes; sleep 2; hciconfig hci0 | grep bytes; cat /proc/net/l2cap; hcitool con'` shows TX bytes growing, an L2CAP table with a `Wmem` column and the ACL link; `adb.exe -s Q2CODA shell 'hcitool rssi MAC; hcitool lq MAC; hcitool afh MAC'` answers for the headset's MAC. A minute into playing, `adb.exe -s Q2CODA shell 'tail -n 3 /mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-bt.0'` shows lines after a START and a CODEC; a field that reads "-" on every line is a signal this Q2 does not give, worth knowing before walking.
2. Note the Q2's clock (`adb.exe -s Q2CODA shell date -u`); the log is in UTC.
3. Walk the route with the first choice (Quality: Auto, which on the Px7 is aptX HD), Q2 in the pocket for one leg and in hand for another, noting the UTC time of each leg and each break-up heard. Stop the music at the end: the STOP is written to the card within seconds.
4. Change Quality to SBC (an `ENCODER` note marks the change within a second), play, and walk the same route the same way.
5. Pull and read: `adb.exe -s Q2CODA exec-out 'cd /mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs; cat q2-bt.3 q2-bt.2 q2-bt.1 q2-bt.0 2>/dev/null' > walk.log; python3 tools/q2bt.py walk.log`. Match the stalls to the break-ups heard; the heat log (`tools/q2heat.py`) has the busiest processes for the same minutes.

What the walk should settle before Phase 2: whether the heard break-ups are link stalls (and so `wq` is the trigger), which of RSSI, transmit power, AFH and Wi-Fi moved in the seconds before them, how far ahead, and what the monitor cost (`own`).

**The first walk** (2026-11-18, 04:36 to 04:50 UTC, the Px7, `tools/q2bt.py`): SBC (260 kbps) 234 s with no stall and nothing ever queued; aptX HD (614 kbps on the link) 96 s with 10 link-stall seconds and the socket's queue backed up (5.7 to 9.2 kB) in 55 of them, the rate swinging 323 to 723 kbps as the radio fell behind and caught up; no encoder or source stall in either. bluealsa used 1.4% of a core on SBC and 8.9% on aptX HD, the same 8.8 to 9.7% the heat log's `top` shows with the headset beside the Q2, so a backed-up link does not make it spin: it waits in `poll`. The user heard aptX HD break up with distance and SBC not at all. The RSSI and the other HCI readings were lost after the first codec switch (the stale handle above), so how far the signal had fallen is for the next walk.

**The aptX encoder.** bluealsa links libopenaptx 0.2.1 (`/usr/lib/libopenaptx.so.0.2.1`, 21 KB, integer only; SBC is built into bluealsa, AAC is fdk-aac 2.0.2, LDAC Sony's). Run under Unicorn on the shipped library (2026-11-18), it takes 105 M instructions per second of 48 kHz stereo for aptX and 109 M for aptX HD, which at 1.2 GHz is the 9% of a core measured on the Q2. aptX and aptX HD cost the same; aptX HD's extra two bits a sample cost the air 576 kbps against 384, not the CPU. A quarter of the time is the adaptive predictor's 24-tap coefficient update, where the shipped build (GCC, MIPS32r2, using `madd`) moves its 64-bit accumulator in and out of HI/LO on every tap. The same source built with clang 18 for MIPS32r2 encodes bit-identically and takes more (117 M at -O2, 123 M at -O3 with or without unrolling), so no faster build is to be had from flags; a source change keeping the accumulator in HI/LO might save about a tenth, or a SIMD path if the X2000 has one (its `/proc/cpuinfo` ASEs, unread), and either is two to three percent of one core, which nothing in the walk needed. ponytail: measured in instructions, not cycles: HI/LO latency on XBurst II would make the shipped loop slower than its count says, by an amount only a Q2 can show.

**Plan: Phase 2, adapting the rate (built for aptX and SBC: the Step-down and SBC bitpool above).** Lower the bit rate when the link is congested or the headset distant, for every headset, not tuned to one. What each codec allows on this stack:

- **SBC**: the bitpool, carried in every frame's header, can change frame to frame within the range the headset accepted (2 to its maximum, usually 53: at 48 kHz joint stereo, 8 subbands and 16 blocks that is about 357 kbps, 35 about 249, 23 about 177), with no renegotiation and no gap. The finest and safest lever; built as **SBC bitpool** above, through a patch at bluealsa's one `sbc_encode` call, as stock has no runtime setter.
- **AAC**: the encoder's bitrate (fdk-aac `AACENC_BITRATE`) can change between frames, 320 to 256, 192, 128 kbps, seamless to the headset; the same bluealsa patch question.
- **LDAC**: Auto already does it (Sony's ABR on queue depth, 990, 660, 492, 396, 330 kbps: [Bluetooth LDAC quality](#bluetooth-ldac-quality)); the fixed Best and Standard could be moved to Auto's controller or stepped with `SetLDACQuality`.
- **aptX and aptX HD**: fixed rates (352 or 384, 529 or 576 kbps) with no lower setting; the only reduction is another codec, which the **Step-down** above does under Auto (aptX HD or aptX straight to SBC, through bluealsa's `SelectCodec`).

A policy would read the Phase 1 signals each second in q2guard, or in bluealsa itself where the queue is known exactly: congestion as the share of the last few seconds with `wq` above zero and `kbps` short of the codec's rate, distance as RSSI and transmit power trending toward their limits, interference as `afh` falling with `wtx`/`wrx` busy. It steps down fast (two link-stall seconds in ten) and up slowly (a minute clean), one step at a time, so it does not oscillate at a threshold; within a codec (SBC bitpool, AAC bitrate, LDAC's ABR) every step is seamless, while a codec switch costs a gap and is kept for sustained trouble, at most once in several minutes, preferably at a track change. The rate it may climb back to is the user's choice; a fixed choice (aptX HD) is kept unless the user picks an adaptive one, and Auto's caption ([Bluetooth page](#bluetooth-page)) already says when Auto is not LDAC. The first walk points the first step at the link, not the CPU: with aptX HD queued in over half its seconds while bluealsa used 9% of a core, Auto should not settle on aptX HD while the link's margin is thin (`wq` backing up), and should step down when it does; the replay below found aptX not worth a stop, so the **Step-down** above goes straight to SBC.

**The commute replayed (2026-11-18), and what it says of the ladder.** Each candidate policy was run over the two stretches logged after the **EDR** change in which the radio fell behind: the commute's tail (14:25:11Z to 14:31:35Z, 379 s, on aptX and then SBC by the user's picks) and a walk at home (06:15:06Z to 06:28:24Z, 746 s, on aptX HD). A second's capacity is what the controller delivered while it held every ACL buffer (`fly` at `bufs`), and otherwise at least the logged codec's rate; a second is starved for a codec when that is under 90% of its rate; a switch is taken as 2 s of silence, which no Q2 has measured. Where the log was on a lower codec with room to spare, what a higher one would have got is not in it, so the commute's figures are a pair: the higher codec never fitting there, and always. Bad seconds are starved plus silent ones.

| Policy | Commute tail: switches, bad s | Home walk: switches, bad s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stay on aptX HD | 0, 91 to 379 | 0, 11 |
| SBC throughout, the bitpool adapting | 0, 23 | 0, 0 |
| The ladder as built: aptX HD, aptX, SBC on any backlog; up after 60 clean s and 3 min | 4, 35 to 50 | 6, 13 |
| aptX HD to aptX and no further | 1 to 3, 77 to 233 | 6, 13 |
| One step, aptX HD to SBC, on any backlog; up after 60 clean s and 3 min | 3, 31 to 43 | 6, 13 |
| One step, on two starved seconds; up as above | 3, 31 to 43 | 2, 11 |
| The same, and up only with `afh` at 60 or more through the clean minute, the wait doubling when a step up is undone | 1, 27 | 2, 11 |
| One step, and no step up in the stream | 1, 27 | 1, 4 |

What it shows: aptX is not worth a stop (where the commute's radio fell behind it carried 321 to 473 kbps on aptX and a median 234 on SBC, under aptX's 412, so the stop costs a second gap and saves nothing; at home it was never needed below aptX HD's own ceiling); the trigger as built fires on a backlog with the rate still whole (224 of the home walk's 746 s, of which 11 were starved), so it spends 12 s of gaps to save 10; and a step up after a clean minute walks back into a band that has not cleared (the commute's `afh` was 20 to 27 of 79 channels in its bad minute and 74 once clean). So the ladder to build is one step, aptX HD or aptX straight to SBC, when two seconds in a row deliver under 90% of the codec's rate with every buffer held; SBC's bitpool does the rest with no gap (**SBC bitpool**); and back up only with the bitpool at its own, a clean minute, 3 minutes since the switch and `afh` at 60 or more throughout, the wait doubling (to 24 minutes) each time a step up is undone within 5. Built so (**Step-down** above). The replay is kept: `test_the_commute_replayed_through_the_step_down` (`test/unit/test_q2bt.py`) feeds the two stretches (`test/fixtures/q2bt-replay-20261118.log.gz` and the commute's log) through `bt_sbc_step` and `bt_step` themselves, each second as the line the codec then in force would have logged, and gets the last row but one, 1 switch and 27 bad seconds and 2 and 11, at both bounds; without the `afh` condition the same code makes 3 switches and 31 to 40 bad seconds on the commute. 19 minutes of one headset on one day, and the pairs above are its honest width.

**A bigger host buffer: not built.** Asked of the 2026-11-18 commute logs (`q2-bt.1` and `.0`, replayed per second): the seconds the stream fell short with the radio as the limit (`wq` above 0, delivered under 90% of the codec's rate) came in runs of a median 1 s on aptX HD (69 runs, 0.30 s of audio short each, 1.15 s at the 90th percentile, the longest 15 s and 4.3 s short), 1.5 s on aptX (6) and 2.5 s on SBC (10, a median 1.01 s short, the longest 5.4 s). In every one of those seconds the Q2 already held audio the controller could not take (`wq` and every ACL buffer full), so the shortfall is air time, not data: more audio queued on the Q2 reaches the headset no sooner, and a gap is bridged only by the buffer at the playing end, the headset's own (bluealsa reports the Px7's Delay, 236 ms on aptX HD), which the source cannot enlarge. What a deeper queue would add is its own length in latency, drained at the link's headroom: saturated, the controller delivered a median 96 aptX HD packets a second against the 100 basic rate carries, about 4%, so a median run's 0.3 s takes some 7 s to win back and the longest 107 s. The levers left are fewer bits on the air (**Step-down**, **SBC bitpool**) and more air time (**EDR**; the scan hold, [Smart Wi-Fi](#scan-hold)). The commute's **source** stalls, the encoder fed short with the link idle, are a different question: **The encoder fed short** below.

**The encoder fed short.** In the 2026-11-18 commute (`q2-bt.1`, the Px7 on aptX HD at 44.1 kHz, 14:02:09Z to 14:25:11Z, a median 567 kbps; server songs, played from their Stream Cache copies on the card) four stretches went under 80% of the median with nothing waiting in the socket (`wq` 0) and every packet handed over delivered (`done` equal to `acl`): 14:03:46Z (1 s, 438 kbps), 14:04:09Z to 14:04:14Z (6 s, 322 to 385), 14:17:18Z (1 s, 450) and 14:24:39Z to 14:24:48Z (10 s, 333 to 534), the 6 s and the 10 s each followed by a burst over the rate (595 to 655, and 726 and 655 kbps), the encoder winding back up. `tools/q2bt.py` calls them source stalls; no 48 kHz segment of the walks had one (06:27:49Z was a stream's restart). The radio was not the limit: the AFH map held 61 to 68 channels, the RSSI -4 to -34. Nor the CPU: in the 10 s one all cores were 3 to 8% busy, bluealsa 4 to 6%, the die 34.6 to 34.7 C with no frequency cap in the heat log; the encoder slept, its `er` falling with the rate (50 ms a second against 80). Nor the network: Wi-Fi carried nothing in any of those seconds (`wrx` 0; the downloads ran 14:02:10Z to 14:03:26Z and at 14:07:20Z, 14:11:51Z, 14:17:36Z and 14:20:55Z), so no song was being read as it arrived. 14:04:09Z came 8 s and 14:17:18Z a second after a burst of `q2-subsonic.bin` work with Wi-Fi idle (all cores at 63 to 66%, it at 117% of a core at 14:03:59Z; 14:03:53Z to 14:04:01Z and 14:17:10Z to 14:17:17Z); the 10 s one followed nothing of the kind. So the player wrote short, and the logs hold nothing of the player's side to say why: the card, the decoder, a song's end (the preload, the resampler's change) or grow.c's wait. The line's player fields (**The line** above) are for that: on the next such stretch, `pw` falling with the rate says the player wrote short; with `dk` near 1000 and `pd` up the card was busy; with `pl` high the player was on the CPU; `gw` 1 is grow.c waiting; a `PLAY` note within the stretch or 6 s after it puts it at a song's end. `tools/q2bt.py walk.log` prints them in the 10 s before each source stall, `--all` every second. Nothing is changed until one of those says which.

## Bluetooth devices

The [link monitor](#bluetooth-link-monitor) sees a device only while a stream runs, and names none. On 2026-11-19 that left four reports unanswerable: a car that thought it was connected while the Q2 did not, until it was removed and paired again; a Forget that took two taps; the Pixel Buds (04:00:6E:D3:96:6D), connected at 14:21:33Z, refused two AVDTP starts (bluealsa's "Couldn't acquire transport: Input/output error") and dropped about 40 s later with nothing logged, as no stream ran; and connects that took minutes with no sign of the attempts or why they failed.

**Where.** `q2guard`'s `bt_sleep` (`patch/q2bt.c`, `mgmt_ok` and `mgmt_drain`) opens a socket on the kernel's Bluetooth management interface, the control channel bluetoothd itself drives (`AF_BLUETOOTH`, `BTPROTO_HCI`, bound to `HCI_DEV_NONE` 0xffff on `HCI_CHANNEL_CONTROL` 3), non-blocking, and waits on it in place of its plain sleep: an event wakes it, is read and logged at once, and the wait goes on to the tick it was going to make, so a line has its event's time and the 5 s tick and the stream's 1 s samples keep theirs. It sends no command. In Linux 5.10 (the Q2 runs 5.10.21) each management event is copied to every bound control-channel socket a root process opened (`net/bluetooth/mgmt.c` `mgmt_event`, `net/bluetooth/hci_sock.c` `__hci_send_to_channel`, the `HCI_SOCK_TRUSTED` flag set at bind for `CAP_NET_ADMIN`); only the socket whose own command caused an event may be skipped, so this one sees what bluetoothd sees, and a socket that sends nothing only queues copies, which changes nothing for bluetoothd or the controller. Each read is one event whole (a datagram); 32 at most a wake, the rest at the next. Where the socket does not open (the emulator), `devices: the management channel does not open` is logged once and it is tried again each minute.

**The lines**, each a unified-log line of source `bt` (`bt_mgmt_parse`, `bt_mgmt_line` in `patch/q2bt_core.c`, layouts from 5.10's `include/net/bluetooth/mgmt.h`), the address and, when known, the name in quotes; ` LE` after them for an LE address:

- `connected 04:00:6E:D3:96:6D "Grayson's Pixel Buds" by=device` (`I`): Device Connected (0x000B). `by=` is who began the link: 5.10's event carries no such flag (`mgmt_device_connected` passes flags 0 at each call in `hci_event.c`), so the drain reads the kernel's connection list (`HCIGETCONNLIST`) for the address and its `out` byte, `hci_conn->out`, which `hci_acl_create_connection` sets for a Create Connection this host sent: `by=q2`, else `by=device` (`bt_acl_out`); left out when the link is no longer listed.
- `disconnected ADDRESS "NAME" reason=N WORDS` (Device Disconnected, 0x000C): 0 `unspecified`, 1 `timeout or link loss`, 2 `this Q2 ended it`, 3 `the device ended it`, 4 `authentication failed`, 5 `suspend`. `W` for all but 2, the Q2's own disconnect, `I`. Streaming or not.
- `connect failed ADDRESS "NAME" status=0x04 no answer (page timeout)` (`W`, Connect Failed, 0x000D) and `auth failed ADDRESS "NAME" status=0x05 authentication failed` (`W`, Authentication Failed, 0x0011). The status is the kernel's management status, into which `mgmt_status()` folds the controller's HCI code: 0x04 is a page timeout (or an LE connection that could not be made), 0x05 a failed authentication or a missing key, 0x08 a connection or LMP timeout, 0x0b rejected, 0x0a busy; the HCI code itself is not in the event.
- `paired ADDRESS "NAME"` (`I`, New Link Key, 0x0009): a pairing finished. The key is never read.
- `forgotten ADDRESS "NAME"` (`I`, Device Unpaired, 0x0016): a Forget completed, the time the device was really gone.
- `discovery started BR/EDR+LE` and `discovery stopped BR/EDR+LE` (`I`, Discovering, 0x0013: its type, `hdev->discovery.type`, a mask of address types, 1 `BR/EDR`, 6 `LE`, 7 both): each search, so the pairing page's 10 s cycles show.
- `found 04:00:6E:D3:96:6D "Grayson's Pixel Buds" rssi=-52 BR/EDR` (`I`, Device Found, 0x0012: the address, the name when its EIR has one, else one seen before, the signal, and `BR/EDR` or `LE`): only each address's first answer in a discovery, as the event comes for every inquiry or advertising result, several a second for one device; 32 addresses a discovery at most (`bt_found_first`, `BT_FOUND_MAX`), then `found: more devices this discovery, not logged` once. With the trace's `page shows found` ([Bluetooth connection trace](#bluetooth-connection-trace)) it sets when the radio heard a device against when the pairing page showed it.

**The name** is the connected event's EIR (the complete name, else the shortened one, as the kernel read it from the device), else the last name seen for that address (eight kept, `bt_names_put`), else BlueZ's store, `/mnt/data/bluetooth/ADAPTER/ADDRESS/info`'s `Name=`, its first KB only (`bt_info_name`). The names seen are what let `forgotten` name a device whose info file BlueZ has already removed. Every event after a device's first finds its name there and puts it back into the same slot, so `bt_names_put` copies a byte at a time: glibc 2.28's `snprintf` empties its buffer before it reads `%s`, and on 2026-11-19 that blanked the name of the second line for an address (`connect failed 60:E6:F0:A1:1F:09` at 20:37:35Z, `"BMW 83828"` at 20:35:46Z). `test/unit/test_q2bt_devices.py` builds `q2bt_core.c` with that `snprintf` (`test/unit/glibc228_snprintf.h`), as the host's newer glibc does not do it.

A `W` line flushes the unified log to the card within `WARN_GAP_MS` (`bt_dev_warned`), as a feed's `E` or `W` does. Tested by `test/unit/test_q2bt_devices.py`, on event bytes built field by field as 5.10's `mgmt.c` sends them.

**Cost.** Nothing while no device event comes: the wait is a `poll` instead of a `usleep`. Discovery (the Bluetooth page searching) sends a Device Found for each answer, each a wake and a read; all but each address's first in a discovery are passed over. A connect reads the connection list once (`by=`).

## Bluetooth connection trace

The kernel's lines ([Bluetooth devices](#bluetooth-devices)) say what the radio did; what the Q2's own Bluetooth page and stock's link thread believed is in demo. On 2026-11-19 (V1JBi) the two disagreed: the kernel connected the Pixel Buds at 20:40:36Z (`paired` at 20:40:37Z), an AAC stream ran from 20:40:42Z (`START ... dev=04:00:6E:D3:96:6D`, about 150 kbps), `bluetoothctl` said Connected and `hcitool con` listed the link, yet the page's row said Connecting for minutes; and at boot and after each stack relaunch demo paged the car (`BTLINKMAC`) and failed with a page timeout, never the Buds.

**The trace** (`patch/bt_trace.c`, `bt_trace_poll`, every 500 ms from the UI loop, `system.c` `power_poll`) logs each change, as a `bt` line from demo (`ulog`), of what the page and the link thread go by. The first poll after demo starts logs all of them once:

- `switch on` / `switch off`: `g_bluetoothflag`.
- `stack status N`: `bt_initstatus`, `W` when negative (-102 is stock's "Bluetooth abnormal").
- `saved device 60:E6:F0:A1:1F:09 "BMW 83828"`: `BTLINKMAC` (`0xa4c0d8`), the device auto-link pages.
- `scan started` / `scan ended`: `bt_searchtime` going from 0 or to 0.
- `link setup to a headset` / `from a phone` / `none`: `bt_a2dp_direction`, `checkBluetoothStatus` setting a link up.
- `link list N, last ADDRESS "NAME" status=5 connecting`: the link list's size and its last item, the one stock's rows and status slot judge (status 1 `queued`, before the thread takes it; 5 `connecting`; 3 `connected`; 4 `failed`, as headset.c and the page's cancel mark it; `?` for another).
- `link thread running (1)`, `ended (2)`, `checking (3)`, `idle (0)`: `bt_connectstatus`.
- `connect starts to ADDRESS "NAME" why=auto|usb|tap|other`: each time the link thread starts (`bt_connectstatus` to 1), its target (the last item) and why: `auto` when `headset_bt_autolink` let auto-link go ahead (at boot and at each Bluetooth on, the stack's relaunch included), `usb` when it did so for a cable in ([Bluetooth on USB power](#bluetooth-on-usb-power)), `tap` when the page's row or a device page's Connect went through `bt_stock_click`, each for that address within the last 3 s; `other` for one stock started with neither.
- `auto-connect (auto) picks 60:E6:F0:A1:1F:09 "BMW 83828": the saved device, paired, nothing connected`, `auto-connect (auto) skips ADDRESS: 04:00:6E:D3:96:6D "Grayson's Pixel Buds" is connected` and `auto-connect (usb) skips ADDRESS: the saved device, not paired` (`W`): each decision of `headset_bt_autolink` ([Bluetooth boot reconnect](#bluetooth-boot-reconnect)), through `bt_trace_autolink`: the device stock's auto-link would page (its target, the saved device `BTLINKMAC` or not), and what stopped it, the link list's connected item, a target `checkPairDev` does not know, or (`skips ADDRESS: the car on the cable, whose audio is Car Audio's`) the car Car Audio has on the USB cable, matched by the name it gave over iAP2 (`usb_car.c` `usb_car_name`) against the device's in the Bluetooth list: on 2026-11-21 a Bluetooth relaunch auto-connected A2DP to the very car the Q2 was playing to over USB (`test/fw/test_bt_ui.py` `test_bluetooth_leaves_alone_the_car_car_audio_plays_to`). A car that connects by itself is not refused. Stock's own `====auto bt[ADDRESS]==` line names only the target. The boot of 2026-11-19 paged the car each time and never the Buds; these lines say why the next time.
- `connect to ADDRESS "NAME" ended: connected after 1000 ms`, `ended: failed after N ms` (`W`), `ended: no link, the link list says connecting` or `its item is gone` (`W`, the thread stopped without a link), `ended: another connect started` (`W`), or `abandoned: Bluetooth switched off` / `abandoned: the stack restarted` (`W`, the switch off or `bt_initstatus` leaving 0, as a [relaunch](#bluetooth-controller-watchdog) does): one line after each `connect starts`, so no connect is left open in the log (`pend_end`). A failure's reason is the kernel's, in q2guard's own `connect failed ... status=0x04 no answer (page timeout)` beside it. Before 1128 the 2026-11-22 drive's `connect starts ... why=usb` at 06:07:06Z had no line after it: the storm's relaunch ended it.
- `forget ADDRESS: unpaired`, `disconnected and unpaired`, `Cancel chosen`, or (`W`) `not in the device list now, nothing done` and `stock's unpair refused it (N), nothing done`: each answer of a device page's Forget card (`bt_detail.c` `forget`), as the last two leave the page open with no toast. On 2026-11-19 22:07:58Z the Buds' link list emptied and they disconnected, and only at 22:08:07Z were they forgotten (`saved device -` after it, the trace seeing `forget_link` clear `BTLINKMAC`): whether the first action was the page's Disconnect or a Forget that did nothing, nothing then said.
- `link list says connecting for ADDRESS "NAME", the kernel holds its link: shown Connected` (`W`): the case of 2026-11-19, once each time it begins (below).
- `page opened` and `page shows found ADDRESS "NAME"`: the Bluetooth page opening, and each found device on its list (Other Devices), once an open, so the gap between the kernel's `found` and the row is in the log.

**BlueZ's own reconnects.** The Q2's `/etc/bluetooth/main.conf` (stock's, kept by the build but for `Name`, discoverability and `Experimental`) sets `[Policy]` `ReconnectAttempts=4` and `ReconnectIntervals=20,20,20,20`, with `ReconnectUUIDs` left at the policy plugin's default (HSP and HFP audio gateway, A2DP source and sink). BlueZ 5.66's `plugins/policy.c` starts them only from its disconnect callback, and only for a disconnect of reason 1 (timeout, the link lost) or 5 (suspend), for a device that had one of those services connected: then 4 attempts 20 s apart, `btd_device_connect_services` each. So a `disconnected ... reason=1 timeout or link loss` line opens a window of up to 80 s in which BlueZ connects on its own, beside demo's link thread, which has its own target (`BTLINKMAC`) and 15 s wait. Which of the two began a link is the kernel line's `by=` together with the trace's `connect starts`: a `connected ... by=q2` with no `connect starts` before it is BlueZ's.

## Bluetooth controller watchdog

On 2026-11-19 the RTL8733BS's UART link wedged three times in one night (00:02Z, 01:26Z, 03:14Z) and once more at 04:12Z while a headset was being picked on the [Bluetooth page](#bluetooth-page) during a scan. Realtek's out-of-tree H5 driver (its strings, "Error in H5 hdr checksum" and "Peer acked invalid packet", are not mainline's) logs each bad frame and carries on; the kernel (5.10, as stock) logs an HCI command left unanswered, `hci0: command 0x0402 tx timeout`, and sends the next. From then on every command timed out and Bluetooth stayed dead until the stack was relaunched: the 03:14Z storm was still running 47 minutes later at about 756 lines a minute, and the two before it ended only when demo happened to relaunch the stack. At 04:12Z one bad header was followed within 2 s by Inquiry Cancel (0x0402) going unanswered, a storm of about 64 lines a second that stopped by itself after 6 s, and every command after it (0x0c56, 0x0c20, Create Connection 0x0405) still unanswered, so a storm's end is not a recovery. The serial port counted `fe:2 pe:12 brk:5` and no overruns with RTS/CTS on: corruption on the wire. Android's rule is the one followed here: an HCI command unanswered for 2 s means a controlled restart of the stack (`system/gd/hci/hci_layer.cc`), and Realtek's own Android HAL restarts on a missed heartbeat (`RtkBtAutoRestart`).

**Signs.** `q2guard` reads `/dev/kmsg` each 5 s tick for the [unified log](#unified-log) and hands every record to `bt_kmsg` (`patch/q2bt.c`), which `bt_wedge_line` (`patch/q2bt_core.c`) sorts: the driver's three error lines ("Peer acked invalid packet", "Error in H5 hdr checksum", "Short H5 packet") and the kernel's `command 0x.... tx timeout`. A timeout makes the controller suspect at once; H5 lines do only as a storm, `BT_H5_STORM` (20) of them within `BT_H5_WINDOW_MS` (10 s) by the kernel's own times, so a single bad frame (16:09:35Z the day before: one checksum error, nothing after it, Bluetooth fine) is not a sign. A suspicion with no new sign for `BT_SUSPECT_MS` (60 s) and no probe failed is dropped.

**The probe.** While suspect, each tick (no closer than `BT_PROBE_GAP_MS`, 5 s) sends Read Local Version Information (0x1001, no side effects) on a raw HCI socket of its own and waits `BT_PROBE_MS` (2.5 s; the kernel gives up at 2 s) for its Command Complete (`bt_probe_answer`). hci0 missing or down (Bluetooth off, the stack starting) gives no verdict. An answer clears the suspicion, notes `BT PROBE answered` and holds the next probe off for `BT_PROBE_CALM_MS` (60 s), so a storm the controller answers through is left alone. `BT_PROBE_FAILS` (2) unanswered in a row, 5 s apart, confirm a wedge: replayed through the 04:12Z log (`test/fixtures/h5-wedge-20261119.dmesg`) the relaunch is asked for about 10 s after the first timeout. A wedged controller's probe adds a `tx timeout` line of its own, which keeps the suspicion fresh. The probe blocks q2guard's loop for at most 2.5 s, and only while suspect; no stream runs on a wedged controller.

**The relaunch.** q2guard does not start the daemons itself: demo holds the link list, the output and the pairing agent that stock registers at each start (`btctl_set_default_agent`), and a stack restarted under it would leave them stale. It asks demo through the [overheat guardian](#overheat-guardian)'s state file, `bt=N` (the relaunches asked for, numbered on from demo's last answer when q2guard starts again), and demo's `heatguard_poll` (`hg_bt`, `patch/heatguard.c`) does what stock's Bluetooth switch does: `switchBluetooth(1, 0)` (the output off Bluetooth, `btStopSearch`, `btDisconnectAll`, `clearBluetoothStatus`, and `closeBluetooth`: `rm /var/run/bluealsa -rf`, `rm /var/run/dbus/pid`, `killall -9` of `bluetoothd`, `bluealsa` and `rtk_hciattach`, `/tmp/rtk_init_success` removed and the radio's GPIO PD20 low), then `HG_BT_OFF_MS` (1 s) later `switchBluetooth(0, 0)`, whose `bluetoothInit` thread runs `openBluetooth` (PD20 high, `rtk_hciattach -n -s 115200 ttyS0 rtk_h5 &`, `bluetoothd &`, `hciconfig hci0 reset`, `bluealsa2 &`, then discoverable, pairable, the agent and the callbacks) and stock's priority, after which `checkBluetoothStatus` reconnects `BTLINKMAC` as at any Bluetooth on ([boot reconnect](#bluetooth-boot-reconnect)). It answers `bt N done` in `/tmp/q2guard.ack` (`bt N off` when Bluetooth was switched off: nothing to relaunch). It does nothing while the stack is starting or failed, a link thread is connecting or pairing, or a link is being set up. A scan does not hold it off: on 2026-11-19 (V1JAi) a storm from 20:36:00Z was confirmed and the relaunch asked at 20:36:26Z, but demo waited for the Bluetooth page's scan until 20:37:26Z, and the scan's own commands had timed out in the kernel (`command 0x0401 tx timeout`, `0x2041 tx timeout`), as a wedged controller answers none, so it could not end by itself; stock's switch off stops a scan first (`btStopSearch`). q2guard asks nothing while a codec switch (`q2bt-codec`, the Quality pick's or the step-down's) runs; an ask demo has not answered in `BT_RESET_WAIT_MS` (60 s) is noted as unanswered and counted as made. An ask already in the file when demo starts is taken as old.

**Backoff.** Lines are not counted for `BT_RESET_SETTLE_MS` (60 s) after demo's answer, while the stack starts. A relaunch within `BT_RESET_CURED_MS` (10 minutes) of the last is in a row and waits `BT_RESET_GAP_MS` (2 minutes), doubled for each before it in the row (said once, `BT RESET waits`); after `BT_RESET_MAX` (3) in a row it gives up (`BT RESET gave up`, an error) and probes once a minute, so a stack someone else brings back (Bluetooth switched off and on) is seen answering and the count starts afresh.

**The log.** Each event goes to the q2-bt log and the unified log (source `bt`): `BT RESET reason=storm after 63s` (`timeout`, or `storm+timeout`, by the signs seen; the time is from the first sign, to q2guard's 5 s tick), `BT RESET demo relaunched the stack`, `BT RESET not made: Bluetooth is off`, `BT RESET unanswered: demo busy or not running`, `BT RESET waits: ...`, `BT RESET gave up: ...` and `BT PROBE answered: the controller is alive`. `test/unit/test_q2bt_wedge.py` replays the 04:12Z and 03:56Z kernel logs and checks the isolated error, the storm's threshold, a storm answered through, no verdict, the backoff and give-up, a codec switch and demo not answering; `test/fw/test_heatguard.py` checks demo's side. ponytail: the relaunch only shortens the outage; why the link corrupts is open. The UART's 3 Mbaud (`rtl8733bs_config`'s baud word `0x04928001`; Realtek's reference config for the chip has 1.5 Mbaud) is not it by itself: with the reference's 1.5 Mbaud config bound over stock's on 2026-11-18 the link wedged again within five minutes, and six hours of streaming that night, three at each speed, moved 1.2 GB with no error counted. To tell a dropped byte from a misread one, `uart_note` (`patch/q2bt.c`) logs the H5 port's counters since boot, from serial_core's `/proc/tty/driver/INGENIC serial` (`bt_uart_counts`; port 0, the `ttyS0` stock's `rtk_hciattach` opens), at each START (`UART start tx=... rx=... fe=0 pe=0 brk=0 oe=0 bo=0`, q2-bt log), at an H5 error line that turns the driver's debug lines on (`UART sign ...`, q2-bt log, below) and after each relaunch's line (`UART reset ...`, both logs), each with the Wi-Fi driver's power-save counts when its `ps_info` is there (`ips=990/989`, entered/left, `bt_wifi_ips`): `oe` (the 64-byte receive FIFO overrun) or `bo` (the tty's buffer full) growing across a storm says bytes were lost at the port, `fe` (framing) a baud the two ends disagree on, and all of them still with checksum errors says the damage is elsewhere, or that the Ingenic driver does not count it. The first 2026-11-20 reading was with Bluetooth off since boot, every count 0 (hw-alignment audit). A relaunch stops the player as the switch does, and the Q2 losing power in the second between off and on boots with Bluetooth off (the switch saved `BLUETOOTH` 0).

**What comes before a storm.** From 2026-11-19 to 22 the logs hold nine relaunches. Five began within 4 s of an inquiry or a page: a scan as the Bluetooth page opened (2026-11-19 22:46:25Z, 2026-11-20 05:18:26Z, 2026-11-21 06:52:35Z), a connect at a cable in (2026-11-22 06:07:06Z) and one after a page timeout (2026-11-19 20:35:46Z); the other four had no Bluetooth line before their first bad frame. One storm, 2026-11-21 17:42Z, had `command 0x2039 tx timeout` (LE Set Extended Advertising Enable) in it, at 17:42:28Z, 8 s after its first `Peer acked invalid packet` (17:42:20Z): a command sent into a link already broken, not what broke it, as the other eight timed out on BR/EDR's commands or none. coda-rc, the Car Remote daemon, sends advertising commands only 2 s after the stack comes up, 30 s after a refusal (`advertising refused: status 0x0b`), at a rename and around a phone's LE link, of which the logs hold one, 13 s after the 17:42Z relaunch; its lines reached no log on the card until 1128 (they were only in `/tmp/coda-rc.log`), so whether one came just before a storm is for the next storm's log to say. Nothing in these logs makes advertising a cause; scans and pages come before most.

**The driver's own numbers.** The error lines say a packet was bad, not which numbers the two ends hold. The stock module carries `pr_debug` lines that do (26 descriptors in its `__dyndbg` section; the kernel has dynamic debug), so at an H5 error line `bt_kmsg` writes four queries, `module hci_uart_h5_kernel_5_10_21 func <f> +p` for `h5_timed_event`, `h5_complete_rx_pkt`, `h5_pkt_cull` and `h5_prepare_pkt` (`bt_h5dbg_ctl`), to `/proc/dynamic_debug/control` (or debugfs's), notes a `UART sign` line and `H5 DEBUG on`, and from then copies the driver's debug lines to the q2-bt log as `H5 <kernel ms> <line>`: `Request for pkt N from card` (the controller's acknowledgement number), `Removing A pkts out of B, up to seqno C` (what it took off the Q2's queue of B unacknowledged packets), `Sending packet with seqno N` and `We request packet no N to card` (the Q2's own numbers), `Received seqno N from card` (a reliable packet from the controller, taken in order) and `hu ... retransmitting N pkts` (the 250 ms resend). A line is logged when it differs from the last of its kind (`bt_h5dbg_line`), so a storm's repeating pair is two lines and each change of a number one more, `BT_H5D_CAP` (240) at most; `BT_H5D_MS` (20 s) after the last error line, `BT_H5D_MAX_MS` (60 s) after they came on, or at the cap, the queries are written again with `-p` (`H5 DEBUG off after N lines`), and only an error line 20 s or more after the last one, another event, turns them on again. No control file taking the queries is noted once, `H5 DEBUG unavailable: ...`. While on, each packet costs the kernel a printk or two, which is why the lines are not left on. Reading a storm: an acknowledgement number that stays put outside the Q2's window (`Removing 0 pkts out of B` with B above 0, or the number unequal to the Q2's next `seqno` with B 0) while no `Received seqno` line comes says the controller's packets are unreliable ones and its H5 link has started over or lost count, which this driver cannot answer (its link-establishment handler is compiled out); `Received seqno` lines coming says the controller still delivers events and only the Q2's commands are refused. `test/unit/test_q2bt_wedge.py` checks the kinds, the once-per-state rule, the cap, the queries and the `ps_info` line.

## Bluetooth name

Stock names the Q2 **Shanling Q2** in `/etc/bluetooth/main.conf` (`Name`), BlueZ's own default for the adapter, and offers no way to change it: the Bluetooth page's second head row, **Bluetooth Name**, shows what `getLocalBtName` (`0x4fabd4`, `btctl_get_controller_info`'s name) reports, and `btmenu_setting_row_on_click` ignores it. BlueZ (5.66, storage `/mnt/data/bluetooth`) uses `main.conf`'s `Name` unless the adapter's `Alias` property was set over D-Bus, which it keeps in that directory's `settings` file across restarts. The build writes `Name = Q2 Muse` (`BT_NAME` in `tools/build.py`), so a Q2 with no chosen name is **Q2 Muse**, new or updated alike: stock never set an `Alias`. A name the user saved, **Q2** included, stays as it is.

A chosen name is `[Q2POD] BTNAME` in `config.ini` (`patch/bt_name.c`), empty or missing for the default. `bt_name_apply` sets `Alias` to it, or to `""`, which BlueZ takes as "back to `Name`" and which drops a stored alias, with `dbus-send` in a background shell that tries every 0.5 s for 20 s, as bluetoothd may not be on the bus yet, and once BlueZ has taken it writes the same name, or **Q2 Muse** with none chosen, into the controller itself (`hciconfig hci0 name`, HCI Write Local Name), which is what a car or a paired phone reads when it asks for the name. That second write is needed at boot: openBluetooth's `hciconfig hci0 reset` (a down and an up) logs `Can't init device hci0: Function not implemented (89)` at every boot and not at a relaunch, and on 2026-11-22 (build 1127, two minutes after boot) `hciconfig hci0 name` read **RT_BT**, the RTL8733BS's own default, while BlueZ's `Name` and `Alias` and the inquiry answer (`hciconfig hci0 inqdata`) all said Q2 Muse; the BMW showed RT_BT that morning. BlueZ does not rewrite it: an `Alias` of `""` with none stored, or one equal to what it holds, changes nothing, and the kernel skips a local name equal to its own copy. After a [relaunch](#bluetooth-controller-watchdog) the controller read Q2 Muse. It runs at every Bluetooth on (`headset_status_register`, the `BT_STATUS` call in `openBluetooth`) and after a rename, so `config.ini` is the one record: Q2 Muse's first-boot defaults and stock's Reset Settings, which replace `config.ini` without `BTNAME` ([Q2 Muse's defaults, once](#first-boot)), bring **Q2 Muse** back at the next Bluetooth on even though `/mnt/data/bluetooth` keeps the old alias until then, and a firmware update keeps the name. The change is live: BlueZ updates the controller's local name and its inquiry answer at once, so a phone searching sees it straight away; a phone already paired shows it once it reads the name again, which some only do after a new pairing.

`bt_page` (from `ringnav_btrows`) puts `bt_name_row` in stock's second row's place, with its height: **Name**, the name as its value and a chevron; with Bluetooth off, where stock builds only the switch, Name follows it at stock's row height. Center opens the letter strip ([oled-design](oled-design.md#text-entry), `search_strip_text`): its own page titled Bluetooth, the name typed in the Name row's own place after its label (`search_strip_label`), "Phones and cars see this name" under the row (`search_strip_note`), the name prefilled, at most 30 characters (`BT_NAME_MAX`; BlueZ takes 248 bytes, the row shows about that many). Next at the end saves: the name without its edge spaces, refused when empty ("Name can't be empty") or holding a character the shell or `config.ini` would misread (a quote, a backslash or a backtick, none of which the strip types: "Can't use that name"); **Q2 Muse** itself saves as none. A held Return leaves it as it was. Car Remote's Bluetooth LE advertisement (`patch/coda_rc_ble.c`) carries the name in its scan response, which has 31 bytes of its own (the advertisement's hold the flags and the 128-bit service UUID); a 30-character name is cut to 29 and marked shortened. The remote app finds the Q2 by the UUID, not the name. Guest Play's hotspot, with no Guest Play name, is named **Q2 Muse** too (`patch/q2_guest.c` `hotspot_ssid`). Stock's AirPlay and DLNA names (Wi-Fi services) are not Bluetooth's and keep stock's.

## Bluetooth pairing card

A device that pairs with the Q2 by numeric comparison (a phone, most cars) asks the user to check a six-digit code on both screens. BlueZ (5.66) asks the pairing agent `libbtctl.so` registers for demo, which hands each `org.bluez.Agent1` call to demo's prompt callback as `(type, text, userdata)` (`btctl_prompt`, `0x11efc`); `patch/bt_pair.c` `bt_pair_prompt` is that callback, in place of stock's (`0x4f9d20`, `tools/stock_map.tsv`). Stock sets its callback twice: before the control thread starts (`platform_init`, where `headset_bt_init` in `patch/headset.c` now registers instead) and again in `openBluetooth` at every Bluetooth on (`0x4fa6e8`, `tools/build.py` `BT_PROMPT`), which runs after it at boot; both calls are `bt_pair_register`'s. libbtctl's callback word (`btctl_set_prompt_callback`, its only writer) otherwise held stock's: a build that replaced only the first registration showed stock's "Bluetooth Code:" dialog on a Q2 with Bluetooth on (2026-11-23, the word read from a running demo as `0x004f9d20`), which the emulator, with Bluetooth off, never runs into. The card is the [pairing card](oled-design.md#pairing).

**What libbtctl does with each call** (its method table at `0x427ac`, read from the disassembly): RequestPinCode is type 1, DisplayPinCode 2, RequestPasskey 3, DisplayPasskey 4, RequestConfirmation 5 (its passkey as `"%06u"`), RequestAuthorization 6, AuthorizeService 7. For 1, 3, 5, 6 and 7 it keeps the call, `dbus_message_ref`'d, as its one pending request (the word at its load address + `0x45900`) before the callback; a callback that returns 0 makes libbtctl answer at once through `btctl_reply`: 1 with the PIN `0000`, 3 refused (`org.bluez.Error.Rejected`), 5, 6 and 7 yes. 2 and 4 are answered before the callback is called. `btctl_reply` (`agent_response`, `0xe380`) answers the pending request, `yes` a method return, `no` Rejected, and clears it; with none pending it does nothing. Stock's callback, like `bt_pair_prompt`, returns 1 for type 5 alone, so only RequestConfirmation waits for the user, and every other type is libbtctl's own answer, as it always was: legacy PIN pairing (an old car kit) gets `0000`, a passkey to type in on the Q2 is refused, and a passkey or PIN for the user to type on the other device (DisplayPasskey, DisplayPinCode) is never shown. That last one is asked of a display-capable responder only when the other device has a keyboard and no display, which no audio device the Q2 pairs with is; ponytail: a card for it would be the same pairing card with the code and Cancel alone.

**Why a card outlived its request.** BlueZ ends a request it gave up on by calling the agent's `Cancel`: the device cancelled or failed the pairing, or its link dropped (`device_cancel_authentication`, `device_bonding_complete`, each `agent_cancel`), or no answer came within `REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, 60 s (`src/agent.c`; `simple_agent_reply` calls `agent_cancel` on the D-Bus NoReply). libbtctl's Cancel (`0xdb30`) unrefs its pending request, clears the word and replies; it never calls the prompt callback. Stock's dialog (`on_wm_timer_dialog`, a modal `confirminfo_dialog` titled "Bluetooth Code:" and the digits) had nothing to close it, and one sat on a Q2 for six and a half hours while `q2update` answered `busy` (`sw_update.c`, while `confirm_up()`).

**How the card ends now.** `bt_pair_poll` (each UI pass, from `bt_ui_poll`) compares libbtctl's pending word with the request the card was raised for: when it differs (Cancel cleared it, or the card's own answer did) the card closes with no answer, and the pairing stays refused by BlueZ. If no Cancel comes, the card counts down BlueZ's 60 s on its Cancel row and at 0 answers `no` itself; the poll does the same should the card never have opened (another card up all that time). A `yes` goes only from the Pair row, and only while the pending request is still the card's; any other end is a refusal or no answer at all. libbtctl's load address comes from `/proc/self/maps` once, at `headset_bt_init`, and is trusted only when the word at `+0xe3b0` is `agent_response`'s `lw $4, 0x5900($17)` (`0x8e245900`); without it the card still opens, closes at the 60 s refusal, and answers whatever is pending. libbtctl answers on its own thread and the UI on demo's, with no lock between them, as stock's were: an answer that crosses a Cancel finds nothing pending and does nothing.

**The device.** The callback is given no device, but the pending request is the RequestConfirmation call itself, its body (the device's object path, the passkey). `bt_pair_msg_path` reads it from libdbus 1.12.24's `DBusMessage` (`/usr/lib/libdbus-1.so.3.19.15`, fixed with the rest of the stock image by `ZIP_SHA`: the header's bytes at `+4`, the body's at `+64`, its length at `+68`, as `dbus_message_iter_init` takes `&message->body`), and keeps the path only when the header is a little-endian method call whose body length matches, the path is under `/org/bluez/hci` and the passkey in the body is the one the callback was handed. The name is BlueZ's `Name` for that path, asked with `dbus-send` in a background shell (`bt_shell`) into `/tmp/q2-btpair-name` once a second until it answers. A phone that has never paired is a new `Device1` whose name BlueZ learns from the new link (the kernel asks the device for it); whether it has it by the time the confirmation request comes was not established (the emulator has no Bluetooth controller), so the card waits for BlueZ's first answer (one second at most) before it opens, opens as "Pair with this device?" over "Unknown device" and the address when there is none yet, and changes to the name in place (`confirm_words`) when BlueZ has it. A path that does not check out names nothing: "Unknown device" alone. BlueZ's `Alias` is not used: for an unnamed device it is the address with dashes.

**Guest Play** registers its own agent (`q2-guest`, `patch/q2_guest.c`) and asks BlueZ to make it the default while Let a Guest Connect is open; BlueZ sends a pairing to the default agent, so a guest's pairing reaches `q2-guest` and its card (`guest_ui.c`), never libbtctl's, and falls back to libbtctl's when `q2-guest` unregisters. `bt_pair.c` changes nothing there.

**Log.** Each decision is a unified-log line of source `bt`: `pair: callback set, libbtctl checked (76eab000)` (or `not found or not the one known`) at each registration; `pair: request 239014, device /org/bluez/hci0/dev_...` (or `not identified`) and `pair: request type N left to libbtctl` from the callback; `pair: name "Pixel 10" for ADDRESS`, `pair: card up: NAME, N s left`, `pair: request ended by BlueZ (Cancel): card closed`, `pair: no Cancel in 60 s: refusing` (`W`), `pair: answered pair` or `refused`, and `pair: answer ... dropped: the request had ended`.

Tested by `test/fw/test_bt_pair.py`, with libbtctl's image and agent doubled: the card raised and named, a Cancel closing it with no answer, BlueZ's timeout refusing, an answer after the Cancel saying nothing, the unknown and late name, a request that does not check out, and `q2update` busy only while the card is up; `test/patch_suite/04_bluetooth_volume.py` checks both registrations on the build (openBluetooth's site a `jal bt_pair_register`, which sets `bt_pair_prompt` whatever it is handed).

## Guest Play screens

`patch/guest_ui.c` draws Guest Play ([oled-design](oled-design.md#guest-play)) from q2-guest's [contract](#contract) alone: `guest_field`, `guest_seq` and `guest_send` (`patch/guest.c`). `guest_ui_poll` (from `bt_ui_poll`, every UI loop pass, at most every 250 ms, as guest.c reads the state) acts when `seq` changes:

- **Asking.** `state=asking` brings up the confirmation card (`confirm`, `CONFIRM_CONSEQUENTIAL`: it opens on its first row, Allow Once, so one Centre answers; Return answers Decline) with the guest's name, a first pairing's six-digit `code` spaced as two threes, and `countdown` as the card's timeout to Decline; `state=replace` the Replace card (Keep, selected, or Replace, its timeout to Keep). The answer goes back as `allow-once`, `allow-always`, `decline`, `keep` or `replace`. A card whose question the daemon settled (its own 30 s, the guest gone) or another guest's is closed (`confirm_close`). The card's own countdown and the daemon's run side by side; whichever ends first answers the same way.
- **Events.** A new `event_seq` toasts `event` about `eventname`, the guest named short where the owner knows them ("Alex" for "Alex's Pixel", `guest_short`; open question 7); the state's event at the first look is old and not toasted. `failed` opens `guestfail_page` (a mode page, Try Again sending `open`).
- **Now Playing.** A phone's guest starting (`state` playing or paused from any other, `source` empty) opens `guestnp_page`, painted by `guest_ui_paint`: the song (`title`, `artist`), "Playing from" the `guest`, the path to `out` (or the headphone jack) and each leg's codec line from `in` and `outcodec` (`CODEC RATE KBPS`, `leg_words`, what is known); Centre sends `stop`, Play/Pause, Next and Previous `key toggle`, `key next`, `key prev`. It closes when the guest is gone. In front while `state` is playing it holds the screen lit under Smart Awake, as the owner's Now Playing does (`guest_ui_keeps_lit`, read by `navigation.c` `keep_lit_poll`); paused, Screen Off Time applies. A receiver's guest (`source` spotify, airplay, dlna) plays on its own page and opens none.
