- **Settings.** `guestset_page` (from the Bluetooth page's Audio row), `guesttrust_page` and `hotspot_page` are `page_list` pages rebuilt at each change; the trusted guests come from the daemon's `/mnt/data/q2-guest/trusted`, read only. A choice's check is `bt_ui.c`'s mark (`BT_MARK_CHECK`). `guestconnect_page` sends `open` and paints the name, the `window` countdown and, while `hotspot_up`, the `hotspot_qr` code; Done sends `close`. The QR codes are libqrencode's (`QRcode_encodeString`, which stock's demo already imports), drawn as modules on a white plate.
- **Elsewhere.** The status row's Bluetooth slot shows the guest's phone while `guest_active` ([Status row slots](#status-row-slots)); Home's first row (stock's Now Playing row, `patch/home_np.c`) reads Guest Play while a guest plays or is paused and shows then even with nothing of the owner's loaded (`lr_home_apply` on `guest_active`); its click and a short Return open the guest's Now Playing (`guest_home_np`, the click through `home_np_bind`'s swap of stock's handler), and Home keeps its eight rows; `guest_ui_poll` lays Home out again when that changes), so Guest Play merely on leaves Home its eight rows, and it opens the guest's Now Playing (`guest_home_click`; Let a Guest Connect if the guest left before the row went); `guest_ui_poll` lays Home out again (`coverflow_home_layout`) when the switch changes.

ponytail: the guest's cover art is not in the contract, so Now Playing shows the art's place with the music glyph. ponytail: seen only in the emulator against a hand-written state file; the daemon, the prompts' timing against a real phone and the hotspot's code on a phone's camera are for a Q2.

## Bluetooth page

Settings > Bluetooth ([oled-design](oled-design.md#bluetooth)) is stock's `bluetooth_page`, whose list stock's `btmenu_rows` (`0x4c3ef8`) rebuilds whole on every scan result and link change: five head rows with Bluetooth on (the switch, Bluetooth Name, Quality over its choice, Bluetooth Headset Volume Control and Scan now; the switch alone off, `btmenu_setting_row_build`), then, when it lists such devices, a 60 px header (`btmenu_msginfo_layout`, `bt_paireddev`) and a row per paired device, and another (`bt_compatiabledev`) and a row per found one, each row's button named by the device's index in `pdeq_btshowlist` (its records 0x124 bytes: the MAC at `+4`, the name at `+0x24`; `getSearchResult` fills it from `btctl_get_device_list`, paired first). A device row (`btmenu_device_row_build`) holds stock's icon, the name, and a state label whose `tr_text` is `msg_connecting` (a link thread runs for it), `msg_connected` (the link list's last item at status 3 with a codec) or `msg_paired`, and on a paired row an Unpair image at x 276 (`navbar_delete`): stock's click (`btmenu_item_on_click`, `0x4c43a4`) reads the pointer's x (`+0x18`) and asks Unpair? from x 276 on, else connects (`handleBluetoothLink`), or disconnects the connected one.

`ringnav_btrows` adds Resume on Connect and Link Volume (`pod_rows`) and hands the list to `bt_page` (`patch/bt_ui.c`), which orders it: the switch, Name ([Bluetooth name](#bluetooth-name)), My Devices' header and rows, Other Devices' (stock's header, or one of its own when nothing is found yet), then an Audio header, Quality, Headset Volume (stock's `btadjustvol_page` row: its page steps the headset's own A2DP volume with `adjustA2dpVolume`, so it is not folded into Link Volume, which links the Q2's volume to the device's), Resume on Connect and Link Volume. Scan now's row is destroyed (stock's `bluetooth_searchicon` finds no `bt_search_icon` and does nothing). `tools/build.py` `LABELS` words stock's strings: My Devices, Other Devices, Not Connected (`msg_paired`), Connecting… (`msg_connecting`), Headset Volume (`bt_adjvol`), LDAC Best (`btcode_ldachq`), Auto (`btcode_ldacauto`). Stock's `LDAC Connection (auto)` is Auto, also the Quality row's value when chosen and the choice a Q2 starts on: stock's default `config.ini` says `BTCODING=2`, which `default_config` (`tools/build.py`) requires (stock reads a missing key as 0, LDAC Best). Quality's row becomes a key/value row: its choice's label is read and destroyed and `list_value` writes "Quality" and the choice, so `set_row_h` no longer doubles it. A header is a disabled item a row high (the wheel passes it), its label in the section header's type. Each device row's click is stock's handler taken off (`widget_off_by_func`) and `row_click` put on: a paired device, connected or not (`msg_connected` or `msg_paired`), opens its page (`bt_detail_open`), where Connect is the first row for one that is not; a paired one connecting (its link thread's target, the link list's last item, at status 5 while its Connect runs) stops connecting, the auto-reconnect at Bluetooth on included: `cancel_connect` marks the target failed (`updateBtLinkStatus` 4, as [Bluetooth boot reconnect](#bluetooth-boot-reconnect)'s adoption ends the wait), the thread's 100 ms loop ends, and `checkBluetoothStatus` takes stock's failure path, which shows nothing: `btDisconnect` (BlueZ answers its pending Connect as cancelled), the link list cleared, `bt_connectstatus` 0, the row back to Not Connected (stock ignores a tap while the thread runs, `0x4c43e4`); a found one is stock's click at x 0 (`bt_stock_click`, a pointer event with only its x set), which pairs it, as is a connecting row whose connect cannot be cancelled yet (stock ignores it); ponytail: whether the controller's page in progress stops with BlueZ's cancel is for a Q2 to show; Play/Pause held on a paired row opens its page too (`bt_ui_hold`, from `ringnav_keylong`).

After stock's layout (`ipod_list_layout`'s `bt_rows_pre`, which makes the connected row 52 px, the two-line pitch, and the others the set's row, and `bt_rows_post`), `dress` puts a row's children on the design's columns: stock's icon and Unpair image hidden, a mark image for the kind's glyph (`bt_ui_paint`, from the paint chain, draws the marks in final colours: the glyph, the Positive dot, the chevron and the spinners), the name at x 52, and the state: the connected row's second line "Connected · LDAC · 72%" (`bt_codec`, stock's `bt_showcoding` as its status bar's badge reads it: 4 LDAC, 13 aptX HD, 3 aptX, 2 AAC, 1 SBC; and `bt_headset_battery`), else the state as a value before the chevron (paired) or the spinner (connecting). The kind is the device's Class of Device (`bt_class`, `bt_kind`: major Audio/Video's minor 1, 2 and 6 headphones, 8 car audio, 5, 7 and 10 speakers; major Phone a phone; else the Bluetooth rune), which a background shell asks BlueZ for (`Device1.Class` with `dbus-send`) for every listed device the file has no line for, once per new set of devices, writing `MAC CLASS` lines whole to `/tmp/q2-btclass`; the page reads it back as it rebuilds and every 500 ms while open, repainting when it changed.

**The row follows the link.** A device's row and its page judge it connected by stock's rule, the link list's last item at status 3, and connecting while a link thread runs for it; but on 2026-11-19 the Pixel Buds' item stayed short of 3 for minutes while their link was up and streaming ([Bluetooth connection trace](#bluetooth-connection-trace)). So where the last item is a device whose connected ACL link the kernel holds (`bt_acl_up`: `HCIGETCONNLIST` on an unbound HCI socket, an ACL link at `BT_CONNECTED`, asked at most every 500 ms; `link_ahead`), `bt_dev_state` says connected too. Stock's own label is not that rule: `btmenu_device_row_build` labels a row `msg_connecting` while its link thread runs, whatever the item's status, and `msg_connected` only at 3 with a codec. On V1JCi (2026-11-19, 22:14Z) the Buds' item went 1, 3, 5 and back to 3 at 22:14:49Z with the link up while the thread ran on to 22:15:02Z: the row, moved from Other Devices to My Devices and rebuilt meanwhile, said Connecting and kept it, as stock rebuilds only when its own state moves. So `bt_rows_pre` sets a device row's label to `msg_connected` before the layout whenever `bt_dev_state` says connected (`state_tr`), making it the two-line Connected row whose Centre opens its page, and the page's poll asks stock to rebuild the list (`g_btsetting_flag`) while any row's label says less than that (`labels_stale`). A label is only ever lifted to Connected: where stock says Connecting or Not Connected and `bt_dev_state` agrees or says less, stock's stands. Stock's own state is left as it is: the status row's slot, the toasts and the codec still go by status 3. ponytail: while stock's link thread still runs, stock ignores taps (`0x4c43e4`), so a Disconnect from the device's page may do nothing until it ends; why stock's item stays short of 3 is for the trace to show.

**Found devices, as they are found.** Stock's page timer reads the search results (`getSearchResult`, which fills `pdeq_btshowlist` from `btctl_get_device_list`) only as a scan's count ends, so a device heard early in a 10 s scan waited for its end: on 2026-11-19 the Buds were heard at 22:14:32.2Z (q2guard's `found`) and listed at 22:14:37.2Z (`page shows found`). While the page scans (`bt_searchtime` past 1), `page_poll` reads them each second (`BT_RESULTS_MS`) and, when the list it read differs from the one the rows were built from (`listed_hash`, taken at each build in `bt_page`), rebuilds the page at once (`ringnav_btrows`, stock's `btmenu_rows` and the page's order), as stock's own timer reads and rebuilds in one call (`0x4c4848`). A row knows its device only by its place in that list (its button's name, which stock's click reads too), so a read left to the 200 ms timer to rebuild (`g_btsetting_flag`, as V1JDi did) had a row, for up to that long, paint the glyph of the device that had moved into its place, and a tap there go to it: on V1JDi the user saw a Bluetooth glyph turn into a headphone one under a row as the list shifted (`test_a_device_found_mid_scan_never_paints_on_another_s_row`).

**Only what the scan heard.** `btctl_get_device_list` (`libbtctl.so`, `0x111f8`) lists every `Device1` proxy its BlueZ client holds, each record the address, the alias and `Paired`, and `getSearchResult` puts the paired ones under My Devices and the rest under Other Devices; it never looks at `RSSI`. BlueZ loads every record in its store at start, so a record with no key in it (`/mnt/data/bluetooth/ADAPTER/ADDRESS/info` with no `[LinkKey]`: a pairing that never finished, kept as `Trusted`, which a temporary device found by a scan is not, so it never expires) is a `Device1` at `Paired` false for good, and was listed under Other Devices wherever the Q2 was: on 2026-11-20 (V1N6i) an Arctis Nova Pro Wireless (20:AF:1B:18:FD:03) stayed there 20 miles from it, and stock's found rows have no Forget. So `bt_page` lists a found device only once BlueZ has had an `RSSI` for it since the page opened (a discovery heard it; BlueZ drops the property as each discovery ends, so a device heard once stays listed until the page closes, `heard`). It asks BlueZ in the background (`seen_fetch`, at each build and poll when the set changes, and every 2 s while the page scans, `BT_SEEN_MS`) about up to 8 found devices not heard yet: `Properties.Get` of `RSSI` with `dbus-send`, `MAC seen` into `/tmp/q2-btseen` for one that has it; and for one that does not, with `Paired` and `Connected` both false and a record in the store with no `Key]` section in it (`[LinkKey]`, `[LongTermKey]` and the rest), BlueZ's `Adapter1.RemoveDevice`, `MAC removed`, and `stale record removed ADDRESS "NAME"` in the unified log (source `bt`). Nothing is removed while a connect or pairing runs (`bt_connectstatus` 1 or a row connecting) or for the link thread's target; a temporary device not heard is only hidden, as BlueZ expires it itself. The file's first line is the ask's number (`#N`), so an answer to an earlier open's ask is not read. A device found mid-scan is listed one poll (500 ms) after BlueZ answers, as the page rebuilds when one is heard. Tested by `test/fw/test_bt_ui.py` against a stand-in BlueZ under `sh` (`test_other_devices_lists_what_the_scan_heard_and_a_stale_record_is_removed`).

**Scanning.** `bt_ui_poll` (every UI loop pass, from `ringnav_sleep`) keeps the page scanning while it is the top window with Bluetooth on: when no scan runs (`bt_searchtime` 0; stock's `btStartSearch` refuses otherwise, and its page timer counts it down and reads the results at 1), no link thread runs (`bt_connectstatus` not 1) and Bluetooth started (`bt_initstatus` 0), it calls `btStartSearch` and sets `g_btsetting_flag`, so the page's 200 ms timer rebuilds the list from the first results: once as the page opens, and again each time one ends only while no device is connected or connecting, as an inquiry beside an A2DP stream takes its air time. Stock ends a scan itself in three places: its page timer at the count's end, the page's close and background handlers (`EVT_WINDOW_CLOSE` and `EVT_WINDOW_BACKGROUND`, `0x4c3240` and `0x4c3274`, registered by `systemset_bluetooth_page_init`; the second also removes the timer), and a device row's click before it connects (`btmenu_item_on_click`, `0x4c4430`); `btStopSearch` calls `btctl_stop_discovery` only while `bt_searchtime` is above 0. So leaving the page, for another page, a dialog over it or Back, ends the inquiry, and so does a connect from a row or from a device's page (`bt_stock_click`). A connect that goes by no click did not: the headset reconnecting by itself, or `headset.c`'s or the boot's connect, while the page scanned ran beside the rest of the scan's 10 s. So `page_poll` stops a running scan when a connect starts (`bt_connectstatus` 1, or a row going to Connecting or Connected since the last poll, `bt.linking`), with stock's `btStopSearch`, then `getSearchResult` and a rebuild as the timer's end does; the opening scan beside a device already connected runs on, so Other Devices fills. Not seen in an HCI log: the emulator has no controller; `test/fw/test_bt_ui.py` holds both. The spinner beside Other Devices shows while `bt_searchtime` is past 1, and a connecting row's spinner while stock's link thread connects it; both are `list_marks.c`'s one activity spinner, which Cover Flow's opening row uses too: its frame is the clock's (`spinner_frame`, a spoke every 100 ms), each painter reports the box it drew (`spinner_painted`), and one timer at `MO_FRAME_MS` repaints just those boxes as the frame changes, stopping once none was painted for two frames. The row's spinner therefore turns whether a scan runs or not.

**Quality.** `btquality_page`'s rows (stock's init: a button named by the choice's index, 0 LDAC Best to 7 SBC, as `g_btcoding`) get their bit rate where the codec fixes one, at 48 kHz (`choice_kbps`: LDAC Best 990, Standard 660, aptX HD 576, aptX 384), right-aligned on the right column (`quality_rates`), the switch's edge, and on the checked row (`g_btcoding`) `BT_CHECK_GAP` (24) before it, the check's 12 px and its gap; a pick moves stock's check with no layout, so `bt_ui_poll` places the rates again when `g_btcoding` changes; Auto a caption (`caption_row`): its rate steps with the signal between 330 and 990 kbps ([Bluetooth LDAC quality](#bluetooth-ldac-quality)) and bluealsa does not report where it is, so the caption says the range, not the live value. Auto is only LDAC's rate: bluealsa offers aptX HD, aptX, AAC and SBC beside LDAC whatever the choice, and a headset without LDAC streams one of those at its own rate (a Bowers & Wilkins Px7 on Auto: aptX HD at 48 kHz, a fixed 576 kbps), so with a device connected on another codec `auto_caption` names it instead, "Best this headset supports: aptX HD, 576 kbps" (`bt_codec`, `bt_kbps` at `bt_headset_rate`; no rate for AAC and SBC), and keeps LDAC's range on LDAC, with nothing connected or the codec not yet known. ponytail: a live value needs bluealsa to say which eqmid `ldac_ABR_Proc` chose (a property, or a word demo can read). `quality_rows` runs on every layout, the caption's own growth included, so `caption_row` keeps one table entry per row: a second, never measured, would set the row's height after the first in `cap_step` and hold it at its title's. **The order** (the user's, 2026-11-18): one list, Adapt to Signal first, a CODEC header, then Auto, LDAC Best, LDAC Standard, aptX HD, aptX, AAC, SBC HQ and SBC. `quality_order`, from `bt_rows_pre` on every layout, restacks stock's eight rows and the two of its own; each stock row keeps its button's name, its `g_btcoding` index, which stock's click reads (`atoi` of the name, `0x4c5540`) and its check finds again by name, so a pick saves stock's number whatever its place, and the picker opens on the checked row (`CHOICE`, [Selection](#selection)). The header is `head_px` at 13 px, a disabled item a header high (`_bt_codec`), made once. The switch row, Adapt to Signal (`step_row`, added by `bt_rows_pre` before the picker's first layout and found again by its item's `_bt_step` on each later one, so it holds no state of its own), saves `[Q2POD] BTSTEPDOWN` 1 or 0 and is off with no key saved (the user's, 2026-11-18: the switch was on by default before, and only turning it off and on again saved a 1, so a Q2 that never touched it is off and one turned on by hand stays on); its caption, "On Auto or SBC, lowers quality to keep playing when the signal is weak", says what it does. q2guard reads the key (**Step-down** and **SBC bitpool** in [Bluetooth link monitor](#bluetooth-link-monitor)); `quality_rows` gives it no bit rate. **A pick with a headset linked.** Stock asks to reconnect and drops the headset to apply any new choice ([Bluetooth link monitor](#bluetooth-link-monitor), **The switch and the link**). `bt_quality_linked` answers the click's read of `bt_linkstatus` instead (`bt_quality_site`, which takes the choice from the click's `$s0` and puts back the `$gp` the click saved, as the click reads `bt_showcoding` through it next): a choice of another codec than the one streaming (`row_codec` against `bt_showcoding`) runs `q2bt-codec` in the background on bluealsa's A2DP source PCM (its path from `GetPCMs`, through a `sed` pattern of what an object path holds) for the choice's codec and then bluetoothd's own order (LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC, SBC), stopping at the first bluealsa takes, so a headset without the choice's codec gets what a reconnect would have given; what each try said is in `/tmp/q2bt.pick`, and the unified log (source `bt`) has the pick. **The device's codecs** (Android's R9 and R10, `~/q2-emu/design/bt-android-study-20261118.md`: the pick is the head of an ordered list, and a codec the sink lacks is refused before the link is touched). Once a link streams (a codec in `bt_showcoding`), `sink_poll` (from `link_poll`) asks bluealsa's `org.bluealsa.PCM1.GetCodecs` on that device's A2DP source PCM (its path from `GetPCMs` by the device's `dev_` part) in the background, `sink_fetch`, which lists each codec of the sink endpoints BlueZ found on it (bluez-alsa 4.0.0 `bluealsa_pcm_get_codecs`; the vendor binary has the method, its strings show, and `SelectCodec`'s "SEP codec not available"); the answer goes to `/tmp/q2bt.codecs` as the MAC's line then each string a line, which `sink_read` reads into `sink.bits` (the five codecs Quality offers, by name; SBC always, as A2DP makes it mandatory), asking again every 3 s, ten times at most, while unanswered. Known, `bt_quality_linked` drops the codecs the device lacks from the list before anything is sent: when what is left starts with the codec streaming (aptX HD picked on a car with SBC and AAC, AAC streaming) nothing is switched and the unified log says `Quality: aptX-HD not on the device, AAC kept`; otherwise `q2bt-codec` is run for what is left only (the same car on SBC: `AAC SBC`, so AAC). Unknown, the whole list is tried as before, bluealsa refusing each codec the device lacks itself. The pick is saved either way (stock's tail), kept for the next device. On the picker, `quality_lacks` (after each layout, and from `bt_ui_poll` when the device, its codecs or the codec streaming change) marks each choice whose codec the device lacks (`_bt_lack` on its item: LDAC Best and Standard, aptX HD, aptX, AAC; never Auto or SBC): its text is drawn as the Library's grayed rows ([server-library: Grayed rows](server-library.md#grayed-rows): #666666 off the selection, the selection's ink at 70% on it; `bt_quality_dim` from `ringnav_style_color`), it stays pickable, and its caption says why, "BMW 6R81 doesn't support aptX HD: using AAC" (the device's name, UTF-8 as BlueZ gives it, cut at 20 characters, never inside one, then the codec streaming; `caption_row` decodes a caption's UTF-8 to the code units the canvas draws, `cap_wide` in `patch/settings_pages.c`); a caption whose row no longer lacks its codec goes (`caption_row` with no text). ponytail: GetCodecs is not yet seen answering on a Q2 (the radio was wedged when the device was read); with no answer the marks never show and picks walk the whole list as before. A link that comes up on a codec other than the first the device takes on the list is not switched at connect: bluetoothd's own choice (stock's priority) stands until the user picks. It answers 0, so stock runs its tail for no link: the priority set for the next connect, `BTCODING` saved, the checks moved, with no dialog, and the music plays on through the switch's gap. A choice of the codec streaming does nothing for aptX HD, aptX and AAC, which have one rate; within LDAC's three and SBC's two choices the rate is one bluealsa reads as the encoder starts, so those answer the link and stock reconnects as before. `codec_follow` (each `bt_ui_poll`) then copies the codec bluealsa's status event named (`a2dp_eventstate`) to `bt_showcoding` on a link that is up: stock's `checkBluetoothStatus` takes the event only while it sets a link up (`bt_a2dp_direction`), so after a switch in place, a pick's or the step-down's, the badge, the connected row and Auto's caption showed the codec the link began on. ponytail: seen under Unicorn and on the build machine only; the gap a pick costs on a Q2, and whether the Px7 keeps its link through it, are for a Q2 to show (the same log check).

**A device's page** (`patch/bt_detail.c`, `btdevice_page`): the status row names it; the path "Q2 → name" and its codec line (`bt_codec_line`: the codec, the stream's rate from `bt_headset_rate`, and the bit rate where it is fixed, `bt_kbps`: LDAC Best 990 or 909 kbps and Standard 660 or 606 by Quality's choice, aptX HD 576 or 529, aptX 384 or 352, at 48 or 44.1 kHz; none for Auto, AAC and SBC, whose rate bluealsa does not report), then Battery when the headset reports one, Disconnect or Connect (stock's click on the device's row, `bt_stock_click`; Connect the first row), Volume Limit (No Limit or the limit before the chevron, `label_btlimit`; the slider page, `xfade_open` context 5, [Headset controls and volume](#headset-controls-and-volume)), Volume Curve (Even or Gentle before the chevron, `label_btcurve`; its picker, `bt_curve_open`, the same section), Rename and Forget This Device (Negative red, `text_ink`). The page follows the link (`bt_detail_poll`): connected or not, and the level. Rename (the letter strip) sets BlueZ's `Device1.Alias` with `dbus-send` in the background and the record's name in place (`bt_dev_rename`), so the list shows it at once. Forget asks on the confirmation card (`confirm`, destructive) and, on Forget Device, does what stock's click does after its Unpair? dialog's OK (`0x4c44b8` to `0x4c45b4`): `handleBluetoothPair`, and when it returned 2 (the device was the output) `check_outputdevice` and `config_outputchannel` put the sound on a jack unless the saved play status is stopped; then `forget_link`, the toast, `getSearchResult`, `player_save_start(1)` and the list rebuilt (`g_btsetting_flag`); the page closes. `handleBluetoothPair` (`0x4fe050`) disconnects only a device at link status 3, then always calls `removePairDev` (`btctl_untrust_device` and `btctl_remove_device`, BlueZ's RemoveDevice, which needs no link) and `btA2dpDirectionDelete` (its line in `/mnt/data/bta2dpfile`), so a device out of range is forgotten too, and `getSearchResult` refills `pdeq_btpairlist` from BlueZ without it. Stock leaves `BTLINKMAC` (`0xa4c0d8`, `[SYSSET] BTLINKMAC`) naming the device, which `autoLinkBluetooth` connects at boot and Bluetooth on ([Bluetooth boot reconnect](#bluetooth-boot-reconnect)) when `checkPairDev` finds it paired: `forget_link` clears it, in memory and in `config.ini`, when it names the forgotten device (any case), so nothing tries it again, and `btlim_forget` drops its Volume Limit and Volume Curve. ponytail: whether stock's list shows BlueZ's Alias (a rename) or the device's own Name is for a Q2 to say; `btctl_get_device_list`'s source is in `libbtctl.so`.

**Toasts.** `bt_ui_poll` looks at the link every 500 ms: a device connected now (the link list's last item at status 3) that was not toasts "name connected" with its kind's glyph, waiting up to 6 s for the device's Class and name (the connection's first battery run reads them) (`bt_headset_class`, `bt_headset_name`) so a car says "name connected · resuming" while Resume on Connect is on; one gone toasts "name disconnected", unless stock's own toast is up (a disconnect the user asked for: stock toasts Disconnected); a headset's level toasts "Headphones low · N%" once as it reaches 20% and once at 10% each connection. The name is the device's record in `pdeq_btshowlist` (filled while the Bluetooth page reads the devices), else BlueZ's `Alias` from the battery run, else "Bluetooth"; the drop's toast names the device the connection's did.

## Bluetooth receiver

When a phone plays to the Q2 over Bluetooth (the Q2 as an A2DP sink), stock opens `bluetoothrecv_page` (`btrecvA2dpFunc`'s stream start, then `on_wm_timer_dialog`'s `navigator_to`; `bluetoothrecv_page_init` stops the player and AirPlay and sets `bt__recv_pageflag` to 2): a 170 px Bluetooth picture, the phone's title and artist from AVRCP in plain labels (`btrecv_info_labels_update`, `0x4da594`, on the page's 500 ms timer), the codec as a picture (`img_btcode`, `btrecv_<codec>`), a back arrow and a gear that opens Audio settings. The wheel there is stock's volume.

`patch/bt_recv.c` draws it as a mode page ([oled-design](oled-design.md#usb), `mode_page_paint`, as USB Audio's): the accent's solid circle with Phosphor's `bluetooth-fill` (`MODE_GLYPHS` in `tools/art.py`, `modepage_receive`), the song's title over its artist, and the codec (LDAC, aptX HD, aptX, AAC or SBC, read off `img_btcode`'s picture) in the pill; before the phone names a song, "Playing from Phone" over "Wheel sets the volume". The status row reads Bluetooth. As the page loads (`bt_recv_load`, from `ringnav_ui_load`) the asset's sample title and artist ("Shaped by time,perfected in chime", "Shanling") are emptied, so a phone that sends none reads as none, and stock's picture, labels, codec and gear are hidden, each paint hiding them again; they stay for stock to fill. The back arrow stays at opacity 0 for stock's Return. ponytail: the gear goes with the rest, as it sat under the status row's battery; Audio settings are Settings > Playback.

## Headset battery

`bt_headset_battery()` (`patch/bt_battery.c`) is a connected headset's battery level, 0 to 100, or -1, for the status row's Bluetooth slot and Settings > Bluetooth; beside it `bt_headset_rate()` is the stream's sample rate, `bt_headset_class()` the device's Class of Device and `bt_headset_name()` its name (BlueZ's `Alias`), each 0 or empty when unknown. BlueZ shows a device's level as `org.bluez.Battery1`'s `Percentage` on the device's object (`/org/bluez/hci0/dev_AA_BB_...`). For an LE device its battery plugin reads the Battery Service. For a classic headset the level comes over HFP (`+IPHONEACCEV`, `+XAPL`), which `bluealsa` (BlueALSA with HFP-AG, `org.bluez.BatteryProvider1` among its strings) reads and hands to BlueZ through `org.bluez.BatteryProviderManager1`; BlueZ 5.66 offers that manager only with its experimental D-Bus interfaces on, which stock's `main.conf` leaves off (`#Experimental = false`), so the build sets `Experimental = true` (`BT_EXPERIMENTAL` in `tools/build.py`). demo has no D-Bus client of its own, so a shell asks with `dbus-send`, one answer a run (`batt_fetch`), started on a thread of its own and never on the UI thread (`bt_shell` in `patch/bt_ui.c`: `system()` forks demo): it writes `MAC PCT RATE CLASS NAME` (each empty for none, the name to the line's end) whole to `/tmp/q2-btbatt`, and the file is read once, as the run ends. The first call that finds a connected device (status 3) in stock's link list asks for all of it: the device's `Class` and `Alias`, `Percentage`, and the stream's rate (bluealsa's `org.bluealsa.Manager1.GetPCMs`, the `Sampling` of the device's `a2dpsrc` PCM). A level moves a percent in minutes and shows only on a lit screen (the status row, the Bluetooth page, the low toasts), so later runs ask for the level and rate alone, the Class and name kept, and only with the screen lit: 5 minutes after the last (`BATT_POLL_MS`), 30 s while no level came yet (BlueZ has it some seconds into a link, as the headset sends it; `BATT_RETRY_MS`, at most `BATT_TRIES` 10 times), and at once when the codec streaming changes, which moves the rate. Dark, nothing runs; a run still going is not started again. A device gone clears it, so its next connection is asked whole. Measured in `test/fw/test_bt_battery.py`: ten minutes connected start 18 programs lit and 11 dark; the test also runs both commands under `sh` with a stand-in `dbus-send`.

ponytail: unproven on a Q2. Whether this `bluealsa` registers its provider with `Experimental` on, whether it runs HFP-AG at all (its launcher, `bluealsa2`, names no `-p`, so its default profiles decide), and which headsets send a level are for a test on a Q2 with such a headset; with none of them a headset reads -1 and the slot shows no level, as before. `Experimental` also turns on BlueZ's other experimental D-Bus interfaces (Advertisement Monitor, the admin policy), which nothing on the Q2 calls. The rate's path (bluealsa's object path and its `GetPCMs` print, parsed with a `sed` range under BusyBox) is unproven on a Q2 too: `test/fw/test_bt_battery.py` runs the loop under a host `sh` and GNU `sed` with a stand-in reply; with no answer the rate reads 0 and the codec line leaves it out.

## Track metadata

A car or headset shows the playing song through AVRCP. `sendBtHeadsetPlayInfo` (`0x4fae8c`) sends the playing song and `sendBtHeadsetPlayStatus` (`0x4fae10`) its play status; they fill a record and hand it to libbtctl's `btctl_notify_track_changed` and `btctl_notify_playback_status_changed`, which call `NotifyChanged` on `shanling.bluez`, a D-Bus service Shanling's bluetoothd runs itself (`bluez_main`, from `libbtctl.so`). That service keeps the record in libbtctl's `g_track_meta` (`+0` track number, `+4` track count, `+8` playing time in ms, then pointers to title, artist, album and genre), the status in `g_play_status`, both under `g_notify_mutex`, and sends the TRACK_CHANGED or PLAYBACK_STATUS_CHANGED notification a controller registered for. Stock's track change (`player_mainscheduling`) sends the play status for every song but the song itself only for an online one (after `get_onlineid3info`, `0x51fb70` and `0x51fc2c`); its other callers are `on_wm_timer_dialog`'s missing-file and not-supported dialogs. So a card file's song (the Library's, Up Next's, a card app's stream download) never reached the record, and a car showed no title or artist for any of them (a BMW, the drive of 2026-11-19). `ringnav_id3_path` (`tags.c`, at every parse of the playing song, `ID3_PATH`) calls `sendBtHeadsetPlayInfo` once the parsed tags, a card app's included (`card_tags`), and the path are in `g_play_id3_info`, which it reads; an online song is sent again after its own tags, as stock does. A song sent on to the Q2 from elsewhere reaches a car the same way once it is in that record.

What a controller reads back depends on the channel. Shanling's browsing-channel handlers (GetItemAttributes on the playing item) answer from `g_track_meta`, and GetPlayStatus takes its status from `g_play_status`. The control channel's GetElementAttributes, which most headsets and cars use (an Echo, a BMW's iDrive), was upstream BlueZ's in stock: it reads a player registered with `org.bluez.Media1.RegisterPlayer`, stock registers none, so it rejected every request and those controllers showed no song.

The build answers it from `g_track_meta` too (`patch_bluetoothd` in `tools/build.py`): `tools/bt_meta.c`, compiled and appended to stock's bluetoothd as a read-and-execute segment at `BT_META`, takes GetElementAttributes's place in stock's control handler table (`BT_META_SLOT`, the word after PDU `0x20`'s, `0x39454` in stock). bluetoothd is position independent, so the table word carries an `R_MIPS_REL32` that the loader adds the load address to, and `bt_meta.c` is position independent by construction (each entry one function with everything inlined, no data or constants; `bt_meta()` refuses an object with a relocation other than its branches'). It reaches `g_track_meta`, `g_notify_mutex` and pthread's lock and unlock through bluetoothd's own GOT slots at the caller's `$gp` (`BT_META_GOT`), and calls pthread with `$t9` and that `$gp` set, as a lazily bound PLT stub needs. Under the mutex it answers the attributes asked for, in order, once each, or all seven (title, artist, album, track number, track count, genre, playing time in ms; numbers in decimal, UTF-8) when none are (an eighth, the cover's image handle, only for a controller that fetches covers: [cover art](#bluetooth-cover-art)), leaving out a missing text or a number below 0; with no track, a one-space title, or the asked-for attributes empty. It answers in one packet: a text that would pass `BT_META_ROOM` (502 bytes of parameters, BlueZ's `AVRCP_PDU_MTU`) is cut at a character's start. A request under 9 bytes, shorter than its attribute count says, or naming no valid attribute is rejected (INVALID_PARAM), as upstream's is. `test/unit/test_bt_meta.py` runs it under Unicorn at a load address of its own; `test/bluetoothd.py BUILD` loads the built bluetoothd at another, applies the table word's relocation and calls GetElementAttributes through it, and checks stock's handler rejects the same request. ponytail: Shanling's other handlers are unchanged, so the browsing channel's GetItemAttributes still ignores which attributes were asked for, and a title past one packet is cut where upstream would continue it; the rebuilt bluetoothd ([third-party](third-party.md#not-replaced)) lifts both.

GetPlayStatus (PDU `0x30`, table word `BT_PLAY_SLOT`, `0x12f6d0`) was upstream's too, and with no registered player it answered every song as length `0xFFFFFFFF` at position 0 (`test/bluetoothd.py` runs stock's handler and shows it), so a car never learnt where a song was and ran its own clock from the track change, on through a pause or a radio. `bt_meta.c`'s `bt_meta_get_play_status` takes that word: it reads `/tmp/q2-bt.play` (`BT_PLAY_FILE`), "position length stamp" in ms written by demo's [Now Playing source](#now-playing-source) (`-1` for none: a stream has neither), the stamp on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, and answers the length, the position plus the time since the stamp while `g_play_status` says playing (never past the length), and `g_play_status` as the status. With no file, or one that does not parse, it answers the record's length and no position (`0xFFFFFFFF`). Stock's bluetoothd offers no PLAYBACK_POS_CHANGED, so a controller polls GetPlayStatus; `test/unit/test_bt_meta.py` covers the answer, `test/bluetoothd.py BUILD` calls it through the built table word.

On a Q2, to confirm: with an Echo paired to the Q2 and playing from it, "Alexa, what's playing?" (or the Alexa app's Now Playing) names the song, and changes at the next song; in a BMW with iDrive 7 the media screen shows title, artist and album and follows Next and a pause; a song with a title over 400 bytes shows cut, not garbled. And unchanged: AirPods' and a car's Play, Pause and skips, Control Device Volume, receiver mode.
## Now Playing source

`patch/now_source.c` is the one answer to what plays, for every reader. `now_owner` says who owns playback: Radio while its receiver runs (its page open or shut, until the Library is chosen again), else `headset.c` `media_owner`'s order, a video, Internet Radio, Spotify, else the Library; `now_status` that owner's play state (0 stopped, 1 playing, 2 paused, AVRCP's and iAP2's order), cheap enough for a paint. For the Library, `now_song` is the song Now Playing shows (a pressed server song from the press on, `catalogue_np_now`, else the queue's at `MCL_POS`, `queue_now`) and `now_time` its second, length and play state (`player_playtime_and_length`, `mclGetPlayStatus`). `now_get` fills a `now_info` (navigation.h) with all of it: the owner, the words (title, artist, album, station), the state, the position and length in ms (-1 none) and, for the Library, the record, its id, path and place in the queue. A station's StreamTitle is taken apart by `tuner_song` (iHeart's `title="..",artist="..",url=".."` pairs, or "Artist - Title", all capitals made title case as the tuner shows them): its song the title, its artist the artist, the station and the frequency ("93XRT 93.1 FM") the album; with no song yet the station is the title and the frequency the artist. Spotify's track comes from `spotify.c` `spot_now`, with its position and length; a video is "Video". `now_scrobbles` is the one rule for scrobbling: the Library's songs alone (the card's files and the server songs card apps stream, less a card app's own `scrobble=0`), never a radio, Spotify or a video.

**The Library held for Radio, Internet Radio and videos.** Radio's page opening (`radio_tuner.c` `tuner_open`), an Internet Radio station starting (`radio.c` `radio_play`), a video starting (`videos.c` `video_play`) and a card game with the sound starting (`addon.c` `addon_game_start`) call `now_hold`: a Library song playing or paused is stopped with its place kept (`player_save_stop`, as Guest Play stops it), since a paused q2player keeps the PCM they need and stock's `player_stop`, which `video_start` calls, forgets the place. For as long as one of them has the output, and through a hand-over from one to another (a video started over a station), `now_time` reads that song paused at that second, so no reader's position for it moves. That includes Now Playing's own bar and elapsed time: stock's page update (`playing_page_update`, `0x53cf08`) writes 0 to both when `mclGetPlayStatus` says stopped, which the held player is, so its call there and its call of `player_playtime_and_length` go through `now_page_status` and `now_page_time` (`NP_TIME_CALLS` in `tools/build.py`), which answer the held song paused at its second and are otherwise stock's two calls. A song loaded paused at a place (a boot resume through `mclSetStartSeekTime`, `now_release`'s `player_save_start(1)`, an output change) reads 0 from q2player until it is heard, as from stock's player, and `resume_poll` counts on that; so `ringnav_start_player` has `now_starting` note the place before stock's `mclStartPlayer` reads and clears it (`MCL_START_SEC`, `0xa50064`, in the file's seconds, less a CUE track's start), and `now_time` and `now_page_time` read that place for the same song while it is paused and unheard, the player's own second from its first heard one, or for another song. Radio's page shut leaves it held, Radio playing on ([Radio (Home)](#radio-home)), and so does a station stopped or left, Internet Radio staying the owner. The Library chosen again ends the hold: Play on its own Now Playing (`playing_page`) plays the song on from that place (`now_take_back`, from `radio_tuner.c` `tuner_key` or `radio.c` `radio_take_back`, ahead of the station's own Play), and any start of its player, a pick among them, plays from the player's own place (`now_drop`, in `ringnav_start_player`, so a Library song the user started is never paused over). A Radio page that found no stations, shut, and a video's or a sound game's end (`video_poll`, `game_poll`, or one that did not start) have `now_release` load it again paused there (`player_save_start(1)`) for the user's Play: never playing on its own, never back at 0. A Library that was stopped is left as it is.

| Reader | What it reads |
| --- | --- |
| Bluetooth: bluetoothd's record and status (`now_poll`, every UI pass) | `now_get`: another owner's words as libbtctl's track record (`btctl_notify_track_changed`; no track number or count, its length only for Spotify) and its status (`btctl_notify_playback_status_changed`), the Library song's cover set aside (`bt_cover_hold`); the Library's song and status again after it (`sendBtHeadsetPlayInfo`, `sendBtHeadsetPlayStatus`), as Guest Play hands back. A Library song's own words and status reach bluetoothd as stock and `tags.c` send them. Nothing while Guest Play relays a guest's song. |
| Bluetooth: GetPlayStatus | `/tmp/q2-bt.play`, from `now_get` ([track metadata](#track-metadata)): written when the item, the state or the length changes, at the first new second after a write (so the stamp is a second's start), and when the position is 1.5 s (`NP_DRIFT_MS`) from where the time since put it (a seek); not every second |
| The car's cable (`q2-iap` `NowPlayingUpdate`) and Car Remote (`coda-rc`) | `coda_rc_shim.c` `cr_now`'s `/tmp/coda-rc.now`, from `now_get`: `source=` the owner, a radio `live=1` with `station=` and no length or position, another owner no hearts and no path ([iphone-mode](iphone-mode.md#car-audio-buttons-and-cover-m3-m2-and-the-cover-from-m6)) |
| Home's first row (`home_np.c`), the status row's play glyph (`lyrics_status_bar.c` `bar_status`) | `now_status` |
| Control Center (`control_center.c`) | `now_status` for the Play glyph and whether anything is loaded; the Library's song by `now_song`, another owner's words by `now_get`, with no cover |
| Now Playing (`np_bar.c`, `nav/now_playing.c`) and lyrics (`lyrics.c`) | `now_song` and `now_time`: these pages show the Library alone |
| Scrobbling (`nav/playback_power.c` `scrobble`) | `now_scrobbles` |
| Up Next (`upnext.c`) | the queue itself (`queue_now`), which is what it lists; `now_song` falls back on the same function |

Before it, Radio streamed while the car (over Bluetooth, the cable and Car Remote) was still told the Library's song and its cover and, over Bluetooth, no position at all; Control Center and the status row showed nothing playing; and the Library's song was stopped, not held where it was. `test/fw/test_now_source.py` covers the owner as it moves (the Library playing, paused, sought, the next song; Radio over it and the Library held paused through it; the Library back paused where it was; Radio left playing and found again where it was, its last station across a restart; the status glyph and Home's row through Radio playing, between stations, paused, its page left, the car's Play and a Library pick) and each reader's view.

## Bluetooth cover art

A car that speaks AVRCP 1.6 shows the playing song's cover: the target names it by an image handle, seven digits, in attribute 8 of the song's attributes, and the controller fetches the picture from the target's BIP imaging responder, OBEX on an L2CAP channel of its own that the target's SDP record names. Three parts make that, and nothing moves for a headset or car that does not ask.

**The handle, from demo.** Where the payload hands a new song's tags to bluetoothd (`tags.c` `ringnav_id3_path`), `bt_cover.c` `bt_cover_note` first writes `/tmp/q2-bip.now` (`BT_COVER_FILE`): the handle, the cover's path, where it came from (`coverflow`, `app`, `folder` or `own`) and the song's path, a line each; a song with no cover removes it. The cover is the first there of: Cover Flow's cached copy for the song's artist and album (`art_path(tags_key(artist, album))`), not its empty "no art" marker; for a server song, the cover its app keeps (`catalogue.c` `catalogue_cover`, `/mnt/mmc/.<app>/covers/<album id>.jpg`, what Now Playing shows); `cover.jpg`, `folder.jpg` or `front.jpg` beside the song, as iPhone mode looks ([iphone-mode](iphone-mode.md#car-audio-buttons-and-cover-m3-m2-and-the-cover-from-m6)); and the song's own picture (`bt_own_picture`, headers only read, each block, frame or box skipped by its length: a FLAC's PICTURE block, an ID3v2 tag's `APIC` frame, `PIC` in 2.2, or an MP4's `moov/udta/meta/ilst/covr`, the `moov` before or after the audio), named by the song's own path, which `q2-bip`'s ffmpeg takes the attached picture of (checked with this machine's ffmpeg on a FLAC, an MP3 and an M4A, each with its picture embedded by ffmpeg). The handle is the cover file's key modulo 10^7 (Cover Flow's key, the same hash of the path for an app's cover or one beside the song, and the album's key, else the path's, for a song's own picture), so it changes exactly when the cover does and the songs of an album share it: a car that has the album's cover fetches nothing at the next song. The last two were missing on the drive of 2026-11-22 (build 1126): the songs streamed from Subsonic's cache, and only the first, Brown Sugar, had a Cover Flow copy (`/mnt/mmc/.coverflow/0e8eef28.jpg`); Pure Heroine and Trillmatic had neither a copy nor an app cover (`covers/6CyQiQAdxCv0Iqb3bYuhmQ.jpg` and `494wAdHZSWEKU2uvIWhO2X.jpg` absent), only the picture in each FLAC, so the file was removed at each later song, attribute 8 left out, and the BMW went on showing Brown Sugar's cover. It is written beside and renamed over, so a reader sees a whole file. While Guest Play relays a guest's song the owner's file is set aside (`bt_cover_hold`, from `guest.c`), as the car is told of the guest's songs then. A song with no cover at all is answered with attribute 8 empty (below), not left out. ponytail: an Ogg's or Opus's own picture (`METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE` in its comments) is not looked for. Nothing tells a controller to ask again when its OBEX session comes up: one that read the song's attributes before it connected to `q2-bip` already has the handle, and whether the BMW fetches then or at the next song is for the car to show.

**Attribute 8, in bluetoothd.** `tools/bt_meta.c` ([track metadata](#track-metadata)) reads the controller's own SDP record as bluetoothd cached it at connect (`session->target->features`, `+0xc` then `+8` in stock's `struct avrcp`): only when it has one of AVRCP 1.6's controller bits for cover art (`0x380`: GetImageProperties, GetImage, GetLinkedThumbnail) is 8 an attribute at all. For such a controller a request for all attributes, or for 8, opens the file read-only (libc's `open`, `read`, `close` through bluetoothd's GOT, before `g_notify_mutex` is taken), and seven digits there are the attribute; anything else (no file, a song with no cover) answers 8 with no value. AVRCP 1.6.2 has GetElementAttributes with no attributes named return "all attribute information" (6.6.1), and an attribute's value may be 0 bytes long, the value then absent (table 6.27); browsing's GetItemAttributes may leave out a value it cannot determine (6.10.4.3.2); none of it says what a controller does with the cover it showed before. Android's target leaves 8 out for a song with no artwork (`com_android_bluetooth_avrcp_target.cpp`, the handle added only when not empty), which is what the Q2 did until 1128 and what the BMW answered by showing the first song's cover for every later one on 2026-11-22; the empty value says outright that this song has none. ponytail: what the BMW does with an empty 8 is not yet seen. For every other controller the answer is byte for byte what it was, the file is never opened, and a request for 8 alone is INVALID_PARAM as before.

**The record.** A controller looks for cover art in the target's SDP record: profile version 0x0106, bit 8 of SupportedFeatures, and in AdditionalProtocolDescriptorLists a second entry after browsing's, L2CAP with the responder's PSM, then OBEX. Stock builds the record inline in its adapter probe (`0x39e..` to `0x3a220`), so `patch_bluetoothd` changes three words there (`BT_SDP_WORDS`: the version's `addiu`, the features `ori` on the browsing path, and the `bal` to stock's helper at `0x383b8`, which adds browsing's entry) and sends that call to `bt_meta.c`'s `bt_cover_sdp`, which adds both entries with bluetoothd's own `sdp_uuid16_create`, `sdp_list_append`, `sdp_data_alloc` and `sdp_set_add_access_protos` (local GOT entries, `BT_SDP_GOT`) and frees what it built as the helper does. The appended code is out of a `bal`'s reach, so the call goes to `BT_SDP_JUMP`, five words laid over stock's own GetElementAttributes (dead since `BT_META_SLOT` took its table word): `$t9 = $gp + (bt_cover_sdp - BT_GP)`, `jr $t9`, with `$ra` the caller's. The record is one for every device, so every headset now reads AVRCP 1.6 where it read 1.5; only the handle is per controller. ponytail: the entries are added on stock's browsing path alone (a byte at `+4` of its server record, whose setter was not traced), which is where stock adds any additional protocol: a Q2 whose record shows no browsing entry today would gain the version alone.

**The responder, `q2-bip`** (`patch/q2bip.c`, `q2bip_core.c`, `q2bip.h`), a process of its own so that nothing reading a car's bytes runs inside bluetoothd. `bluealsa2`, stock's Bluetooth launcher, starts it in the background (`BT_COVER_START`) and it ends with that script (`PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`), which ends when Bluetooth goes off. It listens on PSM `0x1025` (`BIP_PSM`, `BT_COVER_PSM`) in Enhanced Retransmission Mode, which OBEX over L2CAP requires, at BlueZ's medium security (an encrypted link, so a paired device), and serves one controller at a time, asleep in `accept` or `recv` otherwise. `q2bip_core.c` is OBEX and BIP: CONNECT for AVRCP's cover art target (UUID `7163DD54-4A7E-11E2-B47C-0050C2490048`, answered with a connection id and Who; any other target Not Acceptable), GET of `x-bt/img-properties` (the XML: one native version, JPEG, 200*200, its size), `x-bt/img-img` (an image descriptor that a 200 x 200 JPEG does not meet is Not Acceptable) and `x-bt/img-thm`, DISCONNECT and ABORT; a handle that is not the playing song's is Not Found, anything else Not Implemented. The one picture served is AVRCP's thumbnail, a 200 x 200 JPEG: at the first GET for a handle `q2-bip` runs stock's `ffmpeg` once on the file demo named (fitted, centred on black, 4:2:2, niced to 19, killed after 10 s), keeps the result in memory until another song's is made, and leaves nothing in `/tmp`. So a cover costs one ffmpeg run per album a car actually fetches, none at a track change and none for a headset.

**Beside the audio.** The A2DP stream and this channel share the controller's five 1021-byte ACL buffers ([link monitor](#bluetooth-link-monitor)). OBEX's Single Response Mode, in which a responder sends a whole object unasked, is never agreed to: `q2-bip` passes over the SRM header, which OBEX defines as off, so each packet of a cover waits for the car's next GET. And no OBEX packet is larger than `BIP_PKT` (1000 bytes, the L2CAP MTU it asks for too), so with its headers a packet is one ACL buffer: a cover never holds more than one of the five, about eleven round trips for a 10 KB picture. ERTM itself adds nothing to the air but its acknowledgements.

**The log.** `q2-bip` writes one line of the [unified log](#unified-log) to its stderr (demo's stderr file, which q2guard reads, so it reaches the [Bluetooth event log](#bluetooth-event-log) too) for each GET of a cover: `cover 6136261 thumbnail for /mnt/mmc/.subsonic/stream/.../ribs [...].flac from own: 7000 bytes in 412 ms, made`, the handle, what was asked (`properties`, `image` or `thumbnail`), the song and the cover's source from the file's last two lines (`?` in a file without them), the bytes, the time and the outcome: `made` (ffmpeg ran), `kept` (made before for this handle), or a `W` line with 0 bytes for `not the playing song's`, `ffmpeg failed` or `no JPEG from ffmpeg`.

Tested on this machine: `test/unit/test_q2bip.py` (OBEX and BIP: the packets written out from the specifications' values, multi-packet bodies with Continue and Success, the peer's packet size, SRM passed over, handles changing, malformed requests), `test/q2bip.py` (the process over a UNIX packet socket with a stand-in ffmpeg, then a real one whose JPEG must be 200 x 200 and 4:2:2, and the real L2CAP socket's PSM, mode and security on a kernel with Bluetooth), `test/unit/test_bt_meta.py` (attribute 8 with and without the controller's bits under Unicorn, the record's lists, the jump), `test/bluetoothd.py BUILD` (the patched binary's record call run through the jump against bluetoothd's own SDP code: the attribute's bytes are browsing's then cover art's, and stock's the same call browsing alone) and `test/fw/test_bt_cover.py` (the file). Not tested: any controller. No car's SDP record has been read, ERTM on the Q2's kernel and the ffmpeg run's time on the Q2 are unmeasured.

On a Q2, to confirm: from a laptop, `sdptool browse <the Q2's address>` shows A/V Remote Control Target at version 0x0106 with a second additional protocol list (L2CAP PSM 0x1025, OBEX); in the car the media screen shows the album's cover within a second or two of a song starting, changes at the next album and not within one, and shows none for a song without a cover; `ps` shows one `q2-bip` while Bluetooth is on and none after it is turned off. And unchanged: every headset's track info, buttons and volume, and no drop in the q2-bt log's stream while a cover is fetched.

## Clock

The timezone picker keeps stock's saved indices (`g_time_zone`, 0-26) and appends the missing offsets and a few populous zones. The last, `GMT+0 UTC`, is a new install's zone ([Automatic time zone](#automatic-time-zone)). `TIMEZONES` in `tools/build.py` holds every index's label and `TZ`. `toolsSetTimeZone` (`0x5cf024`) is only `setenv("TZ", name, 1)`, and `ringnav_timezone` replaces stock's mapping (`select_timezone`, `0x503b40`) for every index, so glibc resolves an IANA name under `/usr/share/zoneinfo` or, failing that, reads a POSIX rule. The rootfs tzdata is older than 2022, so Mexico City (`CST6`), Tehran (`<+0330>-3:30`) and Fiji (`<+12>-12`) take POSIX rules without the daylight saving they have since dropped. Stock's GMT-12 row set Pacific/Kwajalein, which is +12, so it is `<-12>12` now. Its +6 Almaty row is Asia/Dhaka, since Almaty is +5 from 2024 and the rootfs still says +6. `tools/build.py` writes the labels as literal text (no `strings/*.bin` key, so every language shows them as written) into the existing label table at `0x77efb0`, compacted to 32-byte slots, and extends the row counts and boot validation. The page's row builder (`0x4c1aac`, `(item, i)`; row 0 is the switch) labels, names (`atoi` in the click handler, less one, is the saved index) and ticks a row by the index it is given. As row 1 is built, `ringnav_timezone_row` sets each zone's `TZ` in turn and reads its offset from UTC now (`localtime_r`'s `tm_gmtoff`), then sets the saved zone again; row 1 is handed the saved zone, pinned at the top with stock's check, and the rows after it the other zones west to east by that offset (ties in `TIMEZONE_ORDER`, by city), each plus one. A row is a key/value row (`list_value`): the city (`TIMEZONE_CITIES`) as its key and the offset it has now as its value in Text Secondary on the right column, so New York reads `UTC-4` in summer and `UTC-5` in winter, as its clocks do; the checked row's value ends 24 px short (`TZ_CHECK_GAP`), clear of the check. A zone list sorted by offset has no letter order, so it has no A-Z strip; at 44 rows the wheel crosses it in a few turns. Labelled by standard offset, a New Yorker in summer took GMT-4 Halifax, an hour ahead. ponytail: another thread's `localtime` while row 1 builds may read one of the other zones, as `TZ` is process-wide. Stock's `set_hscroll_label_attribute` scrolls every too-long label once as the page opens; the hook makes the row's label focus-only, so one that does not fit keeps its ellipsis. The table's labels, with the standard offset, are sized to fit stock's 246 px label at 24 px; the rows show the city and the offset in effect. ponytail: the rules are fixed in the build and the rootfs tzdata stays as it is, so a zone that changes its rules later needs a new row or rule here.

Stock loses the time zone across a power-off. Setting the time, by hand or from the network (`toolsSetRtcTime`, `0x5cf290`), runs `date -s` and then `hwclock -w`. BusyBox's `hwclock` writes local time unless `/var/lib/hwclock/adjtime` says `UTC`, and the rootfs has no such file, so the RTC gets the wall time of the `TZ` the player exported (`toolsSetTimeZone`). At boot the kernel (`hctosys`) reads the RTC as UTC and the player adds the time zone again, so the clock comes back off by the zone's UTC offset until the next network sync. The build changes the literal at `0x78bc28`, `hwclock -w` and two NULs, to `hwclock -wu`, so the RTC holds UTC as the kernel expects. An RTC last written by stock still holds local time, so the time has to be set once after updating.

The network time (`networktime_adjust_thd`, with Wi-Fi up and Set Time Automatically on) runs `ntpdate` against a list of servers that names `time.apple.com`, `time.windows.com` and `cn.pool.ntp.org` (`0x7836bc`). The build writes `0.pool.ntp.org` and a second NUL over that one (`NTP_POOL`, `tools/build.py`), the worldwide pool, the same length, so the Q2 asks no China-only server.

The status bar, Auto Light Mode and timezone picker use `localtime_r` with their own `struct tm` buffers. Stock's background time conversions can overwrite `localtime`'s shared buffer while the UI reads it, briefly displaying another time. The status bar's clock and Auto Light Mode read the time once a minute: `clock_show` writes the label, applies Auto's hour and sets a timer for the next minute, and runs at once for a new zone (`ringnav_timezone`), a time set by hand (`time_click`) and a wake, and on the pass after the bar first paints or paints with a new 24-hour setting. Before, every paint of the bar or the top window read the time, and Auto Light Mode's check read it on every UI pass (125 a second). ponytail: a network time sync while lit shows at the next minute. The payload resolves demo's imported `tzset` once (it writes no shared buffer), then calls the pinned libc's `localtime_r` at its checked offset from it. Timezone changes explicitly call `tzset`, since `localtime_r` does not reload `TZ` itself.

## Automatic time zone

**Settings → General → Date & Time → Automatic Time Set → Automatic Time Zone** (`Q2POD AUTOZONE`, on unless the key says 0; `patch/autozone.c`) sets the time zone from the network's location, as a phone does. Its switch row sits under stock's Automatic Time Set switch, above the zone list: `ringnav_timezone_row`, as it builds the last zone row, adds it through `pod_row_at` (a `pod_rows` switch, restacked to the list's second child), captioned "Sets the zone from your network's location".

**When.** `autozone_poll`, from `power_poll` once a second, starts a lookup on its own pthread with the switch on, the link up (the status bar's bars, `get_wifisignal`, and stock's `networkGetConnectStatus`) and not in test mode, when no lookup ran since boot, the last one set a zone 24 hours ago (`AZ_DAY_MS`), the last one failed and the link has just come up at least 10 minutes on (`AZ_RETRY_MS`), or the switch was just turned on (`autozone_due`). With the switch off nothing is sent. A lookup running keeps Smart Wi-Fi's radio on (`autozone_busy` in `smart_needed`). ponytail: the day is counted from boot, so a restart looks up again at the next link.

**The lookup.** `GET https://ipinfo.io/timezone`, then `https://ipapi.co/timezone/` if that fails: each answers with the caller's IANA zone as plain text (`America/Chicago`), over HTTPS, with no key. ipinfo.io is free to 50,000 lookups a month without a token, ipapi.co to 1,000 a day. Their certificates chain to ISRG Root X1 and GTS Root R4, both in `/etc/scrobble-ca.pem`; the peer and host are verified. ip-api.com was left out (HTTPS only with a key), as was worldtimeapi.org (long outages). Each try has a 5 s connect and 10 s total timeout, an answer of 64 bytes or more is cut off, and one that is not a plain zone name (letters, digits, `_ + - /`, starting with a letter: nothing that could leave `/usr/share/zoneinfo` or read as a POSIX rule) counts as a failure. The service sees the network's public address; nothing else is sent (the user agent is `Q2Muse`).

**The match.** `autozone_match`, on the UI thread once the thread is joined (`TZ` is process-wide): the zone's own `TIMEZONES` entry if it has one (America/Chicago is index 38); else, if `/usr/share/zoneinfo/<name>` exists (glibc reads an unknown name as UTC), the entry whose offset from UTC now is the zone's and which agrees with it at the most of 24 times spread over the next year, each read with that zone's `TZ` through `localtime_r` (`tm_gmtoff`), so the closest daylight saving wins: America/Winnipeg takes Chicago (not Mexico City's `CST6`), Europe/Paris Amsterdam, Africa/Abidjan UTC (not London), America/Regina `CST6`. No entry with the offset now, or no such zone: the zone stays. The saved zone's `TZ` is set again after.

**Applying it.** As the zone page's pick: `g_time_zone`, then `ringnav_timezone` (demo's `TZ`, so every program demo starts from then on, and the status bar's clock at once), then `write_int_config(i, "SYSSET", "TIMEZONE")`. `/etc/localtime` is the rootfs's, Etc/UTC, read-only; only a shell not started by demo (adb's) reads it. ponytail: the zone page, if open as the lookup lands, shows its check on the old row until it opens again. A zone picked by hand on that page turns the switch off (`autozone_config`, from `toolsWriteConfig`'s hook, for a `SYSSET TIMEZONE` write that is not the lookup's own while `autotime_page` is on top), so the next lookup does not undo it.

**The default.** Stock's `config.ini` says `TIMEZONE=22`, Asia/Shanghai, and the first-boot copy (`DEFAULTS_MARK`) put it on every new Q2, which showed China time (CST, +8) until the user chose a zone. `default_config` writes `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` instead, a `GMT+0 UTC` entry appended to `TIMEZONES` (index 43): UTC with the network's time is the true time with no claim about where the Q2 is, until the lookup sets the real zone; an "unset" value would read as Shanghai again (`config_init` takes anything out of range as 22). A Q2 that already has a `config.ini` keeps its zone, which the lookup replaces while the switch is on.

`test/fw/test_autozone.py`: the match (each listed zone its own, Winnipeg, Paris, Dublin, Toronto, Abidjan, Regina and Singapore to theirs, a name that is not a zone to nothing), Chicago from the fake service set and saved, the fallback, each failure keeping the zone, the switch off or no link sending nothing, once a day, a retry at a new link, the switch's default and the shipped default.

## Screen off and wake

Q2 Muse has no lock screen: waking the screen shows the page that was showing when it went off. Stock's lock window (`saverscreen_page.bin`) opens from two places only, the Center release that lights a dark screen (`on_wm_keyup_fun`, `0x4f31b0`) and the resume from Standby (`device_standby`, `0x502490`), and each only while `g_screensaver_mode` is set (`SYSSET SCREENSAVER` 1) and no lock window is open (`g_lockscreen_pageflag`). `config_init` stores the key's 0 or 1 there (`sb $2` at `0x504c78`); the build makes it store 0 (`SAVER_OFF`, `sb $zero`), whatever the file says, so neither path opens the window and both light the screen as stock does without one. A lock screen saved on, by stock or by an earlier Q2 Muse, is saved off once at boot (`ringnav_bootmode`, before `config_init` reads the key), so a downgrade comes up with it off too. The only way to turn it on, **System settings → Display → Lock Screen**, goes: `ringnav_display` destroys that stock row, as it does Show Navigation Bar. With nothing able to open them, the lock window, its settings page (`screensaver_page.bin`), that page's About and the images only they and the row show (`screensaver_default`, the `scrsaver_*` set, `display_screenlock`) are left out of the rootfs (`STOCK_PAGES` in `tools/build.py`). `SYSSET SCREENSAVERPATH` and `Q2POD LOCKCLOCK`, the picture and the Large clock of earlier versions, stay in `config.ini` and nothing reads them.

Dark, the wheel does nothing, under either Wake setting: `wheel_lock_gate` drops its ticks before the wake gate ([Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)), so a turn in a pocket changes no volume, moves no list, makes no click and leaves the screen off. Under Any Button every button lights the screen, Play/Pause, Previous and Next acting too; under Double Press only Center does, the media buttons act dark and Return is dropped ([Wake](#wake)).

**A double tap on the dark screen wakes it; on a lit one it does nothing of its own.** The double tap is the touch controller's gesture, not the firmware's. Stock's `screen_action` (`0x501f64`) calls `double_onclick_wake` (`0x501ef0`), which writes `echo %d > /sys/hynitron_debug/hyngescontrol`: 1 as the screen goes off, 0 as it comes on (the driver logs `===fun[hyn_gescontrol_store]===ges_state[0]==ges_control[0]==` at each wake). With it on, the controller reports only gestures, and `hyn_touch.ko`'s `hyn_gesture_report` sends a double tap as `KEY_POWER` (116) on `hyn_ts`, the code Center sends, so it reaches the payload as one Center press in the dark, under [Wake](#wake)'s rules (read from the stock binary and driver, not yet watched on a device). With the screen lit the gesture is off and a double tap is two ordinary taps, each its target's (two on Now Playing's heart like and unlike). Nothing turns a lit screen off on a double tap: on Now Playing that is Center held `NP_HOLD_MS` (`patch/nav/now_playing.c`), elsewhere Center's double press.

## Night Shift

**System settings → Display → Night Shift**, after Smart Awake on the main page (`ringnav_display`, stock's `display_backlight` icon; `patch/nightshift.c`), warms the screen as f.lux does: red is kept and green and blue are scaled to a color temperature, from Tanner Helland's fit to the black-body colors (`ns_green`, `ns_blue`, a pair each 100K from 2000K to 5000K). It reads `Night Shift: Off`, `Night Shift: 3400K` or `Night Shift: Auto` (`Q2POD NIGHTSHIFT`, 0 Off, 1 On, 2 Auto, and `NIGHTK`, a hundred in 2000-5000, else 3400, in `config.ini`). The row opens [Crossfade](#crossfade)'s re-dressed Boot volume page (`xfade_open` context 3): titled Night Shift, the switch and Center cycling Off, On and Auto as Light Mode's row does, the slider 5000K at its left to 2000K at its right, +/- and the wheel 100K a step; a move while it is off turns it on, and one in Auto keeps Auto. **Auto** warms the screen from 19:00 to 06:59 by the device clock, the hours [Light Mode](ipod.md#light-mode)'s Auto is dark (`clock_night`, `patch/theme_engine.c`): roughly the year's average sunset and sunrise on the clock, as daylight saving and most time zones run the clock ahead of the sun. It is off while the clock cannot be read. `clock_show` hands the hour to `night_clock` each minute with the status bar's clock, and a crossing repaints as a change on the page does; at boot the hour is read with the setting. Each change shows at once (`night_set`), a drag's every step too, and is saved as the page saves the rest (`night_save` from `refresh`: at a drag's release, else at once); the row's label (`label_night`) follows.

**Tint.** AWTK draws each frame into the screen's `lcd_mem` buffer (`LCD_OFFLINE_FB`, BGRA8888, `LCD_FORMAT` 3) and `lcd_end_frame` (`0x65aec8`) then calls the lcd's `end_frame` (`LCD_END_FRAME`), which hands the frame to the flush thread that turns it onto `/dev/fb0`. While Night Shift is on, that pointer is `night_end`: before calling stock's, it warms the pixels drawn in the frame and sets their alpha to `0xf7` (`NS_DONE`), which the panel ignores. A pixel already at `0xf7` is skipped, so nothing is warmed twice. `NS_DONE` has to be an alpha stock never leaves on a pixel it draws, and `0xf5`-`0xf8` are the only ones for the lcd's own drawing: its fills (`fill_bgra8888_rect`, `0x6df4f4`) and image blends (the pixel at `0x6c8520` for an RGBA image, `0x6c5140` for a BGRA one, scaled and rotated draws too) copy a source pixel with its own alpha only above `0xf8`, and blend any fainter one, which over a pixel whose alpha is at least `0xf5` writes `0xff`; a glyph writes `0xff` either way (`0x6a5c34`), and `image_copy` is only used for an image whose every alpha is `0xff` (`rgba_data_is_opaque`, `0x642cb8`). So a pixel drawn again in a later frame comes back above `0xf8` and is warmed once more. The mark was `0xfe` at first, an alpha the antialiased rim of most icons has (28 pixels of each round 40 px settings icon, 6,979 pixels over 306 of the shipped images): those were copied with it and never warmed, bright specks round a warmed icon. Limits left: vgcanvas (`agge::pixel_blend`, `0x73b0f4`) writes a coverage above `0xf4` as the pixel's alpha and `clear_rect` its color's, so an edge pixel of a vgcanvas shape or image at exactly `0xf7` stays unwarmed (`0xf7` is the rarest of the four in the shipped images, and no color of Q2 Muse's has it), and a vgcanvas blend leaves the alpha of the pixel under it, so one over a pixel not drawn again that frame would stay a mix; none has been seen, as AWTK repaints a dirty rect from the window's background up (inferred from its dirty-rect painting, not traced through stock). Only the frame's bounding rect (`LCD_DIRTY`, `dirty_rects->max`, which `lcd_begin_frame` sets, `0x65a818`) is scanned: stock calls `tk_init` at 320 x 375 and turns the lcd to 270 without fast portrait, so `lcd_mem_resize` gives it a 375 x 320 buffer (`LCD_LINE_LENGTH` = 4 x `LCD_W`) that the flush thread rotates onto `/dev/fb0`; any other layout is left as drawn. Stock paints each dirty rect apart, so the pixels between them are already warm and cost a test each. A window's snapshot for its animation is drawn on `canvas_offline`'s own lcd, so it reaches the screen as an image and is warmed when shown. The scan costs about 9 instructions for a pixel already warm and 20 for a new one, so only the drawn rect matters: a full-screen redraw is about 2-3 ms, a progress bar's tick a few rows. Nothing paints with the screen off. Videos draw on `/dev/fb0` themselves (`q2video`), so they show untinted.

**On and off.** `night_paint`, from `ringnav_paint` after stock paints each widget, gives the lcd `night_end` once Night Shift is on, or in Auto's hours: the first paint after On whose canvas is the screen's (`LCD_DRAW_MODE` normal, BGRA8888); an offline canvas draws into a bitmap and is never taken. Off puts stock's `end_frame` back at once (`night_set`), so with Night Shift off nothing runs per frame, and that paint check is a flag test: the setting is read once at boot (`ringnav_bootmode`, `patch/playback.c`), so no paint reads `config.ini`. Every change repaints the whole screen (`widget_invalidate_force` on the window manager), so the screen goes warmer, cooler or back to stock's colors in one frame.

Checks in `test/patch.py`: the row from each saved value and its place at the list's end; the page's switch, wheel, +/- and slider, with saving and the repaint; and the tint run through stock's `lcd_end_frame`: the frame's rect warmed with red kept and alpha `0xf7`, a pixel outside it or already warm left alone, a pixel drawn again warmed again, an image pixel of every alpha put through stock's blend warmed once, rotated or padded rows left as drawn, and Off restoring stock's `end_frame`; boot reading the setting and a paint reading none; `night_paint` takes no offline canvas, no other format and nothing while off.

## Frame rotation

demo draws each frame landscape, 375 x 320, into the screen's `lcd_mem` buffer, and the panel is portrait, 320 x 375 (`/dev/fb0`, two pages, [boot](boot.md)). The lcd's swap and flush (`LCD_SWAP`, `LCD_FLUSH`), which `lcd_linux_fb_create` (`0x63a57c`) sets to its copy-and-pan at `0x6398d8`, already copy only what changed: AWTK's `lcd_fb_dirty_rects` keeps, for each framebuffer page, the dirty rects of every frame since that page was last drawn, so the hidden page gets this frame's rects and those of the frame before it, each turned by `image_rotate` 270 degrees, and is then panned to. A frame whose only change is the status row's playing bars costs a turn of that band, not of the screen.

The turn itself was the cost. For BGRA8888 `image_rotate` reaches `rotate_bgra8888_image` (`0x6e11a0`) and its static helper (`0x6e0f30`), which copies the rect one source row at a time down a column of the page, one `memcpy` call per pixel, so every store lands on a different cache line: about 30% of demo's running time on the Q2 while a list scrolled (a `q2remote.py prof` of `memcpy` called from `0x6e115c`, the helper's 270-degree loop). A benchmark on the Q2 (heap buffers; reads of the mapped `/dev/fb0` ran at the heap's speed) puts the miss pattern, not the call, at fault: a whole frame turned stock's way took 3.3 ms, with a word copy in place of each `memcpy` 3.4 ms, and 8 source rows at a time 0.9 ms; a 375 x 40 band 0.32 ms against 0.08, a 179 x 179 art pane 0.65 against 0.17. `fast_rotate_bgra8888` (`patch/fb_rotate.c`, hooked over `rotate_bgra8888_image`) is the same turn: the same arithmetic for where the rect starts in each bitmap (`bitmap_get_bpp`, `bitmap_get_physical_line_length`, the source's physical size), each pixel one word load and store (an unaligned `lwl`/`lwr` pair where a bitmap's data or row length is not a multiple of 4), and at 270 `BAND` (8) source rows together, so each run of stores fills one 32-byte line of a page row. The bands change only the order, and are used only where the bytes the rect reads and the bytes it writes are apart (`apart`), so the order cannot matter; otherwise, and at 90 and 180, the rows go in stock's order. It locks and unlocks the two bitmaps as stock does, and returns stock's `RET_BAD_PARAMS`, unlocking neither, when a buffer is missing. Another angle (0 is `image_copy`'s, not this), a negative width or height, or a bitmap whose depth is not 4 bytes goes to stock's own through `stock_rotate_bgra8888_trampoline`. Every other caller of `image_rotate` for BGRA8888 (`lcd_mem`'s own flushes) gets the same bytes, so nothing else changes. `test/patch.py` runs both on bitmaps made by stock's own code (`graphic_buffer_create_with_data`): every angle, edge and random rects, padded rows, unaligned data, a destination sharing the source's bytes, and the Q2's full 375 x 320 frame, and requires the same bytes and result.

## Parametric EQ

**Stock presets.** Stock's preset slots are `reset_user_eq`'s (`0x503934`) constant 12 × 10 float table, modes 1-3 the zeroed custom slots and 4-11 Pop, Rock, Dance, Blues, Metal, Vocal (the `eq_scene` image), Classical and Jazz in its `eq_*` image order, in dB over the same ten bands (`set_equalizer_value` stores them plus 6). `patch/peq_ui.c` keeps modes 4-11 as `stock_gains`; picking one loads `peq_default` with those gains, bands with a gain on, and Auto preamp into the editor as a saved preset does. Nothing is written until Apply.

The PEQ adds two demo hooks: `playset_equalizer_page_init` (`0x4b9c94`) builds the editor from `patch/peq_ui.c` (ten band rows, plus a spare past the last used band, up to 30), and `set_equalizer_value` (`0x5039c0`) keeps the stock equalizer filter instantiated, then sets `g_equalizer_flag` to the PEQ on/off state so the status-bar EQ icon (`systembar_showface`) follows it. The editor's ON/OFF writes the stock switch's `write_int_config(flag, "PLAYSET", "EQFLAG")`, which boot reads before instantiating the filter, so the state survives a restart. Frequency and Q open a value menu with an AWTK `edit` created at run time over the title (2 px under the status row's foot, `bar_foot`: the page's window is the whole screen, [full-bleed](oled-design.md#full-bleed), and every child of the page, the tab bar, the list and the edit, lays out from that foot), keyed and styled as the stock playlist dialogs' (`kb_default_t9`, `text`, `#2B2B2B` rounded), but with action text `done`. The letter strip's window starts at the row's foot (`search_strip_box`), so as it opens AWTK lifts the page by the edit's last 28 px and the edit rests just under the row's glyphs while the strip types in its own row; as the list's first row (then page y 52-92) it sat under T9, showed none of the typing and lost the keys (the cause of the loss inferred, not traced: stock `edit_on_event` drops `EVT_IM_COMMIT` on an edit without its focused flag). Row 0 names the field and, like Center on it, focuses the edit and asks for the keyboard; on a Frequency or Q edit still focused after Done, which sends no `EVT_FOCUS`, it starts the number-page timer below itself. The rename edit is placed the same way. Return with the keyboard up cancels either edit (`search_key`, see [Internet Radio](#internet-radio)): an empty entry restores the value, or leaves the name for the preset list. The 123 page is set on the input method's own keyboard (`IM_KEYBOARD`, `+0x0c`, while `IM_WIDGET` is the edit), not a window looked up by name, which could be the previous keyboard still closing. The edit's action text is `done`: stock `edit_on_event` acts on the keyboard's OK (`EVT_IM_ACTION`) only for `done` (close the keyboard, then `EVT_VALUE_CHANGED`) or `next`, and the dialogs' `OK` relies on their own handlers, so with `OK` the value only reported on blur; its `EVT_VALUE_CHANGED` applies the text through the preset parser's number reader, clamped like Raise/Lower, and its `EVT_FOCUS` (`0x10e`) starts a 16 ms timer that switches that keyboard's `panel` pages to `symnum`, the number keys, trying up to 20 times since the keyboard can open a moment after the focus, and selects the edit's value (`edit_set_select`), so the first key replaces it. The edit uses text input so stock's numeric validation and auto-fix cannot rewrite unfinished decimals or zero digits; `peq_number` validates the completed text and the editor clamps it to Q 0.1–10 (a notch's to 30) or Frequency 20–20,000 Hz. Auto preamp is one saved cut for every rate: minus the largest combined response peak of either channel over the standard PCM rates (`headroom`, `patch/peq_ui.c`, the loudest of `peq_auto`'s per-rate cuts at 8, 11.025, 12, 16, 22.05, 24, 32, 44.1, 48, 64, 88.2, 96, 176.4, 192, 352.8 and 384 kHz), worked out by demo when a band changes and saved in `preamp`, which the player plays as it plays a picked one (`peq_compile` from `peq_reset` and `peq_update`), through the usual 20 ms ramp. So tracks at different rates play at one level, where a cut per rate made jumps of up to 4.5 dB between them (the reported 26-band preset's cuts: −12.35 dB at 32 kHz, −9.25 at 44.1, −8.81 at 48, −7.87 at 96; Auto is −12.35 at all four), and the player sweeps nothing as a track starts. ponytail: a nonstandard rate (37.8 kHz and the like) can peak between two of these; a cut there would need the player's sweep back. Each rate's sweep is 1024 log-spaced points from 1 Hz to Nyquist, plus DC, Nyquist and the band centers; it never boosts (a flat or cut-only preset gets 0 dB) and is capped at −60 dB. It is one gain for every channel, applied with balance as a set preamp is, so the filters and the left/right balance are unchanged.
