It is a sampled steady-state peak, not a limiter: an unsampled narrow peak (0.003 dB on that preset at 44.1 kHz) and transient or intersample overshoot can still need more. `peq_preset.automatic` records which preamp it is: 1 Auto (the preamp picker's Auto row, a stock preset), 2 a value picked from the preamp list or an import's own `Preamp:` (`peq_parse`; an import without one is 1, Auto, so its boosts can't clip), 0 never picked (a preset or state saved before 1.3.6, or imported before 1.4.4), which the editor takes as Auto and `eq_commit` and `peq_boot` save as Auto with its cut (`auto_level`): a preamp picked before 1.3.6, or an older import's, must be picked again (or the file imported again). A pick on the Preamp picker is also written to the preset on the card the draft was loaded from (`remember_preamp`: its `automatic` and `preamp` only, found by the loaded name in `EQ/`, the file written out again by `peq_export`, so its own comments go), so a file switched to Auto stays Auto when loaded again ([Presets on the card](#presets-on-the-card)). Keyed on the name, a stock preset named like a saved one would write to that file. A picked preamp plays exactly as set at every rate, even when it equals the Auto figure. Every change of what plays goes through `eq_commit`, which puts PEQ's Auto right first, and `peq_boot` does so for a state an older version saved (its Auto `preamp` the 48 kHz cut, which its own player never played), before anything plays; so a rate change rewrites nothing and opening the page offers nothing to apply. The Preamp row and its picker's Auto row show the cut, `Auto (-12.3 dB)`, one decimal, cached until a band changes. A band edit, including a gain picked from the wheel list, recomputes it only on Auto, so a picked preamp stays put. The editor handles Return (key 170) itself, since it replaces the page init that registered `on_common_keyup`. On the main and band screens a `PEQ_GRAPH_H` view heads the list, the scroll view's first child, and scrolls with the rows; it shows the draft's response (`peq_response`, the same `|H|^2` as Auto preamp, at 48 kHz, one point per column, 20 Hz-20 kHz, ±`PEQ_GRAPH_DB`), drawn by `peq_paint` from the paint hook, at the view's own canvas origin and inside the list's clip: a gray grid with 100, 1k and 10k labels, a 2-pixel vgcanvas line in the accent's light tone (white in Stock) with a fill that fades toward 0 dB, the other channel's line dimmer when left and right differ, a ring per band in use, the edited band's larger and filled; gray with no fill when PEQ is off. It takes no click, so ringnav's rows, row 0 first, are the ones under it. The list sets no `item_height`, which stock's layout (`0x5fd484`) would give the graph too; the rows are 48 px themselves, the graph two of them, so whole rows fill the list at either end. Arriving on row 0 shows the whole graph, since ringnav's `reveal` shows everything above the first row when it is reached ([Wheel movement](#wheel-movement)); `eq_key` scrolls nothing. A render on the same screen keeps the list's offset; coming back to the main screen or a band's from a screen it opened (a picker, a band, Presets) lands on the row and offset it was left at (`ui.kept`), the new view's `_ringnav_count` set so ringnav's `load` keeps that row rather than its remembered one, and a band opened from the main screen starts at its top. Rows show the caption on the left and the value right-aligned in gray, left of stock's `list_into` chevron (x 302) on rows that open a screen or picker (`INTO`: Balance, Preamp, Presets, the bands, Frequency, Gain, Q and the Presets menu's five); **Enabled** and a band's **Band** row are switches (`list_toggle`, navigation.c), Channels and Type cycle in place; off bands and display-only rows are gray. Band captions use 16 px, leaving room for the 20 px gain and chevron even with a channel-specific shelf at 20000 Hz. The **Presets** row's value names the preset loaded from there, and keeps the applied one's name until the active preset changes. It is stock's right-aligned ellipsis `hscroll_label` (`long_value`), not the other rows' plain label, in a column fixed from x 130, past the caption in the widest row font, so a long file name stops short of the caption; a theme with a wider row font has to move it. Stock draws a cut name from the label's left (`0x64cd40`), so it can end up to a letter short of the values above it; the selected row's marquee scrolls it uncut. **Rename a preset** lists the saved presets; a pick opens the name in an edit (letters, as the value menu's edit otherwise), focused at once, so the keyboard is up, with `select_none_when_focused` set: stock's focus selects the whole text (an idle, `0x6223f0`), so the first key replaced the name. The cursor stays at the end, where stock's text setter leaves it (`0x627028`), so keys edit the name's end. Done (`EVT_IM_ACTION`, and the `EVT_VALUE_CHANGED` stock sends only for a changed text; `named` acts once) or the one row, **Rename**, renames the file (`rename_preset`): spaces and dots trimmed from the end, as FAT drops them; refused as "Name not allowed" when nothing is left, starting with a dot, holding `/ \ : * ? " < > |`, or too long to read (256 bytes or more: stock's `widget_get_text_utf8` writes nothing for a text that does not fit, `0x72a180` measuring first), and as "Name taken" when naming another preset (`access`, a case-only change allowed); the editor's and the applied preset's names follow it. An empty name (Return's cancel, Done or **Rename** on a cleared edit) goes back to the Rename list with no message on every path. The **Reset to defaults** row puts `peq_default`'s ten bands, all off, and 0 dB preamp and balance into the draft, keeps Advanced's On/Off and clears the loaded preset's name; Apply changes activates it. The filter runs in `q2player` (`player/dsp.c`, which links `patch/peq.c`), reading the state from `/mnt/data/peq-active` ([player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) rows 25 to 28). Stock skips the equalizer above 48 kHz (`slt` against 48001) in two places: the EQ-on command (`beqz` at `0x42cf30`, to the `===setequalizer off===` log) and the per-stream insert (`bnez` at `0x42f708`, around the add-equalizer call `0x42920c`). The build makes the first a nop and the second unconditional (`EQ_RATE_GATES` in `tools/peq.py`, pinned), so the filter runs at every rate; `peq_compile` accepts 8-384 kHz. DSD is the exception: it reaches the chain as integer PCM, possibly DoP, whose bits must arrive unchanged, so config accepts the format as it comes and `play` leaves every block alone when the playing codec (`mpctx`, a pointer at `0xafae30`, `+0x2c` `sh_audio`, `+4` `codec`) has driver `dsdiff` (`+0x3e0`; the vendor's decoder for dsf, dff and SACD iso) or a name starting `ffdsd` (`+0x3d0`); so do rates outside 8-384 kHz and unknown formats. It never detaches (2): the per-stream insert (`0x42920c`) adds it with `af_add` (`0x44ce18`), which returns the new filter even when its reinit (`0x44bf44`) detached and freed it, and the insert then sends the gain set to the freed instance. The player re-adds the filter at each file load (`0x42252c` sets the insert state back to pending), so the next PCM track is equalized again. The player reads what plays from the [EQ state](#3eq) in `/mnt/data/peq-active` on the playback loop, never in the PCM callback; `patch/peq.c` holds the shared parser, storage and biquad DSP.

**Float headroom.** `peq_process` preserves samples above ±1 for downstream software volume and mixing; a picked preamp and balance are applied exactly. Non-finite input is still zeroed while EQ runs, and steady bypass stays bit-exact. The stock float volume path multiplies before clamping (`0x45be84`); the signed PCM converters saturate at final conversion (16-bit `0x451994`, 24-bit `0x452630`, 32-bit `0x4521f4`). With hardware volume or full software volume, a preset with insufficient headroom can still clip there: lowering the DAC's analog volume cannot recover those peaks. No limiter is added: Auto is a fixed gain for the stream's rate.

**Filter types.** A band's `type` is one of eight RBJ Audio EQ Cookbook biquads (`PEQ_*`, `patch/peq.h`), designed in double by `peq_compile` as Equalizer APO's `filters/BiQuad.cpp` designs them: 0 peaking, 1 low shelf and 2 high shelf (Q-form, at the center), 3 low pass, 4 high pass, 5 band pass (the cookbook's 0 dB peak form, `b0 = alpha`), 6 notch and 7 all pass. Only the first three use a gain (`PEQ_GAINED`); a peak or shelf of 0 dB is an identity band that never runs, while the other five act whatever the gain field holds, which the parser leaves 0. Q is 0.1 to 10, a notch's 0.1 to 30 (`PEQ_Q_MAX`), as APO's notch without a Q is Q 30. Every type is the same five-coefficient biquad in `peq_process`, so a band costs the same whatever its type: 78.4 MIPS instructions per stereo frame, about 3.5 M a second at 44.1 kHz, for each of the eight (Unicorn, `peq/peq.elf`, 1 to 10 bands), and nothing changes with the EQ off, which returns before the block. Auto and the graph read the compiled coefficients, so a high pass's resonance at a Q over 0.707 takes its cut as a peak's boost does. The coefficient test (`test_each_type_s_coefficients_are_the_bilinear_cookbook_design`) holds values worked out once in scipy 1.18.1 from each type's analog prototype, prewarped to Fc and taken through `scipy.signal.bilinear`, so it checks the C against an independent design and needs no scipy to run. ponytail: a high or band pass at or past the rate's Nyquist (Fc above 20 kHz never, so only at rates under 40 kHz) is skipped like any band there, passing everything rather than silencing; lifting it needs a per-type rule in `peq_compile`. Firmware before these types rejects an EQ state holding one (its `valid_band` reads types 0 to 2), so a downgrade with one in use starts from the defaults, and leaves such a line out of a text preset (or, before lenient import, refuses the file). Advanced's band screen has a **Type** row that opens a picker of the eight, the menu sheet's (`modal_pick`, [Menus](oled-design.md#menus)), or a screen of them (`TYPES`) when the sheet cannot open, either on the band's own type; under the modal the band's list is not rendered again until a pick (`type_picked`, as a click on the `TYPES` row), since a render under the panel rebuilds the list and drops the wheel's row, and the pick's render is a kept one (`ui.kept`, with `_ringnav_count`), since ringnav otherwise puts a new view's selection on its first row once the panel has closed (seen in the emulator; which of `load`'s branches does it was not traced), so a pick or Return comes back on Type; a gainless type has no Gain row, and its row on the main screen reads On instead of a gain. Moving off a notch brings a Q over 10 down to 10.

A band's `enabled` is 0 off, 1 both channels, 2 left only, 3 right only (stream channels 0 and 1); `balance` (dB) attenuates the left above 0 and the right below, so it never adds clipping. APO `Channel:` sections set the scope of the filters after them, and per-side preamps become the louder side's common preamp plus `balance`. Out-of-range OFF filters, the blank slots some exporters write as `Fc 0 Hz … Q 0`, are skipped. Earlier firmware's binary presets in `/mnt/data/peq-presets` are `Q2PEQ02`; ten-band `Q2PEQ01` files load with `balance` 0 and default bands 11-30, and `Q2PEQ02` files from before 1.3.6, 8 bytes shorter (`PEQ_PRESET_V2`, no `automatic`), with `automatic` 0. Firmware before 1.3.6 rejects the longer files, so a downgrade to it loses saved presets and the EQ state. The DSP runs bands only up to the last one in use, or still draining memory carried from the previous preset.

**The filter without the EQ.** A fade ([Crossfade](#crossfade)), [Mono Audio](#mono-audio), Swap L/R and AirPlay's tap all run in the PEQ filter, which boot instantiates only when an EQ was left on (`PLAYSET/EQFLAG`). With the EQ off, each calls `peq_chain` (`patch/crossfade.c`) while something plays, which calls `peq_attach` (`patch/peq_ui.c`) once per hciplayer connect, unless the EQ is on or any `peq_stock_eq` since has already put the filter in (`peq_chained`, cleared by `ringnav_mode`'s connect-time call when the EQ is off, since a new hciplayer starts without the filter). `peq_attach` does what the editors' Off does, `peq_stock_eq`, which instantiates the filter in bypass, after making sure the [EQ state](#3eq) is saved Off, so a mode saved on while the stock flag is clear stays silent. Bypass is bit-exact, so 16- and 24-bit streams reach the output unchanged through the float conversion. Boot itself is left alone: a listener who uses none of these keeps the stock chain.

## Presets on the card

Saved presets are [Equalizer APO](https://sourceforge.net/p/equalizerapo/wiki/Configuration%20reference/) configuration text, one `EQ/<name>.txt` on the card each, so a preset from AutoEQ is a preset as it is, and one saved on the Q2 is a preset for APO or Peace on a computer. The active EQ stays the binary [EQ state](#3eq) in `/mnt/data`, so playback never reads the card. Advanced's **Presets** lists the folder's `.txt` files (the extension in any case), loads one through `peq_parse` with no copy made (a bad file says `Line N: why`, as an import did), and saves, renames and deletes there; **Save editor preset** writes `Manual NN.txt`. `peq_export` writes a preset as APO's own lines: a comment naming q2-coda, `Preamp`, a balance as one side's `Preamp` under `Channel: L` or `R` (the parser's own reading of per-side preamps), a `Channel` line wherever a band's side changes, and numbered `Filter` lines with `Q`: `PK`, `LSC` and `HSC` with their `Gain`, since a band's frequency is its center (APO's `LS` and `HS` take a corner), and `LPQ`, `HPQ`, `BP`, `NO` and `AP` without one, the names EasyEffects writes too. OFF bands are kept as `OFF` lines, which APO skips. Each number is the fewer digits of `%.15g` and `%.17g` that read back exactly. The one setting APO has no line for, Auto preamp, is a `# q2: preamp auto` comment above the `Preamp` line, which holds the Auto cut, so APO plays a cut and the Q2 its Auto; any other `# q2:` line is ignored, for settings later firmware may add. `parse(export(p))` is `p` field for field (`test_export_round_trips_through_parse`, 1,500 random presets), except that a preamp never picked (`automatic` 0) comes back Auto (1), which both mean. **Earlier binary presets** (`write_out`): the first time Presets lists with the card mounted, each `/mnt/data/peq-presets/*.peq` is written out as `EQ/<name>.txt`, then `.written` there marks it done; a failed write leaves the mark off, to try again. The binaries stay for a downgrade, which still lists them, and can import the text ones. A text file of the same name, most likely the file the binary was imported from, stays unless it reads and differs: then the binary is that import with a preamp picked since, and replaces it. A message an action on Advanced leaves, these included, is a toast over the page instead of the title's text.

## Lenient import

`peq_parse` loads what the Q2 can play from a file and leaves out the rest, a line at a time, as Equalizer APO itself does; it counts what it left out (`peq_error.skipped`) and keeps the first one's line, reason and a short name (`what`: the command, `HP filter`, `Channel C`, `band out of range`, `bands past 30`, or `line N`), so a load says `Loaded; skipped Device, 2 more` (the name cut to 17 characters, so each message fits OLED's toast). A file it can use nothing from fails on its first line left out, as a whole file used to on any, with `Use the ParametricEQ file, not GraphicEQ`, naming no line, for AutoEQ's other format; a file of text with no command (no colon on any line) fails as `no Equalizer APO lines`. Only a file over 16 KB, a NUL, a line over 512 bytes, and a summed preamp or balance out of range still fail whatever else the file holds. What it reads, matched against APO's own parser (`filters/BiQuadFilterFactory.cpp`, `filters/BiQuad.cpp` and `filters/BiQuadFilter.cpp` in [its source](https://sourceforge.net/p/equalizerapo/code/HEAD/tree/), as mirrored at commit `53d885f`): commands and keywords in any case (APO's are case-sensitive; other tools write `filter` and `fc`); a number run into its unit, `1000Hz` or `-3dB`, as APO's `\s*` allows; a line with no colon is no command, as APO ignores it, so REW's header lines (`Filter Settings file`, `Room EQ V5.20`) pass unremarked; `Filter1:` as `Filter 1:`, since APO takes any command starting `Filter`; `Modal` as `PK`; every filter type APO has but `IIR`: `PK`, `LS`, `LSC`, `HS`, `HSC`, `LP` and `LPQ` (the same filter in APO), `HP` and `HPQ`, `BP`, `NO` and `AP`, with APO's defaults where a line has no Q (0.7071 for the passes, 30 for a notch; an `AP` without one is left out, as APO refuses it) and no gain for the five that use none, a `Gain` on them ignored as APO does; `BW Oct` on any of them but a shelf, which APO turns into the RBJ cookbook's `alpha = sin w · sinh(ln 2 / 2 · BW · w / sin w)` at the rate playing, here at 48 kHz (the graph's and Auto's rate) as `Q = 1 / (2^x − 2^−x)`, `x = BW / 2 · w / sin w`, exact there; at 44.1 kHz a 1-octave peak's bandwidth term is 0.06% under APO's at 1 kHz, 1.4% at 5 kHz, 6.3% at 10 kHz and 19% at 15 kHz (ponytail: a per-rate Q would need the bandwidth kept in the preset); a shelf's slope (`LS 6dB`, `LSC 12 dB`) as APO's S of slope / 12, with LS and HS then a corner shifted to the center by 10^(|gain| / 80 / S); a shelf's `BW Oct` ignored, as APO does; `Channel: 1` and `2` as L and R; and `Preamp:` without its `dB`. A `Device:`, `Include:`, `Copy:`, `Delay:`, `Stage:`, `Eval:`, `If:` or `Convolution:` line is left out and named, the lines after it kept (the Q2 has one output and no expressions). A filter type the Q2 has no band for (`IIR`, whose coefficients are free) is left out, `OFF` and `None` ones without a word, as before. A `Channel:` line naming C, LFE or another channel is named once, and the filters and preamps under it play nowhere when it names neither L nor R. A file with lines left out is never written out again: a Preamp pick on it lasts until the next load (`remember_preamp`), and an earlier binary preset of its name does not replace it (`write_out`), since rewriting would lose those lines for APO.

## 3EQ

3EQ is the **Simple** tab of stock's **Playback → EQ** page, which `peq_page_init` builds with two tabs (`ui.tab`), opening on the tab it was last on (Simple after a boot, as `.scratch` is zeroed); **Advanced** is the PEQ editor above. On Simple and on Advanced's main screen the 48 px title label is the tab bar (`ui.bar`, drawn by `tabs_paint`): the open tab white over an accent line, the other gray; a set_switch theme (OLED) draws it as an iOS segmented control instead (`eq_tabs_paint`, [oled-design: Tabs](oled-design.md#tabs)), the open tab a raised gray segment that is the accent only while the wheel is on the bar. A message takes the bar until the next action. A press on the bar picks a tab by its half (`tab_to`, rendered from a timer, never inside the press). Switching tabs changes nothing that plays. Simple is one view that `e3_paint` draws from `ringnav_paint`: the switch, **Presets** and Reset (**R**, a small box; `e3_button`) under the bar, then three sliders over a 0 dB line. `eq_key`, from `ringnav` after `xfade_key`, takes Simple's wheel and Center: the wheel moves through the bar, switch, Presets, R, Low, Mid and High; Center (`center_press`, so a double press still turns the screen off) goes from the bar into the rows, flips the switch, opens Presets, resets or takes a slider, whose gain the wheel then steps by 0.5 dB until Center or Return; the page's key-up handles Return. On Advanced's main screen the list keeps the wheel, except a turn up from its first row (or with none selected), which `eq_key` takes to put the bar in focus (`ui.tabs`, the list's `_ringnav_index` -1, which `paint_selection` leaves unsettled while `eq_tabs_hold` says the bar has the wheel, so no row lights beside the bar's segment; settling would put it on the first row in view, as on a page just opened); a turn up on the bar opens Simple and a turn down, or Center, returns to row 0. On Simple's bar a turn down opens Advanced (`tab_to`, the wheel kept on its bar) and a turn up stays, so the wheel moves along the tabs as on Search's ([Tabs](oled-design.md#tabs)); Previous and Next on either bar open the other tab, `eq_key` called for them from `ringnav` beside `search_strip_key`, before stock's track skip, and passing them on off the bar. A press on Simple's view (`EVT_POINTER_DOWN`) picks a control; the page's move and up handlers (`EVT_POINTER_MOVE_BEFORE`, `EVT_POINTER_UP_BEFORE`, as pull-to-search's) drag a slider in 0.5 dB steps.

**Presets.** Simple's Presets (`e3_presets`) opens Advanced's Stock presets screen (`STOCKS`) with `ui.from_simple` set; Return there goes straight back. When `action` lands back on Advanced's main screen, it returns to Simple with Presets focused: on Return, with nothing changed, or on a pick (`load_draft`), which `apply(1)` saves as the playing PEQ (3EQ off, `hold` cleared) under its name. Like a load in Advanced, a pick replaces unapplied Advanced edits. While PEQ plays (`ui.draft.bypass` clear) the switch shows it on, lit, under `ui.applied` ("Advanced" when unnamed), cut to 12 bytes on a character boundary (16 px past 9), and the sliders are dimmed; a set_switch theme's switch row keeps its title, Enabled, and the name is the Presets row's value instead, right-aligned short of its chevron in Text Secondary, as a settings row's (`eq_rows_paint`); the switch then turns the EQ off with no `hold`, since hold plays 3EQ's preamp. Taking a slider while PEQ plays, by Center or touch, turns 3EQ on first (`e3_switch(1)`); PEQ's preset stays saved. Leaving the page from that screen reopens it on Simple.

**Filters.** `eq3_bands` gives the shared engine three bands, Q 0.707: a 155 Hz low shelf, a peak at 900 Hz for a cut or 1,750 Hz for a boost (0 dB is an identity band), and a 5 kHz high shelf, each -6 to +6 dB. The filter types and rough frequencies follow [Listener's measurements of Apple's AirPods EQ](https://headphones.com/blogs/features/apples-airpods-eq-is-it-any-good); the Q, the 155 Hz within its reported range and the ±6 dB limits are Q2 Muse's own, not Apple's coefficients, and its volume-dependent limits are not copied. The preamp is saved with the gains and played as saved (`automatic` 0), the same cut as PEQ's Auto (`headroom`, over the standard PCM rates); nonstandard rates are not covered. A change crosses over in the engine's 20 ms ramp, including Mid's frequency moving across 0 dB. A shelf above Nyquist is skipped at that rate, as any band is.

**State.** `/mnt/data/peq-active` holds one `eq_state` (`patch/peq.h`), written whole (`.tmp`, `fsync`, rename) with the magic `Q2PEQ03`: the mode (`EQ_OFF`, `EQ_3`, `EQ_PEQ`), `hold`, the last applied PEQ and the 3EQ. `eq_load` reads it, or upgrades a `Q2PEQ01`/`02` preset from before 3EQ (PEQ on unless it was bypassed, 3EQ flat); 1.3.5's record, two presets without `automatic`, loads with it 0; any other short, long or invalid record reads as none (Off, PEQ's defaults). `eq_effective` is what plays: the mode's preset, bypassed when Off; PEQ's never-picked preamp (0) becomes Auto (1) there, and only there, so 3EQ and the hold below keep their saved preamp. The player reads it through `peq_load_active` on the playback loop, as before. Saved presets are text on the card ([Presets on the card](#presets-on-the-card)). Every mode change goes through `eq_commit`, which saves the record, writes `PLAYSET/EQFLAG` when on/off changes and calls `peq_stock_eq`, which sets `g_equalizer_flag`, the status-bar icon, to the mode not being Off. Turning either EQ on selects it and turns the other off; PEQ's Apply keeps the mode unless PEQ is on. Slider edits are saved no more than every 250 ms (`E3_SAVE_MS`) and at once when an adjustment ends, and the player is told only while 3EQ plays, so editing an Off 3EQ changes no sound. A failed save says so in the title and keeps the gains to save again. **Hold:** turning 3EQ off on its page saves Off with `hold` set, which plays the 3EQ's preamp alone (`count` 0), so comparing against bypass is not suddenly louder; closing the page clears it. `peq_boot`, called by `ringnav_bootmode` during `config_init` before queue restoration, also clears a saved hold left by a shutdown while that page was open; the selected EQ mode and both presets stay as saved. Live player updates retain the comparison until the page closes.

**Track changes.** hciplayer negotiates a filter for every file, a new instance or the same one again, and `peq_reset` starts its cascade with zero memory. At a gapless change that zeroed memory under a continuous signal is a step: an audible click on any band with gain, which on music can read as a gap (#137). The instance that played last (`last_id`, set by filtered and passed-through blocks alike) leaves its settled filter memory in `carry` when it is freed or renegotiates (`leave`), unless it is mid-ramp, bypassed, never played, or was last filtered more than `XF_LEAD_S` (2 s) before its length, by crossfade's position and length. The next negotiated instance takes that memory once, on its first block (`adopt`), when rate, channels and preset match and that last block was filtered under 3 s ago (`CARRY_STALE_NS`, as crossfade's `XF_STALE_NS`). A skip or stop mid-track, or a pause near the end, starts the next track from zero: it begins from silence, and the old memory would only ring into it. The position is read only for blocks the EQ filters and the clock only near a track's end, so with EQ off playback reads neither. ponytail: a skip in a track's last two seconds carries, and with Gapless off a track played to its end carries into the next if it starts within 3 s; both start after a cut or silence, where the carried memory is usually small. Gate on stock's Gapless flag if that is heard. A different preset or format starts from zero as before. ponytail: this relies on hciplayer freeing the old instance before the new one plays its first block, which is what the device showed; a new instance that plays first starts from zero. `test/peq.py` (`carry_check`) runs two instances and a renegotiation against one uninterrupted DSP, and checks that a skip mid-track, a pause or a passed-through track in between starts from zero.

## EQ per Output

**Playback → EQ → Advanced → EQ per Output** (`Q2POD EQOUTPUT`, off by default; below Enabled, whether the EQ is on or off; `ringnav_eq_output_toggle`) gives each output its own EQ: the whole `eq_state`, so 3EQ, PEQ, and whether the EQ is on at all. There is nothing to assign: changing the EQ while an output plays is what sets it. `PEQ_ACTIVE` stays what plays, so the player is untouched.

**Which output.** `eq_output_key` (`patch/headset.c`), from `headset_eq_poll` every 500 ms of `ringnav_sleep`: `mclGetOutputWay` 2 is `usb`; 1 is the Bluetooth link list's connected (3) item, its MAC; 0 is a jack, by `g_headset_output`. Stock's `config_bal_output` and `config_po_output` set that byte to 1 (4.4 mm, `PA08`) or 0 (3.5 mm, `PA07`) at each plug-in and `config_outputchannel` sets the way to 0, so the jack last plugged in plays, over Bluetooth too. Unplugging falls back through `check_outputdevice` to Bluetooth, USB, the other jack or 0, so the jack's own `g_bal_status` or `g_po_status` must be set too. No output in use names nothing and changes nothing: an unplugged Q2 keeps the EQ until something else takes over.

**The swap.** `eq_output` (`patch/peq_ui.c`) keeps files in `/mnt/data/peq-outputs/`: an `eq_state` per output (`Q2PEQ03`, named `3.5mm`, `4.4mm`, `usb` or the MAC) and `owner`, the output the EQ that plays was set on. When the named output differs from `owner`, what plays goes to `owner`'s file with `hold` cleared, the new output's comes back through `eq_commit` when it differs (only saved when both are Off, so the filter stays out of the chain for `peq_chain`), and `owner` changes. A new or unreadable slot keeps what plays. With `owner` on disk, nothing needs saving on each edit: an edit just before power-off is filed correctly at the next swap. If the save fails, nothing changes and the next pass tries again, every 500 ms: a card of settings that can't be written has bigger problems, so there's no backoff. A `PEQ_ACTIVE` that exists but can't be read is not filed over a good slot. An open EQ page follows the swap, whether on top or covered: Simple's unsaved gains and a slider in use end and go to the old output's file first, then `page_load` brings up the new output's EQ and caption. Unapplied Advanced edits stay in the draft, and Apply puts them on the output playing then. The swap waits only while a keyboard is up (Frequency, Q, a preset's name), as the render would close it; those screens edit only the draft or a file name, so nothing is filed wrongly, but left up under another page the old output's EQ plays until it closes. The stock preset name shown on Simple is not stored; `peq_page_init` falls back to "Advanced" when the preset differs from the one last applied, as after a restart. With the setting on, the EQ page opens with the output in its bar ("EQ for 4.4 mm") until the first action or turn of the wheel. It names `owner`, whose EQ the page edits, and changes with a swap. Turning the setting off files what plays to `owner`'s file, then removes `owner` and leaves what plays and the other files alone, so an edit made with the setting on is kept, and turning it on again brings back the current output's file, or adopts what plays if it has none. An EQ changed while the setting was off is replaced then, and filed nowhere: the alternative overwrites that output's remembered EQ.

**Limits.** `EQ_DEVICES` caps Bluetooth slots at 32, about 2 KB each: past it, a new headset plays and can edit the current EQ, but it is not remembered. A forgotten device's slot stays, so re-pairing brings its EQ back; removing slots would need a last-used date, and stock's pair list is refilled on another thread without a lock, so it can't safely say which are gone. USB DACs share one slot, since stock does not identify them. Power lost between the swap and `owner`'s save files the new output's EQ under the old output, once; a failed `owner` save does the same at the next boot, since moving back in RAM would do it at the next pass.

**Bluetooth connect.** The swap is inferred safe where stock stops and restarts the player around the same time; if it races, the filter still reads `PEQ_ACTIVE` when playback starts.

## q2eq requests

`q2eq` ([adb: q2eq](adb.md#q2eq)), in `--dev` builds alone, changes the EQ by asking demo, never by writing `PEQ_ACTIVE`, so the page, EQ per Output and the player cannot fall out of step. Its request file and the checks on it are in [adb](adb.md#q2eqs-requests); this is what `q2eq_poll` (`patch/peq_ui.c`, under `#if Q2POD_DEV`, so a release has none of it) does with one. With the page closed it first runs `page_load`, as the page does when it opens: the draft is what plays unless an earlier request left one (`ui.dirty`). It then presses the editor's own rows through `action`: it sets the screen and field a press there would have (`ui.screen`, `ui.band`, `ui.pick`, `ui.adjust`, `ui.file_page`), so a gain, preamp or balance is a picker row (`picks`, a value off its 0.5 dB rows refused), frequency and Q are `TYPED` with the value `peq_number` reads, clamped as typing is, a type is the `TYPES` row, the band switch `ENABLE`, channels `CHANNEL` pressed until it shows the one asked for, and Apply, Reset, Enabled and EQ per Output their rows; Off while Simple's 3EQ plays, which Advanced's Enabled already shows off, is Control Center's EQ circle (`eq_toggle`). Presets are found in `list_files`'s list and pressed on `PRESETS`, `DELETES` (then `YES`) or `RENAMES`, whose rename goes through `rename_preset` with the name given; a save is the `SAVES` row (`YES` with `--replace`), and a save under a name and an import check it with `preset_name`, the rename's rules. An import is parsed with `peq_import_file` before its text is copied to `EQ/` unchanged, then loaded as a preset. Simple's controls are its own functions: `e3_switch`, `e3_take` then `e3_set` and `e3_done` for a slider, `e3_activate` on Reset, and `e3_presets` then the `STOCKS` row, which plays at once as Simple's Presets does. Simple's Off holds 3EQ's preamp only while the page is open to compare against it (`hold`), so with the page closed it holds none. While a request runs (`q2eq_busy`), what `action` would toast is kept for the answer instead (`q2eq_said`). The page's screen and fields are put back afterwards, and an open page renders, so it shows the change where it was left; a request is refused while a keyboard is up there, as EQ per Output's swap waits then. The answer reads the state back (`eq_load`) with the draft, its name and Auto's cut (`headroom`). Unapplied edits go when the page closes (`closed` clears `ui.dirty`), so a draft a request made with the page closed is the one the page opens with. `test/fw/test_q2eq.py` runs it in a `--dev` build of the C; `test/q2eq.py` the helper against a fake demo.

## Bluetooth resampler

Over Bluetooth `q2player` opens `plug:bluealsa` at the transport's rate and resamples with FFmpeg 7.1.5's libswresample on float (`player/output.c`); what the resampler holds back is played at a song's end and at a change of rate, so a gapless change on Bluetooth loses no frame (`test/player/run.py` `test_bt_resample_*`, [player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) row 39).

## USB output buffer

`q2player` asks ALSA for the stock player's buffer, 500 ms in 16 periods, on the DAC, a USB DAC (`hw:1,0`) and Bluetooth, with stock's software parameters (`test_alsa_sw_params`), and keeps the PCM open across any change at the same format on every way, so a natural change neither drains nor reopens ([player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) rows 22, 35, 40, 70). A change of rate, channels or format plays the old song out of the PCM, then reopens. A USB DAC that refuses a song's format is offered `S32_LE`, `S24_3LE`, then `S16_LE` ([player-plan: Deviations](player-plan.md#deviations)).

## Wired start

On output way 0 (3.5 mm and balanced) the CS43131 cuts the first fraction of a second after an unmute. `q2player` mutes the DAC (`dac_mute`, `player/output.c`) before it opens, seeks or resumes, and unmutes with `DAC_RELEASE_MS` (130 ms) of silence before the first frame when a person is waiting for sound: a press, a seek, a resume. Whether a start was pressed is demo's word in `/tmp/q2press` (`press_stamp`, below; `dac_stamp` takes each word once, within 5 s). A natural change adds no wait. Whether 130 ms is enough on every DAC is phase 6's recording ([player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) row 59).


### A press, not a natural change

A track change nobody pressed for adds no sleep unless it really reopens the PCM on a jack, which waits as a press does, after the old track has played to its end ([The old track's end](#usb-output-buffer)). The rest of its path adds `dac_told`'s open, read and close of a tmpfs file, on the wired outputs only, right after the unmute ioctl of a reopen, where the PCM isn't running, and one at `ao_init` on a cold change; a preloaded change at the same format reaches neither. hciplayer can't tell a press from a natural change, but demo can. It writes `/tmp/q2press` (`PRESS_FILE`, an `int` made whole under `.tmp`, renamed and mapped shared, as `/tmp/q2xfade` is; none until the first press or natural start, and no file reads as no press): `now_ms` (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`, in `peq.c`, so both sides read the same clock; `time_now_ms` runs from demo's own origin, `stm_now`), odd, so never 0. `dac_told`, at the two gated sites only, reads the word: fresh means younger than `DAC_PRESS_MS` (5 s, for demo's mute, its sleep and a slow card's open), compared wrap-safely, and each word answers once. Stale, 0, from the future or no file: stock's unmute and on. `shared_int` writes the file's four bytes rather than `ftruncate` them, which allocates no page: on a full tmpfs the first store would SIGBUS, and now the file simply isn't made.

The stamps are opt-in, since a missed site only keeps the old cut, and all of them in `press_stamp` are for a local queue only (folder or library class; DLNA's load as 2 and 3, the online queues as `0xf1` and `0xf2`):

- `ringnav_change`, past its restart guard: every Next and Previous, Folder Skip's sibling included, so `ringnav_next(0)` and `ringnav_prev` need none, their only callers being under it.
- `ringnav_load` outside a restore: `player_start`'s list picks, so every Cover Flow, Home and Library play, through `play_folder` and `playing_page`.
- `ringnav_play_pause` when stopped (demo's call of `mclStartPlayer` at `0x520600`), a headset's own play included, which waits only if the output has since become wired.
- `playback_group_skip`, and Up Next's row (`un_play`, not the `player_start_queue` hook, which DLNA and SyncLink's URL plays reach too).
- A user's seek: the hooks on `player_seek_time` (a chapter, a scrub no tick moved live; a paused scrub sends `mclSetSeek` alone, and Play waits in `dac_resume`; a playing scrub's and the [scan](#scan)'s `mclSetSeek` stamp nothing, so each jump is heard without the wait) and `player_seek_start` (Previous restarting the track, past [its guard](#resume), and only when it will).

SyncLink's phone presses stamp like the Q2's own: `startPlayFolderSong` (class 1) and `startPlayClassSong` reach `player_start`, and its Next and Previous `player_next_music` and `player_prev_music`. `mclStartPlayer` itself would be one site but is the wrong one: the natural routes below all pass through it.

Natural routes, which stamp nothing:

- A preloaded change at the same format never reaches the sites (it neither mutes nor reinits); at another rate it's hciplayer alone (`0xb11df8`), and it reads the word, subject to the limit below. Demo's `ringnav_next(1)` zeroes it after.
- Everything demo drives comes from `player_mainscheduling` → `mclAutoChange` → `mclNextSong(1)`: Gapless off, stock Shuffle's cold start with Crossfade waiting (`XF_COLD_NS`), advanced play's `mclStartPlayer`, Repeat One, DSD to DSD and the queue's end. `ringnav_next(1)` forgets the press and sets `press_natural` to 2 around it, so Folder Skip's rollover inside it (`on_player_autochange` → `player_refresh_playqueue` → `ringnav_load`) stamps nothing.
- `player_reconfig` and `player_save_start` (an output's change, a headset, Standby's resume) call `mclStartPlayer` directly and stamp nothing. They keep the cut.
- Stock's skip past a file it can't play (`on_wm_timer_dialog`, `jalr` at `0x4f4dd4`): `player_next_music` tail-branches into `player_change_music` with `ra` restored, so `ringnav_change` sees `0x4f4ddc` and sets `press_natural`, for a Folder Skip load within it too.
- An app's Stream mode (`stream_start`, from its poll) stamps nothing, nor do DLNA and online queues.
- A natural next into a track with a saved place: its start is natural, and Resume Songs' jump a second on goes past the seek hook (`stock_seek_time_trampoline`), so it doesn't wait.
- A-B Repeat's loop (`check_abrepeatmode`, `open_repeatmode`, `mclSetSeek` from the idle callback) isn't a track change and doesn't wait; the point it loops to already goes mute plus 150 ms in stock, unchanged.

ponytail: every wired manual start comes about 130 ms later. A stamp left unspent under 5 s (a refused Next, a press that opened paused, a seek while paused, whose word stock's paused `player_seek_time` leaves, a press and a track under 5 s) gives a natural reopen one 130 ms gap, at most one per word; a per-file stamp would close that. A rapid double Next can spend its word on the first init, so the last track keeps the old cut. Stock's cut stays on A-B Repeat's loop, Resume Songs' jump (a list pick's too, though its start waits), a phone's seek, Next on an online queue, a Memory Playback boot and stock's View Queue row. Spotify's `aplay` and q2video (Videos, Internet Radio, Spotify's sink) don't go through hciplayer and keep the cut. The tail a rate change loses is as it was. A silence pre-roll would cover a pop with the mute line open before the first frame, and wants a setting.

## Unpause

`q2player` pauses with `snd_pcm_pause` (a device that cannot pause plays out what it holds, then waits) and resumes under the DAC's mute with the 130 ms wait ([Wired start](#wired-start)). On Bluetooth the paused PCM is closed after 20 s and opened again at the Play ([Bluetooth pause](#bluetooth-pause)). The stock player's resume skipped what the DMA held at the pause (`soc_aic.ko` restarts its ring at the first descriptor), which Q2 Muse's patched player rewrote from a ring of its own; `q2player` does not yet, and whether anything is skipped is phase 6's recording ([player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) row 60).

## Large MP3s

An MP3 opens and seeks by its Xing or VBRI header's frame count and table, through FFmpeg 7.1.5's mp3 demuxer: nothing walks the file at the open, so a long VBR file starts at once, and a seek lands on the exact sample ([player-plan: Deviations](player-plan.md#deviations)).

## Forced EOF

A song ends at its decoder's last frame. An MP3 ends at its Xing or Info frame count when no MPEG frames follow it, so junk after the audio (an APE or ID3v1 tag, a padded download) is not heard (`test_mp3_tail_not_played`); frames that chain at the count (two files joined) play on. A WMA file's position starts at 0, so demo's `set-gapless` and Crossfade's hold come at the right time.

## Music info between songs

`media-info` is answered on the command thread from the engine's own record, under its lock (`player/ipc.c`), so a request during a change reads either song or `no-playing-status`, never a half-made one.

## A bad file next

A preload that does not open or has no audio leaves the song playing to its last frame, then `{player-status\error}` (`test_bad_preload`, fixture `pod-badnext`); a next file with no audio ends as it starts, its `exit` at least 300 ms after the one before, so demo hears both (`test_exits_apart`, `pod-emptynext`).

## A FLAC cut inside its metadata

A FLAC whose metadata runs past the file's end fails to open with `{player-status\error}`, as any file that does not open.

## A preload too late

A `set-gapless` the song outruns is opened all the same: `exit` comes at the song's end, and the preloaded file plays once it has opened (`test_preload_outrun`). One canceled (`mcl-closegapless`) or replaced while opening is not played (`test_preload_cancelled`, `_while_opening`).

## A FLAC seek near the end

A seek anywhere in a FLAC, the last block included, lands on the exact sample and plays to the end (fixtures `pod-transport`, `pod-seek`; [player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) row 13). A FLAC stream's seek near its end plays to the end too.

## MP3 gapless playback

FFmpeg 7.1.5's mp3 demuxer reads LAME's and FFmpeg's Xing and Info headers and cuts the encoder delay (plus the decoder's 529 samples) and the padding, so an album encoded with gapless metadata plays as one stream, no sample added or lost at the cut (`test_exact_mp3_gapless`, `test_exact_mp3_no_step_at_the_cut`, `test_gapless_mp3_ffmpeg`). A file with no gapless metadata keeps its delay and padding. iTunSMPB-only MP3s are open: no iTunes-encoded file to test ([player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) row 15).

## Lossy gapless playback

AAC in M4A (iTunSMPB or an edit list), Ogg Opus (its pre-skip and end granule) and Ogg Vorbis are cut by FFmpeg 7.1.5's own demuxers and decoders; four pairs are exact on the host, and in the emulator Vorbis exact, AAC and Opus to the last unit in the last place (`test_gapless_m4a`, `_m4a_itunes`, `_vorbis`, `_opus`; [player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) row 16). ADTS `.aac` has no metadata and keeps its priming and padding.

## MP3 ReplayGain

Playback > ReplayGain (`mcl-replaygain`) scales by the track's or the album's gain from every tag form: Vorbis comments in FLAC and Ogg, ID3v2.3 and 2.4 `TXXX`, an MP4 freeform atom; the peak limits it, and a LAME header's gain is not read (`test_replaygain_track`, `_album`; [player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) row 32).

## MQA detection

Stock V1.36's player detects nothing, and neither does `q2player`: an MQA file is a FLAC or WAV and plays as its PCM, bit for bit; `mcl-mqadecodemode` is stored and unused, and `mcl-pcmstate` answers 0 ([player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) row 55).

## Crossfade

**Playback → Smart Crossfade** (`ringnav_audioset`, stock's `playset_gapless` icon, after Gapless in the order below; `xfade_row` and `xfade_click` in `patch/crossfade.c`) is one switch, `Q2POD XFADE` in `config.ini`, off by default. It replaced a length picker (an on/off switch with a 1-15 s Duration row under it) on 2026-11-23: that picker saved the same `XFADE` key, so a config with Crossfade on at any length reads On, and its `XFADESEC` is left in the file and never read. The fade's length is the player's to choose per change ([Smart Crossfade](#smart-crossfade)); the fixed fade it falls back to is `XF_FALLBACK_MS`, 5 s. Every fade needs stock's Gapless on (below), so turning Smart Crossfade on with Gapless off turns Gapless on as stock's own row does (its click at `0x4bcfa4`: `PLAYSET GAPLESS` written, `mclSetGaplessMode(1)`, and its switch `img_gapless7` set to `switch_on`); off leaves Gapless as it is. The row's caption, under it while selected, says what it does, and while Smart Crossfade is on and Gapless off says "Needs Gapless on: nothing fades while Gapless is off" instead: `xfade_poll` compares the Gapless byte each UI pass and rewrites the caption when stock's row on the same page changes it. Display's Wheel Sensitivity, Night Shift, and Playback's Resume Songs and Volume rows open stock's Boot volume page re-dressed (`xfade_open`, its `xf.ctx` 1 to 4): `playset_bootvol_page_init` (`0x4b7968`) binds `img_bootswitch`'s click (`on_bootvol_switch_onclick`), `img_dec`'s and `img_add`'s (`0x4b7434`, `0x4b73b8`) and `slider_bootvol`'s `EVT_VALUE_CHANGING`/`CHANGED` (`0x4b7704`, `0x4b7110`), each with the window as context; `xfade_open` unbinds them with `widget_off_by_func` and binds its own, so Boot volume is never written. `view_bootvol` (the slider, the minus and plus and `label_vol`) is always shown and enabled (stock disables it with the view hidden while Boot volume's switch is off, which left touch dead on the slider and the minus and plus, #140). A drag shows and plays each value at once but saves only at its release (`slid`: the slider's value-changed, not value-changing), or when the page closes mid-drag, so a quick drag is one config write, not one per value. Stock's slider sends no value-changed for a drag released where it began or an aborted press, so any later step, the switch, or the close saves a value a drag left unsaved (`set_value`'s `held`). `xfade_key`, from `ringnav` after `spot_key`, gives the page the wheel and, on Night Shift's, Center (a single press cycles it, a double press turns the screen off as on any page). The page's close (`gone`) stops a single press still waiting for its double (`stop_timer(&xf.press)`): the timer belongs to no window, so it ran after the page had gone, with `xf.ctx` back at 0.

**Settings order.** Playback and System are restacked by use after stock builds them and the payload adds its rows (`reorder`, `playset_order` and `sysset_order` in `patch/navigation.c`): Play Mode, EQ, Gapless, Smart Crossfade, Memory Playback, Resume Songs, Sleep Timer (Headphones Required hidden: [always on](#no-playback-without-an-output)), Max and Default Volume, Gain, ReplayGain, Balance, Mono Audio, Swap L/R, Digital Filters, DSD Output and USB Audio; and Wireless, Network, Display, Controls, Power, Date & Time, App Store, Update, Reset, About (Language sits hidden after Date & Time, [English](#english)). Stock names each row's button by its position (`"%d"`) and its click handler (`0x4bcfa4` for Playback) reads that back and looks its id up (the table at `0x77e454`), so moving a row keeps its action; a page with an unexpected row count is left as built.

**Stock V1.36's lists.** V1.34 moved rows about, and the hooks put the lists back as they read on V1.32. Its Settings list has nine rows: Language, Wireless, Network, Display, Power, Wheel Function, In-Vehicle Mode, General (Date & Time, Key Tone, Buttons Lock) and System (Update, Reset, About). `ringnav_systemset` hides all but Network, leaving stock's page whole, and adds rows of its own for Date & Time, Update, Reset and About, which open stock's pages (`to_page`) under stock's icons and translation keys; the page is Settings' General ([ipod](ipod.md#settings)). Its Playback page has thirteen rows; the twelfth, Volume and Album Display, opens a page of four (`playset/volcover_page`: Max Volume, Default Volume, Enlarged Album Art, Folder Album Cover). `ringnav_audioset` drops that row and gives the four rows of their own: the two volumes open stock's `playset/maxvol_page` and `playset/bootvol_page`, and the two switches flip stock's bytes and save stock's keys as its page's click does (`0x4c0714`: `g_bigcovermode` and `PLAYSET COVERMODE`, `g_foldercover_flag` and `PLAYSET FOLDERCOVER`; `pod_click`). Headphones Required (`g_block_withoutphone_flag`, `PLAYSET WITHOUTPHONE`), new in V1.34, is stock's own row and switch, after Resume Songs. Display's fourth stock row, Show Navigation Bar, and Settings' Wheel Function are not offered ([Stock options held](#stock-options-held)).

**Settings > Playback > Library** and its Sorting, Playlists and Folders pages (`library_open`, `playset_sub` 1 to 4, `patch/library_settings.c`) open stock's Playback page again, as Display's sub-pages do, Folders keeping stock's Folder Skip row (position 12) and the others dropping every stock row; the main page drops Folder Skip instead. Each page's window carries its number (`SUB_PAGE`), which `context_now` adds to the scope of a `CTX_FIXED` page's position memory, so a sub-page opens on its own remembered row, not its parent's (Display's sub-pages likewise). The two instances share nothing: `playset_playset_page_init` (`0x4bd4d0`) keeps its state in its window (the 500 ms timer's id is a property of each window), and its click handler (`0x4bcfa4`) gets the row as its context and finds its image inside that row, its global writes being saved-setting bytes. Library > Playlists ends with Import Playlists and Export Playlists (`playlists_transfer`), the Playlists page's own rows under the other themes: stock's question (`msg_importplaylist`, `msg_exportplaylist`) through its confirm, then `importPlayList` (the playlist art's build stopped first, as `pl_due` does) or `exportPlayList(1, headers, selection)`, whose first argument 1 exports every header of the deque it is given (`getAllPlayList` through `staged`; 0 would export stock's batch selection), and stock's message for the result in the language (`msg_nottf` for -2, `msg_notplaylist` for -6, else `msg_importsuccess` or `msg_exportsuccess`).

**Rows off stock's General.** In-Vehicle Mode (Power), Key Tone and Buttons Lock (both Controls) are Q2 Muse's rows, In-Vehicle Mode and Buttons Lock under stock's translation keys; stock's own (In-Vehicle on Settings, the other two on its General page) stay where they are, unreached. In-Vehicle and Buttons Lock do what stock's clicks do (`0x4d34c0` for In-Vehicle, `systemset_general_item_on_click` `0x4c93f4` for Buttons Lock): In-Vehicle flips `g_carmode`, saves `SYSSET CARMODE` and clears `g_carmode_state`; Buttons Lock opens `systemset/keylock_page`. Key Tone's row is the Clicker ([Key Tone](#key-tone)), whose Off clears `g_keytone_flag` and saves `SYSSET KEYTONE` 0 as stock's switch would, and whose other values set it. The settings keep their saved values.

<a id="stock-options-held"></a>**Stock options held.** V1.34 added options that Q2 Muse's own systems already decide, so each is held in RAM at the value that behaves as V1.32 did, its row is not offered, and its key is never written (a stock choice survives a visit to Q2 Muse). _Show Navigation Bar_ (`SYSSET NAVHIDE`, `g_navhide_flag`): the theme owns the bar and every list's box, so `config_init`'s store writes 0 (`NAV_SHOWN` in `tools/build.py`) and the 58 calls with which stock's pages move their lists for the switch go to stock's `dummy_destroy`, which returns 0 (`navbar_resize_calls` in `patch/ipod.json`): each list keeps the box its asset gives it, which is the box V1.32 showed. _Wheel Function_ (`SYSSET WHEELMODE`, `g_wheelmode`): the wheel is built on stock's Volume Mode, where a tick Q2 Muse does not take falls to stock's volume, so the byte is 1 whatever the key holds (`WHEEL_MODE`), and the config a reset copies has `WHEELMODE=0`, stock's documented default. _Home's key-up_: V1.36's `home_page_init` binds one of its own (`0x534a74`, Return to Now Playing); Home's keys stay `ringnav`'s, so the bind goes (`HOME_KEYUP`). _Buttons Lock on the lit lock window_: V1.36's `on_wm_keyup_before_fun` locks the buttons there too; it stays the dark screen's (`KEYLOCK_LIT`). _Headset keys_: V1.36 starts an input thread on BlueZ's AVRCP device (`btinput_thread_run`, `0x639320`, `/dev/input/event4`) that posts Play and Pause alike as the Play button and Next and Previous as the skip buttons; `patch/headset.c` reads that device already, so the thread never starts (`BT_INPUT`: the function returns NULL, which its caller takes as no such device) and a press acts once. ponytail: AVRCP Fast Forward and Rewind, which stock's thread posts as the skip buttons, do nothing, as before V1.34. _Centre on Now Playing_: stock's page handler leaves it to `on_wm_keyup_fun` again (`NP_CENTRE`, [Scrub](#scrub-ipod)). _A reloaded page's focus_: since V1.36 the album page (`localmusic_albuminfo_page_on_foreground`, `0x4a8e44`) and Playlists (`localmusic_playlist_page_reload`, `0x4b58d4`) note the focused row before they build their rows again and focus it after (`widget_set_focused`, which also scrolls the list to it) if it is in view by stock's 78 px pitch. A tap leaves a row focused, the selection is `ringnav`'s and the rows are a theme's pitch, so stock could pull a list back to a row tapped earlier: both pages go on as with no focused row (`FOCUS_RESTORE`). Playlists also loads its list again at every return since V1.36, where a delete or another class's list was needed before; its rows were rebuilt either way. _Album Wall, Spectrum and VU pages_: not offered. Their Home card and Now Playing buttons are out of the assets (`tools/ipod.py`), nothing else names the pages, and the three pages and the images only they show are left out of the rootfs (`STOCK_PAGES`).

<a id="no-playback-without-an-output"></a>**Headphones Required, always on.** Nothing plays with nothing to play to. Stock V1.36's switch (`g_block_withoutphone_flag`, `PLAYSET WITHOUTPHONE`) refuses a start with no output (`check_forbid_play_no_headset`, which also shows stock's message; `has_valid_output_device`: either jack, a Bluetooth link with its codec up, or a USB DAC). Q2 Muse holds the switch on (`output_rule_config`, `patch/output_rule.c`, after `config_init`, whatever `config.ini` says) and hides its row in Playback settings, so the rule cannot be turned off; stock's test mode (`g_testmode_flag`) still passes. `has_valid_output_device` is hooked (`ringnav_valid_output`) to count the car's USB audio as well, the player's way 3 ([Car Audio](iphone-mode.md#car-audio-in-the-image)): while the car asks for audio, or its audio went during a relink that may bring it back (`usb_car_output`), so the car's Play is not refused and the restarts below do not pause under it. The refusal is stock's `msg_noheadset` in `dialog/msginfo_dialog` for 2 s, drawn as the one-line toast pill, worded "Connect headphones or Bluetooth to play" (`LABELS` in `tools/build.py`; stock's was two sentences). Stock asks where its own starts begin: Now Playing's opening with a track to start (`playing_page_init`, the way a list row's tap goes), the album pages' Play, a View Queue row, the Play and skip buttons (Now Playing's own key-up among them), and SyncLink's starts and keys. Stock's own ask in `playing_page_init` comes after the navigator has made the page, which closes itself when refused but has already been laid out with its asset's placeholder title and artist and slides in under the toast (the owner's report, 2026-11-22), so the payload asks first, at the navigator: `ringnav_nav_to`, the hook on `navigator_to_with_context` (which `navigator_switch_to_with_context` also reaches), refuses `playing_page` opened with a class other than 0xff, `playing_page_init`'s own condition, before the page exists. Every list row's tap or Centre (Songs, albums, artists, playlists, My Fav, Most Played, Recently Played, the Server Library's rows, a card app's rows, Search, Cover Flow's tracks, all through stock's navigator or `play_folder`) is refused there with the list and its selection left as they were, and nothing is loaded: the song playing or paused, the queue and its place stay, and a server song's request to its app (`catalogue_load`'s `.catplay`, reached only from the page's `player_start`) is never written. The payload's own starts that change something on the way to the navigator ask first: `play_folder` (`patch/coverflow.c`), before it closes a Now Playing on top or writes an album queue's album into the resume record (`album_memory`), and the shuffles (`patch/library_lists.c`): `shuffle_play` (Songs' and Home's Shuffle Songs, an album's, an artist's, a decade's and a playlist's Shuffle) before Up Next's order, stock's Shuffle mode or the "Shuffled Songs" confirmation, still answering the list's size so no caller adds "No songs", and Shuffle Albums and Folders (`shuffle_groups`) before the library is read and loaded as the queue. A pick of the song already paused plays it on (`playback_np`: a View Queue row's, an album page's Play, Up Next's row), so it is refused the same way, Now Playing not opened; Up Next's rows ask before anything (`un_click`), Up Next staying open; and the queue menu's Play, Shuffle and a chapter's Resume ask before they set the queue's class, a seek or the play mode (`qm_run`). The restarts that follow a change of output or setting (`player_save_start`, `player_reconfig`) and a deleted playing file's successor start and pause at once. With the switch on, stock's `home_page_init` skips its start at boot whatever is connected (the test of `g_block_withoutphone_flag` at `0x534c44`, ahead of Memory Playback's), so until 1.8.1 the last queue was not restored; the build makes that branch (`0x534c4c`) a nop, since the restored queue is paused and plays nothing. Car mode's start plays, so `ringnav_boot` asks the same function first: refused, it shows stock's message and restores the queue paused, as outside car mode (the page's own init would have closed itself and restored nothing). Q2 Muse's own starts ask the same function: Play/Pause when not playing (`ringnav_play_pause`; a pause always passes), a headset's or the side buttons' skip (`media_key`), an Up Next row (`un_play`), a video (`video_play`, and a paused one's Play or a headset's resume: `video_key`, `video_set_playing`), an Internet Radio station (`radio_play`, every start and restart of one), and Radio (Home's row: a fresh `tuner_open` opens no page; its Play and a headset's resume, `tuner_key`, `tuner_set_playing`). While the car takes the audio over USB these starts pass (the car counts as an output) and play into it ([Car Audio: other sources](iphone-mode.md#other-sources-over-usb)). A card app's queue that opens Now Playing to start (`addon.c` `stream_start`'s first song, `tidal.c`'s `Q2URLS/1` queue, both through `play_folder`) is refused at the navigator as a list's is. ponytail: a card app's own player, a card app's song started through `player_start_queue` (a playlist session's skip, `addon.c`) or stock's Tidal player, a card game with audio, Spotify (librespot, started from the phone) and AirPlay are not gated: each has several start points or starts from another device, and a gate there needs its own design. Something already playing is not stopped when its output goes, beyond stock's own pause of the local player at a jack's eject and a Bluetooth headset's loss and `usb_car_gone`'s at the car's.

**Policy.** `xfade_poll`, from `playback_poll` each UI pass, writes the next change's word to `/tmp/q2xfade` (an `int`, made whole under `.tmp` and renamed, then mapped shared), only when its inputs change: `XF_FALLBACK_MS` with `XF_SMART` (bit 15; `XF_MS` is the 15 bits under it, where no length reaches) when Smart Crossfade is on, stock's Gapless on (the byte `0xa5002c`, `mclGetGaplessMode`), and the next track another album's (`album_cmp`, so an album, a CUE image or an untagged folder stays gapless) and playable (`fades_into`, only when the inputs change: not `.dsf`, `.dff` or `.iso`, any case, as DSD skips the filter, and for a path on the card not missing or 0 bytes, as that file never plays and so nothing would mix the tail); else 0. With a fade it also writes `/tmp/q2xfade.next` (`XFADE_NEXT`, `next_publish`): the playing song's path and the next one's, a line each, made whole under `.tmp` and renamed, so the player can open the next song 45 s ahead of the change, long before demo's preload; the next line is empty while the next is not known (a Shuffle draw still to come). A Play Next or any other change of the next record rewrites both files on the next pass. The next track is `playback_next`: `playback_successor(1)` while advanced play runs, else `pos + 1` in modes 0 and 3, and in mode 3 position 0 at the queue's end, which is what stock preloads, except with the jump-folder flag (`0x5bb368`), where that's a cold start into the next folder (`mclAutoChange` preloads under 6 s from the end, too late to decide on, so the poll predicts it instead). The file's upper bits (`XF_STOPS`) count stops: a pass that finds `mclGetPlayStatus` 1 moves the count, once per stop, unless it's a file error. A natural end never reads as stopped: hciplayer's `exit` reply clears only the running byte for a local queue, and `mclAutoChange` goes no further at status 1. Status 1 comes from `mclStop` (also a queue's end, `0x5c0814`), `mclOrderStop`, a lost socket (`0x5bb578`), an empty path (`0x5c036c`), `exit` at queue type 2 (`0x5bae20`), and the `error` reply from hciplayer (demo's `0x5bae94`). That last one is no stop: hciplayer touches `/tmp/notfile` or `/tmp/notsupport` first (`0x423538`, `0x423548`), and on a local queue `on_wm_timer_dialog` removes the file and shows `dialog/msginfo_dialog`, then calls `player_next_music` (`0x4f5018`). That toast is modal: its init leaves `to_modal` set, so `navigator_to_with_context` runs `dialog_modal` (`0x4f53e4`) for its 2 s, and UI passes run under it with the status still 1 and the file gone. hciplayer touches the file before its `error` reply, and Next's send stores status 2 (`0x5bf798`) on the UI thread as the toast ends, so no pass finds status 1 with neither file nor toast. So a pass counts a stop only with neither file there and no `msginfo_dialog` open (those two syscalls and the walk run once per stop, only while stopped). The missing-file check above means a song before a missing or empty file plays whole with no hold; a next with junk bytes is found out only by trying it, so its hold is finished and the file after it mixes the tail, up to `XF_COLD_NS`, after the toast. A shuffled change always fades, a next of the same album and even the next track of it too, and only a shuffled one does (`xfade_poll`'s `shuffled`, `playback_shuffled`): stock Shuffle, Shuffle Songs, and a shuffle within albums (the hold menu's 2 and 4); Shuffle Albums' own order (3) and every unshuffled queue keep an album gapless. On a local queue stock Shuffle (mode 2, Now Playing's mode button or Play Mode) is played as Shuffle Songs ([Queue menu](#queue-menu), `shuffle_own`), so its next is known: `/tmp/q2xfade.next` names the real next song, the gapless preload opens it and the change is not a cold start. Where stock Shuffle still draws its next at the change (a DLNA or online queue, or one too large to take), so the policy can ask about the file, `playback_next` draws that next ahead (`shuffle_peek`, once per track, with `rand_below`): `mcl_shuffle_pick` (`0x5ba7d0`) takes the current index out of the pool `MCL_POOL` and sets the position to a random one left there, which stays in the pool until it is current, so `ringnav_shuffle` overrides the position after the pick with the draw, a uniform one of the same set. It doesn't touch the pool. It holds while the position and both records are unchanged, so a queue edit or a new queue draws again; a Play next (`shuffle_forced`) and Previous's way back go first, in the policy as at the pick; a manual Next takes the draw too. With under 2 in the pool stock refills it, or Folder Skip jumps (`-16813`), so that one draw per cycle stays -2, unknown. Stock preloads nothing in Shuffle, so that change is a cold start (`mclNextSong` → `mclStartPlayer`); the held tail waits for the new file's first block (`XF_COLD_NS`), so on the jacks the fade runs on over the open PCM when the file's format matches, and after the reopen's short gap when it doesn't ([The old track's end](#usb-output-buffer)). Before 1.6.0 stock Shuffle never faded (the poll wrote 0), which is what #164's reports describe. While a fade is set, each pass puts the PEQ filter in the chain (`peq_chain`, [The filter without the EQ](#parametric-eq)) when PEQ is off.

A queue edit is read the same way: a Play Next changes the next record, so the next pass rewrites the flag and the filter sees it on its next block. Asked before the window, the track gets the whole fade. Inside it, the hold takes half of what the decoder has left, about half a second ahead of the sound, so an edit 3 s before the end fades about 1.25 s, and one in the last half second joins plainly. Taken back before the window, nothing is held; taken back inside it, the hold finishes and what's held mixes.

**Fade.** The fade runs in `q2player`'s DSP (`player/dsp.c`), after the EQ, reading `/tmp/q2xfade` once a second of audio. From the fade's length plus a margin before the end it holds the song's last seconds while the decoder runs ahead at twice real time, then mixes them under the next song's first frames, at another rate or channel count too; a stop drops the tail. Those last seconds are not kept as PCM where the file can give them again ([The tail, from the file](#the-tail-from-the-file)). A plain fade (no `XF_SMART`) holds `XF_MS` and mixes at equal power (`in × sin(p) + out × cos(p)`); a smart one holds and mixes what its plan says ([Smart Crossfade](#smart-crossfade)). A hold once begun is finished: when demo's fade clears or shortens during it, the hold only stops growing, and every frame still plays in order.

<a id="the-tail-from-the-file"></a>**The tail, from the file.** A hold delays the song by up to its own length while the decoder runs ahead, and the mix then needs the song's last frames. Kept as the chain's float PCM that is 8 bytes a stereo frame: 5.3 MB for 15 s at 44.1 kHz, 11.5 MB at 96 kHz and 23 MB at 192 kHz, in a player whose device has about 6 MB free. So for a file whose decoder gives the same samples however its decode began (`TWICE` in `player/tail.c`: FLAC, ALAC, and PCM in WAV or AIFF) the frames are not kept. `RD_LEAD_S` (6 s) before a hold is to begin, the chain asks for the song's file to be opened a second time (`reader_open`, `tail_open`), `RD_AHEAD_S` (3 s) ahead of the song. Everything that touches the file is on that open's own thread (`reader` in `player/tail.c`): the open, the seek, and a decode that keeps `TAIL_AHEAD_S` (2.5 s) of the file's frames decoded ahead of what has been taken, in the file's own sample format. The playback thread only copies frames already decoded (`tail_read`, `tail_ahead`) and never reads the card for the tail, so a read that is slow, or waits on a page the kernel let go, is that thread's wait and not the song's ([When the card stops answering](#the-tail-and-a-stalled-card) below). When the song reaches the frame it began at, each block the song decodes is compared with the same frames read there (`reader_before`, `reader_after`: `memcmp`), so the second open is level with the song and is known, not assumed, to give the song's own samples. A hold that begins while it is level takes it (`xf.rd`). The first decode still runs ahead at twice real time to the file's end and through its own stages, so the engine, the position demo sees and the preload's timing (the ponytail under [Smart Crossfade](#smart-crossfade)), the exact frame the song ends at and the EQ memory the next song takes on ([Track changes](#3eq)) are what they are with a ring; but its frames are only counted and noted (`tail_note`: each block's length and a hash). What plays through the hold and under the next song is the second open's frames, through a copy of the stages (`stages`: ReplayGain's scale and clip, Swap L/R, the EQ from the memory it had before the hold's first frame, Mono Audio), with each later change of a setting (a new EQ, Mono Audio, Swap L/R, AirPlay's mute) taken at the frame it came in at (`told`, up to `XF_EVENTS`, 16, waiting). The second open's reads check themselves against the notes, and a difference or a file that ends short is logged (`the tail read from the file differs from the first decode`, `the file gave N frames fewer than the tail held`). The mix takes only the held frames each block reaches (`window`), so what is in memory is the 2.5 s decoded ahead and a block, there is no ring to fit (`XF_FILED_S`), and the hold is the plan's at any rate: a 15 s overlap at 192 kHz, where the ring cut even the 5 s floor.

Every other tail is held in memory as before, logged with why (`q2player: crossfade: the tail held in memory, ...`): a song in any other codec, a stream, a song still arriving, an SACD image, a second open that would not open, opened in another format, was not at the song's frames or was not level when the hold began, and a hold that begins after a scan. Its ring is mapped for the hold at the hold's own size (`ring_open`: the hold and `XF_SLACK`, at most `XF_FLOATS`, 6 MB) and unmapped when the mix ends or the tail is dropped (`tail_drop`), so nothing is kept between changes. A plan sized for the file (`smart_want`'s `room`) whose second open then fails is cut to the ring's room when the hold would begin, and that shorter hold begins later, as it does for a song with no second open.

Which decoders qualify was measured, not assumed (this machine, FFmpeg 7.1.5 as the player builds it, 2026-11-24: each file decoded whole, then again from a seek 17, 9.3, 4.1 and 1.7 s before its end, the two compared):

| Codec | A second decode from a seek |
| --- | --- |
| FLAC (16 and 24 bit, 44.1 and 96 kHz), ALAC (16, 24), WAV (16, 24, float), AIFF, WavPack, Vorbis | the first's samples from its first frame, at the frame asked for, ending at the same frame |
| MP3, MP2 | at the frame asked for, never the same: a fifth to a half of the samples one step off (19, 30 and 48% from three seeks) for as long as it plays. FFmpeg's integer decoder carries its rounding from sample to sample (`dither_state`), and a decode begun elsewhere carries another |
| AAC in MP4 | the same only from 71 to 37,113 frames in (0.84 s), depending on where it began |
| Opus | the same from some seeks, never from others |
| AC-3, AAC in ADTS, WMA, DTS | not at the frame asked for (WMA 929 to 1,586 frames early, DTS 72 to 163 late), or never the same |

WavPack and Vorbis qualify by this table and are left out: stock's name for WavPack is WMA's (`codec_name`), and Vorbis decodes to float, where the next FFmpeg may round another way; neither is a format the ring is short for. ponytail: MP3, AAC and Opus keep the ring because only one decoder gives their samples; reading their tail without one needs the first decode itself kept open under the next song (the engine handing the ended song's source to the mix, and the end's frame known ahead from a count), and then the EQ memory the next song takes on is no longer the song's last frame's, which has not been decoded yet. Neither is built. None of them is above 48 kHz in practice, where the ring holds 15 s.

A tail read from the file is left behind, as at a seek, by any block that is not the file's next frames (`xf.next`): a seek of any size, where a ring keeps what it holds through one under `XF_SEEK_S`, and a scan, where a ring plays its delayed frames before the scan is heard. The hold that begins again is a ring's. What plays across it is the song's frames in order with one step forward, at the seek, to the frame sought: none twice, none of the frames from before the seek after it (`filed_check`, a seek of half a second and one of 3 s, each frame carrying its own number). The engine mutes and drops the PCM around every seek, so the step is the seek's own.

<a id="the-tail-and-a-stalled-card"></a>**When the card stops answering the second open.** A ring never reads the card for the tail, so the file's way must not make a new way for the PCM to run dry. A stall shorter than what is decoded ahead (2.5 s) changes nothing: the frames those seconds need are already decoded, and the output is the ring's to the bit. A longer one is taken by where it falls, each logged. _Before the hold_ (`same` finds the frames not decoded): the song does not wait, the second open is given up and the tail is held in the ring, as for a file with no second open (`the tail held in memory, the second open fell behind the song`, or `was not level when the hold began`). _Under the next song_ (`tail_ahead` in the mix finds less than the block needs and `XF_CUT_S`, 0.2 s, more): the tail fades to nothing over the frames there are (`xf.cut`: no step larger than that ramp's), the next song loses no frame and its own gain runs on to the mix's end (`the second open fell behind under the next song, the tail faded out N ms early`). _In the hold_, what plays is the second open's frames alone, so there is nothing else to play in order: the playback thread waits up to `XF_HOLD_WAIT_MS` (4 s) for a frame, as it waits on any read of the playing song, and then leaves the hold as at a seek: the block in hand plays as it came, and the frames between are not heard (`the second open stopped giving frames, N ms of the song left unplayed`). ponytail: that last case is a gap once the stall has outlasted the 2.5 s decoded ahead and the PCM's own half second. It is not a first fault: during the hold the first decode reads the same file further on, on the playback thread, with only the PCM's half second to cover a stalled read, so a card that stalls that long has run the song dry 2.5 s earlier with a ring too; the bytes the second open reads were read by the first decode at most the hold's length before. Closing it by construction means the tail's bytes in memory before the hold (the hold twice over and its margin: 2 to 4 MB of FLAC at 44.1 kHz, 15 to 24 MB at 192 kHz, more than the ring), which is the cost this path exists to avoid.

The same 2 s stall of the tail's reads, 7 s into the hold, at real speed on the car's way, whose file sink counts a PCM that ran dry (2026-11-24, `Q2PLAYER_TAIL_STALL=886410:ms2000`): with the reads on the playback thread, as this was first built, the PCM was dry for 1,500 ms and one underrun was counted; with the reader thread, none, and the song found the reader short 0 times (`the tail's reader was stalled while N frames were taken, and the song found it short 0 times`).

Measured on this machine (x86-64, the player's anonymous memory, `RssAnon`, through a 14.4 s hold: a 12.4 s overlap and 2 s dropped; FLAC unless said): at 44.1 kHz 16-bit the player went from 1.1 MB to 7.35 MB at its first fade and stayed at 7.2 MB with the 6 MB ring kept for its life; reading the file it peaked at 1.8 MB and was back at 1.3 MB after the mix. At 96 kHz 24-bit, 1.8 MB to 8.1 MB and kept, for a hold the ring had cut to 7.5 s; reading the file 4.2 MB at the peak for the whole hold, 2.0 MB after, where a ring large enough maps 11.3 MB. At 192 kHz 24-bit, 2.9 MB to 9.1 MB and kept, the hold cut to 3.75 s; reading the file 7.7 MB at the peak, 2.0 to 3.2 MB after, where a ring large enough maps 22.2 MB. An MP3 at 44.1 kHz peaks at 6.7 MB in a ring mapped at the hold's size (5.5 MB) and is back at 1.2 MB after. The second open costs an open file (0.3 MB at 44.1 kHz, 0.9 MB at 96 kHz, 1.6 MB at 192 kHz: FFmpeg's FLAC parser looks several frames ahead) and the 2.5 s decoded ahead in the file's format (0.44 MB at 44.1 kHz 16-bit, 1.9 MB at 96 kHz and 3.8 MB at 192 kHz in 32-bit samples), for the 6 s before the hold, the hold and the mix. ponytail: a 24-bit file's 2.5 s are kept as 32-bit samples; three bytes a sample would take a quarter off. Its CPU is one more decode of the song's last seconds (the 2.5 s ahead, 3 s, twice the hold and its 2 s margin, less the trail: 36 s of audio here) and, with the EQ on, one more pass of the EQ over them: 21 ms of this machine's CPU at 44.1 kHz 16-bit, 122 ms at 192 kHz 24-bit (0.58 and 3.4 ms a second of audio decoded), lost in the run-to-run spread of the two songs' whole 0.3 to 0.5 s and 1.1 to 1.5 s. On a Q2, by the ratio the analysis measured (about 10 times this machine), that is an estimate of 0.2 s and 1.2 s a change, on the reader's thread, which the second core can take, and while the hold runs three decodes' worth at once (the first at twice real time on the playback thread, the second on the reader's): about 2% of a core at 44.1 kHz and 10% at 192 kHz in all, against 1% and 7% with a ring. Not measured on a Q2. ponytail: a long MP4's sample index is held twice while its second open is there, as it is for the analysis's open ([Podcasts and Audiobooks](#podcasts-and-audiobooks)).
