Checks: `test/player/dsp_test.c` (`crossfade_check`, `midmix_check`; `filed_check`: seven changes, each once with the tail in the ring and once read from a stand-in for the file, the frames out equal to the bit through ReplayGain and its clip, the EQ and its memory carried into the next song, another rate and mono, a plan's trail, and a new EQ, Mono Audio and Swap L/R changed inside the hold; the seeks above; a stand-in that stops giving frames before the hold, in it and under the next song, each as [above](#the-tail-and-a-stalled-card): the ring's output to the bit, one step forward with nothing twice, and a tail that only ever falls to nothing in steps no larger than the 0.2 s ramp's) and `test/player/run.py` `test_tail_file_*` (the player's output with the tail read from the file compared byte for byte with the same change held in a ring, `Q2PLAYER_XF_RING`: FLAC 44.1 kHz 16-bit, FLAC 96 kHz 24-bit with a 12.45 s hold the 6 MB ring cuts, FLAC 192 kHz 24-bit into 44.1 kHz with the 5 s floor the 6 MB ring cuts, ALAC, WAV, the EQ with ReplayGain, the plain fade; `_card_stalls_2s`: the reader's decode stopped for 2 s of the song in the hold and under the next song, the output still the ring's and the song never short; `_card_gone_before_the_hold`, `_in_the_hold`, `_under_the_next_song`: stopped for good, each the fallback above; `_second_open_late`: the 6 MB ring's cut change at 96 kHz, logged), `test_tail_mp3_is_held_in_memory`. These wait for the analysis and the reader by `Q2PLAYER_XF_WAIT` and stall the reader by `Q2PLAYER_TAIL_STALL`, counted in the song's frames (`player/tail.c`), so none depends on how busy the machine is: the whole set passed 20 runs of 20 beside 14 busy loops. `_starved` alone runs without them, on one core, and takes whichever of the unstarved ring's two changes the starved player managed. Each was seen to fail: the second open begun a frame off is refused (`not at the song's frames`), and with that comparison taken out the notes catch it (`differs from the first decode`); the EQ left out of `stages`, a setting's change ignored or taken a frame late, the EQ's memory taken after the block instead of before, and the mix's window a frame late each fail the comparison. `test_crossfade` (two FLACs: the first exact to its last 2 s, those mixed under the second at equal power) for the plain fade; [Smart Crossfade](#smart-crossfade) has its own; `test/patch.py`: the one row, its key read from a config the length picker saved, Gapless turned on with it; `test/fw/test_crossfade.py`: the row's caption with Gapless off and back, `XFADE_NEXT`'s two lines and their rewrite on a Play Next, none without a fade; `test/playback.py`: the policy, the word written for another album's next track and at Repeat All's wrap, none for the same album, a DSD, missing or empty next, with Gapless off, Repeat One or at the queue's end, the change's songs named, the stop count and a file error's status not moving it (status and files set by hand), stock Shuffle's draw (asked about, played, uniform, the pool left alone, a new queue, Previous), no file while Smart Crossfade is off, and the filter put in the chain.

## Smart Crossfade

With **Smart Crossfade** on, the player picks each change's overlap from the two songs' loudness, as the "Smart fades" switch in the Android app Symfonium does: a song that fades out overlaps the next for as long as its fade is quiet, a next song with a soft intro plays that intro under the song ending, every overlap is at least 5 s and at most 15 s, trailing silence is skipped, and the next song comes in at its first sound. demo's word is `XF_FALLBACK_MS | XF_SMART` ([Crossfade: Policy](#crossfade)); the player does the rest (`player/smart.c`, `player/dsp.c` `smart_want`).

**When.** `XF_SMART_LEAD_S` (45 s) before the song's media-info length, the chain asks `smart_begin` for a plan, with the song's file (`dsp_path`) and its ReplayGain scale. A thread of its own (detached, nice `SMART_NICE` 10, below the playback thread) reads `/tmp/q2xfade.next`, checks its first line names the playing song (either path ending with the other) and opens both songs a second time with the player's own decoder (`source_open`). It never plays anything; the song keeps playing from the first open. The hold waits for the plan up to the plain fade's own hold point (length less twice 5 s less `XF_LEAD_S`); then the plan is given up and the plain fade holds as before. A plan that comes too late for its own, longer hold is the plain fade too. The longest hold is what the ring holds, 16.3 s at 44.1 kHz stereo (below), which starts twice that plus `XF_LEAD_S` from the end, 34.7 s; the lead leaves the analysis over 10 s before it.

**Measuring.** The playing song's last `tail_s` (30 s) and the next song's first `head_s` (30 s) are each made a loudness envelope: the RMS of `window_ms` (50 ms) windows over every channel, in dB of full scale, after the song's ReplayGain scale and hard clip as the chain applies them (`sample`), digital silence as -200 dB. The playing song's windows are counted back from its last frame and the next song's forward from its first, so the plan is in frames from the end and from the start, which is how the hold counts too; a seek that lands a little off moves nothing. The tail is decoded twice, once to find the last frame and once to measure: holding the frames instead would take 23 MB at 192 kHz. A song shorter than a span is measured whole: the tail from the song's first frame, the head to its last, and the rules below read the windows there are.

**Rules.** In one table, `SR` in `player/smart.c`; body is a song's median window (the lower one of an even count) over what was measured:

| Point | Rule | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| tail_end | the end of the last window above max(floor, body - tail_below); the frames after it are dropped, never played | floor -60 dBFS, tail_below 45 dB |
| out run | the run of windows below body - quiet_below that ends at tail_end, when it starts inside the 30 s (a run that reaches the span's start is a quiet song, not a fade: none) | quiet_below 12 dB |
| skip | the next song's leading windows below floor, the most skip_max | 5 s |
| next intro | the next song's run of windows from its first sound (after the skip) below its later body - intro_below; its later body is the median of its windows from overlap_max after its first sound to the end of the 30 s, or its body when under later_min of those were decoded | intro_below 10 dB, later_min 5 s |
| overlap | the longest of the out run, the next intro and overlap_min, at most overlap_max; out_point is tail_end less the overlap. The plan's log line names which one decided it (`by the out run`, `by the next intro`, `by the floor`) | overlap_min 5 s, overlap_max 15 s |
| fade-in | none when the next song's start (its loudest window in start_ms after the skip) is within hard_within of its body: a hard start is never faded in. Else fade_min, longer for a quieter start, up to fade_max at fade_span further down | start_ms 200, hard_within 6 dB, 0.3 to 1 s over 14 dB |

The brief that asked for this worded the fade-in rule the other way round ("0.3 to 1 s if it starts within 6 dB of its body") and also said a song with a hard start must not be faded in; the second is the rule here. A plan is the same for the same two files, every time.

The intro's margin, 10 dB under the next song's later body, is about half as loud: a passage that far down (a solo instrument before the band, a spoken or ambient opening) sits under the outgoing song's ending without the two fighting, while a verse a few dB under its chorus is not taken for an intro and does not stretch the overlap. The intro is measured against the next song's later body, not its body over the 30 s, because an intro as long as the cap would be half the windows and pull the median down to its own level, so the intro would not read as soft at all; the intro an overlap can use ends by 15 s, so the windows after that are the song itself. An intro over about 22 s (half of the 15 s measured past 15 s, for a song with no leading silence) still pulls that median down and reads as no intro: that change gets the floor.

**Mixing.** The hold is the plan's overlap and trail (`smart_want`): the overlap capped at `XF_MAX_S` (15 s). A FLAC, ALAC or PCM file's tail is read from the file ([The tail, from the file](#the-tail-from-the-file)) and has no other limit at any rate, but the time there is: the hold begins twice its length and `XF_LEAD_S` before the end, the plan is asked for `XF_SMART_LEAD_S` (45 s) before it, and a plan that comes too late for its hold is cut to what a ring would have held, then given up for the plain fade if still too late; a 15 s overlap with up to 5 s of trail begins 42 s from the end. Any other song's hold is also capped at what the 6 MB ring holds at the song's rate and channels (16.3 s at 44.1 kHz stereo, 15.0 s at 48 kHz, 8.2 s at 88.2 kHz, 7.5 s at 96 kHz, 3.75 s at 192 kHz: the overlap is cut, logged, and a trail longer than the ring is the plain fade), so there the ring, not `XF_MAX_S`, is what bounds a stereo song above 48 kHz, and the 5 s floor too at 176.4 and 192 kHz; at 48 kHz a 15 s overlap is cut by any trail over 20 ms, and at 44.1 kHz by a trail over 1.3 s. A mono song's ring holds about twice as long. When the next song's first block comes, the trail is dropped from the tail's end; if that song is the one the plan named (`xf.plan.next`), its first skip frames are dropped and its fade-in applies, else neither, logged. The tail fades out under it as cos over the overlap when the overlap is its own quiet run, and as cos squared when the next intro or the floor decided it (`in_body`): that overlap begins in the song's body, at full level, and under cos it would stay within 3 dB of it for the overlap's first half while the next song plays, two songs at full level at once. Rendered through the player (a half-scale tone to its last frame, then a hard start at half scale: the floor's 5 s), the sum's RMS over each second of the overlap, over either song alone, was +2.9, +2.1, +1.0, +0.2 and 0.0 dB under cos squared, where cos gives +2.9, +2.5, +1.8, +0.8 and +0.1 dB: at the middle the outgoing song is 6 dB down where cos has it 3 dB down. The first second is the same under any curve, as the next song is at full level from its first frame. Under a 10 s soft intro 22 dB down, the outgoing song is 4.7 dB down 5 s in and 10.8 dB down 7 s in (cos: 2.3 and 5.5), so the intro is heard over the overlap's second half rather than its last 3 s. The next song is at full level, or sin over its fade-in; at another rate the tail is read by linear interpolation, as the plain fade's is. Equal power can sum to 1.41 times either song on matching material, so a smart mix goes through `limit`: a gain that drops at once to what keeps the frame under `XF_CEIL` (0.99) and recovers over `XF_RELEASE_S` (50 ms), carried on into the next song alone until it is back at 1. Nothing is added where the sum stays under the ceiling, so the frames before the overlap and after it are each song's own, bit for bit.

**Falls back** to the plain 5 s fade, with one log line `q2player: smart crossfade: plain, ...` saying why: no next song named, or named for another change; the playing song or the next one a stream, not on the card, or still arriving short of its first 31 s at its average rate (`grow_have`; the playing one must be whole); a decode that fails; no sound in the last 30 s; a trail longer than the ring; the analysis not done by the plain hold's point, or done too late for its own. A plan says what it chose in one line: `q2player: smart crossfade: body ... dB, overlap ... s by the out run|next intro|floor (out run ... s, next intro ... s, floor 5.00 s) from ... s before the end, ... s of tail dropped; next body ... dB, later ... dB, ... s skipped, start ... dB, fade-in ... ms`, the three candidates as measured before the 15 s cap, and the analysis's CPU in another.

**Gapless.** Every fade needs stock's Gapless on, as before: it is what has demo send the next song's preload (`set-gapless`), which the mix needs to start on the open PCM. The owner ruled (2026-11-23) to keep that requirement, and the row turns Gapless on with it ([Crossfade](#crossfade)).

**Cost.** Each analysis decodes the tail twice and the head once: with 30 s spans and the tail's 2 s of seek margin, 94 s of audio for songs longer than the spans, against 59 s with spans of 20 s and 15 s. Measured on this machine (x86-64, 2026-11-24, shared with other builds) on two 200 s 44.1 kHz stereo pink-noise FLACs: 55, 85 and 101 ms of one core's CPU over three runs, against 34, 40 and 64 ms with the 20 s and 15 s spans. On a Q2 the 20 s and 15 s spans measured 0.69 to 0.86 s; scaled by the audio decoded (1.6 times) that is an estimate of 1.1 to 1.4 s, and by this machine's median ratio (2.1 times, a noisy figure) 1.5 to 1.8 s, on the second core, once a song, inside the over 10 s it has before the longest hold has to start. The 30 s figures are an estimate, not measured on a Q2.

ponytail: the position the player reports counts the held frames as heard, so a song's clock runs ahead by up to the hold (15 s and its trail) in its last seconds. Counting them out would hold demo's own preload back: stock's `mclAutoChange` sends `set-gapless` under 6 s from the end by that same position, so any hold over about 5.5 s would reach the file's end before the preload, and the change would be a cold start with a gap. Lifting it needs demo to preload early while a fade is set.

Checks: `test/player/run.py` `test_smart_crossfade` (A: a tone, a 6 s fade to nothing, its quiet run 1.5 s, and 2 s of silence, 24 s in all, shorter than the span; B: 1.5 s of silence and a hard start: the 5 s floor, the plan equal to the rules written again in Python over the reference decodes, A exact to out_point, the overlap within 2 steps of B + A cos squared, B exact after, no step at either end, A's silence never played, the plan's line naming the floor), `_intro` (A loud to its last frame, B a 10 s intro 22 dB down: 10 s by the next intro, B faded in over 1 s), `_cap` (B a 20 s intro: 15 s, and the intro read against B's later body, where its body over the 30 s is the intro's own level), `_long_fade` (A's last 25 s a fade of 2 dB a second: 9 s by the out run, under cos), each checked as the first; `_next_missing`, `_next_unknown`, `_next_arriving` (the grow harness's `.stream`), `_too_slow` (`Q2PLAYER_SMART_DELAY_MS`): each the plain fade exactly, logged once; `_off_is_gapless`: word 0, the two songs bit for bit and nothing analysed; `_starved`: the player on one core with two busy loops on it and stopped for 300 ms of every second (`Q2_TEST_STARVE`), the change still whole, smart or (logged) plain, which a tail dropped too soon fails. `test/player/dsp_test.c` `smart_check`, with the plan given: an `in_body` plan's tail fading out as cos squared; the analysis asked for once, 45 s before a 60 s song's end and not before; the same full-scale tone in phase on both sides stays under `XF_CEIL` where the plain fade reaches 1.3, and the next song is bit for bit again once the limiter lets go; 44.1 kHz stereo into 48 kHz mono reads every frame of the overlap and none of the trail; the skip, a fade-in, a hard start at full level from its first frame; a stop after the hold leaves the next song whole. Each was seen to fail with a rule or a fallback changed in the player; `smart_check` first failed on the code itself, a peak of 0.9904 (the limiter's recovery stepped past what the frame allowed) and a gain stuck at 0.99993 for good (its recovery in float stalled short of 1), both fixed. The floor, intro, cap and long-fade cases failed on the 20 s and 15 s spans and the run rule before them (overlaps of 1.45, 5, 5 and 3.95 s), as did the cos squared and the 45 s lead in `smart_check`.

## Mono Audio

**Playback → Mono Audio** (`ringnav_audioset`, stock's `playset_balance` icon, below Balance; `mono_row` and `mono_click` in `patch/crossfade.c`) reads `Mono Audio: On` or `Off` and toggles `Q2POD MONO` in `config.ini` (default 0). `mono_sync`, from `playback_poll` each UI pass and on each toggle, writes it to `/tmp/q2mono`, an `int` made under `.tmp`, renamed and mapped shared, as `/tmp/q2xfade` is. Nothing is created until Mono Audio is first turned on, and a missing file reads as off. Every reader maps the file and picks up a change within one block:

- **hciplayer** (local music, Tidal; DAC, Bluetooth and USB): the PEQ filter's `play()` sets both channels of each stereo frame to their mean, after `peq_process` and before the crossfade and AirPlay's tap. Per-channel bands and the EQ's balance shape each side first. Stock's Balance acts after the mix. The file is looked for once a second of audio until it appears (`watch`, shared with `xfade_ms`). Boot leaves the filter out with the EQ off, so `mono_sync` calls `peq_chain` while Mono Audio is on, as a fade does. ponytail: `peq_chain` waits for play (status not 1, stopped) for all three callers, since whether an attach while stopped sticks is unknown.
- **q2video** (Videos, Internet Radio, Spotify's sink): `writer` mixes each S16 chunk after the soft volume (`mono`), looking for the file every hundredth chunk until it appears.
- **Spotify on the headphone DAC** normally plays through `aplay`. With Mono Audio on, `spot_output` writes `plughw:0,0 hVOLUME` to `SPOT_OUT`, so `aplay.sh` runs `q2video -s` there instead; the `h` keeps the volume on the DAC, and `sound_open` readies the DAC (`DAC_PCM`, `DAC_MUTE`) for any `plughw:0,0`, volume or not.

ponytail: DSD, DoP and native DSD output pass through bit-exact (`dsd()`) and stay stereo, and so does stock's AirPlay receiver. On the headphone DAC, switching Spotify's sink between `aplay` and `q2video` waits for the sink's next start (pause and play), like a new output device does. q2video already playing on another output follows the switch at once.

Checks in `test/peq.py` (host builds): the filter's mix once the file appears, live, and exact again when cleared; `mono` on S16 at both ends of the range. `test/patch.py`: the row, its place after Balance, the saved key, and the shared int set live, mapped once.

## Resume

`ringnav_sleep` (the UI thread) polls at most once a second. It reads the queue's playing record (`queue_now`) and `player_playtime_and_length` (`0x51ee10`): elapsed and total track seconds, CUE-relative, and -1 while nothing plays. A track is long when its total is at least **Playback → Resume Songs** (`Q2POD RESUMEMIN`, minutes; `crossfade.c` `resume_min`, read once), or its extension is `.m4b` (case-insensitive) anywhere on the card, or it is under [Podcasts or Audiobooks](#podcasts-and-audiobooks), and its record has no CUE start or end (`+0x48`, `+0x4c`). A CUE track (either set) is long only when spoken (`.m4b`, or under those folders), so a music CUE image is left alone. Places are kept by the path's FNV-1a hash in a ring of `RESUME_SLOTS` (512, a 4 KB file), most recent first, as file seconds: a CUE track's place is its start plus its elapsed seconds, so a book's chapters share one place, and the same file played whole resumes there too. The ring is read from the card's `.q2pod/ringnav-resume` on the first long track and written whole, to a `.tmp` then renamed ([Where Q2 Muse writes](#where-q2-muse-writes): kept in RAM while the card is away; the flash's `/mnt/data/ringnav-resume` from earlier releases is read until the card has a copy). That happens every `RESUME_SAVE_S` (60) seconds of movement, once the time stands still for two polls (a pause), and on a track change. A place within `RESUME_EDGE_S` (30 s) of either end of the file is forgotten. A CUE track saves nothing within its own first `RESUME_EDGE_S`, keeping the book's place, so a chapter played becomes the book's place once past its first 30 s; only the last CUE track (no end set) knows the file's end, where the book is finished and its place forgotten. A track change, `listen_key` (the path's hash with a CUE start mixed in, so moving to the next chapter counts), waits one poll before it counts, so the previous track's time never belongs to the new one. When a long track with a saved place first plays (elapsed at least 1 s) with under `RESUME_START_S` (5 s) elapsed, `player_seek_time` jumps there, as Scrub commits. A track paused at 0 waits for Play, so Memory Playback's paused boot does not seek, and its Location restore, already under way, is left alone. A CUE track never jumps when played: a chapter picked is played from its start. Instead the [Queue menu](#queue-menu) of a spoken CUE song row whose file has a place starts with **Resume** (`book_place`): it copies the page's songs (type 8) and plays them as a library queue (`play_folder(..., 0xf001)`, as Most Played) from the last chapter of that file starting at or before the place, with the seconds into it waiting for that chapter's `listen_key`, for up to 8 s. The poll seeks there once that chapter plays under `RESUME_START_S`, so the previous position the player still reports, or a queue that switches a poll or two late, does not consume it; the chapter already playing works the same way. With no place left at the pick, the menu says "Queue unchanged". The ring's format is unchanged, so places saved before stay valid: an earlier release's 32-slot file loads as the first 32 places, and an earlier build reads the first 32, the most recent, of the bigger one. A hash collision only means a wrong resume point.

A restart of the same file reaches the poll as a move to the start, which forgets the place, so hooks stop one before it happens: Previous and Next ask through `restart_refused`, and a pick of the playing file starts nothing. On a track holding a place worth keeping (`resume_held`: over `RESUME_EDGE_S` from either end, at the player's live time, or the last polled one once stopped, and not a CUE track, whose restart leaves the book's place alone), in a local queue, such a press does nothing but toast "Press again to restart", through `playback_poll` since a headset key can arrive off the UI thread. Only a second press of the same key (Previous or Next, `restart_key`) within `RESTART_ASK_MS` (3 s) goes ahead, and the place is forgotten. Another key asks again and arms for itself, so Previous can't confirm what a stray Next asked, and a press that wouldn't restart ends the window. The toast is stock's `msginfo_dialog`, up for 2 s of the 3, and its own key-up handler (`0x49b7c8`) stops Previous, Next and Play; `on_wm_keyup_fun` comes after the window's children in AWTK's dispatch (inferred from that return value, not run). So `ringnav`, ahead of the windows, sends the armed key on to its quick click while a dialog is on top. ponytail: the toast stays up its time over a restart, as closing it early means its private timer's cleanup, and another key under it is still stopped, so it doesn't ask again until the toast has gone. A headset press goes straight to `player_prev_music`, past the dialog. A refused press stamps nothing for the [press gate](#a-press-not-a-natural-change); a confirmed one does as usual. A long track here is what Resume keeps a place for: at least **Resume Songs** minutes (30 by default, 20-120 or Off), an `.m4b`, or under Podcasts or Audiobooks. There is no other length test, as a shorter track has no place for the guard to protect.

- **Previous** (`ringnav_seek_start`, `player_seek_start`, `0x51f090`). Stock's `player_prev_music` (`0x5202e8`) calls it first on anything playing or paused (`mclGetPlayStatus`, `0x520358`). From 3 s of `player_playtime` it seeks to the track's start and returns 1, in any queue and mode, so `player_change_music` is never reached; a refusal returns 1 too. Under 3 s it returns 0 and Previous changes track as below. Stock's threshold was 11 s (`slti $2, $2, 11` at `0x51f0ec`); `PREV_RESTART` in `tools/build.py` makes it 3, an iPod's ([ipod.md](ipod.md#previous-and-next)), and `ringnav_seek_start` asks the restart guard at the same second (`PREV_RESTART_S`). `player_prev_music` is the seek's only caller. Getting from a long track to the one before takes three presses now, as the place has to be given up first: ask, restart, move.
- **Next, and Previous when stopped or under 3 s** (`ringnav_change`, `player_change_music`). `change_restarts` says when a press would start the playing file again. With more tracks stock moves on, Repeat One too, so outside advanced play that is a one-track queue, unless Folder Skip's sibling folder (class 1, not an M3U, and not stock Shuffle's Previous, which goes back to its last position first) or List Play's stop at a library queue's end takes the press (`test/playback.py` holds it to stock's `player_change_music` over the play modes, classes, Folder Skip, M3U and that position); in advanced play, the track's successor or history entry being the playing one. Stock's skip past a file it can't play (`on_wm_timer_dialog`, `press_natural`) is automatic and never asks.
- **A pick of the playing file** (`ringnav_player_start`, `player_start`, `0x520b4c`; `song_playing` in `song_rows.c`). Stock's `player_start` reloads the queue and starts the file at 0, and no caller reads its result; a tap on the playing song's row restarted it (the user's report, 2026-11-18). The hook asks whether the entry is the song playing or paused, by identity, never by title: the same path, CUE start and CUE end as the queue's playing row, so a chapter row while the file plays whole is another track, and a server row (its `fileurl`) is the song its Stream Cache copy plays (`catalogue_row_path`). Any such pick is refused, a long track's or a short song's; a stopped player never is. The same row of the same list (index, size and class equal to the queue's) changes nothing. From another list of the queue's class (stock's class: a folder's, an album's, a playlist's) that list's songs after it replace the queue's after the song playing, as a radio of it does (`playback_queue_rest`), with no load, and Up Next's "From" is that list (`un_source_take`); from a list of another class, or one holding a server row (the firmware plays none after it), the queue stays as it is. What follows goes by the caller, told by its return address:
  - `playing_page_init` (`0x53e50c`, returning to `0x53e514`), which `play_folder` and stock's lists fill: the page goes on and opens itself.
  - The album pages' play (`0x4a97a8`, `0x4abff0`, in handlers such as `0x4a96c0`), which stay on their page after a start: `playback_np` opens Now Playing, class 0xff, as `on_backplay_click` does.
  - SyncLink (`0x5264bc`, `0x5266ac`), off the UI thread: silent, opening nothing. The track keeps playing, which is what the phone asked for.
  - `testmode_test_key` (`0x4d9c60`) goes the same silent way if it ever names the playing file.

  From the first two, a paused file also goes on (`player_play_pause`). Its Play waits for the DAC by itself (`dac_resume`), so it needs no stamp. A refused pick stamps nothing, and a long track keeps its place as it plays on. Not presses, and left alone: an app's `.play` (`press_natural`), Shuffle Albums' own load (`s.grouping`), and DLNA and online classes. Restarting a long track is Previous twice.

- **A queue row of the playing file.** View Queue's (`0x53acf0`, returning to `0x53acf8`; the playing row by `song_playing`, a short song's too) and Up Next's (`un_click`) open Now Playing as the album pages do. `player_start_queue`'s other callers (a queue delete, DLNA, URL plays) keep stock's start, at the cost of one more return address.
- **A shuffle drawing it** (`shuffle_play`, Shuffle Songs and the Queue menu's Shuffle). Not a pick of it: it draws another index, before anything changes, or with one song opens Now Playing.
- **A start after a stop.** `resume_poll` notes a stop (`rs_stopped`: time -1 with `mclGetPlayStatus` 1, not a load's or seek's -1), and a later start of the same key under `RESUME_START_S` goes back to the second it stopped at, whether by a pick, by Play or after List Play's Next stopped it, instead of forgetting the place. A confirmed restart clears it (`resume_restart`).

test/playback.py drives these from `prev_quick_click` and `next_quick_click` (`0x4f2db0`, `0x4f2e54`, from `on_wm_keyup_fun`) through stock's real `player_prev_music` and `player_seek_start`, since a test entering at `player_change_music` runs below the seek and never sees it.

ponytail: other ways back to the same file's start still forget the place, none of which can be told before the press: stock Shuffle at the end of its pool, which refills with the playing track and can draw it again (`mcl_shuffle_pick`, 1 in n), and Folder Skip with no sibling folder, which falls back to a wrap (`mclNextSong`). The hooks' class filter keeps a DLNA or online queue's Previous and Next stock's; `dmr_mainscheduling` only sends a Next with 2 or more rows, so it moves on anyway. SyncLink's Previous and Next arrive as keys (`main_loop_post_key_event`) and can't be told from the Q2's own, so they ask too, on the Q2's screen. A stop isn't noticed if the player stops and starts between two polls, about a second apart: the place is forgotten as before.

Memory Playback's snapshot takes precedence over a track's place only when it has a time to give (`playback_resumed`). **Track** gives none, so a long track there resumes at its own place instead of starting at 0 and then overwriting it, and **Location** with a saved time of 0 does the same.

**Resume Songs** (`ringnav_audioset`, stock's `playset_memplay` icon, after Memory Playback in the reorder) reads `Resume Songs: 30 min` or `Resume Songs: Off` and opens Crossfade's re-dressed Boot volume page (`xfade_open` ctx 2): no switch, the slider and wheel stepping five minutes through 20-120, below 20 Off; each change is saved (a drag at its release, as Crossfade) and live on the next track. `RESUMEMIN` is 30 unless `0` (Off) or a multiple of five in 20-120; anything else reads as 30. Off stops music tracks keeping a place; spoken audio (`.m4b`, Podcasts, Audiobooks) still resumes at any length. The default was a fixed 20 minutes before this row, so a track of 20-30 minutes no longer resumes until the row is lowered.

## Folder entry

Folder opens directly at `/mnt/mmc`, layer 2, when `g_otg_status` is clear and the card is present on entry (`/tmp/mmc_add` readable, stock's `check_tfstatus` at `0x503108`). After stock initializes the page, `ringnav_folder` stores `/mnt/mmc` in `media_root`, sets the path and runs the existing reload, title and refresh functions, the same block a shortcut uses at layer 3. Back where `g_folder_path` equals `media_root` sets layer 1 before stock Back decrements it to 0 and leaves the page, even if OTG was connected meanwhile. With OTG connected or no card on entry, the storage selector and stock navigation remain, and `media_root` is cleared. Nested folders and playback use the existing handlers. Podcasts/Audiobooks shortcuts take precedence and retain their own root exit.

**The title.** Stock's navbar names the storage at layers 1 and 2 (`SD`) and a path or a folder's name below (`SD:/Music`); the status row says **Folders** at the card's root and the storage list, and the folder's own name, the path's last part, deeper (`folder_title` in `bar_title_sync`, `patch/navigation.c`).

**An empty level.** Stock's `folder_page` is its table (`tableview_folder`) and nothing else, so a level with no rows (an empty card, or a folder with nothing stock lists) would be a blank page under its title. `feedback_folder` (`patch/feedback.c`), run on the status bar's paint beside `feedback_songs`, reads the level's rows from `p_deque_showlist`, as the table does, and when the top window is `folder_page` and the count is 0 shows the empty state, **No Folders** with the hint **Copy music to the SD card** (**No SD Card** with no card in; [oled-design](oled-design.md#empty-and-offline)). It writes only when the level's emptiness changes (the window's `_empty_folder`), and a level with rows hides it again.

**Folder delete.** Stock's multi-select Delete in Folder view (touch only; the `msg_delfile` confirm) runs `batch_delete_file(1, ...)`, which takes the marked rows' songs out of the library and calls `remove_file` (`0x4ffff0`) on each row's path: a file goes with `remove()`, but a folder with `rm -rf "<path>"` (format `0x782ff8`) for `system()`, where `/bin/sh`, as root, still expands `$` and backticks inside the double quotes. A folder named `$NOT` removed its parent folder, `Ke$ha` a folder named `Ke`, and a name could run commands. That `snprintf` (`jalr` at `0x5000f0`, `FOLDER_RM_CALL`; the format's `addiu` in its delay slot is pinned) becomes `jal ringnav_folder_rm` (`patch/folder_delete.c`): the same `rm -rf`, the path inside single quotes, each `'` written `'\''`, so nothing in it is expanded. A path that does not fit stock's 0x61b bytes quoted leaves `:`, which removes nothing.

## Folder Root

**Settings → Playback → Library → Folders → Folder Root** (`folder_root_row`, stock's `playset_folderjump` icon, restacked before Folder Skip) reads `Folder Root: Card` or `Folder Root: <name>`: the string `Q2POD FOLDERROOT` in `config.ini` (`toolsReadConfig`, `toolsWriteConfig`), missing or empty for the card. Center or tap (`root_click`) reads `/mnt/mmc` once and saves the next top-level directory (`d_type` 4, or 0 unknown, as `media_find`) after the saved one in `strcasecmp` order (FAT and exFAT hold no two names differing only in case), dot-folders left out; "" (Card) gives the first, after the last it saves "", and a saved name no longer there moves on to the next name after it. ponytail: names over `ROOT_MAX` (200) bytes or starting or ending with a space are not offered, since stock's config line (`toolsWriteConfig`'s `sprintf` into 257 bytes, `toolsReadConfig`'s 255-byte `fgets`, then trimmed) can't keep them.

On a Folder visit with a card (`/tmp/mmc_add`), `ringnav_folder` opens `/mnt/mmc/<name>` at layer 3 through the media roots' block when it is a directory (`__xstat`; a name with `/` or a leading dot is ignored); a pending Podcasts/Audiobooks root wins, and without the folder the visit is as in [Folder entry](#folder-entry). `media_root` stays `/mnt/mmc` without a drive, so the root is an ordinary folder: stock Back (`folder_back`) strips the last name to `/mnt/mmc` at layer 2, titled Folders ([Folder entry](#folder-entry)), and Back there leaves the page; with a drive it reaches stock's storage selector. Every root's open (the card, Folder Root, Podcasts, Audiobooks) first runs stock's `folder_reset_variable` (`0x511f2c`), as Back to layer 0 does: layer, path, `g_m3u_path` and the `g_yoffset_save`/`g_index_save` stacks cleared, and `g_navbar_status` and `g_allselect_flag` zeroed (the multi-select state, which stock's `folder_enter`, `folder_back` and page inits clear too). A visit left without Back (Home, a song opening Now Playing) keeps them, and `folder_back` pops a non-empty stack into the page's position and, inside an M3U (`g_m3u_path` set), reloads the same path instead of stepping up, so Back from the root would have landed on a stale position or stayed in the root a layer short. With the stacks empty the step up keeps the back handler's zeroed position, the top of the card's list.

Checks in `test/patch.py` (stock `folder_back` and `folder_reset_variable` executed): the root at layer 3 after a visit left deep and inside an M3U, Back to `/mnt/mmc` (layer 2, title, position untouched), then out of the page or to the selector with a drive; a gone, file, hidden or path root, no root and no card as before; Podcasts' own root; the row's cycle, order, skipped names (a UTF-8 name with a space kept), saved value and a gone root.

## Podcasts and Audiobooks

Folder's row-name formatter treated names as printf formats, crashing on `99% Invisible` even with Folder Album Cover off. `FOLDER_NAME` in `tools/build.py` changes the call at `0x532cc0` to `tk_strncpy(buffer, name, 511)`, keeping its 512-byte buffer terminated and displaying percent signs literally in folder and file names. The real row callback is exercised in `test/patch.py` with percent signs, format directives and an overlong name.

`ringnav_localmusic` reads `/mnt/mmc` (`opendir`/`readdir`) and adds a row for a directory (`d_type` 4, or 0 unknown) named `Podcasts` or `Audiobooks`, ASCII case aside, last, with build-added 52 px icons drawn in stock's style in `assets/icons/` (`local_podcasts`, purple with a microphone, and `local_audiobooks`, orange with headphones). A press (`media_click`, also Home's Shortcut set to Podcasts or Audiobooks) looks the folder up again and `navigator_to("folder_page")`s, as Home's Folder card (`on_home_folder_onclick`) does; with the folder gone it toasts "No Podcasts folder on the card" instead. Stock's folder browser keeps its place in globals: `g_folder_layer` (1 the storage list `folder_load_top` builds, 2 a storage root, 3 on deeper folders), `g_folder_path`, `g_navbar_name` (the title) and the `g_yoffset_save`/`g_index_save` stacks, which `folder_enter` pushes and `folder_back` pops. `folder_page_init` (`0x533ed0`, hooked as `ringnav_folder`) always starts at layer 1 (`folder_enter(-1, 0)`). After it, a pending press copies the path in, sets layer 3 and runs stock's `folder_reload_data` (`toolsLoadDirectory` into `p_deque_showlist`), `folder_reinit_navbarname` (layer 3 and on: the path's last name) and the page's navbar and table rebuild (`0x531efc`, `folder_refresh`), as stock's back and refresh do. Every check on the layer elsewhere is `< 2`, so the root is an ordinary folder: entering, song presses (`player_load_songlist(..., 1)`, folder play), covers and the refresh on return from Now Playing are stock's. `folder_back` (`0x512778`, `ringnav_folder_back`) has one caller, the page's back handler (`0x532138`, the title arrow and the Return key); at layer 3 on that root it sets layer 1 first, so stock's step down reaches 0, resets the browser and the handler closes the page, back to Local Music. Any other folder_page open clears the root, so the Folder view's own `/mnt/mmc/Podcasts` climbs as before.

An M4B track anywhere on the card, or a track whose path is under either folder (`/mnt/mmc/<name>/`), is resumed at any length (a CUE track by its file's place and the hold menu's Resume, see [Resume](#resume)) and skips the listen count, so it never reaches Most Played or the scrobble log. The stock speed control (`PLAYSPEED` in `playerjumpinfo_page`) now saves its 0–3 mode by exact parent path; a track with no folder (a Tidal stream) takes it for that track only, unsaved. `ringnav_speed` hooks `mclSetPlaySpeed`; calls returning to `player_initconfig` at `0x51e04c` restore rather than save. `ringnav_start_player` (`playback_track_speed`) sets the folder’s mode and sends it to the running decoder before opening a track, since the decoder otherwise keeps the previous track’s speed, and `ringnav_open_preload` declines gapless across a speed boundary. Files under `/mnt/data/ringnav-speed-<path hash>` contain the full, zero-terminated 1024-byte parent path and a 32-bit mode; reads validate both, writes use `blob_io`’s temporary-file rename. Missing or invalid preferences default to normal. Failed saves show a toast and reload the saved preference. The old global speed is not migrated because it does not identify a folder. shortcut: genre-only Podcast/Audiobook tags do not grant spoken-audio behavior; add a genre source if needed. Every local track start (`ringnav_start_player`) and gapless preload (`ringnav_open_preload`) first checks `.m4b`, `.m4a` and `.mp4` files with `mp4_fits` (`patch/chapters.c`). FFmpeg's mov demuxer, which hciplayer uses for MP4 and `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` uses for Chapters, indexes every sample before it plays, so a 47-hour book's millions of AAC frames outgrow the Q2's 128 MB and the device stalls, again at boot through Memory Playback. `mp4_index_bytes` walks `moov/trak/mdia/minf/stbl` with `fopen`/`fseek` and sums the `stsz`/`stz2` sample counts at `MP4_SAMPLE_BYTES`, 16 bytes each. ponytail: 16 is the low end of a 16–24 byte guess, not measured: FFmpeg's own cost (a 24-byte `AVIndexEntry` and a 4-byte `stsz` size, 28) refused an 18-hour 44.1 kHz book (2.8 M samples, 75 MB of estimate, 83 MB with a start's spare) that played before the check existed, whenever another file was loaded; at 16 it needs about 51 MB and a 47-hour book is still refused (about 117 MB). A book that starts and then stalls the Q2 means raising it. A file `fopen` cannot open because it is 2 GB or more (`EOVERFLOW`, demo has no large-file I/O) counts as too long. The index must fit `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo` less `MP4_SPARE_KB` (16 MB); a failed start returns -1, as stock's own checks do, a gapless preload is declined with stock's failed-attempt state so automatic change ticks do not repeat the scan, and the next UI pass (`playback_poll`) toasts it, since `mclStartPlayer` can run off the UI thread. A start is checked differently from a preload (`mp4_start_fits`): hciplayer runs `uninit_player` on the file it holds before it opens the next ([Crossfade](#crossfade)), so that file's index and buffers are freed first, yet `MemAvailable` still counts them at the check. A start of the file last started (`playback_start_fits`' `started`, RAM only), such as a CUE book's next chapter, is therefore not checked, which would need room for the book twice; a start of another MP4 has the held file's index (`mp4_index_bytes(started)`) added to `MemAvailable`, and its spare is `MP4_START_SPARE_KB` (8 MB) instead of 16 MB, since the outgoing decoder's buffers come back too. Without that, a book could not start while another book of its size was loaded, which the one resumed at boot always is: someone who plays only audiobooks saw every other book refused. A start of a nonlocal track clears `started`, as the book is closed by then. A gapless preload opens beside the playing file and is checked in full, with the 16 MB. ponytail: RAM taken since the held file's start is not counted; a boot's first start always checks. ponytail: the 8 MB is reasoned, not measured (stalls were recorded near 3 MB of `MemAvailable`); a book that starts and then stalls the Q2 means raising it. Chapters refuses the same files with its own toast. ponytail: the estimate leaves out chunk tables and the decoder's buffers, and MemAvailable is read while the previous track may still be open; tune `MP4_SPARE_KB` from device measurements. `test/chapters.py` checks the estimate on synthetic and real MP4s; `test/patch.py` checks the Chapters refusal.

All Library music views (Songs, Albums, Artists, Composers, Genres, Hi-Res, Frequent, Recent and Recently Added, including their detail lists) exclude `.m4b`, `/mnt/mmc/Audiobooks/` and `/mnt/mmc/Podcasts/` paths with the same case-insensitive SQL predicate as Coverflow (`MUSIC_WHERE`). `ringnav_localclass` scopes `ringnav_library_query` around category loads, split-album queries and Unknown-row checks; the artist page and music album staging use the same scope. The query hook substitutes a filtered `songtable` subquery before grouping, so shared music/spoken-audio tags keep music artwork and spoken-only Unknown categories disappear. Favorites and playlist contents bypass `songtable`: Favorites keep spoken tracks; `music_records` filters only playlists' displayed song copies with `spoken`, preserving music order, playlist containers and every stored entry. Most Played, Long Songs, category Play Next/Add to Queue and Shuffle Songs, Albums and Folders use music-only loads too. Scoped loads restore the caller's filter state, including empty or failed queries. Ratings, podcast and audiobook folder browsing, playback and folder queue expansion stay unfiltered. My Fav, Frequent and Recent (`0xf00a`, `0xf008`, `0xf007`) list stock's copies of songs as added or played; a copy with an empty title, as a song played from Folder has, takes the library's title by path (`fav_titles`), so its row no longer reads as the file name with its track number.

## Buttons lock

Buttons Lock's rows (Controls) and the quick-settings lock tile offer Off and On. They save stock's `SYSSET LOCKFLAG` and `LOCKMODE` 2 (`lock_set`). Stock's key-down and key-up filters apply the mode only while the screen is off: mode 1 rejects wheel keys 172/173; mode 2 rejects Return, Play/Pause and skip keys 222/223; mode 3 rejects both sets. The dark wheel does nothing, and nothing while the card is up (`wheel_lock_gate`, [Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)), so locking it would only light the card (`keylock_gate`) on a pocket brush: earlier versions' Everything (3), Buttons only (2) and Volume only (1) become On, On and Off once at boot (`keylock_boot`, from `ringnav_bootmode`, which writes the keys and stock's bytes, so either order with `config_init` holds), and any other saved mode is On. Center remains the wake key. `KEY_LOCKOUT` is independent, the short debounce after a button press. `ringnav_keylock_rows` replaces the stock row builder; `ringnav_quick_lock` replaces the lock tile callback, and `ringnav_quick_settings` labels the current choice on open.

The lock is the buttons' alone. SyncLink (Eddict Player) has no path of its own to the player: `synclink_mainscheduling` returns a play control as `0x65`, `0x66` or `0x67`, and `on_wm_idle_status` posts it as a press and release of Play/Pause (171), 222 or 223 with `main_loop_post_key_event` (`0x69ebac`, its only caller), so stock's dark filters dropped them like the buttons (#113). `ringnav_post_key` hooks the poster and keeps each post's key and the `time_now_ms` window around it, which the queued event carries as its stamp (`EVENT_TIME`, low word; four posts kept, a match spent); `ringnav_input` dispatches an event matching one with `g_keylock_flag` cleared, then restores it. A button event never matches: it needs the same key stamped within the same millisecond or two.

**The Hold switch (OLED).** Buttons Lock shows itself as the iPod's Hold switch did (`patch/keylock.c`). While it is on (`g_keylock_flag`) a padlock (Phosphor's lock-simple, filled, 13 px, the theme's `keylock_d` or `keylock_l` in each half's Text Primary) is the status row's leftmost slot (`patch/status_row.c` `SLOT_LOCK`, a 13 px box 5 px left of the slot to its right, [Status row slots](#status-row-slots)), painted with the bar while the flag is set, and the clock keeps its place (`clock_place`: centred, or at the row's left on Home in Split). A press the lock holds with the screen off lights the screen for `KEYLOCK_CARD_MS` (1.5 s) with a card over the page: the whole screen, status row too, dimmed to 45% (`KEYLOCK_DIM`, painted over the top window and the bar in `ringnav_paint`), and on it a #1C1C1E card, 185 x 140 with 22 px corners round the screen's middle, holding a 56 px white padlock (`keylock_card_d`), "Buttons Locked" in Inter Medium 16 and "Press Center to unlock" in 13 px Text Secondary (`keylock_paint`). `keylock_gate`, in `ringnav_input` after the wake gate, decides it from stock's own filter (`on_wm_keyup_before_fun`, `0x4f2660`): the wheel's two keys for mode 1, Return, Play/Pause and the previous and next buttons for 2, all six for 3. Return never gets there, as the wake gate drops it in the dark, and SyncLink's posted keys (`remote_match`, not spent) pass. The gate drops the press itself, its long press and its release (`kl.eat`), since a release reaching stock after the screen is lit would act. The screen lights as `awake_screen` does it, but painted first: `g_backlight_status` set, the whole screen painted with the card (`ringnav_wm_paint`), then `enable_fb`, its 50 ms settle and `screen_action(1)`, so the panel never shows the page as it was left. At the card's end the screen goes off as stock's timeout turns it off (`check_to_poweroption`): `g_backlight_status` cleared, then `screen_action(0)`. While it is up another held press starts its time again, a touch goes nowhere, and Center is the wake the hint names: the card goes, the screen stays lit with stock's timeout started again, and the buttons work, as the lock is the dark screen's (`KEYLOCK_LIT`). Under another theme a held press stays stock's, dropped in the dark.

## Videos

**Videos** is the last Local Music row (`media_find` kind 3, `assets/icons/local_videos.png`, blue with a play screen), for a top-level `Videos` folder, case aside. It opens Folder view at that folder (as Podcasts and Audiobooks do, `media_click`), so each subfolder is its own row and nothing is flattened into one list. Its `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.mkv`, `.avi`, `.mov` and `.mpg` files play from there by a row click: its row click (stock's `0x532414`, hooked as `ringnav_folder_click`; it reads the row's index into `p_deque_showlist`, then `folder_enter`, whose 8, a file, it would queue as songs, so a video failed as one) hands a song record whose `REC_PATH` names a video, not a dot file, to `video_click` (`patch/videos.c`), which plays it through `video_play`; select mode (`g_navbar_status`) and every other row stay stock's. Only other extensions are left to stock, which queues them as songs. Stock's folder listing (`toolsLoadDirectory`) takes audio extensions only, so those rows exist only because its extension check (`ringnav_audio_extension`, at its `0x5d4cac` call, told apart by the return address) also takes a video's while `g_folder_path` is in the card's Videos folder (`folder_videos`); elsewhere, and in the library scan, videos stay unlisted. Without it a Videos folder showed stock's empty-folder "File Not Found" (#128). A song played there would queue them too, so `ringnav_load` hands stock's `mclLoadPlayList` a copy of the tracks without videos (`no_videos`), the start index moved to the same song, and leaves the caller's showlist whole; a list of videos alone loads an empty audio queue. Folder hold actions also exclude videos, and video rows have no audio hold menu. A row (`play_video`, `video_play`) calls stock `player_stop` (`0x5208a8`: hciplayer keeps its PCM, `hw:1,0`, open while paused), readies the headphone output on the DAC as stock's `player_start` does before each track (`dac_take`, shared with Spotify's `spot_take`: `config_outputchannel(g_headset_output, 2)`, which powers the DAC with its firmware in headset mode, or `mclSetDacPwr(1)` for a line out the DAC-off timer powered down; then PCM mode, unmuted, and the volume), then `fork`s and `execl`s `/usr/bin/q2video DEVICE PATH [VOLUME]`, the path a plain argument: nothing passes through a shell. `DEVICE` is `plughw:0,0`, the headphone DAC (the CS43131, the only ALSA card; there is no card 1), whose hardware volume (`mclSetVol`, ioctl `0xc0044d00` on `/dev/shanling_dac`) stays the music's. When `mclGetOutputWay` is 1 (Bluetooth) it is `plug:bluealsa`, the PCM hciplayer opens for that way (`0x439118`, string `0x88f2b0`): demo writes `defaults.bluealsa { device "XX:XX:..." profile "a2dp" }` for the connected device to `/mnt/data/asound.conf`, which `alsa.conf` loads, so the name needs no address. There the volume is hciplayer's soft volume: `device_set_volume` (`0x4fec30`) calls `mclSetBtVol(v, v)`, sending `{mcl-setvol\%d}` with `v << 8 | v`, and hciplayer's handler (`0x42c7d0`) calls its `mixer_setvolume` (`0x4287a4`), which sets an `af_volume` level of `0.1 + 0.018 (v - 50)` from 50, `v * softvol-max (20) / 10000` below, and removes the filter at 100 (no `snd_mixer` is imported, so the soft path is the one taken). So the payload passes the effective `headset_gain()` as `VOLUME` (full gain after accepted headset volume, otherwise `g_volume`, 0-100), and the helper scales its samples by the same curve (`bt_gain`, in 1/65536) and leaves the DAC's mute alone. With a USB DAC (2) `DEVICE` is `usb`, which the helper turns into `plughw:N,0` for the card `/proc/asound/cards` lists as `USB-Audio` (card 1 behind the headphone DAC's 0, as stock's `mclUsbAudioSetVol(…, "hw:1")` has it; hciplayer's `hw:2,0` string, `0x43901c`/`0x88f2c0`, is no card on the Q2), and the plug converts the helper's 48 kHz stereo to what the DAC takes. Its volume is `device_set_volume`'s: `mclUsbAudioSetVol(v, v, "hw:1")`, or 100 when `g_usbvol_mode` (Playback' USB volume) is 0, fixed. That sets the DAC's own volume control; a DAC without one leaves `USB_MIXER` (`0xa50044`, no symbol) at -2 and sends hciplayer `{mcl-softvolflag\1}`, whose set-volume handler then applies the same `mixer_setvolume` curve as Bluetooth's. So `VOLUME` is plain `g_volume` (the helper's `bt_gain`) only for a variable volume on a DAC without its own control; otherwise it is `h` and the volume, which the helper shows on its bar and never applies.

While the helper runs, demo's loop goes on (timers, threads, the status bar) but `ringnav_input` drops every input event before the window manager, sending a key's release (`0x114`) to the helper as a datagram on its `AF_UNIX` socket `/tmp/q2video.sock` (`video_key`): Return `q`, Play/Pause `p`, the side buttons 222/223 `b` and `f`. The wheel is the volume, as on Now Playing: a tick steps `g_volume` as the volume dialog's ticks do (`vol_next`: 1 turned slowly, more at speed, up only below 100 and `g_maxvolume`, down to 0, [Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)), calls `device_set_volume(v, 1)` (the DAC's `mclSetLocalVol` ioctl, so the DAC follows at once, and for Bluetooth `mclSetBtVol`, so hciplayer has it after) and `write_int_config(v, "PLAYSET", "VOLUME")`, without stock's dialog, and sends `v` and the volume byte, at an end too. Center toggles the wheel to seeking (`s`, then `b` and `f` per tick) and back (`v`); `video_poll` also puts it back on the volume `SCRUB_MS` (3 s) after the last tick or Center, like Now Playing's scrub. And `ringnav_wm_paint` skips the window manager's paint. `video_poll`, from `ringnav_sleep`, calls `waitpid(WNOHANG)` every pass, meanwhile `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 1)` (`0x4feb38`, the screen, standby and auto-power-off counters `on_wm_idle_status` and `check_to_poweroption` count down) and zeroes `g_dacoff_time`; a pause that lasts `VIDEO_PAUSE_QUIT_MS` (30 s) without a key sends `q`, as Return, since input belongs to the helper and the hold would otherwise keep a paused video (a dropped headset pauses it) lit until the battery runs out. At the helper's end it closes the socket and repaints the whole screen. Music stays stopped. A video picks up where it was stopped: `video_play` writes the second kept for its path (FNV-1a, in the `VIDEO_MARKS` ring, `/mnt/data/ringnav-books`: 64 key/second pairs, the most recently played first, read again and written whole through coverflow.c's `blob_io` by `mark`) to `/tmp/q2video.place`, which the helper reads as its first `-ss`; on its end it writes there the second a Return left it at (`resume_at`: 0 within `EDGE_S`, 30 s, of either end, as [Resume](#resume)'s `RESUME_EDGE_S`, and 0 when it played to the end), and `video_poll` keeps that for the path, unless it and the start were both 0, so a video never resumed takes no slot from the others. A seek still pending at the Return counts.

**q2video** (`patch/video.c`, about 10 KB) is linked by `tools/build.py` against the rootfs's own `libc-2.28.so`, `libpthread` and `libasound.so.2` (no MIPS sysroot: the file declares what it uses), `nan2008`, `fp64` and `/lib/ld-linux-mipsn8.so.1` as the stock binaries, with its own `__start` like glibc's. It runs stock `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` (FFmpeg 4.2): `-ss` the start, `-vf scale=375:320:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease:flags=fast_bilinear,format=bgra,pad=375:320:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2,transpose=clock` (the picture fitted into the landscape 375 × 320 view, then turned clockwise onto the portrait framebuffer, as the boot logo is stored), `-r 25 -f rawvideo pipe:3`, and `-ac 2 -ar 48000 -f s16le pipe:4`. `/dev/fb0` is 320 × 375, 32 bpp with red at bit 16 (ffmpeg's `bgra`) and two pages: `soc_fb.ko`'s `init_var_info` gives every 32-bit format red 16, green 8, blue 0 and `yres_virtual` = `yres` × `layer0_frames` (2 in `module_driver/soc_fb.sh`, `is_rotated=0`); stock `display_logo` (`0x400bf0`) refuses under 18 bpp and stores each pixel as the word `0xff000000 | R << 16 | G << 8 | B` (`0x400f2c`), the 320 × 375 JPEG unturned; demo's AWTK flush thread pans between the two pages (`FBIOPAN_DISPLAY` at `0x639b2c`, then `FBIO_WAITFORVSYNC`). The helper exits without drawing if `FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO` reports anything else. A thread writes the sound with `snd_pcm_writei` in 512-frame chunks (200 ms buffer) and keeps the frames heard (written less `snd_pcm_delay`); frame n goes to the framebuffer at n / 25 s of that clock, a whole frame late is dropped, and it draws the page demo is not showing and pans (`FBIOPAN_DISPLAY`), panning back to demo's page at the end. Nothing counts as heard while ALSA still holds all that was written: through its first fill, at each start and seek, `snd_pcm_delay` is everything written (more at a start through Bluetooth, whose plugin adds the link's own delay, `0x5b64` in `libasound_module_pcm_bluealsa.so`), and counting that as heard ran the clock up to the buffer's 200 ms ahead, so the frames due in it were dropped as late and the picture then stood until the sound caught up. The picture stays on its first frame until the sound starts. Nor does what ALSA's ring still holds count as heard, whatever a plugin answers: the delay is floored at the ring's own count, the buffer (`snd_pcm_get_params` at open) less `snd_pcm_avail`. After a seek's `snd_pcm_drop` and `snd_pcm_prepare` while playing, bluealsa's plugin answers the link's delay alone through the refill: it counts its queue from the pointer its I/O thread last saved (`+0x20c`, written only at `0x6c20` and `0x6c58`), which its stop (`0x6c64`) and prepare (`0x643c`) leave and only its underrun path (`0x740c`) clears. The kernel's delay (the DAC, USB) is never below the ring, so there the floor changes nothing; a failed `snd_pcm_avail` (an XRUN) leaves the delay alone. The video pipe is 4 MB (`F_SETPIPE_SZ`), so ffmpeg is paced by the sound. A `v` sets Bluetooth's gain to `bt_gain` of its volume. `s`, `b`, `f` and `v` show a bar for 1.5 s (`OVERLAY_MS`), drawn on the page after each frame's copy and before the pan, and redrawn with the next frame when paused: `BAR_H` (8) px high, `BAR_Y` (22) px above the picture's bottom and `BAR_X` (40) px in from its ends, clear of the 80 px glass corners, white for the volume of 100 or the position (start plus frames shown plus pending seek) of the length, black for the rest, by byte fills (white and black in BGRA). The length comes from a second `ffmpeg -nostdin -hide_banner -i PATH` started at once, its stderr read on the main loop's poll until it ends (or 4 KB) for `Duration: HH:MM:SS`; without one the position bar is not drawn. Pause holds the writer (the sound buffer plays out, then the clock stops), and with no bar up and no seek pending the loop then waits on its keys for up to a second a pass, not 100 ms; a key's bar and seek are timed from the key, not from the pass's start; a seek restarts ffmpeg once 400 ms after the last tick, at the position plus 10 s per tick; without a sound stream ffmpeg fails at once and it runs again silent on a monotonic clock. After hciplayer's stop it opens the PCM (retrying 2 s; bluealsa takes one client per PCM, so this also waits for hciplayer's close), sets the DAC to PCM (`0xc0044d1b`, 0, as hciplayer does per PCM track, so a DSD track's mode is undone) and unmutes it (`0xc0044d1f`, 0); at the end it mutes it again, as a stopped hciplayer leaves it. ponytail: the frame rate is fixed at 25 and decoding is software, so sources much above the screen's size can fall behind; a smaller encode then plays smoothly.

Checks in `test/peq.py` (host build of `video.c`): ffmpeg's argv with and without sound, the frame pacing, Bluetooth's gain curve and sample scaling, the `Duration` parse, `resume_at`'s edges, and the bar's pixels on a padded-line frame. `test/patch.py`: the Local Music row, the list, the child's `execl` argv after `player_stop`, the DAC power-on, Bluetooth's device and volume, silent USB, every key's datagram, the volume steps and their limits through `device_set_volume` and `write_int_config`, Center's seek mode and its timeout, no other input or paint while playing, the held timeouts, and the end.

## Games

**Games** is Home's row under the Library (`img_games`, bound by `coverflow_home`; the Library's row after the media rows until 2026-11-19), always shown (card games follow the engine's: [Card games](#card-apps)). The games it ships are one list in `patch/peq.h`, `GAME_SUDOKU`, `GAME_VORTEX`, `GAME_SOLITAIRE` and `GAME_SNAKE` (1 lists a game and builds it in, `GAMES_BUILTIN` their count): all four are 0 in this build (the owner, 2026-11-22, while the games in progress are finished), so the chooser holds Bricks and the card's games. A game left out has every use behind `HAS` in `games.c`, so the payload drops its code, and its save on `/mnt/data` is neither read nor written, kept for its return; `test/fw` builds all four (`GAMES_ALL`) so their tests keep running, and `test/patch_suite/12_cards_clock.py` runs their MIPS checks once `peq.h` ships all four again. `games_open` (`patch/games.c`) `calloc`s the whole state, opens a runtime `games_page` (`CTX_DYNAMIC`) with Coverflow's `page_list` chooser (the shipped own games, the engine's, the card's) and a bare `view` sheet, and frees it all when the page closes; the scratch keeps only the pointer. `show` makes the chooser's list insensitive under a game as well as hidden, since stock's hit test skips only the insensitive and a hidden row still took the game's taps (#302); `pick_game` and `pick_card_game` also act only in the chooser. `games_paint`, called from `ringnav_paint` like `coverflow_paint`, draws the sheet with `canvas_fill_rect`, rounded boxes and frames (`canvas_fill_rounded_rect`, `canvas_stroke_rounded_rect`, square where the canvas declines), `caption` (Solitaire's suits through `draw_centred`, the default font's ♠♥♦♣) and, for Vortex and Snake's apple, vgcanvas arcs and dots, in `accent_tone(2)` ([Look](#games-look)), and puts the fill color back. Everything stays clear of the glass's 80 px corners ([Rounded corners](ipod.md#rounded-corners)): Sudoku's centered board already does; Vortex's score, best, level and lives sit `HUD_X` (24) px in; Solitaire's 45 px cards start `SOL_X` (18) px in and `SOL_Y` (6) down, and its two outer columns close their fan up to end `SOL_LOW` (35) px above the bottom instead of 4.

<a id="games-engine"></a>**Engine games.** The chooser lists the game engine's games ([games-engine](games-engine.md); `eng_count`, `eng_game`) after its own (`GAMES_BUILTIN`, none now) and before the card's, so a card game's index is its row less `GAMES_BUILTIN` and `g->engines`. One is screen `ENGINE` + k on the same sheet: `show` opens it (`eng_open`; with no memory for its state the list stays) and closes the one it leaves, first moving the sheet to the screen's top at 320 rows for a game flagged `ENG_FULL` (Cabin Solitaire, drawn over the status row; `popup` centres on that sheet) and back under the status row for any other, `games_paint` hands the sheet's paint to `eng_paint` with final colors and draws the pop-up over it, and `hold` and `run` are the engine's `eng_hold` and `eng_run` there. Its keys: `games_keydown` (from `ringnav_keydown`, before stock's) gives a running game each press, so it knows a held button and stock clicks nothing; `games_key` gives it each release (`engine_key`), except Return, which opens the same Continue / Quit menu as Vortex's (`arcade_key`), and every key while it is paused. The sheet's and the page's pointer events go to `eng_touch`. The engine pauses a game itself when the screen goes off or another window covers it (`engine_held`) and leaves when the game asks (`engine_left`).

<a id="games-look"></a>**Look.** The games ask the theme for fields, never which theme it is:

- **Boards.** Each board draws in the accent on the page, flipped by Light Mode with it. Sudoku's grid takes `OLED_CELL` (24 px) cells and digits at `OLED_DIGIT_PX` (19, the design's 16), its 216 px centered across and in the window's first `OLED_ROOM` (224) rows, so it sits between the status row and y 282 on screen, clear of the glass (at 30 px it ran to y 328, off the bottom).
- **Pop-ups** (`popup`: New game?, Solved!, You win!, Paused, Game over, and Return's Continue / Quit, under a "Paused" title): the sheet dimmed by a half-black, then a dark box (`#1C1C1C`, 12 px corners) with a hairline frame (`#3A3A3A`), the title white, the chosen row on the accent's bar, white on it, the others `#AAAAAA`. A card game reads the same look from `Q2_POPUP` (`popup_env`, [librespot.md](librespot.md#game-pop-ups) has the format).
- **Text** (`text_at`): the theme's face (`theme_face`). `hud` is the score line every game shares: the name in the quiet ink, the number in the loud one.
- **Bar.** Where the bar holds the page's caption (`page_title_h` 0, OLED's), `show` writes the game's name into the chooser's hidden `PAGE_TITLE` label and "Games" again on leaving (`page_retitle`), so the bar names the game. Vortex's Level starts `HUD_X` + 24 in: flush at `HUD_X` its first letters were under the glass's bottom corner.

**Keys.** `games_key` runs in `ringnav()` right after the rating picker, before stock's key filter, while a game is showing and the screen is usable. It takes every key, so the wheel, Center, Play/Pause and the side buttons never reach the volume, `media_key` or the double-Center screen-off. A held Return's release (`RETURN_RELEASE_LATCH` set) and Power stay stock, so a long Return still goes Home. In the chooser it takes nothing; Return there is the page's key-up (`return_key`), back to the Library.

- **Sudoku**: the wheel moves through the cells in reading order, Previous/Next move a row, Center on a blank or entered cell opens the digit (the wheel picks blank or 1-9, Center writes it, Return cancels), Play/Pause starts a new game (asking first over an unfinished one), Return goes back to the chooser. Clues are on gray; a digit that repeats in its row, column or box is red and underlined. Every cell holding the cursor's digit, or the digit being picked, shows it dark on the tone.
- **Vortex**: Center launches the ball from the paddle, Play/Pause pauses and resumes, Return pauses with Continue/Quit (the wheel picks, Center confirms), and after the last life Center plays again.
- **Solitaire**: the wheel walks the 13 piles (stock, waste, the four foundations, then the seven columns) and Previous/Next jump between a top-row pile and the column under it (the gap's column to the waste). Center on the stock draws (an empty stock takes the waste back); on another pile it picks up its top card, or a column's whole face-up run, framed in the tone, and the cursor turns white. Center on another pile drops what fits there; where nothing does, that pile is picked up instead (the stock draws, an empty pile changes nothing), so a pile held by mistake never has to be put back first; Center on the same pile again sends its top card to a foundation, or puts it back. Return drops the held cards, then goes back to the chooser. Play/Pause starts a new game, asking first unless this one is won.
- **Snake**: the side Next button turns right and Previous turns left, one turn a step and a second waiting for the next (any more are dropped). The touch wheel is ignored during play and in the pause menu; Previous/Next pick Continue/Quit. Play/Pause pauses, Return opens Continue/Quit, and after a crash Center plays again.

**Sudoku.** 24 bundled puzzles, 4 bits a cell, each with exactly one solution. A new game picks one and relabels its digits, shuffles rows within bands, columns within stacks, the bands and the stacks, and maybe transposes it, all of which keep the solution unique. ponytail: fixed puzzles, no generator, pencil marks or hints.

**Vortex.** Three rings of 16 bricks round the center (40-76 px out) and the paddle, a 45° arc at 118 px. All integer: positions and velocities in 16.16 px per 1/60 s step, angles 1024 a turn, sine and arctangent from tables, so the same inputs give the same game. A brick reflects the ball off its radius (ponytail: never off a brick's side); the paddle sends it back towards the center, turned up to 45° by how far off-center it hit. Missing the paddle costs one of three lives, shown as gray balls under Best. A broken brick flashes white and fades over `POP_MS` (240 ms), and the ball trails its last `TRAIL` (4) frames' positions in the tone; `frame()` records both, so the game logic is unchanged, and repaints only while the ball moves or a flash fades. The game-over banner says "New best!" when the game raised Best. Clearing every brick is the next level: one of three layouts in turn (ponytail: fixed layouts), each 15 px/s faster from 120 to a cap of 270, under a ring's 12 px a step, so the ball never crosses a ring without touching it.

**Solitaire.** Klondike, draw one, unlimited passes through the stock. 13 piles of up to 24 bytes, a card `suit * 13 + rank` plus `UP` when face up. A column turns its top card when the one on it leaves. A held run drops the one part of it that fits (only one card in a run can go on a given card, and only its King on an empty column), so there is no depth to choose; a pile at its 24 takes nothing, and a save's cards are checked on load (0-51, face up or not) with its pile lengths and cursor, as its seal (`games_ok`) is unkeyed and a hand-made save must neither read past the suit table nor write past a pile; a foundation takes only the top card, any foundation an Ace. Once the stock and waste are empty and every card is face up, `sol_finish` sends everything home at once (the lowest card left is always a column's top). Columns fan face-down cards 6 px and face-up ones 20 px (the strip with the rank on the left and the suit on the right, `LABEL_PX` 20), closed up to fit the sheet, the two outer columns `SOL_LOW` short of it. A closed-up strip's label is drawn 3 px over the strip's height, so it shows whole instead of cut by the next card; ponytail: at the deepest (6 down, 13 up) that is a 15 px label in an inner column and 12 px in an outer one. ponytail: no undo, score, timer or draw three.

**Snake.** A 20 × 20 board of 11 px cells under the score and best, clear of the glass's corners (`SN_X`, `SN_Y`). The body is a ring of cell indices from the tail, the head last; a step moves the head one cell, and the tail follows unless it ate, so moving into the cell the tail is leaving is allowed. A wall or the body ends the game. An apple adds one to the length and the score and lands on a free cell picked with `rand_below` over the free count. Vortex's `frame` timer runs it: Snake's branch adds the milliseconds passed and takes a step per `snake_ms` (160 ms, 4 ms less an apple, 70 at most), two a frame at most, so the speed doesn't follow the frame rate. Only a record is saved (`/mnt/data/ringnav-snake`, `SNK1`, sealed as Vortex's best); an unfinished game isn't. ponytail: no wrap mode, levels or obstacles.

**Wheel.** Ticks are too coarse for a paddle (about seven a turn), so while Vortex plays `wheel_raw` is set (as on Now Playing's lyrics page, [Lyrics wheel](#scrub-ipod)) and `wheel_sample` (`patch/playback.c`) posts no ticks: it adds the raw travel (200 units a turn) to `wheel_travel` atomically, and nothing is queued for a menu meanwhile. Each frame reads and zeroes it; `VORTEX_GAIN` (percent, 100 a turn for a turn) is the paddle's calibration knob.

**Frame timer.** A 33 ms `timer_add`, only while Vortex plays, runs 60 steps a second (at most 4 a frame) and repaints only when the steps changed something (the paddle, the ball, the state), so waiting to launch paints nothing; only the wheel turning holds the screen timeout off, so a ball left in play lets the screen dim and go off like any page, which pauses it. A key the game ignores paints nothing either (`games_key` compares the state before and after). The screen going off or another window on top pauses the game, clears `wheel_raw` and ends the timer; so do Play/Pause, Return's menu, leaving and closing.

**Saves.** `/mnt/data/ringnav-sudoku` (the grid and the cursor) and `/mnt/data/ringnav-solitaire` (the piles and the cursor) are written only when changed: a written digit, a move, a draw or a new game marks its game dirty and arms one `SAVE_MS` (2 s) timer from the first unsaved change, not per move, and leaving to the chooser or closing the page (Home too) writes whatever is dirty, a moved cursor included; ponytail: a power-off loses the moves of the last 2 s, and a cursor moved since the last write (only moves arm the timer). `/mnt/data/ringnav-vortex` holds the best score, written when a game ends above it. All go through `blob_io`: each a struct whose first word is a magic and last the FNV-1a of the rest, so a short read, another magic or a bad checksum is a fresh game. A failed write shows "Couldn't save".

`test/fw/test_games.py` paints the boards and Return's menu. Checks in `test/peq.py` (host build of `games.c`): every bundled puzzle and 200 shuffled ones have exactly one solution; clues refuse writes, conflicts by row, column and box, completion; the save seal; Vortex's paddle wrap, launch, bricks both ways, the paddle's return, lives to game over, the next level, the speed cap, every launch angle at full speed hitting the outer ring first, and the same inputs giving the same state; Solitaire's deal, draw and redeal, foundation and column rules, a run's part that fits, turning, home, the finish, and 100 seeded random games keeping every card once and every pile sound (some won). `test/patch.py`: the Library row, the chooser, Sudoku's keys and save with no key reaching stock's filter or `media_key`, the confirm, Return game → chooser → Library, Vortex's timer and raw wheel through Play/Pause, screen-off and Quit, Solitaire's draw and save, cursor, pick up, refused and good drops, Center twice home and put back, Return, the confirm, and closing mid-game, the Solitaire resuming. `test/playback.py`: `wheel_raw` posts no ticks.

## Spotify

**Spotify** is Streaming's row after stock's (`ringnav_stream`, after `stream_page_init`'s rows in `scroll_view_streamsset`, a `library_into` row with `assets/icons/stream_spotify.png`, Spotify's logo as a 52 px palette PNG with `list_tidal`'s inode metadata). It opens the browser (below; without `librespot` on the card, `spotify_page` saying so), a runtime window (`patch/spotify.c`), for librespot, a Spotify Connect receiver built from the [q2-librespot](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-librespot) fork (branch `shanlingq2`; hard-float, linked against the stock glibc, 19.5 MB, so it stays on the card). Nothing of it is in the firmware: the card's `/mnt/mmc/.spotify/` holds `librespot`, its launcher `run`, the sink `aplay.sh`, the saved login `cache/` and the logs.

**Starting.** `spot_launch` runs `system("/bin/sh /mnt/mmc/.spotify/run")` once per boot, when the row is first pressed, and only then (while [Smart Wi-Fi](#smart-wi-fi) brings the radio back, once its link is up: `smart_hold`): until it has, `spot_poll` returns at once and nothing reads the card or the state file. The login (`cache/credentials.json`, written after the first Connect handoff) only saves the phone's pick. `run` passes `--cache-size-limit` from `.cache-size` ([Streaming configuration](#streaming-configuration)), `2G` without it. `run` backgrounds a loop that restarts librespot after any exit, waiting 5 s and doubling to a minute while runs keep failing (mDNS needs Wi-Fi up), and leaves the loop's pid in `/tmp/q2-librespot`, which also makes a second run exit. librespot's process is not demo's child, as bluealsa's isn't. Once it has played, `SPOT_IDLE_MS` (30 s) without playing (paused, stopped or handed to another device) while the browser is shut makes `spot_poll` stop it as Home's Rockbox row does (`spot_stop`: the loop's pid, `killall -9 librespot aplay`, the pid file, the state file and `SPOT_OUT` removed), so the keys are local music's again; the row starts it again. Before it has played, the wait is `SPOT_CAST_MS` (150 s), time to cast to the Q2 from the phone; it counts from the launch or the last poll with the browser open, whichever is later. An open browser (pairing prompt and Now Playing on it included, and so any request in flight) restarts the wait every poll while the screen is on, but holds no timer and no DAC: only playing does (`spot_take`). Left open with the screen off, it holds nothing: once the wait runs out, `spot_poll` closes the browser (`window_close`, as Back would) and then stops librespot, so a Q2 left dark on it, with Standby off, doesn't keep librespot connected and its state files read twice a second. ponytail: waking after that finds Streaming, not the browser; its row starts librespot again. Without `librespot` on the card `spotify_page` says so and nothing runs.

**Contract.** librespot runs with `--backend subprocess --device "/bin/sh ./aplay.sh" --volume-ctrl fixed --initial-volume 100 --control-socket /tmp/q2-librespot.sock --status-file /tmp/q2-librespot.state` (the last two are the fork's):

- The status file is rewritten whole (a `.tmp`, renamed) on each player event: `state=` `none` (no Connect session: the phone hasn't chosen the Q2, or chose another device), `stopped`, `paused` or `playing`; `track=` (the Spotify id), `title=`, `artist=` (joined by `, `), `album=`, `duration=` and `position=` in ms, `at=` the `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` ms the position was taken at, and `cover=1` once `/tmp/q2-librespot.state.jpg` holds this track's cover, which librespot fetches itself over its own TLS (the smallest Spotify image at least 160 px wide: 300 px). The payload does no TLS.
- The socket takes `AF_UNIX` datagrams, sent `MSG_DONTWAIT` as Videos' are: `p` play/pause, `P` play, `s` pause, `n` next, `b` previous, `S` and a position in ms to seek. librespot ignores them without a session.
- The subprocess sink starts `aplay.sh` when playback starts and kills it when it stops, pause included, so the DAC's PCM is free while librespot is paused. `aplay.sh` is the stock `aplay -D plughw:0,0 -f S16_LE -r 44100 -c 2`, retried for 3 s: aplay opens the PCM before it reads its input, so a busy PCM costs no audio. Each try first reads `/tmp/q2-librespot.out` (`SPOT_OUT`): when it holds a device and a volume, it runs `/usr/bin/q2video -s DEVICE VOLUME` instead (below). Without the file, which older Q2 Muses never write, it is aplay as before.
- **Output.** Every poll `spot_output` asks `output_device` (videos.c, Videos' and Internet Radio's choice through `video_start`) for the output in use: none on the headphone DAC, `plug:bluealsa` with `headset_gain()` for Bluetooth (`mclGetOutputWay` 1), `usb` with `g_volume`, or `h` and it when the DAC applies the volume, for a USB DAC (2). When the line changes it writes `DEVICE VOLUME` to `SPOT_OUT` (a `.tmp`, renamed) or removes the file, and sends `v` and the effective gain to `/tmp/q2sink.sock`. `q2video -s` opens the device at 44.1 kHz, S16 stereo, with Videos' `sound_open` (retrying 5 s while hciplayer lets go), plays stdin through Videos' writer at `bt_gain` of the volume, as hciplayer's soft volume would (the DAC's mute is left alone), and takes `v` and `q` on that socket as radio's helper does.
