It ends with its input (the sink's kill closes librespot's pipe) or when a write fails even after `snd_pcm_recover`, a headset gone: librespot's subprocess sink then restarts `aplay.sh` once, which reads the file again. ponytail: otherwise an output switched while playing takes over at the sink's next start (pause and play), as Videos and Internet Radio keep their device until they end.

**Polling and power.** `spot_poll`, from `ringnav_sleep` every `SPOT_POLL_MS` (500 ms), reads the file and parses it when it changed. On the change to `playing` (`spot_take`) it does what stock's AirPlay page does for its receiver (`airplay_page_init`, `on_airplayset_onclick`): `player_stop` unless hciplayer is stopped (it holds the PCM even paused), `config_outputchannel(g_headset_output, 2)` (what a headset insert runs: `mclSetHeadsetMode`, `mclSetDacPwr(1)`, which also loads the DAC's FPGA firmware, and `g_dacoff_time` 0), `mclSetPcmMode`, `mclSetMute(0)` (`player_stop` mutes) and `device_set_volume(g_volume, 1)`. With Bluetooth or USB (`g_headset_output` 2 and up) it only powers the DAC on if `check_dacoff_state` turned it off; the sink plays there itself (Output, above). While `playing`, every poll calls `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 0)` (`0x4feb38`: its arguments are standby, auto power-off and the backlight, in that order) and zeroes a counting `g_dacoff_time`, so neither standby nor `check_dacoff_state` ends playback, while the screen still turns off on its timer. On the headphone DAC the volume is the DAC's own: librespot's is fixed at 100%, and `device_set_volume` (stock's volume dialog, the screen-off wheel) sets the DAC with `mclSetLocalVol` whether or not hciplayer plays.

**Keys.** `ringnav()` hands Play/Pause, previous and next (171, 222, 223) to `spot_media` right after stock's key-lock filter (`on_wm_keyup_before_fun`), on any page and with the screen off, while Spotify is the active source: playing or paused, and no local track has played since. They become `p`, `b` and `n`, and stock's own key-up never sees them. On the page Center works as on Now Playing's [scrub](#scrub-ipod) (`spot_key`): a release arms the same `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS` (250 ms) timer (`center_press`, shared with Now Playing), and a second one before it ends starts a scrub; the wheel then moves it `SPOT_STEP_MS` (5 s) a tick and the bar turns white, and a center press (at once, swallowing a quick second one, as on Now Playing), Return or `SCRUB_MS` without a tick seeks there with `S`. Outside a scrub the timer, a single press, replays the release to stock `on_wm_keyup_fun`, so the screen turns off. Otherwise the wheel is stock's volume and `spotify_page` is not in `contexts.inc`, so `ringnav()` leaves it to stock.

**Hand-over.** Local music → Spotify is `spot_take` above. Spotify → local music: `mclStartPlayer` (`0x5c0118`), which every local track's start runs before hciplayer opens the PCM, is hooked (`ringnav_start_player`). With librespot playing, `spot_yield` sends `s` and waits, 20 ms at a time up to `SPOT_YIELD_MS` (1.5 s), until the file no longer says `playing`. The fork's sink stops (aplay killed and reaped) before the `Paused` event, so the PCM is free once it does. The keys are local music's again from then on. Home's Rockbox row kills the loop and librespot (`/tmp/q2-librespot`'s pid, `killall -9 librespot aplay`), as Rockbox takes ALSA.

**Page.** `spot_open` builds Now Playing's layout from `tools/ipod.py`'s `NP_*`: "Spotify" in the top row with a play or pause glyph at its end, the art 166 px at x 16, y 50, the title (22 px white), artist and album (16 px `#AAAAAA`) in a 165 px column at x 194, the bar at `NP_BAR` and the times under it. The art is librespot's cover sized once a track by Coverflow's `thumb` (`toolsThumbSpecCover` under `parse_cover_mutex`) to `/tmp/q2spot.jpg` and loaded with its `image_show`, `default_album_flow` until there is one; it rounds its corners as Now Playing's (`paint_cover`). The position is `position + (now - at)` while playing, clamped to the duration. A 250 ms timer, idle with the screen off, writes the times when the second changes and repaints the bar, which `spot_paint` draws as Now Playing's capsule: the theme's track (`playing.scrubber.track`) with the played part in the accent's light tone (iPod) or stock red (Stock). The remaining time is whole seconds less whole seconds, as Now Playing's. Only a `login` reply or a sign-out shows "Open Spotify on your phone / and choose Q2"; a playing or paused track, or any `ok` reply, confirms the login, and `state=none` makes it unknown again. A successful play shows "Loading…" until a track plays: the one asked for, or any other than before it (a relinked id). After `SPOT_WAIT_MS` (15 s) it says "Playback didn't start", without sending play again, until any track plays. A refused key ends the wait sooner. The play's `ok` notes the length of `.spotify/spot.log` (librespot's stderr, which `run` appends to), and while it loads `spot_poll` reads what was logged since (the last 4 KB of it, re-reading 14 bytes so a line written in two parts still matches). Once that holds `error audio key` ([librespot#1649](https://github.com/librespot-org/librespot/issues/1649): Spotify refused the track's key), it says "Spotify refused this account / Its tracks can't play on the Q2". It also runs `killall -9 librespot aplay`, because librespot otherwise skips through the whole list, a key refused each time, and a pause (`s`) doesn't stop it while it loads. `run`'s loop starts librespot again with no track, and for `SPOT_SIGNOUT_MS` the browser takes a missing socket for that restart (`spot_restarting`). Any track that plays later still clears it. The three labels scroll without focus or an ellipsis and restart when their text changes; `field` cuts only at a UTF-8 character boundary. It sits on the browser, so Return goes back to the list it was opened from. ponytail: the cover is sized on the UI thread, one decode a track; a worker if it stutters.

**Browser.** `spotbrowse_page` (`CTX_DYNAMIC` in `contexts.inc`, so the wheel moves its rows) is one `page_list` rebuilt per level, as Internet Radio's, its rows' clicks run from a timer. A level is a Q2SPOT/1 request ([librespot.md](librespot.md#browsing-protocol-q2spot1)): its op, its arguments and cursor (escaped, `spot_escape`) and its reply, cut in place by `spot_reply` into the header's 4 fields and 6 a row (at most 50), unescaped; a bad escape, `%00`, a NUL, a line of the wrong width or too many rows makes it malformed. IDs, URIs and cursors are sent back exactly as received. The base level asks `account`: `ok` shows the menu (Now Playing, Queue and Playback Settings only with a track), `login` the pairing prompt ("Open Spotify on your phone and choose Q2", "Both on the same Wi-Fi"), which asks again every `SPOT_PAIR_MS` (2 s) and becomes the menu once paired. Liked Songs, Playlists, Albums and Artists list 64 px rows (title over subtitle); an album, playlist or artist row opens its own level (an artist's top tracks, then its albums), and a non-empty cursor adds **More…**, a level of its own, so Back returns to the page and the row left. Up to `SPOT_DEPTH` (8) levels are kept, the oldest past the base dropped; only the top `SPOT_KEEP` (3) keep their replies (64 KB each at most), and Back to an older one fetches it again. Search lays peq_ui.c's T9 edit over the title; its OK with text opens Tracks, Albums, Artists and Playlists for the term, and empty text or the box's blur leaves the menu as it was. A track row sends `play CONTEXT POSITION URI` (`play URI` without a context; a Queue row `skip POSITION URI`) and opens Now Playing once it is `ok`, else toasts the message. Play/Pause held on a track row (`ringnav_keylong` → `spot_hold`) sends `enqueue URI`, its release latched as the radio's, and only toasts a failure message; held on a playlist row it sends `download URI`, as the open playlist's Download Playlist row does, and toasts the reply (it starts, or another playlist is already downloading). Liked Songs has a Download Liked Songs action when the backend advertises saved collections. The persistent Downloads hub, capability negotiation, ordered offline playback and storage controls follow [downloads.md](downloads.md). `caps` is asked once, after the base's `account`; a request that cancels it (any other) leaves `caps_checked` clear, and the page's 250 ms tick asks again once the menu is idle at the base, re-laying the menu with the reply only when no click is pending on its rows. A removal preview is its own act (`A_PREVIEW`), so only its reply asks **Remove Downloads?** (the confirmation card, its body the backend's count over "Playlists can be left incomplete."); one dropped by Return can't turn a later action's reply into a removal. Download Progress polls `jobs` every 2 s only while the browser is on top with the screen on, and a failed poll keeps the list. With an older backend (no saved collections, but `download`), Downloads keeps **Download Status** (`downloadstatus`, its message toasted). Playback Settings shows Shuffle as a switch (`list_toggle`) and Repeat (Off, All, One); a press sends the next value and reads them again. Account shows the name and Premium, and Sign Out asks first on the confirmation card; after `signout` the pairing prompt returns. A list pressed on a level showing its rows loads under the [loading overlay](oled-design.md#loading): `push` keeps it in `br.lv[SPOT_DEPTH]` (one slot past the levels), asks for it with the shown level's own id put back, sets `br.pend`, and `got` enters it once its reply comes; Return (`br_leave`) and a lift off the spinner (`br_touch`, through `list_marks.c` `load_touch`) call `load_cancel`, and `go` does nothing meanwhile. Back to a list past `SPOT_KEEP`, whose rows went, is staged the same way (`P_POP`): `got` drops the top and puts the list in its place once it comes. The first open waits under `list_marks.c` `load_over` over Streaming with no page (`br.hold` and `br.page` 0, as a card app's, `br_make` once the menu, pairing prompt or error is there), and Retry and Playback Settings' reload after a change load in place (`hold_load`: `br.hold` is 1 + the state a cancel puts back, `show` drawing nothing until the answer). Loading ("Loading…", only with nothing shown to lay the spinner over), empty ("Nothing here", unless a cursor offers More…) and errors are page states: the backend's message as the title, with **Retry** for `offline`, `throttled`, `error` or no usable reply. Any `login` reply returns to pairing.

**Worker.** `request` writes `Q2SPOT/1`, the id (`wk.id`, never reused) and the op into a 64 KB buffer and starts `worker` on a pthread: an `AF_UNIX` `SOCK_STREAM` (2, MIPS numbering) to `/tmp/q2-librespot.browse.sock`, the request sent `MSG_NOSIGNAL`, the write side shut (`spot_shut`, the o32 `shutdown` syscall 4182, since demo imports no `shutdown`), then `select` 100 ms at a time and `recv` into the same buffer until EOF, `SPOT_WAIT_MS` (15 s) or a cancel; more than 64 KB fails. One request at a time: a new one, Back from a loading level or the page's close cancels the one before and joins it within 100 ms. `wk.done` is the worker's to set once its thread runs, as it may have finished before `pthread_create` returns: `request` sets it only when no thread started (card apps' `req_send` is the same). The page's 250 ms timer takes the finished reply on the UI thread; one whose header doesn't echo the id, or for a level since left (`level.id`), is dropped. Actions (`play`, `skip`, `enqueue`, `shuffle`, `repeat`, `signout`) are never sent again by themselves. No socket within `SPOT_OLD_MS` (3 s) of librespot's start, or `SPOT_SIGNOUT_MS` (15 s) after a sign-out (librespot exits and its launcher restarts it), is librespot starting: "Loading…" (or the pairing prompt) asks again every 500 ms. After that, a state file means an old add-on: Now Playing and "Update Spotify on the card / to browse on the Q2", still asking every 2 s. Without either, "Spotify isn't running" with Retry. ponytail: a title is cut at 255 bytes by the backend and a search term at 63 by the page; nothing is cached across opens.

Checks in `test/peq.py` (host build): `spot_reply` on escapes in any case, UTF-8, a short header, every malformed shape and the row limit; `spot_escape` and its bounds. Checks in `test/patch.py`: the row and its icon, the page without librespot (nothing starts), the start once per boot from the row and never without it, saved login or not, the session prompt, `spot_take`'s calls and their order and Bluetooth's exception, `SPOT_OUT` and the sink's volume on Bluetooth and its removal on the DAC, the held timers, the art, the labels moving on from `at`, every label inside the glass, the bar's rectangles and color, the keys on another page and their return to local music, `mclStartPlayer`'s wait and its limit, the scrub and Return; the idle stop only with the browser shut. The browser against a fake backend on the socket: the first request's bytes, the menu with and without a track, loading, errors with and without Retry, empty pages, More… on an empty page, a wrong id, a bad escape and an oversized reply, playlists by URI, tracks played in their context (with their URI) or alone and Now Playing only on `ok`, a refused key (the note, one kill, no play sent again, a line from before the play ignored, a line cut between polls found, no kill without one), More… and Back to the row left, Back while loading, an artist's and album's pages and a refetched evicted level, pairing and its polling, an old add-on and a missing librespot, search's empty, left and escaped terms, Add to Queue on hold and its failure, Queue's skip, Playback Settings and an unrepeated failure, Sign Out's confirmation, the restart after it, a lost login, and the idle stop after the browser shuts and the relaunch.

## AirPlay

Stock's receiver is `/usr/bin/shairport`, Shanling's Shairport 1.1.1 (`1.1.1-22-shanling`): AirPlay 1 (RAOP) only, with its own mDNS responder, started and stopped by demo (`airplayStartService`, `airplayStopService`) from Network service's switch (`on_airplayset_onclick`, `0x52c2c0`), with its now-playing page `airplay_page`. Streaming's **AirPlay** row (`ringnav_stream`, stock's `netservice_airplay` icon) only opens `systemset/netservice_page`. ponytail: the row doesn't toggle the service itself; stock's `airplay_switch` (`0x519bf4`) is the way in if it should. AirPlay 2 would be a shairport-sync 4.x add-on with nqptp, an add-on on the card like librespot.

## AirPlay sender

The [q2-airplay](https://github.com/group-a-study/q2-airplay) card app (System settings → App Store) plays what the Q2 plays on an AirPlay speaker, through cliairplay (Music Assistant's AirPlay 1 and 2 sender, built for the Q2). Its manifest has `hidden=1`: no Streaming row (stock's AirPlay row stays the receiver's), its page opened by id (`addon_open_id`, `patch/addon.c`) from a first row on Now Playing's ⋯ page (`airplay_more`, `patch/airplay.c`, from `ringnav_playermore`; "AirPlay: SPEAKER" while one plays). There is no Now Playing button. Without the app on the card the row toasts where to install it; with it, the press waits for Smart Wi-Fi's link (`smart_hold`), and the running app keeps the radio on (`addon_running`).

**The tap.** The app makes `/tmp/q2cast` (`cast_tap`, `patch/peq.h`; `CAST_MAGIC`, whole under `.tmp` and renamed) and beats it: `want`, its `CAST_CLOCK` (CLOCK_MONOTONIC in 2^20 ns ticks, no 64-bit division in hciplayer). hciplayer's PEQ filter looks for it once a second of audio (`cast_live`, reading the magic and size before mapping), and once mapped looks at the beat once a second of audio while the app is away, so an idle tap reads no clock per block. While the beat is under `CAST_STALE_PLAYER` (2 s) old it writes what plays, after Mono, Swap and the crossfade, into its ring at 44.1 kHz, 16-bit (`cast_copy`): other rates through a Blackman-windowed sinc (12 zero crossings a side at the lower rate's cutoff, 0.46 of it; its kernel tabled at 512 points a frame and read between two), dithered (TPDF, 1 LSB) only where a sample isn't 16-bit already; then the filter instance (`id`), the song's place (`pts_ms`) and the stamp, then `seq`. A seek (the place moving more than 0.5 s off its run) or a skip (a new instance while the last song was more than 2.5 s from its end, so gapless and crossfaded changes aren't) sets `jump_seq`, then bumps `jumps`, and restarts the resampler. With `mute` set the filter skips `peq_process` (the EQ is the earphones'; its filters start from rest when it comes back) and zeroes the block after its tap. A song the filter passes through (DSD, DoP) sets `dsd`. A stale beat ends both, so a killed app gives the Q2 back its sound within about 2 s.

**demo** (`airplay_poll` each UI pass) maps the file once it exists, looked for once a second only after the ⋯ row opened the app, or when its loop's pid file was there as demo started (`air.asked`, looked at once), so nothing runs for anyone who never uses it, its header read before mapping. It writes the player's status, `g_maxvolume` and the volume (the speaker's while one plays, else -1, so the app never sends the earphones' level), and while the app beats keeps the filter in the chain (`peq_chain`) and writes the playing song's path and tags to `/tmp/q2cast.track` (`blob_io`), once a song. When the app's state becomes `CAST_ON` the volume is swapped: the earphones' volume, Volume Limit and output kept in RAM (the volume saved under its own key too), the limit lifted (it is the earphones'), and `g_volume` made the speaker's: the app's `spk` (its own level as the speaker reports it, or the one it last had from the Q2, each with a new `spk_seq`), else `Q2POD AIRVOL` (35 by default) for an app that sends none; a new `spk_seq` while it plays (a reconnect) is taken again. While it plays `ringnav_write_config` saves `PLAYSET VOLUME` as `Q2POD AIRVOL`, and an output change (`ringnav_output`, Bluetooth coming or going) leaves the speaker's level alone. When it stops (or its beat goes 1.5 s stale, before the filter's 2 s) the earphones' level comes back from RAM (their output's own key if Bluetooth came or went), applied and saved, an open volume dialog following. The filter stays silent while `volume` is 0 or more, until the pass after that publishes -1, so nothing plays at a speaker's level however the passes fall. `lyrics_now` takes the speaker's place from the app (`pos_ms` at `pos_at` of instance `pos_id`, running on while `pos_run`; 0 while the speaker still finishes the song before), so the lyrics follow what is heard. ponytail: the speaker's own app changing its volume isn't heard; the wheel's next step sets it from the Q2's number. Spotify, Internet Radio and Videos have their own players, which the tap doesn't reach.

**The app** (`cmd/q2-airplay`, its README) plays the tap a fixed delay (1 s, set on its page) behind the filter: it starts frame f heard at its tap time plus the delay, mirrors a gap in the tap as silence, lets a pause play out and then flushes and parks the stream, starts again from the next frame on Play, and flushes at once and starts from `jump_seq` on a jump. It mutes the Q2 from its first start. Ported from group-a-study's fork (8f2aedf0, 4cc10246) without its Now Playing button. Devices fetch `sources.list` from main, so its AirPlay line stays commented until a release carries the tap: on older firmware the app would be a Streaming row with nothing to send.

## Internet Radio

**Internet Radio** is Streaming's last row (`ringnav_stream`, `assets/icons/stream_radio.png`, a broadcast glyph on coral, 52 px palette PNG with `list_tidal`'s inode metadata). It opens `radio_page`, a runtime window (`patch/radio.c`, `CTX_DYNAMIC` in `contexts.inc`, so the wheel moves its rows), one `page_list` rebuilt per level: the menu (Now Playing, when a station has played this boot or `/mnt/mmc/Radio/.last` exists; Favorites; Featured; Top Stations; By Country; By Genre), a country or genre list, and a station list. Rows rebuild the page from a timer (`later`), never inside their own click. A directory fetch from a list on show waits under the [loading overlay](oled-design.md#loading) (`fetch_run` sets `ui.pend`; `radio_paint`, called from `nav/row_paint.c`, lays the spinner over the page), the list kept until the new one or its failure caption is there; Return (`leave`) or a lift off the spinner (`touched`, through `list_marks.c` `load_touch`) stops the transfer (`load_cancel`), and `go` and the rows' clicks do nothing meanwhile. A search typed in the box closes it onto the list first. A fetch Smart Wi-Fi holds back for its link (`ui.wifi`) waits under the overlay too, with a "Connecting to Wi-Fi…" toast, and `tick` starts it once the link is up; only with no list on show is that a "Connecting to Wi-Fi…" caption, then "Loading…". Return goes up a level, from a failure caption back to the list it covered, and from the menu back to Streaming. Each level keeps its selected row.

**Lists.** Favorites are `/mnt/mmc/Radio/favourites.m3u`, then every other `.m3u` and `.pls` there, read whole and parsed as one text (`playlist`): `#EXTINF:…,NAME` names the next line, `FileN=` (a `file://` URL whose name holds an `=` is no key) is a URL and `TitleN=` names the one before; a line without `://` is no station. Favorites start empty: opening the page only creates the `Radio` folder. The six built-in stations (`STARTERS`, each checked against stock-like ffmpeg) are Featured, parsed from the payload. Search is the page's pull-down ([Pull-to-search](#pull-to-search)) on any level: `radio_search` lays a T9 edit (`edit_create`, shared with the EQ editor's value) over the title and focuses it for the keyboard; its OK (`EVT_VALUE_CHANGED`) fetches `/m3u/stations/byname/TEXT` (%-encoded, a substring match), and an empty result shows the empty state, "No Stations", and Return goes back to the level it was pulled over. Empty text, or the box's blur (`EVT_BLUR`, `0x10f`) without a search, rebuilds the page as it was. An empty OK closes the keyboard with neither event, so the keyboard's OK (`EVT_IM_ACTION`, `0x13a`) runs the same handler. Return empties and blurs the box, which shuts the keyboard before the box is destroyed: destroying it under an open keyboard crashes demo. With the keyboard up, Return never reaches the page: `search_key` (`ringnav`, ahead of stock's filter) takes it for the input method's edit when that is one of `edit_create`'s, named `EDIT_NAME` (`q2_edit`): it empties it, blurs it and detaches the keyboard, so every one of them (Radio, Spotify and card-app search, the EQ value and preset name) cancels, and the next Return goes back. Stock's search dialogs and the playlist editor's search, named `search_edit`, are blurred and detached without emptying, the editor's search applying its text on that Return. The directory is [radio-browser.info](https://api.radio-browser.info)'s round-robin `all.api.radio-browser.info`, fetched by `fetch_worker` on a pthread through demo's libcurl, over verified TLS with the firmware's `/etc/scrobble-ca.pem` (ISRG Root X1 signs it), 10 s to connect, 30 s in all, at most 256 KB: Top Stations is `/m3u/stations/topvote/100?hidebroken=true`, By Country `/csv/countries?order=stationcount&reverse=true&limit=60` then `/m3u/stations/bycountrycodeexact/CODE`, By Genre `/csv/tags?…` then `/m3u/stations/bytagexact/TAG` (%-encoded, `url_escape`), each with `?order=votes&reverse=true&limit=100&hidebroken=true`. The m3u is the favorites' parser's; the CSV (`choices`) is read from each line's end, so a quoted name may hold commas. The countries, the genres and a country's or genre's stations are sorted A–Z once fetched (`list_sort`, from `fetch`'s `az`): `ringnav_sort_key`, the library's rule, so "The Netherlands" sorts under N, then `strcasecmp`; an insertion sort, stable, so equal names keep the vote order. The server's order still picks which 60 and which 100 come back. Top Stations and Search, from any level, keep the vote order, and the side buttons step through a list in the order shown. Without Wi-Fi (`get_wifisignal`) the page says "No Wi-Fi"; a failed fetch "Directory unavailable". Return while loading sets a cancel flag that the transfer's progress callback returns, so the join takes at most about a second. A list holds `RADIO_MAX` (200) entries.

**Favorites.** Play/Pause held on a station (`ringnav_keylong` → `radio_hold`, the row from the list's `_ringnav_index`, or on Now Playing the station playing) rewrites `favourites.m3u` (a `.tmp`, synced and renamed) without it when its URL is there, else with it appended, and toasts which; its release is latched as the queue menu's (`st.qm_press`), so it does not stop the radio. A file already at `RADIO_MAX` is never rewritten, so nothing past it is lost.

**Playing.** A station (`radio_play`) copies the list it is in, so the side buttons step through it later, stops a playing q2video, pauses librespot (`spot_yield`), and starts `/usr/bin/q2video -r DEVICE URL [VOLUME]` through `video_start` (videos.c), Videos' own output choice: `player_stop`, the headphone output readied (`dac_take`), `plughw:0,0`, `plug:bluealsa` or `usb`, and the volume for Bluetooth's and soft USB's gain. The station goes to `/mnt/mmc/Radio/.last` as a one-entry `.m3u`. The keys and their output stay demo's: `radio_poll`, from `ringnav_sleep` every 500 ms while it runs, reads `/tmp/q2radio.state`, reaps it (`waitpid(WNOHANG)`), calls `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 0)` and zeroes a counting `g_dacoff_time`, as Spotify's poll does, and sends `v` and the volume byte on `/tmp/q2radio.sock` when `g_volume` changes, so stock's volume (wheel, dialog, screen off) reaches the soft gain. `radio_media`, next to `spot_media` after stock's key-lock filter, takes Play/Pause (stop, or play again), 222 and 223 (the previous or next station, round the ends) on any page while the radio is the active source: it played last and no local track, video or Spotify has played since. Stopping (`radio_halt`) sends `q` and waits up to `RADIO_QUIT_MS` (1.5 s), then `kill -9` on its pid (librespot also uses q2video), and removes the state file. `mclStartPlayer`'s hook, `play_video`, `spot_take` and Home's Rockbox row call `radio_stop`, which also hands the keys back. Nothing starts at boot.

**q2video -r** (`radio` in `patch/video.c`) opens the PCM and readies the DAC as Videos does (`sound_open`), then runs stock ffmpeg with `-loglevel verbose -icy 1 -reconnect 1 -reconnect_streamed 1 -rw_timeout 15000000 -i URL -vn -ac 2 -ar 48000 -f s16le pipe:4` (HTTPS works: ffmpeg's `tls_verify` is 0), the sound to the same writer thread, its stderr read a byte at a time on the main loop's poll. libavformat's http logs `Metadata update for StreamTitle: …` only at verbose; the input dump gives `icy-br` and `Stream #0:0: Audio: CODEC`. `meta` takes a line's value after `KEY :`, so `icy-notice2 : … Network Audio Server` is no codec. The state file is rewritten whole (`.tmp`, renamed) on each change: `state=` `connecting`, `playing` (once the writer has played a frame) or `error`, `title=` (the StreamTitle, which the page splits at `-` into artist and song), `codec=` (upper case), `bitrate=` (kbit/s), `error=` (when `sound_open` found no device: `open:` or `params:` and `snd_strerror`'s reason, which the page shows as "Can't play: …"; Bluetooth and USB get 50 tries, 5 s, the DAC 20, at open and again at `snd_pcm_set_params` while it is busy, since bluealsa claims its PCM there; or `write:` when a write fails past `snd_pcm_recover`, which ends that ffmpeg run, as it ends Spotify's sink; Videos drop such a write instead, so their picture goes on) and `at=` (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC` ms the sound started, for the elapsed time). When ffmpeg ends anyway it starts again after 1 s, 2 s, … up to `RADIO_TRIES` (5) starts in a row without sound, then writes `state=error` and exits. A start with no frame heard after `RADIO_SILENT_MS` (20 s) means the output is stuck (the writer may be blocked inside ALSA, so it can't be joined): it writes `state=error` with `error=no sound from the output` (or the writer's), kills ffmpeg and exits, so the page never stays on "Connecting…". `q` kills ffmpeg, unlinks the state, closes the PCM and mutes the DAC. No FM: the Q2 has no tuner (the device tree's only i2c device is the axp2101, and stock hciplayer was built with `--disable-radio`).

**Page.** `radionp_page` has Spotify's Now Playing layout: "Internet Radio" above, the row's icon unscaled in the art box, the station's list name, the StreamTitle's artist and song, then the codec and bitrate ("Connecting…", "Stopped", "Can't play: REASON" or "Can't play this station" instead). Local Now Playing's heart sits at its place (x 303, y 176, 50 px, `play_fav` / `play_unfav` centered): filled when the station playing is in `favourites.m3u`, which is read again only when `rd.serial` changes (each start and each toggle), and a tap toggles it as the held Play/Pause does (`fav_toggle`), with the same toast and the elapsed time, refreshed on a 500 ms timer idle with the screen off. It is not in `contexts.inc`, so the wheel is stock's volume and Center stock's screen toggle. ponytail: no station logos; the directory's m3u has none, and a logo would cost another fetch and a decode per station.

Checks in `test/peq.py` (host builds): `meta` on ffmpeg's lines; `playlist` on CRLF, BOM, radio-browser's extra tags, `.pls` keys and the limit; `choices` on both CSVs and quoted commas; `url_escape`. `test/patch.py`: the row and its icon, empty favorites, Featured, a 1.0.1 seed removed and an edited one kept, the pull-down's search box, its query, its empty result and its cancel, the pull gesture on `radio_page`, the headphone output readied before the fork, the error's reason, the save from Now Playing and its heart, the favorites from every playlist, the child's `execl` argv after `player_stop`, `.last`, the page's labels connecting and playing, the held timers, the volume datagram, the media keys and the side buttons round the ends, `mclStartPlayer`'s hand-over, the kill after `RADIO_QUIT_MS`, the error, the favorites toggle and its latched release, Top Stations' fetch and TLS options, No Wi-Fi, genres with an escaped tag, countries by code, both A–Z with their stations, a search over them in vote order, a failed fetch and Return through every level.

## Local radio fetch

**`q2radiofetch`** (`patch/radiofetch.c`, a helper of its own linked against the rootfs's `libcurl.so.4`, `libm` and `libc`; `RADIOFETCH` in `tools/build.py`) answers "which stations reach this place, and how do I stream them", for Radio. It prints a list on stdout, or with `--out FILE` writes it there whole (beside it, then renamed), as Radio reads it: the header `#Q2RADIO 2 <fetched> <lat> <lon> <complete|partial> <label>`, then a line per station with tab-separated fields: call sign, `FM` or `AM`, frequency (`93.1`, `780`), km from the transmitter, its strength there (`rf_signal`: a carrier-to-noise ratio of 24 to 80 dB, 47 plus 35 log10 of its reach toward the place over the km, which the tuner's static model takes), the brand the first source to name it gave (`93XRT`; a leading frequency left off, as "93.9 Lite FM" is Lite FM, while one after the name is the brand's own, "Rock 95.5"), the city of licence, then `source=url` for each stream (at most `RF_STREAMS`, 4, the first source's first). `radiofetch_core.c` holds everything that needs no network (`rf_text`, `rf_near`, `rf_zip`, the readers below), tested on this machine by `test/unit/test_radiofetch.py`; the program end to end, against a local server answering as the services did (`test/fixtures/radiofetch/`), is `test/radiofetch.py`, whose `--live` runs it against the real services and prints each source's coverage and the times.

**The place.** `--zip NNNNN` reads `/usr/share/q2radio/zcta.bin`, the Census Bureau's 2024 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (a bitmap of the 33,791 ZIPs, then each one's interior point to a hundredth of a degree, 147,664 bytes); a ZIP the Census does not list (a PO box's, 60690) takes the nearest listed one with its first three digits, labelled "(nearby)". `--at LAT,LON` is a point. The default, `--ip`, races three geolocation services (`ipinfo.io/json`, `ipwho.is/`, `get.geojs.io/v1/ip/geo.json`, all keyless and over HTTPS) and takes the first that answers with a point (`rf_geo`: `loc`, or `latitude` and `longitude` as numbers or strings; 0,0 is a service's "unknown"), within `LOCATE_MS` (3 s); with none, the last place's list (`last` in the cache folder) answers. Nothing is sent but the requests themselves, under a generic `User-Agent` (`Mozilla/5.0`).

**The stations** come from `/usr/share/q2radio/stations.bin`, made by `tools/radiodata.py` from the FCC's FM and AM queries (`fmq`, `amq`, `list=4`, the whole country) and the Audio Division's daily FM service contours (the F(50,50) 60 dBu line, 360 points a station): every licensed US full-power and low-power FM station (13,364 on 2026-11-20, an `STA` only where there is no licence) with its contour as 16 radii, and every licensed US AM station by day (4,251) with a reach of 30 km times the square root of its kilowatts, within 15 and 150 km (`AM_KM`; the FCC publishes no AM contours, and its contour service refuses AM stations without conductivity data). 816,144 bytes, sorted by latitude, so `rf_near` reads only the records within 2.4 degrees of the place (no radius passes 255 km) and keeps those whose reach toward it (the two nearest radii, weighted by angle) covers it, at most `RF_STATIONS` (96), the nearest. Downtown Chicago gets 29 FM and 27 AM stations, North Platte 13 and 4: a 60 km circle would have listed 66 FM call signs in Chicago, most of them suburban stations whose contour stops short of downtown. FM translators (`FX`) are left out (they carry another station, and the FCC's list does not say which), and so are boosters. ponytail: the table is as fresh as the firmware; `python3 tools/radiodata.py DOWNLOADS` refreshes it (its inputs come through the curl program, as fcc.gov answers Python's own client with 403 whatever its `User-Agent`).

**The streams** come over one libcurl multi handle (`PARALLEL` 16 transfers, `PER_HOST` 4 connections a host, reused by its later requests; `REQ_MS` 3 s a request, connection included, `BIG_MS` 4.5 s for a list; gzip asked for), under one deadline for the whole run, `DEADLINE_MS` (8 s, `--deadline`). The first round, all at once: iHeart's `liveStations?lat=&lng=` (a market's stations, whoever owns them: Audacy's, Urban One's, the Spanish groups', with their Shoutcast and HLS URLs; `rf_iheart` keeps the HTTPS one and the plain HTTP one, for a stream host whose certificate the player can't verify), Radio Browser's search by state for the list's three commonest states (`rf_radiobrowser`: a stream its last check found working whose name, tags or home page holds the call sign as a word; a suffix, `FM` or `-AM`, picks the band, else the only station with that call, else the one whose frequency is also written there), and TuneIn's local list (`rf_tunein_local`: same band and frequency, and the call sign in the entry's name or no other station of the list on that frequency, which gives the station's TuneIn id). When those are in, or `PHASE_MS` (3.5 s) after they began, or `PROBE_MS` (2 s) before the deadline, whichever is soonest, each station still without a stream is probed by call sign: Triton's `livestream?mount=WTBCFMAAC`, then the MP3 mount (`WSBCAM`) when that one is not there, as `livestream-redirect/<mount>.aac` (or `.mp3`), a URL that takes no token; Amperwave's `audacy-<call><band>aac-imc` playlist for a station licensed to Audacy (`RF_AUDACY`), as its `direct/` stream; SoundStack's player page, `live.mystreamplayer.com/CALL` (`CALLAM` for AM), whose `streams = [...]` names the host and mount (`rf_soundstack`); and TuneIn's `Tune.ashx` for an id the local list gave, whose Triton or Amperwave playlist is turned into the mount's own URL. A first-round answer that comes after the probes began still counts. What came by the deadline is the list; one cut short is `partial`.

**The cache** is `/mnt/mmc/Radio/.local/` (`--cache`): a list per place, `z<ZIP>.tsv` or `g<lat><lon>.tsv` with the point to a tenth of a degree (11 km), so nearby places share one (`rf_key`), and `last`, the last place's key. A list fresher than `RF_FRESH_S` (a week; `RF_PARTIAL_S`, an hour, for a partial one) is printed and that is all, with no request. An older one is printed at once, stdout is pointed at `/dev/null` so the reader sees its end, and the list is fetched again into the cache (and into `--out`'s file, where the Radio takes it up when the run ends), under `flock` on `.lock` (a second run finds it held and leaves the refresh to the first). A list is written beside its file, synced, then renamed over it. A refresh that found no stream at all keeps the old list. A cached list of another format (`#Q2RADIO 1`, before the strength column) is not one, and is fetched again. With `--ip` the place is looked up first (60 to 240 ms measured), so a warm run is that long; a ZIP's warm run reads one file. ponytail: a clock that is wrong (the Q2's may never have been set) makes every list stale or every list fresh; a list dated in the future is refreshed.

**TLS.** Every host verifies against `/etc/scrobble-ca.pem`, through the rootfs's libcurl and its mbedTLS ([third-party](third-party.md#curl-and-mbedtls)): iHeart chains to GlobalSign Root R3, Amperwave to Amazon Root CA 1, TuneIn to DigiCert Global Root G2, SoundStack, Radio Browser and ipinfo.io to ISRG Root X1, ipwho.is and geojs.io to GTS Root R4, and Triton's StreamTheWorld to Go Daddy Root G2, which the bundle carries for it. Measured on 2026-11-20 with the image's own libcurl 8.23.0 and mbedTLS 3.6.7 under `qemu-mipsel`: without Go Daddy Root G2 each of the 38 Triton probes of a Chicago run failed its handshake (curl's error 60, "signed with an unacceptable hash": StreamTheWorld also sends Go Daddy Class 2's SHA-1 cross-signature), and with it they verified. The streams themselves are not fetched here; the player opens them.

**Coverage and time**, measured on 2026-11-20 from the laptop over Wi-Fi (`test/radiofetch.py --live`, two runs each), cold: downtown Chicago 47 of 56 stations with a stream (FM 27 of 29, AM 20 of 27) in 2.0 to 3.9 s, 71 requests; Austin (78701) 26 of 42 (FM 20 of 25) in 2.0 to 3.0 s; North Platte, Nebraska (69101) 11 of 17 (FM 8 of 13) in 1.1 to 1.7 s; the laptop's own place by IP 47 of 53 in 2.9 s. Warm, from the cache: 5 ms for a ZIP or a point, 58 ms by IP (the lookup). Of Chicago's FM, iHeart gave 23, Triton and TuneIn 4 more (Hubbard's WDRV, WTMX and WTBC and Cumulus's WKQX are not on iHeart's market list), Radio Browser the rest; what stays without a stream is a simulcast (WCFS-FM carries WBBM) or a station on no service (WLPN-LP). Under `qemu-mipsel` with the image's libcurl the same Chicago run took 2.3 s. On the Q2 itself (V1L4i over Wi-Fi, 2026-11-20, wall clock): downtown Chicago 2.93 s (57 stations), North Platte 1.49 s, Austin 2.74 s, the network's place by IP 3.48 s fetched again (`--refresh`) and 0.27 s from the cache. The Q2's own time is not measured yet.

## Radio (Home)

**Radio** is Home's row under the Library (`HOME_ROWS` in `tools/ipod.py`, its tap bound in `coverflow_home`, Edit Home's letter `t` in `library_edit.c`): the stations that reach the Q2's place, laid out at their real frequencies on an FM dial (`patch/radio_tuner.c`, `tuner_page`, a runtime window in `contexts.inc`). The approved prototype (`~/q2-emu/design/radio-tuner/index.html`, 2026-11-20) is its spec, screen for screen; [oled-design: Radio](oled-design.md#radio) has the screens.

**The list.** Opening the page forks `q2radiofetch --out /tmp/q2tuner.list` ([Local radio fetch](#local-radio-fetch)), with `--zip` and the ZIP in `/mnt/mmc/Radio/.local/zip` when the user chose one, and shows the loading screen until the list file appears (`tuner_poll`, every loop pass, also reaps the fetch after the page has gone). A cached list appears at once; when a background refresh ends, its newer list replaces it. `list_read` keeps the FM stations (`RT_MAX`, 64): frequency, call sign, name (the call sign when no source named it), city, km, strength (dB) and the first stream; the status row's "Near <city>" is the nearest station's city of licence. A fetch that ends with no list is the error screen ("No internet connection"): Centre tries again, Return opens the ZIP entry. AM stations stay in the data and out of the UI (the dial is 87.9 to 107.9).

**The dial.** Frequencies are in 10 kHz (`rt->freq`, a station's `freq`), within 87.9 and 107.9 (`LO`, `HI`), and the dial draws the scale alone, no mark for a station. It tunes finely (`fine_turn`, the prototype's `fineTurn`): a step moves `FINE` (0.02 MHz), or `FAST` (0.06) when steps come under `FAST_MS` (35 ms) apart; a station is a detent, so a step that would end within `CAPTURE` (0.04 MHz) of one, or pass it, lands on it, and the next `HOLD` (3) steps the same way only click in place before the dial moves on (sitting on one after a seek, the list or a tap holds alike). Every step that moves the dial also clicks the buzzer under the Clicker ([Key Tone](#key-tone), `ringnav_piezo`): one click a step, and one asked while the last still sounds is dropped (`tone_busy`), so a fast spin is a train of clicks at the buzzer's own pace, never a smear; the steps a detent holds and the band's ends, which do not move the dial, do not click it. Every step clicks: `k` and a loudness in tenths to the receiver, 10 a step, 14 landing on a station, 6 a held detent, 5 a scrub between stations ([Radio static](#radio-static) has the click). On the tuner screen the touch wheel is read raw (`wheel`, `wheel_raw` while the page is the top window and lit, given back to ticks on any other screen or window, with the screen off, so a turn wakes it as a tick does, and at close; no key event comes, so its travel holds the screen on itself, `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 1)`, as Now Playing's lyrics do): 200 units a turn, a step every 12 degrees (`STEP_THIRDS`, 30 steps a turn, the drag the mockup was tuned on), where a tick at 50% Wheel Sensitivity is 51 degrees; a tick that still comes (a key) is a step. The station the receiver hears is the nearest within `HEAR` (0.1 MHz), off centre as on a real set (`at`). The needle the scale is drawn at, and the receiver hears, follows the dial as `needle()`: `to + (from - to) e^(-t/90 ms)`, landed within 2 kHz, so a run of steps glides rather than jumps, and a frame timer (`FRAME_MS`, 16) redraws only while it glides, the list slides or its music bars play. Next and Previous seek the next station up or down that streams, round the ends. **Centre** (approved 2026-11-20, `~/q2-emu/design/radio-tuner/centre-volume/sheet.png`): its press starts a `LR_HOLD_MS` (550 ms, Edit Library's) hold (`tuner_keydown`, from `ringnav_keydown`). Released sooner it is a tap (`tuner_key`): the volume band takes the dial's place (`vol_band`: Now Playing's band, as `vol_paint` draws it over the progress bar, on the dial's row: the bar's ends at 24 and 346 px, a speaker 8 px in from each, the track inset 24 px in the theme's `np_track_rgb`, white to the volume as `vol_bar` eases); the touch wheel goes back to ticks (`wheel`), and each tick sets the volume as Now Playing's wheel does (`vol_next`, `device_set_volume`, saved), the receiver following as before; `SCRUB_MS` (3 s, Now Playing's scrub and Centre-cycle timeout) after the last turn or press (`vol_end`) the dial is back and the wheel tunes. A tap while it shows ends it at once; a second tap within `DOUBLE_CLICK_MS` of the first, the wheel not turned between, undoes the first and turns the screen off (stock's Centre release replayed to `on_wm_keyup_fun`, as Now Playing's `np_single`). Held to `LR_HOLD_MS` (`hold_due`) it opens the stations list on the station heard, removes stock's own Centre hold (`st.centre_hold`, Shut Down? at 1000 ms) as Edit Library does, so Shut Down? is not reached from the tuner, and takes the release. The list, ZIP and error screens keep stock's Centre hold. Play/Pause pauses (the stream stops and the receiver goes silent; Play starts it again). Return leaves to Home. A tap on the dial (y 225 down) tunes to the frequency under it to 0.01 MHz, landing on a station within `TAP_SNAP` (0.15 MHz); a drag along it scrubs, the scale following the finger, a station within `CAPTURE` pulling it in.

**The words** (`tuner_screen`, the prototype's layout): the frequency the needle is at, 64 px, centred between the status row and the dial (baseline y 158); above it the station's name (y 84), below it the song, or Paused (y 186), and the call sign and city (y 208). A line wider than `WORDS_W` (315 px) is the house marquee (`marquee`): still for `MARQ_HOLD_MS` (1.5 s), then 30 px a second with a copy 40 px behind, its ends faded 16 px into the black, each line on its own clock, repainted every `MARQ_MS` (33 ms) only while one scrolls or the words fade in. The words wait for the station, as RDS does (`words_due`, every state read): only once its stream is sounding (the receiver's state `playing`) and its title has come, or `NO_TITLE_MS` (4 s) of sound has passed with none, then they fade in over `REVEAL_MS` (400 ms); they stay while the dial rests on it, paused or cut out included. Between stations, while a stream connects, and on a station with no stream, the frequency stands alone and the hiss says the rest: there is no "No station".

**The sound** is q2video's FM receiver ([Radio static](#radio-static)), one process (`video_start(.., 2)`, `q2video -t`) from the page's open to its close, the output taken from the player, Spotify and Internet Radio as they take it from each other. A receiver that ends (an output it could not open) is reaped by `tuner_poll` and started again by the next turn of the dial, at most every 3 s. A receiver just started binds its socket some time after the page may have named the stream to it (`land`), so that `u` can be lost (seen in the emulator: the receiver idle with no URL while the page held the station's stream); each state read compares the receiver's `url=` with the stream the page wants and names it again, with the carrier, when they differ (a `u` it already has, the receiver ignores). **Wi-Fi lost:** while the Wi-Fi link is down (`wifi_offline`: stock's network monitor, as the status row reads it), the page shows "No Wi-Fi" as a toast that stays (`toast_stay`, [oled-design: Dialogs and toasts](oled-design.md#dialogs-and-toasts)), over every screen, until the link is back; then it goes, and `r` tells the receiver, so the station comes back by itself. The stream meanwhile has stalled into the receiver's static. A stall with the link up is the static alone, with no toast. The page is one of Smart Wi-Fi's network pages (`net_page_open`) and wakes its radio when it opens (`smart_wake`), so Smart Wi-Fi never turns Wi-Fi off under it. `receive()` tells it the carrier and the needle as integers on `/tmp/q2tuner.sock`: a station with no stream is an unmodulated carrier at 9 dB with flutter 0.7, so its channel sputters; else the loaded stream's station at its strength (`rf_signal`) with a flutter of 0.03 to 0.83 as its km run from 5 to 45, however far the needle has gone (the IF filter makes a far one silent); else nothing, an empty channel's hiss; the offset is the needle less the station, so a station swells out of the hiss as the needle closes on it. The stream starts `LAND_MS` (350 ms) after the dial last moved (`land`), so turning through stations starts none, and is the station on the dial or, on an empty channel, a neighbour 0.2 MHz either side at 70 dB or more, which splatters in (`source`). A stream the dial left stays loaded `WARM_MS` (4 s) (`cool`), so turning back finds it playing. The song line is the stream's StreamTitle (`tuner_title`: iHeart's `title="..",artist=".."` pairs as "Artist - Title", all capitals in title case). While the receiver runs, standby and auto power-off are held and the DAC kept on, and the volume goes to it as Internet Radio's does. **Radio as Now Playing** (the user's, 2026-11-20: "radio should remember place when leaving", "it should be Now Playing when radio is playing until library is reselected", "going back on Radio to another menu should not stop it"): the page is a view of a receiver that outlives it. Its close (`closed`: Back, Home, any page over it) keeps `rt` and the receiver, playing or paused, and only drops the page's widgets and timers (`redraw` and `animate` do nothing without a page; the wheel goes back to ticks); a page that found no stations ends with it as before. Opened again (`tuner_open`, Home's Radio row, or Now Playing's ways in while Radio owns it: Home's first row, `home_np.c` `hn_click`; the status row's and Control Center's `playback_np_open`; Return held, `library_pages.c`), it lands on the tuner where the dial was, the same receiver, no new search. Each landing writes the dial to `/mnt/mmc/Radio/.local/freq` (`FREQ_FILE`, `freq_save`), where a page opened with no receiver starts, as the Library resumes. While `rt` lives Radio is the owner: `tuner_state` (1 playing, 2 paused, the user's Play alone, so connecting, between stations, a dropout or the receiver restarting all read playing) leads `headset.c`'s `media_owner` (5), `media_status` and `media_set_playing`, and `media_key` sends a headset's, the car's or Car Remote's Play/Pause and Next/Previous to it (`tuner_set_playing`, `tuner_media`), so the status row's glyph, Home's first row, Control Center and the car follow it on every page. Home's art pane is Radio's while it owns Now Playing ([oled-design](oled-design.md#homes-art-pane-while-radio-plays)): `coverflow.c` `art_source` answers `SHOW_RADIO`, and `patch/radio_pane.c` draws it in software into the pane's frame bitmap: the ground, glow, badge and vignette worked out once (`layers`, freed with the pane) and the rings a table of alpha by quarter-pixel distance from the badge's centre made each frame (`ring_table`), so a frame is one pass over the pane's pixels; `radio_tick` repaints the pane alone every 33 ms only while it moves (`rp_moving`: its way in, or rings while Radio plays and Reduce Motion is off) and shows, and the way in slides it over a copy of the cover the frame last held (`rp_enter`). The ground and its glow are kept whole once the glow has bloomed (`lit`), and the vignette is blended only over the box it reaches. Measured in the emulator (qemu, 2026-11-20, demo's CPU over 10 s on Home): 11.2% of a host core while the rings move, 0.6% with Radio paused; the first cut, which mixed the glow per pixel per frame and blended the vignette over the whole pane, took 27.2%. ponytail: not yet measured on a Q2. It ends only when the Library is chosen again (`tuner_stop`, the dial saved): a pick (`playback.c` `ringnav_load`, not a restore, calls `tuner_yield`, which drops the held song, `now_drop`, the pick playing in its place), or Play on the Library's own Now Playing page (`tuner_key`, before stock: `now_take_back`, the held song playing on from its place, `player_save_start(0)`, or stock's Play with none held); a page open then is shut. ponytail: the list is painted by the page itself (`list_screen`), not an AWTK list view, so it scrolls by the wheel and takes taps but not a drag.

Checks: `test/tuner.py` (a station through a 3 s dropout: the hiss at -25.9 dBFS, never a silent 50 ms, the station back 250 ms after its stream; a dead stream's restarts, every one of them, and the nudge; the click's length, loudness and brightness), `test/fw/test_radio_tuner.py` (No Wi-Fi standing and going, the nudge, a stall with no toast; the list read; fine steps and fast ones, the detents and their hold, a station heard off centre, the glide's 90 ms, the raw wheel's steps and its hand back; the words' reveal; Centre's tap (the volume band, its wheel, its timeout, a tap to close, the double press) and hold (the list, stock's hold removed, the release taken, none off the tuner screen); land, warm and cool; Back leaving it playing, a page that found nothing ending it, the landing's frequency on the card, Radio the owner for a headset's pause and play until the Library's Play takes it back or a pick drops it; the neighbour's splatter; seek round the ends; pause; the list and ZIP entry and the fetch they start; titles).

## Radio static

`q2video -t DEVICE [VOLUME]` (`tuner` in `patch/video.c`) runs `patch/fmrx.c`, an FM receiver simulated at the audio rate, continuously on ALSA: the transmitter's 75 us pre-emphasis and a soft limiter, the IF filter's amplitude at the instantaneous frequency (3 dB at 97 kHz, 82 dB down at 200), the carrier's phasor plus complex Gaussian noise plus a wandering co-channel ghost at 19 kHz, the discriminator and its S-curve, de-emphasis, a 30 Hz DC block, a fourth-order 15 kHz lowpass, the stereo difference with its own hiss and blend (full at 66 dB), a soft mute of up to 24 dB below 26 dB, 3 Hz multipath flutter, and block-rate smoothing of the level (70 ms up, 30 ms down), offset (10 ms) and gain (15 ms), a station change fading the old carrier out before the new one's level is taken up. It is the approved prototype's `fmRxWorklet`, line for line (its spec: `~/q2-emu/design/radio-tuner/static-model.md`), with cheaper parts for the per-sample transcendental functions: sines from a 4096-entry table with linear interpolation, Gaussian noise from an inverse-CDF table (Acklam's quantile), the arctangent from a polynomial (error under 1e-5 rad), tanh from a rational function where the S-curve flattens; libm only at start and once a 128-frame block.

A stream named by `u` is decoded by ffmpeg into a two-second ring, and the receiver plays it as its programme once 250 ms is in (`TUNER_PRIME`); a ring that runs dry drops the carrier (the hiss of a lost signal) until it is primed again, and a stream that ends is started again for as long as its station is tuned, after 1 s, then 2, 4 and 8, then every 15 s (`tuner_wait_ms`), the count starting over once it sounds (`patch/tuner_core.c`). That is the prototype's cut-out (static-model.md, "Cut-outs"): its "waiting" event, the playback buffer run dry, is the ring run dry here, which comes once the 250 ms the ring holds ahead has played out, and the carrier's level then falls with the model's own 30 ms smoothing and comes back with its 70 ms. `r` (demo's word that the Wi-Fi link is back) starts a stream that isn't sounding again at once, without the wait. `k` and a loudness in tenths is the dial's click (`tuner_click_start`, `tuner_click_mix` in `tuner_core.c`, the prototype's `click()`): a 4 ms noise burst decaying over a fifth of it, through a highpass at 2500 Hz, or at 900 Hz for one over 10 tenths (landing on a station), so a detent sounds louder and duller, 0.18 of full scale a unit of loudness, added after the receiver and before the volume, while paused too. `x` stops the stream; `p` sets the carrier (dB, kHz, the fade in thousandths, the gain 0 or 1, an id); `v` the volume; `q` quits. With the gain at 0 the receiver fades out in 15 ms and then computes and writes nothing (`snd_pcm_drop`) until the gain comes back. `/tmp/q2tuner.state` says `state=` (idle, connecting, playing, stalled, error), `title=`, `codec=` and `url=`.

`test/fmrx.py` builds `test/fmrx_test.c` with `fmrx.c` and holds 38 figures to the prototype's: the empty channel's hiss (-26.1 dBFS against -25.9; its 250 ms windows, its spectrum against 1 kHz at 2122 Hz, 4, 8, 15 and 18 kHz, the largest sample step 0.084), the output noise at station levels 0 to 80 dB (-68.2 dBFS at 80), a 1 kHz tone at -12.1 dBFS (residue -68.4 against -66), off centre at 100 to 200 kHz, a carrier appearing and being lost, and fringe reception at 44 and 24 dB. Where static-model.md's table was taken another way than the scenario here (the appearing carrier, levels 0 and 4 dB, the fringe percentiles), the figure is the worklet's own, run in Node on the same scenario on 2026-11-20, and the port matches it within 0.5 dB. On this laptop the receiver takes 1.6 to 2.2 ms a second of audio; `test/fmrx.py --mips OUT` builds the same measurer for the Q2 (`OUT --bench 20` there), which measured 25.6 ms of CPU a second of audio on the Q2 (`--bench 20`, 2026-11-20: 2.6% of a core), 0.43 ms paused. On this laptop a paused receiver takes 0.03 ms a second. ponytail: a station the needle sits on at a strength whose hiss is inaudible still runs the whole model; passing its programme through the same filters, with the carrier's phase kept for the way back, would save most of that 2.6%.

## Output failure

A song that will not play is said once, never a loop round the queue (`patch/output_fail.c`). q2player reports a failed song with `{player-status\error}` after a file for stock's dialog timer (`on_wm_timer_dialog`, `0x4f4d18`): `/tmp/notfile` (missing) or `/tmp/notsupport` (it will not open or decode), either of which shows stock's toast and calls `player_next_music` (`0x4f4dd4`); with neither file the timer returns at `0x4f46d8` and does nothing. A song whose output would not open or take audio (`engine.c`'s `FAILED`, logged `play failed (the output would not open or take audio)`) makes `/tmp/q2outfail` (`OUTPUT_FAILED_FILE`) instead, since every next song would meet the same output: stock toasts nothing and skips nothing, the player stays stopped on that song, and `output_fail_poll` (from `playback_poll`, while stopped) takes the file, logs `stopped: the output would not open or take audio, so no next song` and shows the warning toast "Audio output unavailable" once. The user's next Play tries the song again. A real run of songs that will not open or decode still skips, but `ringnav_change` counts stock's skips (`output_fail_skip`): the third in a row is refused, the player left stopped, with "Couldn't play 3 songs in a row" and a log line; any other start of the player (`ringnav_start_player`: a press, a pick, a song's natural end) begins the count again. When the PCM is busy, q2player's line names the holder from the kernel's status of the card's first playback substream and that process's command line: `q2player: default: Device or resource busy, held by pid 812 (/usr/bin/q2video -t plughw:0,0)` (`pcm_holder`, `player/output.c`).

**Radio's receiver gives the output back.** On 2026-11-25 a Q2 looped for 77 minutes, 1,679 songs failed, every 2.6 s: Radio was opened at 02:12Z (its `mcl-stop`), a station played, and at 02:16:39Z Radio was paused (`q2tuner.state` `state=idle`, no URL, demo's `x`), so the receiver (`q2video -t plughw:0,0`) faded out and, as written then, dropped its PCM and kept it open (read live: `state: SETUP`, `appl_ptr 512`, one `TUNER_FRAMES` write, `hw_ptr 0`). At 02:22:45Z, with the Bluetooth page open and Bluetooth just switched on, stock's restart after the output change (`player_save_start`, `set-songurl` then `mcl-pause`) loaded the Library's held song into q2player under it: `default: Device or resource busy`, `/tmp/notsupport`, "Not Supported" and the next song, round a dozen-song queue about 143 times until the receiver was killed by hand. Two things now stop that. The receiver lets the PCM go after `TUNER_RELEASE_MS` (2 s) with nothing to play (paused and faded), muting the DAC first as hciplayer does at a close, and opens it again when there is (Play, a click), trying every `TUNER_REOPEN_MS` (200 ms) while another holds it (`tuner_release`, `tuner_reclaim`, `patch/video.c`; each says so in demo's log, `q2video: the receiver let go of plughw:0,0: nothing to play`, `... took plughw:0,0 again`). And every start of the Library's player ends Radio first, as it already ended Spotify and Internet Radio (`ringnav_start_player` calls `tuner_stop` after `now_drop`, so Radio's end hands back no held song): stock's own starts (an output change's `player_save_start` and `player_reconfig`, the dialog's skip) never passed through `ringnav_load`'s `tuner_yield`. Radio logs its receiver's start (`the receiver started (Radio opened): pid N`, or `(again)`), its stop and its own end (`radio_tuner.c` `receiver_start`, `audio_halt`, `tuner_poll`), and `the receiver stopped: the Library's player starts`.

Why the unified log did not collapse it: its repeat count joins only a line identical to the one before (`q2log_core.c` `repeated`), and each 2.6 s round was about a dozen different lines (the song's path in `set-songurl` and `play failed`, FFmpeg's cover warning, and the DAC driver's mute, volume, headphone-type and `unknow_cmd` lines), so only the driver's doubled `mute[1]` ever counted. The loop itself is what is capped: an output failure is one stop and one line per Play, and a run of bad songs at most three.

Checks: `test/player/run.py` `test_a_failure_already_replaced_is_not_reported` (an output that fails makes `/tmp/q2outfail`, not `/tmp/notsupport`) and `test_bt_open_waits_out_a_busy_pcm` (the holder named); `test/playback.py`'s output failure block (stock's dialog timer with neither file skips nothing, one toast and the file taken, three skips in a row and the third refused, another start resetting the count, a start ending Radio); `test/alsa.py` (the real receiver under qemu: paused, it lets its PCM go after 2 s, and takes it again on Play).

## Player crashes

`q2player` is `/usr/bin/hciplayer` in every build, and there is no other player to fall back to. It catches its own fatal signals (`SIGSEGV`, `SIGBUS`, `SIGILL`, `SIGFPE`, `SIGABRT`; `player/main.c` `crashed`, async-signal-safe calls only), counts each in `/tmp/q2player.crashes` (one more when it crashed within 60 s of its start, `HEALTHY_S`, else 1 again) and writes "q2player: crashed, signal 11, crash 2 in a row" to the [unified log](#unified-log) (`E`, source `player`), then dies of the signal; demo starts the player again (docs/player.md#start). The count is in `/tmp`, so each boot starts from none.

## Stock HTTPS

Stock's network code turned certificate checks off: its libcurl helpers set `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER` and `CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST` to 0 and no CA file (the rootfs had none, and its libcurl 7.73 has no default), and hciplayer's ffmpeg left `tls_verify` at its default, 0. Anyone on the network path could read or change Tidal's sign-in, its API calls and the music it streams. The build turns the checks on in all of them, against the whole Mozilla CA bundle as curl publishes it (`assets/mozilla-ca.pem`, pinned by `STOCK_CA_SHA` to `cacert-2026-10-20.pem`), installed as `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` (`STOCK_CA`): stock's hosts are not all known (a card app's cover or stream URL is any server), so no shorter list would do. It costs 200 KB, 144 KB in the squashfs. Q2 Muse's own code keeps `/etc/scrobble-ca.pem`, the few roots it needs.

- **demo.** Ten `curl_easy_setopt` calls turn a check off: `SSL_VERIFYPEER` (`0x40`) and `SSL_VERIFYHOST` (`0x51`), each with 0, in `httpRequest` (`0x484d00`, `0x484d18`: Tidal's sign-in, `userRequestUriThd` and `userPollAuthThd`, and every browse, search and favorite), `curl_http_request` (`0x506254`, `0x50626c`: covers by URL in `player_parsecover_thd` and `parse_albumcovertask_thd`, Baidu's calls, and the update check, which asks Shanling over plain HTTP), two unnamed Tidal helpers, `0x484514` (`0x4845a8`, `0x4845c0`: a favorite added or removed) and `0x4847c8` (`0x48485c`, `0x484874`: a playlist's track added or removed) and `baidu_curl_download_file` (`0x481ad8`, `0x481af4`). Each `jalr` becomes `jal ringnav_stock_tls` (`patch/stock_tls.c`, `STOCK_TLS_CALLS` in `tools/build.py`, which checks each site is a `jalr $25` loaded from `curl_easy_setopt`'s GOT slot, `-0x9e0`, with `$5` set to that option in the four words before). It sets `CAINFO` to the bundle, `SSL_VERIFYPEER` 1, `SSL_VERIFYHOST` 2, whichever of the two calls it stands in for, and libcurl checks no certificate's dates ([TLS](#2038)); stock's 0 is dropped. `curl_http_get` and `getDownloadFileLength` never turned the checks off, so they verify too, now with a CA file. Three Tidal API URLs that carry the session's token were plain HTTP: the subscription check, a track's stream URL (`playbackinfopostpaywall`) and an album's tracks (`TIDAL_HTTP`). `tidal_https` makes each `https://` in place, taking one of the NULs that pad it; only each string's start is referenced. Checked from the build's own rootfs under qemu (its libcurl 8.23.0 over mbedTLS 3.6.7, set up as `ringnav_stock_tls` sets them): `auth.tidal.com`, `api.tidal.com` and `resources.tidal.com` verify, and a certificate for another name, a self-signed one and one from an unknown root are refused (curl error 60); `expired.badssl.com` connects, as no dates are checked ([TLS](#2038)). ponytail: libcurl reads the CA file again for each connection, a 200 KB parse a request; a server with a private CA (a card app's own HTTPS server, say) is refused.
- **the player.** `q2player` links FFmpeg 7.1.5 with mbedTLS 3.6.7 and checks every HTTPS stream's chain against `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` and its host name (`test_https_checks`); stock's hciplayer, with its own FFmpeg and OpenSSL 1.0.1, checked neither and is no longer shipped ([player-plan](player-plan.md)). With the clock wrong by years a chain's dates fail, so Tidal's streams wait for the network time.
- **Not changed.** Internet Radio's `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` (`q2video -r`) still opens a station's HTTPS without a check: a station's server may send a chain OpenSSL can't complete (a browser fetches the missing link; OpenSSL doesn't), the stream carries no account, and a station is anyone's server anyway.

## Tidal cache

Stock's Tidal stream thread (unnamed, after `tidalGetFavoritesIdsThd` at `0x487140`) waits for `tidalfurlstart`, which `get_tidal_trackurl` sets after copying the record's song id into `tidalsongid`. It copies that id to its own `malloc` in `$s2` (`0x48721c`), sets `tidalStreamingLevelNow` from `tidalStreamingLevelNext` (at most 3), and asks `playbackinfopostpaywall` for that quality. It then base64-decodes the manifest (`toolsBase64Decode`) and passes its `urls[0]`, a direct file URL, to `mcl_tidalStartPlayer` (`0x5bf948`, called only at `0x487b28`), which sends it to hciplayer. A skip during the fetch rewrites `tidalsongid` but not the thread's copy.

Its idle poll (the `jalr` at `0x4871a4`) is `ringnav_tidal_poll` (`patch/tidal.c`), which waits on a semaphore with no timer, screen on or off, whatever plays. Only `get_tidal_trackurl` (`0x483f28`, store at `0x484018`) sets `tidalfurlstart`, and stock's loop polls before it reads the flag, so `ringnav_tidal_track` posts the semaphore once stock's `get_tidal_trackurl` has returned: the thread wakes once per track asked for (a queue restored at power-on, a pick, the next track), fetches it, and waits again at its next poll. A post made during a fetch is counted, so it only adds one pass that finds the flag clear. Baidu's stock thread (`baidu_pthread_playurl`, poll at `0x4805b8`) calls `ringnav_baidu_poll`, which waits on a semaphore nothing posts. The thread is not exited, since a `pthread_exit` from the payload's frames has no unwind tables to walk.

`mcl_tidalStartPlayer` is hooked by `tidal_start` (`patch/tidal.c`), two instructions that pass `$s2` on as the song id; the build pins the `$s2` set-up and the call. With the extension of the URL's path (`.flac`, or `.mp4` kept as `.m4a`, which stock's file lists take), the card's `/mnt/mmc/.tidal/<id>-<quality> <artist> - <title><ext>` (`tidal_name`: the queue row with that id at `REC_TIDAL_ID` names it; FAT's reserved characters become `_`, and a long label is cut at a whole UTF-8 character) plays in the URL's place when it exists, found by its `<id>-<quality>` prefix and extension. Otherwise the URL plays, and a detached pthread downloads it with demo's libcurl to `.tmp`, flushes and syncs it, and renames it into place on HTTP 200. A skip (a `tidal_play` with another id; a re-fetch of the same id leaves its download running) or Stop aborts it from curl's progress callback, and one under 1 KB/s for 30 s gives up, so the `.tmp` is removed. Stop is inferred, not signalled: the callback reads stock's play status (`mclGetPlayStatus`, 1 stopped) and aborts once it has read stopped for `TIDAL_STOP_MS` (3 s) running, so the stopped state between queued tracks keeps the copy; ponytail: a stream that sits stopped longer than that before it plays drops its copy (cached on a later play). Only one download runs at a time: a track that starts while a skipped one's transfer is still ending leaves its URL as the job the same thread takes next, the latest track's only, and none is queued below `card_space`'s 16 MB. After each download the oldest files by mtime are removed until `.tidal` holds at most the cap chosen in [Streaming configuration](#streaming-configuration) (2 GB by default), read once per trim. The copy is verified against `/etc/scrobble-ca.pem` (`CAINFO`, `SSL_VERIFYPEER` 1, `SSL_VERIFYHOST` 2; no dates, [TLS](#2038)), which carries GlobalSign Root R3 and Amazon Root CA 1 for Tidal's media hosts: `*.audio.tidal.com` on Fastly (`sp-pr-fa`, `lgf`) chains to the first, its CloudFront hosts (`sp-pr-cf`, `ab-pr-cf`) to the second. A host Tidal moves to another authority fails the download, and the track still plays from the stream, whose own check (hciplayer's, [Stock HTTPS](#stock-https)) covers the chain but not the host name. Tidal's files carry no tags, so before the rename the copy is remuxed by stock `/usr/bin/ffmpeg` (`tag`: `-c copy` to `<file>.tmp.tag.tmp`, renamed over the `.tmp` on exit 0 with a non-empty file) with the queue row's title, artist and album; a FLAC also gets the row's cover (`REC_COVER`, `+0x28`, the `/tmp/tidal/*.jpg` that `player_get_id3info` hands the cover thread as type 2), fitted to 640 px by `thumb` into `/tmp/.tidal_cover.jpg` as the job starts, since stock removes a page's covers when another opens, as an attached picture. A track played from Tidal Downloads then shows its artist and art from its own tags. ponytail: no art in an `.m4a`, as ffmpeg 4.2's mp4 muxer writes no cover; a row whose cover file is already gone (a queue restored at power-on) gets tags but no art; any ffmpeg failure keeps the untagged copy; copies cached before this stay untagged until Clear All Downloads; the remux writes the file once more on the card. Only the URL sent to the player changes; the queue record, art and Now Playing are stock's. The API request still runs first, so a cached track started from Tidal's pages needs Wi-Fi but streams nothing. **Streaming → Tidal Downloads** (`tidal_downloads` in `library_lists.c`) lists `.tidal` through `toolsLoadDirectory`, newest file first, by the label after the prefix, and folder-plays a row as local music, so it needs no Wi-Fi; its page name starts `tidal*`, so the playback keys stay with it (`media_focused`). ponytail: oldest download goes first (demo imports no `utime`to touch a replayed file); a`.tmp` left by a power-off stays until that track is cached again, or Clear All Downloads. The list ends in **Clear All Downloads…** (`td_clear`), which, from a 0 ms timer as a row's click may not rebuild its list (`td_show`), puts **Remove Downloads?** in the list's place (the track count, Cancel, Remove), worded as Spotify's Storage Management; Cancel or Return (`td_keyup`) lists the songs again, on the Clear row. Remove (`tidal_clear`, tidal.c) unlinks every name in `.tidal`not starting with a dot: finished copies and`.tmp`ones, nothing outside the folder;`.cache-size`stays. There is no index to keep in step, as the list is`toolsLoadDirectory`of the folder, read again after. It runs under`td.lock`, drops a queued job and counts `td.cleared`; the download thread renames its finished `.tmp`into place under the same lock only if that count hasn't moved since its job began, so a download running across the clear is dropped rather than left behind. A play after it caches as usual. ponytail: on the UI thread, holding the lock, a moment for a full 8 GB cache. The confirmation is the same page rebuilt, not a pushed one: a new runtime window would need its own`contexts.inc` entry, builder allowance and close handling.

Checks in `test/peq.py` (host build): `tidal_ext` on a query string, a dot only in the query, a trailing dot and an extension too long for the buffer; `trim`'s eviction at 2 GB, 4 GB and 512 MB caps and a failed `unlink`.

## Tidal track lists

Stock keeps a Tidal track list in `stTidalTracks` (16 bytes: total, limit, offset, the record deque). `init_infodata` (`0x4e28e8`), run as the album/playlist page (`tidal_albuminfo`) opens, clears the deque and sets limit 50, offset 0. `tidalPlaylistDetailThd` (`0x48c178`, `playlists/%s/items?...offset=%d&limit=%d`) and `tidalAlbumDetailThd` (`0x48c33c`, `albums/%u/tracks?offset=%d&limit=%d`) request one page from the struct's offset and limit into `/tmp/tidal_<thread>` (`httpRequest`; the thread's own id) and set `tidal_albuminfo_thread_run` to 2. The page's timer polls that flag, then parses the file (`parseTidalPlaylistDetailJson` `0x48c650` or `parseTidalAlbumDetailJson` `0x48d2a0`, by the pthread id it started), which appends the records and writes back `totalNumberOfItems` and the reply's `limit`, removes it and lists the deque. Neither page ever asks for another page, so a list stopped at 50. My Collection's Tracks (`tidalColTracksThd`, `0x489074`, `users/%u/favorites/tracks?...limit=50&offset=%d`, its offset the thread's argument, done flag `tidal_collection_thread_run`) does page, parsed the same way (`parseTidalColTracksJson`, `0x48b0a0`): the page's scroll handler (`0x4df79c`) adds 50 to the offset and starts the thread again when a scroll ends near the bottom of a list with pages left. That takes a touch drag to the end; inferred from the issue's report (favorites stop at 50), not traced, the wheel's selection moves don't reach it.

The three threads are hooked (`ringnav_tidal_playlist`, `ringnav_tidal_album`, `ringnav_tidal_favs`, `patch/tidal.c`) and their done stores (`0x48c31c`, `0x48c4ac`, `0x4891d4`, `sb $3,0($2)`) become `nop`s (`TIDAL_PAGE_DONE`). `tidal_pages` runs the stock thread and parses its reply itself with the page's parser, so the deque and total grow per page (without that parse the deque never grew, so 1.4.8's first build stopped at 50), then, while the offset plus the limit is short of the total, adds the limit to the offset (in the struct, and as the argument for favorites) and runs it again; after the last page the hook writes `{"items":[]}` over the reply and sets the done flag, so the page's own parse adds nothing (it returns 1 on an empty `items`) and lists the whole deque once. A first page that fails to parse is left for the page, so its error handling (`subStatus` 11003, a sign-in that ran out) is stock's; a later one ends the run with what loaded. Favorites leave the offset at the last page's, so the scroll handler's check (page `offset/limit + 1` against `ceil(total/limit)`) finds no page left. A run ends early when a page adds no record (a failed request: the parser leaves the deque alone) or the struct's offset is no longer the one it set (`init_infodata` reset it: the page was opened again). ponytail: `TIDAL_MAX_TRACKS` (2,000) caps a list at 40 sequential requests, the page's spinner meanwhile; a page opened again while a request is in flight can still take that page's records, as stock's single request could. Limits: still 50 a request, stock's own size (Tidal's maximum per request isn't known here); favorite albums, artists and playlists and the user's playlist list keep stock's 50 and touch paging.

## Streaming configuration

Streaming's last row, **Configuration** (`stream_config` in `patch/stream_config.c`, `stream_config.png`: `assets/icons/stream_config.png`, a gray disc with a sliders glyph whose strokes stay crisp at the 40px rows (stock's `system_netservice` globe frayed there), with `list_tidal`'s inode metadata, resized on iPod as the other Streaming icons), opens `streamconf_page`, a `page_list` in two levels ([oled-design](oled-design.md#streaming-configuration)): Stop Streaming Services; Download Ahead, Off to 3 songs; a Services header; TIDAL and Spotify, each a row with a chevron and its value, Shown or Hidden by its switch, that opens `streamsvc_page` (`sc_open_sub`, titled by the service: its Show in Streaming switch, TIDAL's Show Downloads switch (Tidal Downloads') and its Cache, Spotify's Cache and Erase Spotify Data); a Show in Streaming header; then a switch per service that has nothing else (the card apps, Internet Radio, AirPlay). ponytail: the approved captions under the selected row are not built here: the settings rows' captions (`caption_row`, settings_pages.c) grow a stock settings list's row, which that list stacks by height, while a `page_list` places its rows at fixed offsets and the selection (`caption_sel`) is handed the row's parent; it needs `page_list` rows that restack and `caption_sel` taking a page row. `sc_text` writes every row that reads a state on whichever of the two pages is open, after each change, so a switch flipped on TIDAL's page reads on Configuration's TIDAL row at once. Both pages are listed in `patch/contexts.inc` (`CTX_DYNAMIC`), so the wheel moves the selection and Center presses the row, as on the other payload lists.

**Cache sizes.** Each provider page's Cache steps through 512 MB, 1 GB, 2 GB, 4 GB and 8 GB (`512 << i` MB) on each press. Each is a file, `.tidal/.cache-size` and `.spotify/.cache-size`, holding `<MB>M` (`2048M`), librespot's `--cache-size-limit` form; the folder is made if missing and the file written with `blob_io` (a `.tmp`, synced and renamed). `stream_cache` reads it back with `state_read`; missing, or anything but those five sizes, is 2 GB. Files, not `config.ini`: `trim` reads Tidal's on the download thread, and the card's Spotify launcher reads Spotify's. The dot keeps Tidal's out of `trim`'s count and `cached`'s matches, and Tidal Downloads lists only songs. A smaller Tidal cap applies at the next download's `trim`. The launcher (q2-librespot's `contrib/shanlingq2/launcher.sh`) reads `.cache-size` before each librespot start, falling back to `2G` when it is empty or not digits with at most one trailing `K`, `M` or `G`, so a new Spotify size applies when librespot next starts. Older launchers ignore the file and keep `2G`.

**Download Ahead** (`ahead_step` in `patch/stream_state.c`) steps Off, 1 Song, 2 Songs and 3 Songs on each press, `[Q2POD] AHEAD` (0 to 3; missing or anything else is 2), read once (`ahead_n`). It is told to the card app whose m3u queue plays, in `/tmp/q2-<id>.ahead`, at its next poll, with the songs it is to fetch; the contract, and the app's `.stream` that says how far each one has come, are in [server-library.md](server-library.md#download-ahead-and-the-streaming-state).

**A streamed song's length** (`stream_length` in `patch/stream_state.c`, `np_stream_length` in `patch/np_stream.c`). A song arriving in place reads short to the player: a constant-bitrate MP3 with no Xing frame is measured by its bytes so far, so its total grows while it downloads. Until its `.stream` line is `done`, the firmware shows the server's length instead, which the app gives in the line's length field (the Subsonic duration) or the catalogue has for the song (`catalogue_copy_seconds`), and `--:--` when it has neither.
