Elapsed time is the player's and keeps counting. `np_sync` writes the right-hand time (the total under Track Time: Total, else what is left of the server's length), `paint_scrubber` draws the track over stock's bar and the fill against the server's length (none while it is unknown, so the bar never runs against the growing figure and nothing rescales when the file is whole: stock's bar takes over at `done`, the same ratio when the server's duration is right), About's length cell and the car remote's `len` (0 unknown, which the daemon fills from the catalogue) follow, and `duration_seconds` and `duration_text` do the same for the rows of Up Next and the song lists (`--:--` for none). The line is read at most every 200 ms (`NS_LEN_MS`). The song at `/stream/` only: a catalogue row's length is the server's already. Home's Playing row shows no time. AirPlay's `length` in `/tmp/q2cast.track` (`air_track` in `patch/airplay.c`) is the server's too, 0 while unknown, looked at again every second (`AIR_LEN_MS`) while the song arrives and written again when it changes. A bar with no length at all (the slider's `max` at its `min`: a pressed server song before the player has it, the previous song stopped) gets the track drawn over it as well: stock's slider still fills about a ninth of it then (38 of 323 px on the emulator, q2player), which read as progress beside 0:00. A seek in a song still arriving goes where it was asked, the player's to answer (`player/grow.c`): while FFmpeg searches, the file's size is the bytes on the card and a read at their end ends (`grow_seeking`, around `source_seek`'s `av_seek_frame`), as its FLAC search, with or without a SEEKTABLE, reads the last frame's timestamp at the file's end and so waited there for the whole song (on the emulator, 2026-11-18, a seek inside the bytes there were sat on the spinner while the download ran on; with this, a tap at 0:28 of a FLAC 12 MB of 28 MB in plays from 0:28 at once). Inside the bytes there are it plays from the target at once; past them the search lands on the last frame there, the frames up to the target are decoded and dropped as they come, and the read waits at the end of the bytes, so Now Playing shows the spinner and the bytes so far, the position the target's (`engine.c` reports a seek's target at once while playing), and the song plays from the target once they come: a tap at 3:58 of 4:11, 5 MB in, waited about 55 s at 3:58 and played on to the end. A seek is not cut short to the bytes there are: one exactly where it was asked, whichever caller asked (a tap or scrub through `ringnav_seek_time`, hold-to-scan backward, Song Radio's seek of its seed to its place, Resume), against a share of the bytes that is only an estimate of the time (embedded art and a song's changing bitrate move it). `stream_reach` (`patch/stream_state.c`) is that estimate, the last second a seek could go to while the song arrives, and nothing calls it. Checks: `test/player/run.py` `grow_seek_inside` and `grow_seek_beyond`, each with and without a SEEKTABLE.

**A streamed song's start** (`start_bytes` in `patch/stream_state.c`, `GROW_ANALYZE_US` in `player/source.c`). A song arriving in place is queued once `START_MS` (3 s) of it is on the card at its average rate, at least `START_MIN` (256 KB). That must cover what q2player's open of it reads, or the open waits in the [growing read](server-library.md#download-ahead-and-the-streaming-state) (harmless, but no sooner). The open reads the headers (a FLAC's embedded cover is in them: up to 189 KB before the audio of the eight songs on a Q2's stream folder, 2026-11-22) and then whatever `avformat_find_stream_info` asks. q2player's FFmpeg has no JPEG or PNG decoder, so a cover's size stays unknown, and FFmpeg's default analysis read on until 5 s of audio, 0.45 to 0.72 MB for those songs, waiting for them to arrive. With an arriving song's analysis capped at 100 ms the open reads its headers and about 1.3 s of audio, its parser's look ahead (FFmpeg's flac demuxer on a 133 KB/s FLAC with a 76 KB cover: 917 KB read uncapped, 308 KB at 500 ms, 252 KB at 100 ms or less). For those eight songs that is at most 189 KB and 1.3 s of audio, under their 3 s (325 to 353 KB). A whole file is opened as before. ponytail: a cover larger than about 1.7 s of the song's bytes makes the open wait past the gate; reading the headers' length in `stream_startable` would lift it.

Measured on a pooled emulator (2026-11-22): a 180 s FLAC of 133 KB/s with a 76 KB cover, written in place from 0.5 s at a steady rate, times from the app's `.play`; a wait is `/tmp/q2player.wait` named, seen in 50 ms looks.

| Rate | Sound, 8 s gate | Sound, 3 s gate | First wait after the start, 8 s gate / 3 s gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 300 KB/s | 4.4 s | 2.4 s | none in 30 s / none in 30 s |
| 125 KB/s (just under the song's rate) | 9.5 s | 4.3 s | none in 45 s / 35.6 s |
| 100 KB/s | 11.9 s | 4.9 s | 40.0 s / 11.5 s |

With the refill after a stall (below), the same runs on the 3 s gate (2026-11-22): at 100 KB/s sound at 5.2 s and 2 waits in 45 s, 12.2 s of waiting in all, where playing on at any byte made 121 waits for 12.1 s; at 125 KB/s none in 45 s, where there were 9; at 300 KB/s sound at 2.3 s and none, the start no later. A download slower than the song always runs out: the smaller gate brings the first wait sooner, and the refill makes the waits few. The downloads measured on a Q2 (2026-11-22) ran at 0.65 to 2.45 MB/s against about 110 KB/s of FLAC. A 10 s stall at 300 KB/s once 1.3 MB had come was waited out at the end of the bytes; the song played on within 0.1 s of the bytes coming again playing on at any byte, and 1.35 s after them with the refill, the time 3 s of the song takes to come at that rate. Once it has stalled, the player waits for a refill before it plays on (`player/grow.c`, `REFILL_S`): 3 s of the song ahead of where it is, at the song's average rate, then 6 s and 12 s (`REFILL_MAX_S`) at the stalls after, or the line done or failed, so a download slower than the song plays in a few long stretches; Now Playing shows the spinner and the amount meanwhile (`/tmp/q2player.wait`). Playing on at any byte, the song broke off at every packet: on the host, a1 arriving at three quarters of its rate ran the car's PCM dry 41 times (3.6 s of silence in all), and 2 times with the refill (5.4 s in all), whole either way (`test/player/run.py` `test_grow_slow_download_plays_in_few_long_stretches`). The open's own reads still go on at any byte, so the start is not delayed.

**Erase Spotify Data**, under Cache on Spotify's page, asks first on the confirmation card ("Erase Spotify Data?", "Its login, cache and logs go; sign in again to use it.", Cancel first, Erase red); its Erase (`sc_erase_answer`) runs the [App Store](#q2-shelf)'s erase job (`shelf_erase` in netupdate.c, on its one job thread, so it says "Wait for the one in progress" while an install, remove or check runs): `spot_stop`, then `rm -rf .spotify/cache .spotify/.cache-size` with the add-on's logs (`spot.log`, to which its launcher appends librespot's messages: the account's name at each login and every track loaded; `aplay.log`, its sink's; and `load.log`, written while a `debug` file is there; ponytail: it comes back within 10 s while that file stays, as the launcher's debug loop isn't killed by `SPOT_KILL`) and `rmdir .spotify` (gone only when Spotify isn't installed), `sync`, `spot_stop` again, and "Spotify's login and cache erased". The row reads "Erasing…" meanwhile; at the end `stream_erased` reads the rows again, so Spotify's Cache shows 2 GB, `.cache-size` being gone. The row is there with or without `.spotify`, as Spotify's Cache is.

**Stop Streaming Services** (`sc_click`) runs `spot_stop` (`SPOT_KILL`: the restart loop, librespot and its `aplay`, the state and `SPOT_OUT` files; `sp` cleared, so `spot_poll` idles, `spot_status` is 0 and the keys and `media_owner` are local music's), `radio_stop` (q2video `-r` quit or killed, `rd.active` 0) and, when the queue is a stock stream (`MCL_TYPE` neither 1 nor `0xf0xx`: Tidal) and hciplayer isn't stopped, `player_stop`. A local queue is left as it is; the next local track readies the DAC itself (`player_start`). It toasts "Streaming stopped" and is harmless with nothing running. Without it, a paused librespot stays the active source (`sp.active`) until a local track plays or `SPOT_IDLE_MS` passes, so Play/Pause, the side buttons, Bluetooth controls and the status bar follow Spotify, and a phone that casts again stops local music (`spot_take`). ponytail: AirPlay's receiver keeps running; its switch is on Network service.

**Shown services.** After Stop Streaming Services, a section header row, "Show in Streaming" in 15 px Text Tertiary (a bare `list_item_create` holding its label, no click, so the wheel passes over it), stands above one switch row per service `ringnav_stream` lists (`svc`: stock's TIDAL row, Spotify, the card apps in `addon_scan`'s order, Tidal Downloads, Internet Radio, AirPlay), each with Shanling's `switch_on` (shown) or `switch_off` (`list_toggle`, at screen x 302 as the settings rows'). Center (`svc_toggle`) flips it and saves the hidden ones in `Q2POD STREAMHIDE` in `config.ini`, comma separated: a fixed row's upper-case key (`TIDAL`, `SPOTIFY`, `DOWNLOADS`, `RADIO`, `AIRPLAY`) or a card app's id, which is lower case, so the two never collide and a hidden app stays hidden when another app changes its place. A missing key hides nothing. `ringnav_stream` tags each row it builds with its service (`SVC_PROP`, `ringnav_svc`) and hides the saved ones with `widget_set_visible`; a toggle finds the Streaming page underneath (`scroll_view_streamsset` from `window_manager`) and shows or hides the tagged row there too, then lays the list out again, so Return shows the change. Configuration has no switch and always stays. The comma list is `csv_find`/`csv_toggle`, shared with Spotify's Remove selection; an empty key is never added. ponytail: an uninstalled app's id stays in the key (the app is hidden again if reinstalled); once the value would pass `ROOT_MAX` (200 bytes, far beyond the five fixed keys and eight app ids; not the 260-byte buffer, as stock's config line is a 257-byte `sprintf` and a 255-byte `fgets`), a toggle that hides refuses with "Could not save setting".

Checks in `test/patch.py`: the row and its icon, the page's labels, each cache row's step, wrap and file, `stream_cache` on a size not in the list, every payload list page on the wheel's allowlist, Erase's two presses (dropped by another row and by leaving, refused while it runs, the erase and Spotify's Cache back to 2 GB), and the stop row's kill, `player_stop` for a stream queue, its toast, and radio and Spotify no longer owning the keys; the service rows' ticks, `STREAMHIDE` and the Streaming rows they hide, at once and on the next open.

## Album artists

Stock has two artist settings. `artist_type` (`0xa4ca3c`, `PLAYSET ARTISTTYPE`, read by `read_artistype_value`) is the artist page's own switch (`btn_artistswitch`), which picks its albums and songs by album artist (`getAlbumByAlbumArtist`, `getMusicByAlbumAndAlbumSonger`) or by artist. `g_artist_type` (`0xa4ca54`) picks `GetAllAlbumArtist` for the Artists list and the album-artist queries for an artist's albums in `load_localclass_list`, but nothing in stock writes it, so Artists always grouped by the Artist tag and a guest artist split an album. `ringnav_localclass` copies `artist_type` into `g_artist_type` before every list load, so Artists, an artist's albums, the artist page and the [Queue menu](#queue-menu) follow one setting. `GetAllAlbumArtist`'s row callback (`0x506798`) fills the name at `+0x18` as `getAllArtist`'s does, and also at `+0x24`, so the rows show and expand the same way. **Playback → Artists** (`ringnav_audioset`, after stock's 15 rows in `scroll_view_playset`) toggles `artist_type` and writes `PLAYSET ARTISTTYPE`, as the artist page's switch does; the lists take it on their next load. Album Artist is the default: stock's read, `read_artistype_value` (`0x4fee80`, `atoi` of the key with `"0"` as its default), is replaced by `ringnav_read_artistype`, which reads a missing key as 1. Stock calls it only from `localmusic_localclass_page_init` and `localmusic_artistinfo_page_init`, so until a Library list or artist page opened, `artist_type` stayed 0 for Playback' row, boot resume (`memeory_startplayer`) and an artist page opened from Coverflow; `ringnav_bootmode` (`config_init`'s play-mode call, before Home restores the queue) reads it once at boot as well. Stock's `config.ini` template has no `ARTISTTYPE`, and only the two toggles write it, so a saved Artist (0) stays Artist. Stock's album-artist queries (`GetAllAlbumArtist`'s `group by albumsonger`, an artist's albums' and songs' `albumsonger like '%s'` and `albumsonger=""`, search) only match the tag, so in Album Artist mode an album without one was missing from its artist and listed under Unknown Artist. `ringnav_library_query` (the `toolsQueryDbTable` hook) rewrites every `albumsonger` in those queries to `ifnull(nullif(albumsonger,''),songer)`, as `ringnav_content_query` does on `toolsQueryContentDbTable` (`0x5db30c`, the same with a row argument and the name sort on the stack), which an artist's albums (`getAlbumByAlbumArtist`) run through, so such a song goes by its artist on both tabs; Unknown Artist keeps only songs with neither tag, its albums as its songs. `select *` records keep the real tag at `+0x24`, and Coverflow's own grouping (`ALBUM_SQL`, recognized by its `ifnull(albumsonger`) is left as is, so an untagged compilation stays one album there. Stock's libtag reads a Vorbis album artist only as `ALBUMARTIST`, so FLACs tagged `ALBUM ARTIST` (foobar2000's spelling) had an empty `albumsonger` and listed under Unknown Artist. `toolsGetMusicInfo` (`0x5d8b98`, called by the library scan, `player_get_id3info` and `get_songid3_info`) is hooked: when stock leaves its album artist (`info + 0x580`, `MUSIC_INFO_ALBUM_ARTIST`) empty, `ringnav_music_info` reads a `.flac`'s VORBIS_COMMENT block itself, seeking past the other metadata blocks, and copies `ALBUM ARTIST`, at most 255 bytes. Ogg Vorbis and Opus are not read for it. Before stock's read, `crash_note` writes the path to `/tmp/q2-scan-file` and, every 500th read, appends the count, demo's VmRSS (`/proc/self/statm`) and the path to `/tmp/q2-scan.log` (each demo starts it afresh, stopped past 64 KB), which a crash log includes ([boot.md](boot.md)), so an OOM kill during Update Local Music names its file and shows whether demo grew.

<a id="oversized-ogg-tags"></a>**Oversized Ogg tags.** TagLib reads an Ogg file's comment header (packet 1) whole: `Ogg::File::packet` joins its pages into one buffer grown by doubling, and `XiphComment::parse` decodes each `METADATA_BLOCK_PICTURE` from base64 beside it, about 4 times the header. MusicBee converting a FLAC to Opus keeps its pictures there, and a 20 MB header got demo OOM-killed (92 MB resident) in Update Local Music. Before stock's read, `ringnav_music_info` measures the header of a `.opus`, `.ogg` or `.oga` from its page headers alone (`ogg_tags`, `patch/xiph.c`: lacing values, seeking past the data, stopped at EOF, a page without `OggS` and version 0, or `OGG_PAGES_MAX` pages). Up to `OGG_TAGS_MAX` (4 MB: a 3 MB cover's 4,000,000 base64 bytes stay under it, about 16 MB at TagLib's peak) stock reads the file as before. Over it, stock's TagLib is not called: `xiph_parse` streams the comments, reading at most `XIPH_VALUE` (1 KB) of each and seeking past the rest, the pictures included, and fills `toolsGetMusicInfo`'s fields as TagLib 2.0.1 and Shanling's getters would: title (`+0x280`), artist (`+0x100`), album (`+0`), genre (`+0x200`, through `ringnav_genre_copy`), composer (`+0x480`) and `ALBUMARTIST` (`+0x580`), each key's values joined with `" / "`, through stock's `toolsFixId3ErrorCode` with libtag_c's Latin-1 copy and `isLatin1` test (`utf8_latin1`); the year (`+0x680`, `DATE`, else `YEAR`), Shanling's packed track, disc (`DISC`, else `DISCNUMBER`, else 1000) at `+0x684` and track (`TRACKNUM`, else `TRACKNUMBER`) at `+0x688`; `MQAENCODER`'s flag (`0x100` in `+0x68c`); and, when audio properties are asked for, the sample rate at `+0x690` (Opus 48000, Vorbis its identification header's) and 16 bits in `+0x68c`. A key matches case aside, a value ends at its first zero byte, and an empty or invalid UTF-8 value is dropped, as TagLib's `addField` and `String` do. A header its pages cut short, or Opus without `OpusHead`, writes nothing, as TagLib's invalid file. The FLAC fallback above reads `ALBUM ARTIST` with the same `xiph_parse` in its raw mode, which keeps the earlier reader's result exactly (the first value with a byte in it, its first 255 bytes as they are, UTF-8 or not, no count check), since albums are grouped by it; the folder tag refresh, lyrics from tags and Long Songs skip TagLib for these files too. Limits: a joined text field keeps 511 bytes, so the GBK test sees only those; UTF-8 is checked in a value's first 1 KB; numbers go through `strtol`, not `wcstol`; the codec is told by the header's magic, not by the extension as `FileRef` does; Ogg FLAC and Speex over the cap still go to TagLib; Long Songs gets no length for such a file and lyrics from tags none. Embedded art goes through TagLib too: `toolsGetAlbumCover` (`0x5d709c`) calls `taglib_album_picture` (`libtag_c` `0x12508`, its only caller), which gives an `.ogg` to `get_oggfile_albumpic`, `XiphComment::pictureList` after the same whole parse; `.opus` and `.oga` have no picture reader there. Its four callers (`player_parsecover_thd`'s Now Playing art at `0x51dc90` and the three `GRID_COVER` sites) and Coverflow's `build_art` all reach it, so its entry is hooked: `ringnav_album_cover` (`patch/coverflow.c`) returns no art for an `.ogg` whose header `ogg_tags` measures over `OGG_TAGS_MAX`, without calling stock, and each caller's fallback hands the file to ffmpeg (`ff_thumb`), whose child the kernel kills first (`oom_score_adj` 1000): Now Playing's through `coverflow_player_cover` (folder images first, then the embedded picture), the grids' through `grid_cover`, Coverflow's after `beside_art`. Any other `.ogg` goes to stock as before, so stock's peak for one is still about 4 times a header of up to 4 MB.

**Artists rows.** Library Artists, Composers and Genres share one row template (built at `0x4b39f4`, bound at `0x4b36b8`); each bind calls `0x4b2268` (`class_icon`), which sets `img_icon` to `default_artist_small` for Artists, a genre icon for Genres, or a `.downpic` picture. That call (`CLASS_ICON`, `0x4b37e4`) is a `jal` to `ringnav_class_icon`, which hides `img_icon` on Artists so the name takes its width (iPod's `compact_row_layout` skips hidden siblings; Stock keeps its 200 px label) and shows it again, through stock's setter, on the others.

**Songs rows.** The Songs template's bind (`0x4ab208`) copies `REC_ARTIST` into `scrlabel_artist`, trimmed; an empty one gets stock's "Unknown Artist" through `getFormatString`. That call (`SONG_UNKNOWN_CALL`, `0x4ab424`) is a `jal` to `ringnav_song_unknown`, which leaves the buffer empty, as the grid has no text-row artwork, so a two-line row with no artist tag has an empty second line, and a record that holds "Unknown" reads so. Every other set calls stock's.

**Row faces.** Stock's long lists are virtual tables (`table_client`: Artists, Composers, Genres, Songs, Albums and the rest), a pool of rows bound to their entries as the list scrolls. Its loader (`0x5dcbac`, which `table_client_reload`, `table_client_set_yoffset` and `table_client_ensure_children` all reach) sets each row's index, shows and moves it, and calls the page's `on_load_data` (`0x5dcdac`), which writes the row's text. No relayout follows, so `compact_row_layout`'s `theme_font` never sees the new text: a row rebound from a Latin name to a CJK one kept the theme's face (Inter has no CJK) and drew blank, and one rebound the other way kept stock's face. That call (`TABLE_LOAD_CALL`) is a `jal` to `ringnav_table_load`, which calls `on_load_data` (from the client's `TABLE_LOAD_DATA`) and then `row_faces`: each label in the row that `theme_font` gave a face (its `_font`, which keeps the role above the answer) is fitted again to its text, at its role's size. A label never themed is left alone, so a row that takes no face binds as stock's do.

## Charge Limit

The charger is the AXP2101 PMIC's integrated one (the device tree's `x-powers,axp2101-power-supply`, driven by `drivers/power/supply/axp2101_charger.c`, which registers `battery` and `axp2101_charger`; there is no bq25890 driver in the kernel or rootfs), set to 1000 mA of charge current, the 2000 mA USB input limit (`pmu_usbpc_cur`), a 4.35 V target (`pmu_init_chgvol` 0x10fe) and 100 mA of termination (`pmu_iterm_limit` 0x64). The fuel gauge is the CW2015 on I2C-0 (`/sys/devices/i2c-0/0-0062/cw2015_capacity`, `module_driver/cw2015.sh`). `toolsGetChargeStatus` (`0x5cf5ec`) reads `/sys/class/power_supply/battery/status` (1 Charging, 2 Full, -1 Discharging or anything else, 0 unreadable); the `bq25890_1_status` paths it probes and the `echo %d > .../bq25890_1_otg_enable` helper are for the other Shanling players that share `demo`. `switch_charge_enable(on)` (`0x4fe42c`) sets the active-low charge enable on GPIO `PE22` through `toolsGpioSetValue` (libgpio, no shell); stock uses it only for USB mode's and AirPlay's charge choice (`g_usbdac_chargeflag`; `usbmode_page_init`, `usbmode_exit`, `airplay_page_init`). With it high, charging is off and the player runs from USB while the battery holds. `get_battery_capacity` (`0x4ff258`) keeps `g_power_capacity` (0-100) and `g_power_chargestate` (a negative status is not stored).

**System settings → Power → Charge Limit** (`ringnav_powermanager`, after stock's rows in `scroll_view_powermanager`; `Q2POD CHARGELIMIT` in `config.ini`). Every `CHARGE_POLL_MS` (5 s) `charge_poll`, from `ringnav_sleep`, stops charging at `CHARGE_STOP` (80%), stops it again if anything turned it back on meanwhile (USB mode's exit, AirPlay) while the charger reports charging, and hands it back at `CHARGE_RESUME` (75%) or when the limit is turned off, on, or `g_usbdac_chargeflag` while `usbmode_page` or `airplay_page` is open. The hand-back goes through `switch_charge_enable`, so the early guard below can keep it off (Audio and DAC with charging Off, or no cable). ponytail: only while demo runs; a powered-off Q2 charges as stock.

### Early USB DAC charging guard

`patch/usb_charge.c` applies the saved USB DAC charging choice before enumeration, for every host.
The added `etc/init.d/S12usbcharge` (from `patch/usb_charge.sh`) drives the active-low charge-enable
GPIO PE22 high after the GPIO driver loads and before the player starts (and turns the ID pin PD18's
pull-up on: [OTG host power](#otg-host-power)). `ringnav_usb_config`
keeps it inhibited while stock `config_init` reads settings, then reconciles those settings and
the detected cable. This covers a running player waiting for insertion; it cannot control the
PMIC before Linux and this startup script execute.

The policy is `requested && ready && g_last_otgid != 1 && (g_usbdac_chargeflag == 1 || (cable == 1 && g_usbmode == 0))`:
USB DAC Charging On permits charging, as does a detected cable with USB Storage selected.
`g_last_otgid` 1 is the Q2 as a USB host: stock's `check_otg_status` (`0x4f3408`), with the ID pin
(`PD18`) low (and only once [OTG host power](#otg-host-power)'s wait is over), turns the bus power on (`PC20` high) and the charger off (`PE22` high) by writing the
pins directly, and `get_battery_capacity` reads no cable while it lasts. Each USB pass reads `PE22`
back and writes the policy again when the two differ, so without that term the guard turned the
charger back on within the same pass (seen in the emulator with the pins recorded, 2026-11-17:
`PC20=1`, `PE22=1`, then `PE22=0` in the same millisecond), charging the battery from the Q2's own
bus power; Charge Limit's hand-back did the same. `test/fw/test_usb_charge.py` covers both.
An unknown setting, failed enumeration or a timeout never establishes a dedicated charger. With
Audio and DAC selected and charging Off, an unidentified wall charger is therefore inhibited too:
select USB Storage or turn USB DAC Charging On. No charger-type detector or PMIC register changes
are added. Disabling battery charging does not establish zero USB current to the system.

The choice is stock's `g_usbdac_chargeflag`, saved as `PLAYSET USBDAC_CHARGE`. Stock's `config_init`
(`0x504234`) reads it with `toolsReadConfig`'s default `"1"`, keeps 0 or 1 and makes anything else 1,
and only the DAC screen's switch writes it (`!flag`, then `switch_charge_enable(flag)`; the code at
`0x52d454`, inside `airplay_page_init`'s range). A missing key is therefore On, but the
`/release/assets/default/raw/config.ini` that `config_init` copies to `/mnt/data` when there is none
(first boot, a reset) holds `USBDAC_CHARGE=0` in V1.32, V1.34 and V1.36, so a Q2 nobody asked reads
Off, the same line the switch writes for a chosen Off. `ringnav_usb_config` (`dac_default`) settles
it after stock's read: until `Q2POD DACCHARGEOWN` is 1 it sets the flag and the key to 1 and writes
`DACCHARGEOWN=1`; from then on the key is the user's, so a saved Off is kept, and a reset (a new
`config.ini` without the mark) starts On again. ponytail: an Off chosen under 1.8.1 or earlier is
turned On once at the update, as nothing on the Q2 tells it from the factory line; the changelog
says to turn it Off again. A per-device record of the switch would have had to exist before the
update to do better.

**System settings → Power → USB DAC Charging** (`usb_charge_row`, from `ringnav_powermanager` after
Charge Limit, stock's `usb_chargeswitch` icon) is that same flag and key, usable with no cable in.
A toggle flips `g_usbdac_chargeflag`, writes `PLAYSET USBDAC_CHARGE` and calls
`ringnav_usb_charge(!st.charge_held)`: it asks for charging as `charge_poll` hands it back outside
the USB and AirPlay pages (on, unless Charge Limit holds it off), so the policy above applies the
new choice to PE22 at once, an earlier Off request from the DAC screen's switch is replaced, and
Charge Limit's hold still wins. Off only matters with Audio and DAC: USB Storage with a cable in
keeps charging. The DAC screen's switch reads the flag when it builds, and the row reads it again
on the Power window's `EVT_WINDOW_FOREGROUND`, so a change on either shows on the other.

`switch_charge_enable` is guarded (`charge_apply` calls `toolsGpioSetValue` itself). Stock's direct `toolsGpioSetValue("PE22", ...)` writes (`into_poweroff`,
`device_reboot`, `device_standby`, `check_otg_status`) and other GPIOs pass through, so power-off, reboot
and Standby still release the pin for a charge with the Q2 off; the next `ringnav_usb_status` poll
inhibits again. `S90play`'s `rockbox()` sets PE22 low before Rockbox starts, which never drives it. A mutex serializes
the policy and GPIO writes. A caller's disable request remains disabled through detection and
mode reconciliation, so the existing charge-limit hold is not undone by these paths. Detection
rechecks PE22 and corrects a mismatched readback. `ringnav_usb_status` reconciles immediately before
stock gadget dispatch, covering a storage-to-DAC transition without waiting for the next poll.
The stock USB audio descriptors, radio behavior and kernel remain unchanged.

Stock's `systembar_showface` picks `bar_charge` from the cable flag alone while the charger is not Full (and the plain icon once a DAC link is up with charging off, or at Full), so a cable held off by this guard or by Charge Limit showed as charging. `usb_charge_held` is 1 while the last PE22 write was the inhibit; `bar_charging` (navigation.c), which the status bar's battery and the dark bar's key read, is `bar_charge` and not held, and a held cable under 15% shows low. ponytail: the pin's state, not the charger's: a cable too weak to charge still shows charging; `/sys/class/power_supply/battery/status` would tell, but `get_battery_capacity` keeps only 0 to 2 in `g_power_chargestate`, so a Discharging read leaves the last value there.

The four hooks use the pinned V1.36 build's symbol/address and PIC-prologue/GOT checks. Source
changes are exercised by `test/fw/test_usb_charge.py`.

### OTG host power

Stock's `check_otg_status` (`0x4f3408`), called once a second from `on_wm_idle_status` (its only caller, `0x4f43dc`), reads the ID pin `PD18` with `toolsGpioGetValue`; when its role `PD18 == 0` differs from `g_last_otgid` it writes `PC20` (bus power, 1 on) and `PE22` (charger, 1 off) to that role and stores it, then on a host pass follows a USB DAC through `/tmp/usb_add` and `/dev/snd/pcmC1D0` (`g_otg_status`). Nothing else in demo writes `PC20` high: `into_poweroff`, `device_reboot` and `device_standby` write it 0 with `g_last_otgid`. `get_battery_capacity` reads no cable (`g_usbdet_value` 0) while `g_last_otgid` is 1, and the dwc2 controller follows the same pin (`13500000.otg/id_status`). The cable sense `PD17` (`usb_detect`: 0 is VBUS on the port) reads the Q2's own bus power as well as a computer's.

A pin log on the Q2 (2026-11-17, build p32b, every 0.5 s) showed the fault: after each unplug `PD18` read 0 with no cable in, stock turned `PC20` on in the next pass (within 0.53 s every time), and `PD18` stayed low for 5 to 19 s. A cable put into a computer in that window met the Q2 powering the bus: `PC20=1` with VBUS on, the battery Discharging, nothing enumerated, until `PD18` read high (dwc2: "Do port resume before switching to device mode") and stock turned `PC20` off in its next pass. Plugs that worked were those made after `PD18` was back to 1.

**The ID pin floats.** The port D registers (read on the Q2, 2026-11-17; offsets from the X2000 GPIO map: `INT` 0x10, `MSK` 0x20, `PAT1` 0x30, `PAT0` 0x40, `EDG` 0x70, `PEPU` 0x80 pull-up, `PEPD` 0x90 pull-down) have `PD18` as a GPIO input with neither pull (`PEPU` `0xC7F83F3F`, bit 18 clear; `PEPD` 0). `PD17`'s bits read as `usb_event.c`'s both-edge request asks (`INT` 1, `EDG` 1), which places 0x70 as `EDG` and the map as the X2000's. The kernel's built-in device tree lists `PD16` to `PD19` under `gpd`'s `ingenic,gpio-sleep-pullup`, a pull-up during Standby only; nothing pulls `PD18` up awake, and `cmd_gpio get_func PD18` read `input pull_hiz`. `S12usbcharge` (`patch/usb_charge.sh`) runs `cmd_gpio set_func PD18 input pull_up` at boot (`soc_gpio.ko` offers `pull_up`, `pull_down`, `pull_hiz`); `cmd_gpio get_func PD18` then reads `input pull_up` and `PEPU` `0xC7FC3F3F`. That did not last: demo's `platform_init` (`0x51cd94`, from `application_init`) sets the USB pins up after `config_init` with `toolsGpioInput(name, pull)` (`0x5d1cdc`: `gpio_set_func` with `input` and `pull_down` for 1, `pull_up` for 2, `pull_hiz` otherwise), and gives `PD18` 0, so a build with only the S12 line read `input pull_hiz` 34 s after boot (2026-11-17 22:36). `ID_PULL_UP` (`tools/build.py`) turns that call's `move $a1, $zero` (`0x51d33c`) into `li $a1, 2`, so stock's own call sets `input pull_up`; `test/build.py` checks the word in the built demo. A Standby and wake kept it, and `usb_record_wake` sets it again at every wake (from `ringnav_standby`, as `toolsIntoStandby` returns) all the same. With it on, 4 of 5 quick replugs into a computer enumerated at once with `PD18` high throughout, about half before.

**The line is still driven low.** With both pull-ups on and nothing attached, `PD18` goes low once, starting 2.15 to 7.02 s after VBUS leaves the port, the Q2's own bus power ending included: for 2.15 s the two times nothing cut it short, and for 3.21 and 4.28 s before stock's bus power came on and held it low (`q2-pull-state.log` 21:0x, `PU18=1` on every line, every 0.54 s: four lows in all). With the pin floating (builds before `ID_PULL_UP`) the lows began 1.1 to 12.1 s after and lasted up to 17 s with the bus power on them (`q2-ab-state.log` 22:43, every 0.25 s, build 8fd0ddcd); those are what a floating pin did and set none of the times below. There is no free-running cycle, so something on the board crosses a threshold as the VBUS net discharges. The Q2's port is USB-C with no ID contact, the role logic is not identified (no Type-C controller is on any I2C bus: only the CW2015, two Hynitron touch parts, the CS43131 and the AXP2101), and nothing in demo, the device tree or the init scripts touches a role or mode pin: demo's GPIO names in port D are `PD17`, `PD18`, `PD20` and `PD22` to `PD26`, and the kernel's dwc2 has `usb_role_switch` code but the device tree gives no `usb-role-switch`, and its `connected`, `dwc2_mode` and `id_status` attributes are read-only (mode 0444, no store). A USB-C laptop will not attach as a source onto a live VBUS, so a cable put in while the Q2 powered the bus enumerated nothing; and on 22:43, the pin floating, a 6 s settle alone made a loop into an empty port: the pulse let stock power the bus, the bus power's end was another VBUS removal, and the next pulse 7 s on powered it again.

`ringnav_otg_status` (`patch/usb_otg.c`) hooks `check_otg_status`. In device role (`g_last_otgid` not 1) a high ID runs stock's pass as before (its device path ends a DAC's output). A low ID read within `OTG_BLANK_MS` (10 s, over the latest start logged with the pull-up on, 7.02 s) of VBUS leaving the port (`PD17` going high, or the bus power ending) is ignored until it reads high again, or until it has stayed low for `OTG_ACCESSORY_MS` (8 s), longer than every low logged with the pull-up on and nothing attached (2.15 s uncut, 4.28 s with stock's bus power on it), when it is an accessory's and stock's pass gets it at once; any other low runs stock's pass only once `PD18` has read 0 and `PD17` 1 on every pass for `OTG_SETTLE_MS` (3 s). Every low logged with the pull-up on and nothing attached began 2.15 to 7.02 s after VBUS left, inside the blank; the second low of `q2-pull-state.log` began 5.37 s after the Q2's own bus power ended, which the blank catches too, but a replay with that power held off (as the blank holds it) puts it 16.7 s after the cable out, so the settle is kept longer than the longest uncut low, 2.15 s: on stock's once-a-second pass such a low spans at most three reads 2 s apart, short of 3 s. (Before 2026-11-25 it was 6 s; the floating pin's 17 s low of 22:43, before `ID_PULL_UP`, passed either.) VBUS on the port, a high ID, or passes more than `OTG_GAP_MS` (5 s) apart (a Standby) start the wait again. The bus power is a trial: with nothing on the host port (`/sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1`) `OTG_TRIAL_MS` (8 s) after it came on, `ringnav_otg_status` writes `PC20` and `PE22` 0 and `g_last_otgid` 0 as stock's device pass would (the charge guard then sets `PE22` its own way), records `otg-trial-off`, and tries no more until a cable's VBUS is seen with the bus power off or the Q2 wakes from Standby. In host role an ID high alone does not end it: stock's pass, reading the pin, turns `PC20` off once the host port's device has gone with the ID high, or after `OTG_ID_HIGH_MS` (2 s) of ID high with no device on the port; until then `ringnav_gpio_value`, which takes `toolsGpioGetValue` (`0x5d1c3c`), answers 0 for `PD18` inside stock's pass, so that pass is the host one (the DAC's discovery) whatever the pin. The AB13X earbuds' ID read high 0.98 s after their power came on (2026-11-23, 12966.731) while the kernel enumerated them (12966.260), and stock's pass cut the power then. Only `check_otg_status` and `usb_otg.c` read `PD18`, all on the UI thread. While the bus power is on with no USB DAC or drive found yet (`g_otg_status` 0) and within its trial, `usb_otg_poll` runs the pass every UI pass as well as stock's once a second, so the DAC is found in the pass after its PCM appears. The X2000's CPM is also held: `USBPCR` (`0x1000003c`) bit 29, the PHY's ID pull-up always on, and `USBRDT` (`0x10000040`) bits 24 and 23, the controller's ID from its register set to device (`otg_hold`, busybox `devmem` read-modify-writes as tested on the Q2 2026-11-17: `id_status` and `GOTGCTL`'s ConIDSts stayed device through a pulse), at boot after `platform_init`, at every wake (the PHY's init writes `USBPCR` again) and whenever the bus power ends; bits 24 and 23 are cleared just before stock's pass is let through, so a real adapter's device enumerates. A USB DAC or drive on an OTG adapter gets bus power 3 to 4 s after it goes in (the fourth once-a-second pass that reads its ID low; 6 to 7 s with the 6 s settle before 2026-11-25, which with about 2.6 s to enumeration and stock's discovery made about 9 s from plug to the DAC found, about 6 s now), or as long into boot, and about 8 s after it goes in when that is within 10 s of a cable out: on 2026-11-23 USB-C headphones put in 5 s after the laptop's cable came out were held off until they were re-seated (the host port saw them 37 s after the unplug, and Play was refused meanwhile for want of an output), as a low the blank caught then waited for a high. `test/fw/test_usb_otg.py` replays the logged sequences over a model of stock's pass and the pins: the p32b unplug-replugs and the pull-up's four lows (the latest-starting one followed by the low after stock's power ended, then a laptop) never power the bus; the floating pin's 22:43 low gets one trial and no loop, and its 8.56 s floating low one trial that ends at the ID's high; the 22:43 low under the settle alone powers the bus; an accessory put in 5 s after an unplug and left in is powered by `OTG_ACCESSORY_MS` on, within 9 s (red before it: never, then 20 s), a trial with nothing enumerated ends and is not repeated until a cable, the adapter's path keeps its power while a device is on the host port, an ID high while its device enumerates keeps the power (the earbuds' sequence; red before: cut in that pass) until the device goes, and 2 s of ID high with no device ends it; the car1129 earbuds (below) keep the power while on the host port and lose it in the pass after they leave, and keep it a minute with the ID high and the device there; the DAC is found in the UI pass after its PCM is there, and stock's once a second once it is (red before: the next second). `test/build.py` runs `S12usbcharge` with a stand-in `cmd_gpio` and checks `ID_PULL_UP` in the built demo.

A start with nothing else to play to while an accessory is on its way (its ID low and being waited out, or its bus power on for less than `OTG_PLAY_GRANT_MS`, 3 s, with no USB DAC yet) gets "Connecting USB audio..." instead of the no-output message: `ringnav_forbid_play` takes `check_forbid_play_no_headset` (`0x4f2cac`), which every start asks, stock's and the payload's (radio, videos, Up Next, the skips, the queue menu). Only a Play of the song there is kept: stock's Play key (`playpause_quick_click`, whose call returns to `0x4f2fd8`, `OTG_PLAYPAUSE_RET`) and the payload's `player_play_pause` (`headset.c`, through `usb_otg_forbid_resume`); started again later, any other start would be the paused song instead of the station, video, skip or row asked for, so those are refused with the message and not kept. Once there is somewhere to play (`has_valid_output_device`: the DAC, whose way stock's host pass switched with `config_outputchannel` and whose volume it set, or a headset that connected meanwhile) `usb_otg_poll` starts the song again at its place (`player_save_stop`, then `player_save_start(0)`, as `now_source.c` `now_take_back` does), so it opens the DAC's PCM: the player takes a new way only at a song's start (`mcl-setoutputway`), and a paused song resumed would go on into the headphone DAC. If nothing comes (the ID back high before the power, or 3 s of bus power with no output), the Play goes with stock's message. The Q2's own bus power ending is not a cable: stock read its dying VBUS as one 1.6 s after an `otg-off` (2026-11-23, 13404.022 to 13405.770) and the Bluetooth connect a cable in starts went to a headset for it. After the bus power goes off, `PD17` reading VBUS is no cable until it has read none once, or `OTG_OWN_VBUS_MS` (3 s) has passed, so a computer's cable put in before that is seen then: `usb_otg_cable` filters stock's cable read (`ringnav_usb_detect`, `usb_charge.c`, and with it `g_usbdet_value`, the cable in, its gadget and its connect) and every `PD17` read of `ringnav_otg_status`, where the dying VBUS of a trial's end had cleared its refusal and started another trial some 15 s later, again and again with an empty adapter in; `usb_otg_own_vbus`, the same state, keeps the connect off in `usb_ui.c`. **Tested** (`test/fw/test_usb_otg.py`, `test_usb_ui.py`): the Play kept and started on the DAC after `g_otg_status` 2, through the blank's wait and through the settle, or on a headset that connects first; given up with stock's message when the ID goes high, or 3 s into the bus power with no output (red before: at the trial's end); any other start refused with the message and nothing started once the DAC is there (red before: the paused song started); stock's gate otherwise; no Bluetooth connect for a "cable" 1.5 s after the bus power ends, one for a cable 4 s after (red before); stock's cable read 0 through the 1.6 s of dying VBUS read every 100 ms and 1 for a cable 4 s on, and one trial only with the empty adapter left in (both red before: a cable read, and eleven more trials in a minute).

**Each end of the bus power says why.** The record's `otg-off` line carries `why=gone` (the host port's device left: the ID high, or still low past the trial), `why=id-high` (`OTG_ID_HIGH_MS` of ID high with nothing enumerated) or `why=stock` (stock's pass reading `PD18` high between this file's read and its own); a trial with nothing enumerated is `otg-trial-off`. On 2026-11-23 (V1SSi, demo ms; dmesg's uptime is demo + 4.052 s) the AB13X earbuds were powered twice after the laptop's cable came out, enumerated, played (the song resumed from 5 s and 6 s at each end) and were cut at 7.3 and 8.6 s. Both ends were `otg-off`, not `otg-trial-off`, so neither was the trial: the device had left the host port with the bus power still on, and S2 ended the host role in the next pass. Grant 1: `PD18=0 hostdev=1` at 1144709, `PD18=1 hostdev=0 PC20=1` at 1144976, `otg-off` at 1146118. Grant 2: dmesg's `usb 1-1: USB disconnect` at 1193.270 (demo 1189218) with `PC20` on, `otg-off` at 1190116, and the port read empty (`PD17` 1) for the 148 s after; demo had sent the player `mcl-pause` 0.46 s before the disconnect, from what is not logged. Why the device left is not in the record: the owner pulling it, the earbuds dropping, or the controller, whose role follows the pad during a grant (`OTG_FROM_PIN`), going to device on an ID high, would each read so, and grant 1's ID high and the device's leaving fell in one 250 ms line. Grant 2's trace had stopped at its trial's end with the ID low; the trace now covers the whole grant ([USB record](#usb-record)), so the next one orders the ID's high against the kernel's disconnect. The seats that came up with the ID low read `PD18=0 PD17=1` until the power (2 of 6 that night, 1 of 3 in `pd18-owner2.log`); the rest read `PD18=1 PD17=0` with `usb/online` 0 and the dwc2 gadget logging `new device is full-speed` (a bus reset, so the earbuds drove the bus as a host: two dual-role ports resolving the Q2 as the sink, an inference), and stayed so until re-seated (38.5 s and 34 s in `pd18-owner2.log`), so the `no-source` toast at 2 s is kept: waiting longer brought nothing. Which way a seat resolves is not in any log. `test/fw/test_usb_otg.py` replays the night (four toasts, two grants, each off in the pass after its device left, with `why=gone`; red before: no `why`).

**A computer the wrong way round.** On 2026-11-23 (`pd18-owner2.log`, a read-only sampler every 0.25 s on V1PXi) the laptop's cable, put back in at 17777.35, brought `PD18` low and no VBUS: the two ports had resolved the Q2 as the source and the laptop as the sink, as two dual-role USB-C ports can, and it stayed so for the 56 s the cable was in; a replug configured in 0.5 s. With the pull-up on, three unplugs of 24.5 to 34 s brought no low at all. That suggests a part on the board that drives the ID line from the CC pins (an inference: no such part is identified). The settle powered the bus, the trial found nothing on the host port and ended it, and the ID stayed low. Now, `OTG_WRONG_MS` (3 s) after a trial's end with the ID still low and no VBUS, `ringnav_otg_status` records `wrong-role` and shows "Unplug the cable and plug it in again" once (`OTG_REPLUG`, a payload string, as "Connecting USB audio..." is), until the ID reads high or VBUS comes; nothing else changes, and no recovery is tried. An empty OTG adapter left in shows it too. `test/fw/test_usb_otg.py` replays the owner's round 3 (one toast, red before: none) and rounds 1 and 2 (nothing).

**An accessory read as a cable.** The same night the AB13X earbuds, put in twice (18191.59 and 18231.97, each orientation), held `PD17` low with `PC20` off and no source anywhere, `PD18` high throughout; stock read a cable (charging shown, a gadget started, `udc=default` and five gadget-side "new device is full-speed" lines in 55 ms), and the earbuds never got power. `/sys/class/power_supply/usb/online`, the PMIC's USB supply and the record's `vbus=`, tells them apart: in the two records (about 640 lines) it read 1 on every line with a computer's or a charger's VBUS, already in the pass of the cable's edge, and 0 only for the Q2's own power dying away and for three such insertions (these two and one on an earlier boot). `usb_otg_cable` therefore reads `PD17` low with `online` 0 as no cable, at every read (stock's `usb_detect`, so no charging, gadget, iPhone or Bluetooth connect, and the OTG pass), and as a cable the moment `online` reads 1; `OTG_NO_SOURCE_MS` (2 s) into it the record says `no-source` and the same one toast asks for a replug, since a re-seat brought the ID low that night. With no such file `PD17` is read as it is. The bus power is not tried for it: with `PD18` high the grant hands the controller's role to the pad (`OTG_FROM_PIN`) and it would stay a device; forcing host by `USBRDT` is the device session's E2. `test/fw/test_usb_otg.py` replays 18191.59 to 18230.12 (no cable at any read, one toast; red before: a cable), a computer's cable at its first read, and no file.

**The DAC's restart.** When stock's host pass finds the DAC (`/tmp/usb_add` and `/dev/snd/pcmC1D0p`, `g_otg_status` 2) it stops the song with its place (`player_save_stop`), switches the way (`config_outputchannel`), sets the volume and starts the song again there (`player_save_start(1)`, paused if it was), all on the UI thread; the DAC's removal does the same back to the jack. Stock's `player_save_stop` (`0x52069c`) is `mclSetMute(1)`, `usleep(100000)`, `mclStop`, which waits for the player's `{player-stopstatus\exit}` (polled every 1.5 ms, up to 1001 times), and `usleep(300000)`. q2player sends that answer only once it has closed the PCM (`player/engine.c`), so the 300 ms after it held the UI and nothing else: on 2026-11-25 (V205i) the pass that found USB-C headphones took 434 ms (`ui pass 434 ms ... longest usb_ui_poll 432 ms`), 101 ms from the pass's start to q2player's `mcl-stop` and 319 ms from it to `set-songurl`, and an earlier one 869 ms, 656 ms of it between the two (300 ms of sleep and 356 ms that the log does not divide between q2player's stop of a PCM paused on the jack and stock's `config_outputchannel` and `device_set_volume`). Inside the pass (`otg_stock` sets `in_pass` around stock's call) the build sends that `usleep` (`0x52077c`, `OTG_STOP_SLEEP_CALL`) to `otg_stop_sleep`, which returns at once; every other caller of `player_save_stop` (a station, a video, a game, Guest Play) keeps the 300 ms, as a q2video or a game opening bluealsa's PCM right after a stop needs bluealsa to have seen the close. The mute's 100 ms stays. **Tested** (`test/playback.py`, stock's own `player_save_stop` run from `ringnav_otg_status`: the mute and the 100 ms only, red before with the 300 ms; called directly, all three; `test/fw/test_usb_otg.py`: no sleep inside the pass, the 300 ms outside it).

ponytail: an OTG adapter put in within 10 s of unplugging a cable waits 8 s for its power, a margin over four lows logged with the pull-up on, not a measured bound on the board's pulse (a device run with nothing attached, the blank holding the power off, gives the pulse's whole length); an adapter whose device does not enumerate within 8 s (or an empty one) loses its power until a cable is plugged in or the Q2 sleeps and wakes; a DAC unplugged from the adapter past the trial ends the power as an empty trial's end does, and the adapter left in loses it until a cable or a wake; and a power-only accessory on an adapter never enumerates, so it gets 8 s of power. An OTG power option (Auto, Always) would lift the last. The [USB record](#usb-record) shows each trial's end. The hook uses the pinned V1.36 PIC-prologue/GOT check.

### USB record

`patch/usb_record.c` writes a line to the card's `.q2pod/q2-usb.log` (moved to `q2-usb.1.log` at 128 KB) at each start (`boot`, from `ringnav_platform_init`, `platform_init`'s hook, once stock has set the pins up), for each cable edge (`usb_ui_status`: `in`, `out`), the same 5 s later (`in+5s`, `out+5s`, from `usb_ui_poll`), each change of OTG bus power (`otg-on`, `otg-off` with its `why=`, around stock's pass in `ringnav_otg_status`, and `otg-trial-off`), a computer the wrong way round (`wrong-role`, [OTG host power](#otg-host-power), and an accessory holding the cable sense low with no source (`no-source`), and each Standby (`standby` just before `toolsIntoStandby`, `wake` as it returns and `wake+5s`, all from `ringnav_standby`; the card is unmounted by then, so these wait in the ring): the wall time and demo's millisecond clock, `PD18`, `PD17`, `PD19` (an input with a pull-up beside them that stock never reads, in case it is the role chip's), `PC20`, `PE22`, `g_last_otgid`, the dwc2's `id_status`, `dwc2_mode` and `connected`, `power_supply/usb/online`, the UDC's state and whether a device is on the host port (`/sys/bus/usb/devices/1-1/idVendor`). `boot` and `wake+5s` also run `cmd_gpio get_func PD18` (into `/tmp/q2-pd18.func`) and end with its answer (`pull=input_pull_up`); one that is not the pull-up is set again and the line's word is `boot-pull-off` or `wake+5s-pull-off`. With the card away lines are held in a 4 KB ring (`card_store.c`'s log), and `usb_record_poll` tries to put them on the card every 5 s (`USB_FLUSH_MS`), so the `boot` line is there soon after the card mounts, not only at the next event. `tools/q2usb.py` reads the two files and flags `BACKFEED` (bus power on with VBUS or a computer's answer seen, or a computer within 3 s of it going off), `EMPTY` (bus power with nothing enumerated), `NOENUM` (a plug not enumerated 5 s on: a charger, or a plug that failed) `IDLOW` (the ID low 5 s after an unplug) `PULLOFF` (a `-pull-off` line) and `WAKEDROP` (a link up at `standby` that is not 5 s after the wake, or the controller in host role at the wake).

Each line also goes to the [unified log](#unified-log) as a `usb` line from its event word on (`ulog`), so it sits in time with the rest; the record's own file stays as it is, for `tools/q2usb.py`.

**The pin trace.** While the ID or VBUS is moving, `usb_otg_poll` (every UI pass) adds a short `pins` line (`usb_record_pins`: the wall time and demo's millisecond clock, `PD18`, `PD17`, `PC20`, `PE22`, `g_last_otgid`, whether a device is on the host port and stock's `g_otg_status` as `otgst`, 2 once its host pass has the USB DAC) on a 250 ms beat (`OTG_TRACE_MS`), or one a pass when passes are further apart with the screen off: while `PD18` reads low out of host role, while the bus power is in its trial or kept over an ID high ([OTG host power](#otg-host-power)), and for `OTG_TRACE_AFTER_MS` (30 s) after VBUS leaves the port. A grant past its trial with its device is sampled on the same beat and writes a line only when `PD18` or the host port's device changes, `OTG_TRACE_CHANGES` (40) a grant at most, so a long listen writes nothing and a device's leaving is timed. An episode, until none of that holds and the bus power is off, writes `OTG_TRACE_MAX` (240) lines at most besides, about 17 KB, so an empty adapter left in traces its first minute; with the ID high, no bus power and VBUS gone or steady, nothing is written. These lines are on the card only, not in the unified log, and `tools/q2usb.py` reads past them (they have no `vbus` or `udc`). An unplug's 30 s are about 120 lines (8 KB), so some 15 unplugs fill the 128 KB before the move to `q2-usb.1.log`. `tools/q2usb.py` counts a `pins` line with `hostdev=1` between `otg-on` and its end as a device seen, so a grant whose device came after the `otg-on` line and left before the `otg-off` one is not `EMPTY`. `test/fw/test_usb_otg.py` checks the silence when idle, the 30 s at four a second, the trial's lines and the cap, and a kept grant's line at the beat after an ID high, before the status pass reads it, none while steady, and its bound (red before: no line).

**At a wake.** `device_standby` (`0x5021bc`) writes `PC20` 0, `PE22` and `g_last_otgid` 0, unmounts the card and USB drive, removes the Wi-Fi and card modules, and calls `toolsIntoStandby` (`0x5d1110`: `mem` to `/sys/power/state`), which returns at the wake; the rest of `device_standby` brings them back and never calls `check_otg_status`, which runs again on the next status pass. The bus power therefore comes back only through `ringnav_otg_status`'s wait, and a computer's VBUS on the cable stops that. The controller's role at the wake is the kernel's: on 2026-11-17 21:27 a wake on a laptop logged `dwc2 13500000.otg: Do port resume before switching to device mode` and the link dropped and came back as a new address (the dwc2 had resumed in host role, so the ID read low as it woke), while a wake at 20:45 kept the link. demo cannot hold the dwc2's role: its `dwc2_mode` and `id_status` attributes are read-only and the device tree gives no role switch. The `standby`, `wake` and `wake+5s` lines record the ID, the controller and the link either side, so the next one shows whether the role chip's ID pulse, not demo, causes it.

## Battery History

**System settings → Power → Battery History** (`patch/battery.c`; the row after In-Vehicle Mode, `ringnav_powermanager`). `charge_poll` hands `battery_tick` the level (`g_power_capacity`) and the cable (`g_usbdet_value`) every `CHARGE_POLL_MS`, screen on or off, so no thread or timer of its own. With the cable out, a level below the last row's is a new row (the time from `wall_time` and the level); the first poll after the cable comes out, or after a boot without it, starts a new history with one row. A level more than `BH_REBOUND` (3) over the last row's also starts again: the Q2 charged while powered off, which demo never saw. A level of 0 or over 100 (not read yet) is ignored. Within a history the level only falls, from 100 at most to 1, so `BH_ROWS` (100) rows always hold it: the record is a fixed 808 bytes, the card's `.q2pod/q2-battery`, written whole (temp, fsync, rename) once a row through `card_store.c` ([Where Q2 Muse writes](#where-q2-muse-writes)): with the card away the rows are kept in RAM and written at the next tick it is back, and the flash's `/mnt/data/q2-battery` from earlier releases is read until then, so the flash is never written. At the first tick or page open it is read once; one that is short, of another layout (`BH_MAGIC`), with more rows than it holds, or whose levels don't fall row by row is dropped and the next tick starts again. Standby is a suspend to RAM and `charge_poll` runs only in the UI loop, so a drop during Standby is one row at the wake (stamped then), and the graph steps there. ponytail: a charge of 3% or less while powered off reads as the same history, and a gauge jump of more than 3 points up while unplugged restarts the record; revisit if a lost history is reported.

The page (`battery_page`, `CTX_DYNAMIC`; 33 v3, [oled-design](oled-design.md#battery-history)) is a graph over the whole page: `page_list` with one row only titles the status row (the list stays hidden) and a view below it is the graph's, which `battery_paint`, from `ringnav_paint`, fills: the reading the wheel is on (`bh_readout`: `Nov 16, 3:10 PM · 51%`, the status bar's 12- or 24-hour form), faint lines at 100 and 50% and the axis at 0% labelled in 15 px Text Tertiary, the level as steps from the start to now in the accent's light tone over a faint fill, through `ui_ink`, so it follows the theme and Light Mode, the reading's hairline and dot, and **Share Log**, the shared gray `ui_button`. The x axis is time up to now; if the times don't run forward on one clock (set or lost mid-history, `CLOCK_SET`) the rows are spaced evenly instead, and a now on the other side of `CLOCK_SET` from the rows ends the axis at the last row. A time before `CLOCK_SET` (September 2020, scrobbling's test) is a clock never set: such a reading reads as hours and minutes since the start, `+1:15 · 97%`. The wheel moves along the readings (`battery_key`, from `ringnav` before the lists: clockwise to the newer, held at either end), and the newest stays the reading as rows join unless the wheel left it on an older one; Center and a tap on the button share the log, so the button is the page's only action and never wears the focus ring. **Share Log** writes the rows to `/tmp/battery-log.txt` (`battery_log_write`), each day's date (`11 Nov 2026`) over its rows as `99% | 12:00`, or a `Clock not set` line first, whole through `blob_io`'s temp and rename, then opens [LocalSend](#localsend)'s share sheet with it; a log that could not be written is a toast. The toasts show in the button's place, so the button gives way while another window is on top. While the page is open each new row repaints it (`widget_invalidate_force`); nothing is built again.

<a id="usb-pages"></a>
## USB pages

What a cable into a computer shows (`patch/usb_ui.c`, the look in [oled-design](oled-design.md#usb)). Stock starts a gadget the moment a cable is in (`check_usb_status`, hooked as `ringnav_usb_status` in `usb_charge.c`, which calls `usb_ui_status` around it) and, once a computer configures it, opens `usbmode_page` in the mode Quick Settings' USB tile last chose. A cable in on **Automatic** (`USBPICK` 0, the setting's default) keeps stock out (`g_usblink_status` 3, which stock's next pass leaves alone until the cable is out) and shows the host an iPhone (`usb_car.c`, `q2car`, `q2-iap`): a car keeps it (Car Audio), any other host gets Transfer Files for the cable (`usb_car_storage`) once the iPhone is gone, a charger only charges; the whole of it is [iPhone mode: Car Audio in the image](iphone-mode.md#car-audio-in-the-image). USB Debugging is reached only by picking it. A cable in on **Ask Every Time** (`USBPICK` 5) keeps stock out the same way and starts stock's storage gadget with no card in it, only to learn whether a computer answers: one that configures it within `USB_PROBE_MS` (3 s) gets the chooser, "Use USB For" (Charge Only, Transfer Files, USB Audio and, in a `--dev` build, USB Debugging) and Always Do This; nothing answering is a charger (`usb_charger_in`, [Charging](#charging)'s toast). Transfer Files and USB Audio hand back to stock (`g_usbmode` for this cable, `g_usblink_status` 0), whose `usbmode_page` is drawn as a mode page: a solid circle and its glyph, a title, a line and Stop, the gray button ringed under the focus rule (Center, as Return, leaves the mode). Charge Only stops the probe; USB Debugging stops it too, which in a `--dev` build hands the controller back to the ADB gadget ([adb](adb.md)), and opens its own mode page, whose Stop parks that gadget. In a `--dev` build with the ADB gadget already on the controller, that gadget is the probe and nothing is stopped. When the cable is seen, and the probe's gadget's stop at a cable out, are in [USB cable events](#usb-cable-events). A remembered choice (`Q2POD USBPICK`, saved by Always Do This) skips the chooser, Transfer Files and USB Audio in their own mode for the cable, and holds until a mode page's Stop (Center) forgets it (`usb_forget`, back to Automatic; Automatic and Ask Every Time stay as they are); Return only leaves. The saved mode (`USBPICKMODE` in older builds) no longer drops it. **The USB picker** (`usb_pick_open`, `usbpick_page`, CHOICE in `contexts.inc`) is opened by Settings > General's USB row (`usb_ui_row` from `ringnav_systemset`, its value `usb_ui_value`, written again on every change while the row is there) and by Control Center's USB row while a cable is in (`usb_ui_cable`, `g_usbdet_value` 1): Automatic, Transfer Files, USB Audio, Charge Only, Ask Every Time and, in a `--dev` build, USB Debugging, the remembered choice carrying stock's `select` image (the theme's check) and its note painted in a footer view under the rows (`usb_pick_paint`). A pick is remembered through the one path the chooser's Always Do This takes (`usb_remember`, which `usb_apply` calls: `USBPICK`, and for Transfer Files and USB Audio stock's `SYSSET USBMODE`); Automatic and Ask Every Time are saved for the next cable and change nothing on this one. With no cable in nothing else changes, so a link stock's mode-exit prompt still holds is left alone. With a cable in the cable takes the pick at once (`usb_switch`): what it had is let go first, stock's mode by force-closing `usbmode_page`, whose `EVT_WINDOW_CLOSE` runs stock's `usbmode_exit` (bound by `usbmode_page_init` through `0x542ad0`; it stops the gadget, mounts the card again and sets `g_usblink_status` 3 itself, `0x542918`; `window_manager_close_window_force` reaches the default window manager's forced close, vtable `0x9b42b0` + `0x30` = `0x69c460`, which dispatches that event at `0x69c558`), Automatic's iPhone by `q2car stop` in the background after the player's release of the car's PCM (`usb_car_stop`; the pick is remembered at once and made by the first UI pass after the stop has returned, `usb_car_busy`, [iphone-mode](iphone-mode.md#the-stream-s-life)), a stock gadget still waiting for a computer by holding the link and stopping its script, USB Debugging's page by closing it and parking its gadget for Charge Only; then `usb_apply`, and USB Debugging runs `q2adb-gadget unpark`, as a stop of stock's gadget may have left it parked. `usbmode_page` gone by any path leaves the cable charging only (`usb_mode_gone`: `u.choice` Charge Only). Leaving Transfer Files while its page is up and the computer has not ejected the card asks first on the confirmation card (`usb_pick_answer`), so a copy in progress is not cut off unasked. Toasts: Unplugged, OK to Disconnect (the computer's eject while the mode page is not on top, `usb_ui_ejected` from `usb_poll`) and USB Audio Ready. In a `--dev` build adbd's question about an unknown computer ([adb](adb.md#authorization)) comes in on its socket here (`auth_poll`) and is asked on `adb_trust.c`'s card, "Allow this computer?" (`adb_prompt_open`), whose answer goes back through `usb_ui_auth_answer`.

<a id="usb-cable-events"></a>
## USB cable events

A plug-in or unplug is acted on in the UI pass after it happens (`patch/usb_event.c`), not stock's next second or two. Stock reads the cable from GPIO `PD17` (low while VBUS is in) in `usb_detect` (`0x4ff220`), called only from `get_battery_capacity` (`0x4ff258`), which only `systembar_showface` calls, on the status bar's 1000 ms timer (`systembar_timer_start`, `0x541f2c`); `on_wm_idle_status` then runs `check_usb_status` only on a pass where `toolsstimer` (`time(NULL)`) has moved to a new second. Up to two seconds passed between the cable and anything reacting, and a cable out and back in within that time was never seen at all. `usb_event_start`, from the first `usb_ui_poll`, asks the kernel's GPIO character device for both edges of line 17 of `/dev/gpiochip3` (GPD, base 96; `GPIO_GET_LINEEVENT_IOCTL`; PD17 is a plain input that no driver holds, its interrupt bit clear in GPD's `INT` register) and starts a thread that blocks on the line's file. Each edge is read with the kernel's timestamp (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), the contacts' bounce slept off (`USB_SETTLE_MS`, 20 ms), the burst's other edges drained, and a count bumped (`usb_event_wait`). `usb_ui_poll`, every UI pass (`ringnav_sleep`), takes a new count (`usb_event_take`) and runs stock's own read, `get_battery_capacity` (which sets `g_usbdet_value` and resets the power-off timers as its timer would), then `ringnav_usb_status`, so `usb_ui_status` and stock's `check_usb_status` see the cable in that pass. The read stays stock's (`/dev/gpio` through `toolsGpioGetValue`), so the event only decides when; stock's timer and second-gated check stay as the fallback, alone if the line cannot be requested. demo's log gets a line per change: `q2 usb: cable in, seen after its edge, N ms` (or `out`), `(stock's once-a-second read)` when the timer saw it first (a cable in, either way, also pages the saved Bluetooth device once: [Bluetooth on USB power](#bluetooth-on-usb-power)), then `a computer answered the probe after the plug, N ms` or `no computer answered: a charger`. While the probe waits, `usb_ui_poll` reads the UDC's state every `USB_PROBE_LOOK_MS` (100 ms), so the chooser follows the computer's answer, not stock's next second. A cable out stops the probe's storage gadget whether it still waited or its chooser was up unanswered (`usb_probe_stop`, `probe_up`): left running, it kept configfs mounted and the ADB gadget parked, and the next cable's `storage_config.sh start` failed ("usb configfs already mounted"), seen on a Q2 on 2026-11-16 as replugs the Q2 did not react to. In a `--dev` build the ADB gadget, when it is on the controller (`/sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget/q2adb/UDC` set), is itself the probe: a computer sees one device at the plug, and USB Debugging or Charge Only keep it; Transfer Files and USB Audio swap in stock's gadget as before ([adb](adb.md#the-usb-gadget)). Each burst also ends the UI loop's idle (`loop_wake`, [The UI loop's wait](#the-ui-loops-wait)), so a plug-in is seen on the pass it starts, dark or lit. In a `--dev` build each edge read is also sent on to the [USB tracer](#usb-tracer). `test/fw/test_usb_ui.py` covers the burst, the pass that acts on it, the probe's look and the unplug's stop.

`PD17` also reads low while the Q2 itself powers the bus as an OTG host (`PC20` high) and for a second or two after, as that power dies away, so an edge then is the Q2's own power, not a cable ([OTG host power](#otg-host-power) reads it as none). After an unplug the ID pin `PD18` can read low for seconds; [OTG host power](#otg-host-power) keeps the bus power off until it has settled low with `PD17` high and ignores a low read within 10 s of VBUS leaving, so a cable put back into a computer in that time is a device's, not met by the Q2's 5 V.

## USB tracer

A `--dev` build runs `q2-usbtrace` (`patch/q2usbtrace.c`, its logic in `patch/q2usbtrace_core.c`, `patch/q2usbtrace.h`), a read-only recorder of the USB port, and feeds what it sees to the [USB shadow](#usb-shadow). `S90play` starts it after the ADB gadget (`USBTRACE_HOOK` in `tools/build.py`) and starts it again 5 s after it ends with an error, three times a boot at most; it runs at `nice` 19. It stops for good, with its lines written out, when `/mnt/data/q2-usbtrace.off` or the card's `.q2muse/usbtrace.off` exists (checked each second; `adb shell touch /mnt/data/q2-usbtrace.off`, or a file of that name made on the card from a computer); removing the file brings it back at the next boot. A release build has no binary, no start line and no forwarding in demo: `test/build.py` checks all three.

**What it reads.** Everything is a read, and none of it can change the port, the charger or the audio:

- `PD18` and `PD19` (gpiochip3 lines 18 and 19, unclaimed) as kernel line events, both edges, input only, with the kernel's `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` time. The request sets the pins' interrupt registers as `usb_event.c`'s does for `PD17`, and leaves their pulls alone; stock reads `PD17` through `/dev/gpio` the same way while demo holds it. demo's `cmd_gpio set_func PD18 input pull_up` at boot and at each wake ([USB record](#usb-record)) sets the pin up again through `soc_gpio`, which the kernel's request does not see: each second the tracer reads `PD18`'s and `PD19`'s bits in GPD's `INT` register and asks for a line again when its bit is clear (a `note` line).
- `PD17` is demo's (`usb_event.c` holds it as `q2-usb-cable`; taking it first would leave demo on stock's once-a-second poll). In a `--dev` build `usb_event_wait` sends each edge it reads, as the kernel gave it, to the abstract datagram socket `q2-usbtrace-pd17`, where the tracer listens (`e PD17 0 fwd`); a send nobody hears fails at once with no signal. Its level is also in every sample.
- `PD14`, `PD15` and `PD16` from the GPIO `PIN` register only, in each sample: unclaimed, `PD16` read 0 with a source attached (the second USB study's candidate for the CC chip's "attached as sink"); a line request would make each a GPIO input, and what the board does with them is not known.
- `PC20` and `PE22` from their `PIN` registers (outputs: the level demo drives), and `USBPCR` (`0x1000003c`) and `USBRDT` (`0x10000040`): `/dev/mem` opened `O_RDONLY` and mapped `PROT_READ`, one page of the CPM and one of the GPIO block.
- The kernel's uevents (`NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT`, beside `mdev`): a `usb_device`'s add and remove (`1-1`, and behind a hub `1-1.1`), card 1's `sound` nodes (`card1`, `pcmC1D0p`), `block`, `power_supply`, `udc`, `extcon`, `typec` and `usb_role`.
- The UDC's `state` by `poll(POLLPRI)` (`sysfs_notify` in the UDC core).
- At each edge, 50 ms and 250 ms after it, and in each sample: `power_supply/usb/online`. At each edge and 50 ms after, and 4 times a second while sampling fast: the AXP2101's `00h` (bit 5 VBUS good) and IRQ status `48h` to `4Ah` (`49h` bits 7 and 6 are VBUS insert and remove, latched with the IRQ off), by SMBus byte reads on `/dev/i2c-6` (`I2C_SLAVE_FORCE` 0x34, as `q2guard` reads the PMIC); its IRQ enables `40h` to `42h` at the start and at edges. A status bit clears only when 1 is written to it, which this never does. And the dwc2's `GOTGCTL`, `GINTSTS` and `HPRT0` from debugfs `regdump`; debugfs is not mounted at boot, so the tracer mounts it at `/sys/kernel/debug`.
- In each sample: the dwc2's `id_status`, `dwc2_mode` and `connected`, whether a device is on the host port (`1-1/idVendor`) and whether `/proc/asound/cards` has a card 1.

**When.** One `poll()` waits on all of it. A sample is taken each second, and every 50 ms for 30 s after any edge, any of those uevents, a UDC change or a sample that moved (`UT_BURST_FOR_MS`). Nothing else wakes it.

**What it writes.** One line per event, `UPTIME KIND ...`, the uptime the kernel's `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` in seconds with six decimals (the [unified log](#unified-log)'s uptime, in ms there), to the card's `.q2muse/logs/q2-usbtrace.0`, moved to `.1` once a write finds it at 256 KB (`UT_FILE_MAX`): about 512 KB in all. Lines wait in a 64 KB RAM ring (`card_store.c`'s log, oldest lines dropped and counted while the card is away) and go to the card every 60 s or every 16 KB, from a child process, so a card that hangs never stops the recording; never while the card is lent to a computer or being let go of (as `q2guard`). The kinds:

| Kind | Says |
| ---- | ---- |
| `start` | how each source came up: `pd17=forwarded`, `pd18=edges` or `sampled` (a line it could not get), `mem=`, `i2c=`, `regdump=`, `uevent=`, `udc=`, and the wall time |
| `e PIN LEVEL` | an edge at the kernel's time; `fwd` for `PD17`'s from demo |
| `on N` | an `online` read made for an edge |
| `s K=V ...` | a sample's changes (the first after a start or a wake whole): the pins, `on`, `id`, `mode`, `conn`, `dev`, `snd`, `pcr`, `rdt` |
| `axp RR=VV ...`, `otg ...` | the PMIC's registers and the regdump's words, when they change |
| `u ACTION SUBSYSTEM NAME` | a uevent |
| `udc STATE` | the UDC's state |
| `stock otg-on`, `stock otg-off` | `PC20` changed: stock's (or the payload's) bus power |
| `shadow: ...` | the [USB shadow](#usb-shadow)'s decisions and state changes |
| `unsafe: ...` | bus power on while `online` reads 1 |
| `cycle n=N at=T type=... stock=... shadow=... agree` | a plug cycle's summary (below) |
| `wake slept=S`, `clock wall=W`, `note ...`, `stop ...` | a Standby (`CLOCK_BOOTTIME` past `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), the wall time every 10 minutes, a line asked for again, the end |

A plug cycle runs from the first movement after quiet to 30 s with none. Its `cycle` line gives the type (`dac`, `accessory`, `computer`, `charger`, `no-source`, `id-low`, `id-low-powered`, `unplug`, `other`), the state the shadow began it in, the time from its start to each milestone (VBUS in and out, the ID low and high, `online` 1, the address and configuration, the host port's device in and out, the PCM, stock's bus power on and off, the shadow's grant and replug), stock's decision and the shadow's (`grant` or `none`), and `agree` or `DISAGREE`, `UNSAFE`. The same in one line goes to the unified log, source `usbtrace` (`I`, or `W` for a disagreement or bus power with `online` 1), written whole to demo's `--dev` console file `/tmp/q2-demo.log`, which `q2guard` passes in as it is. [Building: USB trace report](building.md#usb-trace-report) reads a pulled trace back.

**What it costs.** Idle, one wakeup a second: five small sysfs and `/proc` reads (`online` among them, which the PMIC's driver answers over its bit-banged I2C), three `access()` calls (the host port and the two flags) and four register loads; nothing written but the clock line every ten minutes (466 bytes in a simulated idle ten minutes). After an edge, 20 samples a second for 30 s, the four PMIC status registers 4 times a second (about 0.3 ms of I2C each, the second study's estimate) and the regdump 4 times a second. Counted by `test/unit/test_q2usbtrace.py` over a simulated Q2, not measured on one.

**Tested** (`test/unit/test_q2usbtrace.py`, the device's calls answered by `test/unit/q2usbtrace_host.c`): every device file opened read-only, `/dev/mem` `O_SYNC` read-only and two pages mapped, line requests only for lines 18 and 19 and only input with both edges, PMIC calls only SMBus byte reads of the seven registers, nothing appended but demo's log (red with a line handle's output flag or `/dev/mem` opened read-write); the device's own calls hold only a `PROT_READ` mapping and one `write()`, to demo's log without `O_CREAT`; a DAC's cycle, a disagreement, bus power with `online` 1, the idle cost, a burst's rate, the move to `.1`, the card away, the flag, a line held elsewhere, an interrupt bit cleared, a Standby and the debugfs mount. `test/fw/test_usb_ui.py` checks demo's forwarding (`--dev` only).

ponytail: `PD14` to `PD16` are sampled, not edge-timed; edges on them want a measurement of what drives them first. The `PD18` and `PD19` requests' interrupt setup lives through a Standby only because the GPIO driver's sleep setting for those pins (`ingenic,gpio-sleep-pullup` in the device tree) puts them back to inputs during the suspend, so they wake nothing (an inference: not measured); the first Standby's `wake` line and a read of `/proc/interrupts` over adb after it settle it.

## USB shadow

`patch/usb_fsm.c` (`patch/usb_fsm.h`) is the USB study's state machine as one pure function, `usb_fsm_step(state, event, t_ns) -> actions`, with no I/O. [The tracer](#usb-tracer) feeds it every level change once whatever gave it (an edge, a uevent or a sample: `fed[]` in `q2usbtrace_core.c`), every `online` read, the UDC's address, the host port's device and the DAC's PCM, the bus power seen on `PC20` and each wake, and logs each action it gives as `shadow: would ACTION at T; STATE; RULE`. It changes nothing: in shadow (`shadow` set) a grant only says the Q2 would power the bus then, and its trial is timed from stock's bus power once that is seen. Stock's bus power going on while the shadow had not granted within 15 s (`UT_AGREE_MS`) is `shadow: disagree stock=otg-on at T shadow=none (STATE)` at once; a cycle whose sides differ in granting at all ends with `shadow: disagree in cycle N`.

**States.** `idle`; `sink-debounce` (PD17 low, the PMIC not yet read 1); `residue` (online 0: nothing real, no charging, one replug at 2 s); `sink` (charging, the gadget offered); `host-present` (a host addressed it); `charger` (none in 3 s; a late host is still taken); `src-candidate` (ID low, no VBUS: waiting out the phantom); `src-trial`; `src-cooldown` (a trial found nothing: replug at 1 s if the ID is still low, one more trial at 2 s); `refused` (until a real source, an ID high or a wake); `host` (a device on the host port: kept whatever the ID reads); `host-end` (the device left: the own VBUS dies away).

**Rules and their constants** (`usb_fsm.h`, starting values):

| Constant | Value | From |
| -------- | ----- | ---- |
| `UF_VBUS_GONE_MS` | 20 ms | PD17 high this long ends a sink session (`usb_event.c`'s bounce) |
| `UF_ONLINE_MS`, `UF_RESIDUE_MS`, `UF_RESIDUE_REPLUG_MS` | 250, 500, 2000 ms | the study; the replug as `OTG_NO_SOURCE_MS` |
| `UF_CHARGER_MS` | 3000 ms | `USB_PROBE_MS` |
| `UF_WINDOW_MS` | 10 s | every phantom logged began 2.15 to 7.02 s after VBUS left (`OTG_BLANK_MS`) |
| `UF_ID_FRESH_MS` | 200 ms | outside the window; tCCDebounce 100 to 200 ms (`PD_T_CC_DEBOUNCE`) |
| `UF_ID_PHANTOM_MS` | 5000 ms | inside it. The study's 3.5 s falls short of a logged low that lasted 4.28 s with nothing attached before stock's power held it (q2-pull-state.log, 2026-11-17) [E] |
| `UF_TRIAL_MS` | 3000 ms | from the bus power to the host port's device. The study's 1.5 s would have cut the AB13X earbuds, whose `1-1` came 2.06 and 1.87 s after `otg-on` (2026-11-23) |
| `UF_WRONG_MS`, `UF_RETRY_MS`, `UF_RETRIES` | 1000, 2000 ms, 1 | the study |
| `UF_VBUS_OFF_MS` | 650 ms | tVBUSOFF (`PD_T_SAFE_0V`); `online` judges PD17 after it |

Never: bus power with `online` other than 0, or onto a PD17 low that is not the bus power's own; `online` 1 on a powered bus turns it off at once. A first read of no VBUS is not a VBUS leaving, and a bus power seen off is a leaving only after it was seen on.

**Replayed** (`test/unit/test_usb_fsm.py`, the traces in `test/fixtures/usb_fsm/`, each built from a device log and saying what is measured and what inferred; `tools/usbtrace_report.py` `fsm_events` turns them into events as the tracer does). Properties over random traces: no grant with `online` 1 or onto a real VBUS; no grant inside a phantom shorter than its rule; one `cable-in` or `cable-out` per bouncing PD17 burst. What the shadow would have done differently from the firmware of the day:

- **2026-11-17 back-feed** (p32b): stock powered each ID low 0.53 s in, 1.07 to 3.18 s after an unplug from a computer; the shadow had not by then.
- **The pull-up phantoms**: none powered by the shadow before stock; the two uncut ones never.
- **2026-11-23 earbuds**: four residue seats each get one replug at 2 s (as stock's `no-source`); both grants come 1.0 and 1.65 s before stock's settle, are kept through enumeration, and end as each device leaves.
- **The wrong-way laptop** (2026-11-23 round 3, and 2026-11-25 04:32): the replug about 8 s before stock's `wrong-role`.
- **2026-11-25 grants and headphones behind a hub**: power 5.8 s (V205i's 6 s settle) and 2.8 s (the trunk's 3 s) before stock's; the second wrong-way laptop's empty trial off 3 s before stock's `why=id-high`.
