- **A slow host after a wake** (2026-11-22): configured 5 s after the wake, so the shadow says "charger" at 3 s first, where stock shows nothing.

## Save Diagnostics

A `--dev` build's Settings > General > About starts with a **Save Diagnostics** row, first so it is in sight as the page opens (`patch/diagnostics.c`, added by `ringnav_about`; `about_rows` in `settings_pages.c` leaves its click alone while the table's other rows get `about_click`, which does nothing). Center or a tap runs one shell command (`diag_script`) that writes `/mnt/mmc/q2-diagnostics.txt` beside itself as `.tmp` and moves it into place, then syncs, so a device problem can be read from the card on a computer with no shell open: the build's version (`Q2POD_VERSION`), `date` and `/proc/uptime`, each `/sys/class/udc/*/state`, each configfs gadget under `/sys/kernel/config/usb_gadget` with its `UDC`, its functions, the functions its configs link and a storage function's LUN file, the configfs, FunctionFS and card lines of `/proc/mounts`, both battery gauges (the CW2015's `cw2015_capacity` and `cw2015_voltage`, which the firmware reads, and the AXP2101 supply's unused `capacity` and `voltage_now`: [hardware](hardware.md)), `ps`, `dmesg`'s last 300 lines, and the last 100 of `/tmp/q2-demo.err` and 300 of `/tmp/q2-demo.log`, where demo writes and q2player, which demo starts, writes too. It reads no `config.ini`, Wi-Fi setting or key and lists nothing on the card. Each save replaces the last. With no card in `/proc/mounts` the command writes nothing and exits 2. A toast says where it went ("Saved to SD card: q2-diagnostics.txt"), "No SD card", or "Couldn't save diagnostics". A release build has no row: `Q2POD_DEV` 0 leaves `diag_about_row` empty, and the compiler drops the rest.

## First boot

**Q2 Muse's defaults, once.** A Q2 flashed with this release, from stock or from any earlier q2-coda build, starts on Q2 Muse's own settings, none of the old ones kept (the user's, 2026-11-15: a Q2 kept stock's Enlarged Album Art on after flashing). S90play's start (`BOOT_HOOK` in `tools/build.py`) checks for `/mnt/data/q2-defaults` (`DEFAULTS_MARK`) before demo starts; without it, it copies the config a reset copies (`/release/assets/default/raw/config.ini`, `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, every section: PLAYSET, SYSSET, Q2POD, IPOD and the rest) over `/mnt/data/config.ini` through a `.new` file, synced and renamed, then writes the mark. With the mark there, a later update keeps the user's settings. The build adds one section to that file, `[IPOD]` with `KEEPLIT=1` (`DEFAULT_IPOD`), so Smart Awake starts on, as a missing key reads too. Only `config.ini` is replaced: saved Wi-Fi networks (`wpa_supplicant.conf`), Bluetooth pairings, the library's database and ratings are other files and stay. `test/build.py` runs it under the host's sh: the first boot puts the defaults in place and keeps the Wi-Fi file, the next keeps a changed setting.

Stock's `config_init` (`0x503d0c`) reads `SYSSET LANGUAGE` (`0x5047f8`); missing, it sets `g_guideflag` and the first boot opens stock's language guide (`guide_page`), where Q2 Muse's wheel and Center are off (`usable()` in `patch/navigation.c`). The `config.ini` that a first boot or a reset copies to `/mnt/data` has no such key, so every reset went through the guide. Q2 Muse is English only (Settings has no Language row), so the build writes `LANGUAGE=2`, English, at the top of that file's `SYSSET` (`default_config`, `DEFAULT_LANGUAGE` in `tools/build.py`) and the first boot lands on Home. A `config.ini` already on `/mnt/data` is left as it is.

<a id="config-ini"></a>
## config.ini

The `config.ini` stock copies to `/mnt/data` at first boot or a reset ends on `NAVHIDE=0` with no newline, and stock's `toolsWriteConfig` (`0x5d0284`) appends a section it does not find as `"[%s]\n%s=%s\n"` at the file's end. So the first section written after a reset ran on from that line: `NAVHIDE=0[Q2POD]`, from `usb_charge.c`'s `DACCHARGEOWN` early in `config_init`. `toolsReadConfig` takes a section only at a line's start, so neither it nor its keys were ever read: `synclink.c`'s `SYNCLINKOWN` a moment later appended a second `[Q2POD]`, and the next boot found no `DACCHARGEOWN`, set USB DAC charging On again and wrote the key into the second copy, so an Off chosen in the first session after a reset was lost once (seen in the emulator from a clean `config.ini`). Both of stock's functions take a key's first line in any section of that name, so a file with the section twice still reads. `toolsWriteConfig` is hooked (`ringnav_ini_write`, `patch/config_ini.c`): before stock writes, the file is read whole (up to 16 KB; a larger one is left alone), a line not starting with `[` that ends in `[Q2POD]` or `[IPOD]`, the two sections the payload adds, is split before the header, every line gets its newline, and under a header so split a key that a later section of the same name also holds is dropped, since the later line is the one stock has been reading and writing; a key only the split section holds comes back. A file that changes is written to `config.ini.tmp`, synced and renamed over it (`peq_save_file`); a sound file is only read. ponytail: a value that itself ends in `[Q2POD]` or `[IPOD]` would be split too; no key the payload or stock writes holds one, and telling the two apart would need the file's history. A split section whose every key was dropped stays as an empty header, which both functions pass over.

## Where Q2 Muse writes

The Q2's built-in storage (`/mnt/data`, UBIFS on raw NAND) wears with every write, and a synced write of a few bytes still rewrites at least a page and the index above it. Q2 Muse writes there only what the Q2 needs to boot with no card: anything written often and of use only with the card in (it is about the card's songs, or it is a history) lives on the card, in `/mnt/mmc/.q2pod`, through `patch/card_store.c`; and the settings a wheel steps are written once they settle.

**`card_store.c`.** A *blob* is a file written whole (temp, fsync, rename) to the card. With the card away (out, or lent to a computer as USB storage: `card_mounted` reads `/proc/mounts`, again only once [card_watch.c](#card-watch)'s generation has moved, every call while its thread is not running), a write keeps the newest copy in RAM, bounded by the blob's cap, reads return it, and `card_blob_flush`, called from the record's own poll, writes it once the card is back. A mounted card that refuses a write is reported to the caller, which retries as it did on the flash. A blob names the flash file it replaces: while the card has no copy that file is read (so a Q2 that boots with no card still has its history), and the first read with the card in copies it there; the flash file is left as it was and never written again. Dropping a blob leaves the card's file empty, which reads as none, so the old flash copy is not read again. A *log* is appended to; with the card away its lines go to a RAM ring (the oldest whole lines dropped to fit, counted), appended to the card in order before the next line once it is back, after a line saying how many were lost. Only stdio, `rename`, `mkdir` and the heap, so a separate program (the heat recorder's `q2guard`) can link it with its own `card_mounted`.

**Settled settings.** `config.ini` is rewritten whole (about 1.5 KB) by stock's `toolsWriteConfig` for every key saved, and a wheel turn on the volume saved one per step. `write_int_config`'s hook (`ringnav_write_config`) holds the keys a wheel steps, `PLAYSET VOLUME`, `BT_VOLUME`, `MAXVOLUME`, `BOOTVOLUME`, `BALANCE`, `SYSSET LIGHTNESS` and `Q2POD AIRVOL` (`config_hold`, `patch/config_ini.c`), and `power_poll` writes each `CONFIG_SETTLE_MS` (3 s) after its last change (`config_settle`), so a turn is one write. It holds the play mode's keys too, `PLAYSET PLAYMODE` (stock's `config_playmode` writes it through the same hook: `bal 0x4fe67c` at `0x4fe760`), `IPOD NPSHUFONE` and `IPOD NPREPOFF` (Now Playing's pair, `np_bar.c` `np_mode_set`), each written `MODE_SETTLE_MS` (1 s) after its last change: a Shuffle or Repeat tap sets the mode at once (`mclSetPlayMode`, under a millisecond) and rewrites no file in its own pass, where its two or three rewrites were 60-181 ms each of that pass in the emulator. `config_settle(0)` writes one held key a pass, the pass named `config settle` for the [UI pass watchdog](#ui-pass-watchdog), so a tap's keys land on three passes over a second later rather than all in one. Stock's own volume dialog and play mode setting save through the same hook, so they settle too. What is held is written at once before the payload reads one of them back (`config_value`, `ringnav_output`'s read of the other output's level), at Standby and at a clean end (power-off, Restart, an update, Rockbox). ponytail: a forced restart or a flat battery within 3 s of the last step (1 s of a mode tap) loses that change, the value before it coming back at boot; and a stock reader of these keys between a step and its write (none is known: stock reads them at `config_init`) would read the one before.

| File | Holds | Written | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `config.ini`, wheel-stepped keys | volume, limits, balance, brightness, crossfade length | 3 s after the last step | flash, settled |
| `config.ini`, other keys | settings | once per change | flash (boot reads it) |
| `.q2pod/ringnav-queue`, `-elapsed` | the queue snapshot and its second | each track change; every 30 s playing | card |
| `.q2pod/ringnav-resume` | long tracks' places | every 60 s on a long track, a pause, a track change | card |
| `.q2pod/ringnav-plays` | play counts | each counted play | card |
| `.q2pod/q2-battery` | Battery History | each percent fallen | card |
| `.q2muse/logs/q2-log.0` to `.3` | the [unified log](#unified-log) | batched: every 1 to 5 min, at once on an error, a warning, a snapshot | card (RAM while it is away) |
| `.q2pod/q2-usb.log`, `.1.log` | the [USB record](#usb-record) | each cable edge, 5 s after it, each OTG power change | card |
| `q2-state` | the [state record](#watchdog) | a change once it has held 5 s (a burst is one write); a run's first line and Standby's at once | flash: it must outlive a forced restart before the card is mounted |
| `q2-stall`, `q2-cf-trace` | a stall's, a cold Cover Flow open's record | only on a stall or a cold open | flash, for the same reason |
| ratings, sorts, library and Home order, games, EQ presets, Car Remote pairings, `adb_keys`, `boot-target`, the boot logo, Wi-Fi networks | user data and what boot needs | once per deliberate change | flash |

Stock's own writes are its to make: its settings pages' `config.ini` keys, Memory Playback's record at power-off, `database.db` on a library update, `wpa_supplicant.conf` and Bluetooth pairings.

## SyncLink

SyncLink is Shanling's phone remote for its Eddict Player app: a nearby phone browses the library, plays, changes settings, reads and sets the Wi-Fi network's name and password, and starts an over-the-air update. None of its listeners asks for a password: on Wi-Fi, `responseLogin` (`0x5ada40`), the handler of its login message, answers any caller and marks the session logged in. q2-coda keeps it off unless the user turns it on (`patch/synclink.c`). It cannot be removed: demo needs `libSL.so` (Bluetooth RFCOMM and LE GATT), `libWL.so` (Wi-Fi) and `libprotobuf-lite.so.15` to load, and the message handlers are demo's own code.

**One switch.** Stock's **Wireless → SyncLink** page, no longer reached from Settings (stock's page, `systemset_synclink_page_init`, `0x4d2df4`) is **Off**, **Bluetooth** or **Wi-Fi**: `g_synclinkflag` (`0xa4cbad`) 0, 1 or 2, saved as `SYSSET SYNCLINK`, which `config_init` reads at boot (`0x5049c0`, anything over 2 read as 0) and nothing else writes; the default `config.ini` stock copies in at first boot or a reset says `SYNCLINK=0`. Every start of a listener is stock's, behind that byte:

- Bluetooth: `start_btsynclink` (`0x527990`, `startSyncLink`: `BS_startRfcommServer` and `BLE_startServer`, and `btctl_set_synclink` for bluetoothd's own SyncLink mode) from `checkBluetoothStatus` (`0x4fd558`) only at 1; `addMessage`'s restarts after a phone leaves (`0x523638` on) at 1 (one LE restart at 1 or 2), and `synclink_mainscheduling`'s LE restart at 1.
- Wi-Fi: `synclink_mainscheduling` (`0x527a70`) calls `startWifiSyncLink` (`WSL_startServer(1751, "Shanling Q2(<mac>)", serial)`: the TCP listener on port 1751, a UDP socket on 1751 and the multicast group `239.250.255.225` that answers discovery as `shanling_synclink`) only at 2, with the Wi-Fi switch on and the network connected, and stops it when the link drops. Connecting to a network starts nothing by itself: `wifi_action_connect` and the other Wi-Fi actions only stop it (`stop_wifisynclink`) at 1 or 2.
- The page: choosing Bluetooth or Wi-Fi stops the other, sets the byte, saves it and starts the one chosen (`0x4d2754`); Off stops both.

`initSyncLink` (`platform_init`, after `config_init`) only makes the three transports' objects and their event loops; in the emulator it opens no network socket.

**Off on upgrade.** A Q2 that had SyncLink on keeps it on through a firmware update, since `/mnt/data` is kept. `synclink_default`, from `config_init`'s hook (`ringnav_usb_config`, `patch/usb_charge.c`) before `platform_init` goes on to Bluetooth, Wi-Fi and `initSyncLink`, turns it off once: until `Q2POD SYNCLINKOWN` is 1 it sets `g_synclinkflag` 0, saves `SYNCLINK=0` if it was on, and writes the mark. After that `SYNCLINK` is the user's, and a choice made on the page stays, as `Q2POD DACCHARGEOWN` does for [the DAC's charging](#early-usb-dac-charging-guard). ponytail: a SyncLink the user turned on on purpose before this firmware goes off once too; the changelog says so, as no file tells the two apart.

**Retired.** SyncLink has no row Settings leads to: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are Settings' own rows, so stock's Wireless page, which held SyncLink's, is not reached (the user's, 2026-11-15), and its listeners stay off after the one-time off above. Its caption under the row went with it.

**What off costs.** Eddict Player can't reach the Q2, and its over-the-air update with it; **Network Update** on the Q2 is separate and works. Nothing else needs it: AirPlay (`shairport`), DLNA (`libdmr.so`), USB DAC, Bluetooth output to headphones or a car, and the Q2's own settings never call SyncLink. SyncLink over Wi-Fi is one of [Smart Wi-Fi](#smart-wi-fi)'s reasons to keep the radio up, so off also lets the radio sleep sooner. Its Bluetooth mode changes how bluetoothd answers AVRCP and AVDTP (`g_synclink_mode` in bluetoothd's `avctp.c`, which logs `"AVCTP: SyncLink Mode | disconnect connect from %s"` and takes another branch on an incoming control link), so with it on a car's track buttons and metadata may stop while the audio plays on; read from the code, not seen on a device.

`test/fw/test_synclink.py` boots `config_init`'s hook with each saved choice (on before the mark, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi: off; on after it: kept; never on: only the mark) and lays out the Wireless list with its caption. In the emulator (a --dev build, the network connected), stock's `SYNCLINK=2` from older firmware opened TCP 1751, UDP 1751 and the multicast group; after `synclink_default` none is open after boot or after the network connects, and choosing Wi-Fi on the page opens all three.

## Smart Wi-Fi

**System settings → Power → Smart Wi-Fi** (`Q2POD SMARTWIFI`, off by default; the row after Charge Limit). With it on and the user's Wi-Fi switch on, `smart_poll` (from `power_poll`, every `SMART_POLL_MS`, 1 s) turns the radio off once nothing has needed the network for `SMART_IDLE_MS` (5 min), and back on as soon as something does. An associated radio with nothing to do still keeps its SDIO bus busy (about 90 interrupts a second at a few packets a minute, measured with local FLAC and the screen off, before 1.3.0's power save), so local listening pays for a link it never uses.

Both directions go through stock's own switch, `wifi_switch` (`0x5191b8`), as Quick Settings and the Wi-Fi page call it (`wifi_switch(1)`, a toggle of `g_wififlag`). Off removes `/tmp/wpasupplicant_initsuccess`, stops SyncLink's server (`stop_wifisynclink`, which needs `g_wififlag` still set), clears the switch's flags and `wifi_name`, runs `networkStop` and sets `wifilink_timeout` to 30; stock's `network_checkstatus` then sends `rtwpriv wlan0 pm_set ips=1`, as after the user's switch. On runs `networkStart(1)`, the background `wifi_connect.sh &`. The switch's last act, both branches', is its tail call `write_int_config(g_wififlag, "SYSSET", "WIFI")`; the `write_int_config` hook (`ringnav_write_config`, `smart_config`) drops that write for Smart Wi-Fi's own toggles and passes any other on, so `config.ini`, a reboot and the user's own switch stay stock's. A `SYSSET WIFI` write it passes is the user's (Quick Settings, the Wi-Fi page): Smart Wi-Fi forgets it had the radio off and counts `SMART_IDLE_MS` from the tap. With the row off, or the user's Wi-Fi off, a radio Smart Wi-Fi had off comes back, unsaved, and nothing more happens. Rockbox's own Wi-Fi stop ([Rockbox from Home](boot.md#rockbox-from-home)) is unaffected: demo restarts and reads `WIFI` from `config.ini`, which Smart Wi-Fi never wrote.

`smart_ready` keeps to stock's own conditions for its switch: `networkStart` and `networkStop` act only when `initNetworkModule`'s type (`NET_TYPE`, `0xa500d4`, no symbol; `NET_TYPE_READS` in `tools/build.py` pins both reads) is 2, Wi-Fi; the first scan taken (`wifi_initstatus` 0) and no connect half done (`wifi_connectstatus` not 1), as Quick Settings and the Wi-Fi page require; and never in test mode, while powering off or in the first-boot guide, where `on_wm_timer_networkstatus` also leaves the network alone.

Needing the network (`smart_needed`): a USB cable in; AirPlay or DLNA on (Network service); [Car Remote](#car-remote) while a phone could use the network (`coda_rc_wants_wifi`: a Wi-Fi link up, and Car Remote started, a phone connected by any way or a pairing card up within the last 10 minutes; with no link nothing, since the phone in the car comes over Bluetooth LE, and with no saved network in range the radio only scanned), and Pair a Phone (`carhowto_page`, its QR code and Wi-Fi address); [SyncLink](#synclink) over Wi-Fi (`g_synclinkflag` 2, off unless the user turns it on) or a SyncLink session, LocalSend's daemon (`localsend_running`); a stock stream queue of the types `on_wm_timer_networkstatus` (`0x4f5168`) stops once the link drops (`mclGetPlayType` 2, 3, 0xf1 and 0xf2: Tidal's), playing, paused or stopped, as stock would otherwise stop a paused one and lose its place; Spotify's librespot running (`spot_running`); an Internet Radio station; a card app started (`addon_running`: launched, or restarting after Retry, until it stops by itself, Stop Streaming Services or Rockbox; one stopped for USB storage counts once it starts again, as the cable holds the radio meanwhile); a scrobble upload, the user's or the automatic one (`scrobble_busy`); Network Update's download or an Apps job (`netupdate_busy`); Get Album Lyrics (`album_lyrics_busy`); a Tidal download (`tidal_busy`); an action held for the link (below); a time sync pending on a link (`g_syncnettime_flag`, cleared after one attempt); and a network page open anywhere in the window stack (`net_page_open`: Streaming and its services' pages but Tidal Downloads, a card app's page and its QR code, System settings' Apps, AirPlay's, Network service, SyncLink, the Wi-Fi page and its dialogs, LocalSend's page, the online lyrics and cover search, and Home's [Radio](#radio-home), whose stations stream while it is open). A new link counts as a use, so a fresh connection gets `SMART_IDLE_MS` before Smart Wi-Fi acts, time sync first. A radio that never associates (out of range, scanning) goes off after `SMART_IDLE_MS` too.

Waking. Streaming's page (`ringnav_stream`) and the Wi-Fi page (`systemset_wifi_page_init`, hooked as `ringnav_wifi_page`, before it builds its switch from `g_wififlag`) bring the radio back at once. Users that check the link once when they start would fail during the 3 to 8 s reconnect, so they wait for it through `smart_wifi_wait`, up to `SMART_CONNECT_MS` (15 s), then go on as they would have. The link is up once both the status bar's bars (`get_wifisignal`, which the payload's own actions check) and the network monitor thread's connect status (`networkGetConnectStatus`, which stock's check) say so: each comes from its own poll, about a second apart. A server song pressed ([Server library](#server-library)) waits that way too, before its app is started. Internet Radio's directory fetch and a station's start wait that way ("Connecting to Wi-Fi…", "Connecting…"; a station started from the side buttons too). An automatic scrobble upload due while Smart Wi-Fi has the radio off reads `[SCROBBLE] AUTO` from the card, wakes the radio if it is on, and goes at the next minute's check; a wake that brought no link, or `AUTO` off, waits `SA_RETRY_MIN` as a failed upload does, so an unreachable network is tried every half hour, not held on. A press that needs the link is held (`smart_hold`; Network Update, the Apps rows, Get Album Lyrics and Upload Scrobbles through `need_link`, which says "Connect to Wi-Fi first" when no link is coming): it toasts "Connecting to Wi-Fi…", and a 500 ms timer runs the action once the link is up, or `SMART_CONNECT_MS` on (to fail as it would have), if the page it was pressed on is still the top window past stock's self-closing overlays (toasts, `msginfo_dialog`, and the volume, `volume_dialog`, which a wheel turn opens over a toast) once no page is sliding; otherwise it is dropped. One waits at a time: a press while one waits takes its place, so the action runs once, and it runs unheld (`sw.held`), so a radio that could not come back fails it as before rather than holding it again. The payload's are Spotify's row (librespot never retries a Connect login or an mDNS registration that failed at its start), a card app's row, Upload Scrobbles, Network Update, the Apps page's rows and its opening check, and Get Album Lyrics. Three stock actions that check the link once and show `msg_notnetwork` without it are held the same way, each hooked at its entry (none has a symbol): Streaming's Tidal row (`0x540f7c`, the row click `stream_page_init` binds, on Streaming's page and in Home's Split Streaming list, whose Library list beside it names its rows by index too, so the row is found again in `scroll_view_streamsset`) and Now Playing More's Download Cover & Lyrics (`0x539614`, given More's window; More is no network page, so only this press wakes the radio). None reads its event, and the two rows are found again by name (stock names each row's list_item and button by its index and reads only that name), so nothing pressed is kept but the page. Quick Settings shows Off while Smart Wi-Fi has the radio off, as it is; a tap turns it on and saves it, as stock's does. The Wi-Fi page wakes it first, so its switch shows the user's setting (Off only when `smart_ready` refuses the wake).

`test/patch.py` runs stock's `wifi_switch` from the payload's toggles against the user's tap (the same calls in the same order, without the write), stock's `network_checkstatus` after it, the row, each keep-alive case, the Wi-Fi page, the automatic upload's wake, the held stock actions (stock's own code for the Tidal row, and the Tidal row on Home), Network's third row opening LocalSend and never stock's page, a press that joins the wait for Upload Scrobbles, Network Update, an Apps install and Get Album Lyrics, Spotify's and Internet Radio's waits. `test/fw/test_smart_wifi.py` runs the idle count on the host, Car Remote holding a linked radio 10 minutes past its last use, and letting an unlinked one go. ponytail: on Home the held Tidal row runs while Home is still the page in use, as Spotify's row does, even if the Streaming list has given way to another of Home's lists. ponytail: `network_checkstatus` sends `ips=1` only once its latch (`0xa4db39`) is set, after a connect, so a radio that never associated is left in whatever power state the driver chose. While stock refuses its switch (`smart_ready`), a wait that outlives `SMART_CONNECT_MS` can start one more.

<a id="scan-hold"></a>**Scan hold.** The RTL8733BS is one radio for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth ([hardware](hardware.md)), so a Wi-Fi scan's off-channel dwells are air time a headset's A2DP link loses. Of what scans, only `wpa_supplicant` does so unasked: with saved networks and none joined it scans again `scan_interval` (5 s) after each scan that found none (2.12's `events.c`, "No suitable network found"), for as long as the radio is on. The rest scan for a reason: demo scans only from the Wi-Fi page (as it opens, from its timer while a search counts down `wifi_searchtime`, and Search Again), as the switch turns Wi-Fi on, at start (`networkinit_thread`), going into Standby (`device_standby`) and while a join retries (`network_checkstatus`); Control Center's Wi-Fi circle clicks the switch; the shipped `wpa_supplicant.conf` has no `bgscan` or `autoscan`; the driver has no scheduled scan, its roaming is not the active kind (`roam_flags` starts at 3, without `RTW_ROAM_ACTIVE`, 0x4) and its 802.11d scan is off (`rtw_country_ie_slave_en_mode` 0). So `scan_hold_poll` (`patch/smart_wifi.c`, first in `smart_poll`, every `SMART_POLL_MS`, with Smart Wi-Fi's row on or off) runs `wpa_cli -i wlan0 scan_interval 3600` while music plays to a headset (`media_playing`, `mclGetOutputWay` 1) or a phone streams to the Q2 (`bt__recv_pageflag` 2), with the user's Wi-Fi on, no join trying (`wifi_connectstatus` not 1) and nothing needing the network (`smart_needed`, which counts the Wi-Fi page and its dialogs anywhere in the window stack), and `scan_interval 5` otherwise (or the [dark backoff](#scan-backoff) below). A change of the interval moves the rescan already due (`wpa_supplicant_update_scan_int`), so the hold and its end take effect at once, and it touches neither a joined link nor a scan the Wi-Fi page asks for: on the page the list fills as stock's does, music playing or not, Adapt to Signal on or not. `wpa_supplicant` is told only when what it should hear changes or it is a new one, by its control socket's inode (`/var/run/wpa_supplicant/wlan0`: the switch and Smart Wi-Fi's wake start a new one at 5 s, and a demo started beside a held one puts 5 back); a failed `wpa_cli` is tried again after `SCAN_RETRY_MS` (10 s). `test/fw/test_smart_wifi.py` holds each case. ponytail: not measured on a Q2 (the emulator has no radio); a walk with `wtx` and `afh` in the link monitor's log, Wi-Fi on and no network in range, held and not, would show what it buys. While held, a network that comes into range is joined within the hour, or at once when music stops or the Wi-Fi page opens. <a id="scan-backoff"></a>**Dark backoff.** With the screen off (`g_backlight_status` clear), nothing joined (`networkGetConnectStatus`), no join trying, no cable (`g_usbdet_value`) and no Wi-Fi page or dialog open (`net_page_open`), `scan_interval_s` gives each rescan twice the last, 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 s, then `SCAN_BACKOFF_MAX_S` (120 s), counted from when that state began; any of them ending puts 5 back, which brings the rescan already due forward. The hold, when it applies, wins. Car Remote does not stop the backoff, as it stops the hold while it needs the network: the car's network is joined within two minutes of appearing while dark, or within 5 s of a wake. Why: on 2026-11-19 a Q2 in a pocket with only the car's network enabled scanned every 7.5 to 10 s for hours (`/proc/net/rtl8733bs/wlan0/ps_info`'s IPS leave count; the SDIO bus at about 1,700 interrupts a second through each 3 to 5 s scan), and its fuel gauge fell a percent each 7.0 minutes, against 9.5 with Wi-Fi idle the night before: about 2.3 points an hour (some 40 mA of 1,850 mAh) went to scans. At 120 s a scan is about 3% of the time instead of 40%. `test/fw/test_smart_wifi.py` holds the steps and each way out. ponytail: not measured on a Q2 after the change; the IPS leave count over a dark idle minute (one every 2 minutes, not 6 to 8) is the check.

**The join watch.** A `wpa_supplicant` that never joins says so in the [unified log](#unified-log) (`join_watch`, from the scan hold's poll, every second while Wi-Fi is on and its control socket is there). From the socket's appearance it counts the seconds and says the association (`wlan0`'s `operstate` up or down: `wifi associated, N s after wpa_supplicant started`, `association lost`) and the link (stock's `networkGetConnectStatus`, a lease: `link up (a lease)`, `link down`) as they change. While unassociated, 30 s on (`JOIN_FIRST_MS`) and every minute after (`JOIN_EVERY_MS`), one `W` line runs `wpa_cli status` and `scan_results` and says `wpa_state`, how many networks its last scan saw (a count, never their names), the rescan interval the hold gave it and why (`held: a headset plays`, `dark backoff` or `not held`), and stock's switch flags (`g_wififlag`, `wifi_initstatus`, `wifi_connectstatus`). So a boot that never joins tells a `wpa_supplicant` that stopped scanning (`DISCONNECTED` or `INACTIVE` with an old count) from one that scans and finds nothing, or finds the network and fails to join (`ASSOCIATING`, `4WAY_HANDSHAKE`), and from a hold that should not be on. The udhcpc lines stay the lease's own record.

## Watchdog

The X2000's hardware watchdog (`module_driver/soc_watchdog.ko`, loaded at boot; `/dev/jz_watchdog`, libhardware2's `watchdog_start`, `watchdog_feed` and `watchdog_stop`) is never started by stock, so a demo whose UI loop stalls, or a stalled kernel, stays dark with every button dead until a 15 s Center hold cuts the power: `S90play` only reboots once demo is _gone_ (stock's `checkappprocess.sh` likewise), and a hung demo is still there. `wdt_poll`, from `power_poll` on every UI loop pass, opens the device on the first pass and starts it counting `WDT_MS` (60 s, `patch/offsets.inc`; ioctl `0x8004570d`, an `int` of milliseconds by pointer), then feeds it (`0x2000570f`) every pass, so a stall that long reboots the Q2. The driver counts on the RTC clock, through a suspend, so `ringnav_standby` stops it (`0x2000570e`) before stock's suspend and starts it again after. The driver's `close` is a no-op, so a demo that ends would leave it running: `ringnav_clean_end` stops it on a clean end (`into_poweroff`, through the hooked `save_memoryplay_info`; `device_reboot` and the firmware update dialog, through `reboot_save` in `patch/playback.c`; `rockbox_open`), and nothing is fed or recorded after. No device, or a refused start, leaves stock's behavior. The driver's prescaler caps a start at about 23 minutes. ponytail: the UI loop is the only feeder, so a stalled worker thread is not caught; a legitimate pass longer than `WDT_MS` would reboot. The known long ones, on the UI thread, are `importPlayList` reading every song's tags (stock's Import Playlists row and card apps' imports, through `addon_m3u_dir`) and a folder add loading each directory (`qm_tracks`): `ringnav_wdt_long` restarts the count at `WDT_LONG_MS` (15 min) as they begin, and the next pass, after they return, at `WDT_MS` again. Another long pass found later needs the same call. A hang inside Standby's suspend or resume is not caught: the watchdog is stopped across it.

**State record.** `state_poll` (the same pass) keeps `/mnt/data/q2-state`: one line, `screen:on|off power:running|suspending cable:in|out battery:N play:stopped|playing|paused out:jack|bluetooth|usb`; rewritten (flushed and `fsync`ed) only when the line changes. A change of the screen, cable, battery, playback or output is written `STATE_SETTLE_MS` (5 s) after the first one not yet written, as the latest line, so a burst (a wake that starts playback, say) is one write and the flash sees at most one every 5 s; a change undone within it writes nothing. What the boot check rests on is never held: a run's first line (the file's being there is the forced-restart mark), the power field, `power:suspending` just before Standby's suspend and `power:running` after it, and a clean end's removal. ponytail: a forced restart up to 5 s after a change leaves the line before it, which the crash log then reports. A clean end removes it. One still there at boot means the last session ended in a forced restart (or the battery ran out), and `S90play` puts it in `q2-crash.log` ([boot.md](boot.md)) before that is copied to the card, so a report of a dead Q2 says what it was doing. A Coverflow open that never finished leaves `/mnt/data/q2-cf-trace` ([Build](#coverflow)), which goes in after it as `== cover flow`; boot removes that file either way. On a `--dev` build, `WHEEL_LOG_HOOK` appends `/mnt/data/q2-wheel.log` (the wheel's stale-press notes, `stale_note`, [Hooks](#hooks)) to the card's `q2-wheel.log`, kept apart from the crash record so a note never replaces one.

**Stall record.** After the watchdog's reset, `q2-crash.log` says only that demo did not end, which reads the same as a stalled kernel, a 15 s hold or a flat battery. So once `wdt_poll` has started the watchdog, it starts a thread (`stall_watch`) that wakes every `STALL_POLL_MS` (5 s, `patch/offsets.inc`). `wdt_poll` counts the passes; when the count hasn't moved for `STALL_MS` (20 s), and again at `STALL_AGAIN_MS` (45 s), the thread writes `/mnt/data/q2-stall` and `fsync`s it (`stall_write`; the second appends). It counts from its first wake after the last pass, so up to 5 s short. Each record has these lines:

- `age N ms`, since the pass.
- `toasts N`: `toast()`'s dialogs open, nested ones counted (`st.toasts`).
- The UI loop's thread, which is demo's main thread, so `/proc/self`'s: `state` (the letter after the last `)` of `stat`), `wchan`, and `syscall` (the number and arguments, then `sp` and `pc`; `-1 sp pc` outside a call; `running` on the CPU, with no registers).
- `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo`, and `pgmajfault` and `workingset_refault_file` from `/proc/vmstat`.
- When `syscall` gave an `sp`, the stack words from there that could be code addresses, of the 160 up to the main stack's top (`stat`'s `startstack`), as a `q2remote --prof` line (`tid state pc ra words`, `ra` 0). `tools/q2remote.py prof` names only the samples it takes live, so a saved line's words are looked up by hand: `llvm-nm` on that build's `patch.elf` and `demo` names those in demo (linked at `0x400000`). They are read in place: from a blocked thread's `sp` to that top is its own stack, mapped, and an `sp` 8 MB or more below it is not the main stack's (`mmap`'s area starts at least 128 MB down), so it is left alone. demo imports no `lseek64` for `/proc/self/mem`.

The thread uses only `open`, `read`, `write`, `fsync`, `close` and `unlink` on buffers on its own stack (6.7 KB, kept out of `.scratch`): no stock call, no allocation, no lock the UI thread takes. A pass after a record removes it, as a stall that recovered isn't what it is for, and so does a clean end (`ringnav_clean_end`): Rockbox's demo, started again by `S90play`'s loop with no boot between, would never remove one written just before. Nothing is written while the watchdog is stopped (Standby's suspend, a clean end) or stretched (`ringnav_wdt_long`). At boot `S90play` appends it to `q2-crash.log` as `== stall`, after `== cover flow`, and removes it either way. Reading it: D with the two counts climbing between the records and `MemAvailable` near 0 is memory thrash; R with flat counts, a loop on the CPU; S in a futex wait, a deadlock; D in a driver with flat counts, a kernel or driver hang. ponytail: `wchan` reads `0` on a kernel without `CONFIG_KALLSYMS`, and a library's addresses on the stack line need that boot's `/proc/<pid>/maps`.

## Overheat guardian

`q2guard` (`patch/q2guard.c`, its decisions, log line and log rotation in `patch/q2guard_core.c`, `patch/q2guard.h`, the PMIC's die temperature in `patch/q2guard_pmic.c`; the log's RAM ring is `patch/card_store.c`, linked as `patch/q2guard_card.c`) is a helper process of its own, so that it keeps watching when demo is hung: `S90play` (`BOOT_HOOK`, `tools/build.py` `GUARD`) starts it before demo, `nice -n -5`, in a loop that starts it again 2 s after it ends, with the build's version and how the last session ended (`clean`, `forced` when `/mnt/data/q2-state` is still there, `stall` with `/mnt/data/q2-stall`; read only, before those are moved to `q2-crash.log`). A `flock` on `/tmp/q2guard.lock` keeps it to one; the file holds its pid. It is also the [unified log](#unified-log)'s writer. Every 5 s (1 s once powering off) it reads the temperature (the AXP2101 PMIC's die on the Q2, below) and the CPU's busy share from `/proc/stat`, and `guard_step` decides; it writes nothing to `/mnt/data`, and to the PMIC only the two registers below.

**Sensors.** Read from the stock V1.36 kernel (`vmlinux`, base `0x80010000`) and its device tree: there is no thermal core and no hwmon, so no `/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp` on the Q2. The AXP2101's `battery` supply (`axp2101_charger.c`; its desc built at `0x80536e40`) has twelve properties: present, voltage_now, energy_full_design, status, capacity_alert_min, temp, capacity, temp_alert_min, time_to_empty_now, time_to_full_now, manufacturer (`X-POWERS`) and capacity_level; no `current_now`. Its `temp` (`get_property` `0x80535418`, case 51) reads two bytes of a PMIC register and returns the second raw: the low byte of an ADC count, not tenths of a degree, so it varies within 0-255 and would pass a naive plausibility check; `temp_alert_min` is the constant 85. The device tree sets `pmu_chg_ic_temp = 0` and no TS (thermistor) limits. `read_temp` takes the PMIC's die while its reader is on, else a thermal zone, then a hwmon input, then the battery's `temp` unless its manufacturer is `X-POWERS`, so a Q2 whose PMIC reader is off reads none and watches the CPU.

**The die temperature** (`patch/q2guard_pmic.c`, `pmic_sample`). The AXP2101 (I2C bus 6, address `0x34`; `/dev/i2c-6` with `I2C_SLAVE_FORCE`, as `axp20x-i2c` owns the address, one SMBus byte transaction at a time) has a 14-bit ADC channel for its die: enabled by `0x30` bit 4 (power-on 0, and the stock kernel never writes `0x30`), the result in `0x3C` bits 5:0 (high) and `0x3D`, read high first; `T = 22 + (7274 - raw) / 20` C (XPowersLib and Rockbox; the datasheet gives only 0.1 mV a count). The stock kernel's power-key probe writes `0x34 = 0x40`: `0x34` bits 7:6 with `0x36` bit 6 are the ADC's debug mode `ch_dbg_en`, and 001 is "VBAT uses all channels", so the die channel never converts. Each sample is therefore a window: read `0x30`, `0x34`, `0x36` and `0x50` and go on only if they are as stock leaves them (`0x30` `0x03` or `0x13`, `0x34` mode 01 or 00, `0x36` bit 6 clear, `0x50 = 0x10`: the TS pin detached from the charger); set `0x30` bit 4 (read, modify, write, read back) at the start and whenever it is found clear again; write `0x34` with its mode bits cleared (bits 5:0 are read-only VBAT data), wait 1 s (`PMIC_WINDOW_MS`), read `0x3C`, `0x3D`, `0x3C`, and write `0x34` back as it was, tried three times and written whatever the reads did. A pair whose two high bytes differ, or a count of 0 (no conversion yet), is no reading. Any register not as expected turns the reader off for good with no write; three I2C errors in a row (over samples) too; a restore that fails three times too, leaving mode 00, the chip's own default, until the next boot rewrites `0x40`. Each is a `SENSOR pmic off: ...` note, and the CPU watch takes over. The first window also polls the pair every 50 ms and logs when its first conversion landed (`SENSOR pmic first conversion after N ms`), the measurement a shorter window would rest on. On a Q2 on 2026-11-17 (charging, in hand), outside q2guard with `i2cset`: before, `0x30 = 0x03`, `0x34 = 0x51`, `0x36 = 0xbf`, `0x13 = 0x03`, `0x50 = 0x10`; with the channel on and mode 00, raw 6952, 6950, 6950, 6947 (38.1 to 38.3 C, falling counts as it warmed), charging and the battery voltage unchanged, and `battery/temp` read `raw & 0xFF`, which confirms the kernel's `temp` is the low byte of this pair (q2guard still never trusts it). The bit in `0x30` survives a reboot (it resets only on the PMIC's power-on reset), so a Q2 that ran this firmware shows a varying `battery/temp` after a downgrade. The emulator has no `/dev/i2c-6`: the reader is off from the start (`SENSOR pmic none`), and the boot ends in the No Temperature Sensor card as before. ponytail: the window is 1 s, the device's first test's own wait; the first-conversion note says how much shorter it can be.

**Rules** (`guard_step`, temperatures in tenths of a degree). A reading counts only within 0..100 C and within 3 C of the last one that counted (a die moves tenths of a degree in 5 s; a jump is a misread), or within 6 C for the two readings from a change of the charger's state (`GUARD_STEP_DC`, `GUARD_SETTLE`; q2guard.c reads `ac/online` and `battery/status` each tick): the charger is on the same die, so a cable plugged in or pulled out steps the reading in one sample, +4.5 C and -3.3 C on 2026-11-20, and each step put the sensor down with a "No Temperature Sensor" card until the next two readings brought it back. Two readings, because the die can be read just before the cable is; 6 C, twice the usual bound, as the largest step seen was 4.5 C, so a broken sensor's wild reading at a plug-in is still a misread; three bad, missing or jumping in a row put the sensor down, and so does one that reads a single value for 60 readings (5 min), before it was trusted whatever the load, after it only while the CPU's busy share swung 40 points or more meanwhile (a real die moves then; an idle one may sit still). Down says why in its note (`SENSOR none usable: none read`, `out of range`, `jumps`, `constant`, `stuck while the load changed`). It is trusted once two readings differ, and after going down as soon as it reads and varies again, with no old reading to jump from. A misread neither counts towards a threshold nor breaks a run of readings over one. A suspend between two readings (Standby: `q2guard.c` sees `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` gain more than 2 s, `SLEPT_MS`, on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` since its last tick, `guard_in.slept`) leaves the last reading no bound for the next: the first after it is the one the next are held to, and the sensor stays trusted. On a Q2 on 2026-11-23 a Standby 20 s after a boot found the die at 40.1 C after the boot's load and 35.8 C at the first reading after the 75 s suspend, then 36.0, 36.2 and on; each was a jump from 40.1, so the sensor went down (`SENSOR none usable: jumps`) 15 s after the wake and came back 15 s later, its card left up. Trusted: three readings in a row at 55 C or more toast "Q2 is getting hot" once, again only after it fell below 50 C; three at 62 C or more begin the power-off, which nothing undoes (cooling during it included). **These thresholds are proposed, for the user to approve before release**, and are for the PMIC's die, not the battery. Why these numbers: the AXP2101's own limits are far above (charge-current thermal regulation at `0x65`'s threshold, 100 C by default; over-temperature level 1 at 125 C, `0x13 = 0x03` on the device; shutdown at 145 C, datasheet 6.7.4.3), so they protect the chip, not the battery or a hand, and the guardian has to act long before them. The die sits on the board beside the battery: on battery power the PMIC dissipates little and the die is within a few degrees of the board, and while charging its linear charger heats it, up to about 15 C over the board at 0.5 W (`θJA` 30 C/W, datasheet table 5-4; an upper bound, as the board spreads the heat). A lithium cell is rated to about 45 C charging and 60 C discharging. So 62 C on the die is a battery at about 60 C at worst on battery power, and nearer 50 C while charging; 55 C warns with 7 C to spare. The one reading so far is 38 C charging in hand, 17 C under the warning. Not yet measured: the die against the battery in a long hot run (playing on the charger in a warm room), which would show whether the warning comes too early while charging. The old thresholds (50 C and 58 C) were set for a battery or skin sensor the Q2 does not have. The CPU is logged and never powers off. Not trusted (down or not yet decided): the mean busy share over the last 24 samples (2 min); at 85% or more a 60 s countdown with Cancel; Cancel stands it down until the share stays under 50% for 12 samples (1 min), and the countdown's end begins the power-off. A sensor that comes back ends a countdown.

**demo's side** (`patch/heatguard.c`, `heatguard_poll` from `power_poll` every 500 ms). q2guard writes `/tmp/q2guard.state` every sample, `seq=N card=none|warn|nosensor|loadwarn|off left=MS state=... t=DECI beat=N bt=N`; demo answers in `/tmp/q2guard.ack`, `ack N`, `cancel N`, `card NAME` and `bt N done|off` (`bt=` is the [Bluetooth controller watchdog](#bluetooth-controller-watchdog)'s relaunch). Each new `seq` shows once, through `confirm` (feedback.c), tried again on the next poll while another card is up: `warn` a toast; `nosensor` "No Temperature Sensor" with one OK, which closes by itself (no OK needed, `No Temperature Sensor closed: the sensor is back` in the log) once the state says the sensor is trusted again (`card=none`, `state=ok`), since a card left up holds the screen and makes Software Update's remote check answer `busy`; `loadwarn` "Q2 has been working hard" with Cancel and Shut Down, counting down `left` to Shut Down; `off` answers `ack`, pauses the music if it plays (`player_play_pause`), shows "Q2 is too hot. Shutting down to cool off." counting down 10 s, and then opens stock's `poweroff_page` (its `into_poweroff` saves the queue), at the same time from the poll if the card couldn't show. Where `/usr/bin/q2guard` is installed, a state whose `beat` hasn't moved for 30 s, once demo has run a minute, is "Overheat protection isn't running", once. `hg_confirm` and `hg_toast` are the tests' seams, 0 on the Q2.

**Power-off.** From its start q2guard writes the log out; with no `ack` in 5 s (demo hung) it kills `hciplayer` and `q2player` (demo owns the player's socket, so there is no pause to send) and powers off as soon as the log write has finished; in any case 30 s after the start. Before `sync` and `reboot(RB_POWER_OFF)` the last lines go out in at most 3 s, never past the 30 s. A `reboot` that returns is logged once and tried again every second. On the emulator the guest's `reboot` either ends the sandbox's pid namespace (its power-off) or is refused, depending on which process of the sandbox asks.

**The heat log.** A line (`heat_line`) every 30 s, every 5 s while warm (45 C), plugged in (`ac/online`), at least 50% busy or counting down: the UTC time, uptime, the temperature, the PMIC's die temperature and its ADC count (`die=`, `adc=`: what the PMIC read, the guardian's verdict aside), the battery's raw `temp`, the level (CW2015) and mV, `battery/status`, the cable, the UDC's state and the configfs gadget bound to it, backlight on and brightness, Wi-Fi (`wlan0` up) and Bluetooth (`hci0`), the CPU clock if `cpufreq` exists (it doesn't on the Q2), the CPU busy since the last line, the top three processes by CPU over that time (`top_three`, `/proc/[pid]/stat` utime and stime), demo's threads, the process count and the guardian's state; notes of their own for BOOT, SENSOR, WARN, LOADWARN, POWEROFF, NOANSWER, CARD and POWER. Lines are held in `card_store.c`'s `card_log` (a 64 KB RAM ring, `HEAT_RAM`, the oldest whole lines dropped and counted) and go to `/mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-heat.0`: every 5 min (`FLUSH_MS`), every 30 s while fast or a Bluetooth stream runs (`FLUSH_FAST_MS`, `flush_every`), and at once on a note, by a forked child so a card that hangs never stops the watching. The watching process's `card_mounted` (the function `card_store.c` asks) is false, so `card_log_append` only ever holds; the child sets it true, so its `card_log_flush` appends the ring to the file in order, and the watcher drops what the child was given once the child exited 0 (if the ring moved meanwhile it keeps it all: a line twice beats a line lost). `heat_flush` rotates first: a `.0` that has reached 256 KB (`HEAT_FILE_MAX`) moves to `.1`, `.1` to `.2` and `.2` to `.3` (`HEAT_FILES`, the old `.3` dropped), so each file ends below 256 KB plus one flush (at most 64 KB), the four hold at most about 1.3 MB, and right after a move 768 KB stay: about four hours of the 5 s lines, near the Bluetooth log's six. While the card is away (not mounted read-write, or a configfs `mass_storage` LUN holds a file: USB Transfer Files) or a write fails, the lines stay in RAM and no child is started; the next write that gets through starts with `== N lines lost while the card was away` if the ring had to drop any (`tools/q2heat.py` reads it as a GAP note). Read it back over adb with the one-liner in [adb](adb.md#use). The [Bluetooth link monitor](#bluetooth-link-monitor) keeps its own log beside it, `q2-bt.0` to `.3`, through the same ring and writing child.

**What it costs.** Nothing here runs between ticks: no thread, one `usleep`, so 12 wakeups a minute (60 while powering off), and a quiet Q2 spends them on a few small reads. A tick reads `battery/temp`, the thermal zone, hwmon and `manufacturer` (each a missing file or a few bytes), `/proc/stat` and `/tmp/q2guard.ack`, and writes `/tmp/q2guard.state` (tmpfs, temp and rename); on the Q2 it also opens the PMIC's window: nine SMBus byte transactions (seven reads, two writes) and a 1 s `usleep` inside the 5 s tick, so 24 wakeups a minute instead of 12 (the first window polls every 50 ms, once a start). A log line adds about fifteen sysfs and `/proc` reads and one `/proc` walk, an open, read and close of `stat` for each process (`scan`, at most 512), the one cost that grows with the process count; it is a line every 30 s, or every tick while warm, plugged in or busy. A flush is one `fork` of this small process (its biggest part is the 64 KB ring) plus an append and `fsync` on the card. Measured on the emulator (qemu user mode, about 16 processes): 0.00 s of CPU in 60 s at the quiet cadence, 0.01 s in 60 s (0.017% of a core) at the 5 s one. A line is about 190 bytes: 0.5 MB a day at the 30 s cadence, 3.3 MB a day at 5 s, all on the card; the Q2's flash is never written. Memory is the ring's 64 KB, allocated at the first line, and the binary.

## Unified log

One log for the whole Q2, on the card: `/mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-log.0` to `.3`, beside the heat log and the [Bluetooth link log](#bluetooth-link-monitor), never on the flash (the user's, 2026-11-17). Before it, demo's stderr and the players' went to `/tmp/q2-demo.err` (release) or `/tmp/q2-demo.log` (`--dev`), in RAM and gone at every power-off, emptied whole past 512 KB, with no time or level on a line; only a crash moved a slice of them to the card, in `q2-crash.log`. A boot that finds the last session did not end cleanly copies the files to `/mnt/mmc/.q2muse/crashes/` before they roll on ([boot](boot.md)).

**A line** (`patch/ulog_line.h`, `ulog_line`): `2026-11-17T14:35:02Z 5123456 W usb cable in, seen after its edge, 9 ms`, the UTC time (the Q2's clock: 1970 until Wi-Fi or a computer sets it), the uptime in ms (`CLOCK_MONOTONIC`), a level (`E` error, `W` warning, `I` the rest), a source (`ui`, `player`, `usb`, `bt`, `wifi`, `guard`, `kernel`) and the message, one line, control characters as spaces, cut at about 500 bytes.

**One writer.** `q2guard` ([Overheat guardian](#overheat-guardian)) is the log's only writer, with its own code in `patch/q2log_core.c` (`patch/q2log.h`): its ring is a `card_store.c` `card_log` (`ULOG_RAM`, 64 KB, the oldest whole lines dropped and counted while the card is away), written by the same forked child as the heat and Bluetooth logs, so a card that hangs never stops the watching, and a card lent to a computer or pulled leaves the lines in RAM until it is back, then written in order after a `== N lines lost while the card was away` line if the ring overflowed. The writes are batched: with the heat log's flush (every 5 min, every 30 s while warm, plugged in or streaming, at once on a heat event), and at once on an `E` or `W` line, at most every 30 s for a run of them (`WARN_GAP_MS`). A flush that finds `q2-log.0` at 256 KB or more (`ULOG_FILE_MAX`) first moves `.2` to `.3` (the old `.3` goes), `.1` to `.2` and `.0` to `.1` (`ulog_flush`): about 1 MB in all, a file never split mid-line.

**Its feeds**, each read once a tick (5 s) in `q2guard`'s watching process, bounded, never blocking:

- **demo** (`patch/ulog.c`, `ulog(level, src, msg)`): demo never touches the card log. `ulog` writes a whole stamped line to demo's stderr, so it is in `/tmp/q2-demo.err` (release) or `/tmp/q2-demo.log` (`--dev`) as before, and `q2guard` passes it through as it is (`ulog_is_line`). USB's cable lines (`usb_ui.c` `usb_log`) go through it, their text as it was without its `q2 usb:` prefix, which the source replaces.
- **q2player's own lines**: stamped as demo's are (`player/main.c` `plog`, source `player`): each song demo hands it (`set-songurl`, `set-nexturl`, `set-gapless`, with the path or URL, a URL's query left out as it carries an app's token) and each `mcl-stop`, `I`; its crashes ([Player crashes](#player-crashes)); and each song that would not open or play, `E`, with its path (`engine.c` `log_failed`): `q2player: open failed (missing): /mnt/mmc/Music/a.flac` (or `unsupported`, `other`), `open for the new output failed` (a DSD song moved to another output) and `play failed (the output would not open or take audio)`, where before only `/tmp/notfile` or `/tmp/notsupport` was made for demo's dialog.
- **the player and stock's helpers**: `hciplayer`, `q2player`, `rtk_hciattach`, `wpa_supplicant`, `udhcpc` and `wifi_connect.sh` inherit demo's stderr, so their lines are in the same file without a stamp: `q2guard` stamps them when it reads them (up to 5 s late) and guesses the rest from their words (`ulog_guess`): `E` for one that names an error or failure (`error`, `fail`, `cannot`, `unable`, `refused`, `timed out`, ...), `W` for `warn`, else `I`; the source by who it names, the player first (`hciplayer` holds `hci`; its mplayer's own lines name `mplayer`, `playback` or an `audio codec`), then Bluetooth (`bluealsa`, `rtk_hci`, `hci0`, `bt` as a word of its own), Wi-Fi (`wpa_`, `wlan`, `udhcpc`), USB, else `ui`. `ulog_tail` reads from where it stopped, at most 16 KB a tick, and holds a line's start until its end arrives. In a `--dev` build that file also holds stock's stdout, so all of it comes in too.
- **the card apps** (`ulog_apps`, source the app's id, such as `subsonic`): a card app's launcher leaves its loop's pid in `/tmp/q2-<id>` while it runs ([Card apps](#card-apps)), and an app's Go log goes to `/tmp/q2-<id>.log` in RAM (q2-subsonic's `SetupLog`, rolled by a rename to `.1` at 256 KB, which `ulog_tail` reads across as it does demo's roll). Each tick lists `/tmp` and tails the log of every app whose pid file is there, `ULOG_APPS` (4) at most, from its start (from its end for a `q2guard` started again), Go's date (`2006/01/02 15:04:05` or `2006-01-02`) left out, the level guessed as for the player's lines; an app whose pid file has gone is read once more, then let go. The firmware's own `/tmp/q2-*.log` (`q2-demo.log`, `q2-scan.log`, `q2-iroh.log` and the rest) have no pid file and stay out. An app's log on the card (q2-subsonic's `.subsonic/log.txt`, where its fetches' failures go) is not read here, as the card may hang; Send Logs takes it ([localsend](localsend.md)).
- **coda-rc** (source `coda-rc`): the Car Remote daemon's own `/tmp/coda-rc.log` (`patch/coda_rc.c` `crc_log`, each line after a UTC stamp, which is left out as an app's date is), read as a card app's log is; its `ble:` lines (Bluetooth LE advertising made, refused or waiting, a phone's LE link) go to the [Bluetooth event log](#bluetooth-event-log) too, so each advertisement, an LE Set Extended Advertising command sequence to the controller, can be set beside the kernel's storms.
- **the kernel**: `/dev/kmsg` (the kernel's ring, read without consuming it, unlike `/proc/kmsg`), non-blocking, at most 64 records a tick; only the kernel's own (facility 0) at warning or worse (`ulog_kmsg`: priorities 0 to 3 `E`, 4 `W`), at the record's own uptime. A record overwritten before it was read is skipped (`EPIPE`). Where it does not open (the emulator's sandbox), the log says so once.
- **Bluetooth devices**: connects (and who began them), drops with who ended them, failed connects and authentications, pairings and Forgets, each naming the device, from the kernel's management channel as they come, not once a tick ([Bluetooth devices](#bluetooth-devices)).
- **A2DP transports**: each stream BlueZ sets up, starts, suspends and closes, off the system bus as it comes ([Bluetooth event log](#bluetooth-event-log)).
- **the guardian**: its heat-log notes (`BOOT`, `SENSOR`, `WARN`, `LOADWARN`, `POWEROFF`, `NOANSWER`, `CARD`, `POWER`) as `guard` lines, `W` for the ones that warn or go wrong.

A `q2guard` started again (S90play's loop, `last=respawn`) reads demo's file and `/dev/kmsg` from their present ends: the one before it read the rest.

**Repeats.** A run of one line (the same level, source and message) is the line once and a count: the rest are counted, not written, and `last line repeated N more times`, at the last one's time, goes in when another line comes or before a flush (`ulog_repeats`), and a repeat is no `E` or `W` line to flush for. The emulator's demo prints `gpio: failed to open device` seven times a second: before this it was 2171 of 2400 lines in 5 minutes, 200 KB.

**The roll** (`tools/build.py` `BOOT_HOOK`, and `LOG_HOOK` for `--dev`). demo's file is held open `O_APPEND` by demo and everything it starts, so it cannot be renamed under them: once a minute, past 256 KB (2 MB for the `--dev` file), S90play copies it to `.1` (the one before goes) and empties it. `ulog_tail` sees the file shorter than where it had read to and reads the rest of `.1` from there first, then the emptied file from its start. ponytail: a line written between the copy and the emptying (microseconds, once per 256 KB) is lost to both; and a file refilled past the old offset within one tick would not be seen as rolled (256 KB in 5 s). The crash log, Save Diagnostics (`patch/diagnostics.c`), the Bluetooth abnormal reboot's record (`system.c` `reboot_record`) and `q2remote.py log` read `.1` and the file together, so a tail just after a roll is still whole.

**Snapshots.** A snapshot (`ulog_snapshot`) is a `snapshot WHY` line and what the Q2 was doing, each a `guard` line: `/proc/meminfo`'s totals, `/proc/loadavg`, and the last heat line's state (temperature, battery, cable, screen, radios, the top three processes). Taken at:

- a **power-off**, **Restart** and **firmware update**: demo's `ulog_end("power-off")` (`ringnav_savequeue`), `ulog_end("restart")` (`ringnav_reboot_from`) and `ulog_end("update")` (`ringnav_checkfw`), once a run: a `shutdown: WHY` line, the request written to `/tmp/q2guard.snap`, a SIGUSR1 to the pid `q2guard` keeps in `/tmp/q2guard.lock` (through the shell's `kill`: demo imports none), and a wait for the answer, the request removed, `ULOG_END_MS` (2 s) at most. The signal ends `q2guard`'s sleep (`bt_sleep` returns on `guard_woke`), so it reads the feeds, takes the snapshot, writes all three logs out within 3 s (`flush_final`) and removes the request;
- a **crash**: S90play, once the crash log is written, asks the same way with `crash demo exit N` (`E`), and waits 3 s at most before the reboot;
- a **heat event**: the warning, the load warning and the protective power-off (`W`), once that tick's heat line is made;
- a **SIGTERM** (busybox init's, a second before its SIGKILL, when the system goes down another way): `snapshot shutdown signal`, the logs written out, `q2guard` ends.

With no `q2guard` to answer (none running, or a stale pid), nothing waits and no request is left.

**The boot marker.** Each start writes `boot build=V last=clean|forced|stall|respawn` (S90play's word, as the heat log's `BOOT`): `clean` when the last session ended through a clean end, `forced` when `/mnt/data/q2-state` was still there (a forced restart, a flat battery, or a crash, whose snapshot says which), `stall` with a stall record; `W` for all but `clean` and `respawn`.

**Reading it back.** `q2guard --dump` (also in release builds) asks the running `q2guard` for a flush (a `flush` request: no snapshot), waits for it (6 s at most), then prints `q2-log.3` to `.0`, oldest first: `adb exec-out q2guard --dump` ([adb](adb.md)). `tools/q2log.py` reads it, alone or merged by time with the heat and Bluetooth logs (`--adb` reads all three), and filters by level and source.

**What it costs.** No process, thread or wakeup of its own: each 5 s tick adds an `open`, `lseek` and `read` of demo's file (nothing read when it has not grown), a listing of `/tmp` and the same for each running card app's log and one non-blocking `read` of `/dev/kmsg` that finds nothing; a snapshot reads `/proc/meminfo` and `/proc/loadavg`. Memory is the 64 KB ring, the 16 KB read buffer and 512 bytes held for a line's end. Measured on the emulator (2026-11-17, a `--dev` build, `BLUETOOTH=0`, a pool slot, `smoke.py`'s walk four times over in 5.3 minutes: Library, Now Playing with a song playing, Cover Flow, four Settings pages, Control Center, Search) against the trunk's build doing the same: `q2guard` used 0.10 s of CPU against 0.03 s (qemu user mode, which counts its translation too: about 0.8 s an hour more, 0.02% of a core); the card took 7 flushes against 1 (about 80 an hour, each an append and `fsync` of a few KB to `q2-log.0` and `q2-heat.0`, set by the 30 s gap for the errors the emulator's stock code prints) and 13 KB of `q2-log` (about 150 KB an hour: the 1 MB covers about 7 hours of that use, longer on a Q2, where the emulator's missing devices do not fail). A release build reads only demo's stderr, without stock's stdout, so it writes less.

## UI pass watchdog

A UI loop pass that takes long enough to see (the wheel stops answering, a spinner stops turning) leaves a line in the [unified log](#unified-log), so a hitch reported from a real Q2 names its cause on the next occurrence. `patch/ui_watch.c` times each pass's work: from the end of stock's sleep (`main_loop_sleep`, after `ringnav_sleep`'s own `loop_wait`, `ui_watch_woke`) through its input, timers and paint to the next `ringnav_sleep` (`ui_watch_enter`), plus that call's polls up to its wait (`ui_watch_polled`). The sleeps are not counted. A pass of `UI_LATE_MS` (150 ms) or more with the screen lit is a `W ui` line, `ui pass 340 ms, step stream play, 0 more late since; events 330 ms, polls 10 ms (longest addon_poll 6 ms)`: the step is the last one a caller marked in that pass with `ui_watch_step` (a string constant; `-` for none); events is the pass's time before `ringnav_sleep` (stock's input, timers and paint, with the payload's handlers, timers and painters inside them) and polls the time of `ringnav_sleep`'s polls, each wrapped in `POLL` (`patch/nav/playback_power.c`), which names it to `ui_watch_poll` so the line names the longest. A pass whose step is `-` still says which half held it and, in the polls, which poll. The lines are at least `UI_LOG_MS` (1 s) apart, the late passes left out in between counted in the next. It changes nothing a pass does; its state is 40 bytes of `.scratch`. The owner's 17,308 ms pass of 2026-11-24 said only `step -`; the split names where such a pass went.

**The Library's lists.** Each Library list load names its step: `ringnav_localclass` (`patch/nav/library_pages.c` `class_step`) marks `songs list`, `albums list`, `artists list`, `composers list`, `genres list`, or `library list` for any other class (an album's songs, Favorites, Recent and the rest), and `library warm` while one of them is loaded again after a library change ([Name order](#name-order), Sorted ahead); Years marks `years list` (`era_menu`), `decade albums` (a decade's page opening), `decade rows` (its rows made after, [Era](#era)), and `decade play all`, `decade shuffle` and `decade album` for its rows. The owner's 2026-11-24 report ("choosing a decade locks up screen and runs slowly") left passes of 779, 2,076, 747, 802 and 4,792 ms, every one `step -`. In the pool emulator on the same library (its 9,199 songs, a pass there about a third of the Q2's), opening Artists was a pass of 451 ms, Albums 1,390 ms, Songs 1,422 ms and Genres 70 ms ([inefficiencies 35](inefficiencies.md#35-a-large-librarys-songs-albums-and-artists-load-and-sort-on-every-open)).

**A stream's start.** `stream_start` (`patch/addon.c`) marks its steps (`stream songs`, then `m3u_songs`'s `stream list` for each folder listing and `stream tags` for each song's tags, then `stream play`, `play_folder` opening Now Playing) and logs one `I ui` line when a session starts playing: `stream start: 1 songs in 8 ms (list 2, tags 6), play 172 ms`. `m3u_songs` adds its listing and tag times to `sst` whenever it runs; `stream_start` zeroes them first. On a pooled emulator (2026-11-22), a song written in place at 100 KB/s waited for its start (`stream_startable`) with no late pass; the start itself was one pass of 176 ms, nearly all `play_folder` (168 ms), and Now Playing's amount then followed the bytes as they came (4.7, 5.6, 6.5 of 24 MB, 8 s apart, while q2player waited for them).

**Measured on the owner's shape of library** (2026-11-24, a pool emulator, the Subsonic app signed in to `q2-fakesonic` with 9,199 songs in albums of two; a pass there is about a third of the Q2's): the first Songs open sorted in one pass of 1,824 ms (`songs list`); a server song started with the network up in passes of 351 and 596 ms before its `stream play` pass of 682 ms (play 512 ms); with the server's host name not resolving the press played the card's rows instead, its first pass 439 ms in `addon_poll` and then about 420 ms in events every 2.5 s while those short card songs started; with the server holding its stream 30 s, passes stayed under 660 ms and Return left Now Playing at once while it buffered. Shuffle on and off over a queue of the 9,212-song list, which the app streams with a few songs held in demo's queue, cost at most 627 ms in eleven presses, and one press off once cost 2,767 ms that did not come again in four more; the line for such a pass names its half and its longest poll.

## Loading wait

Every action that has to load before its result is on screen waits the same way (`patch/list_marks.c`; its look is [oled-design: Loading](oled-design.md#loading)): the window it was taken on stays as it is under the busy spinner, captioned with what loads when the action names it ("Shuffling songs…"), and the overlay shows only once the wait has lasted `LOAD_SHOW_MS` (300 ms), so a quick action never flashes it. Input is held from the press on, shown or not: the wheel's Centre and a touch go nowhere, so a second press asks nothing twice, and the wheel and Play/Pause stay the page's (Now Playing's volume). Return's release, or a lift off the spinner, gives the wait up; so does the window going away.

**Over a window, work in slices** (`load_wait(win, caption, step, cancel)`): `step` runs on the UI thread every `LOAD_STEP_MS` (16 ms, a frame) from a timer until it answers 1; each call is a slice of the work or a look at its worker, never a wait, so the screen stays live. A give-up calls `cancel`, which stops the work or marks its result to be dropped. `load_over(win, cancel)` is the same wait with no step and no caption, ended by its caller once a page opens (a card app's first open, Spotify's, Chapters). `load_over_paint` (from `ringnav_paint`) draws it and `load_over_input` (first in `ringnav_input`) holds the input. A page's own overlay (a card app's, Spotify's or Radio's list loading in place) paints through `load_spinner_paint`, which keeps the same delay: paints on one window less than two frames apart are one wait, counted from the first.

**Steps the UI thread cannot leave** (`load_wait_sync(win, caption, step, cancel)`: each step is one call that holds the UI thread, as a stock library query does; `load_block(done, caption)`: a wait for another thread's `done` inside a stock call, a Library list's sort under `load_localclass_list`, [Name order](#name-order)). No frame is painted while such a call runs, so the overlay goes straight onto the shown framebuffer page (`/dev/fb0` at its `FBIOGET_VSCREENINFO` y offset; the panel's x is the screen's 319 - y and its y the screen's x). Around each step (`sync_begin`, `sync_end`) the UI thread draws the square and the caption once, through an off-screen canvas holding what the framebuffer shows there (`LOAD_AREA`, 240 x 100 px from the square's top), and a thread of its own (`fb_painter`), which touches only those buffers and the framebuffer, puts that plate and the frame's dots on the screen every `LOAD_TICK_MS` (20 ms) from what is left of the wait's `LOAD_SHOW_MS` on; the end joins it and puts back what was covered. Input waits until the step returns, and the next frame's timer runs only after the UI thread has taken it: Return between two steps gives the wait up. Its cost while it is up is one 240 x 100 copy every 20 ms on the second core.

**Shuffle.** The Library's Shuffle page (`library_lists.c` `sp_pick`: Shuffle Songs, Shuffle Albums, Shuffle Folders) runs its job under `load_wait_sync` over the page, captioned "Shuffling songs…", "Shuffling albums…" or "Shuffling folders…": `shuffle_songs_start` (`shuffle_groups_start` for albums and folders, whose gate asks first) takes the request, and `shuffle_songs_poll` is a step a frame, the read of every song (one stock query) and then the play (`shuffle_play`, or `playback_groups` for albums and folders), answering 1 once none is left; the two passes are `shuffle read` and `shuffle play` for the [UI pass watchdog](#ui-pass-watchdog). A `--dev` build adds 1.5 s to the read while `/mnt/mmc/.q2pod/slow-read` exists, so the wait can be seen in the emulator, where the read of 9,199 songs is about 200 ms. Return before the play's step lets the songs read go (`shuffle_songs_cancel`) and leaves the page and what plays as they were; the play's step, once begun, runs to its end. Now Playing's Shuffle tap waits on nothing: the order's build is a few milliseconds ([Shuffle order](#shuffle-order)), and the tap's `config.ini` writes are held ([Where Q2 Muse writes](#where-q2-muse-writes)).

## Cover Flow log

"Cover Flow never loaded" (the owner, 2026-11-24) left nothing to read: `patch/coverflow*.c` wrote no line to the [unified log](#unified-log), and its phase trace (`cf_trace`, `/mnt/data/q2-cf-trace`) is removed when an open ends and reaches the card only after a forced restart. Home's Cover Flow open now leaves a few lines, source `cf` (`patch/coverflow.c`, `cw_*`): `I cover flow open: 6173 albums kept, their art known` (or `their art to look for`, or `the albums to query` when none are kept); `I cover flow shown: covers, 6178 albums, 1120 ms after its open, art looked up for 6178 albums in 240 ms (2 folder reads), 3090 covers to build` when the covers first show (`covers`; the look's albums, time and folder reads when this open made one, and the count when an art build starts behind them), or `no albums` for the empty page; and while neither has happened, a `W` line `CW_FIRST_MS` (5 s) after the open and every `CW_AGAIN_MS` (60 s) after that, looked for by the tick that waits (`open_step`'s every 16 ms while Home's spinner turns; the watch has no timer of its own), naming where it waits: `the albums' query (step 1 of 3)`, `the Sort's order`, `the cover lookup, 2400 of 6173 albums looked at, 1610 without a cover file` (`art_find`'s count so far, `art_state` 2: a server album whose app has no cover file, drawn as the placeholder), or, in a closed page's line, `its page, the covers not shown`. An open given up (Return, another key or touch, another window) is `I cover flow open given up after N ms, in <phase>`, and a page closed before its covers showed `I cover flow closed N ms after its open, not shown: <phase>`. Any of them ends `; no memory for <what>` when a calloc was refused that open: the art look's or the art build's jobs, or the covers' frame (drawn flat). An art build behind the covers (any Cover Flow page's) ends with `I cover flow art built: 3090 of 3090 covers, 19988 ms`, or, stopped first by a close or the card going, `I cover flow art stopped: 665 of 3090 covers, 3825 ms` (`cw_art`). The watch's state is 12 bytes of `.scratch`; scoped Cover Flow pages (an artist's albums, Ratings, Playlists) are not watched.

**The owner's shape, measured** (2026-11-24, the emulator, `--dev` builds of integ/q2-1201 and of this build behind the covers, the same slot and card): the device's catalogue (9,199 server songs, 6,173 album ids, 6,178 Cover Flow albums) imported into `servertable` as on the Q2, with an app cover file for half the albums (3,086; the owner's card had 2,048 that day, about 3,200 later). With the page held on a progress count until every cover was made, the covers showed 12.5 to 21.2 s after the press on a first open and 20.3 to 22.4 s on a reopen whose art was gone. With the build behind the covers they show 1.1 to 2.1 s (the albums' query) and 48 to 75 ms after the press, the whole build taking 20.0 to 25.7 s behind them, as long as the held one did at the host's load then; a turn of 30 albums mid-build had the new centre's art at the next look. A page left after 665 of 3,090 kept them, and the next open built the 2,425 left. With covers arriving 88 a minute (the app's cover rounds), no build restarted: each warm open showed the new albums on the placeholder and the next built only them (108 and 114 covers, 0.8 to 1.3 s). No state was found where an open never ends. On the Q2, at three to four times the emulator's time, that build is a minute or more behind the covers. Not covered: the device's card speed (the build syncs a note per album) and its own cover files.

## Bluetooth event log

On 2026-11-19 a day of Bluetooth trouble (a spotty link, a Forget that took two taps, a car that showed itself connected while the Q2 did not, songs in the car that did not play, the Pixel Buds slow to connect and dropped about 40 s after two refused AVDTP starts) left nothing to read: the logs that were pulled were `/tmp`'s, in RAM, and a restart had emptied them. The [unified log](#unified-log) is on the card, but it is 1 MB shared with every source, about 7 hours of use, and its `I` lines wait up to 5 minutes for a flush. The Bluetooth event log is the same lines kept apart and longer: `/mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs/q2-btev.0` to `.3`, beside the unified log, the heat log and the [link log](#bluetooth-link-monitor). It is instrumentation only: nothing in it changes what Bluetooth does.

**What goes in.** Each line that goes into the unified log's ring and is about Bluetooth is copied, byte for byte, into a second ring (`patch/q2log_core.c` `ulog_bt_to`, `ulog_bt_wanted`): every line of source `bt`; every line of any source that names bluealsa, BlueZ, Bluetooth, A2DP, AVDTP, `rtk_hci`, L2CAP or `hci0` (a word of its own); the player's `E` lines; and the `boot`, `snapshot` and `shutdown:` lines, so a restart between two lines shows. A run of one line repeated is counted in both logs, its `last line repeated N more times` following it. So the log holds:

- the kernel's device events ([Bluetooth devices](#bluetooth-devices)): connects with who began them (`by=q2` or `by=device`), disconnects with the reason and who ended it, failed connects and authentications, pairings, Forgets, discoveries and the devices found;
- the A2DP transports (below): each stream set up, started, suspended and closed;
- bluealsa's own lines, which come through demo's stderr, source `bt` (before 1128 they were guessed the player's, as `alsa` was matched before `bluealsa`): `Couldn't acquire transport: ... Input/output error` is an AVDTP start the device refused, `Couldn't release transport` a release BlueZ had already done;
- stock's link state as the [connection trace](#bluetooth-connection-trace) logs it, and each auto-connect's choice (`auto-connect (auto) picks ...` or `skips ...` and why);
- the player's errors: a song that would not open, with its path (`q2player: open failed (missing): ...`, [Unified log](#unified-log)), and an output that would not open (`plug:'bluealsa:...' ... Device or resource busy`);
- the stack's relaunches (`BT RESET`), the controller watchdog's lines ([Bluetooth controller watchdog](#bluetooth-controller-watchdog)) and the kernel's `Bluetooth:` warnings;
- coda-rc's `ble:` lines ([Unified log](#unified-log));
- hciconfig's `Can't init device hci0: Function not implemented (89)`, at every boot's Bluetooth on and no relaunch, as an `I` line that says it is expected ([Bluetooth name](#bluetooth-name)).

Left out though they name Bluetooth: the player's `parse_bluealsa_status_msg event = N` (its reading of bluealsa's events, numbers only), and the kernel's `debugfs: File 'force_bredr_smp' in directory 'hci0' already present!` at each stack start. Both stay in the unified log.

**Order.** The lines come from two places at two times: q2guard's own (the kernel's device events, the transports) as they happen, demo's from its stderr file at q2guard's next 5 s tick, with demo's earlier stamps; on 2026-11-22 demo's `auto-connect (usb) skips` (uptime 2071502) was written after q2guard's `transport ... pending` (2072148). Each line goes into the Bluetooth ring by its uptime, carried back past at most 64 later lines (`insert_sorted`), and a periodic flush writes only the lines more than `BTEV_HOLD_MS` (10 s) older than now (`ulog_settled`), so one read a tick late still lands before the later ones; a final flush writes all. While the writer has the ring's first bytes they are frozen (`ulog_bt_freeze`): no late line goes in among them, and the watcher drops exactly them when it is done. A line demo's file holds without a stamp (stock's printf, hciconfig's) was stamped when q2guard read it, up to a tick late (`====auto bt[...]` at 13040 between demo's 8493 and 8520 lines); it now takes the time of the stamped line before it in the file when that is at most a minute older, so it stays where it was written, in both logs. The unified log keeps the order its lines were read in.

The link log's one-a-second samples stay in `q2-bt` and are not copied.

**A2DP transports** (`patch/q2dbus.c`, `q2dbus.h`). The kernel's management channel sees links, not streams; whether a headset's audio stream started is bluetoothd's to know. BlueZ makes an `org.bluez.MediaTransport1` object for each A2DP stream once it is configured (AVDTP SET_CONFIGURATION and OPEN), sets its `State` to `pending` when the device sends AVDTP START and the stream waits for bluealsa to acquire it, `active` once a start is accepted (the device's, or bluealsa's Acquire), `idle` at a suspend or when a start fails, and removes the object at the stream's close. `q2guard` connects to the system bus (`/var/run/dbus/system_bus_socket`, the Q2's `/etc/dbus-1/system.conf`), authenticates as root (`EXTERNAL`, `DBUS_AUTH_MS` 500 ms at most), says `Hello` and adds three match rules: `PropertiesChanged` with `arg0='org.bluez.MediaTransport1'`, and the object manager's `InterfacesAdded` and `InterfacesRemoved` for objects under `/org/bluez/` (`arg0path`: BlueZ's object manager is at `/`).
