It calls nothing on BlueZ and waits for no answer: the socket is non-blocking, polled with the management channel in `bt_sleep`, so a signal is read and logged as it comes. Each one naming a transport is a `bt` line, the device's address from the object's path and its name as the device lines have it: `transport 04:00:6E:D3:96:6D "Grayson's Pixel Buds" opened: A2DP stream configured /sep1/fd0`, `... pending: the device asked to start, not yet acquired`, `... active: AVDTP started`, `... idle: AVDTP suspended or not started`, `... closed`. A refused start is then an `idle` (or no `active`) beside bluealsa's `Couldn't acquire transport`. The parser (`dbus_transport`) reads only the little-endian wire format's header fields, strings, object paths, signatures, arrays, dict entries and variants; a message too long for its 8 KB buffer is passed over whole, one that does not parse is dropped, and a bus that closes (or never opens: the emulator says `transports: the system bus does not open` once) is tried again a minute later (`DBUS_RETRY_MS`). `test/unit/test_q2dbus.py` checks the parser on messages built field by field; `test/q2dbus_bus.py` runs the socket side against a `dbus-daemon` of its own, with the signals sent by `gdbus` as bluetoothd sends them.

**Writing.** The ring is `BTEV_RAM` (32 KB, about 300 lines) while the card is away or between flushes, its oldest whole lines dropped and counted as the unified log's are. It is written by the same forked child, in the same flush as the other three logs (`flush_start`), so a card that hangs never stops `q2guard`: with every unified flush (every 5 minutes, every 30 s while warm, plugged in or streaming, within 30 s of an `E` or `W` line), and besides at least every minute while it holds a line (`BTEV_FLUSH_MS`); and at the power-off, restart, update, crash and SIGTERM snapshots (`flush_final`), so a clean restart loses nothing and a sudden one (a flat battery, a forced reset) at most the last minute of `I` lines. No line is written or `fsync`ed on its own. A flush that finds `q2-btev.0` at 128 KB (`BTEV_FILE_MAX`) or more first moves `.2` to `.3` (the old `.3` goes), `.1` to `.2` and `.0` to `.1`, never splitting a line: about 512 KB in all. The unified log of 2026-11-19 (27 hours, the Q2 on for most of them) held 134 KB of lines that count, so the four files keep about four such days.

**Reading it back.** `q2guard --dump-bt` asks the running `q2guard` for a flush, as `--dump` does, then prints `q2-btev.3` to `.0`, oldest first; `python3 tools/q2log.py --adb --btev` reads it over adb with the unified log's filters (`--level`, `--src`), and saved files are read as unified ones (`tools/q2log.py q2-btev.3 q2-btev.2 q2-btev.1 q2-btev.0`). Send Logs ([localsend](localsend.md)) sends the whole logs folder, so it is in there. Its lines are copies of the unified log's, so `--adb` without `--btev` does not merge it.

**What it costs.** Each line into the unified ring is also checked against the words above (eight case-blind scans of at most 500 bytes) and, when it counts, appended to a second ring: microseconds a line, at the unified log's few hundred lines an hour. Memory: the 32 KB ring (allocated at its first line), the bus's 8 KB read buffer and its socket. The bus wakes `q2guard` only for its three rules: a transport's state (a few times a stream, at each start, pause and codec change), a transport's volume (each volume step a headset reports, read and dropped), and the objects BlueZ adds or removes under `/org/bluez/` (a stream's transport, and each device a discovery finds for the first time). The card: at most one more flush a minute, only in a minute in which a Bluetooth line came, each an append and `fsync` of what came (that day averaged 5 KB an hour) beside the other three logs' own appends; a quiet Q2 takes none. ponytail: not yet measured on a Q2; the figures here are the 2026-11-19 log's line rate and the code's bounds.

## Modal dialog close

A modal dialog (every toast, `msginfo_dialog`, and the confirms) runs its own loop in `dialog_modal` (`0x65271c`); when the loop ends, stock queues the close (`0x6521dc`: `window_manager_close_window` on the dialog's parent) with `idle_add` and the bare dialog, not `widget_add_idle`, whose idles `widget_destroy_sync` (`0x6759b8`) removes with the widget. A dialog freed before that idle ran was read from freed memory. A `q2-crash.log` of 2026-11-10 (1.7.6) shows it: demo's SIGSEGV at `0x680554` (`window_manager_close_window`, reading the window manager's `0x94` from `0x43030000`), `ra` `0x739520` in `idle_info_on_idle`, through that close's tail calls, 2 s after a Standby resume while playing, at a track change. That call (`DIALOG_CLOSE` in `tools/build.py`) is now `ringnav_dialog_close` (`patch/system.c`), which queues `dialog_close` instead: it closes the dialog only while it is still one of the window manager's children, as `widget_destroy` takes a window out of its parent before it frees it, and otherwise does nothing. What freed that dialog first is not known; the log names only the stale close. ponytail: a window opened at the freed dialog's address before the idle runs is closed in its place.

## Coverflow sort

**System settings → Display → Coverflow → Coverflow Sort** (a `pod_rows` row after Artist View, `POD_CF_SORT`; the library's covers had a Sort card for it, and a Refresh library card, which 1.4.2 moved to Display as Coverflow Sort and Refresh Coverflow, so nothing but albums follows the last one) cycles **Album** (stock order), **Artist**, **Year**, **Recently Added**, **Most Played** and **Random** (`coverflow_sort_step`), saved in `/mnt/data/ringnav-coversort` (an int, through `blob_io`, so Refresh keeps it); the row's label reads the file (`coverflow_sort_name`). A press sets `cf.resort`, and Coverflow's next open reads the order again (`sort_check`) and sorts its kept list on the open's own thread with Home's spinner up (`sort_albums`, [Coverflow](#coverflow)'s Opening), so a Coverflow page open under Settings keeps its order until then. The stock album list is still queried and kept as before (`cf.stock`); the shown list is a sorted copy of it. Artist, Year and Recently Added rank albums by `toolsQueryDbTable(db, sql, row, 0)` with `split_row` over Coverflow's `ALBUM_SQL` grouping with an `ORDER BY` (Artist's year order and Year over `YEAR_SQL`, which adds the year as a sixth column): `ifnull(max(year),0)=0, max(year), album` (oldest first) or the same with `max(year) desc` (newest first) for Artist's year order and Year, as Playback settings' **Year Order** (Q2POD `YEAROLD`, `ringnav_year_old`; a change re-sorts on the next open), undated last, and `max(time_create) desc` for Recently Added (the 0 skips stock's name sort, `0x5dadf0`). Recently Added's query also returns that newest `time_create` (`ADDED_SQL`): albums that share it (a card's albums copied in one go, each file dated to the same second) came back in the grouping's order, the Album order, so the Sort looked as if it had not applied; such a run goes newest file first by its art track's modification time, which a copy keeps, then by that track's path (`added_places`, one stat for each album in a tie). Rows are matched back to the album rows by `album_cmp`, as the grouping is. Artist then sorts by artist without a leading article (`ringnav_sort_key`, as [Sorting](#sorting)), then that year rank. Most Played sums the [play counts](#play-counts) of each album's songs (`album_plays`, one pass over `getAllMusic`). Random ranks each album by `rand_below` (`patch/playback.c`) with no query, so it reshuffles whenever the list is rebuilt: choosing it, Refresh, a library change or a reboot. Ties and albums without a rank keep the stock order; the Unknown card stays last. A new order queries only the ranking. The rated albums' covers (Library → Ratings → Albums) keep their own Sort card, last, which cycles Rating, Album, Artist, Year and Most Played (`rated_sorts`, appended so saved values keep their order) in `ringnav-ratedsort`, stays centered when pressed, and queries only the ranking. An artist's page orders its albums the same way: `ringnav_artist_list` takes the artist's split albums (`artist_albums`), ranks them by `coverflow_by_year` (the same year query, or `album COLLATE NOCASE` with Playback settings' **Artist Album Order** at A–Z, Q2POD `ARTISTAZ`, matched to that short list), and restacks the grid's rows to match (`artist_order`, rows it cannot match last) before the art keys are made; the artist Coverflow gets that list as is.

## Artist View and Go to Album in Coverflow

**Playback → Library → Artist View** (`Q2POD ARTISTCF`, a `pod_rows` row of three values, Grid, Cover Flow (the default) and List) is read only by Go to Album (`qm_goto`): on Cover Flow or List, Go to Album opens the album's tracks in Cover Flow, on Grid the album page. `artistinfo_page` is always drawn as the design's artist page ([Library artist page](#library-artist-page)), whose Albums row opens cover rows whatever Artist View says. `ringnav_artist_list` still copies a stock albums tab that loads under another window (class `0xff01`), `coverflow_split`s it and keeps its art keys (`art_keys`) and album ids (`art_ids`). A Coverflow already open (the one a song was played from, under Now Playing or Ratings' Albums, issue #73) is closed once the new page is up (`scoped_open`), along with the Playlists page right under the playlists' covers (`page_under`, as Return does), `closed` run on it at once and its later `EVT_DESTROY` ignored (its ctx is no longer `cf.page`), since the covers keep one page's state; ponytail: Return from Now Playing then skips it.

Go to Album opens through the same `scoped_open` as a one-album page (`ALBUM_TRACKS`): `cf.albums` is a one-record copy of the song's record and the page goes straight to its tracks with no covers under them, so Return (`keyup`) closes it with `navigator_back` instead of showing covers. Playing a track is the covers' `play`, `play_folder` at `0xff10`, so Shuffle Songs' mode comes back as from any other load (`ringnav_load`).

Under a theme with one-line song rows (`list.songs.painter="inline"` and no title row of its own: OLED's), an album's tracks, from the covers or Go to Album, are the album page's rows (`to_tracks`, `song_tracks`): one `page_row_detail` line a track, and `song_list` reads a list whose window `coverflow_tracks` names as an album, its record the track at the row's index, so `song_row` draws the number before the title and the length on the right column. The caption (`page_title`'s label, which `page_retitle` still writes) stays hidden whatever its length, the list taking its place from the top, and the bar reads it: `bar_title_of` asks `coverflow_bar_title`, which is 0 on these tracks (the caption is the bar's source), empty over the covers (the status row shows the clock), else "Cover Flow". The bar keeps a page's source until it goes, so `to_tracks` and `to_covers` drop it (`title_gone`) and sync again (`retitle_bar`).

<a id="library-artist-page"></a>**A Library artist's page.** Stock's `artistinfo_page` is drawn as the design's artist page ([oled-design.md](oled-design.md#artist-page)) instead of its tabs, whichever way it opened (Library > Artists, Go to Artist and Now Playing's artist tap through `qm_goto`, Search's artist rows), as `patch/library_artist.c` does it. At the page's first tab load `artist_list` asks `artist_local`, which hides the window's children (the tabs and the toolbar), puts a view of its own in their place with `artist_page.c`'s header (`hero_open`), a lone Shuffle (`pair_open` with one label: one stop, the pair's width) and the drill-down rows, and returns 1, so stock's albums tab is not dressed; the window, its name and its Return stay stock's. Its data is read once, then: the artist's songs by the Songs tab's own query (`artist_songs` through `staged_music`, so with a server signed in the server library's songs of the name count too), their albums (each album_cmp album once, by its first song) ordered newest first with their years by `coverflow_newest` (YEAR_SQL descending, matched back by `album_cmp`; the undated last, with year 0), the genre the commonest `REC_STYLE` of the first 256 songs, and Top Songs `plays_ranked` (Most Played's ranking, `mp_rank`, over the artist's songs). Top Songs is a row only when one of the songs is counted; Radio, Singles & EPs and Similar Artists are never offered (the library has no similar songs, release types or similar artists). Albums opens `artistrows_page`, a page of `cover_row`s (40 px, the year right), whatever Artist View is; Top Songs and All Songs open it as song rows (36 px, the album after the title, the length right) that play the list from that song (`play_folder`, 0xf001, as Most Played's); an album row opens its album page (`album_page_open`, `qm_goto` as Look up Album opens `playerjumpinfo_page`, [Library album page](#library-album-page)). A row's cover is the server library's for a server row (`catalogue_cover`), else Cover Flow's cached `<album_key>.jpg` when Cover Flow has made it and it is not empty (Cover Flow's note of an album with no art), else the placeholder; the covers leave the image manager as the page closes. A Play/Pause hold on the page is taken and does nothing (`ringnav_keylong`: its rows are no showlist records), `song_list` reads its list as no song list, and the bar is untitled (`bar_title_of`). `artist_page.c` keeps one header: should a card app's artist page take it over this one, `la_front` draws the page again as it comes back to the front. ponytail: read once per page, so a library change while it is open shows at its next open; a whole artist's songs are rows, one widget each.

**The artist page's Albums grid.** The Albums tab's grid (`0x4ae3cc`) puts three 110 × 160 tiles in each 160 px `list_item` of `list_view_album`. A set whose list pitch is its settings row's (OLED's, 32) needs care: `tools/ipod.py` gives every re-pitched list an `item_height` (else `settings_list` would take it for a settings list), and stock's layouter forces `item_height` on every row (`0x5fd454` onward): each grid row was one pitch high, the rows overlapped, and stock's list painter, which culls a row by its own box (`canvas_is_rect_in_clip_rect` on the row, `0x5fe6a8`), skipped the tiles' covers and names wherever a repaint missed that box, while the scroll view's selection card painted there. The selected tile showed as a blue block with no name and its cover cut short. `ipod_list_layout` now clears `item_height` for the stock layout of a list whose rows hold a tile (a button narrower than half the list) and puts it back after, so each row keeps its own height; a list of text rows keeps the pitch. The page's title, stock's navbar label, is `g_play_info + 0x7680` (`ARTIST_TITLE`), copied by `localmusic_artistinfo_page_init` from `g_local_classinfo_save + 0x10d`, which `load_artistinfo_list` writes as `"%s"` of the record's `REC_ARTIST`: an artist with no name (Unknown Artist's row, or Go to Artist on an untagged song) read "(null)". `ringnav_artist_list`, which runs before each tab's navbar build (`0x4ad020`), writes `player_unknown` ("Unknown Artist" in English) over it; the query keeps stock's own Unknown flag (`g_local_classinfo_save + 0xa`). The bar's title (`bar_title_sync`, and `bar_title`) also shows no title rather than any other stock label reading "(null)".

## Playlist art

`patch/playlist_art.c` makes a playlist's picture for its rows (the grid has row art and no toolbar) and for its cover when Playlist View is Cover Flow. All of its calls are on the UI thread; one worker pthread builds the files and touches only files, its own SQLite connection (as `era_sql`: the device's libsqlite3 is `THREADSAFE=1`, not shared) and Cover Flow's art calls (`thumb`, `ff_thumb`, `album_art`, `ff_wait`, with `parse_cover_mutex` then `g_playcover_mutex` around `toolsGetAlbumCover` as for album art). `playlist_art(cd_num, name, small, url, size)` writes the `file://` url of the art that is ready and returns 1; else it queues a build and returns 0.

**Files.** In `/mnt/mmc/.coverflow/`, Cover Flow's cache: `pl_<cd_num>_<hash8>.jpg` (160 px) with `pl_<cd_num>_<hash8>_s.jpg` (52 px, the rows'), and `plc_<cd_num>_<hash8>.jpg` with `_s.jpg` for a playlist's own picture; `%08x` of an FNV-1a hash. The name holds what the file shows, so a changed playlist or picture asks for a new name and a file is never rewritten under one the image cache holds. A playlist's `pl_` hash runs over each song's `fileurl` in id order (the order `getMusicByPlayList` reads), so adding, removing or reordering songs, or a song's file changing, names a new file, the same songs imported again under new ids (stock's Import, a sync's) keep theirs, and an empty playlist has the seed's. The refresh reads every playlist's songs in rowid order (`select id,cd_num,fileurl from playlist where id>%u order by id limit 1024`: stock's table has no index on `cd_num`, and `order by cd_num,id` sorted the whole table into a temp b-tree, spilled to `/tmp` past about 18k rows), finding each row's playlist in the table and leaving out a `cd_num` outside 0 to 100 (Q2 Muse gives its own playlists ids from 0), no playlist's; a build reads its own playlist's the same way (`... and cd_num=%d`). Each read goes `PL_PAGE` (1024) rows at a time, each page from the last id the one before read (`page_row`; ratings' `rc_page` pages the same way), from 100 until a page comes back short, a statement each, so ids far apart (stock's import adds at `max(id)+1`, so they grow with every sync) cost no empty pages ([Songs' hashes](#playlist-art), the lock); `query` sets `PRAGMA cache_size=64` first, as `era_sql` does, so a 55k-row table's read stays under 1 MB of SQLite heap (`test/fw/test_playlist_art.py`). A `plc_` hash runs over the picture's full path, size and mtime. The old file stays on the card until Refresh Cover Flow, which empties `.coverflow/`, these files with the albums'.

**Own picture.** `_explaylist_data/<name>.jpg`, else `.png`, else, for a server playlist, its card app's cover of it (`covers/pl-<pid>.jpg`, Navidrome's collage of its albums, [server-library: Covers](server-library.md#covers)), the file `catalogue_playlist_cover` names from the mapping `catalogue_playlist_covers` reads at each `playlist_art_refresh` (`cat.serverlists`, one query on the UI thread per Playlists rebuild, none for a set that shows no art); the UI thread looks it up as it asks and hands the path to the job (`server`), so the worker reads no catalogue state. It is built and named as an own picture is (`plc_`, its hash over its path, size and time, so the app's new collage is a new file) and comes before the 2x2. The rest of this paragraph is the same for both: where `<name>` is the playlist's name with each of `\ / : * ? " < > |` and each control character turned into `_` (so a name FAT cannot hold finds its file; a longer one is cut at 255 bytes), a regular file only. `ff_thumb` makes it 160 px, by ffmpeg alone: the file is anyone's, and stock's decoder runs inside demo, so a picture it died or hung on would take demo down at every Playlists open, where an ffmpeg child dies alone. A picture over 12 megapixels (`PL_PICTURE_PX`, w × h by its header, `picture_size`), one whose header gives no size, or one that will not decode leaves an empty `plc_` marker with no ffmpeg run for the first two, and the playlist shows its 2x2 until the picture's size or time changes: the cap bounds ffmpeg's memory and the wait a page close makes for the conversion in hand (a 12 MP photo is about a second). A run of ffmpeg the kernel kills (`child_oom_first` makes the child its first choice) met memory short just then, so the next ask tries the picture again. The firmware only reads `_explaylist_data`.

**The 2x2.** Without a picture: up to four of the playlist's albums, from its first 64 by song id (`PL_ALBUMS`, which bounds the worker's dedup, heap and pick however many albums a playlist holds; the hash and count still cover every song), each told apart as `album_cmp` does (`album_ident` on the song's album, album artist and path). They are taken in song id order, the order the songs were added, the first four with art: an album whose Cover Flow art is built is used, one not built yet is built, and one Cover Flow marked as having none is passed over. So the same songs give the same four, and songs added after those four leave the picture as it is (a new file of the same covers, as the name follows the songs). An album not built is built as Cover Flow's build does (its song's embedded art, else its folder's cover), at most 16 builds for one playlist; an album whose song's file is gone (deleted over USB, a bad m3u line: stock's rescan leaves playlist rows) is passed over, with no ffmpeg run and no try spent. Each build runs under a synced note of its own, `.coverflow/pl-building` (`art_note`, as Cover Flow's `building`; its own file, so neither worker's note takes the other's place), removed when the build returns; one still there at the worker's next start names an album whose build demo died or hung on, and `art_strike` gives it Cover Flow's empty marker and a `q2-crash.log` line, so such an album costs one restart, not one per Playlists open. A clean end (`coverflow_clean_end`, as for Cover Flow's worker) sets the worker's cancel and removes the note (`playlist_art_clean_end`), so no cover is begun after it and no note of one is left for the kill that follows. One cover is copied; two make `a b / b a`, three `a b / c a`, four `a b / c d`. One ffmpeg child cuts each input to 80x80, fills it and stacks them (`hstack` and `vstack`: ffmpeg 4.2 has no `xstack`) into `<name>.tmp.jpg.ff`, renamed on success. Then `_s.jpg` is written first and `.jpg` last, so a `.jpg` that exists has both. A playlist with no album art, or whose 2x2 failed with ffmpeg run to its own exit, gets an empty `pl_` marker (not when the card went away or an ffmpeg was killed, so the next ask tries again), so it is not built again at every ask and shows the placeholder. A non-empty file means ready; a marker means none. ponytail: an album Cover Flow hasn't built is decoded inside demo (`album_art`: `toolsGetAlbumCover` under stock's art locks), so a bad embedded cover can take demo down, once per album (the note and strike above). Building those with ffmpeg alone (`ff_thumb`, then `beside_art(..., ff_thumb)`) would keep such a cover out of demo, let the worker hold no stock lock, and delete `PL_BUILDING`, the shared note and strike, the `album_art` split and `playlist_art_clean_end`, for one or two processes per album not built.

**Worker.** One pthread over a queue of 128 jobs (`PL_JOBS`, heap; each name a copy), a playlist at a time, which first lowers itself (`thread_lower(0)`, `coverflow_loader.c`, the loader's: nice 19 and best effort's lowest I/O level, which the ffmpeg runs it forks inherit; not the idle class, as the worker holds stock's art locks, which the UI thread takes for Library's and Spotify's art, and an idle-class holder gets the disk only when no one else wants it), so a first build stays below the player and the UI, so 100 playlists asked at once fill in one after another with one job's buffers. The UI appends at `total` and the worker advances `done`, both with release stores; the worker sets `idle` and ends when it finds none, and `playlist_art_poll` (a 250 ms timer, started by the first queued job) joins it, calls `playlist_art_ready(cd_num)` for each job that made a file, and starts another worker for jobs queued as it ended. Each job first checks that `.coverflow/` exists and `card_space` (16 MB) has room, and the worker stops when the card goes or fills: no file is named unless whole. A build reads the playlist's songs itself, and the hash of that read names the file, so songs that change while it builds are shown only by the next ask's own file. `playlist_art_stop` stops and joins it and drops the queue: the Playlists page destroyed; USB Storage (`ringnav_usbmode`), before stock hands the card to the computer, as a first build can hold card files open and write `.coverflow`, and no worker starts while `usbmode_page` exists; Refresh Cover Flow (`coverflow_refresh_art`), before it empties the cache, or a 2x2 whose cover it deleted would fail and be marked as none; and Import Playlists (`pl_due`), before stock's import writes its songs, the rebuild after it asking again; the cancel is checked at each song row read and each album step, so the join waits for at most one cover build, ffmpeg run or thumbnail, as Cover Flow's stop does, and it stays set until the queue is dropped, so a stopped job names and marks nothing. A build stopped is retried at the next open. While a worker runs, each 250 ms tick holds off Standby and auto power-off (`reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 0)`, as Get Album Lyrics does), so stock's `umount /mnt/mmc` never meets the build's open files; the screen still times out.

**Songs' hashes.** The UI thread runs no SQL for playlist art. `playlist_art_refresh`, once per Playlists rebuild (by the rows' first ask, else, when the covers are about to open, by `ringnav_playlist`; none when no row shows art), and as the covers come back to the front, only asks the worker (`want_lists`, starting one if none runs), which reads every playlist's songs in one pass over the table (a statement a page), at its start and between jobs, into a fresh heap table of up to 128 playlists (hash and song count each) and publishes it whole (`fresh`, an atomic exchange, so one the poll has not taken yet is replaced). The poll swaps it in (`pl_take`) and calls `playlist_art_ready` for each playlist it changed (new, gone, or its hash or count another), so those rows and covers ask again; the rest keep what they show. Until the first read of the table lands (the first Playlists open after boot) `playlist_art` answers none and queues nothing; later rebuilds draw from the table there was at once. A read that fails (the database busy while stock writes, or the page closed: the cancel fails it) publishes nothing, the table stays, and nothing retries per ask; the next rebuild reads again. A cover's "N songs" caption (`playlist_songs`, from the same table) reads 0 until the first read lands, and `playlist_ready` names it again when it does. A finished build hands the poll the hash and count its worker read, and the poll writes that one entry (`pl_note`); not when a read since the job was queued changed the entry, as that is newer. The worker's reads hold SQLite's shared lock on the rollback-journal database, and nothing in demo had a busy handler, so a write that met one failed at once: ours roll back and toast, stock's (Import's inserts, Add to Playlist, Rename) drop songs silently. Our writers open through `pl_db` and stock's shared connection, which it opens lazily and again after any error closes it, through `stock_db_open` (its open helper `0x5c8d30`'s `jalr sqlite3_open` at `0x5c8d64`, GOT `-0x544`, becomes `jal`); both set `PRAGMA busy_timeout=500`. Since V1.36 that helper runs `PRAGMA auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL` on a connection it has just opened, after the hook's own pragma, and `toolsInitDatabase` runs `PRAGMA incremental_vacuum(50)` six times once it has dropped an old `songtable`. The worker's reads hold the lock for one page of 1024 rows at a time and none between, so a writer waits for one page at most and commits between two (`test/fw/test_playlist_art.py`: a writer with no wait at all commits before every page of the messy table's read). The worker's own connection has no busy timeout: a page that meets a writer's commit (its PENDING lock stops new readers) fails the read, which steps aside, and the next rebuild reads again. ponytail: the wait is on stock's connection for every reader, so a stock write on the UI thread (a track start's play record, Rename) that meets Home's or the update dialog's count (`count_worker`, `msg_count`: a read of the whole `songtable` on their own connections, seconds on a big library) now holds the UI up to 500 ms per statement before it fails as it did; a shorter timeout is the knob.

**Rows.** `ringnav_playlist` (`patch/playlists.c`) leaves stock's row constructor (`0x4b4ee8`) and its 52 px `playlist_default` image, which `pl_art_image` finds and names `_pl_art`; the rows take `pl_fit`'s places. After each rebuild (outside the picker, which keeps its text rows), `pl_arts` calls `playlist_art_refresh` once, at the first shown art, and sets each shown art image to `playlist_art(..., small=1)` when it is ready; `pl_art_ready` sets only the rows of the playlist just made. Stock's index names the row's button, which gives its record in `p_deque_playlist` (`REC_DISC` is `cd_num`, `REC_TITLE` the name). The rows never load or unload an image themselves: they name the file again, so a Light Mode, Corners or Theme change (the image cache dropped) loads it again by name. The `_s.jpg` names join the rounding rule of `ringnav_image_add` (`navigation.c`), which skips them under square art; the 160 px files are not rounded there, as Cover Flow insets its covers' own corners.

**Where the covers open.** `load_albums` starts the library's covers (not a scoped page's, nor a load from the Sort card) on the album of the queue's song (`queue_now`, playing, paused or restored at boot), matched to the list by `album_cmp`, so a compilation's track finds its album ([#350](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/issues/350)); failing that, on the album last centered (`saved_album`, kept in `.coverflow/album` across a reboot), which is all it did until 1.8.2. A song with no album tag is not looked for (a folder play's records carry none, and the Unknown Album card is told apart by folder), nor is one the list lacks (a stream's, a spoken one's): those open on the last center.

**Cover Flow scope.** With Display's **Playlist View** set to Cover Flow (`POD_PL_CF`, `ringnav_playlist_coverflow`), the first rebuild of an open Playlists page that is not the picker and has at least one playlist veils it (`cf_veil`) and sets a 0 ms timer; `coverflow_playlists(p_deque_playlist)` then opens `coverflow_page` over it with a copy of the list as `cf.albums`, `cf.scoped = PLAYLISTS`, and unveils the page. The `PLAYLISTS` scope has no cards, stops at both ends as an artist's covers do (`coverflow_bounded`, so one or two playlists never repeat round the shelf), no letters (`lettered()` is false when scoped), no album hold (`coverflow_album` returns 0) and no position memory (`coverflow_scope` is 0, `saved_album` unwritten), and no covers are built for albums. The covers are the playlists' art: `ringnav_playlist` asks for the songs' read (`pl_arts`). One function, `art_url`, serves `fx_fill` and `cover()`: a playlist's 160 px url from `playlist_art`, which queues the build until the file exists; a playlist's cover is always that full art, with Fast Navigation on or off: `fx_fill` reads no half copy for it and `coverflow_halves` makes none while the playlists are up; the covers' `playlist_art_ready` is `playlist_ready`, which decodes the slot again by name and repaints, and is cleared when the covers close; the rows under them, hidden, hear nothing meanwhile, and ask again when the page comes to the front and stock rebuilds them (`pl_arts` takes the pointer back). Return closes the covers and the page under them (`page_under`). A song plays as `play_folder` with class `0xf001`, a song list, so `album_memory` is not set. The playlist's own list plays as `0xff13` (`0x4b4bdc`, as SyncLink's playlist play, `0x5268cc`), which stock pairs with the playlist's `cd_num` (`0xa55ca8` `+4`), and Now Playing's Delete (`delete_playqueue_file`, `0x501150`) takes a `0xff13` song out of that playlist (`deleteMusicFromPlaylist`). A cover's play sets no playlist, so it keeps `0xf001`: the queue snapshot restores either the same, and the payload reads every `0xf…` class alike, but for `ringnav_player_start`, to which the same song picked in the playlist's list after a cover play is another list (stock loads it, and the place comes back), not the same row. So Now Playing's More, whose Delete on a `0xf…` song list takes the song out of the library (`deleteMusicFromMusicDb`, `0x501214`), not the playlist, has no Delete row for a song played from a cover: `play` keeps `playback_loads` (`ringnav_load`'s count of queue loads, which `play_folder`'s synchronous start has just stepped) in `cover_load`, and while no queue has been loaded since (`coverflow_playlist_queue`) `ringnav_playermore` hides the row whose kind is Delete (`PLAYMORE_DELETE`, 7), as Display's hidden rows go (the list's layout and the wheel skip it). Any other queue started from anywhere loads through `mclLoadPlayList` and steps the count, so the row shows again. ponytail: the mark is RAM only, so after a restart the resumed queue's Delete shows and removes from the library, as for any song list; a flag in the queue's snapshot would keep it.

**Center.** `playlist_open(page, cd_num)` dispatches a click at x 0 on the row button of that `cd_num` on the page under the covers (stock's `PLAYLIST_PICK`), its list opening over them: by `cd_num`, since the list may have been read again since the covers copied it. Stock's click reads its add mode global (`PLAYLIST_ADD_MODE`, `0x4b49e0`), which an Add to Playlist picker opened over the covers leaves at 1 (a song's hold) or 2 (Now Playing's, left with Return), and would then add to the playlist instead of opening it, so `playlist_open` writes the page's own mode (`PL_MODE`) back first, as `ringnav_playlist` does. Stock resolves the row by its name, the playlist's index in the live `p_deque_playlist`, which is in name order and read again by any Playlists page built since (the picker's too), while the page's rows are its list as it was built. So a playlist whose place in the live list is past the page's rows (one added since, by a song's Add to Playlist → New, sorts in by name and pushes the last ones past) has no row: Center on it closes the covers (`coverflow_playlists_close`) and the page, on top, builds its rows again; the new playlist itself, at a place the rows still reach, opens.

**Hold.** A playlist cover's hold reuses `QM_PLAYLIST`: `qm_hold` finds the cover's record, then its `cd_num` in the live `p_deque_playlist` (a playlist gone holds nothing), and the menu is titled with the cover's own name (`qm_name`), as the live list keeps a renamed playlist's old name until its page is on top again (More…'s page, stock's, still heads itself from that list). The menu is the menu sheet's playlist menu (Play, Shuffle, Rename, Delete).

**Back to the covers.** More…'s Rename and Delete, Edit Playlist, and a song's Add to Playlist change the playlists under the covers, and the page under them reads its list again only when it is on top. So each time the covers come back to the front (`EVT_WINDOW_FOREGROUND`, `playlists_front`) or from a playlist's songs (`to_covers`), a 0 ms timer of its own (`pl_again`, which a Center's `cf.timer` does not cancel, and which leaves the covers to a Center still queued there, whose way back reads them again) reads the headers again (`getAllPlayList` through `staged`, which leaves `p_deque_playlist` and the page's rows as they are) and compares them with the covers' copy by `cd_num` and name. Changed, the copy is replaced and the covers built again (`load`), on the same playlist, or on the cover now in a deleted one's place; none left, the covers close and the list shows, with New Playlist. Unchanged, or the read failed (`getAllPlayList` below 0), nothing is rebuilt. Then, the covers still up, every cover left on the placeholder (`FX_PLACEHOLDER`, or a flat cover's image) is asked again, since a stop of the art's builds under them (USB Storage, Refresh Cover Flow) dropped their jobs and nothing else would queue them: a playlist with art builds again, one with none is answered from `playlist_art`'s table. `playlist_art_refresh` asks the worker to read the songs again, and `playlist_ready` names and decodes again each cover whose count or art changed.

## Hold Return

**Controls → Hold Return: Home** (`Q2POD HOLDRETURN`, [ipod.md](ipod.md#hold-return)) sends a hold to stock `navigator_back_to_home`, which closes windows and opens none: with a modal dialog on top it calls `dialog_quit` and goes on once the dialog is destroyed, otherwise it closes the stack from an idle. That is the call stock's own long Return made at that point, so the payload leaves `RETURN_RELEASE_LATCH` armed for stock's release filter, as the switch to Now Playing does. Where the hold's key-up reaches that filter, the release is swallowed and the next short Return passes; clearing the latch instead would let the release act on Home (on iPod, select or open Now Playing), or on the Now Playing just opened: until 1.8.0 the switch cleared it, as on V1.32 a release after the page's open event never reached the page; stock V1.34 delivered it, the held button's repeat having revived the press ([Queue menu](#held-keys)), so Now Playing closed again as Return was let go (#303). `KEY_ABORTED` drops it again, and the latch stays armed for a release let go before the open event. A release that never gets there leaves the latch armed, so `chord_gate` clears it on Return's next new press. Over quick settings, `ringnav` leaves a Return release to that filter while the latch is armed, before its own close (`dialog_quit`), so the release cannot close the dialog and leave the latch for the next Return.

## Play counts

The Resume poll also counts listens, for every track but [Podcasts and Audiobooks](#podcasts-and-audiobooks). It adds the seconds heard: a step of 1 or 2 s between polls, so seeks, pauses and Resume's jump add nothing. Once a track longer than `LISTEN_MIN_S` (30 s) has had half its length, or `LISTEN_MAX_S` (4 minutes), heard, its path's FNV-1a hash (with a CUE track's start mixed in, as a CUE image's tracks share one path) is counted, once per play; a new key (another track, or another CUE track of the same image) or the time falling back under 2 s from past 30 s (repeat one, or a seek to the start) starts a new play. The counts are a fixed table of `PLAYS_SLOTS` (512) hash/count pairs, 4 KB, in the card's `.q2pod/ringnav-plays`, read on first use and written whole like Resume's ring. A counted track moves first; with no free slot, the furthest back of the lowest counts, the least recently played, is replaced. The file never grows, whatever the library's size. Keys are paths, so counts survive Update Local Music and a moved or renamed file starts again from zero.

<a id="most-played"></a>**Most Played** (Local Music, under Shuffle) runs unsorted `getAllMusic` through `staged` as Shuffle Songs does, looks each song's path hash up in the table and lists the top `PLAYS_TOP` (100) on a runtime `mostplayed_page` (`page_list`, in 64 px `page_row_detail` rows: the title over "Artist · N plays", or the count alone when untagged, in 16 px `#AAAAAA`, stock's `s_scrlabel_gray24l` gray), most played first and, among equal counts, the most recently counted first (the table's order). A row folder-plays that ranked `stSongInfo` deque from itself and leaves the play mode alone. A Play/Pause hold opens the song menu over the same deque, as on Coverflow's tracks; for that the page is `CTX_FIXED`, so it also comes back on the last row. Nothing counted shows the empty state, "No Plays Yet", under the page's name. The ranked deque is kept after the page closes, and a song counted while it is closed that is not in it is appended (up to 2 × `PLAYS_TOP`), so a later open ranks only those, not the library. The library is read again after Coverflow's `library_gen` moves (scan or delete), when the deque would grow past that or such a song is counted with the page open, or when a full table drops the count of a song in it, since the next best could be any song. A song first counted from stock's folder browser has that queue's record, without library tags, until then.

**`staged`'s memory.** Saving the staging deque and copying a query's result out of it held two copies of every row at once, which got demo OOM-killed at 93 MB on a 47,283-song library. `staged_into` now points `tools_pdeq_directory` at the caller's deque for the query and back, so nothing is copied, and `staged` gives it a new one. **Library → Songs** does the same into the showlist (`songs_load`), where stock's `load_localclass_list` holds the staging deque and its copy together. This rests on stock writing the pointer once, at init (`0x5d12cc`), its 97 other uses reloading it through the GOT slot, and every `staged` caller being on the UI thread. A stock thread filling the deque meanwhile (a scan, a Bluetooth key's Folder Skip) writes into the caller's, the same race the copies had. ponytail: one copy per whole-library read is the floor, and lists already held add to it: Songs' rows stay in the showlist after its page closes, as stock's do, and a queue of the whole library (Shuffle Songs) is a copy of its own, so the next whole-library read holds two. Most Played can rank with `sqlite3_exec` over `fileurl` and fetch only the top rows, if that proves too much.

**Cover tasks.** A Library list's page runs stock's `albumcoverinfo_init` (`0x4f77e4`) over its rows when it opens and each time it comes back: Songs at its page init (`0x4acda8`) and in both branches of its return (`0x4ab788` reloads the list, `0x4ab830` keeps it). It refills the art thread's `pdeq_albumcoverlist` with a 12-byte task a row (two ready flags, the name, the path), each built on the stack from a `malloc`'d copy of the row's name and path and pushed. The list's element copy (`0x5c639c`) duplicates both, and stock never freed its own: about 127 bytes a song (with 90-byte paths) at every call, 8.3 MB each time Songs opened or came back at 65,000 songs. That push (`0x4f79c4`, `COVER_PUSH`) becomes `jal ringnav_cover_push`, which frees the two once the list has its copies. Only the stack task had their addresses, and the list's copies are freed as before, by its destroy (`0x5c5c48`) at the next clear. Albums, Artists and the other callers stop losing theirs too, as does Folder view's `foldercoverinfo_init` (`0x4f79d4`), which builds the same task at its own push (`0x4f7b6c`).

## Ratings

A song has 0 to 5 stars and, apart from them, a like (the user's ruling, 2026-11-18: "heart is only for liking a song"). The like is stock's My Fav (the `myfav` table, `checkFavExist`), so Now Playing's heart, the queue menu's Favorites rows and the Loved list stay one value; it sets no stars, and five stars like nothing. The stars, 1 to 5, are kept in `/mnt/data/ringnav-ratings`, a table of 4,096 words that doubles whenever three quarters of it would be in use, up to `RATE_SLOTS` (16384, 12,285 ratings; 64 KB on the heap and in the file at most), each a song's `listen_key` (the [play counts](#play-counts)' path hash) with its low three bits replaced by the stars, 0 for a free slot, 7 for a rating taken out; a key's slot is probed from its hash's place (`rate_home`, open addressing), so a lookup reads a few words, and the probes stay short as no table is more than three quarters full; the file's last two words say it is laid out that way (`RATE_LAYOUT`) and how many slots are in use, so it is read as it is, while an older file, whose ratings fill it from the first slot (16 KB), is laid out at its first use in a table with room for them (`rates`) and keeps them; a walk of the table (the card copy, `rate_all`) stops once it has seen every slot in use; a slot reading 6 or 7 counts as none. Before this the table held only 1 to 4 (five was My Fav), so it needed no rewrite: a song rated 1 to 4 keeps its stars, and a song whose only rating was the favourite stays liked and has no stars. Unrated rather than five, because nothing told a favourite apart from a deliberate five, and five for every like would fill Top Rated with the whole of Favorites and send a `setRating` 5 for each. Stars are set only on Now Playing's [rating page](#rating-page) (and Car Remote's Rate). The table is `calloc`'d and read whole on first use and written whole through `blob_io` on each change; a full table refuses a new rating with a toast rather than drop one.

**Now Playing.** `playing_page_init` is hooked (`ringnav_playing`). Stock binds `img_fav`'s click to `0x53c968` with the window as context: for a local track it runs `manage_myfav` (`0x5219ec`, My Fav toggled for the queue's playing index) and swaps the heart's image. `rate_bind` finds that binding in the heart's emitter, takes it off and binds its own click (`rate_fav_click`) and nothing else: the heart has no hold, so a press held on it is a tap. The heart's click returns 0, as stock's does: after a child's STOP stock's `widget_on_pointer_up` skips the parents' own release, so the `slide_view` kept the window's grab, and the seek bar and More took no taps until the page closed. The queue menu's "Queue unchanged" pick returns 0 for the same reason (its list's `scroll_view`). A tap runs stock's click (or takes a server row's like out, below), tells the card app (`fav_told`) and the server (`catalogue_liked`), and leaves the stars as they are. Centre on the Centre cycle's ring round the heart clicks it as a tap does (`np_centre`, `stock_dispatch_trampoline`). Every 500 ms with the screen on, `rate_tick` runs `rate_heart` (`rate_row_heart`, a server row's favourite on its Stream Cache copy).

<a id="rating-page"></a>**Rating page.** Now Playing's third page (`patch/np_rate.c`; [ipod.md](ipod.md#rating-page), [oled-design](oled-design.md#rating-page)) shows the playing track's stars, 0 to 5, read through `rate_now` (`rate_kept` alone: the like adds none) and set through `rate_now_set`, the `rate_song` Car Remote uses too, so the table, the card's copy and `catalogue_rated`'s `stars=` line in `ratings.out` (the app's `setRating`) follow; My Fav is never touched. The table's form is unchanged, so 1-4 kept before are 1-4 stars. `tools/ipod.py` `np_rate_page` adds `view_rate`, an empty view, to the `slide_view` after the lyrics' page, so the swipe reaches it and the slide_view's `value` is its index. `np_rate_bind` (from `ringnav_playing`, after `np_slide` and `np_lrc`) finds it and the lyrics' page and binds the touch; everything else is the payload's. `np_rate_poll`, in `lyric_poll`, makes the column full screen with `np_full` once the slide_view rests on the page, untouched and with no window sliding, and puts it back once it is on another page (a swipe drags the pages full height; no abort reaches the page, measured in the emulator); full-screen lyrics keep it onto the page and end on the art's, as before. `row_paint`'s state row (`np_modes`) and `np_stream_paint` are skipped while it is full screen, as the column covers their rows. `ringnav_paint_bg` calls `np_rate_bg` after stock's background: the glow on both pages, then the page itself (title and artist through `ui_text`, the stars as `oled_npstar_*` art, `tools/art.py` `NP_STAR_PX` and `NP_STAR_BIG_PX`, the outlines at `NR_FAINT` global alpha, the dots by `round_row`), laid out in screen rows less the page's own top, so it stands where the design has it at rest and slides with the page. The wheel reaches `np_rate_key` ahead of the lyrics in `ringnav` and Centre `np_rate_centre` at the top of `np_centre` (after a short hold's screen off), each only while the page is the window in front's current page with no scrub or Centre cycle; the target's timeout is `NR_TARGET_MS` (4 s). The rating is read again at most every `NR_POLL_MS` (500 ms) while the page shows, so a change from the server or Car Remote reaches it. Smart Awake (`keep_lit_poll`) counts the lyrics page alone. **Glow.** `nr_glow` makes a window-sized opaque BGRA8888 bitmap (480 KB: the window is the whole 375 x 320 screen, full-bleed under the status row) when a glow page first paints for a cover not seen yet, keyed by `st.np_art` and `img_cover`'s image name: `nr_cover_grid` averages the image manager's decode on a 4 x 4 grid (8 x 8 samples a cell, over black where clear), `nr_cell` raises each cell's colour about its luma (`NR_GLOW_SAT`), dims it (`NR_GLOW_GAIN`) and scales it so no channel passes `NR_GLOW_MAX` (60: `#3C3C3C`'s luminance, 0.045, leaves `#ABABAB` at 4.8:1), and `nr_glow_paint` spreads the cells bilinearly, shades them by an ellipse round `NR_GLOW_CY` whose brightness is the approved mock-up's falloff (`nr_fall`, its CSS gradient blurred 30 px, measured on its PNG at each sixteenth of r squared, black from 15/16), with a grain of one level. Above the column (the lyrics page at rest, under the status row) `np_rate_bg` on Now Playing's window draws the glow's rows over each glow page the `slide_view` shows, at its place across less the slide_view's `xoffset` (the drag), and `np_rate_poll` invalidates that band when the page, the drag or the glow changes (`nr_band_poll`), as nothing else repaints it. Each paint after that copies its rows (`np_glow_rows`, `canvas_draw_image` of an opaque image, a row at a time); `lyrics_fade` draws its fade rows from it at the fade's alpha instead of a fill of black. `np_rate_builds` counts them for the tests; `np_gone` (`np_rate_gone`) frees it, and Light Mode makes none. The state is one heap block behind one scratch pointer (`nr`), the scratch arena being full; the badge's two fields went with it. ponytail: a cover shown while the player still writes the next one makes a glow for each; a second open of Now Playing on the same song makes it again.

**Lists.** Library's **Ratings** row (`library_into`, stock's `local_fav` icon) takes My Fav's place, whose stock row stays hidden next to it. It opens `ratings_page` with Top Rated (4-5 stars), Loved (the liked songs, My Fav's, whatever their stars), All Rated (1-5) and Disliked (1). Each runs `getAllMusic(0)` (title order; `all_songs` with `LIBRARY_ALL`, so with a server signed in `library_query` reads every card song, spoken ones too, with the server's beside them) and `getAllFav` (`0x509a94`, `select * from myfav` through the same row callback, `0x506428`) through `staged`, reads every song's stars from the kept keys and its like from the fav keys (`rate_all`, `RATE_LIKED` above the stars: those keys sorted once by key, each song's found by binary search, so a list costs songs times log rated, not songs times rated), and lists the matches most stars first on `rated_page`, as Most Played's: five stars then "· Artist" under the title (Phosphor `star-fill` and `star` glyphs at 14 px in Text Primary, white on the selection, no colour, `oled_rate_on_*` and `oled_rate_off_*` from `tools/art.py`: `rate_row` moves the line's words past them and marks the row, and `rate_stars_paint`, which `ringnav_paint` calls only while a Ratings list is open (`st.rt_page`), draws them with it; a liked song with no stars, in Loved, has none), a row playing the list from itself as a library queue, the queue menu on a Play/Pause hold (`CTX_FIXED`).

**Albums.** An album has its own 0 to 5 hearts in `/mnt/data/ringnav-album-ratings`, the same `RATE_SLOTS` word table (5 included, an album having no stock favorite of its own), keyed by `album_id` (coverflow.c): an FNV-1a hash of what `album_cmp` compares, the name and album artist ASCII-lowercased, else the name and the album folder (`album_dir`, disc folders as one, case kept); the Unknown Album card is one album. A slot reading 6 or 7 counts as unrated, and a file shorter than the table (one written when it held 4096 slots) is read as far as it goes, the rest free. A save writes the table whole; a failed write puts the slot back and toasts "Rating not saved", a full table "Ratings are full": at its largest a table keeps 12,285 ratings (`RATE_SLOTS` words, three quarters of them in use, so a lookup's probe stays short), and a new song's rating past that is refused with that toast, nothing written and every kept rating as it was (a kept song's can still change). Raising it is `RATE_SLOTS`: each doubling costs that table's heap and file twice over (64 KB each now at most) and a synced write of the whole file per rating. The first time a Q2's older file (16 KB, from before the hashing) is read, it is kept as it was beside the new one, `/mnt/data/ringnav-ratings.v1` (and `ringnav-album-ratings.v1`), once, never written again, so an older firmware or a fault in this layout can't lose what was there. The queue menu gives an album **Favorite** or **Unfavorite** (5 or 0; `qm_album_id`): a Coverflow cover's record, a Library Albums row (split as Coverflow's), or an artist's albums tab row, whose split album `ringnav_artist_list` finds as for art keys and keeps in `art_ids`. There is no Rate Album: the [rating page](#rating-page) is the one place to rate, so 1 to 4 kept before stay and are listed, and no new ones are made. An album's favourite is its songs' like: reaching 5 puts the album's tracks (`qm_collect`) in My Fav and leaving it takes them out (`rate_album_favs`; stock's `0xf00a` add skips those already there), each told to the server as a like (`catalogue_liked`), their stars left alone. ponytail: taking an album out takes every song, even one favorited on its own, as nothing records which were; an album made a favourite before albums liked their songs has no songs in My Fav until it is made one again. **Ratings → Albums** (after Loved) is `coverflow_rated`: `getAllAlbum`, `split`, the albums with hearts, on a Coverflow page scoped as an artist's (`RATED_ALBUMS`: no saved album, no Refresh, Return goes back) whose one card sorts by Rating (most first), Album (library order), Artist or Year (as Year Order, undated last), kept in `/mnt/data/ringnav-ratedsort`; the library's albums and Sort come back on close.

**Card copy.** `/mnt/data` isn't shared over USB, so the card keeps a plain copy for a computer, `/mnt/mmc/.ratings.tsv`: two comment lines naming the columns, then tab-separated `song`, stars, liked (1 for My Fav's, else 0), path and a CUE track's start; `album`, hearts, name, album artist and, for an album without one, its folder (`album_dir`). It is output only: nothing reads it back. With no `songtable` yet (no scan so far) it lists My Fav's alone. The tables hold hashes, so `ratings_copy_poll` (`power_poll`) walks `myfav`, then `songtable`, then a signed-in server's `servertable` (its catalogue attached as `cat`, whose songs' stars are kept under their row's `fileurl`) on its own SQLite connection, 64 rows a poll on the UI thread, and none within `RC_QUIET_MS` (1 s) of input. Stock's `libsqlite3` is serialized (`THREADSAFE=1`), and its shared connection waits up to 500 ms for a reader since playlist art (`stock_db_open`), but a worker holding a read lock longer could still make a UI-thread My Fav write fail; on the UI thread the two can't overlap. It fills each row into a record and takes `listen_key` and `album_id` from that, so the keys cannot drift from the ratings'. A pass starts `RC_WAIT_MS` (5 s) after a rating or favorite changes through Q2 Muse's own rows, at boot, when the card comes back (`logo_poll`), and after `library_gen` moves (a scan); a scan during a pass ends it, and it goes again after. The whole file is built in memory, and running out ends the pass unwritten. It is written through `blob_io` only if it differs, so a boot's pass normally leaves the card alone. Once the new one is written, a file with more lines is renamed `.ratings.tsv.1`, unless that has more still, so a lost table or half-built library can't take the only copy, and neither can a rating given and cleared after it. ponytail: a favorite changed through stock's own rows (batch selection, its queue delete) reaches the file at the next change or boot; a song or album in none of those tables (deleted from the card, or its server signed out) has only its hash, so it stays out of the file until it returns; so is a song rated from Folder but never scanned. A write that fails waits for the next change or boot. A rating with no row keeps a pass walking to the end of `songtable`, up to about 1000 UI passes at the 65,000-song limit, so the wait for quiet is all that keeps those pages from the wheel.

**Refused boot logo.** `logo_sync` keeps the size and modification time of the card file it refused in `/mnt/data/boot-logo.bad` (8 bytes through `blob_io`), and says nothing at a later mount while the file still matches; a good logo or none removes the record. A failed `stat` records nothing, so that file is reported each time. ponytail: the key is size + mtime, and FAT/exFAT time has 2 s steps, so a different bad file of the same size and time stays silent. The record is written on the sync thread before the toast shows, so a power cut or a missed 2 s toast in between leaves the file recorded as told; it is reported again only after the file changes or is removed for one mount. The write stays off the UI thread (an fsync there would stall it).

## Era

**Era** (Library, after Genre, `local_era`, a build-added copy of stock's `local_genre`) browses by decade, as Rio Karma's Year menu and Eversolo's Era do. `era_menu` runs one grouped query through `sqlite3_exec` on `/mnt/data/database.db`. Era connections use a 64-page SQLite cache and file-backed temporary sorting to reduce peak memory alongside the library records; the query includes the entire library. A query failure toasts "Years unavailable". The query groups: albums as Coverflow splits them (`ALBUM_GROUP`, now in `offsets.inc`), music only (`MUSIC_WHERE`), named (`album` not empty), each dated by its tracks' latest year (`ALBUM_YEAR`, shared with Coverflow's Year sort, taking the first four digits of full dates such as `20220510` and `2022-05-10`), then counted per `year/10*10` with `year > 0`. No decade opens the page on the empty state, "No Dated Albums Yet", "Albums need a year tag". `era_page` (runtime, `page_list`) has a 64 px row per decade, oldest first, titled "60s" to "90s" then "2000s" on, the album count under it. A row opens `era_albums_page`: **Play All**, **Shuffle**, then the decade's albums (`having release_year between N and N+9`, by year then name, then `ALBUM_GROUP`'s other two keys, `ERA_ORDER`, so two albums of one name and year keep one order), each with "Artist • 1989" under it (album artist, else artist). Only the groups of albums with a track dated in the decade (`TRACK_YEAR`, the per-track year `ALBUM_YEAR` takes the max of) are grouped, as an album's year is its latest track's: on the owner's library (9,199 server songs, 2026-11-24) host SQLite took the 60s from 17 to 6 ms and the 2010s from 20 to 17 ms. The rows (album, artist, year and one track's `fileurl`) are copied into `era.v`, sized from the decade's count, and freed when the page closes. The page makes Play All, Shuffle and the first `ERA_FIRST` (16) album rows as it opens, then `ERA_CHUNK` (96) more each UI pass on a timer (`era_rows_due`) until all are made; closing the page stops it, and the search bar's Centre makes the rest first (`era_rows_finish`), since its search reads the page's rows. Every row in the open's pass held the screen: the owner's 2010s (2,664 albums) was likely the UI pass of 2,076 ms his Q2 logged (2026-11-24), and in the pool emulator on that library the open was a pass of 402-560 ms, 247-372 ms of it the rows (four widgets each, the scrolling title label most of it) and 124-168 ms the query. Made a chunk a pass, the open is one pass of 131-181 ms (106-146 ms the query, 2-4 ms the rows), then about 27 passes of 30-66 ms, about 1.1 s, where an idle pass there is about 30 ms. The query still runs in the open's pass, about 0.4 s on a Q2. Scrolling the whole page costs 30-45 ms a pass either way. A failing albums query toasts "Years unavailable" too and opens no page, rather than an empty decade. An album's record is the album name's songs (`getMusicByAlbum` through `staged_music`), the one at that path, so it splits as Coverflow does. Decade and album rows carry the `list_into` chevron (`page_row_detail_into`). Center on an album opens `coverflow_goto_album` (its tracks alone, see [Artist Albums in Coverflow](#artist-view-and-go-to-album-in-coverflow)). Play All and Shuffle find the decade's songs in one query (`era_decade_songs`: the files of `ERA_SELECT`'s groups dated in the decade, joined on `ALBUM_GROUP`'s keys) and filter the library's music by those song-table IDs. Play All's query is ordered as the page (year, name, `ERA_ORDER`'s keys), each album by disc, track and path as `album_before` orders Coverflow's tracks, and each song takes its query place (the first, if the query gave it twice); it plays from the first song as a library queue (`0xf001`, as Coverflow's All albums). Shuffle is Shuffle Songs (`shuffle_play`, one-shot as ever) over them in the library's order. Two stock queries an album (`getMusicByAlbum`, then `coverflow_album_tracks`) took Play All's pass 1,392 ms for the 2010s in the emulator (1,234-1,330 ms the songs; the owner's Q2 had 4,792 and 4,507 ms passes after the decade's); the one query and the library load take 257-328 ms, its pass 319-410 ms. A missing first file toasts "Storage unavailable"; a failing query (either of the songs' two, or an album row's `getMusicByAlbum` count of -1) toasts "Years unavailable". ponytail: decades only (no year level, no cover view), and the album rows have no hold menu; a year page under the decade, the decade as a scoped Coverflow (`coverflow_rated`'s pattern) or an album route through `qm_record` are the upgrades.

## Song durations

`durations.c` owns one duration cache and one worker, shared by Cover Flow's song lists and Long Songs. The database keeps no length, so each file's is measured through stock's TagLib on the worker: `taglib_file_new` and `AudioProperties::length()`, vtable slot 3, as libtag_c's `taglib_audioproperties_length` calls it. An Ogg file whose header is oversized (`ogg_tags`) gets no length: TagLib would cost about four times the header. A pass starts two ways. Long Songs starts one at each open, whatever the switch, unless a complete pass already ran at this `library_gen` or every song already has a length. **Display → Cover Flow → Scan Song Durations** (`[Q2POD] SCANDURATIONS`, 0 by default) adds the other: `library_scan`, the hook every Update Local Music and Scan Folders runs through on stock's scan thread, ends by calling `durations_scanned`, which, with the switch on and the scan not stopped (`toolsGetUserStop`: Back, or `/mnt/data` full), marks a pass due. Nothing else starts one: not the switch, not boot, not a remount. Turning the switch off cancels a running pass (`pod_click`).

The pass doesn't run inline on the scan thread: `wait_scan` sets the done flag only when the hook returns, so Update Local Music's modal dialog, and the playback its init stopped, would stay up for the whole pass with nothing on it moving, minutes on a large library. So the UI's `durations_poll`, once `library_scanning()` is clear, takes the mark and reads the library's paths in one `sqlite3_exec`, on its own connection with Era's pragmas (`cache_size=64`, `temp_store=FILE`): `select fileurl from songtable where … MUSIC_WHERE …`, through `library_scope_query`. That happens inside the closing dialog's own loop (its 200 ms timer ticks twice after the done flag, then sleeps 2 s on the UI thread and closes it, about 2.4 s; the read holds the same thread, so the dialog can't close before it ends), so on a large library the dialog holds its last frame about a second longer while input queues, as Era's whole-library query does. Only paths are read, strdup'd into the jobs, never a whole-library `staged()` copy; any failure, or the 100,000-song cap, drops them all. Each job is seeded from the cache on the UI thread (`duration_find`). The worker starts, lowered as the cover loader is (`thread_lower(1)`: nice 19, idle I/O), at the first poll once `updatemusic_dialog` (Update Local Music's and Scan Folders') and `usbmode_page` are both gone: AWTK's nested loops quit newest first, so a toast opened under the closing dialog would take its quit, and USB mode's exit prompt asks for the scan before its page goes. Long Songs hands its own records instead, so its pass replaces an update's waiting jobs.

At that start, if a job has no length in the cache (a song new to it) and the worker is running, a 2 s `toast("Measuring song lengths…")` shows once, under `usable()`, no Shut Down? prompt (`g_poweroff_state`), no toast of ours up (`st.toasts`: a card app's "Playlists updated" follows the same dialog) and no touch in flight (`pointer_down`); failing any of them drops the message, never defers it, so no late pop-up meets a later page. The toast's own loop polls again and finds the pass running. No message at the end. ponytail: a song whose file went before any pass measured it stays without a length until an update drops its row: each update with the switch on shows the message, and the first Long Songs open after each power-on checks every song; edits in place are measured without the message.

The worker sorts the jobs by key and statx's each file (`ringnav_statx`: 64-bit size, mtime with nanoseconds). A job whose signature matches its seed keeps the seed, statted once; a new or changed file is measured, then statted again, and kept only if it didn't change meanwhile. A file that can't be statted, or changed during the read, keeps its seed, so a card gone under the worker (pulled, or a hand-over missed) changes nothing. CUE tracks of one file share one measure. The worker then builds the next cache from its jobs, every one with a length (0: TagLib couldn't read it), so a canceled pass loses nothing it measured, and any pass, canceled or complete, drops songs not among its jobs, and saves it there, off the UI thread, only when it differs: a changed record, or a different count. The jobs are the scoped library (`library_scope_query`, and Long Songs' `songs_unsorted`): with folder markers active the cache keeps only the visible songs, and widening the scope measures the rest again. The UI joins an exited worker in its next pass and swaps the table in; that is the only publish. ponytail: lengths show only when a pass ends, so a large library's first pass shows nothing new for as long as it runs; an open song list is a snapshot until reopened.

While a pass runs, `durations_poll` calls `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 0)`, as playlist art does, so Standby's `umount /mnt/mmc` never meets an open file; the screen still sleeps. `ringnav_usbmode` stops it (`durations_shutdown(0)`) before stock's USB storage page unmounts the card, and the poll cancels one while the USB page shows or a scan runs; that cancel only flags the worker, so a scan's fresh mark stays. ponytail: a clean end (`ringnav_clean_end`, `durations_shutdown(1)`) waits up to 5 s for the current TagLib call, one still running past it left to the kill, its pass unsaved; USB storage waits it out, as playlist art's stop does, the armed watchdog its bound. Cancelling is cooperative: Long Songs' Cancel, the switch, USB storage and a clean end set a flag the worker reads before each file.

`/mnt/data/ringnav-durations-v1` is the table itself: the 8-byte magic `Q2DUR2\0\0`, then 24-byte records `{FNV-1a 64 of the path, size, mtime, mtime nanoseconds, seconds}`, little-endian, ascending by key. A file of another magic or size, keys out of order or repeated, or a negative length is no cache; up to 100,000 records are read, and a library over 100,000 songs gets no pass (ponytail: the scan has had no song limit since V1.36). #347's first format (`Q2DUR1`) and Long Songs' old hash-only `ringnav-lengths` aren't read, so Long Songs measures every song once more after the update. Saves use `blob_io`'s temporary file, fsync and rename; a cache that exists but couldn't be read is never written over in that session, and a failed save keeps the new lengths in memory. ponytail: two paths sharing a 64-bit key (about 1e-10 across 47,000) share the first's length; the signature is size (mod 4 GiB) and mtime, so a file replaced by one of the same size and mtime keeps the old length, and the filesystem's mtime precision applies.

`duration_seconds` and `duration_text` are UI-thread cache lookups, no stat or TagLib. A CUE track with both ends is `end - start`; the last track is the file's length less its start, at least 0. `duration_text` is stock's `toolsTimeItoa`, whose formats `tools/ipod.py` rewrites without the leading zero (`3:45`, `1:02:05` from an hour, as Now Playing), empty for an unknown or unreadable length. Cover Flow's track list gives every row the 64-pixel detail height once any track has a length, the unknown ones' detail empty, since stock's layouter forces one `item_height` on every row.

## Long Songs

Long Songs lists the library's tracks over `LONG_SONG_S` (600 seconds), longest first, with artist and length, and the same queue and hold actions as other library lists. Each open runs the shared pass above over its own `staged()` copy of the library, whatever Scan Song Durations is, unless a complete pass already covered this `library_gen` or every song already has a length (so a restart walks nothing, except that a song whose file went before any pass measured it stays without a length until an update drops its row, so the first open after each power-on checks every song; edits in place with the switch off go unmeasured until an update's pass with it on), and shows "Measuring songs… n/N" over a Cancel row on a 250 ms timer. A running pass, Long Songs' own or an update's, is observed, never doubled. With Scan Song Durations off, closing the page stops the pass as Cancel does, keeping what was measured; on, the pass goes on. Cancel shows once the current file's read returns; the poll then joins and lists what is known.

## Scrobbling

The same listen also appends a line to `/mnt/mmc/.scrobbler.log`, the card's root, in Rockbox's AudioScrobbler portable-player 1.1 format, so any `.scrobbler.log` uploader can send it to Last.fm or ListenBrainz. A missing file (`access`) gets the `#AUDIOSCROBBLER/1.1`, `#TZ/UTC` and `#CLIENT/Q2 Muse` header first. Each line is artist, album, title, track number, the length in seconds, `L` (listened), the start time and an empty MusicBrainz ID, tab-separated, from the record's `REC_ARTIST`, `REC_ALBUM`, `REC_TITLE` (the tag's; without one, `REC_NAME`, the file name, less its extension) and `REC_TRACK` (left empty when 0); tabs and newlines in tags become spaces. The start time is `time()` less the seconds heard, UTC since the clock fix keeps the system clock in UTC. Artist, album and title are the player's parsed tags once it has parsed the track (`now_tag`, see [Now Playing](#now-playing-ipod)), so a folder's untagged records still log their tags, an `.m3u` opened from Folder included; a parsed title that is empty or stock's `(null)` falls back as above. A track with no artist, or a listen while the clock reads before 2020 (never set), is not logged, as scrobblers reject both. With `[SCROBBLE] ALBUM_ARTIST=1` in `.scrobble.ini` (`scrobble_flag`, read at each listen), the artist column is the album artist instead, when the song has one: the player's parsed one (`ID3_ALBUM_ARTIST`, `g_play_id3_info + 0x984`, which `player_get_id3info` parses through `toolsGetMusicInfo` for a folder play's track and copies from the record for any other queue's), else the record's (`REC_ALBUM_ARTIST`, `+0x24` `albumsonger`, which the song row callback `0x506428` fills for library rows; folder-queue records have none, and the player copies none for a CUE track). The log stays in the 1.1 format, so any uploader sends the same artist. With `[SCROBBLE] PERCENT=N` (1 to 100, `scrobble_value`, read when a play begins), a listen is logged once N% of the length less 2 s has been heard instead (`ls_sent`; a poll a second apart may never see the last second, so 100 still logs); play counts keep half or `LISTEN_MAX_S` (`ls_done`). Any other value keeps the default. A song in a card app's folder whose `q2app` holds `scrobble=0` is not logged (`addon_scrobbles`, read at each listen: no line and no `scrobble_auto` count), while its play still counts; a missing key or any other value logs as usual. ponytail: this goes by the song's folder, not by who queued it, so a song an app's `.m3u` or `local` row names outside its own `.<id>/` still logs. The file is only appended to, about 100 bytes a listen, by `scrobble_append` in `patch/scrobble.c` under the upload's lock. A listen the card can't take whole (a full card) is not logged: once the file is closed, which may still write the rest of the buffer, it is cut back to its old length (if that cut fails, the torn line stays), or removed if that listen started it (it would have no header). A torn line left there would spoil the next listen, and often the torn one too, as the next is appended straight after it.

With `[SCROBBLE] AUTO=1` (`scrobble_flag`), uploads also start by themselves (`scrobble_auto`, every UI loop pass). Each logged listen counts in RAM, with the time of the first since the last upload; once that first is `scrobble_auto_ms(listens)` old, `SA_MAX_MIN` (180) less `SA_STEP_MIN` (4) per listen, never under `SA_MIN_MIN` (60) minutes, it reads the setting and Wi-Fi (`get_wifisignal() > 0`, never turning it on) at most once a minute and starts `scrobble_start`'s thread, joined silently by the same pass: no toasts. Success, or Upload Scrobbles' success, clears the count; a failure tries again `SA_RETRY_MIN` (30) minutes on. Listens from before the boot, or logged while an upload runs, are not counted, so the loop never reads the card for them; they stay in the log and go with the next upload. None starts while USB mode's page is open (a computer has the card). ponytail: one already uploading when the cable goes in still reads and rewrites the log, a window at a time, until it ends, and a window it can no longer read ends it as a success; `ringnav_usbmode` could join it if that ever bites.

**Upload Scrobbles** (Local Music, index 2, after Most Played, with a build-added copy of stock's 52 px `wifiset_wifi` as `local_scrobble`) is created only when `/mnt/mmc/.scrobble.ini`, read with `toolsReadConfig`, has `[LISTENBRAINZ] TOKEN` or `[LASTFM] API_KEY` and `API_SECRET` with either `SESSION_KEY` or both `USER` and `PASSWORD`. A press with `get_wifisignal` (`0x5190d8`, the status bar's bars, -1 unless connected) at 0 or below says "Connect to Wi-Fi first". Otherwise `scrobble_start` reads the accounts again and starts one pthread, and a 500 ms timer (`upload_wait`) polls it and joins it, then toasts the count sent, "Nothing to upload" or "Upload failed, N sent". The thread reads the log a megabyte (`LOG_HEAD`) at a time, takes complete lines in batches of 50 (Last.fm's limit) and skips comments, lines over 2,560 bytes (`LINE_BYTES`: Rockbox's Last.fm Scrobbler plugin writes the same log on this card, with tags from its 2,168-byte ID3 buffer, a title from the file name, and the numbers; 50 such lines fit the 384 KB body URL-encoded), lines not rated `L` and lines without artist, title or a time of 1-10 digits (a damaged time field would go raw into the ListenBrainz JSON and Last.fm's form and spoil the batch; such a line leaves with the junk). It sends a batch through demo's own libcurl imports: ListenBrainz `submit-listens` as `import` JSON with `Authorization: Token`, and Last.fm `track.scrobble`, form-encoded and signed (`api_sig`, the MD5, from demo's libcrypto `MD5_*` imports, of the sorted names and values followed by the secret), with the file's `SESSION_KEY`, or without one a session key from `auth.getMobileSession` fetched once per upload, before the first batch: the one call that carries the password. `tools/lastfm_key.py` makes that call on a computer and writes the key over the file's `PASSWORD` line (or asks for a password the file doesn't hold), so the card needn't carry the password: Last.fm's keys don't expire, only sign API calls, and are withdrawn under the account's Settings → Applications. It takes every `PASSWORD` line out of `[LASTFM]`, shows neither the password nor the key, and writes the new file whole beside the old one (`.scrobble.ini.tmp`, mode 0600 where the filesystem has modes, synced) before renaming it over it, so a failure leaves the old file and no copy of the key. It does not wipe a password the card has held from the card's free space. A key in the file is used even beside a password, and one Last.fm refuses fails the upload as any refusal does; the password is not tried in its place. A batch counts as sent only when every configured service answered 200 (and Last.fm's reply has no `error`). The first failure stops the upload. A service that took a batch the other refused gets it again next time. Then, under the lock, the bytes of every sent batch go to `.scrobbler.log.sent` (comments dropped) and the log is rewritten, to a `.tmp` then renamed, as the header plus what follows them, copied through in 4 KB pieces. Listens appended during the upload are therefore kept. Skipped lines leave with the sent ones, so one over-long line never blocks the uploads after it. Only one window of the log is held at a time: each is retired before the next is read, until a window comes back short, so one press sends the whole log and its count is every window's. The line cut at the megabyte waits for the next window, unless that unfinished part is over 2,560 bytes, when it is junk and goes too. ponytail: each pass rewrites the rest of the log under the lock, so card writes grow with the square of the backlog (a 3 MB log writes about 3 MB extra, a 10 MB log about 45 MB); carrying an offset across windows and rewriting once would remove it. Uploads always enable `SSL_VERIFYPEER` and `SSL_VERIFYHOST`; `/etc/scrobble-ca.pem`, packaged in the firmware, supplies `CAINFO` because stock has no CA bundle; no certificate file is required on the card. It contains the ListenBrainz and Last.fm trust roots from [Mozilla’s CA store converted by curl](https://curl.se/docs/caextract.html) (MPL-2.0), checked against both services when updated. Archive writes must flush and sync successfully before pending listens are removed, and storage failures are reported to the UI.

## Battery

The kernel has no cpufreq core (no governor to set) and stays stock; six rootfs drains change instead.

PEQ's steady bypass skips its sample loop; the filter still requests float PCM, so bypass doesn't remove every format conversion in the player. ponytail: the format is picked once per track, at the filter's `af_reinit` (`control(0x10000100)`, from `af_add` at each file load); nothing on our side reinits mid-track, so a native-PCM bypass would leave EQ and the outgoing crossfade dead until the next track. Native bypass needs a mid-track reinit (re-sending stock's EQ-on, unverified) or int PCM converted in `play()` (needs the vendor's format codes and stock's rounding); the filter is only in the chain once EQ, Crossfade, Mono Audio or AirPlay has been used.

- **drop_caches.** `check_mem_thd` (`0x51cd00`, started by `platform_init`) writes `3` to `/proc/sys/vm/drop_caches` every sixth second for the life of the player, throwing away the page, dentry and inode caches: the library database, the card's directories, the playing file's readahead and squashfs assets are read again. `toolsGetSysMemFree` has no callers, so nothing depends on it. Its first two words become `jr $ra; move $v0,$zero` (`DROP_CACHES` in `tools/build.py`), so the thread exits as soon as it starts: no write, and no one-second wake. `platform_init` detaches it and nothing joins it.
