- **UI loop.** `main_loop_sleep_default` sleeps at most 8 ms (its expected-sleep argument can only shorten that), so AWTK's loop runs at 125 Hz, screen on or off. `ringnav_sleep` first idles the loop while `g_backlight_status` is clear: `SCREEN_OFF_SLEEP_MS` (100 ms, `patch/offsets.inc`); stock then finds its 8 ms gone, sleeps 0 and updates its own timestamps. Once nothing plays (`media_playing`: local, Spotify, radio or video; no AirPlay or Bluetooth receiver) and `check_dacoff_state` has powered the DAC off (`g_dacoff_time` -1, about 31 s after playback stops), it idles `DARK_IDLE_SLEEP_MS` (250 ms) instead: a Q2 left dark without Standby otherwise keeps waking both cores for nothing. For `WAKE_MS` after a dropped Wake press the pass stays at 100 ms, so the second press is timed as before. A wheel turn keeps stock's pace: for `DARK_TURN_MS` (500 ms) after a wheel tick passes `tick_gate` (`st.tick_at`; before stock's lock filter, so a tick Buttons Lock then drops counts too) a dark pass idles neither. The loop dispatches every queued event before it idles again, so an idling pass that slept through a turn handed the volume every tick at once: it moved in jumps and Key Tone clicked in bursts, two clicks 16 ms apart wherever the first tick, loading the volume dialog, outlasted its own click (#303; in a tester's recording a dark turn's clicks sat on a 110 to 130 ms grid, singles and pairs, and the lit turn's followed the thumb, one a step). With the screen on, once `IDLE_MS` (2 s) pass without input (`ringnav_input` times every event) or a window animation, each pass idles `IDLE_SLEEP_MS` (25 ms). Each of these idles is a `poll()` that any input ends at once, and each may run longer when nothing needs the loop sooner: [The UI loop's wait](#the-ui-loops-wait).
- **the player's loops.** `q2player`'s threads wait on condition variables (`player/engine.c`, `player/ipc.c`): stopped or paused, nothing wakes it but a command, and demo's status queries, about one a second with the [push](#player-status-push), wake only the command thread that answers them (phase 6 measures it on a device: [player-plan: Parity checklist](player-plan.md#parity-checklist) row 62).
- **Player scheduling.** `on_wm_idle_status`, stock's idle callback, runs every UI pass and calls `player_mainscheduling` (`0x51f958`), whose `mclAutoChange` (with Gapless on and the player connected) asks hciplayer for `player-status` and waits for the answer on the UI thread: 40 round trips a second on an idle lit screen, up to 125 while it animates, each waking demo's reply thread and hciplayer's command thread, and 12% of the UI thread's samples asleep waiting. `MAINSCHEDULING_CALL` in `tools/build.py` turns its `jalr $t9` (`0x4f42a4`) into `jal ringnav_mainscheduling`, which runs it every `MAINSCHEDULING_MS` (100 ms), or every `DARK_POLL_US` while `dark_slow`, as the status sync below, or on q2player's [push](#player-status-push). A lyric line and the play-state notifications follow within that. From a second before the playing track's end (`player_playtime_and_length`'s cached times, a CUE track's own end, no round trip) until `MAINSCHEDULING_END_MS` after, it runs every pass as stock did, so a change without Gapless (`mclAutoChange` → `mclNextSong`), a CUE track's change, a folder's rollover and Now Playing's new track are not delayed; paused there it stays paced. Gapless changes are hciplayer's own. ponytail: a length that overstates the audio (a VBR MP3 without a Xing header) ends outside the window, up to 100 ms late (a second dark); `mclAutoChange`'s own end flag would catch it.
- **Player polls dark.** With the screen off, `ringnav_sleep` sets `dark_slow` (`dark_slow_ok`), and the two polls above, stock's status sync and the scheduling, run a second apart instead of 5 and 10 times a second: always once dark and quiet, and while the local player plays or is paused too, since only the screen reads its position closely, unless something else follows it. They keep stock's pace for the playing track's last `DARK_END_LEAD_S` (10 s, by the cached position) and until `MAINSCHEDULING_END_MS` after its end, or while playing with no length or position to go by (`player_quick`, set by `ringnav_mainscheduling` each pass): `mclAutoChange`'s Gapless preload (under 6 s from the end) and a change without Gapless see what they saw lit, and so do Crossfade's next track, the sleep timer's end (`addon.c` `sleep_check`, which counts `auto_nexts` too) and Download Ahead's `.ahead`, which follows the change. They keep it while A-B Repeat loops (`REPEAT_INFO` on and both points set: `check_abrepeatmode` seeks back to A from the cached position and waits for the cache to arrive there), while Car Remote is on (the phone shows the position, `coda_rc_shim.c` `cr_now`), and for another player (AirPlay, the Bluetooth receiver, a video). Headset and screen-off keys need neither pace: `mclSetPause` and `mclSetResume` write the status word themselves. Dark the cached second is up to a second older: Resume's place, a card app's `.now` and the listen count see the position that much later (a step of up to 3 s counts as heard, `resume_poll`), and a pause's second settles a poll later. ponytail: lit again, the status thread finishes its long sleep first, so Now Playing's time and a lyric line can lag up to a second at wake.
- <a id="player-status-push"></a>**Player status push.** Lit, or dark while something follows the position, the two polls would still ask 15 times a second with nothing changing (paused, or between two of the position's seconds). `q2player` sends a one-byte datagram to `/tmp/q2player.push` each time what `player-status` or `media-info` would answer changes (the state, the song's details, the position's whole second) and after each event it sends, a song's `exit` or an `error` (`player/ipc.c` `ipc_status_note`, `ipc_event`), since stock reads those events through the status poll. demo binds that socket on the UI pass's first look (`patch/player_push.c`), and while nothing follows the position more closely (`nothing_follows`: none of `player_quick`, A-B Repeat's loop, another player) the two polls wait on it (`push_pace`): the status thread sleeps in `poll()` on the socket for up to `DARK_POLL_US`, never asking sooner than stock's own 200 ms after its last ask, and `ringnav_mainscheduling` runs on the pass after the status thread took a push, not sooner than `MAINSCHEDULING_MS` after its last run, else `DARK_POLL_US` after it. Paused with nothing moving each asks once a second; playing, once a second as the second turns, so Now Playing's time and a lyric line follow the second's turn closer than the 200 ms poll did. Car Remote needs no stock pace here, as the push brings each second. Without the socket (the kernel refused it, the bind failed) both keep stock's pace; a push lost (demo not yet bound, the player restarted) costs at most `DARK_POLL_US`. Dark, `dark_slow` keeps its blind second.
- **Stock pollers.** `mclSyncPlayerStatus`' 200 ms loop sleeps through `ringnav_dark_usleep`: at least `DARK_POLL_US` (1 s) while the pass sets `dark_slow`, until q2player's push while `push_pace`, as above. `parse_albumcovertask_thd`'s 50 ms and `player_parsecover_thd`'s 100 ms waits park until a cover is asked for, lit or dark ([Cover threads](#cover-threads)).
- **Battery reads dark.** The status bar's one-second timer (`systembar_showface`, hooked as `ringnav_showface`) calls `get_battery_capacity` (`0x4ff258`), which reads three sysfs files every second, lit or dark: the CW2015 gauge's level and voltage (`toolsGetBatterycapacity`, `toolsGetBatteryVoltage`) and the AXP2101's battery status (`toolsGetChargeStatus`), storing them in `g_power_capacity`, an unnamed voltage word (`0x9b3208`) and `g_power_chargestate`, and then reads the cable (`usb_detect`, PD17) into `g_usbdet_value`. Its three read calls are `jal` to `ringnav_batt_level`, `ringnav_batt_voltage` and `ringnav_batt_status` (`BATTERY_READS` in `tools/build.py`, `patch/system.c`): with the screen off, on battery, they read at most every `BATT_DARK_MS` (30 s) and hand stock the last values in between, which it stores again unchanged. The gauge has no interrupt and no power-supply registration (`cw2015_driver.ko`), and the level moves about 1% a minute at most. Stock's second is kept lit; whenever the cable is in or the status is charging or full, so Charge Limit's `charge_poll` sees the level within its own `CHARGE_POLL_MS` and the OTG host's charger-off guard (`usb_charge.c`) is untouched; on the first pass after `g_usbdet_value` changed (it is written after the reads, so a plug-in is read the second after, an unplug twice); and below `BATT_DARK_FLOOR` (20%), where `check_lowbattery_state` counts five low-voltage seconds (under 3401 mV) to its power-off and warns under 16%. The cable's read stays stock's, every second, and so does anything that calls `get_battery_capacity` on a cable edge: the battery is read the pass after, by the flag's change. Charging stays a read: the stock kernel's AXP2101 charger driver has interrupt handlers that call `power_supply_changed` (`axp210x_irq_handler_usb_in`, `_usb_out`, `axp210x_irq_handler_thread`, which would send a `KOBJ_CHANGE` uevent through `power_supply_changed_work`), but `axp2101_charger_probe` requests no interrupt and nothing references them (symbols from the kernel's kallsyms, `vmlinux-to-elf` on `recovery-update/xImage`); its battery work (`battery_chk_online`, every 50 jiffies) calls `power_supply_changed` only on some of its paths. Whether a uevent comes at a charge start or end is for a device to show: a `NETLINK_KOBJECT_UEVENT` listener (`udevadm monitor --kernel` or a socket bound to group 1) while the cable goes in and out and the charge ends. ponytail: dark on battery, a new level reaches Battery History up to `BATT_DARK_MS` late, and a wake shows a level that old until the next second's read.
- **Painting.** Stock's screen-off (`screen_action`, `0x501f64`, with 0) turns the backlight off and blanks the framebuffer (`disable_fb`, `0x4fe2fc`), but nothing in the UI loop reads `g_backlight_status`: `main_loop_simple`'s step paints every pass (`window_manager_paint` at `0x69e828`), and Now Playing's 250 ms timer (`0x53d810`) runs its page update (`0x53cf08`) whatever the screen. So a Q2 left dark on Now Playing kept drawing its times and bar into a blanked framebuffer. `ringnav_wm_paint` returns `RET_OK` without painting while the backlight is off, unless a window animation runs (`window_manager_is_animating`): AWTK steps it from the paint, so it would otherwise wait for the screen. Invalidated regions keep, and the first lit pass repaints the whole screen as above.
- **Wi-Fi power save.** The RTL8733BS driver loads with Leisure Power Save on (`rtw_power_mgnt` 2, `PS_MODE_MAX`, in the module's `.data`), but once Wi-Fi connects, `network_checkstatus` (from home's 500 ms timer) runs `rtwpriv wlan0 pm_set lps=0` (`0x519084`) and nothing turns it on again: the radio stays awake for the whole connection. The build makes that `lps=2` (`WIFI_LPS` in `tools/build.py`, the byte at file offset `0x37133d`), which the driver applies at its next 2 s watchdog. That alone would keep little: `networkGetWifiSignal` (`0x5c25d8`), which the status bar (`get_wifisignal`) and the network monitor thread (a `bal`) each call about once a second, asks with `SIOCGIWSTATS`, which the driver answers through `get_station`, whose TX report (`rtw_get_sta_tx_stat`) leaves LPS every time; only the watchdog enters it again. So `ringnav_wifi_signal` takes the function's entry and reads `signal_strength` from `/proc/net/rtl8733bs/wlan0/rx_signal` instead, at most every `WIFI_SIGNAL_MS` (1 s): the same percentage `get_station` reports less 100 as dBm, from a read that touches no hardware. The one difference is 100%, 0 dBm, which stock's unsigned level wrapped to -256 (one bar) and is 0 here (four). Unreadable, it is 0, as stock's failed ioctl. While Bluetooth A2DP streams with Wi-Fi on 2.4 GHz, the driver's coexistence keeps LPS off anyway (its PS-TDMA cases on this chip force it). Why Shanling turned LPS off is unknown.
- **Watchdog.** `platform_init` starts `checkappprocess.sh`, which forks `pgrep` every 2 s and reboots if `demo` is gone. Its `sleep 2` becomes `sleep 10` (`WATCHDOG` in `tools/build.py`), so a crashed player reboots within 10 s.

### The UI loop's wait

`ringnav_sleep`'s idles (above: `IDLE_SLEEP_MS` lit, `SCREEN_OFF_SLEEP_MS` and `DARK_IDLE_SLEEP_MS` dark) are `loop_wait` (`patch/loop_wake.c`): a `poll()` on an eventfd (o32 `eventfd2` and `poll` through `lw_syscall`; demo imports neither) instead of `sleep_ms`, so whatever brings the UI work ends the idle at once, and `loop_span` lets an idle run longer while nothing needs a pass sooner. Without an eventfd (the kernel refused one, or a host test) it is the `sleep_ms` it replaces, the same length.

What ends the wait (`loop_wake`, from any thread: an 8-byte write): every event `ringnav_queue_event` queues, which is every key, wheel tick, touch and SyncLink key and every timer or idle another thread hands AWTK (`main_loop_queue_event` is the queue's one way in); the wheel's raw samples while the loop idles (`loop_wake_touch` in `wheel_sample`: Cover Flow's thumb and the selection bar's lean read that travel with no event); a headset key `headset_worker` queues; a BlueZ volume signal `bt_vol_event.c` counts; a USB cable's edge `usb_event.c` settles; and a Cover Flow half the loader has read. Everything else a pass picks up is read by a per-pass `*_poll` or a stock timer and rides the wait's bounds below: a worker thread's result, another process's file (q2guard's state, Car Remote's commands, Guest Play's), stock's globals (a Bluetooth link, the player's status).

How long (`loop_span`): never less than the idle it replaces, so a timer already due, or a suspended one, never makes the loop pass more often than before. Longer only when the loop has its eventfd and none of these holds: a timer of `LOOP_ANIM_MS` (50 ms) or less runs (a frame: `ui_kit.c`'s motion loop and the level bars at 33 ms, a marquee's or a spinner's step); the widget animator manager has an animator (its own timer runs every 8 ms whether or not, so it counts only then: `AM_FIRST`); more idles wait than the fewest seen (stock's `on_wm_idle_status` repeats every pass, so it is the floor; a new `idle_add` runs on the next pass); stock's key lockout counts down (`KEY_LOCKOUT`, which `on_wm_timer_setup_state` steps every 100 ms; the wheel's ticks wait on it). Window animations, input in the last `IDLE_MS` and Now Playing's motion already keep the loop at stock's pace before an idle starts. Lit, the idle then runs to the next AWTK timer due (the timer list walked at `TM_LIST`, a timer's start and period at `TIMER_START` and `TIMER_DURATION`), at most `LOOP_LIT_MAX_MS` (250 ms), and not past a pass that left the screen dirty (the top window's native window has dirty rects, `NW_DIRTY`, cleared by each paint's `native_window_clear_dirty_rect`: a poll changed a label after this pass painted). Stock's own 100 ms timer `on_wm_timer_setup_state` runs lit and dark, so a lit idle wait is at most about 100 ms in practice. Dark, stock's timers already ride the dark idle late (a 100 ms timer ran every 250 ms dark and quiet), so the wait does not follow them: it runs to `LOOP_DARK_MAX_MS` (1 s) while `dark_slow` holds (the player polls already run a second apart; not near a track's end, nor for A-B Repeat, Car Remote, Car Audio or another player), input has been still `IDLE_MS`, and no stock stream queue plays (`mclGetPlayType` 2, 3, `0xf1`, `0xf2`, whose network state stock's 500 ms `on_wm_timer_networkstatus` follows). Animations are untouched: a frame timer, an animator or a window animation keeps every idle at its old length, so their frames come as before.

Measured on pool emulator slot 1 (`BLUETOOTH=0`, Car Remote off except in the lit Home and dark idle baselines, whose pace it does not set, 60 s a state, demo's main thread's sleeps ended per second), `release/p32` at `9afab913` then this change: Home lit, a track paused, 45.5 to 28.4 (the loop's passes about 35 to 15 a second; the rest of the thread's wakes are its waits on stock's player locks); dark, idle, the DAC off, 5.1 to 2.1; dark and playing 11.0 to 6.2 (the emulator's 25 s tracks keep the player polls quick for their last 10 s); Now Playing lit and playing, 65.5 to 56.4, and a list lit with the level bars moving, 46.5 to 47.5, both at their frame timers' pace as before. A wheel tick to the framebuffer's change on lit, paused Home, from the input's write: median 9.3 ms (p90 10.8) after, 11.4 ms (p90 26.8) before. Frame gaps unchanged: the level bars on a list median 42.7 ms before, 42.9 after; bars and marquee median 36.5 ms before, 35.1 after (p90 53.2, 53.6); Home's art drift and a Centre press's row and page slide within run-to-run noise. ponytail: a source with no wake (a worker's result, q2guard, a Bluetooth link's end) is seen at most `LOOP_LIT_MAX_MS` late lit, which stock's 100 ms timer bounds to about 100 ms, and at most `LOOP_DARK_MAX_MS` dark and slow (headset disconnect's pause included); give such a source a `loop_wake` call where it lands if that shows.

### Cover threads

Stock's two art threads, started by `platform_init`, polled for work with nothing to do: `parse_albumcovertask_thd` (the Library's album grids, artist pages and folder rows) every 50 ms and `player_parsecover_thd` (Now Playing's art) every 100 ms, 30 wakeups a second on every lit screen. Each loop's only `usleep` (`COVER_WAITS` in `tools/build.py`) is a jal to `patch/cover_wake.c`: a thread with work keeps stock's pace between its tasks; one with none parks in a futex wait on a generation word of its own, `COVER_WAIT_S` (5 s) at most, and a request wakes it.

- **Now Playing's art.** The thread's work is the first byte of `g_play_cover_info`, the start flag. Only `player_set_coverinfo` sets it (`player_get_id3info` on a track change, `get_onlineid3info` through `tidal.c`'s `app_coverinfo`, and two stock page handlers at `0x52c7c8` and `0x5360f8`), and `player_get_coverinfo` clears it: those three are the only functions that reach the struct (its one GOT slot; no page-relative reference). `player_set_coverinfo` is hooked (`HOOKS`): `cover_set_info` runs stock's, then wakes the thread.
- **The Library's art.** The thread's work is `plist_albumtasklist` (a libcstl list, under `actasklist_mutex`) not empty while `albumcover_taskstate` is not 2 (a page scrolling pauses it), or a state of 3 to 6 (a cover cache to clear, then 0). About 35 stores to the state in 25 stock functions set it (a producer such as `local_albumcover_task` pushes its rows, then stores 1; a page's scroll stores 2 and its end the state it saved), with no one function to hook, so `ringnav_sleep` calls `cover_wake_poll` at the start of every UI pass: while the thread is parked and has work, it wakes it. A request made on the UI thread, as the pages' are, is seen in the pass that made it; one from another thread (`loadclasspthread`, a Tidal list) by the next pass.
- **No lost request.** The waker moves the generation before it reads `cover_parked`, and the thread marks itself parked before its last look at its work and waits only while the generation is the one it read first, so a request lands in that look or in a wake. ponytail: a request from another thread while the UI loop is stalled waits for the loop's next pass or the 5 s timeout.

Measured on a pool emulator (`BLUETOOTH=0`, 60 s a state, against the trunk at `d3f243fa`): the two threads' wakeups fell from 1,800 a minute to 24 (the timeout) on lit Home, Now Playing, Songs and Cover Flow scrolling, demo's from 7,857 to 6,019 on Home and 8,989 to 7,099 on Now Playing. Covers come sooner: Next to Now Playing's cover parsed 412 ms on average before, 323 after (12 changes each); Library > Albums' request to its first cover 181 ms, 151 after. Cover Flow loads its own art (`coverflow_loader.c`) and is unchanged.

### Charging

The status row's battery (`list_marks.c` `battery_slim`, from `navigation.c` `battery_now`'s key) fills to the level whatever the cable does; it once filled to the end while charging, which hid how much was left. Its fill is green while a cable charges it, with Phosphor's lightning (fill, 7 px, Text Primary) on the body's center and a 1 px gap in the Canvas cut round it where it crosses the fill (`tools/art.py` `inset_glyph`, `battbolt_d` and `_l`); green with an upright plug in the bolt's place (`plug_glyph`, drawn on whole pixels rather than from Phosphor, `battplug_d` and `_l`) on a cable that holds it full (`g_power_chargestate` 2) or at [Charge Limit](#charge-limit); white, or red under 20%, on a cable that charges nothing (USB DAC charging Off). The cable is `g_usbdet_value`, not stock's icon: `systembar_showface` picks `bar_charge` for a cable only while `g_power_chargestate` is not 2 (`0x541e2c`; at 2 it is `bar_battery`), and the plain icon over a USB DAC link with its charging Off (`g_usblink_status` 2, `g_usbmode` 1, `g_usbdac_chargeflag` 0), so a battery Full on the cable read as unplugged and was drawn white with no glyph (seen on a Q2 on 2026-11-17: status Full, 100%, VBUS in). `g_usbdet_value` is 0 while the Q2 is a USB host (`get_battery_capacity`), so its own bus power never counts. A charger too weak to keep up would make it orange with Phosphor's warning in the bolt's place (`battwarn_d`, `_l`), from `charging.c` `charge_weak`. ponytail: nothing reports that, so `charge_weak` is always 0 and the orange state is never reached. Searched: the kernel's AXP2101 driver (`axp2101-power-supply`; its strings name the battery's status, level, voltage, temperature and times to empty and full, and the BC1.2 detection enable `pmu_init_bc_en`, but no input current limit or charger type it reports), stock's `demo` (it reads only `battery/status` and `voltage_now`, plus the bq25890 paths of Shanling's other players) and these docs. A real signal, such as the PMIC's input-limit state or the battery's current going negative while it says Charging, would lift it; a guess from the level would not.

A tap on the battery toasts its state (`charging.c` `charge_tap`, from `status_row.c` `status_touch`, which takes `ringnav_input`'s pointer events turned upright from the panel's portrait axes: x is the event's y, y 319 less its x): a press inside a 44 x 40 px target round the body's center (the slot's, on Battery: Percent) (`SR_TAP_W`, `SR_TAP_H`; `status_slot_at`, in the bar's own pixels, the screen lit and `usable`; where it meets the level bars' target the nearer center has it) whose lift lands within `SR_TAP_SLOP` (12 px) of it and still on the same slot. The touch goes on to stock, so a pull down from the row still opens Control Center. The words come from the key the battery shows (`charge_words`): too weak, held at Charge Limit ("Charge Limit Reached (80%)", `CHARGE_STOP`), full, charging, under `BATT_LOW_PCT` (20%, where the fill turns red) "Low battery", else "Battery" and the level. The toast waits for the next UI loop pass (`charging_poll`, from `usb_ui_poll`), as the USB toasts do, and is `toast_icon`'s: 16 px each side, a 15 px glyph, 8 px before the words.

The cable's own feedback (`charging.c`, its look in [oled-design: Plug-in screen](oled-design.md#plug-in-screen)). `usb_ui_status` calls `charge_plugged` at every cable put in after its first pass (`det_known`): a cable already in at boot is no plug-in, as a plug-in screen then would turn the screen off under the boot. With the screen off (`g_backlight_status` clear; Buttons Lock is the dark screen's alone, so a locked Q2 is a dark one), the next UI loop pass (`charging_poll`, from `usb_ui_poll`, not stock's USB pass) lights it as `keylock.c`'s card does (painted first, then `enable_fb` and `screen_action(1)`) and paints the plug-in screen over the top window and the status bar (`charge_paint`, from `ringnav_paint`) for `S1_MS` (3 s), a frame every `S1_FRAME_MS` (50 ms), then turns the screen off again (`screen_action(0)`). Not while a video or a card game has the screen. A key or a touch while it shows (`charge_gate`, in `ringnav_input` after Buttons Lock's) ends it with the screen left on and is dropped down to its release; a window opening over it (the chooser for a computer, `awake_screen`) ends it the same way, so the screen stays on for that. Its level is `g_power_capacity` at the plug-in. With the screen on there is no screen: `usb_charger_in` (a cable no computer answered within `USB_PROBE_MS`, or a remembered Charge Only) toasts the battery's state as a tap would (T1, "Charging · 62%"); a computer gets the chooser instead. `system.c`'s `charge_poll` toasts "Charged to 80%" (`charge_limited`, T3) when Charge Limit first holds charging off on a cable, and `charging_poll` toasts "Charger too weak" (T6) when `charge_weak` turns 1 on a cable, which nothing does yet. Unplugged (T2), OK to Disconnect (T4) and USB Audio Ready (T5) are [USB pages](#usb-pages)' (`usb_ui.c`). Every one waits for the next pass (`feedback.c` `toast_later`, shown by `toast_later_poll` from `usb_ui_poll`; the last asked for wins) and shows only with the screen on.

A cable in also chirps in the headphones (`charge_plugged` → `clicker.c` `clicker_chirp`): `{mcl-click\charge}` on the player's socket, which q2player mixes into what it plays as it mixes the Clicker's clicks ([player-plan: The Clicker](player-plan.md#the-clicker)), a 340 ms tick and two rising blips. The Q2 has no speaker but the MCU's buzzer, which can only click, so the chirp is never the buzzer's. It is sent under Clicker Headphones or Both, and only while q2player plays a song (`player_mixes`); paused, stopped or on the stock hciplayer there is none: q2player's PCM is closed then, and hciplayer keeps its PCM (`hw:1,0`, no `dmix`) open and muted while paused and mixes nothing while it plays ([Key Tone](#key-tone)), so a sound of its own would have to open the device under the player or stop it. Mixing while it plays and skipping otherwise disturbs nothing.

## ALSA startup lock

The stock ALSA 1.1.6 library can deadlock with an ioplug behind `plug`. Preparation locks the wrapper while the ioplug callback unlocks and relocks its slave, leaving a slave mutex owned by the setup thread, so the writer blocks at its first write. `q2video` sets `LIBASOUND_THREAD_SAFE=0` in its own process before opening ALSA. Its PCM calls are sequential: setup precedes the writer, and drop, prepare and close follow joining it. BlueALSA's locks, the local player, the codecs and the services are unchanged.

To reproduce the old hang and verify the fix against the stock MIPS library, run `python3 test/alsa.py BUILD QEMU_MIPSEL`. The regression covers one and two plug layers and rate conversion.

## Audio writes and the queue checkpoint

The shared audio writer keeps partial ALSA writes and retries the remaining frames after an underrun, instead of discarding unwritten samples. Native tests exercise partial writes, zero progress, recovery and lost outputs. This is independent of the ALSA startup lock workaround.

Queue and traversal changes commit the full queue snapshot, for queues up to `SAVE_LIMIT` (999) tracks; a larger one keeps no snapshot (it would be rewritten whole on every track change), so a reboot resumes it as stock does, and its file is emptied once (`queue_drop`), not again at each save. `ringnav_memory` reads none larger either, so a damaged header asks for no more memory than a real snapshot takes (about 1 MB; `QUEUE_LIMIT`'s would be 68 MB). Version 3 snapshots carry Play Next's pending list after the history (count, then indices). Stock Shuffle on a local queue is Shuffle Songs here ([Queue menu](#queue-menu)), so its snapshot is version 3 too: the order and the next pass, what this pass has played, the history (the rows Up Next lists above the playing song) and Play Next's list, so after a restart the queue opens on the same song with the same songs below and above it; a version 4 snapshot restored under Shuffle (one saved before) is given a new order on the first UI pass, the restored song first. A version 2 file, written before the list existed, restores its one run (`forced`, `force_end` in its header) as the list, in order; the next save writes version 3. Without advanced play a local queue (folder, `MCL_TYPE` 1, or library, `0xfxxx`; not AirPlay) is kept too, while Memory Playback or car mode is on (the only readers; off, the save returns without touching the file, and one left from before is rewritten within 5 s of the setting coming back on, as the queue's hash no longer matches `saved_queue`, or at power-off), as a version 4 snapshot: version 3's layout with the queue's own order twice, nothing seen, no history or Play Next list, the cursor at the track. `ringnav_memory` loads it without `rebuild`, so it comes back as it was, still without advanced play; stock's Memory Playback record could only rebuild a queue from its class and source album or folder, so a queue grown with Play Next or Add to Queue came back as the whole library at the same track. Play Next and Add to Queue mark it dirty; stock's own edits (View Queue's delete) are seen by hashing the whole queue (`queue_hash`, `saved_queue`) each save, at most every 5 s and every 30 s while playing on, after the `SAVE_LIMIT` check. An empty queue saves nothing, so the UI loop's first passes at boot don't drop the snapshot before Home restores it, and nor does a position outside the queue. The snapshot and its checkpoint are on the card, `.q2pod/ringnav-queue` and `ringnav-queue-elapsed` ([Where Q2 Muse writes](#where-q2-muse-writes)): a queue's songs are there too. Every write of the three records is [the queue writer](#the-queue-writer)'s, on its own thread: `playback_save` builds a record on the UI thread and posts it. With the card away a save is kept in RAM (a snapshot up to `QUEUE_HELD_MAX`, 256 KB; a larger one fails and is retried as below) and posted for writing at the next poll that finds the card; a dropped snapshot leaves the card's file empty, which reads as none, so the flash's `/mnt/data/ringnav-queue` from earlier releases, read and copied to the card once while the card has none, is not restored again. Elapsed-only changes atomically replace the 16-byte `ringnav-queue-elapsed` checkpoint, which applies only when it matches the snapshot's checksum and position. The UI loop posts it every 30 s while the same track plays on and within 5 s of a pause, seek or track change, and retries a failed write every 30 s (a full snapshot rebuilt and synced each time, so a failing card isn't hammered every 5 s); power-off (`ringnav_savequeue`) writes the exact second. A crash mid-track resumes up to 30 s early. The progress check itself runs at most every five seconds (`playback.poll_stamp`), so UI passes between checkpoints do not repeatedly take the playback-time mutex.

**Reboots.** Stock writes Memory Playback's record (`save_memoryplay_info`, `0x521058`: play class, track, second and the album or folder the queue came from, through `write_memory_to_file`) only from `into_poweroff`, the power-off page's. `device_reboot` (`0x502004`: Power's Restart, a long power-key press on the power-off page, and `on_wm_idle_status`'s Bluetooth recovery) and the firmware update never call it, so after a TF card update or Network Update the Q2 resumed the queue and second of the last power-off, however long ago. Both now save first (`ringnav_reboot` and `ringnav_checkfw` in `patch/playback.c`), through the hooked `save_memoryplay_info`, so the snapshot's exact second is written too. The update saves when its dialog opens (`dialog_checkfw_dialog_init`, `0x49982c`, after stock's confirmation, both rows'), since that init stops the player before its thread (`0x499548`) runs `update_firmware` and the countdown's `device_reboot`. A stopped player (`mclGetPlayStatus` 1) saves nothing, as stock's save skips it, so that later `device_reboot` leaves the saved place alone and the snapshot keeps its second. The update's flash then takes about a minute with the UI loop running and the player stopped, and those passes would write the stopped player's 0 over the saved second, so every boot after an update started the song at 0:00 (Memory Playback: Location; a crash, which keeps the last 30 s checkpoint, resumed at its second): `ringnav_checkfw` sets `going_down` after its save and `playback_save` writes nothing while it is set and the player is stopped; the dialog closing without the reboot (stock's answer: no file, the same version, a bad tar) clears it (`sw_update.c` `sw_dialog_gone`). `q2update install` over adb runs the same dialog ([adb](adb.md#installing-an-update-over-adb)). `test/fw/test_playback.py` `test_an_update_keeps_the_second_while_it_flashes` (playing or paused at 90 s, the stopped player's -1 or 0: the boot resumes at 90, and a streamed queue's app is asked for 90; it failed before, the checkpoint 0) and `test_an_update_that_does_not_restart_lets_the_saves_go_on`. When the reboot is stock's Bluetooth recovery (`bt_initstatus` -102), `ringnav_reboot` first leaves `q2-crash.log` ([Bluetooth boot reconnect](#bluetooth-boot-reconnect)).

## Shuffle order

Stock Shuffle on a local queue plays an order the payload owns (`shuffle_own`, `playback_shuffle` in `patch/playback.c`; what lists and walks it is in [Queue menu](#queue-menu)). This section is what the order is made of and what each Shuffle action costs, as `test/fw/test_shuffle_order.py` and `test/playback.py`'s `LibraryMachine` checks hold it.

**The tables.** `order` is the pass being played, the queue's indices in play order at 2 bytes each (`qix`, `QUEUE_LIMIT`'s range), `cursor` the place of the song playing. `mark` is 2 bytes a queue entry: bit 0 says it has played this pass, the 15 bits above are its identity (`rec_id`), by which `follow_queue` tells which entries a stock edit took out. `history` is the last 4,096 songs played, 16 KB whatever the queue's size, the rows Up Next lists above the playing one and Previous walks. Shuffle Songs holds nothing else: 4 bytes a song. Its next pass (`cycle`) is drawn only when something reads past the end of this one (`next_pass`: a listing longer than what is left of the pass, a save of a queue short enough to save, or the pass's end), 2 bytes a song more until the pass wraps, when it is copied over `order` and let go (`pass_wrap`). The album or folder of each entry (`groups`, 4 bytes) is kept only while a mode reads it (`groups_wanted`: Shuffle Albums and Folders, a shuffle within them, a repeat of one), sorted then by `group_table` with 12 bytes a song of working rows freed at the end of `rebuild`; Shuffle Songs under Folder Skip sorts them at the first skip (`playback_group_skip`).

**Turning Shuffle on** is one UI pass (`playback_poll`, `shuffle_own`, `rebuild(0)`): four allocations, one look at each queue row for its identity (a library row's id, disc, track and CUE start, read from the record; a row with no library id, a folder's or a card app's download, by its path's length and last 24 bytes), and a Fisher-Yates draw over the indices (`make_order`), which is uniform over every order and needs no sort, no album and no second look at a record. The song playing then moves to the front, the rest closing up behind it in their drawn sequence, and it starts the history. `rand_below`'s generator (xorshift32) is seeded once from stock's and the tick clock and runs on from one draw to the next, so each turn-on is another order. On 9,198 songs that is 9,203 stock calls (`deque_at`, one a row) and, in payload instructions under Unicorn, about 100 a song with library ids and 590 without; `test/playback.py` bounds it at 150 and 700 a song and fails if an album comparison runs. A grouped mode's sort of the same queue into albums (`group_table`) is 18 million instructions more, with 36,105 `strcasecmp`, which is why Shuffle Songs keeps no groups ([inefficiencies](inefficiencies.md#36-shuffle-sorted-the-queue-into-albums-and-saved-it-on-the-ui-thread-resolved) has the measurements). Nothing is written in that pass ([the queue writer](#the-queue-writer)).

**Turning it off** frees the tables (`ringnav_mode`, `playback_clear`). The queue itself is never reordered, so its own order is there at once, whatever its size.

**Next and Previous** cost the same at any size: `commit` finds the next song a step after the cursor, and `cursor_to` finds the song Previous goes back to by looking outwards from the cursor, where it is a step away (about 430 and 180 payload instructions, at 64 songs and at 9,198, at the pass's start and 3,000 songs in). A pass's end costs one draw.

**An edit** (Play Next of songs, Add to Queue, Remove from Queue, a stock delete) keeps the pass's sequence (`pass_keep`): the identities are read again, the indices renumbered, and songs new to the queue stand last in this pass, in queue order, and somewhere in the next one if it is drawn. Up Next's Play Next of a queued row (`playback_move`) only changes Playing Next's list. Remove from Queue on 9,198 songs is 4.6 million payload instructions.

**The car's listing.** `coda_rc_shim.c` `cr_queue` lists up to 5,000 rows of the order, each asked whether it can play. It walks them again only when `playback_stamp` (which moves with the order, the cursor, the history and Playing Next), the song or the queue has moved, or `CR_FILES_MS` (5 s) on, as a server row coming or going changes what plays next and moves none of those; between, a poll's part of this (every `CR_POLL_MS`) is a few compares. A walk is 575,000 payload instructions and 15,000 stock calls on 9,198 songs.

**Shuffle Songs in steps.** Home's and the Library's Shuffle Songs reads every song from the library and loads them as the queue, both stock's and both a few hundred instructions a song and several allocations: seconds on a large library, which a loading indicator has to cover. `patch/library_lists.c` gives it three calls, each to be made on the UI thread: `shuffle_songs_start()` takes the request and does nothing else; `shuffle_songs_poll()` does the next step, one a call, first the read of the library (`songs_unsorted`), then the play (`shuffle_play`: the mode, the queue's load, the start of the first song and the order), and returns 1 once no step is left, 0 before; `shuffle_songs_cancel()` lets the songs read go. Until the play's step nothing the user hears or sees has changed, so a cancel before it leaves everything as it was; the play's step cannot be undone. A caller shows its indicator, lets a UI pass draw it, and calls the poll once a pass until it returns 1. `shuffle_songs` itself, the rows' handler, runs every step at once.

## The queue writer

The queue's three records (`.q2pod/ringnav-queue`, `ringnav-queue-elapsed`, `ringnav-queue-stream`; [Audio writes and the queue checkpoint](#audio-writes-and-the-queue-checkpoint)) are written whole, synced and renamed (`card_store.c`), which on a card busy with a download takes from tens of milliseconds to seconds. The UI thread makes none of those writes. `store_post` (`patch/playback.c`) takes a record (a heap block the writer frees), a drop or a flush for one of the three stores; the newest post for a store replaces one not yet written, except that a flush never replaces a record; and one detached thread at a time (`w_thread`) writes what is posted, in the stores' order, snapshot, tail, checkpoint, and ends when nothing is left. A post while it runs is taken by it; with no thread to be had the post writes on the caller's thread. A write the card refuses sets the store's bit in `w_failed`: the poster reads it back at once when the writer has already run, and otherwise `playback_poll` reads it on a later pass (`store_failures`) and marks the snapshot dirty and failed, which the 30 s retry then saves again. `store_drain` waits for the writer (up to 10 s) and then writes anything still posted itself: the restore calls it before it reads the files (`ringnav_memory`), and power-off and a reboot after their save (`ringnav_savequeue`), so the exact second is on the card before the power goes. Only the writer, or a caller after `store_drain`, touches the three `card_blob`s. A queue past `SAVE_LIMIT` posts one drop of its file (`queue_drop`), not one at every save.

## M4B recognition and audit

Stock has two audio extension checks: folder enumeration at `0x5d4cac` and recursive scanning at `0x5d69fc`. Both also feed playlist loading. `ringnav_audio_extension` accepts `.m4b` case-insensitively and otherwise calls the original `strstr` with its original format list. The builder asserts the original import load and call bytes before replacing each call; `audio_extension_calls` records both edits in the manifest and packaging audit. The installed TagLib already sends M4B to the MP4 constructor, and the decoder probes the original MP4 container. Neither needs a binary dispatch change. Cover extraction has a separate extension dispatcher in `libtag_c.so.2.0.1`, which stock recognizes as MP4 artwork only for M4A/MP4. `patch_m4b_cover` in `tools/build.py` checks the whole library hash and adds a case-insensitive M4B comparison that reaches the existing MP4 image extractor. Its 48-byte appended segment is read/execute only, uses relative branches and GP-relative data, and preserves the other formats. Now Playing retains stock’s external folder-cover fallback when embedded extraction fails; Coverflow retains its folder-image fallback. Files and paths are preserved. `test/m4b.py` executes the native metadata and cover dispatchers at two load addresses, while `test/patch.py` covers the patched checks, short-book persistence and shared resume/count exclusions.

## Headset controls and volume

`patch/headset.c` restores the AACP handshake and AVRCP input from `6799d59`, without the battery state or connection card. One generation-tagged worker uses nonblocking socket/input I/O and one `select` over both descriptors, up to 1 s a pass, so a still connection wakes it once a second. It rescans for the AVRCP input (the `/dev/input/event*` node whose name ends in ` (AVRCP)`, read to uinput's 79 characters with `EVIOCGNAME(80)`: a 64-byte read cut a long name before the mark, so a headset named past 55 characters never had its keys read) each pass for the first 10 passes, then every 2nd, and retries AACP every 5th. It drains the AACP socket each pass (AirPods send other reports between ear reports), validates complete ear packets, retries discovery throughout a connection, queues only key presses, and closes descriptors on disconnect. The UI loop discards stale generations and dispatches commands every 100 ms. No player API runs on the worker.

The internal dispatcher chooses video, radio, Spotify, then the stock local/Tidal player, independently of the visible page. Explicit play/pause operations and session identities support ear detection; the number of buds originally worn (counted, since the report's primary/secondary slots swap when the primary leaves an ear), a manual-command epoch and the player/session identity gate automatic resume. Recent AVRCP pauses are coordinated with ear reports, and duplicate commands are suppressed. Player starts, track changes, manual controls and disconnects invalidate pending resume. Video retains its commands and adds idempotent `a`/`r` pause/resume, an atomic pause-state file and a separate `g` gain command. Radio resumes the current station by restarting it.

Bluetooth output remembers `PLAYSET BT_VOLUME` independently of wired/USB's stock `PLAYSET VOLUME`. The `write_int_config` hook routes volume saves to the active output's key; the `mclSetOutputWay` hook saves the departing level and restores the incoming one before stock switches output, clamped to the volume limit (and to the device's Volume Limit, below), then applies it to the mixer. A missing or invalid saved level inherits the current volume. Stock boot volume behavior keeps the wired key. While receiving Bluetooth audio from a phone, the gear's Playback and its submenus accept normal wheel navigation; the receiver player and volume dialog keep stock volume control. A headset's own volume (its absolute volume, below) moves the Q2's on any page and with the screen off: [Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)'s rule is the wheel's alone. A headset's change shows at once with the screen lit, as a wheel's does (`vol_show`, `patch/volume.c`, from `bt_volume_poll`): the volume dialog in front takes the value and its 3 s start again (stock's close count, `VOL_DIALOG_COUNT`, zeroed as its own keyup zeroes it); Control Center's slider eases to it (`level_follow`); Playback's Volume page (`xfade_open` 4) and its row follow it (`xfade_volume_shown`); on Now Playing (and the other volume pages, `vol_page`) stock's `dialog/volume_dialog` opens on it, Now Playing's band (`vol_paint`), so for 3 s the wheel is the volume there; on any other page the status row's [volume pill](#volume-pill) shows it, and the wheel keeps its page. Not with the screen off or over a video (its own volume).

**Bluetooth → Link Volume** (`Q2POD BTVOLLINK`, `bt_vol_link`, a `pod_rows` switch after Resume on Connect, last in the Bluetooth page's Audio group; stock's word was Control Device Volume) never chosen, follows the device connected now (`bt_link`, `patch/nav/rows_settings.c`): on for headphones and headsets (its Class of Device, which the connection's first battery run reads, `bt_headset_class`, is `bt_kind`'s headphones: major Audio/Video, minor 1, 2 or 6), off for a speaker, a car or a device whose Class is not known yet. A device whose own volume tracks the Q2's turns down with it, so a low Q2 volume plays thin through a speaker's weak amplifier stage; headphones have no such stage and are expected to follow. A choice saved (`BTVOLLINK` 0 or 1) applies to every device; the switch shows what applies now, and a click saves the other way from there. Off, the Q2's volume is stock's software gain alone and the device keeps its own volume, never read or written (`bt_audio_ready` is 0, so `ringnav_btvol` passes the levels straight to stock, `headset_gain` is `g_volume` and `bt_volume_poll` stops), and Rockbox's launch leaves the device's volume alone too. The Class arrives with the connection's first battery run, a moment into a connection, so headphones start linked from then. On, the rest of this section applies. A switch while Bluetooth plays resets the sync and re-applies the volume at once (`headset_volume_reset`, `device_set_volume`): off, stock's gain comes back; on, the next poll writes the Q2's level to the device.

With it on, volume starts by writing the Q2's saved volume to the headset, unless the headset's level already reads as it, so a level of the headset's own that reads as the same volume is left alone. The Q2's 0 to 100 reaches the headset's 0 to 127 on the connected device's **Volume Curve** (`bt_vol_avrcp`, `bt_vol_level`, `patch/nav/playback_power.c`; the choice is `vol_gentle`, kept with the device's Volume Limit, below). **Even**, the default, is the same share of its range: 127 v / 100 rounded, at least 1 above 0 so only 0 mutes, which is what a phone sends for its own volume. A headset that shapes the value into loudness itself (Pixel Buds do) is then as even on the Q2 as on a phone: every Q2 step moves the headset one level or two, half volume is 64 of 127 and 90 is 114. A 40 dB curve on such a headset stacks on its own taper (on Pixel Buds the Q2's 0 to 90 reached only 80 of 127), which is why Even is the default. **Gentle** is for a headset that takes the value as a plain gain (the Bowers & Wilkins Px7 seemed to), where Even puts the top half of the Q2's range in the headset's last 6 dB: 127 × 10^(−40 dB × (100 − v) / 100 / 20) (`bt_vol_gentle`, a table), so each Q2 step is the same 0.4 dB louder and half volume is 16 of 127, 20 dB down; under v 58 the curve's levels come closer together than AVRCP's steps, so there it rises no slower than 127 v / 400, at least 1 above 0. A headset level reads back on the same curve as the volume whose level is nearest, the lowest of those as near (`bt_vol_q2`), so a level the Q2 wrote reads back as a volume that writes it again: on Even the volume that wrote it, on Gentle's low steps, where up to four volumes share a level, the lowest of them. Polling then consumes headset changes, maps 0–127 back to 0–100, enforces the limit (`vol_cap`: Max Volume and the device's Volume Limit, below), saves Q2 state and shows the change (above). The change comes by BlueZ's signal (`patch/bt_vol_event.c`): bluetoothd emits `PropertiesChanged` on `org.bluez.MediaTransport1` when the headset's absolute volume moves, by its keys or by our write. On the first ready pass `bt_volume_poll` starts a thread that connects to the system bus (`/var/run/dbus/system_bus_socket`) and speaks the wire protocol itself, as demo imports neither libdbus nor gio nor `dlsym`: SASL `EXTERNAL` with its uid, `Hello`, and `AddMatch` for that signal from `org.bluez` with `arg0` the transport's interface; then it sleeps in `recv`, frames each message the bus sends by its fixed header and counts each signal whose header names `PropertiesChanged`. The UI loop's next pass sees the count change and reads the level (`btctl_transport_get_volume`) at once, so a lit change opens the volume overlay on that pass (within 8 ms, 25 ms idle); a burst (the wheel's own writes echoed back, a held key) reads at most once every `BT_VOLUME_EVENT_GAP_MS` (400 ms, the old lit pace). With the signal subscribed, the timed read is a fallback every `BT_VOLUME_FALLBACK_MS` (5 s), lit or dark, for a stack or headset that sends none; the dark volume limit is held on the signal too. A headset that refused absolute volume keeps `BT_VOLUME_SLOW_MS`. No bus, a refused login or the bus gone ends the thread, and the timed reads take over as they were without it: 400 ms lit, `BT_VOLUME_LIMIT_MS` dark under a volume limit, else `BT_VOLUME_SLOW_MS`. The match also passes the transport's other properties (`State`, `Delay`), each one read that finds the level unchanged. Remembering the accepted absolute value prevents feedback loops. Confirmed headset volume uses full helper gain except at zero; unsupported or failed reads/writes restore software gain. Spotify, radio and video consume the same effective gain. The AAC 48 kHz capability fix remains in place.

**A device's Volume Limit** (`patch/bt_vol_limit.c`). Each paired device may cap the Q2's volume, 0 to 100 on the Q2's scale, while it is the Bluetooth output; 100, No Limit, is the default and is never stored. Its row is on the device's page ([Bluetooth page](#bluetooth-page)), reachable for a device connected or not, and opens [Crossfade](#crossfade)'s slider page (`xfade_open` context 5): titled Volume Limit, no switch, 0 to No Limit, the wheel `wheel_level`'s steps as Max Volume's, a drag saved at its release. The limits live in `/mnt/data/q2-btvollimit`, one `AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF 60` line a device with one, 16 devices at most (`BTLIM_MAX`, counting those with a Volume Curve, below; a new device past that taking the oldest one's place), written whole to a `.tmp` and renamed, read once into a cache in `.scratch` (376 bytes with the rest of its state); a line that does not read as an address, a space and 0 to 99, or as an address, a space and `gentle`, is passed over, so a cut, corrupt or missing file is no limit and Even for every device, and the address matches in any case. Forget This Device drops the device's lines (`btlim_forget`). The volume's top is `vol_cap`: `g_maxvolume` (at most 100), lowered to the device's limit while the output is Bluetooth (`mclGetOutputWay` 1, no AirPlay speaker) and stock's link list's last item, connected or connecting, has one; the wheel (`vol_next`, so the volume dialog, Now Playing's ticks and Videos), Control Center's slider (`cc_volume`, `cc_drag`), Playback's Volume page (`vol_limit`), the Car Remote's `volume N` and the headset's own keys (`bt_volume_poll`, pulled back as to Max Volume, Link Volume on; the dark pace `BT_VOLUME_LIMIT_MS` holds for either limit) all stop there. Wired and USB outputs and another device never see it. A device's limit pulls the volume down without saving it: `BT_VOLUME` is every Bluetooth device's level, so a saved level above a device's limit is held to it as the device connects, not rewritten. Three places pull: the output becoming Bluetooth (`ringnav_output`, `btlim_entering`, on the saved level before stock's switch applies it), `btlim_poll` every 250 ms from `bt_volume_poll` (a device that became the output by another path, a device already connected at boot), and a limit lowered under the volume while its device is the output (`btlim_set`, at once). The level pulled from is kept until the volume is next saved (`btlim_saved`, from `ringnav_write_config` on a `VOLUME` or `BT_VOLUME` write): leaving Bluetooth writes it back as `BT_VOLUME` (`btlim_departing`) when the volume has not moved since, and another device connected in the first one's place starts from it. Tested by `test/fw/test_bt_vol_limit.py` (the store, every input path, the pull and the levels kept) and `test/patch.py` (`BtLimitMachine`: the headset's keys pulled back on the MIPS payload). **A device's Volume Curve** (the same file and cache): the device's page's **Volume Curve** row (its value Even or Gentle, `label_btcurve`) opens a picker, stock's Buttons Lock page with its rows ours as Songs' and Cover Flow's Sort (`bt_curve_open`, `PICK_BT_CURVE`, `patch/library_settings.c`), titled Volume Curve, the device's choice checked. Even, the default, is never stored; Gentle is a line of its own, `AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF gentle`, so a build that knows only limits still reads each limit line and passes over the curve's. A pick is saved at once (`btlim_edit_curve_take`) and, when the device is the Bluetooth output now, sends the volume again (`device_set_volume`, so `ringnav_btvol`), so the headset moves to the new curve's level for the same Q2 volume; `bt_sync_volume` writes it as the old level does not read as the volume on the new curve. Its effect is in Link Volume's mapping alone (above): the Volume Limit and Max Volume are on the Q2's scale, so a limit of 40 sends 51 of 127 on Even and 13 on Gentle. Tested by `test/fw/test_bt_vol_limit.py` (the store, the picker, the page's row, a restart), `test/fw/test_nav_loop.py` (both curves' levels, the round trip, the limit on either, the change sent at once) and `test/patch.py` (the Gentle levels and the limit on the MIPS payload).

`test/patch.py`'s headset cases run routing, ear counts and slot swaps, single-bud listening, first reports, manual cancellation, player/session changes, duplicate commands, malformed reports and volume limits against the MIPS payload. `test/headset_io.py` runs the actual worker with simulated kernel I/O, including late input discovery, handshake, draining queued reports, release/repeat filtering, cleanup and stale reconnect reports. `test/fw/test_bt_vol_event.py` checks the login, `Hello` and `AddMatch` bytes, the framing (split reads, two in one, an oversized message dropped, a big-endian sender's), the pace with the signal, and the overlay opening on the pass after a signal with the clock unmoved; where the machine has `dbus-daemon` and dbus-python it also logs in to a real daemon and hears a signal sent by a process owning `org.bluez`, while another interface's is filtered out.

## Resume on Connect

Two paths start playback when a headset connects. Stock's `checkBluetoothStatus` (`0x4fd42c`), once a headset's A2DP comes up with the Q2 as the source, runs `player_save_stop` (saves `mclGetPlayStatus` unless stopped, then `mclStop`), `config_outputchannel(2, 3)`, `device_set_volume` and `player_save_start(0)` (`0x4fdcbc`). That restarts the saved local or Tidal queue unpaused, so a paused queue plays, and a stopped queue with a stale saved status starts over Spotify or Internet Radio (`mclStartPlayer`'s hook yields them). AirPods also send AVRCP PLAY as the link comes up, which `headset_command` turns into a start for whichever player is active.

**Bluetooth → Resume on Connect** (`ringnav_btrows`, hooking stock's list builder `0x4c3ef8`, which rebuilds the whole list on every search and link change; `Q2POD RESUME` in `config.ini`; On, 1, is stock's behavior) is Off by default. With Bluetooth on, the row is in the page's Audio group after Headset Volume ([Bluetooth page](#bluetooth-page)), text only and 78 high like stock's rows; with Bluetooth off it isn't added. The jalr at `0x4fdcbc` becomes `jal ringnav_bt_connect_start`, which, unless a card game has the sound (A game with the sound, under Card apps), with the setting On calls `player_save_start(0)` as stock; Off, it lets a playing queue go on, reloads a paused one paused (`player_save_start(1)`, as stock's disconnect does) and starts nothing for a stopped queue or while a stream owns playback. Off, `headset_command` also drops PLAY (200, 207, or 164 while nothing plays) within `CONNECT_HOLD_MS` (5 s) of the link, which covers the worker's AVRCP discovery (about a second) and the headset's PLAY after A2DP setup; a press after that plays. Ear detection is a separate path: the first ear report after a connect never resumes, and putting worn buds back resumes only what removing them paused, with the setting either way. AirPlay and DLNA keep their senders' control (stock skips the restart while AirPlay plays).

## Wi-Fi page flows

Settings > Wi-Fi is stock's page (`systemset_wifi_page_init`, its list rebuilt by `wifimenu_rows_build`, `0x4d5950`), with `patch/wifi_flows.c` hooked onto four of its pieces: the switch and Search Again rows' click (`wifimenu_switch_row`, `0x4d61e0`; stock names the rows `0` and `1`), a network row's click (`wifimenu_network_row`, `0x4d62d8`; the button named by its scan record's index in `wifi_showlist`), the list's builder, and `network_checkstatus` (`0x518cf0`, stock's 500 ms Wi-Fi poll from `on_wm_timer_networkstatus`).

**A join that is trying.** Both click handlers return at once while `wifi_connectstatus` is 1, and a join stays at 1 for up to a minute: `network_checkstatus` counts `wifilink_timeout` down from 30 per poll and, with the radio still associated (`networkGetPhysicStatus` 1), grants one more 30. So the switch could not turn Wi-Fi off, nor a row be pressed, until the join gave up. Now the switch ends the join first, with the steps stock's own timeout takes (`networkDisconnect`, `wifi_name` cleared, status 0, without the toast), and stock's click then turns Wi-Fi off (`wifi_switch`'s off clears the rest and stops `wpa_supplicant`). The joining network's own row ends the join the same way and the list is rebuilt, the row idle again; another row stays stock's. Search Again during a join says "Connecting to Wi-Fi…". Control Center's Wi-Fi circle ends a trying join the same way (`wifi_flows_cancel_join`, called by `cc_act` before it clicks stock's switch), so a tap or Centre there turns Wi-Fi off at once too.

**The network first.** The network joining, joined or whose join failed is the first row under "Networks", one settings row high like every other row, the rest in scan order (`wifi_rows.c`, `wa`): `wifi_rows_pre` reads stock's rows before the layout (a row stock gives its `msg_connecting` line is joining, `msg_connected` joined) and moves that row's `list_item` to just under the header with `widget_restack`; the buttons keep their names, the scan records' indices, so `wifi_flows.c`'s lookups are untouched. Stock's own second line is hidden on every row, and every row without a state drops a caption its item holds (stock's rebuild can make an item at a freed one's address, which showed a failed network's "Wrong password" under Search Again on the emulator); the state is drawn by `wifi_mark` before the lock (the list's spinner while joining, the Accent check and the trash once joined, Phosphor `warning-circle` in Negative once failed) and said by the caption under the selected bar (`caption_row`: "Connecting…", "Connected", "Wrong password" or "Couldn't connect", the last two `ringnav_wifi_checkstatus`'s verdict, `wifi_rows_failed`). A failed network stays first until the next join or scan (Search Again's scan, `wifi_rows_scanned`; a scan ends in a rebuild, which is when the list is laid out); the user's end of a join, a Forget of the joined network and Reset Network Settings clear it (`wifi_rows_end`). Stock's check can clear `wifi_connectstatus` for a poll before setting it again, so a joining or joined network it stops showing stays first for `WIFI_SETTLE_MS` (2 s), and a timer then has the page rebuild (`g_wifisetting_flag`). The selection keeps its network through a rebuild: `ringnav_wifi_rows` notes the selected network's name before stock rebuilds (`wifi_rows_keep`) and `wifi_rows_post` puts the selection back on it by its tap target id (`ringnav_select`); a press on a network (`ringnav_wifi_network_row`, and the password entry `ask_again` opens, `wifi_rows_follow`) leaves the selection on that network once it is first, for up to `WIFI_PRESS_MS` (60 s) after the press.

**Search Again.** Stock's click runs `wifi_scan`, which starts the scan and sets `wifi_searchtime` to 10; the page's timer counts it down and rebuilds the list when it reaches 0. OLED's "Searching..." line is written only when the list is laid out (`wifi_rows.c` `wifi_rows_pre`), so a search showed nothing until it had ended, and the row seemed dead. `wifi_busy_show` writes the line as the click returns.

**A failed join asks again.** Stock's timeout returns 2 from `network_checkstatus`, and its caller turns that into "connect failed" (`msg_linkerror`) and nothing else; the password tried was saved by the join (`networkAddSsid`), so the next tap on the network joined with it again unasked. While a join tries, the hook samples `wpa_supplicant`'s `wpa_state` from `g_wifiStatus` (`+0xd8`, written by stock's monitor thread from `STATUS` once a second): a join that reached `4WAY_HANDSHAKE` (or `GROUP_HANDSHAKE`) and never `COMPLETED` was refused its key, as `wpa_supplicant` judges it (`events.c` `could_be_psk_mismatch`), and reads "Wrong password"; one that never got there reads "Couldn't connect". When the failed network asks for a password and the Wi-Fi page is in use, the hook returns 1 (the page rebuilds, no stock toast) and a timer opens stock's password entry (`kbwifipass_dialog`) for it, its empty box's tips the reason. A password entered replaces the saved one (`wifi_action_deleterecord`, then `wifi_action_connect`); Cancel, or an OK with no password fit for the network (`networkCheckSsidPassword`; Return can give one, empty), keeps it. The entry opens from a timer, as stock's own dialogs open from `on_wm_timer_dialog`: opened from `ringnav_sleep`'s polls it took no input until it closed. An open network's failure, or one off the page, keeps stock's toast.

**Forget and Reset.** Stock's Forget is a tap on a saved row's right end (`check_wifinextaction`'s x range 276 to 375), which the wheel cannot reach. Play/Pause held on a saved network's row (`wifi_flows_hold`, from `ringnav_keylong`) asks "Forget *name*?" on the confirmation card, then runs stock's `wifi_action_deleterecord`. **Reset Network Settings**, the list's last row on and off, asks on the card and puts `/mnt/data/wpa_supplicant.conf` back to the shipped one (`/release/assets/default/raw/wpa_supplicant.conf`, no network in it) rather than removing it as stock's Reset Settings does before its reboot: `wifi_connect.sh` starts no `wpa_supplicant` without the file. With Wi-Fi on it goes off first and comes back searching, and stock's saved list is read again (`networkClearSsid`, `networkGetSsidList`).

`test/fw/test_wifi_flows.py` holds each flow. In the emulator, which has no radio, a stand-in `wpa_cli` in the slot's rootfs printing a scan (stock reads `wpa_cli scan_result > /tmp/scan_result` and skips its first line, `Selected interface`) lists networks, and `Q2EMU_WIFI=0` lets a join time out.

## LocalSend

Settings > Network's third row, stock's Wi-Fi File Transfer (`netservice_wifitrans`, renamed **LocalSend**), opens `patch/localsend_ui.c`'s page (`smart_wifi.c` `ringnav_netservice_row`, row 2); the design, the protocol and the daemon `q2send` are in [localsend](localsend.md). Stock's own server never starts: `switch_wifitransport`'s hook returns at once for on and runs stock's for off, which only stops it, so no stock path brings thttpd and port 8888 back; stock's thttpd, `/etc/thttpd.conf` and `/usr/share/web` stay in the image as shipped.

**The daemon's life.** `localsend_poll` (from `power_poll`, every `LS_POLL_MS`, 250 ms) starts `q2send --alias <Bluetooth name>` while one of the five windows is open (`localsend_page`, `lssend_page`, `lsshare_page`, `lstrust_page`, `lsxfer_page`) or a transfer is in `ask`, `wait` or `run`, through the shell (`system`, backgrounded, as Car Remote's), and stops it once neither holds (`kill $(cat /tmp/q2send.pid)`); a daemon that died is started again after `LS_RESTART_MS`. While it runs, Smart Wi-Fi keeps the radio up (`localsend_running` in `smart_needed`; the page itself is a network page too), and `/tmp/q2send.hold` exists while USB storage has the card (`usbmode_page`), so the daemon refuses every request.

**Reading it.** Each poll reads `/tmp/q2send.state` whole (`ls_read`): the devices (`peer`), the trusted devices (`trusted`) and the two transfers (`recv`, `send`), byte counts taken as KB as they are parsed so nothing needs a 64-bit divide. The lists are built again only when the hash of the device and trusted lines (and the Wi-Fi switch) moves, never for progress; the transfer page is repainted each poll. A phase that changed is shown once: a receive's end is a toast (`toast_later`, so never from inside another toast's loop and never on a dark screen), a send's end closes the transfer page and toasts, and a trusted sender's `run` is the "Receiving from <name>" toast in place of the card.

**The Accept card.** `/tmp/q2send.ask` (id, name, model, type, files, bytes) is the [confirmation card](oled-design.md#confirmation-card) once per id, over whatever is on screen (`awake_screen` first): Accept and Decline, Decline answering itself after `LS_ASK_MS` (59 s, inside the daemon's 60), Return declining, and the Always Accept switch (USB debugging's form, "Always Allow"; the approved "Always accept from this device" is wider than the card). The answer goes to `/tmp/q2send.answer` whole: `<id> 1`, `<id> 1 trust` or `<id> 0`. Another card up first leaves the request for the next poll; the ask file gone (the sender gave up) closes the card.

**After a receive.** The paths the daemon lists in `/tmp/q2send.received` are read and the file removed; one with a song's extension sets a library scan due, which opens stock's Update Local Music dialog (`dialog/updatemusic_dialog`, the whole library: stock's scan takes no single folder without a new hook) once the daemon has stopped and `library_quiet` (`addon_library.c`) allows it: only known pages open, nothing playing, no song paused under a lit screen.

**Sending.** Send Logs and a device's Logs ask q2guard for a flush first (`ulog_flush`: `/tmp/q2guard.snap` "flush" and a SIGUSR1, waited for at most `ULOG_FLUSH_MS`, 1 s), then send every file in `/mnt/mmc/.q2muse/logs` and the battery log, written to `/tmp/battery-log.txt` (`battery_log_write`); Battery History's Share Log sends that file alone. The request is `/tmp/q2send.cmd`: `send\t<fingerprint>` and a path a line. Tests: `test/fw/test_localsend_ui.py` (the state as read, sizes, the request), `test/fw/test_battery.py` (Share Log), and the daemon's in `test/unit/test_localsend.py` and `test/localsend_e2e.py`.

## Quick-settings holds

Holding Wi-Fi or Bluetooth for `QUICK_HOLD_MS` (550 ms, the house hold) opens `systemset/wifi_page` or `systemset/bluetooth_page`. `ringnav_quick_settings` adds pointer-down handlers to the stock images. Release, movement over 10 pixels, pointer abort, keys, window close, background or destruction cancels the one-shot timer. A successful hold aborts the native press before closing the dialog and suppresses any late click, so it cannot also toggle the radio or open Playback settings. Ordinary taps keep their stock click handlers.

Holding Playback (`img_playset`) the same way opens `playset/equalizer_page`, the path stock's Playback EQ row opens (`0x4bd114`), after closing the panel. Pulled down over the page a hold opens (anywhere in the window stack), the hold only closes the panel (`cc_page`, `patch/control_center.c`): that page is already the goal. Stock's navigator would stack a second copy on it, so Return took two presses to leave Settings > Wi-Fi (the emulator, 2026-11-17), and `peq_ui.c` keeps one EQ page's state, so a second `equalizer_page` over the first would leave the first dead. Quick Settings gets the touch hold only; a held Play/Pause there is stock's, the wheel walking its rows.

Under Control Center (`patch/control_center.c`) every toggle holds the same way. `cc_open` gives each of its own clear buttons that has a settings page `quick_hold(button, QUICK_CC + stop)`, and `quick_long` hands those to `cc_hold` after closing the page: Wi-Fi `systemset/wifi_page`, Bluetooth `systemset/bluetooth_page`, AirPlay `systemset/netservice_page`, Car Remote `carremote_open`, Smart Wi-Fi `systemset/wifi_page` and EQ `playset/equalizer_page`, each through `cc_page` (not a second one); AirPlay's tap opens `systemset/netservice_page` the same way. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth need buttons of their own too: stock's `label_wifi` and `label_bt`, hidden, still take a touch (the dialog's hit test skips no hidden widget) and lie over the two switches inside `view_menu`, so a tap or hold on those circles reached the label, never the switch (the device and the emulator, 2026-11-17); the buttons, made after `view_menu`, are found first, and a tap there clicks stock's switch as Center does (`cc_act`). Center held as long with the ring on such a stop does the same: `cc_keydown` (from `ringnav_keydown`) arms `cc_hold_due` once, a held key's repeats leaving it be, and once it fires the release is swallowed (`cc_key_release`, in the key filter before every page's own keys), so neither the stop nor the page then in front sees it. A shorter press drops the hold on its release and acts as a tap. The sliders and the Now Playing block have no hold.

## Control Center volume drag

A finger on Control Center's Volume slider (`cc_drag`, `patch/control_center.c`) sets the volume where it is, from the press through the drag, and the release (`EVT_POINTER_UP_BEFORE`) sets where it stopped. Two costs are kept off each move. **The repaint:** a move invalidates only the slider's box and its ring (`CC_RING` past it), as stock's Brightness slider invalidates its own; the fill follows every move, drawn from the level the drag holds (`ccv.want`) until it is set. **The set:** `device_set_volume` and `write_int_config` run at most once every `CC_VOL_WRITE_MS` (30 ms, about a frame): a move that soon after the last set is held, and a one-shot `timer_add` (`cc_vol_due`, not tied to the window, so it runs if the page closes first) sets the latest. The final level is the last move's, as before; the saved `PLAYSET VOLUME` (or `BT_VOLUME`) is the set's, which `config_hold` writes `CONFIG_SETTLE_MS` after the last ([Where Q2 Muse writes](#where-q2-muse-writes)), so config.ini was never rewritten a move. Measured on the emulator on 2026-11-18 (`q2emu swipe` across each slider, 1.5 s a pass, the shim's flip count sampled every 1 ms, `cc_paint` timed in a build with timing added): before, a volume drag ran at 20 to 37 frames a second against 29 to 41 for a brightness drag in the same runs (0.67 to 0.92 of it), `cc_paint` 2.0 to 16.8 ms a frame on average (p90 to 48 ms) against 1.2 to 3.6 ms; after, 33 to 35 against 35 to 36 (0.93 to 1.0). On the emulator a set itself is cheap (`device_set_volume` 4 us, `write_int_config` 4 us on average, about 46 a second of drag), because it has no DAC and no Bluetooth: the device's costs are argued from the code. Wired, `device_set_volume` is the DAC's `mclSetLocalVol` ioctl, and the cs43131 driver `printk`s two lines for each (`==dac==left[..]==right[..]==volvalue[..]` and `user_mute`), written to the console in the caller's context when the console's log level lets them through; with Bluetooth it is `mclSetBtVol`, whose hook (`ringnav_btvol`) with Link Volume on makes `bt_sync_volume` read the headset's absolute volume and set it (`btctl_transport_get_volume`, `btctl_transport_set_volume`, each a D-Bus round trip to bluetoothd), then sends hciplayer its level. The release's set is the one Link Volume sends last. ponytail: the set stays on the UI thread, at most once a `CC_VOL_WRITE_MS`: stock's `mcl*` calls and libbtctl's D-Bus connection are also used by the UI thread's own polls (`bt_volume_poll`), and neither is known to be safe from a second thread; a worker that owned every volume set would lift that.

## On-The-Go

Library > Playlists is dressed by `pl_dress` with no select mode and no action rows but **On-The-Go** (`pl_otg_row`, while Settings > Playback > Library's `Q2POD OTG` is 1, the default): its tile, its name and its count, read by `otg_count` (`getMusicByPlayList(100)` through `staged`). The playlists' rows are `pl_oled_row`'s: 44 px (`PL_OLED_H`), the art image 36 px (`PL_OLED_ART`) at x 22 and the text from x 66 (`pl_oled_fit`, which `compact_row_layout` calls again on each relayout), stock's dots and other images hidden, a `list_into` image for the chevron, "N songs" in 16 px (the design's 13). The art is the playlist's own picture only (`playlist_art` with `PL_ART_OWN`: no 2x2), else a server playlist's cover (`catalogue_playlist_cover`: the app's `covers/pl-<pid>.jpg`, by the playlist's `cat.serverlists` row, the mapping read once per list built by `catalogue_playlist_covers`); with neither the image is empty and `pl_tile_paint` draws the tile under the `PL_TILE` prop (1 playlist, 2 On-The-Go), two int compares for every other widget painted. `pl_pitch` keeps the list at 44 px. A row's Center opens `playlist_page_open` (`pl_pick`) instead of stock's song list.

**On-The-Go's songs** are rows of stock's `playlist` table with `cd_num` 100 (`ON_THE_GO`) and no header: headers are ids 0 to 99 (`ringnav_playlist_create`, the catalogue's), and every reader of the headers asks `id <= 100` for headers or `cd_num = N` for one list's songs, so nothing lists it as a playlist, while stock's `batch_add_file`, `checkPlayListExist`, `getMusicByPlayList` and `sort_playlist_addtime` and our `ple_mutate` (whose bound is now `ON_THE_GO`) take it as any list's. It lasts in `database.db` across a restart. `otg_save` makes the header "On-The-Go N" (`ringnav_playlist_create`, the first N it doesn't refuse as taken) and moves the songs to it in one statement (`update playlist set cd_num=id where id>100 and cd_num=100`), so their ids and order stay; `pl_made` lands the list on it. `otg_clear` deletes the rows. Stock's Update Local Music drops `songtable` only, and Import replaces playlists by name, so neither touches it. ponytail: Export leaves it out, as it has no header.

**A playlist's page** (`playlist_pages.c`, `playlistsongs_page`) is `page_list` rows: Shuffle (when it has songs), Add Songs, and for On-The-Go Save as Playlist and Clear, then the songs in the playlist's own order (`sort_playlist_addtime`). `pv_paint` draws an action row's glyph (`plact_<name>_<a|w>`, `tools/art.py` `PL_ACTIONS`) and keeps its label in the accent, white on the selection, and right-aligns a song's artist, narrowing the title's label to end 8 px short of it. Clicks run on the next pass (`pv_run`). A song plays as stock plays a playlist's own list: `g_local_classinfo_save + 4` set to the `cd_num`, then `play_folder(songs, i, 0xff13)`, so Now Playing's Delete takes it out of this list (`deleteMusicFromPlaylist`), not the library. The page reads its songs again on `EVT_WINDOW_FOREGROUND`. A Play/Pause hold on a song (`playlist_page_hold`, from `ringnav_keylong`) is a Library song's whole menu (`qm_song_hold` in `navigation.c`: `QM_COVERFLOW` over the page's own list, `qm_held`, with Go to Album as well), then Remove from Playlist (or On-The-Go), `QA_REMOVE`, last after a gap in red, which asks on the [confirmation card](oled-design.md#confirmation-card) ("Remove "Two"?", "It stays in your library.") and on Remove runs `playlist_remove` (`ple_mutate`) on the song held, if it is still that row (`pv_remove_answer`).

**Menus.** In the menu sheet `qm_open` builds a song's menu as Play Next, `QA_OTG` (Add to On-The-Go, `playlist_add(r, ON_THE_GO)`) or, with On-The-Go off, Add to Queue, then Add to Playlist…, Favorite, then the Go to rows; a playlist's (`QM_PLAYLIST`) as `QA_PLAY` (its songs, `qm_collect`, played as its own list), Shuffle, `QA_RENAME` and `QA_DELETE` after a `modal_gap`. A playlist row's hold finds the playlist by its button's name, stock's index, as OLED's rows have no dots. Add to Playlist… is `playlist_pick_open`: the song copied into a one-record deque, the headers read (`getAllPlayList`), `modal_actions` with New Playlist first; a pick adds (`playlist_add`: stock's batch add through a private one-entry selection, checked with `checkPlayListExist` after) and toasts. New Playlist creates "New Playlist N" from the count plus one. Rename opens the letter strip (`search_strip.c` `playlist_rename_open`, `ss.rename`), which saves through `playlist_rename` (name and filename, as stock's, refused when another playlist has the name); Delete asks through stock's confirm (`playlist_confirm`) and runs `playlist_delete`. Each sets `g_delete_flag`, so the Playlists page reads its rows again when it is on top.

## Add Songs

`add_songs.c` (`addsongs_page`) is one sheet the page paints itself, as Search's strip is: a stack of up to four levels (the chooser; Recently Played, `getAllRecentRecord`; Recently Added, `getAllRecentAddRecord`; Artists, `getAllArtist` or `GetAllAlbumArtist` as Playback's Artists says; Albums, `getAllAlbum`; Songs, `all_songs`; an artist's songs, `getMusicBySonger` or `getMusicByAlbumArtist`, and its albums, each once by `album_cmp`, `coverflow_newest`; an album's tracks, `coverflow_album_tracks`), each a deque through `staged_music`, so a list of any length costs its records and no widgets. Its keys come before stock's in `ringnav` (`add_songs_key`): the wheel moves the selection and keeps it whole above y 282, Center acts, Return pops a level and leaves from the chooser. A tap acts on its row, a drag scrolls a row per 32 px. A cover row's picture is `catalogue_cover`'s for a server album, else Cover Flow's cached cover (`art_path(album_key)`), a `#2C2C2E` square till it exists. The A-Z index past `AZ_MIN_ROWS` is az_index.c's own column and bubble, driven through `az_mark` (the letter from the selected row on a fast spin, or the finger's on the right edge, which jumps to `az_target`).

**Marks.** `add_songs` reads the playlist once into `as.was`, and `as.now` starts the same: each a set of keys, a song's path hashed with its CUE start (`as_key`), `AS_MAX_KEYS` (4096) at most. A song is in before and now (check), added now (plus), or in before and not now (minus). Center (`add_songs_toggle`) adds through `playlist_add`, or takes the song out by finding its entry in a fresh read of the playlist and `playlist_remove`, and changes `as.now`. Add All adds each song not in now. Search's strip in its pick mode (`add_songs_search`, `ss.pick`) lists songs alone, found by title or artist, and hands a Center to `add_songs_toggle`, its rows marked by `add_songs_mark`.
