## Local playlist editing

The other themes keep stock's Playlists page and this editor; OLED's playlists are [On-The-Go](#on-the-go)'s pages and menus, with no Edit Playlist. `ringnav_playlistsmore` extends stock `localmusic_playlistsmore_page_init` (`0x4b6614`). Its context is the index into `p_deque_playlist`; the container's `REC_DISC` (`cd_num`) fixes the editor's destination. Stock Rename and Add to Playlist routes remain in use, while New Playlist's allocator and Delete are replaced (`ringnav_playlist_create`, `ringnav_playlist_delete`); the More page's Delete row is relabelled Delete Playlist, as it deletes the whole list; the label is set as its translation key (`widget_set_tr_text`; no language has it, so it reads as given), which a re-translation keeps. The added Edit Playlist row reuses the Rename icon and the stock rows' list item, 335px button, 52px icon, 20px label and spacing. The runtime `playlistedit_page` uses the shared `page_open` / `page_list` helpers, its own staged records and a local song picker. Touch/Center song actions include adjacent movement and removal confirmed on the confirmation card (`ple_remove_answer`, Cancel first); Add Songs leaves the picker open after each stock batch addition, checking a fresh load before reporting success. Add Songs' first row opens the same T9 box as Internet Radio's pull-down (`edit_create`, named `search_edit` so `search_key` closes the keyboard before Return destroys it); the picker filters case-insensitively on tagged title, artist and album, and keeps the query while several songs are added. Holding Play/Pause on a playlist row opens its [queue menu](#queue-menu), whose last row, More…, opens `localmusic/playlistsmore_page` with the playlist index from the row's `img_more<n>` dots, as the dots themselves do (the list's row index also counts Import and Export, and a row without dots keeps stock's hold); the shared `playlist_page` add picker is excluded by `PLAYLIST_ADD_MODE`. Stock duplicate checking runs before addition. The picker ticks a song the playlist already holds (same path and CUE start, matched against the staged entries in memory, no query per row) with stock's `select` check at x 340, the caption shortened to stop before it; a successful add ticks its row in place. A private one-entry libcstl selection vector lives for demo’s lifetime, so adding never rewrites a covered stock picker’s global batch selection. Done/Back exits; destroy cancels pending work and releases both deques.

Playlist creation (`ringnav_playlist_create`) allocates a free header ID from 0–99 under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, independent of the displayed name order. Stock's allocator assumed ID order and could reuse an occupied ID after name sorting. Duplicate names keep stock's `-2` result; database failures roll back and show “Could not create playlist”. Delete Playlist asks for confirmation, then removes the header and its entries in one transaction. It sets stock's reload flag and shows “Playlist deleted” only after a successful commit; failure keeps the playlist and shows “Could not delete playlist”. Music files and the current playback queue stay intact.

Stock `getMusicByPlayList` (`0x50b6c8`) selects `playlist` records with `id > 100` and the destination `cd_num`. V1.34 gave playlists a Sort: by `g_playlistsort_flag` (`SYSSET PLAYLISTSORT`) the function hands over `sort_playlist_first_alphabet` (0, by name) or `sort_playlist_addtime` (Time added: the stored order, V1.32's only one, and the default, which an unset or out-of-range key also gives). The page, its play and the M3U export follow the Sort; Edit Playlist reads `sort_playlist_addtime` itself (`ple_query`), since a move swaps two neighbours' ids, which means nothing in a list sorted by name. `getAllPlayList` (`0x509b20`) lists the playlists themselves with `select * from playlist where id <= 100`; `ringnav_library_query` appends `order by name collate nocase, id` to exactly that query, so Library → Playlists and Add to Playlist list them by name (stock Rename updates `name` and `filename` together). It also adds explicit `order by id asc` to that exact stock query, including its export (`saveExternM3uFile`) and later playback callers. `ple_mutate` opens the existing SQLite library, takes `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, validates both entry IDs, playlist membership, path and CUE bounds, then swaps IDs through a verified free ID above the table maximum. Every update/delete checks `changes() == 1`; errors and failed commits roll back. Removal uses entry ID, so duplicate paths and CUE segments remain distinct. Only the chosen entries change; records omitted from a view keep their IDs. UI reload and selection movement follow successful commits. No live playback queue is rewritten, and no schema is added.

Previous/Next press, repeats, native delivery, long press and release are consumed while the editor is open, including under a success/error toast; movement requires the editor to own the top window. One press moves once; a release latch survives page closure. The wheel retains ordinary row selection. `test/patch.py` exercises the MIPS editor with SQLite transactions at the import boundary, including rollback, stale selections, ignored writes, duplicate/CUE entries, isolation, limits, picker behavior, touch actions and selection retention. Hardware reboot, stock export/import round trips and subsequent playback still require device validation before release.

## 1.3.5 audio and input fixes

Swap L/R (`Q2POD SWAPLR`, default 0) follows Mono Audio in settings. `crossfade.c` publishes `/tmp/q2swap` using the existing atomic shared-int pattern. The float PCM filter swaps after EQ and mono, before Crossfade; q2video swaps S16 after soft gain and mono for video, radio and Spotify’s helper. Spotify uses that helper on the headphone DAC when either switch is on, with the existing sink-restart limitation. Neither option changes DSD/DoP or AirPlay.

The stock title sorter queries `toolsQueryDbTableAndSort` (`0x5daf44`), now scoped through `ringnav_sorted_query` just like the other Library queries. Folder loads and stored playlist records retain their scope. Bluetooth absolute volume keeps the larger requested channel gain on the headset and normalizes each software channel against it. Reconnect/read-back uses `device_set_volume` to retain stock Balance rather than applying equal gains. `bt_volume_poll` reads the headset's volume back on BlueZ's signal and every `BT_VOLUME_FALLBACK_MS` (5 s) besides ([Headset controls and volume](#headset-controls-and-volume)); without the signal, every 400 ms lit, and dark every `BT_VOLUME_LIMIT_MS` (1 s) while a volume limit has to be held on the headset's own keys, else `BT_VOLUME_SLOW_MS` (2 s). A headset that refuses absolute volume, or can't report it (a read above 127, as before its AVRCP is up), gets the 2 s pace lit too, so its reconnect `device_set_volume` isn't repeated 2.5 times a second. ponytail: without the signal, dark, the headset's own keys can pass the limit for up to 1 s before it is pulled back.

`ringnav_input` handles the disconnected USB confirmation before stock input routing. During a Now Playing animation it applies fresh wheel volume directly and consumes the event; held list-navigation ticks are discarded. Once the animation ends, normal stock feedback resumes.


## Release signatures

q2-coda's releases are signed, so a GitHub account or repository taken over can't ship code that Network Update or the App Store runs as root. The key is Ed25519. Its private half lives in the maintainer's password vault and never in the repository; its public half is `assets/signing/q2-coda-release.pub`, which `tools/build.py` (`signing_key`) reads into `stock.h` as `Q2POD_SIGN_KEY`, and `patch/release_sig.c` keeps as `release_key`. A release build refuses to run without that file, and `--signing-key` (another public key, for a test build whose private half is at hand) requires `--dev`. The manifest records the key (`signing_key`), and `tools/release.py` refuses a package built with any other.

A signature covers a short ASCII message, never the file itself, so the Q2 hashes a 55 MB `update.tar` in 64 KB pieces (`sig_hash_file`) rather than holding it in memory:

- `update.tar`: `q2-coda-update-v1 TAG SHA512\n`, `TAG` the release's tag and `SHA512` the file's SHA-512 in lowercase hex. The tag is in it so that an older release's file and signature, published under a newer tag, fail. Its signature is the release's `update.tar.sig`, 64 bytes ([Network Update](#network-update)).
- `sources.list`: `q2-coda-sources-v1 SHA512\n` over every byte before the list's last line, which is `signature ` and the 64-byte signature in hex ([Q2 Shelf](#q2-shelf)).

`tools/signing.py` writes the same messages; [releasing](releasing.md#signing-a-release) has the commands. Monocypher 4.0.2 (`patch/monocypher/`, BSD-2-Clause or CC0: its `LICENCE.md`) checks the signature (`crypto_ed25519_check`, RFC 8032's Ed25519, which `openssl pkeyutl -rawin` makes) and hashes with SHA-512; `release_sig.c` adds SHA-256 for the App Store's pins. Its four files are Monocypher's own, unchanged (the release tarball's `src/` and `src/optional/`, SHA-256 `38d07179738c0c90677dba3ceb7a7b8496bcfea758ba1a53e803fed30ae0879c`, the same as GitHub's 4.0.2 tag but for the version line), and `--gc-sections` keeps only what the checks use, about 26 KB. `test/fw/test_release_sig.py` checks that a good signature passes and a flipped byte in the file or the signature, another tag, another key and no signature fail; `test/patch.py` swaps `release_key` for a test key in the emulated payload, whose private half it holds.

ponytail: the key can't be rotated without a release signed by the old one: a Q2 trusts only the key it was built with. A compromised private key is the one thing a signature can't survive; the next firmware would have to carry a new key, and be installed from the card by hand.

## Network Update

General's **Software Update** row (`ringnav_systemset` in `patch/navigation.c` binds it to `sw_update_open`, `patch/sw_update.c`) checks online and the SD card at once ([SD Card Update](#sd-card-update) for the card's half and the page); this is the online half, in `patch/netupdate.c`. **The check** (`netupdate_check`, on `sw_update.c`'s thread `sw_net`, only while `g_wififlag` is set) makes two header-only requests of at most `NU_CHECK_S` (5 s, connect and all) each: `releases/latest`'s redirect for the tag (as in step 1 below; a tag that isn't newer is `NET_LATEST`), then the tag's `update.tar`, following its redirects, for `CURLINFO_CONTENT_LENGTH_DOWNLOAD`, the size the offer shows. Any failure (no link, no DNS, a timeout, a code other than 302 then 200) is `NET_FAILED`, which only adds "Couldn't check online · Try Again" under the card's answer. Stock's own System Update page (`systemset_fwupdate_page_init`, hooked by `ringnav_fwupdate`) is no longer on General; should it open, stock's row builder (`0x4c8660`) names each row's button by its index, and stock's click (`0x4c84cc`) runs `atoi` on the name: 0 is the TF card update (`0x4c7eb4`), 1 Shanling's plain-HTTP server (`openwin.shanling.com:9000`, `/tmp/versioninfo`, `download_ota_thd`). The hook renames the second button "2", which stock's click ignores, and binds it to `sw_update_open`.

**The download**, Download and Install on the offer (`netupdate_start`): one pthread (`worker`) runs three transfers through demo's libcurl, all verified against `/etc/scrobble-ca.pem` (`SSL_VERIFYPEER`, `SSL_VERIFYHOST` 2; `easy` sets what every transfer shares), and checks the release's signature ([Release signatures](#release-signatures)):

1. A header-only request for `https://github.com/312-dev/q2-coda/releases/latest` (`Q2POD_REPO`, another repo's with `tools/build.py --update-repo`), without following the redirect. The tag is what follows the last `/` of `CURLINFO_REDIRECT_URL` (`netupdate_tag`, `.../releases/tag/TAG`), 1 to 31 of `A-Za-z0-9._-`, as it goes into the next two URLs and the signed message; anything else is no tag ("Can't reach GitHub"). A tag equal to `Q2POD_TAG` (`VERSION` in `tools/build.py`; empty in `--dev` builds) says "Latest firmware installed", as stock's updater would refuse that tag anyway. A beta of that version says so too, though its update identity differs (`BETA`), so its testers install the release itself from the card; Network Update offers them the version after it.
2. `releases/download/TAG/update.tar.sig` (`signature`), through `/tmp/q2-update.sig`, deleted once read: 64 bytes, the release key's signature. A 404, or any other length, is "Release not signed: not installed", and nothing more is fetched. q2-pod's upstream releases (DiamondBond/q2-pod) carry no signature, so a q2-coda Q2 never installs one; a Q2 pointed at them with `--update-repo` refuses every update.
3. `releases/download/TAG/update.tar`, the tag's own asset rather than `releases/latest`'s (the one the signature names, if the latest release changes in between), following the redirect to GitHub's asset host, into `/mnt/mmc/update.tar.part`, flushed and `fsync`ed. curl fails a body shorter than its `Content-Length`, and a transfer under 1 KB/s for 30 s ends. Then the part is read back from the card, the bytes stock will flash, through SHA-512 a 64 KB piece at a time (`sig_update`; the row says "Verifying…", `nu.verifying`), and only if the release key signed `q2-coda-update-v1 TAG SHA512` is it renamed over `update.tar`. Any failure deletes the `.part` and keeps the old `update.tar`: "Can't reach GitHub" (curl or no redirect), "No update for this build" (not 200), "Can't write to the card", "Signature check failed: not installed" (the file, the tag or the signature changed since signing, or another key signed it).

Software Update's page polls it every 250 ms (`netupdate_poll`, from `sw_update.c` `sw_dl_tick`): the percent from the transfer's progress callback and `nu.verifying` for its page, `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 0)` while it runs so standby and auto power-off wait (the screen still sleeps), and, once it ends, the thread joined and its state, which the page says (`netupdate_said`) unless it is `NU_DONE`, when the card's check runs on the new file. Leaving the page calls `netupdate_cancel`, which sets `nu.cancel`, which the progress callback returns, so curl stops ("Download cancelled"), and which the signature check reads after each 64 KB; a cancel that lands after the transfer finished still deletes the `.part` and reads as cancelled: the state is settled after `fclose` and the check, so a press while the card takes the whole part's `fsync` (seconds on a slow card, the label at 100%) or during "Verifying…" says "Download cancelled", not "Can't write to the card". The header request has no progress callback, so a cancel there waits for it (30 s at most), then skips the download. Leaving the page drops the label (`EVT_DESTROY`) and cancels, as the card may be unmounted or shared over USB next. A tag not newer than the build's (`strcmp`, as tags are single-digit `x.y.z`) is "Latest firmware installed", so an older release is never offered; `--dev` builds take any tag. After the rename the card's root directory is `fsync`ed (demo imports no `sync`), so the new entry is on the card before stock flashes. When it finishes on the page, `fwupdate_tf` runs [SD Card Update](#sd-card-update): its checks, its confirmation and stock's flash. Elsewhere it says "Update downloaded: use SD Card Update".

`tools/release.py` uploads `update.tar` and `update.tar.sig` under fixed names (`ASSET`, `SIGNATURE`), which `NU_ASSET` names in each tag's `releases/download/TAG/`. `github.com` chains to USERTrust ECC (Sectigo E46) and the asset host to ISRG Root X1; both roots are in the bundle.

ponytail: only releases that carry the fixed-name assets and a signature can be fetched, and a CA change at GitHub needs a bundle refresh. The card needs room for the new tar (about 55 MB) beside the old one. The signature binds the file to its tag, not to "latest": someone holding the repository could still hold back a newer release, though never install an older one over a newer build. A `--dev` build takes any signed tag, an older one too. Checking the signature reads the whole part back from the card (seconds), on the worker, so the UI keeps going. Plugging in USB storage mid-download unmounts the card under the write (the card-corruption risk of any card write); the `.part` then fails and is deleted. Leave USB unplugged until it finishes.

## SD Card Update

Software Update's card half (`patch/sw_update.c`, the look in [oled-design](oled-design.md#software-update)). `sw_update_open` starts the online check's thread (above) and then this one; `sw_tick` waits for both, and `sw_offer` weighs their answers apart: low battery stops either; the internet's update is offered first, with "Install from SD Card instead" when the card has one too; else the card's, with "Turn on Wi-Fi to check online" (`ON_OFF`) or "Couldn't check online · Try Again" (`NET_FAILED`, which runs the online check again and keeps the card's answer) under it; a card file that can't be used says why; else You're Up to Date. The wheel moves between the offer's button and that line (`sw_update_key`, from `ringnav`'s key handler), and taps hit either (`sw_touch`). Stock's row (`fwupdate_tf`, `0x4c7eb4`) asked first (`msg_confirmupdate` in `confirminfo_dialog`), then ran its checks, then opened `checkfw_dialog`, whose thread does the work and whose 1 s timer reports it; every answer was a message dialog. The hook (`ringnav_fwupdate_tf`, no trampoline: none of stock's function runs) checks first and asks only about an update stock's updater would take; the flash is still stock's `checkfw_dialog`. The download ends in the card's check alone (`ringnav_fwupdate_tf`'s path, `ON_NONE`), which asks Install Update? at once ([Network Update](#network-update)).

1. **Stock's checks**, `check_updatefw_exist(SW_CARD, SW_FILE)` (`0x5034f0`, exported), on the UI thread as stock calls it: -15 when `g_charge_state` (a cable in, `usb_detect`'s) is 0 and `g_power_capacity` is under 16 ("Charge to Update", "Needs 16% or a charger · now N%", `SW_BATTERY`); -2 with no card mounted (`toolsCheckMountNew`: "No SD Card"); -11 when `update.tar` can't be read ("No Update Found"); -12 under 0.1 GB free (`getDiskMemoryInfoAndSetFormat`'s GB, rounded to hundredths: "Not Enough Space", "Free 100 MB on the SD card"), as stock's tar unpacks the update beside it. Each opens its mode page at once (`swupdate_page`, `sw_stock_answer`).
2. **The tar**, read on a thread (`sw_check`, `sw_check_file`) while the page shows "Checking for an Update…" with a twelve-spoke spinner, as `update_firmware` (`0x5028e0`) will take it after `tar xvf`: its first member must be `firmware_v20.info` (at most 1 KB), whose first line, trimmed, is `Shanling Q2` and whose second, trimmed, holds a `V`; an equal version is "You're Up to Date" (stock refuses it with -14: `Q2POD_FW_TAG` is the patched version literal, [building](building.md#versioning)); then each member's header in turn, the MD5 of `recovery-update/xImage` against the third line's first 32 characters and `rootfs.squashfs`'s against the fourth's (stock's `strncmp`), streamed through demo's libcrypto 64 KB at a time. Anything else (another model, a missing image, a wrong MD5, a file cut short) is "Update Can't Be Used". Return leaves the page and sets `swu.cancel`, which the thread reads after each read. An 80 ms timer (`sw_tick`) turns the spinner and joins the thread, then acts on the answer only once the check's page has stopped sliding in (`window_manager_is_animating`), so a fast check still shows the spinner before its answer.
3. **Install Update?** on the confirmation card (`sw_ask`, `feedback.c` `confirm`) over the check's page: the update's name from its tag (`sw_update_name`: `V1820` is Q2 Muse 1.8.2 (`SW_PRODUCT`, the one product name), `V1822` 1.8.2 beta 2, a dev tag "Q2 Muse Dev", anything else the line itself) in the title, "55.6 MB, over TAG. Takes about 2 min;" and "your music and settings stay." as its body, Cancel (selected) and Install and Restart. Either answer closes the check's page (`sw_answer`); Install and Restart then, from an idle callback once the card is done, runs `navigator_to("dialog/checkfw_dialog")` as stock's function did. No card (another up) closes the page.
4. **Restarting to Install** is stock's `checkfw_dialog` (`ringnav_checkfw` in `playback.c` saves the place, then `sw_update_restarting` hides its `scrlabel_checkfw`): its thread stops the player, unpacks the tar to `/mnt/mmc` (`tar xvf ... -C mnt/mmc`, relative to demo's working directory, `/`), checks it as above and, at 1, marks mtd6 for the recovery (`ota:kernel2`) and restarts; the recovery flashes. The page's bar is the two images' bytes unpacked so far (`SW_PARTS`) of their sizes in the tar (`swu.parts`), stat'ed every 250 ms. Should stock's own check fail after all, its `dialog_quit` code comes back from `navigator_to`: 9 "No Update Found", 13 "You're Up to Date", 18 "Update Can't Be Used".

`test/fw/test_sw_update.py` covers the tar check (tars built as `tools/build.py` builds them), stock's answers, the names and the flow; `test/patch.py` runs the hook and the pages on the real payload.

A `--dev` build also runs this path from a computer: `q2update_poll` takes `q2update`'s request (`check` or `install`) and calls `ringnav_fwupdate_tf`; the check's answer is written back for it, and an update stock will take goes straight to stock's dialog (`install`) or closes the page with a toast (`check`) instead of asking Install Update? ([adb: Installing an update over adb](adb.md#installing-an-update-over-adb)).

ponytail: the check reads the whole 55 MB once more before stock's updater unpacks and checks it again, a few seconds the user sees as the spinner; skipping it would mean asking before knowing whether the file is any good. The bar stays full while stock checks the unpacked images and counts down its 3 s, which it reports nothing of.

## Card apps

Card apps (`patch/addon.c`, apps on the card, or carried in the firmware ([Bundled apps](#bundled-apps)), that Q2 Muse knows only by their folder: q2-deezer, q2-soulseek, q2-filebrowser, q2-subsonic, q2-podcasts, q2-lma) draw their pages over Q2SPOT/1, as Spotify's browser does ([librespot.md](librespot.md)). Each row's kind sets what a press does: `list` opens a level (its uri the op, its context the argument), `action` sends its uri with the context and toasts the reply, `needslib` is an `action` (once one that needed the server library on; there is no such setting now, below), `search` opens the T9 box, `sort` opens a level as `list` does (below), `remote` the QR code page, `local` plays a song or a folder from the card, a path under `/mnt/mmc/` with no `..` segment as a playlist's lines must be (context `album`: in track order, by name), `page` shows another window of the same list (below), `field` opens the T9 box for a value the app keeps (**Fields**, below), `info` nothing; `position` is the op a held Play/Pause sends, and a reply message `refresh` asks again every 2 s. A `progress` row (`progress_row`) is inert as `info`, Play/Pause held included: its title on the left and subtitle on the right of one line, over a flat 8 px bar of its `position` in permille (clamped to 0–1000, text that isn't a number as 0), kept in the bar's `_pml` prop for `addon_paint`: a square rectangle the caption's width, a dim gray track (`PROGRESS_TRACK`, #3A3A3A) filled from the left in the accent's light tone, as Spotify's bar, with no rounded ends and no knob; at 0 it draws no fill at all. Firmware without the `progress` word shows it as a plain title and subtitle row, so an app sends `info` with a text bar there. A press is queued for the next timer pass as a row index (`pg.go`), so any rebuild of the rows (`show`: a refresh that changes them, an error page's [Retry, Stop], a pop or push) drops it rather than let it land on whatever row now has that index. ponytail: a short first page that `append` rebuilds drops it too, the row kept or not; the press is just made again.

**One copy at a time.** An app is started with its launcher in the background (`launch`: `system("<run> &")`), which copies the app to `/tmp` before it writes its loop's pid file, so for a moment after a start nothing on the card says the app runs. A second start then would find none too, and both copies would run, each writing the same state, queue and cache files. So a start under way counts as running (`starting`: launched, no pid file yet, `ADDON_START_MS` not past): `addon_wake` answers 1 (started) and launches nothing, and an app's page opened then waits for that start. A boot that resumes an app's stream is the case that needs it: the resume's request (`resume_poll`) and the catalogue's autostart (`catalogue.c` `cat_autostart`) each wake the app in the same `addon_poll`. The app's own launcher and binary refuse a second copy too (q2-subsonic's README, What it touches).

**The QR code page** (`qrcode_page`, `qr_open`, `qr_paint`) is a `remote` row's page: the app's phone page, from its status file, read again every 500 ms while the screen is on. With a code and no `step` it draws the code (`qr`, `qrsize` rows of hex, the leftmost module the high bit) on a white plate centered under the status row, 166 px with two quiet modules each side, the app's `note` under it ("Scan with your phone" without one), and dimmer the address (`addr`) and PIN (`pin`) for a phone that types it in; without an address (no Wi-Fi) or a file (not running) it says so. Once the file has a `step` the page is a mode page instead ([oled-design](oled-design.md)): one solid circle with its glyph (`MODE_GLYPHS` in `tools/art.py`, `modepage_<step>`), drawn by `feedback.c`'s `mode_page_paint`, the file's `title` and `line`, the stack centered between the status row and the screen's foot. `phone` (the phone has the form) and `check` (the server is being asked) are the accent's, `done` green, `fail` (not reached) and `error` (anything else) red; `done` closes the page after `QR_DONE_MS` (1.5 s), so the app's page, now signed in, shows. The status row names the app (`addon_qr_title`), and the wheel does nothing there, as on every page but a playback screen ([Wheel volume](#wheel-volume)). An action whose live level's refresh puts a `remote` row under the cursor opens the page at once (`pg.qrnext`), so a sign-in row takes one press. While the page is open `/tmp/q2-<id>.qrpage` exists, removed as it closes, so an app knows the page was left by the file going, not from the pauses in its page's refreshes, which the screen turning off also makes. The `signin` word in the caps says the firmware does all of this; an app keeps writing `note` with each step for older firmware, which draws only the note, beside the code.

**Search in the title bar.** A list whose first row is of kind `search` shows it as a magnifying glass at the right of the title bar, in line with the page's name, as stock Tidal's (`s_img_search`), instead of as a row: `take_find` takes the row out of the reply's rows when the reply arrives (`lv_t.find`), and `find_icon` keeps the title centered on the screen in a box ending at the glass's box, x 73 to 302 (with a sort icon, at its ink: 95 to 280, below), so a longer title scrolls clear of them; it then adds a 50 px image after the rows, at x 302 in line with the rows' chevrons (`row_into`), and marks it clickable (an image sends no click otherwise; stock Tidal's `img_search` is clickable in its page too). A tap is queued as a row's press is (`G_FIND`) and opens the same T9 box (`search_box`, the row's press too); closing the box rebuilds the page, icon included. Only the first row of a level's own reply moves, its title and subtitle no longer shown, and a sole Search row stays a row so the list isn't left empty. A search row further down stays a row. A More… level is a level of its own and a `page` row's window is the level's reply, so their first row is taken; a later `pages` page is appended to the list, so a Search row there stays a row. Under a theme without a title bar (`page_title_h` 0, OLED's, where the name is in the status bar) the row stays as it was. No capability word: apps need no change, and older firmware shows the row. Not covered: the icon takes taps only, so the wheel and buttons no longer reach search on such a list.

**Sort in the title bar.** A row of kind `sort` (the `sort` word, below) is a `list` row: a press opens its uri as a level, its context the argument and its title the level's, and it has the chevron (`opens`, `open_list`). Where the first Search row was taken (`lv_t.find`), a `sort` row right after it (now the first) is taken too (`take_sort`, `lv_t.sort`), unless it is the last row left: its six fields are kept in `pg.sort`, pointers into the shown reply, which lives as long as the level is ready, and `find_icon` adds a second 50 px image left of the glass, in stock's Sort style (`s_img_order_navbar`, the Sort of stock's Songs page, image `song_order`), clickable, and the title's centered box ends where the sort's ink starts, 95 to 280. The sort's image is made before the glass's: their boxes overlap at 302 to 315, and a tap goes to the child made last, so the glass keeps all of its box. A tap is queued as a row's press is (`G_SORT`) and opens the kept row's level exactly as its press would. The icon's place is set by the glyphs' ink, not their boxes: stock V1.36's `navbar_search` and `song_order` are 50 px images whose ink (alpha above 0) is columns 15 to 35 and 15 to 34, so at `FIND_X` 302 the glass's ink is 317 to 337, 37 px from the screen's edge (in line with the chevrons), and at `SORT_X` 265 the sort's is 280 to 299: midway between the end of a centered 150 px title (a section's "Newly Added 1/5" at 20 px, ending at 262) and the glass, 17 px from each. Light Mode recolours the glyphs but keeps their alpha. `s_img_search` centers its image in the box (no draw type: AWTK's center), while `s_img_order_navbar` sets draw type 0, from the box's top left, so the sort's box is 50 px high and centered on the title's line, `(h - 50) / 2`, which puts both glyphs at the same height. A `sort` row anywhere else (no Search row taken before it, further down, the sole row left, a later `pages` page, or a theme without a title bar) stays a row; `page_to` counts a Search and a Sort row kept as rows before Previous page. A refresh whose sort row comes or goes rebuilds the list. Not covered: as the glass, the icon takes taps only.

**An action in flight.** While an action's request is out (`pg.act`), `go` sends nothing for another press of an `action` row: the app has usually done the first by then, and a second request would cancel it (`req_send` calls `req_cancel`), so its toast never came and a toggle pressed twice undid itself. Nothing else changes: a `list`, `sort`, `page`, `local`, `remote` or `search` row, the title bar's icons, a section swipe and a held Play/Pause's op go ahead as before, taking the request's place (the app has done the action; its toast is lost), and Return, the wheel, the volume and the player keys are not the page's to hold back. Return still pops the level or leaves the page, dropping the request as before. When no reply has come after `BUSY_MS` (400 ms, checked by the page's 250 ms tick), `busy_row` writes **Working…** over the pressed row's detail, or over its title when the detail is empty (under a theme with separators the empty detail's label lies under the centered title), as the App Store's rows say Installing…; `got`, and `action` for an op that takes the request's place, write the row's own text back before the reply's toast, so it clears on an answer, a refusal and a failure alike, and a live level whose reply doesn't change is left as it was. A reply within `BUSY_MS` changes nothing on screen. A list drawn again while the action waits (`show`, such as the search box closing) has its own texts, so `show` clears `pg.busy` and the next tick says Working… again.

**A row's own menu** (the `holdmenu` word). A row whose hold op (`position`) is `hold` has its own menu, the app's: Centre held `CENTRE_MENU_MS` on it or a finger held on it (`addon_row_hold`, from the hold menu's song row hold, [Centre hold menu](#centre-hold-menu)) or Play/Pause held on it (`addon_hold`) sends `hold` with the row's context as a hold (`hold_send`, `pg.act` `A_HOLD`), not while another request is out, and Centre's hold is taken at once, so the press never reaches Shut Down? and its release plays nothing; a finger's touch is aborted, so its lift clicks nothing. The reply's `action` rows, up to `HOLD_ROWS`, open as a menu sheet (`hold_menu`, `modal_actions`), headed by the row's title and its subtitle's first part (`sub_parts`), each with its op's symbol: `next` and `last` the queue menu's Play Next and Play Last, `toggle` Sync Offline's (`cloud-slash` for a title starting "Stop"). The reply is kept while the menu is up (`hm`); a pick sends that row's op with its context as an action (`hold_pick`), whose reply is toasted, and the level is asked again after it, as after any action. A reply with no rows is an action's: its message toasted. On an album's page Play/Pause keeps the album's own sync menu (`artist_hold`). **Play Next and Play Last** ([librespot: a row's own menu](librespot.md#browsing-protocol-q2spot1)): the app fetches the song to the card and names it in `/tmp/q2-<id>.queue`, written whole, a line a request, `<seq> next <card path>` or `<seq> last <card path>`; each app's poll (`queue_poll`, from `poll_one`, and at once after an action's reply) queues each new seq once with the queue menu's insert (`queue_add`, `library_pages.c`: Play Next after the song playing, Play Last at the end of Playing Next; a stream's queue takes none) and toasts Playing Next, Playing Last or Queue unchanged. A seq queued is kept (`app_t.taken`, `QUEUE_KEEP`), so a line the app keeps is not queued twice; what the file holds at the first look since demo started was there before, and none of it is queued. A path off the card, or one whose folder's listing has no such song, is Queue unchanged; the file is read to `QUEUE_RAW` (4 KB), a line cut there left out whole.

**Live lists.** An action on a live level (the app's last reply for it said `refresh`) leaves it shown: once the action's reply has come, the level is asked again rather than after `ADDON_LIVE_MS`, after the toast when the reply has a message (2 s) and at once when it has none, with no Loading… page in between, so a choice page's mark moves as soon as the app answers (written in place when every row keeps its shape, else the list drawn again, its row kept selected) and pressing the current choice changes nothing on screen. A refused action, or one on a level that isn't live, reloads it under the loading overlay (`hold_load`), its rows on show until the answer. A `refresh` reply that differs from the shown one is written into the shown rows in place when it has the same rows (`same_rows`, on the reply as `take_find` and `take_sort` left it): as many, on one page, each of the same kind, uri and context (so a press queued on a row still does what it did), each with a detail where it had one and none where it had none, More… there or not as before, a first Search row and a Sort row after it taken or not as before, and as many covers (`art_rows`, a count). `relabel` then walks each row's children: its `hscroll_label`s are the title and then the detail, each set only when its text changed, then given the face that text needs (`theme_font`, `ROLE_TALL` and `ROLE_META`, the roles `page_row_detail` set however the row was dressed) and put back to its left end (`xoffset` 0), and a progress row's bar (the child with `_pml`) takes the new permille and is repainted (`widget_invalidate_force`). A label's `text` prop is a wide string, so `widget_get_prop_str` returns NULL for it; the shown text is read with `widget_get_text_utf8`. So the list, the selection, a queued press, a cover's bitmap (the `drop` that lets covers go is skipped) and a long title's marquee carry on while, say, a sync's percentage moves, where a rebuild would start the marquee over every 2 s. When the selected row's title itself changes, `relabel` calls `marq_restart`, which clears `st.marq_row`, so the next paint re-arms the row's marquee (`paint_selection`) for the new text's width; a detail changing leaves the title's marquee alone. Any other change (a row added, removed, or of another kind, uri or context, a detail appearing or going, the first Search row or a cover coming or going) rebuilds the list with `show` as before. ponytail: covers are counted, not compared, so one cover replaced by another in the same reply stays until the next rebuild.

**The loading overlay** ([oled-design: Loading](oled-design.md#loading)). `push`, `page_to` (a Next page or Previous page row) and `field_sent` (a field's text) over a level showing its rows (`stageable`: `K_READY`, `pg.view`) do not change the levels: `stage` keeps the new level in `pg.lv[ADDON_DEPTH]` (the level array has one slot more than its depth), sends its request, sets `pg.pend` to how it will be taken (`P_PUSH` entered over the top one, `P_PLACE` in its place, sliding in from `pg.pmoved`'s side; the op sent is the new level's own, a field's its row's uri) and leaves the shown level, its reply and its rows alone; `addon_paint` lays `load_spinner_paint` (`list_marks.c`) over the page while `pg.pend` holds. `got` takes the staged level (`load_take`: entered, the old level letting its reply go, or in the top's place, its reply let go) when the finished request is the staged level's (`req.id`, which is never reused, so it is the generation counter) and takes the reply as that level's own: rows, an error page or the app's wait. Return (`leave`) and a tap off the spinner (`swipe`, which hands every touch to `list_marks.c` `load_touch` while `pg.pend`: it aborts the row the touch pressed and returns `RET_STOP`, so no row is clicked) call `load_cancel` (so a slow load needs no Stop row of its own: `l->slow` is a Loading… page's): `req_cancel` joins the worker within 100 ms and frees its buffer, so nothing is left to deliver. `go` does nothing while `pg.pend`, so the wheel's Centre and a row's click send nothing twice. A row pressed while a next page is on its way (`pg.paging`) lets that page go first: `stage` clears `paging` and `append` turns the trailing Loading… row back into More… at the cursor it was asking for (`pg.f[3]`), so a cancel leaves the list with a way on, as a failed page does. A search or a field's text typed in the box (which took the page's rows away, `pg.view` 0) first closes the box onto the level's rows (`show`), so it too loads under the overlay over them.

**Loading in place, and the first open.** A level asked for again where it stands (`hold_load`: Retry on an error page, the reload after an action) keeps what the page shows: `pg.hold` holds 1 + the level's state, `show` returns before drawing anything while the level is `K_LOAD` or `K_WAIT`, and draws its rows or error once they come; `load_cancel` puts the state back, the page never having changed. A swipe to another section is staged as a push is (`P_SECTION`, the section in `pg.psec`), `load_take` keeping the old one's selected row and moving `pg.cur` only then. The first open (`page_at`, from Streaming, Go to, More or Storage) makes no page at all: `pg.hold` is set with `pg.page` 0 and `list_marks.c` `load_over` lays the spinner over the window it was opened from (`page_in_use`), through the app's start (`K_WAIT`, asked again every 500 ms) and with no Stop row; the first answer that is not a wait makes the page (`page_make`) and ends the overlay. `load_over`'s window is another module's, so it is painted from `ringnav_paint` (`load_over_paint`) and its input taken first in `ringnav_input` (`load_over_input`, as `coverflow_wait_input` is): Centre and Return go nowhere, nor do touches, the wheel and Play stay the window's; Return's release, a lift off the spinner (the panel's portrait point turned to the screen's) or the window's `EVT_DESTROY` call its cancel, here `closed(0, 0)`, which frees the page's state and leaves the app running. With no window to lay it over the page opens at once, on its Loading… or Starting… page. Chapters (`nav/chapters_streams_folders.c` `chapters_open`) uses the same gate over the window the hold menu was on (past its sheet, `window_under`): `chapter_poll` opens `chapters_page` when ffmpeg is done only while `load_over_for(chapters_gone)`, and a cancel ends ffmpeg (`chapters_cancel`), the poll freeing it once reaped as for a closed page.

**Back.** Nothing waits on Back, so it has no overlay: `enter` keeps the reply of a level showing its rows when one goes over it (`pg.kept[depth]`, a `kept_t`: its pages, a calloc'd copy of their `4 + 6 * n` fields and the sort icon's row), and `pop` puts them back in `pg` and draws the level at once, sliding in from the left with its selected row, then asks for it again (`fetch`). The answer is taken as a live level's refresh is: the same bytes as the kept first page (`lv_t.hash`) redraw nothing, anything else rebuilds the list with its row kept (a live level's rows that keep their shape are written in place instead, `same_rows`); a pages list is not paged again unless it is rebuilt. A row pressed before the answer comes loads under the overlay as any (`stage` lets the refresh go). A level that kept nothing (it was on its error or Loading… page) is asked again under its Loading… page, as before. ponytail: every level under the top keeps its pages, up to five levels of ten replies each, and only the first page is compared, so a later page that changed shows as it was until the level is asked again whole.

**More….** A level keeps its list's own arguments apart from a page's cursor (`lv_t.base`, the bytes of `args` before it), and More… asks for the list's arguments and the new cursor alone, the op's last argument as Q2SPOT/1 has it. Up to 1.4.1 each More… appended its cursor to the page's arguments, cursor included ("albums 30 60"), which q2-deezer read as the second page again; q2-deezer v3.3 reads the last argument either way.

**Full lists.** A reply whose message is `pages` (the app opts in, as `refresh` does for a live list; [librespot.md](librespot.md)) and whose cursor isn't empty is followed by its next pages (`page_next`): each is asked with the same op, the list's own arguments (`args` up to `base`) and the newest cursor as the last argument, exactly what More… sends. Any other reply with a cursor keeps More…, so apps that don't send `pages` (q2-deezer, q2-soulseek, q2-filebrowser) see no change and no extra requests. A page's rows are appended to the same `page_list` without rebuilding it (`append`): the trailing row is destroyed, the new rows and a new trailing row added, `virtual_h` grown, and `ringnav_select` given the new count, so ringnav keeps the selection and the scroll and the wheel's acceleration and big letter run through the whole list. Limit (`ponytail:`): each page's new count makes ringnav's `load` drop a spin's speed-up and the big letter, as for any list whose count changes, so a spin while pages are still arriving starts slow again at each one; a ringnav call that grows a list in place would keep them. A page that lands while another window is on top (Now Playing, a menu) only records the count and selection: `ringnav_select` skips `load` for a list whose window isn't the top one, which took ringnav's list state and the top list's glide and big letter from under the wheel. While a page is on its way the trailing row is **Loading…**, which a press ignores. The list ends when a reply has no cursor or isn't `pages` (then at More…); at `ADDON_PAGES` (10) replies, or after a failed page (an error status, no socket, or the 15 s deadline), the trailing row becomes **More…** with the last good cursor, the rows already shown kept. Only a first page shorter than the screen is rebuilt (`page_list` shrank its view); pages that arrive while the search box is open are kept and drawn when it closes. A live level (`refresh`) never pages, its 2 s refresh asking for its first page alone. An action or a held Play/Pause reloads the level from its first page and pages it again (Back from a deeper level shows every page it kept and compares only the first, below); the selected row (`lv_t.sel`) comes back when the page holding it arrives, unless the user has moved off the trailing row meanwhile; once reached or left it is the selection, so a later page never moves it. A last page with no rows leaves the selection on the last row, not past it. The cap is 500 rows because ringnav navigates at most `MAX_ENTRIES` (512) rows of a `scroll_view` and walks every row per wheel event and paint; past that, More… asks for the rest as a level of its own. The shown reply, the top level's, lives in `pg` (a level under it keeps its own in `pg.kept` until Back, below): up to ten replies (`pg.buf`, each `realloc`'d to its own size before `spot_reply` cuts it, where the request had 64 KB) and 500 rows of fields (`pg.f`, 12 KB, calloc'd with the page). Progress rows belong in live lists, which never page.

**Sections.** An app's first level can be a row of sections, such as a music app's Home, Albums and Playlists, the way a phone app has tabs. A first-level reply whose message is `sections` makes each of its `list` rows a section: its uri the op that fills it, its title the section's name and its context the op's argument (other kinds and a `list` row with an empty uri are left out, and so is a context too long for a level's arguments; at most `ADDON_SECTIONS`, 8). Sections are taken once per page: a section whose own reply says `sections` shows its rows as an ordinary list, so a confused app can't make the page ask for the first section again and again. `sec_take` keeps them (`pg.sec`, a level each, calloc'd, freed with the page) and `sec_open` puts the first in the first level's place at once, asked for and titled with its name and, when there are two or more, its position (`Albums 2/3`), so the reply with the names is never shown. A sideways swipe on the page opens the next section (to the left) or the previous one (to the right); there is none past the first or the last. `swipe`, bound on the page's pointer events before its rows see them, works as Pull to search's pull (`pull_event`): a move of `SWIPE_CLAIM_PX` (24 px) sideways and at least twice as far as up or down takes the touch, the rows are sent a pointer abort so the lift clicks nothing, and the moves and the lift go no further; at the lift, `SWIPE_PX` (60 px) sideways and more than up or down changes the section, on the next timer pass (`G_SECTION`), as a row's press does. A move of `SWIPE_CLAIM_PX` up or down before that is the list's scroll, however far it went sideways. Only the first level swipes: a level opened from a section is an ordinary level, and Back returns to the section, asked for again. Leaving and opening the page starts at the first section again. ponytail: the wheel never changes section, on purpose (it moves the selection, as on every list), so the sections past the first are reached by touch alone. A swipe shows no movement until the lift, and a section is asked for again each time it opens (only the shown level keeps a reply), its selected row kept across the swipe; a section paged by `page` rows (**Windows**, below) comes back to its first window.

**Covers.** An app gives a row a cover by leaving a JPEG at `/tmp/q2-<id>.art/<key>.jpg` before it replies: the key is FNV-1a 32 (`hash_bytes` from `FNV_SEED`) over the row's uri, a tab and its context (as the app sent them, before Q2SPOT/1's `%` escapes), written as 8 lowercase hex digits (`art_file`). When `show` draws a level's rows it reads each row's file's header (`art_rows`, `picture_size`, stopping only at a progress row, whose bar belongs to the plain row, with the whole first page counted); if any row has one, the whole list is drawn as stock Tidal's lists are (`art_row`): `ART_ROW_H` (78 px, stock `tidal_*_page.bin`'s `list_view` `default_item_height`) rows, the cover `ART_PX` (64 px) square at the theme's text column, centered in the row's height and scaled to fit (draw type 4, as Cover Flow's), and the title over the subtitle beside it, with the chevron for a row that opens a page and the trailing More… or Loading… row in the same height. A row without a file keeps the cover's room empty, so the titles line up. The app sizes its covers: one over `ART_MAX` (128 px) either way, or whose size can't be read, counts as no cover, as each decoded bitmap stays in demo's memory; one up to 128 px is scaled to fit the 64 px. A row's bitmap is unloaded from the image manager before its image is set, so a file changed since is decoded again. Stock never releases decoded bitmaps, so a list a user scrolled would keep up to 500 x 128 x 128 x 4 (32 MB) until it closed: `art_window`, in `show`, `drop` and the page's 250 ms `tick`, keeps at most `ART_KEEP` (24, about 1.5 MB at `ART_MAX` px) rows' covers decoded around the list's real scroll position (`yoffset` over the row height, so wheel, touch and a fling all count). `[pg.art_lo, pg.art_hi)` names the rows whose bitmaps may be decoded; each tick the range is widened to all a move crossed since the last and the rows now outside the window are unloaded by name (`image_manager_unload_bitmap_by_name`), so the cost is the rows crossing, not the list's length. It is reset wherever the rows are rebuilt (`show`) and when a level's reply is let go (`drop`, unloading only that range while `pg.f` still has the rows, with no dependence on `l->art` and no file read); no row build decodes a cover. A row scrolled back paints by name again: stock's `image` widget paint (`0x627c6c`) keeps only the name (`image_base + 0x78`) and calls `widget_load_image` (`0x66f75c`) into a `bitmap_t` on its stack each paint, which `image_manager_get_bitmap` (`0x65823c`, `0x657e70`) fills from the cache or by decoding, so a released bitmap leaves nothing dangling (the same as `np_art_poll` and Home's cover, `navigation.c`, `coverflow.c`). ponytail: at most `ART_KEEP` covers plus what a fling paints in one 250 ms tick; a cover scrolled back decodes again on the UI thread. A list with a `progress` row is drawn as before, since its bar belongs to the plain row. The protocol is unchanged: an app that leaves no files, or firmware without the `art` word, shows the plain rows. Not covered: the choice is made when the list is drawn, so in practice the first page decides: pages appended later (`append`) keep it, and Back or an action reloads from the first page, so a later page's covers don't count then either (a list rebuilt whole with its pages there, a short first page or the search box closing, counts them); and a cover written after the reply counts only once the list is drawn again, which a live level does only when its rows change, though a row already drawn reads its file again whenever it scrolls back into the kept rows, so an app that deletes the file gets a blank there, the size being checked only when the row is built; and a theme with separators between two-line rows draws none between covered rows, whose height isn't its two-line rows' (`paint_separators`). Checks in `test/patch.py`: no file, another row's key and a progress row leave the list as it was; a cover's row, a row without one and a chevron's, in 78 px rows; and later pages joining as 78 px rows; `test/fw/test_addon.py` checks the key (a `%` in a uri too), the 128 px limit, the choice, and the bitmaps let go.

**Windows.** An app can keep a long list to a window of it at a time instead (the `window` word, below): a card app such as Jellyfin sends a window of a few `pages` replies, the last ending with a **Next page** row instead of a cursor, and a later window's first reply starting with **Previous page**. A row of kind `page` has a cursor of the level's own list as its context (empty: the list's start, no argument sent); a press asks for the list from it (`page_to`: the list's own arguments up to `base` and that cursor) **in the level's place**, not as a level over it, so Back leaves the list instead of stepping back through its windows, and the firmware holds at most one window, which Back from a deeper level shows as it was kept and asks for again. uri `prev` slides the window in from the left and selects its last row once its pages are in; any other uri (the app sends `next`) slides it in from the right and selects row 1, the row after its Previous page (past a Search and a Sort row kept as rows, under a theme without a title bar). A page row is a plain list row with an empty subtitle: `row`'s usual path and a list's row height (`row_h`), so in a list drawn with covers it is 78 px with the cover's room empty, as the trailing row. Without the word an app pages as before (up to 500 rows, then More…).

**Capabilities.** Every Streaming scan writes `/tmp/q2-addon.caps` (`ADDON_CAPS`), so a stale or half-written file never outlives the next scan: one line of words, the card-app features this firmware has, as a set (an app tests for a word, and order means nothing). Firmware without a feature lacks its word. `/tmp` is empty after every reboot and firmware update, so the file always describes the running firmware. Older firmware never writes it, so an app that finds no file knows it is on older firmware and falls back. The word `libsource` says the firmware writes the server library's state to `/tmp/q2-addon.library` (always `server`) and takes `needslib` rows ([Server library](#server-library)). `ahead` (always) says the firmware writes `.ahead` and reads a streaming app's `.stream`, and `grow` (only while q2player is the player: its `/tmp/q2clicks` is there at the scan, `ahead_caps`) that a song may play while it arrives ([Download Ahead](server-library.md#download-ahead-and-the-streaming-state)). `holdmenu` says a row whose hold op is `hold` gets its own menu on a held Centre, finger or Play/Pause, and the firmware queues the songs the app names in `.queue` (a row's own menu, above).

Words: `playlist` (Stream mode plays an `.m3u`), `progress` (the progress row), `pages` (full lists), `window` (`page` rows, **Windows**, above), `library` (**Library update**, below), `sections` (**Sections**, above), `art` (**Covers**, above), `urls` (**Stream mode: URL queues**, below), `sort` (the `sort` row, **Sort in the title bar**, above), `field` (the `field` row, **Fields**, below), `more` (`q2app`'s `more=`, **Now Playing's ⋯**, below), `fav` (**Hearts**, below), `status` (a reply led by an info row `status` is drawn as one centred stack, the empty state's form: the row's context its glyph, its title, its subtitle's lines, its position, a number, a progress bar of that permille; the reply's first action row its button, pressed as that row (`status_press`), and an info row `foot` its footer; `status_view`, [oled-design: Sync](oled-design.md#sync)).

**Stop and Retry.** A page that can't show the app's rows ends in **Stop <name>** whenever the app may be running (launched, a restart pending, or its loop's pid file there): an error page under its Retry, and a level loading or starting for `SLOW_MS` (3 s; a frozen app holds a request up to `ADDON_WAIT_MS`, 15 s). It ends the app as Stop Streaming Services does, a TERM to its loop (`app_stop`), so a frozen app, which can't answer a stop op of its own, stops too; then it toasts and leaves the page. Retry on "<name> isn't running" while the loop's pid file is there (the app running, its socket gone) restarts it: the loop is asked to end, the page waits as for a start (a pending `restart` counts as starting), and `poll_one` starts the app again once the pid file is gone, or after `RESTART_MS` (20 s) regardless; q2-soulseek's launcher kills an app still there 15 s after its TERM. Otherwise Retry asks again, starting the app first if it isn't running. An app whose `q2app` says `stop=0` (`app_t.nostop`, read as text at the scan, as `scrobble=0`, a Windows editor's `\r` taken) has no Stop row: `stoppable` is 0 for it, so a slow level stays at Loading… with no rows (`l->slow` never set), and its error page's second row is **Cancel**, which does what Return does (`pop`, or `navigator_back` from the first level), the app left running. No capability word: older firmware keeps Stop.

**Fields.** A row of kind `field` (the `field` word) is a value the user types, such as a sign-in page's user name and password, whose subtitle the app chooses (the name, `***`). Its press opens the search box (`search_box(i + 1)`: `pg.field` names the row, its title the box's hint); OK with text (`searched`, `G_FIELD`) calls `field_sent`, which sends the row's uri with its context, when not empty, and the text as the last argument, under the [loading overlay](#card-apps) over the level's rows, the box closed onto them first (`show`, then `stage` with `P_PLACE`: the staged level is the shown one, its `id` the request's), and the reply, when it comes, taken in the level's place (`load_take` lets the shown reply go): no `push`, nothing titled with the text, and the selected row kept (`search_box`'s `keep_sel`). `got` takes the reply as the level's: `ok` draws its rows, anything else is the level's error page, whose Retry is the level's own `fetch`, so the text is never sent again; a `refresh` and Back ask the level's own op too, and the app answers with the page as it stands. The row is checked again when OK comes (still `K_READY`, still a `field` at that index, a uri), so a reply that landed under the box sends nothing. A text of 64 bytes or more, a plain search's too (`searched` reads into a 256-byte buffer, wiped after) is not sent, with a "Too long" toast: a cut password would be the wrong one. Done sends `searched` twice (EVT_IM_ACTION and EVT_VALUE_CHANGED), so `pg.field` stays set when the text is refused (`field_sent` and `search_box` clear it) and the toast waits for no pending `go` (its modal loop would run it under the edit's own handler): the second call must not toast again or send the text's first 63 bytes as a `search`. ponytail: a text of 256 bytes or more closes silently, as stock's `widget_get_text_utf8` writes nothing for a text that does not fit; a field that long is not worth a bigger buffer. A field's request (`req.field`) that finds no socket while the app starts or restarts is the level's error page ("<name> isn't running", Retry and Stop or Cancel), not the wait a level's own fetch gets, which would ask the level's op and drop the text unsaid. The text never reaches a title, a toast or a file: `pg.term` is cleared once it is in the request, the worker clears the request's bytes past the reply once it has ended (`memset`), and `req_send` clears the buffer itself when no worker starts, so the freed buffer keeps none of it. ponytail: the T9 box shows the text while it is typed, as for a search (AWTK's password edit isn't tried with the T9 keyboard); a text is at most 63 bytes (`pg.term`), checked at OK rather than with the box's `max_length`, which isn't tried with T9 either.

**Now Playing's ⋯**, below).

**Stop and Retry.** A page that can't show the app's rows ends in **Stop <name>** whenever the app may be running (launched, a restart pending, or its loop's pid file there): an error page under its Retry, and a level loading or starting for `SLOW_MS` (3 s; a frozen app holds a request up to `ADDON_WAIT_MS`, 15 s). It ends the app as Stop Streaming Services does, a TERM to its loop (`app_stop`), so a frozen app, which can't answer a stop op of its own, stops too; then it toasts and leaves the page. Retry on "<name> isn't running" while the loop's pid file is there (the app running, its socket gone) restarts it: the loop is asked to end, the page waits as for a start (a pending `restart` counts as starting), and `poll_one` starts the app again once the pid file is gone, or after `RESTART_MS` (20 s) regardless; q2-soulseek's launcher kills an app still there 15 s after its TERM. Otherwise Retry asks again, starting the app first if it isn't running. An app whose `q2app` says `stop=0` (`app_t.nostop`, read as text at the scan, as `scrobble=0`, a Windows editor's `\r` taken) has no Stop row: `stoppable` is 0 for it, so a slow level stays at Loading… with no rows (`l->slow` never set), and its error page's second row is **Cancel**, which does what Return does (`pop`, or `navigator_back` from the first level), the app left running. No capability word: older firmware keeps Stop.

**Fields.** A row of kind `field` (the `field` word) is a value the user types, such as a sign-in page's user name and password, whose subtitle the app chooses (the name, `***`). Its press opens the search box (`search_box(i + 1)`: `pg.field` names the row, its title the box's hint); OK with text (`searched`, `G_FIELD`) calls `field_sent`, which sends the row's uri with its context, when not empty, and the text as the last argument, under the [loading overlay](#card-apps) over the level's rows, the box closed onto them first (`show`, then `stage` with `P_PLACE`: the staged level is the shown one, its `id` the request's), and the reply, when it comes, taken in the level's place (`load_take` lets the shown reply go): no `push`, nothing titled with the text, and the selected row kept (`search_box`'s `keep_sel`). `got` takes the reply as the level's: `ok` draws its rows, anything else is the level's error page, whose Retry is the level's own `fetch`, so the text is never sent again; a `refresh` and Back ask the level's own op too, and the app answers with the page as it stands. The row is checked again when OK comes (still `K_READY`, still a `field` at that index, a uri), so a reply that landed under the box sends nothing. A text of 64 bytes or more, a plain search's too (`searched` reads into a buffer one byte larger than `pg.term`, so a full one was cut) is cleared and not sent, with a "Too long" toast: a cut password would be the wrong one. A field's request (`req.field`) that finds no socket while the app starts or restarts is the level's error page ("<name> isn't running", Retry and Stop or Cancel), not the wait a level's own fetch gets, which would ask the level's op and drop the text unsaid. The text never reaches a title, a toast or a file: `pg.term` is cleared once it is in the request, the worker clears the request's bytes past the reply once it has ended (`memset`), and `req_send` clears the buffer itself when no worker starts, so the freed buffer keeps none of it. ponytail: the T9 box shows the text while it is typed, as for a search (AWTK's password edit isn't tried with the T9 keyboard); a text is at most 63 bytes (`pg.term`), checked at OK rather than with the box's `max_length`, which isn't tried with T9 either.

**Now Playing's ⋯.** An app's `q2app` can say `more=<op> <title>` (`app_t.more`, read at the scan, a trailing `\r` taken). Each queue an app's `.play` starts (`stream_start`'s `play_folder`, or `urls_start`'s `app_urls_play` when it returns 1) notes the app and `playback_loads` after its load (`qa`). The click on Now Playing's `img_more` (`ringnav_dispatch` in `patch/navigation.c`, before stock's handler, and the hold menu's More…, which clicks it through `stock_dispatch_trampoline`) asks `addon_more` first: while `playback_loads` is still `qa.loads` (no queue loaded since), the app has a `more` and its binary is still on the card (as `addon_goto` asks), it closes the app's page if one is open (as `addon_goto`) and opens the page at `op`, no arguments, titled `title` or the app's name (`page_at`), and the click goes no further (STOP), so stock's `playermore_page` never opens; otherwise stock's ⋯ opens as before. An op of 16 bytes or more, or none, leaves ⋯ stock's. ponytail: a stock reload of the app's own queue steps `playback_loads`, so ⋯ is stock's after it until the app plays a queue again; it errs toward stock's page. Checks in `test/fw/test_addon.py`: the click opening the page or stock's, the keys, the queue's mark.

**Stream mode.** An app that plays as well (q2-deezer's Stream mode) writes `/tmp/q2-<id>.play`, "<seq> <folder>": a hidden card folder (under `/mnt/mmc/.`, no `..` segment) it fills with a list's songs named in play order ("01 - Title [id].flac"), each renamed into place once whole. `stream_poll`, every `ADDON_POLL_MS` while the app runs, follows it: a new one is played from its first song once one is there (a 0 ms timer: the folder's songs by name, `app_album_songs`, through `play_folder` as a local album, Now Playing opening); while the queue playing is still the folder's (its first song's path in it), songs named after the last one queued join its end through `playback_queue_insert`, as Add to Queue; and the path of the one playing goes to `/tmp/q2-<id>.playing` (`blob_io`), from which the app fetches a couple ahead and deletes the ones long played. Once another queue plays, the session is left; a new seq starts again. A session is one app's (`sm.app`): each app's `.play` is kept hashed in its slot (`app_t.play`), and only a change to an app's own starts one, so two apps' files left in `/tmp` (q2-deezer and q2-subsonic keep theirs while they run) never take the queue from each other at every poll. The folder is listed only when its mtime changes (`stream_newer`, `sm.seen`), not every poll; an mtime within a second of now is scanned again on the next poll, as a file could land later in that second. A song that is added and then rejected (no `stSongInfo` for it yet) is picked up only at the folder's next change. Songs are queued by name after the last one queued, so a song that finishes downloading before an earlier one is never queued. The library scan skips hidden folders (`SCAN_DIRS`: the folder walk's `"."` test is `ringnav_scan_dir`, which skips any name starting with a dot, as Folder view's list does), so streamed songs never join the Library.

**Stream mode: a playlist.** `.play` may name a playlist file instead, "<seq> <path>.m3u" (`.m3u` in any case): it must be on the card: any path under `/mnt/mmc/` without a `..` segment, a hidden folder or not. A `.play` path of 160 bytes or more (`sm.dir` holds 159), or a `.play` of 190 bytes or more (`raw` holds that much, so its path may be cut), is refused in either mode, as cut it would name another file or folder. q2-subsonic writes one per queue, `/mnt/mmc/.subsonic/stream/queue-<seq>.m3u`. It is UTF-8 with one absolute card path a line; `#` lines (`#EXTM3U`, `#EXTINF`) and blank lines are ignored, and a leading BOM and CRLF line ends are taken. Its songs are queued in its order, wherever on the card they are (synced ones in their album folders, streamed ones in the app's folder). `m3u_songs` reads the file whole (up to `M3U_MAX`, 256 KB; of a longer file, it reads one byte more and drops the last line whose newline it didn't read, so a cut line is never taken as a path or waited for) and goes on from the entries it has already passed (`sm.next`); an entry not there yet (`access`) is waited for (`sm.want`), and nothing after it is queued before it, so order holds while streamed songs land out of order. A line off the card (not under `/mnt/mmc/`, or with a `..` segment: `/../`, a trailing `/..`; a name with an ellipsis, "Hello... (Live).flac", is fine, `dotdot`) is passed over, as is a file there that its folder's listing (`app_album_songs`, `REC_TYPE` 8) doesn't take as a song; neither is waited for. Nor is a line of 512 bytes or more (`sm.want`, `sm.first` and `sm.playing` hold 511), so a path the buffers would cut is never waited on forever. The app changes the file only by writing it aside and renaming it into place. Entries are counted, not compared: the ones already passed (`sm.next`) are never read again, so the app keeps every entry before the one waited for as it was (appending is always safe), and may rewrite the rest. An entry the firmware waits for (a card path under 512 bytes, its file not there) is never passed while it is missing, so from the first such entry on, the app may drop or replace a song that won't come (a download that failed, a synced file deleted since), and the songs after it then play. To change an entry before it, the app writes a new seq. At most `M3U_BATCH` (32) folders are listed a poll (a song's folder, `app_album_songs`, unless the song before it was in the same one), so a long list's start doesn't stall the UI, however many albums it spans; the rest follow on the next polls. The first batch plays as a folder's first song does; later ones join the queue's end through `playback_queue_insert`. The session is identified by its first song's path (`sm.first`) and by its queue's load: `playback_loads` counts `mclLoadPlayList` calls (`ringnav_load`); `stream_poll` notes it as the session starts, and `stream_start` again after its `play_folder`, whose load is synchronous. Once the queue's first song is another, or any queue has been loaded since (a Library or Folder play of the same album is the user's, even though it starts with the same file), the session is left, before its first song too (`S_WAIT`, and `stream_start` checks again): a song that lands later never replaces a queue the user started meanwhile. A stock reload of the same queue ends it too: it errs toward leaving the user's playback alone. A session still waiting for its first song (any mode, URL queues too) is also left once the user moves to another song of the queue playing (`moved_on`: `playback_picks`, which `playback_pick` counts at a manual Next or Previous, a Shuffle Albums or Folders group skip, an Up Next pick and a car remote jump, never at a skip nobody pressed): on the device a shuffled server song finished downloading half way through the song Next had played, and played over it. The song waited for stays on the card. Folder mode keeps its own test for a session that plays (the queue's first song in its folder) and no load test: a hidden folder can't be played from Library or Folder view, so the test would gain it nothing. The file is read again only when its mtime changes, the song waited for lands, or a batch filled (`m3u_ready`). Folder mode wakes for any new name that isn't hidden or a `.part` or `.tmp`, so `.m4a`, `.opus`, `.ogg`, `.wav`, `.ape` and `.dsf` stream too; whether a file is a song is stock's listing's call (`ringnav_audio_extension` over stock's format list). In either mode no folder is listed while a library scan runs (`library_scanning`, coverflow.c: its thread started and not done), the scan dialog's own loop included, as a listing (`toolsLoadDirectory`) refills `tools_pdeq_directory`, which the scan's thread fills too; nor while its window (the user's Update Local Music page, `updatemusic_page`, or its dialog, `updatemusic_dialog`, which a library request opens without the page) is still open after it, as `play_folder` would open Now Playing over it (`scanning`): nothing is armed or queued until both are over, a `stream_start` that finds one running clears `sm.seen` so the next poll after it looks again, and `.playing` still follows the song playing. A user's Next on the last song queued while the playlist waits for its next entry (`sm.want`, still downloading) does not reach stock, whose Next on a queue's last song wraps to its first (a radio's seed, played again; the device, 2026-11-17): `addon_next_waits` (from `change_music`; not under advanced play while its next song, Up Next's first, is a queued one this pass has not played, `order_next_queued`, as under Shuffle, where that Next is the order's) notes `playback_picks` in `sm.skip` and moves Now Playing to the waited song at once: a record of its path and file name, named by `card_record_tags` (below), shown as a pressed server song is (`catalogue_np_show`, `np_press`: the song playing stops, and `np_stream.c`'s spinner turns from the song's own `.stream` line), with no toast; the poll that queues the waited song plays it (`player_start_queue`). With stock's player that is once the app's download is whole (it renames it into place), as stock skips or hangs on a file still arriving; with q2player (`grow` in the caps) once `START_MS` of it is there (`stream_startable`), as q2player waits at the end of the bytes there are. Any other move of the user's meanwhile (Previous, a pick) changes `playback_picks` and drops the wait, and the player's parse of that song ends the pressed one's display. `sm.skip_at` is the queue's place the waited song joins at (`want_show`): the queue's end, where the poll that queues it puts it. <a id="pending-rows"></a>**Pending rows.** Up Next shows a session's whole list, not only the songs queued: Download Ahead fetches about two ahead and `m3u_songs` queues nothing past the first song not there, so a radio's Up Next stopped at two rows (the user's, 2026-11-17). `addon_pending` gives Up Next the playlist's entries from `sm.next` on that `m3u_songs` would queue (`pending_walk`, reading the file as it does), at most `UN_PENDING` (40), each a heap record of its path named by `card_record_tags` (the server row's title, artist and album, so a song not downloaded yet is named; its cover is its album's, [Album covers](#album-covers)); `addon_pending_sig` (the session, `sm.next`, the file's size and time) is in Up Next's `un_sig`, so the rows follow the songs as they join the queue and as the app adds a radio's next songs to the file. They follow the queue's rows under its "From" heading, the title in Text Secondary and the server row's cloud on the right ([oled-design](oled-design.md#up-next)). Centre on one runs `addon_pending_play`: a pick (`playback_pick`), then as a Next to it: `sm.next` moves to its entry, so the songs before it are passed over, `sm.want` names it and `want_show` shows it on Now Playing at the queue's end (`sm.skip_at`), so the queued songs after the one playing are passed over too; `sm.jump` makes `.playing` name it while it waits, so the app fetches it first (its plan starts at the song playing, [server-library](server-library.md#download-ahead-and-the-streaming-state)); it plays once the poll queues it, as a Next's song does. ponytail: the playlist file is read whole at each Up Next fill, which runs only when `un_sig` moves; a pending row has no bump or lift. The user's words, 2026-11-17 23:56, of the toast this replaces: "why doesn't it go to next song and show it buffering? it shouldn't reject".

**Stream mode: URL queues.** An app that streams (a Jellyfin app, say) can have stock's Tidal player play its songs instead of saving them to the card. It writes `/tmp/q2-<id>.urls` whole (temp + rename) and names it in `.play` as `<seq> /tmp/q2-<id>.urls`; only the app's own file there is taken (`sm.urls`). The file is `#Q2URLS/1<TAB>start=<index>` (and `<TAB>now=1` for a queue whose app is to be told what plays, below), then one line a song, `<url or card path><TAB><title><TAB><artist><TAB><album><TAB><cover url><TAB><seconds>` (no field holds a tab or a line break; a field missing is empty; a line with no URL is passed over, and so is one whose first field is neither a web URL, `http://` or `https://`, nor a card path, under `/mnt/mmc/` with no `..` segment, the rule a Stream mode playlist's lines pass: a server's string reaches stock's player as nothing else; a cover is fetched by stock's cover thread with curl, so one that isn't a web URL is dropped; `seconds` is optional and not read yet), read up to `AU_MAX` (256 KB, a last line cut there dropped) and kept up to `AU_SONGS` (5,000 songs, the rest of the file passed over; `start=` counts the songs kept, so a skipped line doesn't move it). A line whose URL or card path is `AU_PATH` (1,024) bytes or more, each `}` counted as five, is passed over: stock's `mcl_tidalStartPlayer` and `mclStartPlayer` both `strcpy` it into a `0x600`-byte stack buffer (`0x5bf9a8`, `0x5c023c`), then expand every `}` to `%0x7d` in place, unbounded (`toolsReplaceString`). `stream_poll` starts it on a 0 ms timer, as a folder's first song (`urls_start`, not during a scan or its dialog), and the session ends there: the queue is stock's. `app_urls_play` (`patch/tidal.c`) builds stock Tidal records as `load_titaltracks_ex` (`0x48670c`) does: an 88-byte `stSongInfo` zeroed, `REC_TIDAL_ID` `app:<gen>:<n>` (the queue's generation and the song's place), `REC_NAME` and `REC_TITLE` the title (`Unknown` without one, since stock prints them with `%s`), `REC_ARTIST`, `REC_ALBUM` and `REC_COVER` when given, `REC_PATH` empty for a URL or the card path, `REC_TYPE` 8 and `+0x38` `0xf1`, each `malloc`'d. `_deque_push_back` copies the record and `toolsFreeStSongInfo` frees the original, as stock does. It plays them as a Tidal page does, `play_folder(q, start, 0xf1)` (Now Playing with `{q, start, 0xf1, 2}`), and keeps the URLs (`au`) by generation.

For a `0xf1` queue `mclStartPlayer` calls `get_tidal_trackurl` (`0x483f28`, hooked as `ringnav_tidal_track`), which for an `app:` record (the queue's record at `MCL_POS`) does what stock does around a track itself (`app_track`), so the id never reaches Tidal's API or stock's stream thread: offline it returns `networkGetConnectStatus()` (`0x483f54`); online it calls `tidal_playurl(0)` and `mclStop()` (`0x483ff8`), then on a detached thread hands the URL to stock's `mcl_tidalStartPlayer` past the `tidal_start` hook (`stock_tidal_trampoline`), and then, as the stream thread does after it (`0x487b38`, `0x487b64`), pauses if `savestartbt` was set and sets `transposition` to 1, which arms Now Playing's online tick (`get_onlineid3info`, its notifications and auto-advance). These threads start one URL at a time (`au.start`), as stock's one thread does, and a later start drops one still waiting (`au.play`); an id from a queue replaced since has no URL, and the player stays stopped. A start also drops one still waiting, and a stream thread's Tidal fetch still in flight (`tidalfurlstart`, as stock at `0x483f5c`), so the last Now Playing asked for wins; a job waiting is dropped too when a queue has loaded since (`playback_loads`). A card-path record arms stock's auto-advance flag itself (`tidal_playurl(1)`: `mclAutoChange` only moves on with `-0x426c` above 0, which the stream thread's `transposition` sets for a URL), waits for a stream still inside stock's start to finish (`au.start`, its 100 or 150 ms start sleep), and returns, and `mclStartPlayer`, which has no `mclStop` on its local path, writes its own play command after it, playing `REC_PATH` as a local file, so its Now Playing is a local file's: no `get_onlineid3info`, no cover by URL. Next, Previous and a song's natural end come through `mclStartPlayer` the same way. Only stock's idle tick (`player_mainscheduling`, on the UI thread) reads the flag, and a UI-thread start is running before the tick's next pass; ponytail: a start from another thread (`player_save_start`'s jack and Bluetooth restarts) could in principle be passed by that tick while the player is stopped. `tidal_play` never sees an `app:` id, the trampoline being past its hook ([Tidal cache](#tidal-cache)). The cover: `get_onlineid3info` calls `player_set_coverinfo(REC_COVER, REC_NAME, 4)` at `0x493708`, and type 4 fetches from Tidal's image server with Tidal's session; `COVERINFO_CALL` (`tools/build.py`) turns that `jalr` into `jal app_coverinfo_call` (`move $a3, $s1; j app_coverinfo`), which passes type 2 for an `app:` record instead: curl to `/tmp/dlnadownpic.jpg` on stock's cover thread, scaled to 320 px. The stock routines this calls by address (`APP_URL_CALLS`, checked against the demo's symbols at build time) are not in `FUNCTIONS`, so `test/patch.py` runs them as stock's.
