Stock gives the rest: Now Playing's spinner shows while a `0xf1` stream buffers (`mclGetCacheBuffer() <= 0`, `0x53cf70`), and the player seeks with HTTP ranges (a Jellyfin `/Audio/{id}/stream?static=true` URL answers them). None of `get_tidal_trackurl`, `mclStartPlayer`, `mcl_tidalStartPlayer` or `get_onlineid3info` checks for a Tidal session, so no Tidal sign-in is needed. The capability word is `urls`. ponytail: a stream that fails leaves the player stopped, and it doesn't skip on (`mclAutoChange` returns at status 1, `0x5c1170`); online match and scrobbling skip `0xf1` queues, as for Tidal; an app's queue isn't kept for the next power-on; there is no gapless playback for `0xf0`–`0xf2`; Now Playing's heart is stock Tidal's for a song whose line names no item (**Hearts**, below). Checks in `test/patch.py`: a queue's records and start, another app's or a stray `.urls` never read, a start offline and online (the URL on its thread, the pause and tick after it, a later start or a queue loaded since dropping an earlier one), a card song arming the advance, a Tidal fetch stopped, a Tidal track still stock's, a replaced queue's old ids, files that aren't a queue, over-long URLs and card paths passed over, and the cover's type.

**Stream mode: lyrics for a URL queue.** Stock's lyrics loader and the tag lookup in `ringnav_lyric` (`patch/lyrics.c`) skip a `0xf1` queue, so a streamed song had none. The app can leave each song's lyrics, as its server gives them, in `/tmp/q2-<id>.lyrics/<n>.lrc` beside its queue, `<n>` the song's place among the songs kept (counted from 0, as the id's). The app empties the folder before naming a new queue and writes each file whole (temp + rename): a file carries no generation, and it is read once. `app_urls_play` keeps that folder with the queue (`au.lyr`: the queue's path with `.lyrics` for `.urls`), and for a `0xf1` track whose id is `app:<gen>:<n>` of the latest queue, `ringnav_lyric` reads `<n>.lrc` (`app_lyrics`, `file_text`: its first `LYRIC_TAG_MAX` bytes, a UTF-8 mark skipped) with the parser a tag's lyrics take, synced or plain. An id from a replaced queue, a Tidal track or a song with no file gets none. ponytail: the file is read once, as the track loads; a song whose file the app hasn't written yet (a skip far ahead just after the queue starts) shows none until it is played again. Checks in `test/patch.py`: synced and plain lyrics, an older queue's track, a song with no file and a Tidal track.

**Hearts.** Stock's heart click on Now Playing (`0x53c968`, `img_fav`'s, which `rate_bind` swaps for `rate_fav_click`, [Ratings](#ratings)) refuses queue types 2, 3 and `0xf2`; for `0xf1` it calls `tidal_collection` (`0x488d2c`), which toggles stock's `isFav_playing` byte and starts `addFavouriteTrack` or `removeFavouriteTrack` on a thread with `atoll` of the record's id (0 for `app:…`: Tidal's API, without a session), then sets the image `tidal_fav_add` or `tidal_fav_rm`; any other type is `manage_myfav` and `play_fav` or `play_unfav`. Now Playing's update (`0x53cf08`), on a track change or a forced refresh, draws a `0xf1` track's heart from `isFav_playing` (`0x53d178`), which otherwise only Tidal's favorites thread (`tidalGetFavoritesIdsThd`) sets, started by `get_tidal_fav_flag` (`0x493458`) when the Tidal page or its More opens, not per track. A URL queue's line may carry two more fields: the song's item, the app's own id (`au.items`; an empty one, or one of `AU_ITEM`, 128 bytes, or more, is none), and its heart (`au.fav`, `1` a favorite, a CR after it taken), kept per queue with its app's id from the queue's path (`au.app`). `app_track` sets `isFav_playing` as every `app:` song starts, before its URL or file goes to the player, so the page's update draws it: `au.fav` for one with an item, 0 for any other. A queue loading (`ringnav_load`) clears it again when an app's song set it last (`app_fav_load`, `au.hearts`), so a Tidal queue played next doesn't show the last app song's heart; stock's own value is left alone. A tap on the heart asks `app_fav` first: for a `0xf1` record whose id is `app:<gen>:<n>` of the latest queue with an item, it appends `item\t<0|1>\t<item>` to `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/fav.log` (`addon_fav`, `patch/addon.c`), then flips `au.fav` and `isFav_playing`, and `rate_fav_click` sets the image as stock's click would, stock's never called; a press the card refuses changes nothing and toasts "Favorite not saved". An `app:` record with no item (its line named none, or its queue was replaced) returns -3: the tap only toasts "This app has no favorites", so an app's song never reaches Tidal's API. Any other song's tap is stock's, as before. For a song on the card, each change Q2 Muse makes to My Fav (the heart, the picker's 5 in or out, the queue menu's Favorites rows and `rate_album_favs`) goes through `fav_told` to `addon_fav_path`, which reads every card app's `q2app` (each `.<id>` in the card's root: no scan needed, and a press is rare) for `favdir`, one folder name in the card's root (a Windows editor's `\r` dropped; empty, `.`, `..` or one with a `/` names none), and appends `path\t<0|1>\t<path>` for the first whose folder holds the song; a refusal toasts "Favorite not sent to the app", and an album's songs stop at the first. An album's Off tells the app only of songs that were in My Fav, so a song liked on the server and never hearted on the Q2 is not unliked. Each press is one `fwrite` of an LF and its line, appended on the UI thread with no fsync, as `scrobble_append`'s listen (the LF first ends a line a cut write left, so it never joins the next press); the app takes the file by renaming it ([librespot.md](librespot.md)). The word is `fav`. ponytail: stock's own batch-select Add to My Fav and its queue delete don't tell the app (the next change through Q2 Muse does, for that song); a synced song's heart is the Q2's, not the server's; a streamed song's heart is its queue's, so a change made on the server meanwhile shows only in the app's next queue; stock's `notifyFavor` (`0x525c70`, after its own toggle) isn't called for an app's press. Checks in `test/fw` (`test_tidal.py`, `test_addon.py`, `test_nav_library_pages.py`): the fields kept (a CRLF line, a field after them), the press flipped and written, an app's song without an item and every other song's heart, a refused press, the start's flag and a load clearing it (through `ringnav_load`), the favdir rule, a press after a cut one, and the synced song's line from the heart, the picker's 5 and 0, the hold menu's rows and an album's (stopping at a refusal; Off only for songs that were in My Fav); in `test/patch.py`: the start's `isFav_playing` and a load clearing it.

**Stream mode: what a URL queue plays.** An app that reports plays to its server (Jellyfin's `/Sessions/Playing`, Progress and Stopped) has to know which of its songs plays, and how; the queue is stock's once it starts. A queue whose header holds `now=1` (a field of its own: a tab before it, a tab or the line's end after; `au.now`) is told in `/tmp/q2-<id>.now`, `<seq><TAB><n><TAB><playing|paused|stopped><TAB><sec><TAB><length>` ([librespot.md](librespot.md) has the app's side). `urls_start` hands the session's app and its `.play` seq (`sm.seq`: up to the first space or control byte, 23 bytes at most) to `now_start` once `app_urls_play` played the queue; an earlier queue whose file says it plays is written `stopped` there first, whichever app's it was. `urls_now_poll`, in `addon_poll` every `ADDON_POLL_MS` whether the app runs or not, asks `app_urls_at` (`patch/tidal.c`) for the song's `n`: the record at `MCL_POS` of a `0xf1` queue (`MCL_TYPE`), as `get_tidal_trackurl` finds it, whose id is `app:<gen>:<n>` of the latest queue (`au.gen`) with `au.now` set; and reads the state and position as the sleep timer does (`mclGetPlayStatus`, `player_playtime_and_length`, `media_owner`). It writes the line whole (`blob_io` through `/tmp/q2-now.tmp`; tmpfs, so cheap on the UI thread) only on a change: another song, state or length at once, a position at once while paused or after a seek back, else after `NOW_STEP_S` (5 s); nothing while nothing changes, and nothing before the queue first plays. Another queue or player (`app_urls_at` -1, `media_owner` not 1) writes `stopped` at once, the player stopped `NOW_STOP_MS` (3 s, so not between songs, as `sleep_check` counts) writes it after that, once (`nw.live`); playing again writes `playing`. `addon_stop` writes `stopped` at once: Home's Rockbox row (`rockbox_open`) kills demo right after it, `/tmp` kept, and Stop Streaming Services stops a `0xf1` queue after it. A demo restarted with `/tmp` kept (a crash, the watchdog) starts with `nw` zeroed, so `now_sweep`, at the first `addon_poll`, turns the state of every `/tmp/q2-<id>.now` (a valid id) that says `playing` or `paused` into `stopped`, the rest of its line kept: an app never sees a play that never ends. `n` is the songs-kept index the record id and the lyrics use, so it needs no per-line field. Never the URL: it carries the app's token. ponytail: a stream that buffers past 3 s before it plays reads as `stopped`, then `playing`, for the same song; the position is the player's, so a seek forward under 5 s while playing is told at the next 5 s step. Checks in `test/fw/test_addon.py` and `test_tidal.py`: the header field, the song, states and steps, a stop between songs and a real one, another queue, player or older queue, a queue that didn't ask, the next queue (the same app's or another's), `addon_stop`, a restart's sweep, and the seq.

**Library update** (`patch/addon_library.c`). After a sync an app can ask for Update Local Music and the import of its playlists, so the user does neither by hand. It writes `/tmp/q2-<id>.library` whole (temp + rename): `<seq>` on its first line (at most 23 bytes; the file's end ends it when no newline follows), then `scan`, `import <path>` and `add <path>` lines, LF or CRLF, each path a `.m3u` (any case) directly in `/mnt/mmc/_explaylist_data/`, with no `/` in its name (so never `..`; a name with an ellipsis is fine), that exists, and whose playlist name (the file's name less `.m3u`) is at most 63 bytes (`LIB_NAME`). That limit is stock's: `ringnav_playlist_create` cuts a longer name into `char title[64]` and skips its duplicate check, so the stored name would never match the file's again, `import` would never replace it and `add` would never find it, and every sync would add another copy (a name in Chinese, Japanese or Korean reaches 64 bytes at 22 characters). `import` replaces a playlist of the same name, for a name the app owns (one it imported before); `add` imports the file only when no playlist has its name yet, and otherwise leaves that playlist alone, so a playlist of the user's with the same name is never replaced.

`addon_poll` calls `library_poll` once a pass, every `LIB_POLL_MS` (500 ms), for every app on the card (`addon_id`) whether it runs or not, so an app that exits right after its sync is still served, and no app's poll drives another's request. It reads each app's first line alone (the file's first 62 bytes); a seq that app hasn't had taken (each app's last one is kept, by id, in RAM; a seq `.done` already answers, as after demo restarts for Rockbox from Home with `/tmp` kept, is taken as done) reads the whole file once, and that read's own first line must be the seq: a file gone between the two reads, or replaced by a newer seq, is looked at again at the next poll, so no seq runs another's lines and none is answered without its own. The request is then checked whole: an error is written at once and nothing runs. A seq of 24 bytes or more, or an empty first line, is never run: it is answered `<seq> error Seq too long`, or ` error Missing seq` (no seq, so the line starts with a space), written again only once `.done` no longer holds that answer. One request runs at a time; a newer seq is taken once it is done.

The answer goes to `/tmp/q2-<id>.library.done`: `<seq> ok`, or `<seq> error <why>`, where `<why>` is `No memory card` (`/tmp/mmc_add` missing, or the import returned -2), `Unknown request: <line>`, `Not a playlist in /mnt/mmc/_explaylist_data: <path>`, `Name too long: <name>`, `Not found: <path>`, `Request too long` (the request fills `LIB_MAX`, 32 KB: more than 300 imports of the longest names), `Couldn't start the scan` or `Couldn't import <name>` (both below); then one `exists <path>` line for each `add` left alone, after an error too. It is built whole in one buffer and written with `blob_io` through `/tmp/q2-library.tmp`, renamed only once all of it is written and synced (`/tmp` full would cut the `exists` lines, and the app would take a user's same-named playlist for its own); otherwise `<seq> error Couldn't write the answer` is written the same way, and if that fails too, the temp is removed and nothing is published. The request is read into heap (`libup.list`, `LIB_MAX` for the request and `LIB_ANSWER` after it for the answer), taken at the first request and kept; its files are then moved to its start, each as its op (`i` import, `a` an add not looked up yet, `e` an add left alone) and its name, NUL-ended.

The scan and the import each wait for the same check (`library_safe`): nothing plays, as `ringnav_sleep`'s quiet check has it — the player, Spotify, the radio or a video (`media_playing`), AirPlay (`airplayGetFlag` 2) or the Bluetooth receiver (`bt__recv_pageflag` 2) — since the scan dialog's init, `dialog_updatemusic_dialog_init`, calls `player_stop` unconditionally at `0x4a2d78`, which stops paused playback too and loses its place: so the scan alone also waits while a local song is paused and the screen is on (`mclGetPlayStatus` 3 and `g_backlight_status`); with the screen off it goes ahead and stops the song, as Library → Update Local Music does; no scan runs (`library_scanning`, coverflow.c's: `SCAN_THREAD` set and `SCAN_DONE` clear); and every open window, the window manager's children less the status bar (`system_bar`), is on an allowlist of windows that show no library records: `home_page`, `stream_page`, `streamconf_page` and `streamsvc_page` (Streaming's Configuration and its provider pages), `addon_page` and `qrcode_page` (a card app's page and its QR code), `playing_page` (Now Playing, which plays its own copies, `mcl_pdeqplaylist`), and System and Playback settings' own pages, `sysset_page`, `display_page`, `backlight_page`, `lighttime_page`, `keylock_page`, `language_page`, `datetime_page`, `autotime_page`, `manualtime_page`, `standby_page`, `powermanager_page`, `sleepshutdown_page`, `about_page`, `bluetooth_page`, `btquality_page`, `btadjustvol_page`, `wifi_page`, `wifiset_page`, `netservice_page`, `playset_page`, `audiosetting_page`, `playmode_page`, `replaygain_page`, `filter_page`, `dsdoutput_page`, `memplay_page`, `usbvol_page`, `maxvol_page`, `bootvol_page`, `balance_page` and `equalizer_page`. Any other window holds the request until it closes, so the check fails safe: a dialog (`library_poll` also runs inside every modal loop, a toast's or a confirm's, and no request starts there); stock's Library pages, whose rows are records of the lists the import reloads (`p_deque_playlist` and `p_deque_showlist`, `load_localclass_list(0xf00b)`), so a press on one afterwards would take the wrong record; Q2 Muse's own library pages, which keep records read from the database the scan rebuilds; the user's own Update Local Music (`updatemusic_page`, awaiting its OK: no second dialog); USB storage; firmware update, reset, Wi-Fi transfer and the App Store; and any page added later until it is listed.

A request with neither line reports `ok` at once and runs nothing. The scan opens stock's own `dialog/updatemusic_dialog` (a zeroed 16-byte context, as stock's four callers do), a modal dialog: its init starts the scan's thread, and its own loop runs until it closes. The state is `L_SCAN` before the call; a `library_poll` from inside that loop (`libup.busy` set) runs nothing but notes the scan it sees (`scan_seen`: the thread running, or `updatemusic_dialog` open), as does a check right after the call. The scan is over once it was seen and is gone; one never seen (the dialog didn't open) is answered `Couldn't start the scan`, never `ok` without a scan. Then the payload loads Library → Playlists' list itself (`ringnav_localclass(0xf00b)`), looks each `add`'s name up in it as stock's replace does (`library_adds`: the file's name less `.m3u`, compared whole with each playlist's), drops the ones found from the import, and calls stock `importPlayList` (`0x5186c8`), as the Import Playlists row does; with nothing left to import it is not called, and no toast follows. Stock stops at a create that fails (-1: a database error, or the 100 playlists' cap) and returns 1 as if done, so afterwards each imported file's name must be in the reloaded `p_deque_playlist`; the first that isn't gives `Couldn't import <name>`. The result is written to `.library.done` first, then toasted ("Playlists updated", or the error): stock's `msginfo_dialog`, like Update Local Music's dialog, runs a loop of its own that polls again, so `library_poll` is guarded (`libup.busy`) and a nested poll runs nothing. For each file stock looks its name up in `p_deque_playlist` (`checkPlayListByName`, a `strcmp` against each playlist's name) and deletes a match, header (`deletePlaylist`) and entries (`deleteAllMusicByPlaylist`), before it creates the playlist again (`createPlayListItem`, Q2 Muse's `ringnav_playlist_create`) and adds the file's songs, their tags read from the files, so a playlist of the same name is replaced, not doubled. `p_deque_playlist` is empty until Playlists first loads it, hence the load: without it the name is missed, the create fails on the duplicate name (-2) and stock adds the songs to playlist -2. The playlist takes the file's name without its extension (`toolsGetDirectoryM3u8` cuts it at the last dot; paths are `/mnt/mmc/_explaylist_data/<file>`), and absolute `/mnt/mmc/...` entries are accepted. Stock lists the whole folder; `importPlayList`'s `toolsGetDirectoryM3u8` call (`M3U_DIR_CALL`, `0x518768`, a `jalr` with `addiu a0, a0, 0x12e0` in its delay slot, which stays) becomes `jal addon_m3u_dir`, which keeps only the records whose path is `/mnt/mmc/_explaylist_data/` and an `i` name of the request while `libup.only` is set, around the app's import alone. Stock's own Import Playlists row is unaffected and still imports the whole folder. Limits (`ponytail:`): a scan canceled with the dialog's Back still reports `ok`, as stock keeps no cancel flag; the import reads every song's tags on the UI thread, as stock's Import row does, so a long playlist freezes the UI for a while.

<a id="artist-page"></a>**An artist's page.** Under a set with the menu sheet (OLED's), a level whose reply has `shuffle` and `radio` actions on an `artist:` context (q2-subsonic's artist page, reached by Go to Artist, Now Playing's artist tap or the app's Artists) is drawn as the design's artist page ([oled-design.md](oled-design.md#artist-page)) instead of as its rows: `artist_view` builds it, `patch/artist_page.c` draws it. `lv_t.lay` says how a level is drawn (`LAY_ARTIST`, and `LAY_ALBUMS` and `LAY_TOP` for the pages its rows open) and `lv_t.stop` which of the pair is lit, so both survive the rebuilds an action or a Back makes. The header (`hero_open`) names the level's title and counts the reply's album rows; its monogram stands 6 px above the status row's foot, painted by the header on the page's full-bleed window under the row's overlay. The pair (`pair_open`) is two stops above the list, as Songs' Shuffle row is: `pair_key` runs in `ringnav` after `shuffle_key`, and `pair_holds` hides the list's bar while a stop is lit. Albums is no reply row: its click context is `AR_ALBUMS`, which pushes the level's own op and arguments again as `LAY_ALBUMS`, whose album rows are sorted newest first by the year their subtitle starts with and drawn as `cover_row`s with the app's catalogue cover (`/mnt/mmc/.<id>/covers/<album id>.jpg`, [server-library.md](server-library.md#covers)) when the file is there, a placeholder otherwise; the covers leave the image manager when the level drops its reply. A cover row keeps its reply row's index (`_ar_row`) for `addon_hold`, and `busy_row`, `relabel` and `append` leave a laid-out level alone or draw it again whole. Play/Pause held on the page opens `modal_actions` (menu_modal.c) with the reply's sync rows (`toggle`, `quality`, `sync`), each pressed as its row would be. With the caps word `artist` the app adds the rows of [librespot.md](librespot.md#artist-rows): `artist_view` takes the header's counts and genre from the `about` row (else it counts the album rows), and offers `singles`, `similar` and `songs` as drill-down rows, each opening a level whose `lay` `drill_lay` sets (`LAY_ALBUMS`, `LAY_SIMILAR`, `LAY_TOP`); a count is the number its subtitle starts with (`lead_count`). A song row's album and length come from its subtitle (`song_parts`: the first part of digits and colons is the length, all before it the album) and its cover from the `album:` word its context ends in (`row_album`), read only when that word is there, so an older app's rows show their title alone; `cover_after` draws the album after the title where 30 px are left, and `cover_mono` gives a Similar Artists row its monogram and chevron. The covers of a songs page leave the image manager as the Albums page's do.

<a id="album-page"></a>**An album's page.** Under the same sets, a level whose reply has a `play` action on `album:<id> 0`, a `shuffle` action on `album:<id>` and an `about` info row (q2-subsonic's album page with the caps word `album`, [librespot.md](librespot.md#album-rows)) is drawn as the design's album page ([oled-design.md](oled-design.md#album-page)): `album_view` builds it as `LAY_ALBUM`, before `artist_view` looks for an artist. The header is `hero_open`'s with `hero_cover`: the album's catalogue cover (`album_cover` on the Shuffle row's `album:` id) drawn by `hero_art` cropped square, scaled to 64 px and its corners scrubbed to the color behind, in the header's paint; the header's own destroy lets the decoded cover go. The pair is Play and Shuffle, `lv_t.stop` starting on Play. The song rows (an `action` `play` on a `song:` context) become `track_row`s numbered in the reply's order, their length read from the subtitle (`sub_parts`, `song_parts` without its `album:` check), the number and length painted by `artist_paint`. Play/Pause held anywhere on it opens `artist_hold`'s sync rows, which take an `album:` toggle as an `artist:` one. A reply without all three rows keeps the plain rows, so an older app's album is as before.

<a id="library-album-page"></a>**A Library album's page.** Stock's two album pages, `albuminfo_page` and `playerjumpinfo_page`, are dressed in place (`patch/library_album.c`), as their UI loads (`ringnav_ui_load` calls `album_local_load` before stock's init runs): their navbar and Songs' action row (the Shuffle row) are hidden, the list (`list_view` with its `scroll_view`, or `table_view` with its `music_table_client`) moved under the pair by `drill_list`, and the header and pair made in the window. Stock's rows stay: their clicks, the album track drawing of `song_rows.c`, the hold menu and the playing colors. The header's lines need the songs, which stock's init loads into `p_deque_showlist` after the UI, so `album_local_paint` fills them at the header's paint (`lb_fill`) whenever the page is on top and the songs' count is not the one last read: the first song's album and album artist (else artist), its year (`songtable` by `fileurl`, the first four digits, or `catalogue_np_info` for a server song), the count and the sum of `duration_seconds`. The cover is `album_cover_url`'s ([Album covers](#album-covers)) for the first eight songs; while it fetches one, `lb_art_wait` draws the header again once it lands, and `lb_fill` reads it then (`lb.art`, `album_cover_gen`). Play is `play_folder` of the songs from the first, as class `0xff10` (Cover Flow's album tracks); Shuffle is `shuffle_play`. `bar_title_of` gives the page no title. One page is dressed at a time: `artist_page.c` keeps one header, so the page dresses again at each `EVT_WINDOW_FOREGROUND` (back from an artist or album page over it), keeping its lit stop. Cover Flow's album tracks keep their own page.

<a id="album-covers"></a>**Album covers.** A list that names an album by its songs, the album page's header and Up Next's rows (`un_cover`), takes its cover from `album_cover_url` (`patch/album_cover.c`), in this order: Subsonic's saved cover of a server album (`catalogue_cover`), Cover Flow's cached `art_path` of `album_key` when Cover Flow made it and it is not empty, the cover Now Playing shows when the song playing is of that album (its parsed tags' `tags_key` is the album's `album_key`, and `now_cover` answers only once the player's cover thread parsed that very song, so another album's never shows; AWTK's bitmap of the player's file is dropped first, as every song's cover is written to that one file, and `un_unload` drops it too through `now_cover_forget`), else none yet. A card album, or a server album Subsonic has not fetched a cover of, was grey until Cover Flow drew it (the user's, 2026-11-17: "Idle Moments"). With none and no Cover Flow note of no art, a detached thread (`ac_worker`, one at a time; nothing when Cover Flow's folder has under `card_space`'s room, checked there, not on the UI thread) fills Cover Flow's cache for the album as `build_art` does (`album_art`: the embedded art, a folder image, ffmpeg) from the first of the songs with a copy on the card: a song's own file, or for a server row a download of it in its app's stream cache, found by its sid in the cache's top folder and the three levels under it (not a `.part` or `.tmp` still arriving) (`<account>/<quality>/<shard>`, q2-subsonic's `cache.go`'s 16 shard folders; `ac_find`, as the car's `stream_picture` globs them, [car remote streams](#car-remote-streams)). A song whose copy has no art gets Cover Flow's note of none, as `build_art` leaves it, but not a server album's, whose cover Subsonic may still fetch; an album with no copy at all is not asked again (`AC_NONE`, 4, the last ones). Each cover written moves `album_cover_gen`, which Up Next's `un_sig` and the album page's `lb_fill` read. ponytail: the thread's search reads the stream cache's folders on the card, a few dozen `readdir`s; the songs looked at are the first eight.

### Card app sync

A card app says what it syncs in its state file (`/tmp/q2-<id>.state`, the file that carries `hold=` and `server=`): `sync=check` while it checks its server or its metadata, `sync=down DONE TOTAL` while it downloads songs (DONE of TOTAL in any unit; q2-subsonic writes bytes), and no key while idle. `poll_one` reads it with `hold=` every `ADDON_POLL_MS` from the read it already makes (`sync_read`; past 20 bits both numbers halve together until the total fits, so the permille is 32-bit arithmetic), a stopped app's key goes with its `hold`, and `addon_sync` answers for the status row: a download ahead of a check, with its permille. The row shows turning arrows (`arrows-clockwise-bold` in Text Primary, 30 frames of a half turn a second) for a check and a ring filling in the accent from 12 o'clock with `arrow-down-bold` in it for a download ([Status row slots](#status-row-slots)). ponytail: like `hold=`, only the file's first `QR_RAW - 2` bytes are read and an app writes its keys in name order, so a `sync=` behind a sign-in's long `qr=` reads as none; q2-subsonic never signs in and syncs at once.

### Card app reach

A card app says whether its server can be reached in its state file: `reach=down <code>` while it can't be, until a request to it succeeds, and `srverr=<unix> <code>`, each failure to toast once. `<code>` is an HTTP status, `none` (no answer: a refused or timed-out connection, a body that stopped) or `dns` (a name that doesn't resolve). q2-subsonic (`reach.go`) sets `reach=` for no answer, `dns` and a proxy's 502, 503 or 504, and writes `srverr=` as the server goes out of reach and for each streamed song it gives up for a server's reason (a 5xx of the server's own too); an answer from the server itself, a Subsonic error or a 404, changes neither. `poll_one` reads both with `sync=` (`reach_read`): `app_t.reach` for the status row's offline glyph (`addon_offline`: a running app's, and only while Wi-Fi is connected, [Status row slots](#status-row-slots)), and a `srverr=` new to this demo (`app_t.srverr`, the last read) and no more than `REACH_FRESH_S` (10 s) from the clock's now becomes `toast_later("srvtoast", ...)`: "Server error 502", "Server not answering" or "Server not found", the icon toast's `cloud-slash-fill` in Warning ([oled-design](oled-design.md#dialogs-and-toasts)); none with Wi-Fi off, where the missing Wi-Fi glyph says why. A stopped app's `reach` goes with its `hold`. ponytail: as with `sync=`, only the file's first `QR_RAW - 2` bytes are read, so a `reach=` behind a sign-in's long `qr=` reads as none; a signed-out app asks no server.


### Sync offline

A Library item a signed-in card app's server has can be chosen for the app's next Sync from the Library itself (the user's, 2026-11-19): the hold menu of a song, an album, an artist (the Artists list, `0xf004`) or a server playlist, and Now Playing's ⋯ for the song playing, has **Sync Offline**, or **Stop Syncing Offline** for an item already chosen (`patch/offline.c`, `nav/hold_menu.c` `QA_OFFLINE`, `onlinematch.c` `more_rows`, `menu_modal.c` `modal_more`'s symbol). The item's server identity is `catalogue_offline_key`'s: a song's sid from the index (`cat_lookup`, a linked card file too), an album's id from the path of one of its server rows (`cat/<album>/<sid>`, matched by album and album artist or artist), an artist by name (`artistname <name>`: the catalogue has no artist ids), a playlist's id from `cat.serverlists`. Its state is the app's own list, `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/offline.txt` (`<kind>\t<id>\t<name>` a line, read up to 64 KB, an artist by name in any case; `library\tall` hides the row, as Entire Library holds everything), `offline_state`. Only an app whose `q2app` says `offline=1` gets the row (`addon_offline_ok`). A press asks the app (`addon_offline_ask`): `/tmp/q2-<id>.offline`, `<seq> <add|remove> <kind> <id>`, written only once its browse socket is there (an app takes a request present at its start as answered), the app started first when it isn't running (`addon_wake`); `poll_one`'s `offline_read` sends a waiting request and toasts the answer, `offlineack=<seq> <words>` in the app's state file, once (`toast_later`, whose text holds 96 bytes for an album's name), or "<name> didn't answer" after `OFF_WAIT_MS` (25 s). One request waits at a time; a new press replaces it.
## Radio

Now Playing's Radio (the antenna in the OLED row under the progress bar, `np_bar.c`) starts an endless radio of songs like the playing one; the car's `StartRadio` does the same ([remote-protocol: Radio](remote-protocol.md#radio)). `patch/song_radio.c` owns it.

**The tap.** `np_mode_click` runs `song_radio_tap` on a timer (a radio's queue opens Now Playing). With no radio playing it starts one seeded by the playing song (`playing`: `mcl_pdeqplaylist` at `MCL_POS`) from its place (`player_playtime_and_length`); on the pill it stops the radio, the songs queued playing on, and toasts "Radio Off". `song_radio_on` is the pill: the app's radio (`addon_radio`, its state file's `radio=`) or the local one.

**A server song's radio is its app's.** `addon_radio_start` (`addon.c`) finds the app: the one whose folder holds the song's path (a streamed file, a Library server row's `cat/` path), else the playing queue's app, when its `q2app` says `radio=1` (the `radio` word in `/tmp/q2-addon.caps` tells the app the firmware asks). It starts the app if needed (`addon_wake`) and writes `/tmp/q2-<id>.radio`, one line, `<seq> start <path>` or `<seq> stop`, only once the app's socket is there (the app takes a request already there at its start as answered, as a `.catplay`). The app answers in its state file, `radioack=<seq> <code>`: 0 started (or stopped), 1 not its song, 2 no radio, 3 no one signed in to its server. `song_radio_poll` reads it: on 1 it plays the local radio of the same song if it still plays, on 3 it toasts "Sign in to use Radio" and starts no local radio, on 2 or after `SR_WAIT_MS` (25 s) it toasts "Radio isn't available for this song". The path is the seed: a streamed song (the player's id 0) is its stream-cache file, whose name carries the server's id between its last brackets ([stream_path.h](#car-remote-streams)), and the app reads the id there (q2-subsonic's `songOf`). The app plays the seed then the server's similar songs as a new queue (`.play`), and says `radio=<the seed's title>` while it plays; q2-subsonic asks `getSimilarSongs2` with the song's id, adds more when 10 or fewer are left after the one playing, and leaves out the last 200 songs played or queued (its `radio.go`).

**The local radio**, for any other song, one the app declines, or one whose app is too old to play radios (no `radio=1`: q2-subsonic before q2-v1.0): the library's songs (`staged(songs_unsorted)`, server rows and videos left out) by the seed's artist, then those of its genre (`REC_STYLE`), compared without ASCII case, each group shuffled, none of the last `SR_RECENT` (128) played or queued, `SR_BATCH` (25) at a time. Songs are told apart by their path's FNV-1a (`key`), not `REC_ID`: a queue's records and the library's number one song differently, and by id a radio of a song from Songs queued that song again. The queue is the seed then those (the seed playing on, as below; a seed the car names that isn't playing, `play_folder`), with Now Playing's shuffle and repeat off (put back when the radio ends); when `SR_LOW` (10) or fewer are left after the one playing, `song_radio_poll` adds another batch at the queue's end (`playback_queue_insert`, an app's Add), and looks again `SR_RETRY_MS` later when it found none. Another queue (`playback_loads` moved) ends it. A new radio that finds nothing but songs played lately forgets them and picks again. One that finds nothing toasts "No similar songs on this Q2 Muse", or, for a server song whose app has no `radio=1` (`addon_radio_missing`), "Update <app> to use Radio": the library rarely holds a server song's artist, and on 2026-11-16 the first message, from q2-subsonic v0.9 on a streamed song, read as the server having no similar songs when it had many.

**The seed plays on.** A radio of the song playing (Now Playing's tap, the car's `StartRadio` with no song) leaves that song alone: the queue keeps its row, and every other row is replaced by the radio's songs (`playback_queue_rest`, `playback.c`: the other rows popped, the playing one moved to place 0, stock's indices remapped as Up Next's Clear remaps them, a preload of the next row closed, Playing Next emptied, a Shuffle Songs mode put back as a load puts it back, then the radio's songs added as an app's Add). Nothing loads, so the player is sent no new song (no `set-songurl`), and the song plays on with no gap and no seek, under q2player as under the stock player, which both take the next song from the queue as it ends. The local radio does this itself (`local_start`). An app's radio starts with the seed, so its playlist session (`addon.c`) asks `song_radio_keeps` of its first entry: when an app's radio of the song playing was asked at the tap (still waiting for its answer, or answered with no queue loaded since) and the entry is that song (`catalogue_same_song`: the same path, the same server row, or two downloads with the same app and sid, [stream_path.h](#car-remote-streams)), the entry is passed over, not waited for, `sm.keep` is set, and the session's first songs replace the rows after the playing one as above; `sm.first` takes the playing row's path, so the session's later songs join the same queue. A session whose first entry is any other song (a song the car names, which plays from its start) loads its queue as before, and once the radio's queue plays the seed (a queue loaded since the tap, its song at the seed's path) it is sought to the place it had at the tap (`player_seek_time`), within `SR_SEEK_MS` (30 s).

**While a radio plays** the antenna is the blue pill and shuffle and repeat are dimmed and ignore taps and the Centre cycle ([oled-design](oled-design.md#now-playing)); `/tmp/coda-rc.now` carries `radio=1` for the car. Either radio plays with shuffle and repeat off, put back when it ends: the local one sets them in `local_start` and puts them back in `local_end`; an app's is followed by `app_modes` in `song_radio_poll`, which turns them off when `addon_radio` first says radio= and back on when it stops saying so (the app's stop, its songs run out, another queue loaded). Left on under an app's radio, Repeat One would play each song twice in a row and shuffle would reorder the radio's queue, while the dimmed buttons can't turn either off. A local radio started while an app's holds the modes keeps the modes from before the app's. ponytail: the modes held are in RAM only, so a radio cut by a power-off leaves shuffle and repeat off, as a local radio's does.

Checks: `test/fw/test_song_radio.py` (the local radio's order, the seed playing on with no load or seek, the pill and its stop, another queue ending it, the refill with nothing twice, the car's `radio` commands, a streamed song's request carrying its stream path, the server's "none" and a too-old app's toasts), `test/fw/test_nav_painters.py` (the tap runs `song_radio_tap`), `test/fw/test_addon.py` (the app's request and answer, and its radio of the song playing keeping that song), `test/unit/test_coda_rc_daemon.py` and `test_coda_rc_lib.py` (`StartRadio` and `NowPlaying.radio`). ponytail: an artist's radio from the car is one of its songs' radios, so a server-only artist's needs its app signed in; the app's own artist Radio row seeds `getSimilarSongs2` with the artist.

## Bundled apps

The firmware carries the Subsonic app, so it is in Streaming with nothing installed, and it is the firmware's alone: the App Store no longer lists it, and a new version of it comes in a firmware update. `tools/build.py` installs each app in `BUNDLED_APPS` from its release zip, pinned by version, size and SHA-256 and read from `--apps` (`~/.cache/q2-apps`; [building](building.md#bundled-apps)), into `/usr/lib/q2apps/<id>` on the read-only root filesystem: the zip's `.<id>/` files (`q2-<id>`, `q2app`, the icons), a `version` file holding the pinned version (`q2-v1.0`), a `bundle` file naming the zip, its SHA-256, the program's SHA-256 and the zip's commit stamp (`bundle_record`; `cat` it on a Q2 to say which build runs), and the app's own `run` changed by `bundled_launcher` in two lines, each checked to occur once: its data folder is the card's `/mnt/mmc/.<id>`, made if missing, not the launcher's own folder, and `/tmp/q2-<id>.bin` is a link to the image's binary, not a copy (7.9 MB of RAM for q2-subsonic). The app's credentials, catalogue, covers and log stay on the card, as they do for a card install. A `BUNDLED_APPS` entry's last field, `builtin` (Subsonic's is `True`), adds a `builtin` file holding `1` beside the app, which `addon_builtin` reads; a zip that ships one of its own is refused. The manifest records each app's version, zip, SHA-256, `builtin`, the program's SHA-256 and the stamp (`bundled_apps`).

**Which copy runs** (`addon_dir` in `patch/addon.c`): for a builtin app, always the firmware's, whatever the card holds. A card copy of it, from an App Store install or unzipped by hand before the firmware carried the app (`q2-subsonic`, `run`, `q2app` and the icons in the card's `.subsonic`), is never run or listed, and is left where it is rather than deleted: the folder is the app's data folder too (sign-in, settings, catalogue, downloads), so nothing is deleted from it, and a firmware without the app still finds a working copy there. Each Streaming scan deletes the App Store's tag and file list for a builtin app (`builtin_untag`: `/mnt/mmc/.q2/apps/<id>.tag` and `.files`), so nothing about the old install is left in the App Store's records. With the card's copy out of the way, Radio never says "Update Subsonic to use Radio" for an old card copy (`addon_radio_missing` reads the running copy's `q2app`, the firmware's, which says `radio=1`). For any other carried app, the card's `.<id>` runs when it holds the app (`q2-<id>`) and either the firmware carries none or the card's is newer; else the firmware's. Newer is the card copy's App Store tag (`/mnt/mmc/.q2/apps/<id>.tag`, [Q2 Shelf](#q2-shelf)) against the carried `version` file, compared by `addon_version_cmp`: the dotted numbers after a `v` and a digit (else from the first digit), in turn, a missing one as 0. A card copy without a tag was unzipped by hand and counts as newer, since whoever put it there chose it. So an App Store update past the carried version takes over, and an older install left on the card is passed over without being deleted. `addon_scan` reads both folders and keeps each app's chosen one (one Streaming row), and every reader of an app's manifest (`addon_q2app`: Go to, scrobbling, favorites, the server library's `catalogue.c`, Storage's `storage.c`) reads the chosen copy's `q2app`. Those readers find apps by their folder on the card, so a carried app the card has no `.<id>` for yet is listed in Streaming but not in the Server Library or Storage until its first start makes the folder. ponytail: for an app that is not builtin, a hand install shadows the carried app forever, whatever its version; reading the binary's own version would lift that.

**A new version** of a builtin app ships as a new `BUNDLED_APPS` pin in a firmware update ([building](building.md#bundled-apps), [releasing](releasing.md#the-app-list)); nothing on the card or in `sources.list` changes.

## Server library

While it is signed in to its server (its `credentials` file on the card), a card app that declares `catalogue=1` in its `q2app` (the [Subsonic app](https://github.com/andsuor/q2-subsonic) does) supplies a music server's songs and playlists, and they join the Library's lists beside the card's. The firmware never speaks to the server; the file formats are the contract in [server-library.md](server-library.md), and all of it is `patch/catalogue.c`. `ADDON_CAPS` carries `catalogue` and `ratings`, so an app writes nothing until it sees them. There is no setting (the user's, 2026-11-19: "there is no toggle, that just how it works"; an older build's `[Q2POD] LIBRARYSOURCE` is never read): with no app signed in nothing is indexed, attached or unioned. `catalogue_poll` (from `addon_poll`, once a second, `CAT_DARK_MS` (10 s) while the screen is off, nothing plays and no catplay waits on its app; with the screen off and no app's rows indexed it looks at nothing, so a Q2 with no server signed in leaves the card alone while dark; each app's `catalogue.tsv` head is read once a poll) looks for such apps every 10 s, reads each one's `/tmp/q2-<id>.state` for `server=down`, and starts a job when an app's `catalogue.tsv` has a new `seq` (header `#Q2CAT/1`), or when `library_gen` has moved since the last match (Update Local Music, and the scans after USB storage and Wi-Fi transfer, move it around each stock scan), never while a scan runs or with the card away.

**The apps' state and needslib** (`patch/library_settings.c`). Apps that read `/tmp/q2-addon.library` (an older q2-subsonic pauses its Show in Library on `local`) find `server` and a newline, written atomically (`blob_io`) at every Streaming scan just before the caps file (so an app that finds the caps word `libsource` finds the file too; every app start scans first). A `needslib` row, an older app's "needs the server's songs" press, is an action: its action goes at once, with nothing asked. **Signed in and out** (`cat_signed_in`): only a signed-in app's `catalogue.tsv` is imported, and stock's connections attach `cat` (`catalogue_attach`), and server playlists' changes and covers are read (`catalogue_playlist_sync`, `catalogue_playlist_covers`), only while some app's rows are indexed (`catalogue_has`); an app with rows in the index (`cat_ix.apps`, a bit per slot) that is no longer signed in, or whose `catalogue.tsv` is gone (q2-subsonic's Sign Out deletes both), gets a job with no seq (`cat_start(slot, 0)`): it copies the old file less the app's rows (`copy_old`), imports nothing, matches and builds the index again, and answers nothing; with no rows left nothing is attached.

**Autostart** (`cat_autostart`). Each catalogue app that is signed in is started in the background once, by the same path as a catplay's start (`addon_wake`: the caps and state files written first, then its `run`), at the first app scan with the card in after boot; it idle-exits as it does from its page, and Smart Wi-Fi keeps the radio up while it runs (`addon_running`). Signed in is the app's card folder holding its `credentials` file, which the firmware looks for and never opens (`catalogue_signed`): the app's status file is in `/tmp`, empty at boot, and signing out deletes the file. A signed-out app starts nothing.

**The job** (`cat_worker`, its own pthread and SQLite connection on `/mnt/data/database.db`) writes a whole new `/mnt/mmc/.q2pod/catalogue.db.new`: the old file's tables less the imported app's rows, then the app's file streamed a line at a time (`import_file`; a line over 8 KB is skipped), 64 songs to an insert, in one transaction with the new file's journal off. Server rows go to `serverall` with `songtable`'s columns (ids from `0x40000000`, a 16 M span per app; `fileurl` `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/cat/<album id>/<sid>.<suffix>`, a hidden path no file has, so ratings, favorites, playlists and play counts key on it as on a card path; `filename` the title alone, since stock's Search lists a song by its file name, and a card file's has the title in it) and the rest to `servermeta` (sid, seconds, size, MusicBrainz id, suffix, offline copy, the normalised tags' hashes). The header's `rows=` must equal the `s`, `p` and `i` lines read, so a file cut short is answered `<seq> error Read N of M rows`, not imported as a smaller library. SQL is built against the buffer's end less 64 bytes of slack (`PUT`, `sq`), and a statement that did not fit is never run, so a cut `delete` can't lose its `where`. Then the duplicate match (below), `servertable` (what the lists read) rebuilt as `serverall` less the duplicates, every app's playlists, and the index. The UI thread joins it in `cat_swap`: it detaches `cat` from stock's shared connection, renames the new file over the old, takes the index, answers `/tmp/q2-<id>.catalogue.done` (`<seq> ok <rows>` or `<seq> error <why>`), and bumps `library_gen` so open lists query again. A scan that moved `library_gen` while the job ran leaves the match due again (`cat.gen` is the generation the job started at).

**At boot** (`cat_load`, `load_worker`). The index lives in RAM, and the Library's queries read `servertable` only while one is built (`cat_live`, `cat_ready`), so a boot whose first job was the import showed the card's songs alone until that import ended: on the owner's Q2 (9,198 songs, about a dozen on the card) "the library is empty" after a restart for an update (2026-11-24), and in the emulator with that catalogue and the import held 40 s, Songs listed the card fixture's 13 songs while Albums, opened after the import, listed the server's. The first poll with the card and a catalogue app found now reads the file the last session left, as it is: a job that attaches `catalogue.db` as `nw`, builds the index from it (`ix_build`) and reads `serverseq` (each app's seq that file was imported at, written by every import and carried by `copy_old`), writing nothing. Its swap takes the index and those seqs, so the server's rows are in the Library from then (293 ms after the job started in the emulator), and a catalogue at the seq the file holds is not imported again; a newer one is imported as before, the old rows shown until its swap, which replaces file and index together. A file from before `serverseq` is read the same and its catalogue imported again behind it. The log says what the Library holds and each import: `I cat library at boot: 13 card songs, 9199 server rows kept from the last import (81), read in 293 ms` (the emulator's figure), `I cat catalogue import started: subsonic seq 82, 9199 server rows shown meanwhile`, and `I cat catalogue import done: subsonic seq 82, 13779 rows in N ms, 9199 server rows shown until then, M now` (or `failed` and why). A late UI pass in the swap, in `catalogue.avail`'s read or in `ratings.in`'s is named `catalogue swap`, `catalogue avail` or `catalogue ratings` ([UI pass watchdog](#ui-pass-watchdog)).

**Nothing yet.** While a signed-in app's rows are on their way with none shown (`catalogue_filling`: the boot's read, or an app's first import), a press on the Library's All Songs, Album or Artist row, on the Library page or Home's Library list, opens nothing yet (`library_row_wait`, from `ringnav_dispatch` for a tap and from Centre's `confirm_center`): the [loading wait](#loading-wait) holds that window captioned "Loading server songs…", and once the rows are in the press is made again; Return gives it up and opens nothing.

**Duplicates** (`cat_match`, `cat_same`): the card's songs are read from `songtable` once per job and sorted by their normalised title (`cat_norm`: lower case, letters and digits only, a "feat." part and trailing bracketed or dashed edition notes such as "(Remastered 2009)" or "- 2012 Stereo Mix" cut, unless the note says live). A server song is compared only with card songs of its title, and with untagged card files of its size (stat'd once per job). Strongest first: equal MusicBrainz recording ids (`cat_mbid` reads the first 128 KB of the card file for a Vorbis `MUSICBRAINZ_TRACKID` or an ID3 `UFID` owned by `http://musicbrainz.org`; when both have one and they differ, nothing weaker is tried); equal size, suffix and a length within 1 s (`ringnav_statx`, taglib's length); equal normalised artist (or album artist), album, title and track and a length within 2 s. A match sets `servermeta.dup` to the card path, which leaves the row out of `servertable` and links its sid to the card file for ratings. A size alone that differs stops nothing: a retagged copy differs. ponytail: a tagged card file whose title differs from the server's is never a candidate, even at equal size; indexing every card file by size would stat the whole card at each job.

**Where it is read.** `serverall` and `servertable` are indexed by `fileurl` (`serverall_url`, `servertable_url` in `SCHEMA`, so every import's new file has them, a catalogue made before them included at the boot's first import): Up Next's tags (`catalogue_copy_tags`), Now Playing's info and `fav_set` look rows up by path, a search where the plan was a scan of every row (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` in `test_serverall_is_looked_up_by_fileurl_through_an_index`). `stock_db_open` (stock's shared connection, its `0x5c8d30` reopen, and the payload's other opens through it) attaches the file as `cat` while a signed-in app's rows are indexed and the file exists (there is no setting; stock's scan thread opens through it too); `cat_live` attaches it again to a new stock handle. `library_query`'s music loads read `(select * from songtable where <music> union all select * from servertable)` (`catalogue_rows`), and Era's SQL each `from songtable` as the union (`catalogue_union`, with `cat` attached to Era's own connection). Stock's Search (`SearchMusicByName` and its kin, a `like '%<text>%'` query through `toolsQueryDbTable` outside a music load) reads the union too (`catalogue_search`), so server songs are found; its rows are grayed (below, from `p_deque_searchshowlist`, Search's own results, which each tab of its `tab_button_group` fills: `ringnav_search_rows`), and a press on a song goes through `search_track_row_on_click`'s play check. Home's song count (`library_count`, Era's path) counts the union; the Updating page counts `main.songtable`, the card's files the scan walks. Everything off the UI thread (stock's scan thread through `stock_db_open` and `library_query`, the count and Era workers) reads the index the UI thread swapped in (`cat_ready`, `cat_live`: rows indexed and the file there). The index (`cat_ix`, built by the job): every server row by its `fileurl`'s 64-bit FNV-1a, and every linked card file by its path, each with the sid, seconds and offline copy, sorted for a binary search, plus a by-sid order for `catalogue.avail` and `ratings.in`.

**Availability.** A server row can play when it has an offline copy (its `local` from the catalogue, then each `catalogue.avail` line in order: `<sid>\t<path>` sets one, `-<sid>` clears it, and a line naming the copy the row has already adds nothing; the file is read on from where it stopped, and whole again when it shrinks or after an import; a copy's path finds its row by a binary search on the path's hash, `copies_build` making that index on the UI thread each time `local_gen` moves and publishing it whole, as stock's cover thread reads it too: 1.8 microseconds a lookup where the walk of every row took 21, at 9,199 rows and 2,000 copies on the host build), or when online: `networkGetConnectStatus()` above 0, or [Smart Wi-Fi](#smart-wi-fi)'s radio off or coming back (`smart_wifi_back`), and no app's `server=down`. A press while Smart Wi-Fi has the radio off wakes it (`smart_wifi_wait`) and waits for the link (`cp_link`, polled by `catplay_poll`) before it starts the app or writes the catplay; no link `SMART_CONNECT_MS` (15 s) on, the list plays offline. **Grayed rows:** `ringnav_table_load`, as stock binds a pooled Library row to its index in `p_deque_showlist`, calls `catalogue_bind`, which keeps the row in a 48-entry set when its record is a song that can't play, or an album that can't (`catalogue_album_unavailable`, when the showlist is albums: `g_class_type` `CLASS_ALBUMS`, or on `artistinfo_page` its classinfo's `0xff01`-`0xff03`): offline, its name (ASCII case folded, as the list's `COLLATE NOCASE` groups it) is no card song's album and none of the server rows of that name has an offline copy (`group_unavailable`). The job keeps, for each group (album; artist, a song's artist and album artist both; genre), every card song's names (`cards`) and every server row's (`servers`), as sorted sets of their `group_hash`, and each server row's four names (`cat_ent.grp`); the names of the rows with an offline copy (`local`) are gathered again on the UI thread when `local_gen` has moved (an import, a `catalogue.avail` line). A name the catalogue doesn't know is the card's. ponytail: by name, so a server-only album sharing a card album's name stays white, and so does a server-only artist named as a card song's album artist. Lists that are not pooled tables but a scroll_view with one row per record in order are grayed as their surface's background paints (`grey_rows`, after `paint_selection`): an album's songs (`albuminfo_page`, `playerjumpinfo_page`: the showlist), Cover Flow's tracks (`coverflow_tracks`: Go to Album lands there with Artist View on), Most Played's and a Ratings list's songs (`page_tracks`: `st.mp_list`, `st.rt_list`) and Search's results (`p_deque_searchshowlist`, which each tab fills with its own rows: `ringnav_search_rows`, with the lit tab), each only when the list holds as many records as the surface has rows, and each row in sight through `catalogue_mark` (a row scrolled out of sight is forgotten, `catalogue_forget`, so a long list never fills the `CAT_GREY_ROWS` slots): a song's record by `song_mark` (below), a row of Search's Artists, Albums or Genres tab (a directory record its tab's callback, `0x506904`, `0x506e94` or `0x506d60`, fills with the name in `REC_ARTIST`, `REC_ALBUM` or `REC_STYLE`) by `group_unavailable` of its group; a grayed row is forgotten when it is destroyed (an `EVT_DESTROY` handler, once per widget, `_catgrey`), so a widget made later at its address is not grayed with it. `ringnav_style_color` runs stock's mapping first (`style_color`), then hands every text color painted at depth 0 to `catalogue_greyed`: inside a grayed row it is `#666666`, or on the selection (`ringnav_row_selected`: the row holds `g_menu.at[st.sel_row]`, or is inside it) the theme's own ink at 70% alpha (`CAT_DIM`), so a grayed row on OLED's Accent Blue bar reads white, not gray on blue; the color is kept per row (`grey_ink`). After the rows, `paint_offline` (from `ringnav_paint`, beside `paint_chevrons`) draws each grayed row's offline mark in that color: Phosphor's `cloud-slash` bold (MIT), rasterised once at 20 px by `tools/art.py`'s `path` and `coverage` into a 20 x 16 table of 16-step coverage in `catalogue.c` (`MARK`), painted a run of equal coverage per `canvas_fill_rect` at the row's alpha times the coverage. It sits in the chevron's column (the row's right less `CHEVRON_W` plus 25), or 28 px left of it on a row that shows a chevron (`offline_x`: a drill row of the payload's under a theme without `chevron_sel`, or the selected row when it holds stock's `list_into`). Before the rows paint, `grey_rows` also has `catalogue_fit` end each grayed row's labels (`label`, `hscroll_label`, four levels down, as deep as an album row's artist in `view_artist`) so their text stops `SONG_COL_GAP` (12 px) short of the mark's ink (`CAT_MARK_W` wide), as a length's does, their own width kept in `_catw` and given back when the row is no longer grayed or the limit moves (the selection leaving a drill row). **Play:** each Library song row and Play All asks stock's `access(path, R_OK)` first and says File Not Found when it fails; those eight calls (`CATALOGUE_ACCESS` in `tools/build.py`) go to `catalogue_access`, which passes a server row that can play now and fails one that can't, as a missing file (stock then says File Not Found and opens no Now Playing; a refused load after a pass would leave Now Playing open on the last song). `ringnav_load` then asks `catalogue_load`: a queue with no server row loads as before; a start row that can't play (reached another way) says "Not available offline" and loads nothing; online, the list is handed to the row's app as `/tmp/q2-<id>.catplay` (`<seq> <start>`, then each row's path) and nothing loads, the app's `.play` playing it through the card-app channel; when that `.play` has not changed in 4 s (`CATPLAY_WAIT_MS`), or offline at once, the firmware loads the list itself. The app plays the catplay's order from `<start>` on, so a shuffle (`shuffle_play`) of a list holding a server row hands over a shuffled copy, the drawn song first and `<start>` 0 (`library_lists.c` `shuffled_for_app`): Shuffle Songs' own order (`playback_shuffle`) is drawn over the queue stock already has, never the app's, and before 2026-11-19 a shuffle of server songs played the Library's title order from a random song to the list's end. An app that isn't running (none of its launcher's pid file: not opened since boot, or gone after its own 30-minute idle exit) is started first (`addon_wake`: `addon_scan` if Streaming hasn't listed it since boot, which also writes the capability line the app reads at its start, then `launch`, as its Streaming row starts it, after removing a socket a killed app left), and the catplay is written only once its socket is there (`addon_ready`, polled each second by `catplay_poll`): the app reads the catplay file at its start as one already answered and makes its socket after that, so one written earlier would never be answered. The 4 s wait runs from the write; an app that hasn't listened within `CATPLAY_START_MS` (15 s) has its list played the firmware's way. Nothing is started for a signed-out app, offline (the list plays from the card), or for an app whose binary is not on the card; a running app that `addon.c` was not tracking (demo restarted under it) is marked launched, so its `.play` is polled. An app started this way holds Smart Wi-Fi's radio as one opened from Streaming does, until its idle exit; the next press starts it again. The firmware's offline load: card rows, and server rows by their offline copies (the record's path replaced by the copy's), the start moved to the pressed row or the next kept. While a catplay waits, Now Playing shows the pressed song ([server-library.md](server-library.md#now-playing-while-it-loads)): `catalogue_load` keeps a copy of its record (`np_press`), its place in the list and its album's cover (`catalogue_cover`, else `play_defaultcover`), and once stock's press is over (a 0 ms timer, `np_stop`) stops the song playing or paused (`mclStop`), so its time and sound don't run on under the new title. Stock's `player_start`, after a `ringnav_load` that loaded nothing, starts the queue it had again (`mclStartPlayer`, a `set-nexturl` of its song): a paused song was then heard from its start until the stop reached the player, 20 to 50 ms on (the device, 2026-11-18, a blip of the paused song at a search pick; `q2player` takes a song at once when paused, and while playing the race went the stop's way). `ringnav_player_start` marks stock's call, `ringnav_load` notes a load of nothing within it, and the `mclStartPlayer` hook refuses that start (`playback_start_refused`, `patch/playback.c`), so nothing reaches the player before the stop; a greyed row's press, which toasts and loads nothing, leaves the song playing where it was rather than at 0 (`test_a_press_that_loads_nothing_does_not_start_the_queue_stock_had_again`). `np_sync` (`np_bar.c`) takes the album and "2 of 12" from that record (`catalogue_np_now`) and has `catalogue_np_text` write its title and artist into `scrlabel_title` and `scrlabel_artist`, again whenever their text is not what it wrote last (stock's page update writes `g_song_name` and `g_song_artist` there on its own refreshes); `np_art` gives the cover whenever the art shows another image: stock's page opens on the last song's, and its own reload (the restarted song's cover thread) can replace ours. It ends at the player's next fresh parse (`id3_parses`, counted in `ringnav_id3_path`), when the fallback finds nothing to play, or after `CATPLAY_SHOW_MS` (60 s); then the player's title and artist go back on the page. Stock's update (`0x53cf08`) writes them only while `g_forcerefresh_flag` or `g_autochange_flag` is set, and every library list page's timer clears those flags too, so the flag `np_done` sets from inside Now Playing's update (`np_sync`, after its title) was taken by the Songs page under it and the pressed song's title stayed on the next song (the device, Shuffle Songs then Next). `np_done` still sets the flag and marks `np_back`, and `catalogue_np_text` writes the playing song's title and artist (`now_tag`, the record's name for a missing title, as `g_song_name` has it) once `g_play_id3_info` names its path, which `ringnav_id3_path` writes after the tags. `play_folder` (`coverflow.c`) closes a Now Playing on top before it opens the new one: stock's `navigator_to_with_context` opens a second `playing_page` over the first (an app's first song starting under the pressed song's page), and two pages' updates race for the same flags, the one under winning as often as not. Shuffle Songs plays the whole library through the same load, so offline it leaves the unplayable out. Mid-queue, `upcoming()` (`playback.c`) passes over a row `catalogue_unavailable` refuses. Go to Album and Go to Artist on a server row open the Library's pages (stock's `playerjumpinfo_page` and artist page, by the row's tags), not its app's: `goto_app` (`addon.c`) leaves a catalogue path out, so `addon_goto` declines it, and `addon_goes` offers Go to on it although its path is in the app's folder. Now Playing's info page (`ringnav_np_info`) asks `catalogue_np_info` for the playing path, a server row's or its offline copy's (found by a pass over the index's copies, `cat_copy_of`): the catalogue's genre and year (`style` and `year` of `cat.serverall` by `fileurl`, kept for the last path, as the page fills every 250 ms) replace stock's Unknown, which comes of the Stream Cache file having no `songtable` row, and Location reads `Server`. **Covers:** `catalogue_cover` maps a server row's path (`/mnt/mmc/.<id>/cat/<album id>/<sid>.<suffix>`), or its offline copy's (`cat_copy_of`), to the app's `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/covers/<album id>.jpg` when that file is there. `grid_cover` (stock's Library album rows and grids, Folder's rows: `GRID_COVER`) gives a server row that file through `toolsThumbSpecCover` under the lock its caller holds, and nothing else (no file to read tags from); `coverflow_player_cover` tries it after the folder images and before ffmpeg's embedded probe, through `ff_thumb`, as its lock order wants. The app writes a baseline JPEG of at most 160 px, which stock's decoder takes whole. Durations of server rows are the catalogue's seconds (`durations.c`). A listen of a server song's offline copy (what the app's `.play` and the offline queue both play) counts under its server row's key (`play_count` asks `catalogue_song_key`: the listen_key of the row's `fileurl`, found by the copy's path in the index, the last answer kept until `local_gen` moves; hearts given on Now Playing while the copy plays take the same key through `rate_song_key`, `catalogue_rated` writes the row's sid, and `rate_all` counts the copy's My Fav, which stock's heart keeps by the copy's path, as the row's), so Most Played and Cover Flow's Most Played order, which rank the Library's rows, find it; Most Played's kept tracks take only a counted song's own record (`mp_counted`), never the copy's, so its next open reads the library again. **Cover Flow** (`coverflow.c`): with a server signed in its album queries (`getAllAlbum`, `ALBUM_SQL`, `MUSIC_ALBUM_SQL`, the Sort ranks, the rated albums) run as music loads (`cf_staged`, `staged_music`), so `library_query` reads the union and the carousel has the server's albums; with none signed in they run as before (`catalogue_has`). An album whose first track is a server row is queued for art only once its app's cover is there (`load_albums`: `catalogue_cover`, one `access` per uncached server album per open), and `build_art` thumbnails that cover into the cache (`thumb`, `ART_SIZE`); a cover that won't decode gets the "no art" marker, and one removed meanwhile none, so the next open asks again. Until then the placeholder shows, with no marker to clear. The centered album's captions are grayed as a row is (`caption_offline`: `catalogue_grey` on the name and artist labels, so `ringnav_style_color` grays their text) while `catalogue_album_unavailable` says none of its songs can play, the name narrowed `CF_MARK_W` (28) a side so it stays centered, and `caption_mark` paints the offline mark in the name's right margin as the covers' view paints; `titles` checks it as the center changes, and the slide's paint again each frame (`album_offline`), so a lost connection grays the centered album at the next frame. A track row of a server album, and Cover Flow's All albums card (`play_all`) and Era's Play All and Shuffle (`era_pick`) whose first song is a server row, check no file before they play (`catalogue_missing`: `access` for a card file, none for a server row), so `ringnav_load` hands the list to the app or says why it can't, where `access` said Storage unavailable.

**Where a song lives** (OLED, [oled-design.md](oled-design.md#song-rows)): the same slots that gray a row carry a mark kind (`grey_mark`: `MK_OFFLINE`, `MK_CLOUD`, `MK_DOWN`), set by `song_mark` wherever a song row is bound or made (`catalogue_bind`, `catalogue_mark`). A row that can't play now is `MK_OFFLINE`, grayed with the offline mark as above; a server row that can play is `MK_CLOUD` (it streams), a card file under a catalogue app's downloads folder (its `q2app`'s `downloads=`, one folder at the card's root, read by `cat_scan`: q2-subsonic's `Subsonic`) is `MK_DOWN`, and the user's own file has none. Only `MK_OFFLINE` changes the row's text color (`catalogue_greyed` and `catalogue_row_ink` skip the others; `cat.noff` counts the offline ones, so a list with none spends no time in `grey_of` per text color). `paint_offline` hands each marked row to `catalogue_row_mark`, which draws the offline mark as before or the theme's own 18 px glyph (`tools/art.py` `MARKS`: Phosphor's `cloud` and `arrow-circle-down`, regular, `oled_mark_<cloud|down>_<d|l|w>`) in Text Tertiary, white on the selection, centered where the offline mark would be; the title, artist and length end clear of either as they do of the offline mark (`catalogue_row_greyed` answers for every marked row). Marks follow the catalogue: with no app signed in, or before an app's `q2app` is read, there are none.

**Playlists** (`cat_playlists`, in each job, for every app): each catalogue playlist is a stock playlist (a header row with an id 0-99 whose `cd_num` is itself; items above 100 with that `cd_num`), its items a card file's `songtable` row (a synced song's path from its `i` line, or the linked file) or the server row's. `serverlists` remembers which header is whose. A new catalogue playlist whose name a stock playlist already has is compared with it (`pl_twin`: that playlist's items, in order, equal to the catalogue playlist's card files, in order): equal, it is the app's synced `.m3u` twin, and the catalogue playlist takes its place (`twin` 1; its items replaced by the catalogue's); not equal, it is the user's own, and the catalogue's is left out. A playlist gone from the catalogue is deleted, a twin only unlinked. The pass runs in its own transaction on stock's database; a failure there rolls it back and leaves the import as it is, to be tried again at the next job. Signing out keeps them, their server rows gone from the index.

**Ratings** ([server-library.md](server-library.md#ratings-and-favorites)): `rate_close`, the heart page's My Fav button, an album's favorites (`ratings.c`) and the queue menu's Favorite and Unfavorite (`qm_rated`, which clears the song's 1-4 as the heart does) call `catalogue_rated`, which appends `<listen_key>\t<sid or empty>\t<hearts>\t<unix time>` to `ratings.out` of each app with `ratings=1` (the sid a server row's, or a linked card file's; for a Stream Cache copy, its server row's key and sid, `cat_row_of`). `ratings.in` is renamed to `ratings.in.taking` before it is read (lines the app writes meanwhile go to a new `ratings.in`), each line applied unless that song's newest line in `ratings.out` is newer (`rate_keep` by the key; My Fav set or cleared by the path: a server row's or a linked file's from its sid, any other card file's found by its `listen_key` in one pass over `songtable`), then the file is deleted. The file is one pass: `ratings.out` is read and indexed by key once (`out_index`), the stars kept in the table and written once (`rate_hold`, `rate_release`), and My Fav's rows set on one connection in one transaction; measured in `test/fw` at 1,000 lines (`test_a_thousand_ratings_from_the_server_are_one_database_write_and_one_table_write`), 500 database opens and 500 synced table writes became one of each, 2,079 ms to 16 ms on the host build. `catalogue_poll` reads it only while no job runs and the app's `catalogue.tsv` seq is the one imported, so at a boot's first poll, before the import has built the index, a server row's line waits rather than lose its My Fav (its path comes from the index). A server row in My Fav (from `ratings.in`, or the queue menu on its Library row) is a favorite of its Stream Cache copy too, which stock's `checkFavExist` can't see as it checks the copy's own path: `rate_fav` (Now Playing's heart and picker, the queue menu's Favorites and Rate rows) asks `catalogue_row_fav` as well (`select 1 from myfav` by the row's `fileurl`, kept until the row, `local_gen` or `fav_gen` moves; `fav_told`, `ratings_in` and `rate_bind` move `fav_gen`). Now Playing's 500 ms heart tick (`rate_heart`, `rate_row_heart`) fills the copy's empty heart for it and empties a heart it filled once the row leaves My Fav, or one stock drew from the copy's own path once `checkFavExist` no longer finds it (asked only when `catalogue_fav_gen` has moved since the last tick, not twice a second); `ratings_in` takes a copy's own path out of My Fav with its row's whatever the hearts (`fav_set`'s third argument, the row's `local` from the index), so a copy hearted here and then rated 4 or unstarred on the server shows the empty heart and the server's 4, and five from the server leaves the row in its place, the song in Favorites once; a tap on that heart, a picked rating under five and the queue menu's Remove take the row out (`catalogue_row_unfav`) instead of running stock's toggle, which would put the copy in. ponytail: a row taken out of My Fav by stock's own lists is seen when Now Playing next opens, not while it shows.

**Measured** on the emulator (`q2emu` under qemu-user on a laptop, not a Q2): see [server-library.md](server-library.md#scale).

## Storage

**System settings → Storage** (`storage_open` in `patch/storage.c`, the `storage_page` runtime window; between App Store and System Update, `sysset_order`) shows how the card is used: the line "33.9 GB of 60 GB used", a 10 px bar from the text column to the right column (round ends, the track `#2C2C2E`, then Your Music in white, Downloads in the accent's top tone and Stream Cache in `#6E6E73` from the left, square where they meet with 1 px of track between them), four rows, each with its 10 px legend dot and size: **Your Music**, **Downloads** (opens its page), **Stream Cache** (opens the app's own Settings, where its size and Clear Cache are) and **Free**, and **Update Library** (the Library's Update Local Music until 2026-11-19, which stays in the Library's page hidden, `lr_retire`): stock's scan, `dialog/updatemusic_dialog` as Scan Music Now opens it, its second line when the last whole scan ended unstopped (`library_scan` calls `storage_scanned`, which saves the wall time to `/mnt/data/q2-library-updated` through `blob_io`; `st_updated` reads it as "Last updated today, 18:11", "yesterday, ..." in the clock's 12 or 24 hours, else the date, `when_said`), none before a scan this firmware saw, under two footers in Text Tertiary at 13 px ("Your Music is never changed by Sync." and "Downloads stay under the limit you set."). Sizes are MB of 10^6 bytes, as the apps and a card's label count (`mb_mib`: MiB times 1.049, so no 64-bit division), shown as "512 MB" or "24.1 GB". **Storage → Downloads** (`downloads_page`) is a **Limit** row (No Limit, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64 GB, picked in the menu sheet's picker, `modal_pick`) and the app's downloaded items, each with its mark (Phosphor's `arrow-circle-down` in the accent for one the user picked, `arrows-clockwise` in Text Secondary for one the app keeps on its own; `oled_store_<pick|auto>_*`), its size and a chevron when the app has a page for it, which a press opens (`addon_open_at`); Play/Pause held on an item (`storage_hold`, from `ringnav_keylong`) asks the app to remove it and toasts "Removed from Sync". Its footer says so: "Hold Play/Pause on an item to remove it.", or "Nothing downloaded yet." with no item. The rows are `page_row_detail` rows; the header and footers are views above and below the list (as Battery History's graph), and `storage_paint` (from `ringnav_paint`) draws them and each row's dot, mark, value and chevron, under OLED only (other themes show the rows' names).

**The channel.** A card app that keeps downloads says `storage=1` in its `q2app` (the first found is the page's, `st_app`), and the firmware adds `storage` to its capability line. The app writes `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/storage.tsv` whole (temp and rename), tab-separated with the card-app channel's escapes (read with catalogue.c's `tsv_split`, at most 32 KB and `ST_ITEMS` 64 items):

```text
#Q2STORE/1	limit=<MB, 0 for none>	downloads=<bytes>	cache=<bytes>
i	<pick|auto>	<key>	<bytes>	<op>	<arg>	<name>
```

`downloads` is what the app downloaded for the user, `cache` its own folder (Stream Cache, covers, its files). The firmware asks for a change by appending a line to `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/storage.out` (`st_ask`; an LF first ends any line a cut write left): `limit\t<MB>` or `remove\t<key>`, and starts the app (`addon_wake`) to take it; the app takes the file by renaming it, applies it and writes `storage.tsv` again. The page's opening appends `look` (`st_note`) without starting the app: q2-subsonic counts its folder file by file (the covers: about 4 s of CPU on a Q2) only when that size can be seen to change, at its start, at a `look`, and at most every 10 minutes after it wrote there or while the page may still be open (its `storage.go` `stOwn`). It walked every 10 minutes while it ran: measured 2026-11-20, one walk was 443 ticks (4.4 s of CPU, nearly all system time). A limit chosen here shows at once (`so.pending`) until the file says so. While either page is open the file is read again every second (`st_poll`) and the pages rebuilt, their selection kept, when it changed. **Your Music** is measured, never walked: the card's used space (`statfs`: blocks less available, so a card's reserved blocks count as used) less the app's downloads and cache, so it holds every file the user put there, other card apps' folders and the firmware's own (`.q2pod/catalogue.db`, Cover Flow's art) with them. Without such an app, or before it has written the file, Downloads and Stream Cache read 0 MB and open nothing.

## Q2 Shelf

**System settings → App Store** (titled **App Store**; just above Storage; `shelf_open` in `patch/netupdate.c`, the `apps_page` runtime window) installs, updates and removes the apps in [`sources.list`](../sources.list), each from the one release zip the list pins. The firmware names no app but its own three. The list is fetched from `raw.githubusercontent.com/312-dev/q2-coda/main/sources.list` (`Q2POD_REPO`'s, as Network Update's releases, so `--update-repo` moves both), taken only when the release key signed it ([Release signatures](#release-signatures)), and kept as `/mnt/mmc/.q2/sources.list` so the page works offline. The first row, **Check for Updates** (`ROW_CHECK`), runs a check when pressed, so with no list yet it is the one row and fetches the list.

Each line is `owner/repo TAG ASSET SIZE SHA256 [Name]` (`#` starts a comment, `-` before it marks a dropped app), and `shelf_sources` reads up to 16 (`SH_MAX`). The owner is `A-Za-z0-9-`, the repo also allows `._`, and the name defaults to the repo's. `TAG ASSET SIZE SHA256` is the app's pin (`parse_pin`, into `shelf_app`'s `latest`, `asset`, `size` and `sha256`): the release's tag (1 to 31 of `A-Za-z0-9._-`), its zip's name (up to 63 of the same, ending `.zip`; both go into the download's URL), the zip's bytes (1 to 1 GB, `SH_CAP`) and their SHA-256 in lowercase hex. A line is skipped when any of these fail, it has no pin (only a dropped app needs none; a dropped app's pin is let go), its id repeats an earlier one's, or the firmware carries the app as its own (`addon_builtin`, [Bundled apps](#bundled-apps)): such an app is never shown, installed, updated or removed here, whichever list names it, the signed one or the card's copy of an older one, and so never kept as dropped either. `serial N` numbers the list (`shelf_serial`) and the last line, `signature <128 hex>`, is the release key's; neither is an app. `tools/shelf.py` writes the pins, from each app's latest release's first `.zip`, and signs the list ([releasing](releasing.md#the-app-list)).
