The list is the store's trust: card apps come from many people's repositories, which no single key signs, so q2-coda's maintainer vouches for each exact zip instead, and the Q2 checks two things. `fresh_list` takes a fetched list only if `sig_list` finds the release key's signature over everything before its last line, and its serial is at least that of the card's list (an older signed list, served again from a repository taken over, would roll the pins back); otherwise "App list not signed: not used", and the page keeps the list it has. `install` downloads only `https://github.com/OWNER/REPO/releases/download/TAG/ASSET` from that list, reads the part back from the card through SHA-256 and goes on only if it is the pin's ("Download doesn't match the list" otherwise, before anything is unzipped). So neither a repository's owner nor anyone holding it can put a new zip on a Q2 without a new signed list, and q2-pod's upstream list, unsigned, is never taken. The id is the repo's name less `q2-`, and must be 1 to 15 of `a-z0-9-`, addon.c's rule, since it goes into shell commands. A card app's folder is `.<id>`, its binary `.<id>/q2-<id>`, and nothing in it is kept from unzip.

Q2 Muse's own apps are matched by the repo's name, so a fork is the same app; another repo whose id would be one of theirs is skipped:

- `q2-rockbox` → `rockbox`: binary `.rockbox/rockbox`, keeps `.rockbox/config.cfg`.
- `q2-rockbox-themes` → `themes`: folder `.rockbox`, no binary, keeps the same file.
- `q2-librespot` → `spotify`: binary `.spotify/librespot`, keeps `.spotify/cache/*` and `.spotify/.cache-size`.

The app rows follow the list's order. Each one shows its app's state as the row's detail:

- **Installed** with a tag in `/mnt/mmc/.q2/apps/<id>.tag`.
- **Update** when that tag differs from the pin's (string equality, not order), or when the app's binary is there without a tag (a manual install).
- Otherwise **Install**.

Rockbox Themes is listed only while `.rockbox/rockbox` is a regular file. The rows are built when the page opens, and again when a job's end changes which (`sh_rows`). Themes says "Install Rockbox first" without Rockbox.

ponytail: a card app keeps nothing from an update. Its settings survive only because its release zip doesn't ship them; an app whose zip ships its settings file overwrites the user's copy on every update. The fix belongs in that app's release, or in a `keep` list here if one ever needs it.

See [the user guide](manual/guide.html#apps) for install, removal, confirmation and cancellation controls.

One pthread runs one job at a time, all transfers through netupdate.c's `fetch` (the same CA bundle and TLS checks, `User-Agent: Q2Pod`, progress and cancel through its transfer callback). Opening the page with Wi-Fi checks: it fetches the signed list, one request, as each app's latest is its pin's tag (no GitHub API request is made). This is skipped if the last check fetched it in the last 10 minutes (`SH_STALE_MS`, kept until power-off). The worker parses the fetched list into `sh.next`, adds back any app it dropped that still has a tag (so it can still be removed), and writes the result to the card: `serial N`, then each app's line with its pin, a dropped one's with a `-` before it and no pin, without the signature (the card's copy is the page's offline and the floor for the next list's serial; nothing installs from it). A dropped app (`shelf_app.dropped`, from that check or a `-` line) has no pin, its last tag is let go, `install` refuses it, and its row shows only while it is installed: with the pins, dropping an app is no longer the only thing between a taken-over repo and a Q2 ([GHSA-8wpr-pmqx-538x](https://github.com/DiamondBond/q2-pod/security/advisories/GHSA-8wpr-pmqx-538x)), but it is how the maintainer takes an app away. The UI thread adopts it when the check ends, so the rows never change under a job. A list that fails to fetch or parses to nothing leaves the old one in place. So the rows can be the card's list of days ago: after opening with no Wi-Fi, after a row's press stops the opening check, or while the list can't be fetched. An install therefore fetches the signed list itself first (`listed`, through `fresh_list`) and takes the app's pin from it, going on only if it names the app's repo, not dropped: "Can't reach GitHub" or "GitHub is busy, try later" with no list, "App list not signed: not used" with one that fails its signature or serial, "No update for this build" with the repo gone from it. The rows themselves change at the next check.

**Check for Updates** checks inside those 10 minutes, but not within a minute of the last whole check (`SH_RECHECK_MS`): then it says that check's count again without fetching. Its row reads "Checking…" during any check; pressing it then starts nothing, but the check's end answers it. When a check ends with the page on top (not covered, nor stopped by another row's press), `sh_told` toasts the number of apps whose tag file differs from the latest release: "1 app can be updated", "3 apps can be updated". A manual install's **Update** isn't counted, as its version is unknown. With none, after Check for Updates (`sh.manual`, cleared by the next `sh_start`) it says why the list wasn't taken (`SH_NET`, `SH_BUSY` for a 403 or 429, `SH_UNSIGNED`: "Can't reach GitHub", "GitHub is busy, try later", "App list not signed: not used"), or else "All apps are up to date". No list at all, on the card or fetched, is `SH_NET`. The opening check says nothing unless an app can be updated.

An install:

1. Fetches the signed list (`listed`) and goes on only if it names the app's repo, not dropped, taking its pin; then deletes any leftover `/mnt/mmc/.q2/staging` (an interrupted install is retried, never resumed), and needs the pin's size plus 64 MB free (`statfs`).
2. Downloads `releases/download/TAG/ASSET` to `.q2/staging/<id>.part`, then reads it back through SHA-256 (`sig_hash_file`) and stops unless it is the pin's.
3. Lists it with `busybox unzip -l -qq`, restricted as the unpack is: the app's folder only (`.rockbox/*` or `.spotify/*`), never `*/._*` or the kept paths (`.rockbox/config.cfg`; `.spotify/cache/*` and `.spotify/.cache-size`). `shelf_unpacked` rejects an absolute path or a `..` component and a total over 1 GB, and needs at least one entry; the card then needs that total plus 64 MB free.
4. Unpacks with `busybox unzip -o -qq -d .q2/staging/<id>` and the same patterns, so `INSTALL.txt`, `__MACOSX/` and macOS `._` files stay off the card. busybox's unzip matches with `fnmatch` without `FNM_PATHNAME` (so `*` spans `/`), and strips a leading `/` and `../` from names itself before listing and unpacking.
5. Stops Spotify (`SPOT_KILL`) again before touching `.spotify`, in case it was started during the download, lists the staged files with `find <dir> -type f`, and renames each over its target on the card (the same file system), making folders as needed; the app's binary goes last, and only when every other file moved, so `.rockbox/rockbox` is the old file or the new one, never part of one, and never new beside a half-moved set. The list becomes `.q2/apps/<id>.files`, then `sync`, then the tag through `blob_io`. Staging is deleted after every install, whatever the outcome.

Every Spotify job starts and ends with `spot_stop` on the UI thread, so spotify.c forgets the librespot it started and Streaming → Spotify starts the new one (or says it is missing).

**Remove** unlinks the app's binary first (a remove cut short still boots Q2 Muse), then each path in `<id>.files` that no other app's list holds (two fonts are in both Rockbox's and the themes' zips), then each folder left empty, up to and including the app's own, then, for a card app (not in `special[]`), its folder whole (`rm -rf .<id>`, with the login and settings it saved there, which no release lists), then the list and tag. So `shelf_sources` refuses a card app whose id names one of the firmware's own card folders (`reserved[]`: `q2`, `q2muse`, `q2pod`, `tidal`, `coverflow`, `downpic`, `sldp`), as it does Spotify's; `test/peq.py` fails when a card folder in `patch/` is missing from it. Before removing anything, `addon_quit` asks a running card app to end and waits for its loop's pid file to go, up to `QUIT_MS` (20 s), so an app saving its login on its TERM has done so before the folder goes; if USB storage has taken the card meanwhile (`card_mounted`), nothing is removed and the job ends in **Can't write to the card**, so the app is still there when the card comes back. ponytail: one still saving after 20 s can write files back, and the card is checked once, so USB storage taking it during the unlinks still ends in removed. Removing Rockbox removes the themes first, after the same check. Removing Spotify stops it and keeps `cache/` and `.cache-size`, which were never installed by it; [Streaming configuration](#streaming-configuration)'s **Erase Spotify Data** runs on this thread as a job too (`shelf_erase`), stops it and deletes those two.

A 500 ms timer refreshes progress and holds standby and auto power-off during app jobs; `sh_wait` joins the worker and reports its result wherever the user is, including after leaving the page.

ponytail: an app's own runtime downloads, if it makes any, and what it runs once installed, are its own: the pin vouches for the zip, not for what the app does. A new app release reaches Q2s only once the maintainer pins and signs it. Cancel stops the download at once, otherwise it lands after the step it was pressed in (the list or API request, the listing or the unpack); once files move it is ignored. A power cut while files move leaves those moved so far beside the old ones, with the old tag and list; the next install starts over. Staging left by a power cut stays on the card until the next install. A release that drops a file leaves the old one on the card and off the new list. The card is FAT32 or exFAT, which hold no symlinks or special files: busybox fails on one, so nothing checks for them.

### Card apps

Every other app in the list is a card app: it installs through the same rows and runs from **Streaming** through one generic host, `patch/addon.c`. It lists up to 8 card folders `.<id>/` (id: 1 to 15 of `a-z0-9-`, since it goes into shell commands) holding `q2app` (`name=`, `search=`, `qr=1`, `goto=1`, `scrobble=0`: see [Scrobbling](#scrobbling); `favdir=`: see Hearts in [Card apps](#card-apps); `stop=0`: no Stop row, see Stop and Retry; `game=1` and `audio=1`: see Card games below; `lyrics=1` and `downloads=`: see [Lyrics from a card app's server](#server-lyrics); `covers=1`: see [Car remote: A cover the card lacks](#car-remote-covers); `resume=1`: see [Memory Playback and a streamed queue](#memory-playback-and-a-streamed-queue)), `run` and `q2-<id>`, and optionally `icon.png` (52 px) and `icon-40.png` (40 px), each at most 128 px either way (`ART_MAX`: demo decodes it whole, so a larger one, or one whose size can't be read, is not used): Streaming's row shows the 40 px icon 1:1, else the other scaled down, else the shared `stream_app` (`addon_icon`); under `list.icons.addon_mono` (OLED's) it grays as Streaming's own icons do (`addon_is_icon` in `ringnav_image_add`). The launcher's loop leaves its pid in `/tmp/q2-<id>` and must remove it as it ends; a TERM to it stops the app. Every wait for an app to end (USB storage's `AWAY_MS`, a remove's or update's `QUIT_MS`) ends when the pid file goes, so a loop that leaves it behind costs each wait its full limit. `run` is started with `system()` on the UI thread each time the app starts (`launch`), so it must return at once: anything slow, such as a copy, goes inside the loop it starts in the background (`&`), and it exits straight away when the loop already runs; until it returns, the screen and buttons are frozen, and a minute of that restarts the Q2 ([Watchdog](#watchdog)). `/tmp/q2-<id>.browse.sock` serves the page over Q2SPOT/1, and `/tmp/q2-<id>.state` holds `hold=1` (standby kept off) and the QR page's `addr`, `pin`, `qr`, `qrsize`, `note`, in any order. The QR page (`qr_refresh`) reads it whole, up to `QR_FILE`; `poll_one` and the answers' readers (`resumeack`, `lyricsack`, `radioack`, `radio=`) read it line by line (`app_state`), keeping each line that fits in the reader's buffer (`QR_RAW`, 1,536 bytes, for most) and leaving out a longer one, a sign-in's `qr=` (7,965 bytes of hex at version 40), so a `hold=` or `sync=` written after the code still reads; at most `STATE_SCAN` (16 KB) of the file is looked at. The app is started by its `run` script in the background (`launch`: `system("/bin/sh <dir>/run &")`), so the UI pass waits for the shell's start alone, not for the script's copies to `/tmp` and its loop's fork: about 210 ms a launch on the emulator before, 65 ms with the `&` (2026-11-22, under qemu; the device's is shorter). USB storage (`usbmode_page_init`'s hook, `addon_card_away`) asks every app to end at once and waits up to `AWAY_MS` (3 s) in all, on the UI thread (ponytail: an app still saving on its TERM after that can write to the card as USB takes it; the fix is to defer stock's USB-mode call until the apps are gone, without sleeping), then starts each again once the card is back. No app starts while the Apps page installs or removes its folder (`shelf_busy`). Its Streaming row opens no page while the folder is being removed or an update's files are moved into place (`shelf_moving`, stage 3 on), or while an update downloads for an app that is not running (its page would be refused as it started): it says "Wait until the App Store finishes", as its Games row does; a running app's page works during the download. A stop removes a pid file whose loop is gone, but it trusts the pid inside: a loop that died without removing it, its pid since reused, would TERM that process (a `flock` in `run` would close this). The QR page draws any code the apps' encoder makes, to version 40's 177 modules (`QR_MAX`): its status file read as far as `QR_FILE` and the code's rows `QR_HEX` bytes, both on the heap with the page, the plate a pixel a module and its quiet zone past 162 modules.

**Card games.** A card app whose `q2app` holds `game=1` (q2-fidget, named Buddy) has no Streaming row and needs no `run`: `addon_scan` keeps it in its own by-name list, which Home's Games chooser lists after Bricks, the engine's (`addon_games`, `addon_game_name`; `games.c` `pick_card_game`). A row forks and `execl`s `.<id>/q2-<id>` from the card (`addon_game_start`), as Videos' q2video runs, and the game draws on `/dev/fb0` itself while demo runs on: `ringnav_wm_paint` skips the window manager's paint and `ringnav_input` hands every event to `addon_game_input` instead of stock, except Play/Pause and the side buttons (222, 223), down, up and long, which stay stock's media keys under the Games page unless the game has the sound (below). The rest go as text datagrams to `/tmp/q2-<id>.input.sock`: `k d CODE` and `k u CODE` for a key's down and release, `t d X Y`, `t m X Y` and `t u X Y` for a touch, in the 375 × 320 view's pixels (this hook sees the portrait panel's coordinates, before the window manager turns them, so X is the panel's y and Y is 319 less its x; the pointer types `EVT_POINTER_DOWN`, `_MOVE_BEFORE` and `_UP_BEFORE` less one or not, an abort as `u`). `wheel_raw` is set while it runs, and `game_poll` (from `addon_poll`, each UI loop pass) sends the travel gathered since as `w N` (200 a turn, rising anticlockwise). Return held `GAME_HOLD_MS` (700 ms, timed in `game_poll` from its key-down, since stock makes `EVT_KEY_LONG` after this hook) TERMs the game, and one still there `GAME_KILL_MS` (3 s) later is KILLed, as often as it takes. So does `GAME_IDLE_MS` (2 min) without input, unless Smart Awake (`IPOD KEEPLIT`, `ringnav_smart_awake`) is on, which holds it open and lit with no limit (asked once each `GAME_IDLE_MS`); meanwhile `reset_poweroptions_timer(1, 1, 1)` holds the screen, standby and auto power-off. Its end (`waitpid` `WNOHANG`) clears `wheel_raw` and repaints the whole window manager. The child gets `Q2_POPUP` (`popup_env`, `games.c`): the theme's pop-up as the Games page draws it, so a game's menus can match ([librespot.md](librespot.md)); it is built before the fork and set with `setenv` in the child alone (demo imports no `execve` or `environ`), after its files are closed. ponytail: a fork while another thread holds libc's environment lock (stock's `toolsSetTimeZone` sets `TZ`) leaves the child waiting in `setenv`, before its exec, until Return's hold ends it; setting it in demo instead would race other threads' `getenv` and change demo's environment. The capability word is `game`. ponytail: the game runs from the card, so USB storage's prompt, under it, can't be answered until it ends; and the screen can't go dark under it, as for a video.

**A game with the sound.** A card game whose `q2app` also holds `audio=1` (q2-groovebox, named Groovebox) owns the audio output while it runs, as a video does. Before the fork `addon_game_start` runs what `video_play` and `video_start` run: `headset_manual`, `spot_yield`, `radio_stop`, `now_hold` (the Library's song stopped with its place kept, as for a video: a paused player holds the PCM; [Now Playing source](#now-playing-source)) and, for the headphone output, `dac_take` (power, PCM mode, unmuted, the volume). The binary gets q2video's arguments: the output device, `plughw:0,0`, `plug:bluealsa` or `usb` (`output_device`), and on Bluetooth or USB the volume as a second argument (`NN`, or `hNN` to show only), since the DAC's hardware volume is out of those paths and the game applies the soft volume itself; on the jack there is no second argument. The game opens them as q2video does (`video.c` `sound_open`), which the contract in [librespot.md](librespot.md) spells out: `usb` is the card `/proc/asound/cards` lists as USB-Audio, `plughw:N,0`; hciplayer lets go of the PCM, muting the DAC, a moment after the stop, so the open is retried (2 s on the jack, 5 s on Bluetooth and USB, and up to 5 s more at `snd_pcm_set_params` off the jack, since bluealsa claims its PCM there) and, on the jack, `DAC_MUTE` and `DAC_PCM` are cleared through `/dev/shanling_dac` after it, the mute set again when it closes; `hNN` is applied by the DAC, so the game plays at unity; Mono Audio and Swap L/R are `/tmp/q2mono` and `/tmp/q2swap` (an int each), applied to its output as q2video applies them. Play/Pause and the side buttons then reach it as `k d|u 171`, `222` and `223` (stock makes a key's long press after the hook, so none arrives, and no Play-hold action of stock's runs; power-off is Center's hold, which stock still has). A headset's buttons do nothing meanwhile: `media_key` and `media_set_playing` (headset.c) return while `addon_game_audio` says a game has the sound, as otherwise, with video, radio and Spotify all stopped, a headset's Play (AVRCP PLAY, 200 and 207, which `headset_command` sends to `media_set_playing`, not `media_key`) would reach `player_play_pause` with the player stopped and start hciplayer over the game; a pause still passes, Play/Pause's included, for a Spotify a phone resumed meanwhile. Every other start of stock's player meanwhile fails with -1 as a too-long track's does, silently (`ringnav_start_player`, mclStartPlayer's hook: a jack or USB DAC change and a Bluetooth drop come through `player_save_start`), and a headset's link coming up starts nothing (`ringnav_bt_connect_start`, Resume on Connect either way). Stock's `player_save_start(1)` ignores the -1 and still marks the player paused, on nothing, so the game's end, when no song was held, stops it when it finds it paused (`game_poll`), and Play then starts the queue as from a stop. A launched card app's first song waits for the game's end (`stream_poll` keeps `S_WAIT`); stock's own steps before the hook (`config_outputchannel`, the volume) still run. `game_poll` zeroes a counting `g_dacoff_time` each pass, as `video_poll` does, so the DAC stays on, and skips the `GAME_IDLE_MS` close: only the game knows whether it is playing, so the idle close is its own (Groovebox ends itself after 5 minutes stopped and untouched). Return's hold still ends it. When it ends the Library's song held at its start is loaded again paused where it was (`now_release`), as after a video (one that cannot start gives it back at once), and the DAC powers off on stock's count. Standby needs the screen dark, which a game keeps lit, so nothing else changes; `media_playing` does not count a game. The capability word is `audio`. ponytail: a headset's Play could be forwarded as a datagram instead of ignored; a live volume change while it runs is not mirrored (Videos' `video_sync` does that), the game has its own volume gesture; a Spotify a phone resumes meanwhile opens its own PCM beside the game's, as beside a video's.

**Go to on a card app's song.** The hold menu's Go to Album and Go to Artist (`qm_goto`) on a song under `/mnt/mmc/.<id>/` first ask `addon_goto`: when that app's `q2app` holds `goto=1` (the app rewrites the line from its own setting; `goto=0` hides the rows again, as below), its page opens with the Q2SPOT/1 level `goto` (`album` or `artist`, then the song's path) as its first level, titled by the record's album or artist tag (`card_tags` fills the playing song's), and the app answers with that album's or artist's own level; More… keeps both arguments, and Back from it closes the page as from a menu. An app page already open (the song played from it) is closed first, as Coverflow's scoped page (`closed` then `window_manager_close_window_force`); `closed` ignores the late destroy of a page it no longer holds. An app not yet scanned this boot is scanned for its name. A song in an app's folder whose app doesn't have `goto=1` (Tidal's downloads too) has no Go to rows (`addon_goes`): the Library never scans those hidden folders, so stock's pages would be empty. `goto` in `/tmp/q2-addon.caps` tells an app the firmware has it. Checks in `test/patch.py`: the request and its title, More…, Back, the replaced page and its late destroy, and no page for an app without `goto=1`, a song outside a card folder or an id that can't be one.

**Tags.** A card app's songs come from its folder's listing (`card_songs`, `toolsLoadDirectory`) or an `.m3u`, which read no tags, and play as a library queue (`0xf001`). `player_get_id3info` parses only a folder play's file (`MCL_TYPE` 1) and copies any other queue's record into `g_play_id3_info`, so such a song read as its file name by an Unknown artist. `card_tags`, from `ringnav_id3_path` as each song starts, gives the playing record (`queue_now`, its path the parsed one, under `/mnt/mmc/`, no album yet, not a CUE track, whose tags are its sheet's) and the parsed tags its file's title, artist, album and album artist, and the record its track and disc, read as the library scan reads them (`toolsGetMusicInfo`): one TagLib open as a song starts, once a queue, since the record then has its album; a song on the card without an album tag played from a list (Shuffle Songs, Most Played) is read at each start, as stock reads every folder play's. A song without tags keeps its record's. A song a playlist session queues from an app's own folder (a path under `/mnt/mmc/.`: the Stream Cache, never the user's synced albums), and the song a Next waits for, are named before they play by `card_record_tags`: the server row's title, album, artist and album artist when the catalogue knows the download (`catalogue_copy_tags`, by `cat_copy_of`: no file read, and a song not there yet is named), else its file's tags when the file is there, so Up Next and Now Playing read "Take It Easy", Eagles, not q2-subsonic's file name, the title in lower case and the server's id (the device, 2026-11-17 23:51, a radio's Up Next). A record with an album is left. Streamed songs land one at a time, so this is one TagLib open per song as it joins. ponytail: Up Next shows a card app's synced songs (in its folders at the card's root) not yet played by their file names, and holding a song in an app's list has no Go to rows (Now Playing's has); reading a whole folder when it's queued froze the UI for seconds on a few hundred songs. A queued row's cover is its server row's album cover (`catalogue_cover`) or Cover Flow's of its album: with no app signed in, or an album whose cover the app has not fetched yet, it is the placeholder.

**Sleep timers.** An app's `/tmp/q2-<id>.sleep` (q2-podcasts' Sleep Timer) holds `until <time>` (seconds since the epoch) or `end`; `sleep_read`, in the app's poll, takes a new request (its contents hashed per slot), and its removal by the app cancels the one it set. Q2 Muse keeps the timer, so it fires once the app has stopped too: `until` is kept as the time left on the boot clock (`boot_s`, `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`), which counts Standby and doesn't move when Wi-Fi sets the clock (stock's NTP), so neither shifts it (a time already past pauses at once; no digits, more than 11, anything after them, or more than a week away, `SLEEP_MAX_S`, is dropped without pausing; a time the Q2 slept through by more than `SLEEP_LATE_S`, a minute, is let go without pausing). `end` waits on the track playing (its place, `MCL_POS`) and follows its elapsed time and length (`player_playtime_and_length`, a pass reading -1 between tracks skipped) every pass: ending by itself (`mclNextSong`'s automatic call, counted in `auto_nexts` by `ringnav_next`, so a VBR file whose length is overstated still counts) or leaving its last `SLEEP_END_S` (2 s) for another place pauses, the next track waiting at its start, and so does starting over in place (repeat one); a move from anywhere else (another track picked, Next, a seek back) waits for that track's end instead, since stock refills the same deque for a new queue (`mclLoadPlayList`), so a pick and Next look alike. A length unknown counts any move on as the end. The player stopped for `SLEEP_STOP_MS` (3 s, as Tidal's: stock reports stopped between tracks for a moment), or another one taking playback (`media_owner`), lets it go. `sleep_check`, every `addon_poll`, pauses with `media_set_playing(0)` (whatever owns playback: the local player, Spotify, radio or a video) and removes the file, the app's sign the timer is over. One timer at a time: the latest request, from any app, replaces the one before; another app's removes the earlier one's file. `sleep` in `/tmp/q2-addon.caps` tells an app the firmware has it. Checks in `test/patch.py`: a timer before and at its time, canceled, already due, slept through, the clock set a day on, a bad or far-off time, a time replaced by `end`, and `end` at the next track, at a natural end before the length's last seconds, at repeat one, after another track picked and a seek back, and at a stop.

## Car remote

Settings > Car Remote lets a phone (the q2-auto-remote Android Auto app) browse the library, start songs and lists, and follow Now Playing while the Q2 plays into the car. The protocol is coda-rc ([remote-protocol](remote-protocol.md), `remote/coda-rc.proto`); this section is how the Q2 serves it.

**Two halves.** The protocol runs in `coda-rc` (`/usr/bin/coda-rc`, `patch/coda_rc.c`, `coda_rc_core.c`, `coda_rc_lib.c`, `coda_rc_ble.c`, `coda_rc_mdns.c`, with Monocypher), a program of its own built by `compile_helper` (`tools/build.py` `CODA_RC_SOURCES`) against the rootfs's libc and SQLite. Nothing of it is in demo's payload, so its parser, sessions, keys and buffers cost neither the payload's code room nor its scratch state, and a network-facing service is not in the UI process. demo keeps a shim (`patch/coda_rc_shim.c`, `coda_rc_poll` in `ringnav_sleep`, paced to 500 ms), whose state is a few words: it does what only demo can, and talks to the daemon through files in `/tmp`, reading the daemon's when the daemon [tells it](#car-remote-tell).

**Off means off.** The switch (`Q2POD CARREMOTE`, 0 by default) is the only thing that starts the daemon: the shim starts it on the first poll after boot when the switch is on (no init script, so the emulator, which runs no init scripts, behaves as a Q2), starts it when the switch goes on, starts it again if it has died (at most every 30 s), and kills it (`/tmp/coda-rc.pid`) when the switch goes off. The daemon runs at nice 19. Off, no port is open and nothing advertises. On, it holds Smart Wi-Fi's radio while a phone could use it ([Smart Wi-Fi](#smart-wi-fi)): with a Wi-Fi link, for 10 minutes (`CR_NET_IDLE_MS`) after Car Remote started and after a phone was last connected by any way or a pairing card was up (`coda_rc_wants_wifi`); with no link it holds nothing, since with no saved network in range the radio only scanned for one, and the phone in the car comes over Bluetooth LE, which advertises whatever Wi-Fi does. The heat log of 2026-11-22 had the radio on and scanning (the Wi-Fi driver's thread and `wpa_supplicant` among the busiest) in the idle samples on battery with Car Remote on and no network joined.

**Discovery.** While Wi-Fi has an address, `coda_rc_mdns.c` answers mDNS for `_q2muse._tcp` (the records are [remote-protocol: Discovery](remote-protocol.md#discovery)), so Q2 Muse Remote's Pair a Q2 Muse lists the Q2. It is one socket more in the daemon's poll, no thread: once a second while a phone is connected or a pairing is up, every 5 s while the daemon is quiet (`mdns_pace`, `MDNS_CHECK_IDLE_MS`), `mdns_poll` reads `wlan0`'s address (`SIOCGIFADDR`), and every 5 s the Bluetooth name from config.ini (`BTNAME`, checked as `bt_name_valid` checks it); a new address or name says goodbye to the old records, closes the socket and opens one on the new address, which announces twice a second apart. A socket the kernel refuses is tried again on a new address or after 30 s (`MDNS_RETRY_MS`), with one log line each time. The socket binds 5353 with `SO_REUSEADDR`, beside shairport's own responder (built into stock's AirPlay receiver, which offers no registration) and librespot's, and joins 224.0.0.251 on that address. `IP_MULTICAST_IF` is not required: qemu-user 8.2 refuses it in every form (EADDRNOTAVAIL, a MIPS probe under the emulator's qemu, 2026-11-17), and without it sends follow the route, which on a Q2 is `wlan0`. `mdns_query` and `mdns_reply` are the packet half, pure and bounds-checked: names are read with compression pointers that may only point back, at most 255 bytes, and any count, length or pointer past the packet makes it malformed (`test/unit/test_coda_rc_mdns.py`, each packet against an unreadable page). `--mdns-if IF` names another interface (the emulator's: it has no `wlan0`), `--no-mdns` turns it off; the host build answers only with `--mdns-if`.

**Transports.** TCP port 7720, and Bluetooth LE through a GATT server of the daemon's own (`coda_rc_ble.c`), not bluetoothd's and not `libSL`'s. V1.36's bluetoothd has no GATT or advertising D-Bus API: `/org/bluez/hci0` has `Adapter1`, `Media1` and `BatteryProviderManager1` but no `GattManager1` or `LEAdvertisingManager1` (`UnknownMethod`, a real Q2, 2026-11-17), as its adapter registration (`0x826d0`) never calls `btd_gatt_database_new` or `btd_adv_manager_new`; SyncLink's `libSL.so` serves LE by itself instead, listening on the ATT channel and advertising through the kernel's management socket (`ble_mgmt_adv`: Remove Advertising, then Add Advertising, instance 1). The daemon does the same: an L2CAP `SOCK_SEQPACKET` listener on the LE ATT fixed channel (CID 4, LE public, any address), a hand-written ATT server over a fixed 13-handle table (GAP's Device Name and Appearance, then coda-rc's service: control, event and its CCCD, info), and `MGMT_OP_ADD_ADVERTISING` on an `HCI_CHANNEL_CONTROL` socket (instance 2; connectable and discoverable flags, the kernel adding the Flags field; the 128-bit service UUID in the data and the Bluetooth name, read every 5 s as mDNS reads it, in the scan response). Nothing needs encryption or a bond: coda-rc's pairing and sealing protect the session, and a bond could make the phone take the Q2 for an audio device. One phone at a time: its connection removes the advertisement (one less thing on air beside A2DP) and its end adds it again; a second phone's connection is closed. Its frames go to the session one at a time, each once the answer before it has left the daemon's queue (`feed`), and the accepted socket's send buffer is 4 KB, so a cover's answer drains at the link's pace before the next request is read; more than two whole frames waiting drops the link. A send that fails marks the link and it ends after the pass (`ble_handle`), never inside the session's own call. The connection interval is the kernel's to keep: Linux 5.10 asks the phone for 30-50 ms when a peripheral link comes up outside that range (`l2cap_le_conn_ready`, `conn_min_interval` 24 and `conn_max_interval` 40 units by default). While SyncLink is on (`[SYSSET] SYNCLINK` above 0) libSL owns the channel, so nothing for LE is opened and the log says `ble: off while SyncLink is on` once; config.ini is read again every 5 s and LE opens or closes to follow it. With Bluetooth off there is no `hci0` (Add Advertising answers Invalid Index, or the kernel sends Index Removed): the daemon logs `ble: Bluetooth is off; waiting for it` once and asks nothing until the kernel's Index Added, then advertises 2 s later. Any other refusal is tried again every 30 s, logged once (`log_once`). `/tmp/coda-rc.ble` exists while the advertisement stands (`crc_ble_advertising`), for the Pair a Phone page. ponytail: the kernel does not refuse a phone's later move to a shorter interval (Android's `CONNECTION_PRIORITY_HIGH`), so the app must not ask for one; and the radio side (advertising, the LE link beside A2DP) is proven only on a real Q2 ([remote-protocol: Testing on a Q2](remote-protocol.md#testing-on-a-q2)); on the host `test/unit/test_coda_rc_ble.py` drives the daemon through `--ble-sim`.

**Security.** Every session authenticates before anything but the handshake is answered, and seals every frame after; pairing needs the code on the Q2's screen ([remote-protocol: Pairing and authentication](remote-protocol.md#pairing-and-authentication)). Keys are in `/mnt/data/coda-rc/peers` (0600, never the card). The schema carries no credentials, settings writes, paths or updates. The daemon validates every length and offset it is sent; SQL takes ids only after `arg_ok` refuses quotes, and search text only as a bound parameter.

**Its log.** `/tmp/coda-rc.log` (`crc_log`, emptied past 64 KB, `LOG_MAX`; its start line names the ports it listens on, `start: tcp 7720 listening, q2-iroh's port 7721`, and a port it cannot take ends it at once with a `start failed` line and no pid file, so the shim starts it again 30 s later instead of taking a daemon with no listener for alive): each line starts with its UTC time as the unified log writes it (`2026-11-20T00:25:27Z demo: play 0 1 9199 done`; `log_stamp` turns `time()` into the date itself, as the daemon has no `gmtime`), so a Play or a cover ask can be set beside the player's and Bluetooth's lines. A Play's line is the shim's verb, `play <start> <shuffle> <count>`.

**The library** (`coda_rc_lib.c`). Each request opens `/mnt/data/database.db` read-only, attaches `/mnt/mmc/.q2pod/catalogue.db` when it is on the card (only signed-in apps' rows are in it; `lib_has_server`), builds two temporary views over `songtable` (and `servertable`, joined to `servermeta` for its lengths: the two share column names such as `track`, so each column the view takes from them is named by its table), answers and closes, so no lock or schema outlives a request and a rebuilt catalogue (renamed over the old one) is simply opened anew. The tree, its orders and the letter buckets (over 120 entries; a bucket over 500 splits by two, then three letters; year orders by decade) are those of q2-auto-remote's `tools/q2bridge.py`, so the app's `LibraryTree` maps onto it unchanged; titles go out unnumbered, and an album's rows carry their track number in `Item.number` (no other row does), which the app shows as q2bridge's "N • Title". After Folders the Library level lists **Favorites** (`favorites`: the liked songs, stock's `myfav`, by path, in the tracks' orders) and **Recently Added** (`recent`: the `RECENT_CAP`, 100, songs with the latest `time_create`, newest first, never lettered), advertised as `CAP_FAVORITES` and `CAP_RECENT` ([remote-protocol](remote-protocol.md#favorites-and-recently-added)). An id whose list comes out empty answers NOT_FOUND, except a playlist that exists, Favorites and the top folder; the bucketing needs SQLite's window functions, which the rebuilt SQLite 3.54.1 has ([third-party](third-party.md)). Ids: `song:t<id>` for a card song, `song:c<id>` for a server one (the catalogue's ids start at `0x40000000`), `album:` with the folder's FNV-1a hash or the server album's id. Lengths come from Long Songs' cache (`ringnav-durations-v1`, [Song durations](#song-durations)) and the catalogue's `servermeta`. A cover is Cover Flow's 160 px cache file when the phone asks for 160 px or less, else the server app's cover (its 512 px `covers/512/<album>.jpg` for an ask over 160 px when the app has fetched it, else its 160 px one: a 160 px cover looked soft in the car's ~350 px art box, 2026-11-16; the Q2's own screens keep the 160 px ones, as its rows hand the file to AWTK, which decodes it whole on the UI thread into its image cache, 1 MiB a cover at 512 px against 100 KiB at 160), a picture in the folder, or the first FLAC's embedded picture, sent in pieces of up to 4 KB; a server album with none of these is asked of its app first ([A cover the card lacks](#car-remote-covers)). A playlist row's art is its first song's album's, except a server playlist's (`cat.serverlists`) once its app has its cover, `covers/pl-<pid>.jpg` (Navidrome's collage, [server-library: Covers](server-library.md#covers)): then its art id is `p<pid>` (`plart`, a SQL function that looks for the file, so a playlist whose cover is not fetched yet keeps its first album's), and `GetCover` for it finds the app by `pid` in `cat.serverlists` and sends that file (`pl_cover_find`); a name with `/`, an app id over 15 characters or a pid over 46 has no such art. ponytail: `norm` folds ASCII case only, and the Library's scope markers (`q2-library-scope`) are not applied; both as q2bridge.py does.

**Now Playing out.** The shim writes `/tmp/coda-rc.now` (`key=value` lines: play state, position, length, the song's id, path and tags, shuffle, repeat, volume, the song's hearts, the queue's place, length and version, and `qlist`, the queue's own version, which a shuffle's listing does not move) whenever any of it changes, so once a second while playing, through `blob_io`'s rename. The toast the Q2 Muse showed last is in it for 4 s (`note`, and `noten` counting them; `coda_rc_note`, from `toast`). What it names is [now_source.c's](#now-playing-source) `now_get`: the queue's song at `MCL_POS`, or a server song pressed and not yet the player's (`catalogue_np_now`), from the press, as Now Playing shows it; or another owner (`source=radio`, `netradio`, `spotify` or `video`), with no hearts or path, a radio `live=1` with `station=` and no length or position. On a queue change (its deque, its length or `playback_loads`) it writes `/tmp/coda-rc.queue`, the queue's song ids (a song with no library record, a card app's stream download, also its path, title and artist after tabs), with the place it had then; GetQueue answers the place from `/tmp/coda-rc.now` instead while both name the same queue version, since the queue file is not written again when only the place moves. The daemon reads the file whenever one of the shim's files is renamed into `/tmp` (an inotify watch, `IN_MOVED_TO`, in its `poll`) and pushes what changed to subscribed sessions, the position once a second while playing; the song's album and album artist pages ([remote-protocol: Links from now playing](remote-protocol.md#links-from-now-playing), `np_nodes`) are looked up in the library once a song, not at each push; its `poll` otherwise sleeps until the next thing falls due (`wait_ms`: the second's tick, mDNS's next look or announcement, the next position push for a phone that follows it, held-back bytes, a command's `ACK_MS`), at most `TICK_MS` (1 s), where it woke every 250 ms. With no phone connected and no pairing (`quiet`), it leaves that watch unread and its tick is `TICK_IDLE_MS` (5 s), the paired phones' check (`peers_poll`) skipped: nothing a file or a second could change goes anywhere then, and a phone connecting or an mDNS query wakes it as before. Measured on this machine with a host build, no session, mDNS on an interface with no address, and Now Playing renamed in twice a second as while a song plays: 159 context switches a minute before (10 ms of CPU), 24 after (none measurable) (2026-11-22). <a id="car-remote-tell"></a>The daemon also tells demo when it has written or removed a file the shim reads (`.cmd`, `.pair`, `.pair-end`, `.wake`, `.online`; `coda_rc.c` `tell_shim`): one byte down a pipe whose write end the shim hands it at its start (`cr_start`: `pipe2` with `O_CLOEXEC`, the write end made inheritable for that one `system()` and closed in demo after it, `--tell-fd N`, which the daemon takes only if it is open for writing only, and makes nonblocking and close-on-exec). The byte carries nothing: the files stay the one channel, and the pipe has no name, so nothing that could not already write `/tmp` can reach demo by it, and no authentication is needed beside the phones'. A thread in demo (`cr_tell`) sleeps in `read` on the other end, counts each byte and wakes the UI loop (`loop_wake`), so the files are read on the next pass, a command run at once instead of up to 500 ms later; otherwise the shim reads them every `CR_FILES_MS` (5 s) as a check, and every `CR_POLL_MS` (500 ms) while a play waits for its timer or the pairing card is up, whose next steps are a poll's, and while Car Audio's iPhone is on the cable, where a q2-iap from before the command queue ([Commands in](#car-remote-commands)) writes the car's buttons in `.cmd` and never tells (on the drive of 2026-11-22 the car's held Next reached the scan every 5 s, and the scan ran in bursts). Now Playing out, the daemon's restart and the Car Remote pages keep `CR_POLL_MS`. Without the pipe (a daemon this demo did not start, `pipe2` refused, the daemon gone and its end closed) the files are read every `CR_POLL_MS`, as they always were. ponytail: another thread's fork in the moment the write end is inheritable would hold it too, so the thread would end only with that child; the tells still come. Under a shuffle the file lists the play order Up Next shows (`cr_queue`): the songs played (at most half the 5000 lines), the one playing, then what plays after it, this pass and the next; its pos and Now Playing's `qpos` are the playing song's line and `qlen` the lines, and a jump names a line (`cr_jump` maps it back to the queue's index). The three run on into each other, so a Next moves only the place and the file is written again only when the order changes. Its version (`qgen`) moves with the lines, so a shuffle turned on or off moves it though the queue is the same; Play's resume asks instead whether the queue is still the list it started by `qlist`, which moves only with the deque, its size or a load (`cr_queue`; `coda_rc.c` hands it to `lib_played`, `lib_now` and Play), so Shuffle on and off from the car leave Resume carrying on. Otherwise it is the queue's own order, pos its index; up to 5000 are listed. Car Audio's iPhone list (`q2-iap`'s Up Next on iDrive, `PB_QUEUE_INDEX`) reads the same file and place.

<a id="car-remote-commands"></a>**Commands in.** Every command goes to the shim, which runs it inside demo. They go down one FIFO, `/tmp/coda-rc.cmdq` (`patch/coda_rc_cmdq.h`), from the daemon (a phone's) and from q2-iap (the car's buttons): each a line `<seq> <verb>`, one `write()` under 64 bytes (`crc_cmdq_send`), which a FIFO keeps whole and in order. The shim makes it (`cr_cmdq_start`: `mknod` through the o32 syscall, a stale file of that name removed first) and a thread of its own reads it (`cr_cmdq_read`; the FIFO open read-write, so a sender closing it is no end of file), hands each line to the UI pass through four slots (`CR_QN`; the FIFO holds the rest) and wakes the loop, so a command runs on the pass after it is sent, in order, with no file read on a timer. A sender that finds no reader (the open refused: no demo yet, or one from before the queue) writes `/tmp/coda-rc.cmd` as before; the shim reads that first, every `CR_POLL_MS` with q2-iap's cable in. Through that single file alone (reproduced in `test/fw/test_coda_rc_shim.py` on the shim before the queue) two commands inside one poll were one, the second renamed over the first unread (the car's Next tapped twice 300 ms apart skipped one song), the phone's and the car's replaced each other, a command waited up to 500 ms for the poll, and a play, which its timer read again from the file, was dropped with no answer when another command came first; a play or a radio now keeps its line for its timer (`cr.play_line`), and no command after it runs until the timer has. The answers go to `/tmp/coda-rc.ack` as the last four, newest first (`cr_ack`, `CR_ACKS`), and the daemon looks for its own among them (`ack_poll`), so a car's command answered after a phone's no longer leaves the phone's to time out as UNAVAILABLE. A play or a radio, whose work runs on a timer, is answered "taken" as the shim takes it (`CRC_ACK_TAKEN`, 9, `coda_rc_cmdq.h`) and again when its timer is done: the daemon, seeing "taken", waits `ACK_TAKEN_MS` (7 s, under the 8 s Q2 Muse Remote waits for any answer before it drops the session) for that answer instead of `ACK_MS` (4 s). A shuffled Play's start held a loaded emulator's loop for 9 s (`ui pass 9076 ms`, `coda_rc_e2e.py` on 2026-11-23), and the phone was told UNAVAILABLE for a Play that happened. A command the shim has not taken within `ACK_MS` (demo's loop held before it could) is still UNAVAILABLE. The daemon numbers its commands from the clock (`cmd_seq`), under q2-iap's, which start at `0x51000000`, so a restarted daemon's never meet answers the shim still keeps. Play, Pause and Play/Pause (`resume`, `pause`, `toggle`), Next and Previous are `media_key`'s, a headset button's ([Headset controls](#headset-controls-and-volume)): they reach whatever plays without passing through a window, since the window in front may take a press of the Q2's own button for itself: a toast's `msginfo_dialog_on_keyup` stops Play/Pause, the wheel's steps and the skip buttons while it is up ("Pixel 10 Pro paired" just after a pairing), and OLED's Shuffle confirmation (`feedback_shuffled`) closes on any key and stops it, for its 1.2 s after a shuffled list starts. Pause and Play press only when the player is not already as asked, and are answered once `media_playing` shows it, or refused after 3 s (`CR_SETTLE_MS`), so an Ack is the player's state, not a press sent. The daemon logs each Transport (`transport <verb>: state ...`) and the shim's answer (`demo: <verb> done` or `not done`) in `/tmp/coda-rc.log`. The shim logs each command it takes in the unified log (`remote`, `cr_said`): its words, `from the phone` or `from the car` by its number, the player's status before it (2 playing, 3 paused) and, where it says more, what came of it (`play 1 0 2 from the phone: the player 2, 2 songs from 1`, `jump 2 99 from the phone: the player 2, not that song now`), so a phone's pick can be told from a song's end (on the drive of 2026-11-23 two songs were cut by a `set-nexturl` with no car button, and the log could not say who). Playing a list: the daemon writes the list's song ids to `/tmp/coda-rc.list` and sends `<seq> play <index> <shuffle> <count>`; the shim, on a timer (play_folder opens a window), matches the ids against the whole library's records (`staged(songs_unsorted)`, sorted by `REC_ID`), plays them with `play_folder(…, 0xf001)` or `shuffle_play`, and answers `<seq> 0` in `/tmp/coda-rc.ack` (2 while a scan, a card game's sound or USB mode holds it off: the phone gets UNAVAILABLE). Seek is `player_seek_time`; volume is set as AirPlay's is, up to Volume Limit and saved for the output in use. `mode <shuffle> <repeat>` (SetMode, -1 for a mode left alone) goes where the Q2 Muse keeps the pair: while playback.c's extended play runs (`playback_active`), `playback_set`, as the hold menu's Shuffle and Repeat rows ([Queue menu](#queue-menu)), mapped to the nearest Q2 mode; otherwise Now Playing's buttons' `np_mode_set` (`np_bar.c`: stock's `MCL_MODE` and `[IPOD] NPSHUFONE`/`NPREPOFF`), so their icons follow (`cr_mode`). Now Playing out reads the pair from the same place (`cr_modes`: `playback_option` while active, else `np_mode_shuffle`/`np_mode_repeat`). Before, the shim read and set only playback.c's pair, which plays only while active, so a mode changed on the Q2 Muse never reached the car and the car's never moved the Q2 Muse's buttons (2026-11-16). `radio <record id>` (0 the playing song) and `radio stop` are StartRadio's, run on a timer as play's, through `song_radio_car` ([Radio](#radio)). `rate <hearts> <song id>` is `rate_now_set` (`ratings.c`): the picker's own `rate_song`, through Now Playing's heart click while that page is open so its heart follows, else batch-select's Add to My Fav or `deleteMusicFromFav` as the queue menu's Favorites rows; the hearts go out in `/tmp/coda-rc.now` (`rate_now`, -1 for a stream), read again on a new song, a My Fav change made here (`catalogue_fav_gen`) or every 5 s, since stock's lists change My Fav without telling. `jump <index> <song id>` plays a queue entry as Up Next's row does (`player_start_queue`, after `press_stamp`, refused while Headphones required forbids it); the playing entry plays on. Rate and jump check the song id first and answer 3 when it is not there, which the daemon sends as NOT_FOUND. Resume ([remote-protocol](remote-protocol.md#modes-rating-the-queue-resume-and-radio)) is the daemon's alone: the shim writes Now Playing before a Play's ack, so the daemon has the new queue's version, and from the ack on, while that version plays, it keeps the list's song in `/mnt/data/coda-rc/places`, rewritten on each song change (the first song at the ack itself, so a list left within a second still has its place).

<a id="car-remote-streams"></a>**A streaming song.** A card app's song streamed without an offline copy plays from its download, `/mnt/mmc/.<app>/stream/<account>/<quality>/<x>/<title> [<sid>].<suffix>` (`x` a hex digit of the sid's hash), with no library record: the shim's id is 0 and its title the file's name (the Q2 Muse's own Now Playing reads the file's tags). The daemon's `np_stream` (`coda_rc.c`) looks the path up once per song with `lib_stream_song` (`coda_rc_lib.c`): `stream_sid` takes the sid from the name's last brackets (letters, digits, `-` and `_` only) and the app from the path (`stream_path_sid`, `patch/stream_path.h`, which the payload's `cat_copy_of` reads the same paths with: on the Q2 itself such a download is its server row for the cover, the play key, the hearts and the info page's genre and year), and the catalogue's `servermeta` row for that sid and app, joined to `servertable` by `fileurl`, gives the song id (`song:c<id>`), title, artist, album, length and the album's art id (`akey` of the row's `cat/<album>/` path). NowPlaying carries those, the length only while the player reports none (a stream's is 0 until it has downloaded), and `rateable` from the shim's hearts: Rate takes the server song's id and sends the shim the record's, 0, which it compares, and `rate_now_set` rates the download through its catalogue row as Now Playing's heart does (`ratings.c` `rate_fav`, `catalogue_song_key`). `cover_find` for a server album with no `covers/<album>.jpg` tries `stream_picture`: each of the album's sids, `glob`bed in `/mnt/mmc/.<app>/stream/*/*/*/*[<sid>].*` (any account, quality and shard folder), and the first FLAC picture found (the user's screenshot, 2026-11-16 14:34: Android Auto showed `hello [VcF5XCDqrNB23RlHx35Z0w].flac`, no artist, 0:00 and no cover; reproduced with the build's coda-rc under qemu-user). ponytail: the cover needs its app signed in (the art id is looked up in the songs view, which holds server albums only then); and the player switches to a stream only once it has downloaded (about 6.7 s for a 20 MB FLAC).

<a id="car-remote-covers"></a>**A cover the card lacks.** A server album whose app has no cover of it yet (no `covers/512/<album>.jpg` or `covers/<album>.jpg`, the app's rounds not there yet) and no picture in a streamed song of it (`stream_picture`) is fetched for the car on demand. `lib_cover` (`coda_rc_lib.c`), for a `GetCover` at offset 0, calls `crc_cover_ask` (`coda_rc.c`) with the app's id, the album id and the size, 512 for an ask over 160 px, else 160. When the app's `q2app` says `covers=1` (read from the card at each such miss), the daemon adds a line to `/tmp/q2-<id>.coverask`, `<seq> <px> <album>`, one per cover asked and not yet answered (the file is rewritten without the answered ones, and removed when none is left), and, while the app's `/tmp/q2-<id>.browse.sock` is not there, names the app in `/tmp/coda-rc.wake`, which the shim's next poll hands to `addon_cover_wake` (`addon.c`: started with `addon_wake` only when its `q2app` says `covers=1`) and removes. The app reads the file whenever it changes, a line there at its start included, fetches each new line's cover at the size asked and saves it where `cover_find` reads it, then answers in its state file, `coverack=<seq> <code>`, in seq order (q2-subsonic: 0 saved, 1 not its album, 2 the server has none, 3 failed; it notes the second in the folder's `.none` and remembers the third for 10 minutes, so the server is asked once). The `GetCover`'s answer is held meanwhile (`holds`, 8 at most; a ninth is answered `NOT_FOUND` at once, its ask still made), without blocking the daemon's loop: every pass reads the state file of each app with an ask waiting (`cover_poll`; the app's rename into `/tmp` ends the loop's sleep), and a hold whose ask is answered, or that is `COVER_HOLD_MS` (5 s) old, is answered through `lib_cover` again, the cover if the app saved it, else `NOT_FOUND`. 5 s is under the 8 s the phone waits for any answer before it closes the session (q2-auto-remote `CodaSession.TIMEOUT_MS`); its `ArtProvider` keeps no failed cover, so the car's placeholder gives way to the cover the next time Android Auto asks for the row's art. An ask the app hasn't answered in `COVER_ASK_MS` (60 s) is dropped from the file; one answered without a cover is not asked again for `COVER_AGAIN_MS` (10 min), and a hold for it is `NOT_FOUND` at once. Seqs start at the boot clock's milliseconds (`crc_now_ms`) when the daemon starts, so a restarted daemon's are above the last run's, and the app takes a line by its text, not its number. An app that has not said `covers=1` (one from before) is never asked, and its misses are `NOT_FOUND` at once. ponytail: a cold app (started by the wake, signing in) can take longer than the hold, so the first ask of a drive may show the placeholder until the row is drawn again; the asks are serial in the app, so of a page of 20 new albums the last ones come after the hold too. Checks: `test_coda_rc_lib.py` (the ask and the answer after it), `test_coda_rc_daemon.py` (a cover saved and sent, an answer of none, the hold's end with other requests answered meanwhile, an app without `covers=1`), `test/fw` `test_addon.py` and `test_coda_rc_shim.py` (the wake).

<a id="car-remote-iroh"></a>**Across networks.** While the switch is on and Wi-Fi has a link, the shim also runs `q2-iroh` (`/usr/bin/q2-iroh`, `remote/iroh-sidecar`, [remote: Car Remote across networks](remote.md#car-remote-across-networks)): `cr_iroh_poll`, every `CR_POLL_MS`, starts it once stock's `networkGetConnectStatus` shows a link (`cr_iroh_start`: `--key /mnt/data/coda-rc/iroh.key --relay-file /mnt/data/coda-rc/relay --info /tmp/coda-rc.iroh --pid /tmp/q2-iroh.pid --nice 19 --log /tmp/q2-iroh.log --forward-named 127.0.0.1:7721 --allow-file /tmp/coda-rc.iroh-allow --open-while /tmp/coda-rc.qr`), unless it runs or the image has none, removing a dead one's `/tmp/coda-rc.iroh` first; a dead one is started again at most every 30 s; and once the link has been gone a minute (`CR_IROH_DOWN_MS`, which rides out a short drop) it is stopped (`cr_iroh_stop`), its pid and id files removed, so Pair a Phone's QR code goes with it. With no network it reaches no one, and the heat log of 2026-11-22 had it the idle Q2's largest CPU user in the 485 samples on battery with Wi-Fi down (its share summed 198, against demo's 125); on this machine, with no network at all (a namespace with only `lo`), it woke 23 times in 120 s and used no measurable CPU, so the device's cost is not reproduced off the device, and stopping it removes it either way. `cr_stop` kills both by their pid files and removes the id file. Its log, `/tmp/q2-iroh.log` (RAM), is its own (`--log`: each line opened, appended and closed, the file emptied first when a line would take it past 64 KB, `LOG_MAX`), where its stderr went to the file with no limit. It is an iroh endpoint registered with a relay (n0's, unless `/mnt/data/coda-rc/relay` names others, one URL a line) that carries each QUIC stream to the daemon's q2-iroh port, `127.0.0.1:7721` (loopback only, `--iroh-port`), as a TCP connection whose first 32 bytes are the phone's iroh key (`--forward-named`); after them the daemon serves it as any TCP session (`tcp_read` takes the key into `iroh`, `iroh_via` set). `GetRemote` (`get_remote`, `CAP_REMOTE`) reads its id and home relay from `/tmp/coda-rc.iroh` (`id HEX`, `relay URL` lines, rewritten whole whenever the home relay changes). <a id="car-remote-allow"></a>Only paired phones come in ([remote-protocol: Across networks: only paired phones](remote-protocol.md#across-networks-only-paired-phones)): the daemon keeps each phone's registered key in `/mnt/data/coda-rc/iroh-peers` (`peer_id[8] | key[32]`, `iroh_register`: from `RegisterRemote` over any session, and by itself from a session through q2-iroh that pairs or authenticates, `crc_iroh_proved`) and writes the keys of the phones still paired to `/tmp/coda-rc.iroh-allow`, 64 hex digits a line (`iroh_allow`), at its start, on each registration and whenever the paired phones' folder changes (an inotify watch on `/mnt/data/coda-rc`, polled even while quiet), so a Forget on the Settings page takes the key off at once. q2-iroh reads that file at each handshake and each new stream (`Gate::admits`) and refuses a key not in it, but while `/tmp/coda-rc.qr` exists (Pair a Phone's code). The daemon checks the same again: a session through q2-iroh whose key is not registered gets only the handshake and the pairing while that code is shown, and nothing at any other time (`frame` in `coda_rc_core.c`); one that leaves without pairing or Auth is refused at its next connection for 10 s, doubling to 5 minutes (`iroh_hold`, eight keys kept). Pair a Phone (`carremote_page.c`) shows a QR code while that file names an endpoint, a code was made and either a relay or a Wi-Fi address reaches it (`CR_BY_QR`; the address line is left out with none): `Q2MUSE:1:<code>:<id>:<address>:<relay>` in capitals (QR's alphanumeric mode: version 6, 4 px a module on the page's 180 px plate), its code drawn as the daemon draws one (`cr_qr_code`, four bytes of `/dev/urandom`) and kept in `/tmp/coda-rc.qr` while the page is open, with or without a QR code. `pair_start` (`coda_rc_core.c`) takes that code for the next pairing (`crc_code_shown`) instead of a new one, still shows it on the pairing card, and when that pairing ends, paired or not, the daemon removes the file (`crc_code_spent`), so the page draws a new code at its next poll: one guess per code shown, as with the card's ([remote-protocol: Pairing by QR code](remote-protocol.md#pairing-by-qr-code)). The QR painter is `ui_kit.c` `ui_qr`, Guest Play's. Measured: `q2-iroh` is 5,325,056 bytes (2.6 MB of the compressed rootfs) and about 8 MB resident under qemu; its key and id survive a restart, a phone's pairing does not depend on them. ponytail: an endpoint registered while Wi-Fi has a link costs some radio and battery, not measured on the device; a phone connected through it shows as "Connected over Wi-Fi", as the daemon sees a TCP session from `127.0.0.1`.

**Pairing on the Q2.** While `/tmp/coda-rc.pair` holds a code, the shim asks on the [pairing card](oled-design.md#pairing) (`patch/pair_prompt.c` `pair_prompt`, the confirm card's): "Pair with Pixel 8?", the code in two groups of three, "Enter this code in Q2 Muse Remote", and Cancel, which with Return or the daemon's 120 s (`CRC_PAIR_TIMEOUT_MS`, the card's bar) writes `/tmp/coda-rc.pair-cancel`. It closes when the daemon removes the file, and `/tmp/coda-rc.pair-end` says whether to toast the phone's name and "paired" ("Pixel 8 paired", `carremote_paired`, with Positive's check-circle; it closes How to Connect too) or "Pairing failed". Guest Play's guest asks on the same card (`guest_ui.c` `ask_card`); `confirm_t`'s `glyph` puts the phone over its title, and a title wider than the card's text column scrolls in it (`card_title`: the house marquee's hold, speed, gap and faded ends, a 33 ms frame timer while the card is up). A file holding another code than the card shows (the daemon ended one code and showed the next between two of the shim's polls) closes the card, and the next poll opens it on the new code (`cr_pairing`, `cr.pair_code`). The code outlives its phone's connection: a session that closes while pairing leaves the code and the card up (`pair_leave` in `coda_rc_core.c`), and a `PairStart` from the same client name within the code's 120 s gets that code again, so a phone that reconnects while the user types is not handed a new one; a wrong code, Cancel, the 120 s or another phone's `PairStart` ends it ([remote-protocol: Pairing](remote-protocol.md#pairing-a-pake-on-the-6-digit-code)). <a id="car-remote-settings"></a>**Settings > Car Remote** (`patch/carremote_page.c`, `carremote_page`) is the switch, its caption under it while selected; while on, Pair a Phone (the accent's top-action row) and a two-line row per paired phone, or, with none, the empty state with Pair a Phone as its button ([oled-design: Car Remote](oled-design.md#car-remote)). That button is a row of the page's own list (`K_CTA`, row 1 after a gap that keeps it under the empty state's words as the switch grows and shrinks; `empty_state` keeps its place but gets no row of its own), painted with `ui_cta_paint` and marked `_rings_itself`, so `paint_selection` draws no bar behind it. Its row reaches only as far past the capsule as the focus ring (`CR_CTA_OUT`, 5 px: the ring's 2 px, 3 px out), so under the switch its foot (y 280) stays inside OLED's list end (282) and the wheel moving on to it scrolls nothing; a foot past the list end by a pixel has `reveal` scroll it and `fit_top` take the list on to the row's top, the switch gone (the user's device, 2026-11-16, with an 8 px band, reproduced on the emulator). The ring (`ui_kit.c` `cta_ring`) is two images for its round ends, `tools/art.py` `cta_ring_end`'s annulus between radii 24 and 22 at 16 x 16 samples a pixel in the half's Text Primary (`ctaring_l_d`, `ctaring_r_l` and so on), and two whole rows of ink along its top and foot between them, so its arcs are graded as smoothly as the capsule's own edge. The row-at-a-time `round_ring` is kept for a set without those images (anti-aliased at any radius, [Rounded corners](#rounded-corners)); before `corner_cover.c` it had no coverage table for radii 24 and 23 and drew them in hard one-pixel steps, the jagged ring the user saw; two one-pixel `canvas_stroke_rounded_rect` pills still stepped unevenly where the strokes met at 6x (the user, 2026-11-16). As the empty state's own list it sat beside the page's, each holding a selection, and `surface_under` gives the wheel no surface when two do: the wheel moved nothing and the switch showed no bar (emulator, 2026-11-16). It reads three files the daemon writes. The peers file gives each phone's id, name and pairing time; `/tmp/coda-rc.online` holds a 9-byte record per authenticated session, the peer id and its link (0 Wi-Fi, TCP; 1 Bluetooth, BLE), written whenever that set changes (`online_poll`) and removed when the daemon stops; `/mnt/data/coda-rc/seen` holds a 12-byte record per paired phone, its id and the wall clock (u32 LE) when a session of it last authenticated or ended (`seen_stamp`, written only when a phone comes or goes, so the flash is not worn; a phone no longer paired is dropped). A row says "Connected over Wi-Fi" (with the Positive dot) or "Not connected · last seen Friday" (today, yesterday, a weekday within the week, else the date; nothing after "Not connected" for a phone not seen since this firmware or a clock never set). Its rows sit at their own heights: the list's `item_height` is 0 and stock's layout stacks them (`cr_fit`), the switch growing for its caption while selected, 10 px before Pair a Phone. Before this, `page_list`'s `item_height` forced every row to the one-line 32 px, so a phone's 52 px row lost its second line (Connected or Not connected) to its row's foot or to the next phone (the user's screenshot, 2026-11-16, reproduced on the emulator). Centre on a phone opens its page (`carphone_page`): Status, Paired (the date), Last Connected (Now while connected), Rename, then Forget Phone in red after a 12 px gap; it opens on Rename. The count each page hands `ringnav_select` is the rows the wheel stops on, the gaps passed (`collect`), so Forget Phone is row 4 and Pair a Phone row 1: a count with a gap in it does not match ringnav's own at its next load, which then drops the selection (`nav/lists.c` `load`), and the phone's page opened on Status that way (emulator, 2026-11-16). Rename is the letter strip (`search_strip_text`), which rewrites the record's name in the peers file; the name is the Q2 Muse's alone (the phone's own is unchanged). Forget asks on the confirmation card, Cancel first, then rewrites the peers file without that phone and closes the page; the daemon closes the phone's sessions within a second. Pair a Phone opens `carhowto_page`, one page in three modes (`cr_howto_mode`), each in the words of Q2 Muse Remote's one Pair a Q2 Muse screen (Scan QR code, and a list of the Q2 Muses it finds by Bluetooth and on the Wi-Fi at once, a code typed on the one tapped). The page's code shows in both modes a phone can pair in, since `pair_start` takes it whichever transport the phone came over. `CR_BY_QR` (above): the QR code, the code under it, and beside it "On your phone, open Q2 Muse Remote", "Tap Pair a Q2 Muse, then scan this or type the code", "Works from any network" only with a relay (without one iroh cannot cross networks, so "Phone on the same Wi-Fi as this Q2 Muse"), "Or nearby, by Bluetooth" while the daemon advertises, the Wi-Fi address, "Waiting…". `CR_BY_CODE`, no QR code (no `q2-iroh` id, no code, or neither relay nor address) but the daemon advertising (`g_bluetoothflag` and `/tmp/coda-rc.ble`; the flag so a killed daemon's file is not believed) or a Wi-Fi address (`SIOCGIFADDR` on `wlan0`): the code in Inter Medium 40 near the top, "On your phone, open Q2 Muse Remote, tap Pair a Q2 Muse and type this code", "Bluetooth  Phones nearby can find it" while it advertises, the address with "Phone on the same Wi-Fi" (the app's port, 7720, is coda-rc's, so no port is shown), "Waiting for a phone…"; with no code made the words say it shows when the phone asks (the daemon makes one and shows it on the pairing card). `CR_BY_NONE`, neither: "Turn on Bluetooth, or join a Wi-Fi network in Settings > Wi-Fi", "Come back here to pair", "Not reachable yet", and no "Waiting". Bluetooth on is not enough for the Bluetooth line: while advertising is refused, SyncLink holds the LE channel or a phone is connected over LE (above), a scan could not find the Q2. Each poll hashes what the page shows (`cr_howto_sum`: the mode, the address, advertising, the relay, the code and the QR code's text) and paints the page again when it changes, so Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or the relay coming or going, or a spent code, shows at once. The Q2 Muse cannot start a pairing (the phone sends `PairStart`), so the page only says how; it closes when a phone pairs, and the toast names the phone ("Pixel 10 Pro paired", with the Positive check). While a page is open each poll hashes the three files and the switch (`cr_read`) and rebuilds the page when the hash changes (`carremote_poll`, from the shim's poll), the selection kept on its row, so a pairing, a Forget, a rename, a connection or a disconnect shows within half a second.

## 2038

The rootfs is glibc 2.28 on 32-bit MIPS, so stock's `time_t` is 32 bits, and the root certificates in `assets/scrobble-ca.pem` expire between 2035 and 2046.

**TLS.** Every verified libcurl handle (Network Update, Q2 Shelf, Internet Radio, scrobbling, lyrics and covers, Tidal Downloads, and stock's own HTTPS through `ringnav_stock_tls`) checks the server's chain against its CA file and its name, but no certificate's dates: the rootfs's libcurl does its TLS with an mbedTLS built without `MBEDTLS_HAVE_TIME_DATE` ([third-party](third-party.md#curl-and-mbedtls)), so a chain still verifies after its roots expire (2035 on) and after the 32-bit clock wraps, and a Q2 whose clock was never set still connects. ponytail: an expired or retired server certificate is accepted too, and there is no revocation check. That is the price of working with a firmware nobody can update. hciplayer's streams are the exception: they do their TLS with the OpenSSL 1.0.1 linked into the player, which checks certificate dates ([Stock HTTPS](#stock-https)).

**Clock.** Linux 5.10 keeps 64-bit time, and glibc 2.28's `time()` truncates it to 32 bits. `wall_time` reads that unsigned, which is right until 2106. Scrobble timestamps use it. The iPod status bar takes it back in 28-year steps, a span over which dates and weekdays repeat, before stock's 32-bit `localtime`, which is right until 2100. ponytail: stock code stays 32-bit. Its clock screens and its network time sync (`ntpdate`, then `hwclock -wu`) will show or write wrong dates after January 2038, and NTP's 2036 era rollover depends on stock's `ntpdate`. Stock's own HTTPS calls go through the same libcurl, so they check no dates either, all but hciplayer's streams, which do ([Stock HTTPS](#stock-https)). Card apps' folder poll (`addon.c`) compares a 32-bit `st_mtime` with `time()`; both wrap together, so only the second of the wrap misjudges a change. librespot carries its own fix (DiamondBond/q2-librespot).
